entries.zh: 諺曰「力田不如逢年，善仕不如遇合」，固無虛言。
entries.en: As the proverb goes, "Hard work in the fields counts for less than a good harvest year, and skill in office counts for less than finding the right patron." These words ring true indeed.
entries.literal: A proverb says, 'Toiling at farming is not as good as encountering a good year; being skilled at officialdom is not as good as meeting the right opportunity.' These are certainly not empty words.

entries.zh: 非獨女以色媚，而士宦亦有之。
entries.en: It is not only women who win favor through their looks—men in service at court have done the same.
entries.literal: It is not only women who ingratiate themselves through beauty; officials and eunuchs also have such people among them.

entries.zh: 時會聚宮下博士諸先生與論議，共難之曰：「蘇秦、張儀一當萬乘之主，而都卿相之位，澤及後世。
entries.en: Once, the court academicians and scholars assembled and challenged him in debate: "Su Qin and Zhang Yi each won audience with the mightiest rulers of their age, rose to the rank of minister and chancellor, and their influence was felt for generations to come.
entries.literal: Once, the court scholars and academicians gathered and debated with him, challenging him together: "Su Qin and Zhang Yi each faced the rulers of ten-thousand-chariot states, rose to the positions of minister and chancellor, and their benefits reached to later generations.

entries.zh: 今子大夫修先王之術，慕聖人之義，諷誦詩書百家之言，不可勝數。
entries.en: Now you, sir, have cultivated the arts of the former kings, revered the righteous ways of the sages, and committed to memory the Odes, the Documents, and the writings of the hundred schools — more than can be counted.
entries.literal: Now you, sir, have studied the arts of the former kings, admired the righteous ways of the sages, and recited the Odes, the Documents, and the words of the hundred schools — too numerous to count.

entries.zh: 著於竹帛，自以為海內無雙，即可謂博聞辯智矣。
entries.en: Your writings fill scroll after scroll, and you consider yourself without peer in all the realm — a man of vast learning and eloquent wit, by any measure.
entries.literal: Your writings fill bamboo and silk, and you consider yourself without equal in the realm — one might indeed call you broadly learned and eloquently wise.

entries.zh: 然悉力盡忠以事聖帝，曠日持久，積數十年，官不過侍郎，位不過執戟，意者尚有遺行邪？
entries.en: And yet, for all your exhausting loyalty in the emperor's service, over the course of decades your office has never risen above Attendant Gentleman and your rank has never surpassed Halberd-Bearer. Could it be that there is something wanting in your conduct?
entries.literal: Yet despite exhausting your strength and devotion in serving the sage emperor, over the long course of decades, your office has never risen above Attendant Gentleman, your rank never beyond Halberd-Bearer. Could there perhaps still be some fault in your conduct?

entries.zh: 其故何也？」
entries.en: Why might that be?"
entries.literal: What is the reason for this?"

entries.zh: 東方生曰：「是固非子所能備也。
entries.en: Dongfang Shuo replied: "This is something that lies entirely beyond your understanding.
entries.literal: Master Dongfang said: "This is something you are simply unable to comprehend.

entries.zh: 彼一時也，此一時也，豈可同哉！
entries.en: Those were different times, and these are different times — how can the two be compared!
entries.literal: That was one era, and this is another — how can they be compared!

entries.zh: 夫張儀、蘇秦之時，周室大壞，諸侯不朝，力政爭權，相禽以兵，并為十二國，未有雌雄，得士者彊，失士者亡，故說聽行通，身處尊位，澤及後世，子孫長榮。
entries.en: In the days of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, the house of Zhou lay in ruins. The feudal lords no longer came to court; they governed by force and vied for supremacy, waging war upon one another. The world was divided among a dozen states, with no clear victor. Those who won talented men grew strong; those who lost them perished. And so these men's counsel was heeded, their plans put into action. They rose to the highest offices, their influence endured for generations, and their descendants prospered long after them.
entries.literal: In the time of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, the house of Zhou was in great ruin, the feudal lords no longer attended court, they governed by force and contended for power, seizing one another through warfare, merged into twelve states with no clear victor — those who won scholars grew strong, those who lost them perished. Therefore, their counsel was heeded, their proposals accepted, they occupied the highest positions, their influence reached later generations, and their descendants prospered for ages.

entries.zh: 今非然也。
entries.en: Today, things are entirely different.
entries.literal: Now it is not so.

entries.zh: 聖帝在上，德流天下，諸侯賓服，威振四夷，連四海之外以為席，安於覆盂，天下平均，合為一家，動發舉事，猶如運之掌中。
entries.en: A sage emperor reigns above, and his virtue flows to every corner of the realm. The feudal lords submit in deference, his authority makes the barbarians of the four directions tremble. The lands beyond the four seas lie before him like a spread mat, as steady as an overturned bowl. All under heaven is unified and at peace, joined as one great family, and every enterprise the emperor undertakes is as effortless as turning an object in the palm of his hand.
entries.literal: A sage emperor sits on the throne, his virtue flows throughout the realm, the feudal lords submit as guests, his authority shakes the four barbarian peoples, the lands beyond the four seas are spread like a mat, as stable as an overturned bowl, the empire is level and equal, united as one family, and every undertaking he sets in motion is as easy as turning something in the palm of his hand.

entries.zh: 賢與不肖，何以異哉？
entries.en: In such an age, what difference is there between the worthy and the unworthy?
entries.literal: Between the worthy and the unworthy, what difference is there?

entries.zh: 方今以天下之大，士民之眾，竭精馳說，并進輻湊者，不可勝數。
entries.en: Now, given the vastness of the empire and the sheer multitude of its people, those who pour out their talents and hawk their ideas, pressing forward from every direction — they are beyond counting.
entries.literal: At present, given the vastness of the empire and the multitude of scholars and common people, those who exhaust their talents and rush about peddling their ideas, pressing forward and converging from all sides, cannot be counted.

entries.zh: 悉力慕義，困於衣食，或失門戶。
entries.en: They devote every ounce of their strength to the pursuit of virtue, yet they can scarcely clothe and feed themselves, and some have lost even their family standing.
entries.literal: They devote all their strength to pursuing righteousness, yet are reduced to poverty in food and clothing, and some even lose their family standing.

entries.zh: 使張儀、蘇秦與仆并生於今之世，曾不能得掌故，安敢望常侍侍郎乎！
entries.en: If Zhang Yi and Su Qin were alive today, born into this same age as I, they could not so much as land a post as a petty archivist — how then would they dare dream of becoming Regular Attendant or Attendant Gentleman!
entries.literal: If Zhang Yi and Su Qin were born together with me in this present age, they could not even obtain the post of a minor archivist — how would they dare hope for the rank of Regular Attendant or Attendant Gentleman!

entries.zh: 傳曰：『天下無害菑，雖有聖人，無所施其才；
entries.en: As the tradition has it: 'When the world is free of calamity and ruin, even a sage has no occasion to display his talents.
entries.literal: The tradition says: 'When the world is free from harm and disaster, though there be sages, they have no occasion to exercise their talents;

entries.zh: 上下和同，雖有賢者，無所立功。』
entries.en: When those above and below are in harmony, even a worthy man has no occasion to win distinction.'
entries.literal: When high and low are harmonious and united, though there be worthy men, they have no occasion to establish merit.'

entries.zh: 故曰時異則事異。
entries.en: The saying goes: different times call for different measures.
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said: when the times change, affairs change with them.

entries.zh: 雖然，安可以不務修身乎？
entries.en: And yet, how can a man neglect the cultivation of his own character?
entries.literal: Even so, how can one fail to devote oneself to self-cultivation?

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：『鼓鐘于宮，聲聞于外。
entries.en: As the Odes say: 'When drums and bells sound within the palace, their music carries beyond the walls.
entries.literal: The Odes say: 'When drums and bells sound in the palace, their sound is heard outside.

entries.zh: 鶴鳴九皋，聲聞于天。』。
entries.en: The crane cries from the deepest marsh, and its voice reaches the heavens.'
entries.literal: The crane cries at the ninth marsh, and its voice is heard in heaven.'

entries.zh: 茍能修身，何患不榮！
entries.en: If a man can truly cultivate himself, what need has he to worry that recognition will not come!
entries.literal: If one can cultivate oneself, why worry about not being honored!

entries.zh: 太公躬行仁義七十二年，逢文王，得行其說，封於齊，七百歲而不絕。
entries.en: The Grand Duke practiced benevolence and righteousness in person for seventy-two years before he met King Wen, gained the chance to put his ideas into practice, and was enfeoffed in Qi — where his line endured unbroken for seven hundred years.
entries.literal: The Grand Duke personally practiced benevolence and righteousness for seventy-two years before he met King Wen, was able to put his ideas into action, and was enfeoffed in Qi, where his line endured for seven hundred years without interruption.

entries.zh: 此士之所以日夜孜孜，修學行道，不敢止也。
entries.en: This is why the scholar toils day and night without respite, cultivating his learning and walking the Way, never daring to cease.
entries.literal: This is why scholars toil day and night without rest, studying and walking the Way, never daring to stop.

entries.zh: 今世之處士，時雖不用，崛然獨立，塊然獨處，上觀許由，下察接輿，策同范蠡，忠合子胥，天下和平，與義相扶，寡偶少徒，固其常也。
entries.en: The recluse scholars of our age, though the times have no use for them, stand tall and solitary, dwelling apart in their grandeur. They look upward to Xu You for inspiration and downward to Jie Yu; their stratagems rival those of Fan Li, and their loyalty matches that of Wu Zixu. The world is at peace, and they sustain themselves through righteousness. That they have few companions and fewer followers — this is simply their lot.
entries.literal: The recluse scholars of our age, though the times do not employ them, stand towering and alone, dwelling in solitary grandeur. They look up to Xu You, study Jie Yu below, their strategy matches Fan Li, their loyalty accords with Zixu. The world is at peace, and they support each other with righteousness. Having few companions and fewer followers — this is simply their normal lot.

entries.zh: 子何疑於余哉！」
entries.en: Why then do you question me!"
entries.literal: Why should you doubt me!"

entries.zh: 於是諸先生默然無以應也。
entries.en: At this, every one of the scholars fell silent, with not a word to say in reply.
entries.literal: At this, all the scholars fell silent, having nothing to say in reply.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「六藝於治一也。
entries.en: Confucius said: "The Six Arts all serve a single purpose in governance.
entries.literal: Confucius said: "The Six Arts are united in governance.

entries.zh: 禮以節人，樂以發和，書以道事，詩以達意，易以神化，春秋以義。」
entries.en: The Rites temper human conduct, Music inspires harmony, the Documents illuminate affairs of state, the Odes give voice to the heart's intent, the Changes reveal the workings of the divine, and the Spring and Autumn Annals uphold righteousness."
entries.literal: Ritual regulates people, Music brings forth harmony, the Documents speak of affairs, the Odes convey meaning, the Changes work spiritual transformation, and the Spring and Autumn Annals uphold righteousness."

entries.zh: 太史公曰：天道恢恢，豈不大哉！
entries.en: The Grand Historian remarks: How vast and all-embracing is the Way of Heaven!
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: The Way of Heaven is vast and all-encompassing — is it not great!

entries.zh: 談言微中，亦可以解紛。
entries.en: A well-placed jest, hitting subtly upon the truth, can untangle even the most knotted affairs.
entries.literal: Casual words that subtly hit the mark can also resolve disputes.

entries.zh: 褚先生曰：臣為郎時，游觀長安中，見卜筮之賢大夫，觀其起居行步，坐起自動，誓正其衣冠而當鄉人也，有君子之風。
entries.en: Master Chu says: When I served as a Palace Gentleman, I wandered through Chang'an observing its sights. I encountered worthy gentlemen among the diviners and observed their daily conduct: how they walked, how they rose and sat with natural composure, and how they straightened their caps and robes when greeting their neighbors. They had the bearing of true gentlemen.
entries.literal: Master Chu says: When I served as a Palace Gentleman, I wandered about and observed in Chang'an. I saw worthy gentlemen among the diviners and observed their daily conduct and manner of walking, how they rose and sat with self-possession, and how they straightened their caps and robes when facing their fellow townspeople. They had the bearing of gentlemen.

entries.zh: 見性好解婦來卜，對之顏色嚴振，未嘗見齒而笑也。
entries.en: When flirtatious women came for divination, the diviners received them with stern, dignified expressions and never once bared their teeth in a smile.
entries.literal: When flirtatious women came for divination, they faced them with stern and dignified expressions and never once showed their teeth in a smile.

entries.zh: 從古以來，賢者避世，有居止舞澤者，有居民閒閉口不言，有隱居卜筮閒以全身者。
entries.en: Since ancient times, worthy men who withdrew from the world have taken different paths: some dwelt in remote marshes, some lived quietly among the people and spoke not a word, and some concealed themselves among the diviners to preserve their lives.
entries.literal: Since ancient times, when the worthy have shunned the world, some have dwelt in remote marshes, some have lived among the people with mouths shut and silent, and some have hidden among diviners to preserve themselves.

entries.zh: 夫司馬季主者，楚賢大夫，游學長安，通易經，術黃帝、老子，博聞遠見。
entries.en: Sima Jizhu was a worthy grandee of Chu who traveled to Chang'an to study. He mastered the Book of Changes, practiced the arts of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, and was a man of wide learning and far-reaching insight.
entries.literal: Sima Jizhu was a worthy grandee of Chu who traveled to study in Chang'an; he was versed in the Book of Changes, practiced the arts of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, and was broadly learned with far-reaching insight.

entries.zh: 觀其對二大夫貴人之談言，稱引古明王聖人道，固非淺聞小數之能。
entries.en: When one observes his discourse with the two noble grandees—how he cited the Way of the wise kings and sages of antiquity—it is clear that his was not the talent of a man of shallow learning and petty skills.
entries.literal: Observing his discourse with the two noble grandees, in which he cited and invoked the Way of the wise kings and sages of antiquity, it is clear this was not the ability of one with shallow learning and petty skills.

entries.zh: 及卜筮立名聲千里者，各往往而在。
entries.en: As for the diviners whose reputations carried a thousand li, they could be found scattered across every region.
entries.literal: As for those diviners who established reputations reaching a thousand li, they could be found here and there in every region.

entries.zh: 傳曰：「富為上，貴次之；
entries.en: The tradition says: 'Wealth comes first, rank second.
entries.literal: The tradition says: 'Wealth is best, rank comes next.

entries.zh: 既貴各各學一伎能立其身。」
entries.en: Once rank is secured, each person should master a skill to establish himself.'
entries.literal: Once one is of rank, each should learn a skill with which to establish himself.'

entries.zh: 黃直，大夫也；
entries.en: Huang Zhi was a grandee.
entries.literal: Huang Zhi was a grandee.

entries.zh: 陳君夫，婦人也：以相馬立名天下。
entries.en: Chen Junfu was a woman; the two of them established their names throughout the realm by judging horses.
entries.literal: Chen Junfu was a woman: together they established their names throughout the realm by judging horses.

entries.zh: 齊張仲、曲成侯以善擊刺學用劍，立名天下。
entries.en: Zhang Zhong of Qi and the Marquis of Qucheng made their names throughout the realm through their mastery of swordplay—the arts of striking and thrusting.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhong of Qi and the Marquis of Qucheng established their names throughout the realm through their skill at striking, thrusting, and swordsmanship.

entries.zh: 留長孺以相彘立名。
entries.en: Liu Changru made his name as a judge of pigs.
entries.literal: Liu Changru established his name by judging pigs.

entries.zh: 滎陽褚氏以相牛立名。
entries.en: The Chu family of Xingyang made their name as judges of cattle.
entries.literal: The Chu family of Xingyang established their name by judging cattle.

entries.zh: 能以伎能立名者甚多，皆有高世絕人之風，何可勝言。
entries.en: Those who established their names through mastery of a skill are far too many to count. All possessed the spirit of men who stood above their generation and apart from ordinary folk—how could one possibly list them all?
entries.literal: Those who were able to establish their names through skills are very many; all had the bearing of men who surpass their age and stand apart from other men—how could one recount them all.

entries.zh: 故曰：「非其地，樹之不生；
entries.en: As the saying goes: 'In the wrong soil, a tree will not grow.
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said: 'In the wrong soil, a tree will not grow.

entries.zh: 非其意，教之不成。」
entries.en: Without the right inclination, no amount of teaching will bear fruit.'
entries.literal: Without the right inclination, instruction cannot succeed.'

entries.zh: 夫家之教子孫，當視其所以好，好含茍生活之道，因而成之。
entries.en: When a family raises its children and grandchildren, one should observe what naturally draws them. If what draws them contains a way to make a living, then one should nurture it and bring it to fruition.
entries.literal: When a family teaches its children and grandchildren, one should observe what they are inclined to enjoy. If what they enjoy contains a way to make a living, then nurture it to fruition.

entries.zh: 故曰：「制宅命子，足以觀士；
entries.en: As the saying goes: 'By how a man arranges his household and directs his children, one can judge his character.
entries.literal: Therefore, it is said: 'By how a man arranges his household and directs his children, one can assess the man.

entries.zh: 子有處所，可謂賢人。」
entries.en: If one's children each find their proper place, then one may truly be called a worthy man.'
entries.literal: If one's children have their proper places, one may be called a worthy man.'

entries.zh: 臣為郎時，與太卜待詔為郎者同署，言曰：「孝武帝時，聚會占家問之，某日可取婦乎？
entries.en: When I served as a Palace Gentleman, I shared an office with a man who had served as a Gentleman-in-Waiting under the Grand Diviner. He told me, "In the time of Emperor Wu, the various schools of diviners were assembled and asked: Is such-and-such a day auspicious for taking a wife?
entries.literal: When I served as a Palace Gentleman, I shared an office with a man who had been a Gentleman-in-Waiting under the Grand Diviner. He told me: "In the time of Emperor Wu, the various schools of diviners were gathered and asked: Is such-and-such a day suitable for taking a wife?

entries.zh: 五行家曰可，堪輿家曰不可，建除家曰不吉，叢辰家曰大凶，歷家曰小凶，天人家曰小吉，太一家曰大吉。
entries.en: The Five Phases school said it was acceptable. The Geomancy school said it was not. The Construction and Removal school said it was inauspicious. The Cluster of Stars school said it was deeply inauspicious. The Calendar school said it was slightly inauspicious. The Heaven and Man school said it was slightly auspicious. The Grand Unity school said it was highly auspicious.
entries.literal: The Five Phases school said it was acceptable; the Geomancy school said it was not; the Construction and Removal school said it was inauspicious; the Constellation Cluster school said it was greatly inauspicious; the Calendar school said it was slightly inauspicious; the Heaven and Man school said it was slightly auspicious; and the Grand Unity school said it was greatly auspicious.

entries.zh: 辯訟不決，以狀聞。
entries.en: The dispute could not be settled, and the matter was reported to the throne.
entries.literal: The debate could not be resolved, and the matter was reported to the throne.

entries.zh: 制曰：『避諸死忌，以五行為主。』」
entries.en: The imperial decree stated, 'Avoid the taboos associated with death, and take the Five Phases school as the standard.'"
entries.literal: The imperial decree said: 'Avoid the taboos associated with death, and follow the Five Phases school as the standard.'"

entries.zh: 人取於五行者也。
entries.en: And so people follow the Five Phases school.
entries.literal: People follow the Five Phases school.

entries.zh: 自古受命而王，王者之興何嘗不以卜筮決於天命哉！
entries.en: Since ancient times, those who received the mandate have ruled as kings—and when has the rise of any king not been decided through divination and the will of Heaven?
entries.literal: Since antiquity those who received the mandate became kings; when has the rise of kings ever not been determined by divination according to the mandate of Heaven!

entries.zh: 其於周尤甚，及秦可見。
entries.en: This was especially true of the Zhou dynasty, and can be seen clearly in the case of the Qin as well.
entries.literal: This was especially so with Zhou, and also visible with Qin.

entries.zh: 代王之入，任於卜者。
entries.en: When the King of Dai ascended to the throne, the matter was entrusted to the diviners.
entries.literal: The King of Dai's accession was entrusted to the diviners.

entries.zh: 太卜之起，由漢興而有。
entries.en: The office of the Grand Diviner was established with the rise of the Han dynasty.
entries.literal: The establishment of the Grand Diviner arose with the founding of the Han.

entries.zh: 《周書》曰：「農不出則乏其食，工不出則乏其事，商不出則三寶絕，虞不出則財匱少。」
entries.en: The Book of Zhou says: 'When farmers do not produce, food grows scarce. When artisans do not produce, goods grow scarce. When merchants do not trade, the three treasures are cut off. When foresters do not extract, resources are depleted.'
entries.literal: The Book of Zhou says: 'When farmers do not produce, food is scarce; when artisans do not produce, goods are scarce; when merchants do not trade, the three treasures are cut off; when foresters do not extract, resources are depleted.'

entries.zh: 財匱少而山澤不辟矣。
entries.en: When resources are depleted, the mountains and marshlands are left unopened.
entries.literal: When resources are depleted and scarce, the mountains and marshes are not opened up.

entries.zh: 此四者，民所衣食之原也。
entries.en: These four occupations are the wellspring from which the people draw their clothing and food.
entries.literal: These four occupations are the source from which the people clothe and feed themselves.

entries.zh: 原大則饒，原小則鮮。
entries.en: When the source is ample, there is abundance; when it is narrow, there is scarcity.
entries.literal: When the source is large there is abundance; when the source is small there is scarcity.

entries.zh: 上則富國，下則富家。
entries.en: At the top, it enriches the state; at the bottom, it enriches the household.
entries.literal: Above, it enriches the state; below, it enriches the household.

entries.zh: 貧富之道，莫之奪予，而巧者有餘，拙者不足。
entries.en: The path to wealth and poverty is not imposed by anyone from above. The skillful end up with a surplus; the clumsy are left wanting.
entries.literal: The way of poverty and wealth — no one seizes or bestows it; yet the skillful have surplus, and the clumsy fall short.

entries.zh: 故太公望封於營丘，地澙鹵，人民寡，於是太公勸其女功，極技巧，通魚鹽，則人物歸之，繦至而輻湊。
entries.en: When the Grand Duke Wang was enfeoffed at Yingqiu, the land was salty and barren and the people few. He encouraged women's handicrafts, perfected artisanal skills, and opened up trade in fish and salt. People and goods streamed toward him, arriving as if carried in swaddling clothes, converging like spokes toward the hub of a wheel.
entries.literal: Therefore, when the Grand Duke Wang was enfeoffed at Yingqiu, the land was salty and alkaline and the people were few. Thereupon the Grand Duke encouraged women's handicrafts, perfected technical skills, and opened trade in fish and salt; then people and goods flowed to him, arriving in swaddling clothes and converging like the spokes of a wheel.

entries.zh: 故齊冠帶衣履天下，海岱之閒斂袂而往朝焉。
entries.en: And so Qi came to supply caps, sashes, clothing, and shoes to the entire realm. From the shores of the sea to the slopes of Mount Tai, the people gathered their sleeves and hastened to pay homage at Qi's court.
entries.literal: Thus, Qi supplied caps, sashes, clothing, and shoes to all under Heaven, and between the sea and Mount Tai people gathered their sleeves and went to pay homage at its court.

entries.zh: 其後齊中衰，管子修之，設輕重九府，則桓公以霸，九合諸侯，一匡天下；
entries.en: Later, when Qi fell into decline, Guan Zhong revived it by establishing the system of price regulation and the Nine Treasuries. With this, Duke Huan achieved hegemony, convened the feudal lords nine times, and brought order to the entire realm;
entries.literal: Later, when Qi fell into decline, Guan Zhong restored it by establishing the system of light-and-heavy regulations and the Nine Treasuries; thereupon Duke Huan achieved hegemony, convened the feudal lords nine times, and brought order to all under Heaven;

entries.zh: 而管氏亦有三歸，位在陪臣，富於列國之君。
entries.en: And Guan Zhong himself, though he held only the rank of a vassal's vassal, possessed the 'three returns' and amassed wealth exceeding that of the rulers of the feudal states.
entries.literal: and Guan Zhong himself possessed the 'three returns,' held the rank of a mere vassal's vassal, yet was wealthier than the rulers of the feudal states.

entries.zh: 是以齊富彊至於威、宣也。
entries.en: And so the wealth and power of Qi endured all the way down to the reigns of Kings Wei and Xuan.
entries.literal: Thus, the wealth and power of Qi continued down to the reigns of Kings Wei and Xuan.

entries.zh: 白圭，周人也。
entries.en: Bai Gui was a man from the state of Zhou.
entries.literal: Bai Gui was a man of Zhou.

entries.zh: 當魏文侯時，李克務盡地力，而白圭樂觀時變，故人棄我取，人取我與。
entries.en: In the time of Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Ke devoted himself to maximizing the yield of the land, while Bai Gui took delight in reading the shifts of the seasons. His principle was: what others discard, I collect; what others seek, I release.
entries.literal: In the time of Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Ke devoted himself to exhausting the productive capacity of the land, while Bai Gui delighted in observing the changes of the seasons; therefore, what others discard, I take; what others take, I give.

entries.zh: 夫歲孰取穀，予之絲漆；
entries.en: In a good harvest year, buy grain and offer silk and lacquer in exchange;
entries.literal: When the harvest year is good, buy grain and give silk and lacquer in exchange;

entries.zh: 繭出取帛絮，予之食。
entries.en: When the cocoons come in, buy silk floss and cloth, and offer food in exchange.
entries.literal: when cocoons come out, buy silk floss and cloth, and give food in exchange.

entries.zh: 太陰在卯，穰；
entries.en: When Taiyin is in mao, crops will be abundant;
entries.literal: When Jupiter is in the mao position, there is abundance;

entries.zh: 明歲衰惡。
entries.en: The following year will bring decline and hardship.
entries.literal: the following year there will be decline and hardship.

entries.zh: 至午，旱；
entries.en: When Jupiter reaches the wu position, there is drought;
entries.literal: When it reaches the wu position, drought;

entries.zh: 明歲美。
entries.en: The following year will be a good one.
entries.literal: the following year will be good.

entries.zh: 至酉，穰；
entries.en: When it reaches the you position, there is abundance;
entries.literal: When it reaches the you position, abundance;

entries.zh: 明歲衰惡。
entries.en: The following year will bring decline and hardship.
entries.literal: the following year there will be decline and hardship.

entries.zh: 至子，大旱；
entries.en: When it reaches the zi position, there is severe drought;
entries.literal: When it reaches the zi position, severe drought;

entries.zh: 明歲美，有水。
entries.en: The following year will be a good one, though with flooding.
entries.literal: the following year will be good, with flooding.

entries.zh: 至卯，積著率歲倍。
entries.en: By the time it returns to the mao position, accumulated stores have generally doubled each year.
entries.literal: When it returns to the mao position, accumulated stores generally double each year.

entries.zh: 欲長錢，取下穀；
entries.en: To increase your cash, buy low-grade grain;
entries.literal: If you wish to increase your money, buy low-grade grain;

entries.zh: 長石斗，取上種。
entries.en: To increase your stores of grain by the bushel, buy top-grade seed.
entries.literal: if you wish to increase your bushels and pecks, buy top-grade seed.

entries.zh: 能薄飲食，忍嗜欲，節衣服，與用事僮仆同苦樂，趨時若猛獸摯鳥之發。
entries.en: He ate sparingly, suppressed his desires, and economized on clothing. He shared both hardship and ease with his servants, and when opportunity arose, he seized it with the ferocity of a predatory beast or a raptor striking its prey.
entries.literal: He could eat sparingly, suppress his desires, economize on clothing, share both hardships and pleasures with his working servants, and seize the moment as fiercely as a predatory beast or a striking bird of prey.

entries.zh: 故曰：「吾治生產，猶伊尹、呂尚之謀，孫吳用兵，商鞅行法是也。
entries.en: He declared: 'My approach to managing commerce and production is comparable to the stratagems of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, the military art of Sunzi and Wu Qi, and Shang Yang's implementation of the law.
entries.literal: Therefore, he said: 'My management of livelihood and production is like the stratagems of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, the deployment of troops by Sun and Wu, and the implementation of law by Shang Yang.

entries.zh: 是故其智不足與權變，勇不足以決斷，仁不能以取予，彊不能有所守，雖欲學吾術，終不告之矣。」
entries.en: If a man's intelligence is insufficient for weighing circumstances and adapting, and if his courage is insufficient for decisive action, he may wish to learn my methods, but I will never teach him. If his benevolence is insufficient for knowing when to give and when to take, and if his firmness is insufficient for holding his ground, I will never teach him.'
entries.literal: Therefore, if one's intelligence is insufficient for weighing circumstances and adapting, one's courage insufficient for making decisions, one's benevolence insufficient for knowing when to give and take, and one's firmness insufficient for holding one's ground — though one may wish to learn my methods, I will never divulge them.'

entries.zh: 蓋天下言治生祖白圭。
entries.en: And so throughout the realm, all who speak of managing commerce regard Bai Gui as their founder.
entries.literal: Thus, all under heaven who speak of managing livelihood regard Bai Gui as their founder.

entries.zh: 白圭其有所試矣，能試有所長，非茍而已也。
entries.en: Bai Gui had truly put his principles to the test. His proven methods had real substance — they were no idle boast.
entries.literal: Bai Gui had indeed put his principles to the test; his tested methods had genuine strengths — it was not mere idle talk.

entries.zh: 老子曰：「至治之極，鄰國相望，雞狗之聲相聞，民各甘其食，美其服，安其俗，樂其業，至老死，不相往來。」
entries.en: Laozi said: 'In the most perfectly governed age, neighboring states are within sight of one another, the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs can be heard across the border, the people savor their own food, take pride in their own clothing, rest content in their own customs, and delight in their own occupations — and they grow old and die without ever setting foot in one another's lands.'
entries.literal: Laozi said: 'At the height of perfect governance, neighboring states can see one another, the sounds of roosters and dogs can be heard between them, the people each relish their own food, admire their own clothes, feel at ease in their own customs, and take pleasure in their own work; they grow old and die without ever visiting one another.'

entries.zh: 必用此為務，輓近世涂民耳目，則幾無行矣。
entries.en: If one insists on making this the governing principle, attempting to drag the modern world backward by stopping up the eyes and ears of the people, the task would prove virtually impossible.
entries.literal: If one insists on making this the guiding principle and tries to pull the modern world back by stopping up the people's eyes and ears, then it is virtually impossible to put into practice.

entries.zh: 九月己亥朔，命潭州防禦使潘美為賀州道兵馬行營都部署，朗州團練使尹崇珂副之。
entries.en: At the jihai new moon in the ninth month Pan Mei, defense commissioner of Tan, was made overall commander of the Hezhou expedition, with Yin Chongke, regimental commissioner of Lang, as his deputy.
entries.literal: On the jihai new moon of the ninth month, Tanzhou defense commissioner Pan Mei was made overall commander of the Hezhou route army and horse, with Langzhou regimental commissioner Yin Chongke as his deputy.

entries.zh: 遣使發十州兵會賀州，以伐南漢。
entries.en: He sent envoys to raise troops from ten prefectures at Hezhou for the campaign against Southern Han.
entries.literal: Envoys were dispatched to mobilize troops from ten prefectures to assemble at Hezhou to attack Southern Han.

entries.zh: 甲辰，詔︰西京、鳳翔、雄、耀等州，周文、成、康三王，秦始皇，漢高、文、景、武、元、成、哀七帝，後魏孝文，西魏文帝，後周太祖，唐高祖、太宗、中宗、肅宗、代宗、德、順、文、武、宣、懿、僖、昭諸帝凡二十七陵嘗被盜發者，有司備法服、常服各一襲，具棺槨重葬，所在長吏致祭。
entries.en: He decreed reburial for twenty-seven violated imperial tombs in the west—ranging from the Zhou kings Wen, Cheng, and Kang and Qin Shihuang through seven Han emperors, Northern Wei Xiaowen, Western Wei Wendi, Later Zhou Taizu, and the thirteen Tang emperors Gaozu, Taizong, Zhongzong, Suzong, Daizong, Dezong, Shunzong, Wenzong, Wuzong, Xuanzong, Yizong, Xizong, and Zhaozong. Each site was to receive fresh ceremonial and everyday robes, new coffins, and sacrifices from the local magistrate.
entries.literal: An edict: for the twenty-seven imperial tombs at Xijing, Fengxiang, Xiong, Yao, and other prefectures—of the three Zhou kings Wen, Cheng, and Kang; Qin Shihuang; the seven Han emperors Gao, Wen, Jing, Wu, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen; Western Wei Emperor Wendi; Later Zhou Taizu; and the Tang emperors Gaozu, Taizong, Zhongzong, Suzong, Daizong, Dezong, Shunzong, Wenzong, Wuzong, Xuanzong, Yizong, Xizong, and Zhaozong—that had been opened by grave robbers, the relevant offices were to prepare one set each of ceremonial and ordinary robes, provide coffins for reburial, and have the local chief officials offer sacrifices.

entries.zh: 己酉，幸開寶寺觀新鐘。
entries.en: On jiyou he went to Kai Bao Temple to see the new bell.
entries.literal: On jiyou, he visited Kai Bao Temple to view the new bell.

entries.zh: 丙辰，女直國遣使齎定安國王烈萬華表，獻方物。
entries.en: On bingchen Jurchen envoys arrived with the memorial of King Liewanhua of Ding'an and tribute goods.
entries.literal: On bingchen, the Jurchen state sent envoys bearing the memorial table of King Liewanhua of Ding'an, presenting local products.

entries.zh: 丁卯，潘美等敗南漢軍萬眾於富州，下之。
entries.en: On dingmao Pan Mei and his colleagues routed more than ten thousand Southern Han soldiers at Fuzhou and captured the city.
entries.literal: On dingmao, Pan Mei and others defeated more than ten thousand Southern Han troops at Fuzhou and took the city.

entries.zh: 太祖二
entries.en: Annals of Taizu, continued.
entries.literal: Taizu II.

entries.zh: 冬十月甲申，幸迎春苑，登汴隄觀戰艦東下。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on jiashen, he went to Welcome Spring Garden, climbed the Bian dike, and watched the fleet head downstream.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, he visited Welcome Spring Garden, ascended the Bian embankment, and watched the warships sail east.

entries.zh: 丙戌，又幸迎春苑，登汴隄觀諸軍習戰，遂幸東水門，發戰櫂東下。
entries.en: On bingxu he returned to Welcome Spring Garden, reviewed troop exercises from the dike, then went to East Water Gate and launched the battle fleet eastward.
entries.literal: On bingxu, he again visited Welcome Spring Garden, ascended the Bian embankment to watch the various armies drill, then visited East Water Gate and sent the war fleet east.

entries.zh: 江南進絹數萬，御衣、金帶、器用數百事。
entries.en: Southern Tang sent tens of thousands in silk, court robes, gold belts, and several hundred pieces of ritual ware.
entries.literal: Jiangnan presented tens of thousands in silk, imperial robes, gold belts, and vessels numbering in the hundreds.

entries.zh: 壬辰，曹彬等將舟師、步騎發江陵，水陸並進。
entries.en: On renchen Cao Bin's river and land columns left Jiangling in combined advance.
entries.literal: On renchen, Cao Bin and the others led the fleet and infantry and cavalry to depart from Jiangling, advancing by land and water together.

entries.zh: 丁酉，命吳越王錢俶為昇州東南行營招撫制置使。
entries.en: On dingyou King Qian Chu of Wuyue was named pacification commissioner on the southeastern front against Shengzhou.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Wuyue king Qian Chu was made pacification and disposition commissioner of the Southeast Route Army for Shengzhou.

entries.zh: 己亥，曹彬收下峽口，獲指揮使王仁震、王宴、錢興。
entries.en: On jihai Cao Bin seized Xiakou and took commanders Wang Renzhen, Wang Yan, and Qian Xing prisoner.
entries.literal: On jihai, Cao Bin took Xiakou and captured commanders Wang Renzhen, Wang Yan, and Qian Xing.

entries.zh: 太祖三
entries.en: Annals of Taizu, continued.
entries.literal: Taizu III.

entries.zh: 冬十月甲辰，雷有終大敗賊黨，復益州，殺三千餘人。
entries.en: On jiachen in the tenth month of winter Lei Youzhong routed the rebels, retook Yizhou, and slaughtered three thousand men.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, Lei Youzhong greatly defeated the bandit party, recovered Yizhou, and killed more than three thousand men.

entries.zh: 壬子，綿、漢都巡檢、澄州刺史張思鈞削籍流封州。
entries.en: On renzi Zhang Sijun, inspector of Mian-Han and prefect of Cheng, was disranked and banished to Fengzhou.
entries.literal: On renzi, Mian and Han circuit inspector and Cheng prefecture prefect Zhang Sijun was struck from the rolls and exiled to Feng prefecture.

entries.zh: 乙卯，幸元份宮視疾。
entries.en: On yimao he called on the ailing Prince Yuan Fen.
entries.literal: On yimao, he visited Prince Yuan Fen's palace to inquire after his illness.

entries.zh: 令諸州兼群牧。
entries.en: He required every prefecture to take charge of local herd administration.
entries.literal: Ordered each prefecture concurrently to oversee the herd offices.

entries.zh: 己未，濱州防禦使王榮削籍流均州。
entries.en: On jiwei Wang Rong, defense commissioner of Binzhou, was disranked and sent to Junzhou.
entries.literal: On jiwei, Binzhou defense commissioner Wang Rong was struck from the rolls and exiled to Jun prefecture.

entries.zh: 己丑，雷有終追斬王均于富順監，禽其黨六千餘人。
entries.en: On jichou Lei Youzhong ran Wang Jun down at Fushun Prison, took his head, and rounded up six thousand rebels.
entries.literal: On jichou, Lei Youzhong pursued and beheaded Wang Jun at Fushun Prison and captured more than six thousand of his followers.

entries.zh: 詔原川峽路繫囚雜犯死罪以下。
entries.en: He pardoned every Sichuan prisoner below capital grade implicated in the rebellion.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned mixed offenders in Sichuan and the mountain passes below capital crime.

entries.zh: 雷有終等以功進秩有差。
entries.en: Lei Youzhong and his officers received graded promotions for the victory.
entries.literal: Lei Youzhong and others were promoted in rank according to merit.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以翰林學士王欽若、知制誥梁顥分為川、峽安撫使。
entries.en: On bingyin he sent Wang Qinruo and Liang Hao to pacify Sichuan and the mountain passes as paired commissioners.
entries.literal: On bingyin, Hanlin Academician Wang Qinruo and drafting drafter Liang Hao were made Sichuan and mountain-pass pacification commissioners respectively.

entries.zh: 延州言破大盧、小盧等十族，獲人畜二十萬。
entries.en: Yanzhou reported crushing the great and lesser Lu confederations and eight allied tribes, taking two hundred thousand captives and animals.
entries.literal: Yanzhou reported defeating the great Lu and lesser Lu tribes and ten others, capturing two hundred thousand head of men and livestock.

entries.zh: 真宗應符稽古神功讓德文明武定章聖元孝皇帝，諱恆，太宗第三子也。
entries.en: Emperor Zhenzong—full posthumous style Responding to the Signs through Primordially Filial—whose personal name was Heng, was Taizong's third son.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, entitled Responding to the Signs, Examining Antiquity, Divine Merit, Yielding Virtue, Civil and Bright, Martial and Settled, Manifest and Sagely, Primordially Filial, taboo name Heng, was the third son of Emperor Taizong.

entries.zh: 母曰元德皇后李氏。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Li, later honored as Empress Yuande.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Yuande, née Li.

entries.zh: 初，乾德五年，五星從鎮星聚奎。
entries.en: Legend dated his destiny to Qiande year five, when the five planets trailed Jupiter into a cluster at the Kui asterism.
entries.literal: At the beginning, in the fifth year of Qiande, the five planets followed Saturn to gather at Kui.

entries.zh: 明年正月，后夢以裾承日，有娠，十二月二日生于開封府第，赤光照室，左足指有文成「天」字。
entries.en: The next spring his mother dreamed the sun rested in her lap; she conceived, and on the second of the twelfth month delivered him at the Kaifeng mansion in a room flooded with red light—on his left great toe the skin bore the character "Heaven."
entries.literal: In the first month of the following year the empress dreamed that her skirt caught the sun; she became pregnant, and on the second day of the twelfth month gave birth at the Kaifeng commandery residence; red light filled the chamber, and on the left great toe a pattern formed the character "Heaven."

entries.zh: 八月甲辰，錄周世宗後。
entries.en: Eighth month, jiachen: survivors of Later Zhou Shizong were enrolled.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day jiachen: the descendants of Later Zhou Shizong were recorded.

entries.zh: 甲寅，太白入太微垣。
entries.en: On jiayin, Venus entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
entries.literal: Day jiayin: Venus entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

entries.zh: 乙卯，遣兵部員外郎呂誨等四人充賀契丹太后生辰、正旦使，刑部郎中章岷等四人充賀契丹主生辰、正旦使。
entries.en: On yimao, Lu Hui's party would greet the Khitan dowager; Zhang Min's party, the Khitan emperor.
entries.literal: Day yimao: Ministry of War vice director Lu Hui and three others were sent as envoys to congratulate the Khitan empress dowager's birthday and New Year's Day; Ministry of Punishments director Zhang Min and three others as envoys to congratulate the Khitan emperor's birthday and New Year's Day.

entries.zh: 丙辰，內侍都知任守忠坐不法，貶保信軍節度副使、蘄州安置。
entries.en: On bingchen, eunuch Ren Shouzhong fell for misconduct to a Qizhou exile post.
entries.literal: Day bingchen: Chief eunuch Ren Shouzhong, guilty of unlawful conduct, was demoted to Baoxin military deputy commissioner and assigned to Qizhou.

entries.zh: 丁巳，以上供米三萬石振宿、亳二州水災戶。
entries.en: On dingsi, thirty thousand piculs of tribute grain fed Suzhou and Bozhou flood victims.
entries.literal: Day dingsi: thirty thousand piculs of tribute grain were used to relieve flood victims in Suzhou and Bozhou.

entries.zh: 贊曰：昔人有言，天之所命，人不能違。
entries.en: Praise: The ancients said what Heaven decrees, man cannot defy.
entries.literal: Praise says: The ancients had a saying—what Heaven decrees, man cannot defy.

entries.zh: 信哉！
entries.en: Truly so!
entries.literal: True indeed!

entries.zh: 英宗以明哲之資，膺繼統之命，執心固讓，若將終身，而卒踐帝位，豈非天命乎？
entries.en: Yingzong's clear mind took the succession yet he refused as if for life—and still became emperor. Was that not Heaven's mandate?
entries.literal: Yingzong with his clear wisdom received the mandate to succeed, yet steadfastly declined as if for life, yet in the end ascended the throne—is this not Heaven's mandate?

entries.zh: 及其臨政，臣下有奏，必問朝廷故事與古治所宜，每有裁決，皆出群臣意表。
entries.en: In power he asked every memorial what precedent and antiquity required; his judgments consistently surprised the court.
entries.literal: When he held government, whenever ministers memorialized he asked what court precedent and ancient governance required; each decision went beyond what ministers expected.

entries.zh: 雖以疾疹不克大有所爲，然使百世之下，欽仰高風，詠歎至德，何其盛也！
entries.en: Illness limited his deeds, yet posterity would admire and hymn his height—how grand!
entries.literal: Though illness kept him from great deeds, he left a loftiness that a hundred generations would admire and hymn—how majestic!

entries.zh: 彼隋晉王廣、唐魏王泰窺覦神器，矯揉奪嫡，遂啟禍原，誠何心哉！
entries.en: Yet Sui's Yang Guang and Tang's Li Tai coveted the throne, twisted succession, and loosed disaster—what were they thinking?
entries.literal: Yet Sui's Prince of Jin Guang and Tang's Prince Wei Tai coveted the vessel, twisted succession, and opened the floodgate of disaster—what were they thinking?

entries.zh: 誠何心哉！
entries.en: What hearts had they!
entries.literal: What were they thinking!

entries.zh: 英宗體乾應曆隆功盛德憲文肅武睿聖宣孝皇帝，諱曙，濮安懿王允讓第十三子，母曰仙游縣君任氏。
entries.en: Emperor Yingzong—full style from Aligning with Heaven through Proclaiming Filiality—personal name Shu, was the thirteenth son of Prince of Pu’an Yunrang; his mother was Lady Ren of Xianyou.
entries.literal: Emperor Yingzong, entitled Aligning with Heaven, Responding to the Calendar, Lofty Merit, Abundant Virtue, Constituting Culture, Solemn Martiality, Sagacious Governance, Proclaiming Filiality, taboo name Shu, was the thirteenth son of Prince of Pu’an the Respectful Wang Yunrang; his mother was Lady Ren, county mistress of Xianyou.

entries.zh: 明道元年正月三日生於宣平坊第。
entries.en: Bright Path 1, third of the first month: he was born at the Xuanping mansion.
entries.literal: In the first year of Bright Path, first month, third day, he was born at the Xuanping ward residence.

entries.zh: 初，王夢兩龍與日並墮，以衣承之。
entries.en: His father dreamed two dragons and the sun falling into his robes.
entries.literal: At first the prince dreamed two dragons and the sun fell together; he caught them in his robe.

entries.zh: 及帝生，赤光滿室，或見黃龍遊光中。
entries.en: At his birth red light filled the room; some saw a yellow dragon in the glare.
entries.literal: When the emperor was born, red light filled the chamber; some saw a yellow dragon moving in the glow.

entries.zh: 四歲，仁宗養於內。
entries.en: At four he was raised in the palace by Renzong.
entries.literal: At four sui he was raised in the inner palace by Renzong.

entries.zh: 寶元二年，豫王生，乃歸濮邸。
entries.en: Precious Origin 2, when Prince Yu was born, he returned to the Pu mansion.
entries.literal: In the second year of Precious Origin, when Prince Yu was born, he returned to the Pu residence.

entries.zh: 帝天性篤孝，好讀書，不爲燕嬉褻慢，服御儉素如儒者。
entries.en: He was deeply filial, bookish, never frivolous or rude, and dressed as plainly as a scholar.
entries.literal: By nature he was deeply filial, loved reading, did not indulge in frivolous amusement or disrespect, and dressed plainly like a scholar.

entries.zh: 每以朝服見教授，曰：「師也，敢弗爲禮？」
entries.en: Meeting his tutor in court dress he said, “You are my teacher—I must show full ritual.”
entries.literal: Whenever he met his tutor in court dress he said: “You are my teacher—how dare I not show ritual?”

entries.zh: 時吳王宮教授吳充進《宗室六箴》，仁宗付宗正，帝書之屏風以自戒。
entries.en: Wu Chong’s Six Admonitions for the Clan were set on his screen as a daily warning.
entries.literal: At the time Wu Chong, tutor of the Wu prince’s palace, presented the Six Admonitions for the Imperial Clan; Renzong gave them to the clan court and the emperor wrote them on a screen for self-warning.

entries.zh: 景祐三年，賜名宗實，授左監門衛率府副率，累遷右羽林軍大將軍、宜州刺史。
entries.en: In Jingyou 3 he received the name Zongshi and was appointed deputy commandant in the Left Palace Gate Guard; he later rose to Great General of the Right Feathered Forest Army and prefectural military commissioner of Yi Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jingyou he was given the name Zongshi and appointed deputy commandant of the Left Palace Gate Guard command, later rising through the ranks to Great General of the Right Feathered Forest Army and prefectural military commissioner of Yi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 皇祐二年，爲右衛大將軍、岳州團練使。
entries.en: Imperial Blessing 2: right guard general and Yue commander.
entries.literal: In the second year of Imperial Blessing he was great general of the right guard and regimental commander of Yue prefecture.

entries.zh: 嘉祐中，宰相韓琦等請建儲，仁宗曰：「宗子已有賢知可付者，卿等其勿憂。」
entries.en: Jiayou: Han Qi urged naming an heir; Renzong said, "Among the imperial sons there is already one of worthy knowledge who can be entrusted—you need not worry."
entries.literal: In the Jiayou era chief minister Han Qi and others asked to establish an heir; Renzong said: “Among the imperial sons there is already one of worthy knowledge who can be entrusted—you need not worry.”

entries.zh: 時帝方服濮王喪。
entries.en: He was then mourning Prince of Pu’an.
entries.literal: At the time the emperor was in mourning for the Prince of Pu’an.

entries.zh: 六年十月辛卯，起爲秦州防禦使、知宗正寺，帝以終喪辭。
entries.en: Year six, tenth month, xinmao: he was recalled as defense commissioner of Qin Prefecture and administrator of the Court of the Imperial Clan, but declined because his mourning was not complete.
entries.literal: Sixth year, tenth month, day xinmao: he was raised as defense commissioner of Qin and director of the imperial clan court; the emperor declined on grounds of unfinished mourning.

entries.zh: 奏四上，乃聽。
entries.en: Four memorials later, he was allowed to refuse.
entries.literal: He memorialized four times; only then was he heard.

entries.zh: 喪終，復授前命，又辭。
entries.en: After mourning the same posts returned; he refused again.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, the former appointment was renewed; he again declined.

entries.zh: 七年八月，許罷宗正，復爲岳州團練使。
entries.en: Year seven, eighth month: he left the clan court and returned to Yue command.
entries.literal: Seventh year, eighth month: he was permitted to leave the clan court and again became regimental commander of Yue.

entries.zh: 戊寅，立爲皇子。
entries.en: On wuyin, he was made imperial son.
entries.literal: Day wuyin: he was established as imperial son.

entries.zh: 癸未，改今名。
entries.en: On guiwei, he received his present name Shu.
entries.literal: Day guiwei: his present name was given.

entries.zh: 帝聞詔稱疾，益堅辭。
entries.en: On hearing the edict he pleaded illness and refused harder.
entries.literal: Hearing the edict, he claimed illness and declined more firmly.

entries.zh: 詔同判大宗正事安國公從古等往喻旨，即臥內起帝以入。
entries.en: Conggu and others were sent to explain; they lifted him from his bed and brought him in.
entries.literal: Edict: Co-director of the great clan court Duke of Anguo Conggu and others were sent to explain the intent; they raised the emperor from his bed and brought him in.

entries.zh: 甲辰，見清居殿。
entries.en: On jiachen, he appeared at Qingju Hall.
entries.literal: Day jiachen: he was received at Qingju Hall.

entries.zh: 自是，日再朝，或入侍禁中。
entries.en: Thereafter he attended twice daily or served in the inner palace.
entries.literal: From then on he attended court twice daily or entered to serve in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 九月，遷齊州防禦使、鉅鹿郡公。
entries.en: Ninth month: he became Qi defense commissioner and Duke of Julu.
entries.literal: Ninth month: he was moved to defense commissioner of Qi and Duke of Julu.

entries.zh: 九月丁丑，詔減諸路逃田稅額。
entries.en: Ninth month, dingchou: abandoned-field tax quotas were cut across the circuits.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day dingchou, edict: tax quotas on abandoned fields in all circuits were reduced.

entries.zh: 壬午，祧僖祖及文懿皇后。
entries.en: On renwu, Xizu and Empress Wenyi were moved to distant-line status.
entries.literal: Day renwu: Emperor Xizu and Empress Wenyi were moved to distant-line status.

entries.zh: 乙酉，祔英宗神主于太廟，樂曰《大英之舞》。
entries.en: On yiyou, Yingzong's tablet entered the Grand Temple to the dance "Great Splendor."
entries.literal: Day yiyou: Yingzong's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple; the dance was called "Great Splendor Dance."

entries.zh: 戊子，減兩京、畿內、鄭、孟州囚罪一等，民役山陵者蠲其賦。
entries.en: On wuzi, capital-region prisoners gained one-grade leniency; tomb laborers were exempted from taxes.
entries.literal: Day wuzi: prisoners in the two capitals, metropolitan region, Zheng, and Meng prefectures had sentences reduced one grade; commoners serving on the imperial tomb were exempted from levies.

entries.zh: 辛卯，徙封顥爲岐王，頵爲高密郡王。
entries.en: On xinmao, Hao became Prince of Qi and Yun Prince of Gaomi.
entries.literal: Day xinmao: Hao was transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi; Yun as Prince of Gaomi.

entries.zh: 富弼爲尚書左僕射。
entries.en: Fu Bi became left vice director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Fu Bi was made left vice director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 遣孫思恭等報謝於遼，且賀生辰、正旦。
entries.en: Sun Sigong was dispatched to Liao to give thanks and greet the new year and imperial birthday.
entries.literal: Sun Sigong and others were sent to Liao to return thanks and also congratulate on birthday and New Year's Day.

entries.zh: 壬辰，錄周世宗從曾孫貽廓爲三班奉職。
entries.en: On renchen, Shizong's collateral descendant Yikuo was made third-rank attendant.
entries.literal: Day renchen: Later Zhou Shizong's collateral great-great-grandson Yikuo was enrolled as third-rank attendant.

entries.zh: 甲午，遼遣耶律好謀等來賀即位。
entries.en: On jiawu, Liao envoys including Yelü Haomou came to congratulate the accession.
entries.literal: Day jiawu: Liao sent Yelü Haomou and others to congratulate on the enthronement.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以王安石爲翰林學士。
entries.en: On wuxu, Wang Anshi entered the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: Day wuxu: Wang Anshi was made Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 辛丑，韓琦罷爲司徒、鎮安武勝軍節度使、判相州。
entries.en: On xinchou, Han Qi left office as minister of education and Xiangzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: Day xinchou: Han Qi was dismissed as minister of education, military commissioner of Zhen'an Wusheng Army, and Xiangzhou administrator.

entries.zh: 吳奎、陳升之罷。
entries.en: Wu Kui and Chen Shengzhi were removed.
entries.literal: Wu Kui and Chen Shengzhi were dismissed.

entries.zh: 樞密副使呂公弼爲樞密使，張方平、趙抃並參知政事，邵亢爲樞密副使。
entries.en: Lü Gongbi became military affairs commissioner; Zhang Fangping and Zhao Bian joined the Secretariat; Shao Kang became vice commissioner.
entries.literal: Vice commissioner of military affairs Lü Gongbi was made commissioner; Zhang Fangping and Zhao Bian were both participating administrators; Shao Kang was made vice commissioner.

entries.zh: 壬寅，以曾公亮爲尚書左僕射，文彥博爲司空。
entries.en: On renyin, Zeng Gongliang became left vice director and Wen Yanbo minister of works.
entries.literal: Day renyin: Zeng Gongliang was made left vice director; Wen Yanbo was made minister of works.

entries.zh: 潮州地震。
entries.en: Chaozhou shook.
entries.literal: Chaozhou earthquake.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以權御史中丞司馬光爲翰林學士。
entries.en: On guimao, acting censorate director Sima Guang joined the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: Day guimao: acting censorate director Sima Guang was made Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 九月甲子朔，交州來貢。
entries.en: Ninth month, jiazi new moon: Jiaozhi sent tribute.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day jiazi, new moon: Jiaozhi came to offer tribute.

entries.zh: 乙丑，以古勿峒效順首領儂智會爲右千牛衛大將軍。
entries.en: On yichou, Nong Zhihui of Gumu Cave received a general's rank.
entries.literal: Day yichou: Gumu Cave submitter chief Nong Zhihui was made great general of the right thousand-oxen guard.

entries.zh: 丁卯，立常平給斂法。
entries.en: On dingmao, the ever-normal granary system was proclaimed.
entries.literal: Day dingmao: the ever-normal granary loan-and-storage law was established.

entries.zh: 戊辰，出內庫緡錢百萬糴河北常平粟。
entries.en: On wuchen, a million strings bought Hebei reserve grain.
entries.literal: Day wuchen: one million strings from the inner treasury bought ever-normal grain in Hebei.

entries.zh: 丁丑，遣孫固等賀遼主生辰、正旦。
entries.en: On dingchou, Sun Gu's mission left for Liao.
entries.literal: Day dingchou: Sun Gu and others were sent to congratulate the Liao ruler's birthday and new year.

entries.zh: 辛卯，廢奉慈廟。
entries.en: On xinmao, Fengci temple was closed.
entries.literal: Day xinmao: Fengci temple was abolished.

entries.zh: 壬辰，以秘書省著作佐郎呂惠卿爲太子中允、崇政殿說書。
entries.en: On renchen, Lü Huiqing entered the heir's school and lecture hall.
entries.literal: Day renchen: Secretariat registrar Lü Huiqing was made crown prince attendant and lecturer at Chongzheng Hall.

entries.zh: 神宗紹天法古運德建功英文烈武欽仁聖孝皇帝，諱頊，英宗長子，母曰宣仁聖烈皇后高氏。
entries.en: Emperor Shenzong—full style from Continuing Heaven through Sagely Filial—personal name Xu, was Yingzong’s eldest son; his mother was Empress Xuanren, Lady Gao.
entries.literal: Emperor Shenzong, entitled Continuing Heaven, Patterning Antiquity, Transporting Virtue, Establishing Merit, Civil, Martial, Reverent, Benevolent, Sagely, Filial, taboo name Xu, was the eldest son of Yingzong; his mother was Empress Xuanren the Holy and Liege, Lady Gao.

entries.zh: 慶曆八年四月戊寅生於濮王宮，祥光照室，群鼠吐五色氣成雲。
entries.en: Glorious Calendar 8, fourth month, wuyin: born in the Pu palace amid auspicious light; rats were said to have breathed five-colored clouds.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Glorious Calendar, fourth month, day wuyin, he was born in the Prince of Pu’s palace; auspicious light filled the chamber; a swarm of rats spewed five-colored vapor that formed clouds.

entries.zh: 八月，賜名仲鍼。
entries.en: Eighth month: he was named Zhongzhen.
entries.literal: Eighth month: the name Zhongzhen was bestowed.

entries.zh: 授率府副率，三遷至右千牛衛將軍。
entries.en: He rose from guard deputy to right thousand-oxen general in three steps.
entries.literal: He was made deputy chief of the guard office and thrice promoted to general of the right thousand-oxen guard.

entries.zh: 嘉祐八年，侍英宗入居慶甯宮，嘗夢神人捧之登天。
entries.en: Jiayou 8: he entered Qingning Palace with Yingzong and dreamed a spirit bore him to Heaven.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Jiayou he attended Yingzong into residence at Qingning Palace and once dreamed a spirit lifted him to ascend Heaven.

entries.zh: 英宗即位，授安州觀察使，封光國公。
entries.en: At Yingzong’s accession he became An commissioner and Duke of Guangguo.
entries.literal: When Yingzong acceded, he was made observation commissioner of An and Duke of Guangguo.

entries.zh: 是年五月壬戌，受經於東宮。
entries.en: That year, fifth month, renxu: he began classical study in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: That year, fifth month, day renxu: he received the classics in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 帝隆准龍顏，動止皆有常度。
entries.en: With a high nose and dragon-like bearing, his every motion was measured.
entries.literal: He had a high nose and dragon countenance; movement and rest all had constant measure.

entries.zh: 而天性好學，請問至日晏忘食，英宗常遣內侍止之。
entries.en: He studied until he forgot meals; Yingzong often sent eunuchs to make him stop.
entries.literal: Yet he loved learning by nature, questioning tutors until dusk and forgetting meals; Yingzong often sent eunuchs to stop him.

entries.zh: 帝正衣冠拱手，雖大暑，未嘗用扇。
entries.en: He kept cap and robes formal and never used a fan even in summer heat.
entries.literal: He wore correct cap and robes with joined hands; even in great heat he never used a fan.

entries.zh: 侍講王陶入侍，帝率弟顥拜之。
entries.en: When Wang Tao lectured, he had his brother Hao bow with him.
entries.literal: When lecturer Wang Tao entered to attend, the emperor led his brother Hao in bowing to him.

entries.zh: 九月，加忠武軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，封淮陽郡王，改今諱。
entries.en: Ninth month: Zhongwu command, co-chancellor, Prince of Huaiyang, and the name Xu.
entries.literal: Ninth month: he was added military commissioner of Zhongwu, co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Prince of Huaiyang, and his present taboo name was given.

entries.zh: 治平元年六月，進封潁王。
entries.en: Zhiping 1, sixth month: he became Prince of Ying.
entries.literal: Zhiping year one, sixth month: he was advanced to Prince of Ying.

entries.zh: 三年三月，納故相向敏中孫女爲夫人。
entries.en: Year three, third month: he married Xiang Minzhong’s granddaughter.
entries.literal: Third year, third month: he took the former chief minister Xiang Minzhong’s granddaughter as consort.

entries.zh: 十月，英宗不豫，帝引仁宗故事，請兩日一御邇英閣講讀，以安人心。
entries.en: Tenth month: with Yingzong ill, he asked to lecture in Yingying Hall every two days, citing Renzong’s precedent.
entries.literal: Tenth month: Yingzong was unwell; the emperor cited Renzong’s precedent and asked to lecture in Yingying Hall every two days to steady hearts.

entries.zh: 十二月壬寅，立爲皇太子。
entries.en: Twelfth month, renyin: he was made crown prince.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, day renyin: he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 六月丁亥，詔安南將吏，視軍士有疾者月以數聞。
entries.en: Sixth month, dinghai: An Nam officers were to report sick rolls monthly.
entries.literal: Sixth month, day dinghai, edict: An Nam commanders and clerks were to report monthly the number of ill soldiers.

entries.zh: 己丑，綿州都監王慶、崔昭用、劉珪、左侍禁張乂援戰茂州，死之。
entries.en: On jichou, Wang Qing, Cui Zhaoyong, Liu Gui, and Zhang Yiyuan fell at Maozhou.
entries.literal: Day jichou: Mianzhou controller Wang Qing, Cui Zhaoyong, Liu Gui, and left palace guard Zhang Yiyuan fought at Maozhou and died.

entries.zh: 詔慶等子與借職，女出嫁，夫與奉職；
entries.en: Their sons gained provisional rank; sons-in-law of their daughters gained palace rank.
entries.literal: Edict: sons of Qing and the others received provisional rank; daughters upon marriage, their husbands received palace rank.

entries.zh: 白丁王禹錫等二人，賜錢其家。
entries.en: Wang Yuxi and two other commoners’ families received cash.
entries.literal: Commoners Wang Yuxi and two others were given money for their families.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔濱海富民得養蜑戶，毋致爲外夷所誘。
entries.en: On xinmao, coastal magnates could keep Dan boat people—but not lose them to foreigners.
entries.literal: Day xinmao, edict: wealthy coastal households might keep Dan households in service, but must not let them be enticed by foreign tribes.

entries.zh: 己亥，慮囚，降死罪一等，杖以下釋之。
entries.en: On jihai, death sentences dropped a grade and lesser punishments were cleared.
entries.literal: Day jihai: prisoners were reviewed; death sentences were reduced one grade, and those liable to beating or flogging were released.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以水源等洞蠻主儂賀等七人爲定遠、甯遠將軍。
entries.en: On guimao, Nong He and six other cave chiefs became Dingyuan and Ningyuan generals.
entries.literal: Day guimao: seven cave chiefs including Nong He of the Shuiyuan district were made generals of Dingyuan and Ningyuan.

entries.zh: 三年春正月癸丑，錄唐李氏、周柴氏後。
entries.en: Spring, year three, guichou: the court registered heirs of Tang’s Lis and Zhou’s Chais.
entries.literal: Third year, spring, first month, day guichou: descendants of Tang’s Li clan and Zhou’s Chai clan were enrolled.

entries.zh: 乙卯，詔諸路散青苗錢禁抑配。
entries.en: On yimao, circuits were ordered to release Green Sprouts money and ban coerced quotas.
entries.literal: Day yimao, edict: all circuits were to disburse Green Sprouts funds and forbid forced allotment.

entries.zh: 戊午，判尚書省張方平罷知陳州。
entries.en: On wuwu, Zhang Fangping left the Secretariat for Chen prefect.
entries.literal: Day wuwu: Zhang Fangping, who adjudicated the Secretariat, was dismissed and made Chen prefect.

entries.zh: 九月己丑，建州軍校張員等作亂，執守臣張動，轉運副使毛奎、判官曹仔為所殺，嬰城自守。
entries.en: Ninth month, jichou: Jianzhou soldiers under Zhang Yuan mutinied, seized Zhang Dong, killed Mao Kui and Cao Zai, and held the city.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Jianzhou soldiers under Zhang Yuan and others mutinied, seized defender Zhang Dong, and killed transport vice commissioner Mao Kui and judge Cao Zai; they held the city in defense.

entries.zh: 范瓊捕斬李孝忠於復州。
entries.en: Fan Qiong captured and beheaded Li Xiaozhong at Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Fan Qiong captured and beheaded Li Xiaozhong at Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 壬辰，以金人犯河陽、汜水，詔擇日巡幸淮甸。
entries.en: On renchen, with Jin attacking Heyang and Sishui, an edict chose a day to tour the Huai region.
entries.literal: Day renchen: because the Jin attacked Heyang and Sishui, an edict chose a day to tour the Huai region.

entries.zh: 鑄建炎通寶錢。
entries.en: Jianyan universal treasure cash was cast.
entries.literal: Jianyan universal treasure cash was cast.

entries.zh: 命淮、浙沿海諸州增修城壁，招訓民兵，以備海道。
entries.en: Huai and Zhe coastal prefectures were ordered to heighten walls, train militia, and guard the sea routes.
entries.literal: Coastal prefectures of Huai and Zhe were ordered to heighten walls, recruit and train militia, and prepare the sea routes.

entries.zh: 甲午，命揚州守臣呂頤浩繕修城池。
entries.en: On jiawu, Yangzhou defender Lü Yihao was ordered to repair the walls.
entries.literal: Day jiawu: Yangzhou defender Lü Yihao was ordered to repair walls.

entries.zh: 宗澤往河北視師，七日還。
entries.en: Zong Ze went to Hebei to inspect the armies and returned in seven days.
entries.literal: Zong Ze went to Hebei to inspect the armies and returned in seven days.

entries.zh: 是夜，辛道宗兵潰於嘉興縣。
entries.en: That night Xin Daozong’s troops collapsed at Jiaxing.
entries.literal: That night Xin Daozong’s troops collapsed at Jiaxing county.

entries.zh: 丁酉，詔荊襄、關陝、江淮皆備巡幸。
entries.en: On dingyou, Jing–Xiang, Guan–Shaan, and Jiang–Huai were ordered to prepare for the imperial progress.
entries.literal: Day dingyou: an edict ordered Jing–Xiang, Guan–Shaan, and Jiang–Huai all to prepare for the imperial progress.

entries.zh: 戊戌，罷買馬。
entries.en: On wuxu, horse purchases were abolished.
entries.literal: Day wuxu: horse purchases were abolished.

entries.zh: 己亥，以子旉為檢校少保、集慶軍節度使，封魏國公。
entries.en: On jihai, the son Fang was made acting Junior Guardian and Jiqing military commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Wei.
entries.literal: Day jihai: the son Fang was made acting Junior Guardian and Jiqing military commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Wei.

entries.zh: 詔內外官司參用嘉祐、元豐敕，以俟新書。
entries.en: Inner and outer offices were ordered to apply Jiayou and Yuanfeng statutes provisionally pending new codes.
entries.literal: An edict ordered inner and outer offices to apply provisionally the Jiayou and Yuanfeng statutes pending new books.

entries.zh: 庚子，二帝徙居霫郡。
entries.en: On gengzi, the two emperors were moved to Xi commandery.
entries.literal: Day gengzi: the two emperors were moved to Xi commandery.

entries.zh: 辛丑，陳通劫提點刑獄周格營，殺格，執提點刑獄高士曈。
entries.en: On xinchou, Chen Tong raided judicial intendant Zhou Ge’s camp, killed Ge, and seized Gao Shitan.
entries.literal: Day xinchou: Chen Tong raided judicial intendant Zhou Ge’s camp, killed Ge, and seized judicial intendant Gao Shitan.

entries.zh: 壬寅，遣徽猷閣待制孟忠厚迎奉太廟神主赴揚州。
entries.en: On renyin, Imperial Writings attendant Meng Zhonghou was sent to escort the ancestral tablets to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Day renyin: Imperial Writings Hall attendant Meng Zhonghou was sent to escort the ancestral temple tablets to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 以直秘閣王圭為招撫判官，代張所，尋責所廣南安置。
entries.en: Direct Secretariat academician Wang Gui replaced Zhang Suo as pacification judge; soon Suo was exiled to the far south.
entries.literal: Direct Secretariat academician Wang Gui was made pacification judge, replacing Zhang Suo; soon Suo was blamed and placed in the far south.

entries.zh: 乙巳，宗澤表請車駕還闕。
entries.en: On yisi, Zong Ze memorialized asking the throne to return to the capital.
entries.literal: Day yisi: Zong Ze memorialized asking the imperial carriage to return to the capital.

entries.zh: 戊申，河北招撫司都統制王彥渡河擊金人，破之，復新鄉縣。
entries.en: On wushen, Hebei pacification overall controller Wang Yan crossed the river, defeated the Jin, and recovered Xinxiang.
entries.literal: Day wushen: Hebei pacification headquarters overall controller Wang Yan crossed the river, defeated the Jin, and recovered Xinxiang county.

entries.zh: 己酉，以諜報金人欲犯江、浙，詔暫駐淮甸捍禦，稍定即還京闕。
entries.en: On jiyou, hearing the Jin meant to attack Jiang and Zhe, an edict halted temporarily in the Huai region for defense and promised return to the capital once settled.
entries.literal: Day jiyou: on intelligence that the Jin meant to attack Jiang and Zhe, an edict ordered a temporary halt in the Huai region for defense and return to the capital once settled.

entries.zh: 募民入貲授官。
entries.en: Commoners were recruited to buy office with wealth.
entries.literal: The people were recruited to buy office with wealth.

entries.zh: 軍賊趙萬入常州，執守臣何袞。
entries.en: Army-bandit Zhao Wan entered Changzhou and seized defender He Gun.
entries.literal: Army-bandit Zhao Wan entered Changzhou and seized defender He Gun.

entries.zh: 罷諸路經制招撫使。
entries.en: Circuit commissioner-generals and pacification commissioners were abolished.
entries.literal: Circuit commissioner-generals and pacification commissioners were abolished.

entries.zh: 庚戌，始通當三大錢於淮、浙、荊湖諸路。
entries.en: On gengxu, the three-large cash was first circulated in Huai, Zhe, and Jing–lake circuits.
entries.literal: Day gengxu: the three-large cash was first circulated in Huai, Zhe, and Jing–lake circuits.

entries.zh: 壬子，命湖南撫諭官馬伸持詔賜張邦昌死於潭州，並誅王時雍。
entries.en: On renzi, Hunan reassurance commissioner Ma Shen was ordered to grant Zhang Bangchang death at Tanzhou and execute Wang Shiyong.
entries.literal: Day renzi: Hunan reassurance commissioner Ma Shen was ordered to carry an edict granting Zhang Bangchang death at Tanzhou and also to execute Wang Shiyong.

entries.zh: 癸丑，詔有敢妄議惑眾沮巡幸者，許告而罪之，不告者斬。
entries.en: On guichou, whoever rashly debated to obstruct the progress might be reported and punished; non-reporters were to be beheaded.
entries.literal: Day guichou: an edict—whoever rashly debated and misled the masses to obstruct the progress might be reported and punished; those who did not report were to be beheaded.

entries.zh: 乙卯，王彥及金人戰，敗績，奔太行山聚眾，其裨將岳飛引其部曲自為一軍。
entries.en: On yimao, Wang Yan fought the Jin, was defeated, fled to the Taihang to gather troops; lieutenant Yue Fei led his detachment separately.
entries.literal: Day yimao: Wang Yan fought the Jin and was defeated; he fled to the Taihang Mountains to gather troops; his lieutenant Yue Fei led his own detachment as a separate army.

entries.zh: 趙萬陷鎮江府，守臣趙子崧棄城渡江，保瓜洲。
entries.en: Zhao Wan took Zhenjiang; Zhao Zisong abandoned the city, crossed the river, and held Guazhou.
entries.literal: Zhao Wan took Zhenjiang prefecture; defender Zhao Zisong abandoned the city, crossed the river, and held Guazhou.

entries.zh: 是秋，金人分兵據兩河州縣，惟中山、慶源府、保、莫、邢洺、冀、磁、絳、相州久之乃陷。
entries.en: That autumn Jin divided troops to hold Two He prefectures; only Zhongshan, Qingyuan, Bao, Mo, Xing, Mozhou, Ji, Ci, Jiang, and Xiang fell after long resistance.
entries.literal: That autumn the Jin divided troops to hold Two He prefectures and counties; only Zhongshan, Qingyuan prefecture, Bao, Mo, Xing, Mo prefecture, Ji, Ci, Jiang, and Xiang fell only after long resistance.

entries.zh: 高宗受命中興全功至德聖神武文昭仁憲孝皇帝，諱構，字德基，徽宗第九子，母曰顯仁皇后韋氏。
entries.en: Gaozong—Received-the-Mandate, Restored-the-Dynasty, Full-Merit, Utmost-Virtue, Sage, Divine, Martial, Literary, Illustrious, Benevolent, Constitutional, Filial—taboo Gou, style Deji, Huizong’s ninth son, born of Empress Xianren Wei.
entries.literal: Gaozong, the emperor who received the mandate, restored the dynasty, accomplished full merit, utmost virtue, sage, divine, martial, literary, illustrious, benevolent, constitutional, and filial—taboo name Gou, courtesy name Deji—was Huizong’s ninth son; his mother was Empress Xianren of the Wei clan.

entries.zh: 大觀元年五月乙巳生東京之大內，赤光照室。
entries.en: Daguan 1, fifth month, yisi: born in Dongjing’s inner palace; red light washed the room.
entries.literal: Daguan year 1, fifth month, day yisi: he was born in the great inner palace at Dongjing; red light filled the chamber.

entries.zh: 八月丁丑，賜名，授定武軍節度使、檢校太尉，封蜀國公。
entries.en: Eighth month, dingchou: named and made Dingwu commissioner, Grand General, Duke of Shu.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day dingchou: a name was granted; he was made military commissioner of Dingwu army, checked Grand General, and enfeoffed Duke of Shu.

entries.zh: 二年正月庚申，封廣平郡王。
entries.en: In the second year, first month, gengshen: Prince of Guangping.
entries.literal: In the second year, first month, day gengshen: he was advanced to Prince of Guangping commandery.

entries.zh: 宣和三年十二月壬子，進封康王。
entries.en: Xuanhe 3, twelfth month, renzi: Prince of Kang.
entries.literal: Xuanhe year 3, twelfth month, day renzi: he was advanced to Prince of Kang.

entries.zh: 資性朗悟，博學強記，讀書日誦千餘言，挽弓至一石五鬥。
entries.en: Bright of wit, deep in learning and memory, he recited a thousand characters a day and drew the bow to one stone five pecks.
entries.literal: By nature bright and quick, he studied widely and remembered strongly, reciting more than a thousand characters a day in reading, and drawing the bow to one stone five pecks.

entries.zh: 宣和四年，始冠，出就外第。
entries.en: Xuanhe 4: capped, he moved to an outer mansion.
entries.literal: Xuanhe year 4: he received the capping rite and went out to an outer residence.

entries.zh: 九月庚午朔，命大臣朝饗太廟。
entries.en: Ninth month, gengwu new moon: great ministers offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day gengwu new moon: great ministers were ordered to offer at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 辛未，宗祀徽宗於明堂，以配上帝，大赦。
entries.en: On xinwei, Huizong was enshrined in the Bright Hall with the High God; a great amnesty followed.
entries.literal: Day xinwei: Emperor Huizong was enshrined in the Bright Hall with the High God as correlate; a great amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 甲戌，金人犯黃牛堡，守將李彥堅拒卻之，金兵遂扼大散關，吳璘駐青野原，遣將高松等援之。
entries.en: On jiaxu, Jin hit Huangniu Fort and Li Yanjian drove them off; they seized Dasan Pass; Wu Lin camped Qingye Plain and sent Gao Song to help.
entries.literal: Day jiaxu: Jin troops attacked Huangniu Fort; defender Li Yanjian repulsed them; the Jin then blocked Dasan Pass; Wu Lin camped at Qingye Plain and sent Generals Gao Song and others to reinforce.

entries.zh: 庚辰，以給事中黃祖舜同知樞密院事。
entries.en: On gengchen, Huang Zushun became Associate Privy Council Signatory.
entries.literal: Day gengchen: Supervising Secretary Huang Zushun was made Associate Privy Council Signatory.

entries.zh: 壬午，流星晝隕。
entries.en: On renwu, a meteor fell by day.
entries.literal: Day renwu: a meteor fell in daylight.

entries.zh: 乙酉，詔劉錡、王權、李顯忠、戚方嚴備清河、潁河、渦河口。
entries.en: On yiyou, Liu Qi, Wang Quan, Li Xianzhong, and Qi Fang were told to brace Qinghe, Yinghe, and Guo mouths.
entries.literal: Day yiyou: an edict ordered Liu Qi, Wang Quan, Li Xianzhong, and Qi Fang to ready Qinghe, Yinghe, and Guohe mouths strictly.

entries.zh: 丁亥，成閔渡江，屯應城縣，遣吳拱戍郢州。
entries.en: On dinghai, Cheng Min crossed to Yingcheng and posted Wu Gong at Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Day dinghai: Cheng Min crossed the river and camped at Yingcheng county; he sent Wu Gong to garrison Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 博州民王友直聚兵大名，自稱河北安撫制置使，以其徒王任為副，遣軍師馮穀入朝奏事。
entries.en: Wang Youzhi of Bozhou raised Daming, called himself Hebei pacification commissioner, made Wang Ren vice, and sent Feng Gu to court.
entries.literal: Bozhou commoner Wang Youzhi gathered troops at Daming, styled himself Hebei pacification commissioner, made his follower Wang Ren vice, and sent strategist Feng Gu to court to report.

entries.zh: 吳璘遣將彭青至寶雞渭河，夜劫金人橋頭砦，破之。
entries.en: Wu Lin's Peng Qing reached the Baoji Wei, raided the bridgehead fort by night, and took it.
entries.literal: Wu Lin sent General Peng Qing to the Baoji Wei River; at night he raided the Jin bridgehead fort and broke it.

entries.zh: 庚寅，成閔遣統制趙撙部兵五千駐德安。
entries.en: On gengyin, Cheng Min sent Zhao Zan with five thousand to De'an.
entries.literal: Day gengyin: Cheng Min sent controller Zhao Zan with five thousand to camp at De'an.

entries.zh: 辛卯，金國趣使臣書至楚州，守臣以聞，其辭多悖慢。
entries.en: On xinmao, an insolent Jin dispatch reached Chuzhou and the prefect reported it.
entries.literal: Day xinmao: a Jin urgent dispatch reached Chuzhou; the prefect reported it—its wording was mostly insolent.

entries.zh: 壬辰，監盱眙軍淮河渡夏俊復泗州。
entries.en: On renchen, Xia Jun of the Chuyang garrison retook Sizhou.
entries.literal: Day renchen: Chuyang garrison inspector Xia Jun recovered Sizhou.

entries.zh: 癸巳，金人犯通化軍，守將張超拒卻之。
entries.en: On guisi, Jin hit Tonghua Army and Zhang Chao drove them back.
entries.literal: Day guisi: Jin troops attacked Tonghua Army; defender Zhang Chao repulsed them.

entries.zh: 甲午，冊諡大行皇帝曰恭文順德仁孝皇帝，廟號欽宗。
entries.en: On jiawu, the late emperor was styled Respectful, Cultured, Accordant, Virtuous, and Filial with temple name Qinzong.
entries.literal: Day jiawu: the late emperor was given the temple posthumous title Respectful, Cultured, Accordant, Virtuous, and Filial and the temple name Qinzong.

entries.zh: 吳璘遣將劉海復秦州，金守將蕭濟降。
entries.en: Wu Lin's Liu Hai retook Qinzhou; the Jin prefect Xiao Ji surrendered.
entries.literal: Wu Lin sent General Liu Hai to recover Qinzhou; Jin prefect Xiao Ji submitted.

entries.zh: 乙未，金人犯信陽軍。
entries.en: On yiwei, Jin attacked Xinyang Army.
entries.literal: Day yiwei: Jin troops attacked Xinyang Army.

entries.zh: 丙申，吳璘遣將曹㳜復洮州。
entries.en: On bingshen, Wu Lin's Cao Sui retook Taozhou.
entries.literal: Day bingshen: Wu Lin sent General Cao Sui to recover Taozhou.

entries.zh: 戊戌，劉錡發揚州。
entries.en: On wuxu, Liu Qi marched from Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Day wuxu: Liu Qi marched from Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 詔以金人背盟，降敕榜招諭中原軍民。
entries.en: Because the Jin had broken treaty, a placard called the central plain to arms.
entries.literal: An edict, because the Jin had broken the alliance, issued a placard to summon the armies and people of the central plain.

entries.zh: 己亥，蘭州漢軍千戶王宏殺其刺史溫敦烏乜來降。
entries.en: On jihai, Lanzhou Han officer Wang Hong killed Commissioner Wendun Wuma and defected.
entries.literal: Day jihai: Wang Hong, a thousand-household chief of the Lanzhou Han army, killed his commissioner Wendun Wuma and came over.

entries.zh: 吳璘遣將彭青復隴州。
entries.en: Wu Lin's Peng Qing retook Longzhou.
entries.literal: Wu Lin sent General Peng Qing to recover Longzhou.

entries.zh: 是月，金主亮以尚書右丞李通為大都督，造浮梁于淮水之上，遂自將來攻，兵號百萬，遠近大震。
entries.en: That month Hailing made Li Tong grand marshal, bridged the Huai, and came himself with a host said at a million; the realm shook.
entries.literal: That month, the Jin ruler Hailing made Right Vice Director Li Tong grand marshal, built pontoon bridges on the Huai, then came in person to attack; his troops were said to number a million; near and far were greatly shaken.

entries.zh: 冬十月庚子朔，詔將親征。
entries.en: Tenth month, gengzi new moon: Gaozong announced he would take the field.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengzi new moon: an edict said the Emperor would campaign in person.

entries.zh: 魏勝攻沂州，敗，還海州，金人圍之。
entries.en: Wei Sheng attacked Yizhou, lost, fled to Haizhou, and the Jin besieged him.
entries.literal: Wei Sheng attacked Yizhou, was defeated, returned to Haizhou, and the Jin besieged it.

entries.zh: 李寶以舟師至東海縣，金人解圍去，寶遂入海州。
entries.en: Li Bao's fleet reached Donghai; the Jin broke the siege; Bao entered Haizhou.
entries.literal: Li Bao with his fleet reached Donghai county; the Jin lifted the siege and left; Bao then entered Haizhou.

entries.zh: 辛丑，金人自渦口渡淮。
entries.en: On xinchou, the Jin crossed the Huai at Wokou.
entries.literal: Day xinchou: Jin troops crossed the Huai from Wokou.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以吳璘兼陝西、河東招討使，劉錡兼京東、河北東路招討使，成閔兼京西、河北西路招討使。
entries.en: On guimao, Wu Lin also took Shaanxi and Hedong; Liu Qi Hebei East; Cheng Min Jingxi and Hebei West.
entries.literal: Day guimao: Wu Lin was also made Shaanxi and Hedong pacification commissioner; Liu Qi also made Hebei East and East-Hebei pacification commissioner; Cheng Min also made Jingxi and Hebei West pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 金人陷蔣州。
entries.en: The Jin took Jiang prefecture.
entries.literal: Jin troops took Jiang prefecture.

entries.zh: 李顯忠遣統制孔福與金人戰于大人洲，敗之。
entries.en: Li Xianzhong's Kong Fu beat the Jin at Daren Islet.
entries.literal: Li Xianzhong sent controller Kong Fu to fight the Jin at Daren Islet and defeated them.

entries.zh: 乙巳，金人復犯海州，魏勝、李寶擊卻之。
entries.en: On yisi, the Jin struck Haizhou again; Wei Sheng and Li Bao repulsed them.
entries.literal: Day yisi: Jin troops again attacked Haizhou; Wei Sheng and Li Bao beat them back.

entries.zh: 劉錡引兵次淮陰，金人將自清河口入淮，錡列兵于運河岸以扼之。
entries.en: Liu Qi halted at Huaiyin; as the Jin aimed for Qinghe mouth, he lined the canal to block them.
entries.literal: Liu Qi led troops to Huaiyin; the Jin were about to enter the Huai from Qinghe mouth; Qi arrayed troops on the canal bank to block them.

entries.zh: 丁未，命宣撫制置司傳檄契丹、西夏、高麗、渤海諸國及河北、河東、陝西、京東、河南諸路，諭出師共討金人。
entries.en: On dingwei day, the Pacification and Control Office was ordered to send proclamations to Khitan, Western Xia, Goryeo, Bohai, and the Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, Jingdong, and Henan circuits, instructing them to send troops and join in attacking the Jin.
