entries.literal: Day dingwei: the pacification and commissioner offices were ordered to proclaim to Khitan, Western Xia, Goryeo, Bohai, and the circuits of Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, Jingdong, and Henan, urging them to march and join in attacking the Jin.

entries.zh: 是日，金人立其東京留守葛王褒為皇帝，改元大定。
entries.en: That day the Jin made Eastern Capital regent Prince of Ge emperor with era Dading.
entries.literal: That day, the Jin set up their Eastern Capital regent, the Prince of Ge, as emperor and changed the era name to Dad ing.

entries.zh: 戊申，王權聞金兵大至，自廬州引兵遁，屯昭關。
entries.en: On wushen, hearing the Jin host was vast, Wang Quan fled Luzhou to Zhaoguan.
entries.literal: Day wushen: Wang Quan, hearing the Jin army was great, led troops from Luzhou in flight and camped at Zhaoguan.

entries.zh: 己酉，知均州武钜招納北界杜海等二萬人來歸。
entries.en: On jiyou, Jun's Wu Ju brought in Du Hai and twenty thousand northerners.
entries.literal: Day jiyou: Jun prefect Wu Ju recruited Du Hai and twenty thousand others from north of the border to submit.

entries.zh: 庚戌，復置機速房。
entries.en: On gengxu, the Rapid-Response Office was restored.
entries.literal: Day gengxu: the Rapid-Response Office was restored.

entries.zh: 知廬州龔濤聞金兵將至，棄城走。
entries.en: Luzhou's Gong Tao fled before the Jin arrived.
entries.literal: Luzhou prefect Gong Tao, hearing the Jin would come, abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 辛亥，金將蕭琦陷滁州，守臣陸廉棄城走。
entries.en: On xinhai, Xiao Qi took Chuzhou; Lu Lian fled.
entries.literal: Day xinhai: Jin general Xiao Qi took Chuzhou; the prefect Lu Lian abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 壬子，改建王瑋為鎮南軍節度使。
entries.en: On renzi, the Prince of Jian became Zhennan Army military commissioner.
entries.literal: Day renzi: the Prince of Jian was changed to military commissioner of the Zhennan Army.

entries.zh: 劉錡遣統制王剛等擊敗金人於清河口，金人復來戰，剛失利。
entries.en: Liu Qi's Wang Gang beat the Jin at Qinghe mouth, then lost the rematch.
entries.literal: Liu Qi sent controllers Wang Gang and others to defeat the Jin at Qinghe mouth; the Jin came again and Gang was defeated.

entries.zh: 吳拱遣將侯俊、郝敦書復唐州。
entries.en: Wu Gong's Hou Jun and Hao Dunshu retook Tangzhou.
entries.literal: Wu Gong sent generals Hou Jun and Hao Dunshu to recover Tangzhou.

entries.zh: 癸丑，借江、浙、荊湖等路坊場淨利錢三百八十萬緡以備賞軍。
entries.en: On guichou, 3.8 million strings of market profit from Jiang, Zhe, and Jinghu were borrowed for rewards.
entries.literal: Day guichou: three million eight hundred thousand strings of net profit from Jiang, Zhe, Jinghu, and other circuit market stalls were borrowed to fund army rewards.

entries.zh: 金人圍廬州，都監、權州事楊春率兵突陣出，守水砦。
entries.en: The Jin besieged Luzhou; Yang Chun broke out and held a water fort.
entries.literal: Jin troops besieged Luzhou; garrison inspector and acting prefect Yang Chun led troops in a breakout and held a water fort.

entries.zh: 金人又攻海州，李寶力戰敗之，解圍去。
entries.en: The Jin struck Haizhou again; Li Bao fought them off and they withdrew.
entries.literal: The Jin again attacked Haizhou; Li Bao fought hard and defeated them; they lifted the siege and left.

entries.zh: 甲寅，金人攻樊城，吳拱遣守將翟貴、王進與戰，貴、進俱戰死，金兵亦退。
entries.en: On jiayin, the Jin hit Fancheng; Zhai Gui and Wang Jin died fighting and the Jin withdrew.
entries.literal: Day jiayin: Jin troops attacked Fancheng; Wu Gong sent defenders Zhai Gui and Wang Jin to fight; Gui and Jin both died in battle and the Jin also withdrew.

entries.zh: 劉錡遣兵渡淮及金人戰，死者十七八。
entries.en: Liu Qi's men crossed the Huai and lost seven or eight in ten.
entries.literal: Liu Qi sent troops across the Huai to fight the Jin; seven or eight in ten died.

entries.zh: 金主亮以大軍至廬州城北之五里，築土城以居。
entries.en: Hailing camped five li north of Luzhou and threw up an earthen wall.
entries.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing with his great army reached five li north of Luzhou city and built an earthen wall to dwell in.

entries.zh: 戚方遣將張寶復蔣州。
entries.en: Qi Fang's Zhang Bao retook Jiang prefecture.
entries.literal: Qi Fang sent General Zhang Bao to recover Jiang prefecture.

entries.zh: 乙卯，以金人渝盟告於天地、宗廟、社稷。
entries.en: On yimao, the Jin breach was proclaimed to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars.
entries.literal: Day yimao: the Jin breach of treaty was announced to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altars of Soil and Grain.

entries.zh: 命州縣諭富民捐貲助國。
entries.en: Counties were told to urge wealthy households to donate to the war effort.
entries.literal: Prefectures and counties were ordered to tell wealthy households to donate funds to aid the state.

entries.zh: 劉錡聞王權遁，自淮陰引兵歸揚州。
entries.en: Hearing Wang Quan had run, Liu Qi pulled back from Huaiyin to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Qi, hearing Wang Quan had fled, led troops from Huaiyin back to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 丙辰，金主亮入廬州，王權自昭關遁，金人追至尉子橋，破敵軍統制姚興戰死，權退保和州。
entries.en: On bingchen, Hailing entered Luzhou; Wang Quan fled Zhaoguan; at Weizi Bridge Yao Xing fell; Quan held Hezhou.
entries.literal: Day bingchen: the Jin ruler Hailing entered Luzhou; Wang Quan fled from Zhaoguan; the Jin pursued to Weizi Bridge; Break-the-Enemy controller Yao Xing died fighting; Quan fell back to defend Hezhou.

entries.zh: 金州都統制王彥遣統制任天錫出洵陽，復豐陽縣。
entries.en: Wang Yan's Ren Tiansi left Xunyang and retook Fengyang.
entries.literal: Jinzhou overall commander Wang Yan sent controller Ren Tiansi out of Xunyang and recovered Fengyang county.

entries.zh: 丁巳，帝聞王權敗，召楊存中同宰執議於內殿，陳康伯贊帝定議親征。
entries.en: On dingsi, hearing of Wang Quan's defeat, Gaozong called Yang Cunzhong and the councilors within; Chen Kangbo praised his resolve to take the field.
entries.literal: Day dingsi: the Emperor, hearing Wang Quan was defeated, summoned Yang Cunzhong with the chief ministers to discuss in the inner hall; Chen Kangbo praised the Emperor for fixing on campaigning in person.

entries.zh: 武钜遣將荀琛復鄧州。
entries.en: Wu Ju's Xun Chen retook Dengzhou.
entries.literal: Wu Ju sent General Xun Chen to recover Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 戊午，任天錫復商洛縣。
entries.en: On wuwu, Ren Tiansi retook Shangluo.
entries.literal: Day wuwu: Ren Tiansi recovered Shangluo county.

entries.zh: 命吳璘趣出兵漢中，葉義問督視江、淮軍馬，中書舍人虞允文參謀軍事。
entries.en: Wu Lin was urged out of Hanzhong; Ye Yiwen oversaw Jiang and Huai; Yu Yunwen advised on the war.
entries.literal: Wu Lin was ordered to hurry troops out of Hanzhong; Ye Yiwen supervised Jiang and Huai forces; Secretariat drafter Yu Yunwen joined in planning the army.

entries.zh: 金人犯真州，步軍司統制邵宏淵逆戰於胥浦橋，兵敗，真州陷。
entries.en: The Jin took Zhenzhou after Shao Hongyuan lost at Xupu Bridge.
entries.literal: Jin troops attacked Zhenzhou; Infantry Bureau controller Shao Hongyuan met them at Xupu Bridge, was defeated, and Zhenzhou fell.

entries.zh: 金人不入城，遂犯揚州。
entries.en: They bypassed the city and struck Yangzhou.
entries.literal: The Jin did not enter the city but then attacked Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 己未，任天錫復商州，執其守完顏守能。
entries.en: On jiwei, Ren Tiansi retook Shangzhou and seized Wanyan Shouneng.
entries.literal: Day jiwei: Ren Tiansi recovered Shangzhou and captured its prefect Wanyan Shouneng.

entries.zh: 趙撙引兵渡淮。
entries.en: Zhao Zan crossed the Huai.
entries.literal: Zhao Zan led troops across the Huai.

entries.zh: 庚申，以楊存中為禦營宿衛使。
entries.en: On gengshen, Yang Cunzhong became Palace Guard commissioner.
entries.literal: Day gengshen: Yang Cunzhong was made Palace Guard commissioner.

entries.zh: 趙撙復褒信縣。
entries.en: Zhao Zan retook Baoxin.
entries.literal: Zhao Zan recovered Baoxin county.

entries.zh: 王權自和州遁歸，屯於東採石。
entries.en: Wang Quan fled Hezhou to East Caishi.
entries.literal: Wang Quan fled from Hezhou back and camped at East Caishi.

entries.zh: 辛酉，復湯思退觀文殿大學士、充醴泉觀使兼侍讀。
entries.en: On xinyou, Tang Situi was restored to Cultivating Culture academician, Sweet Spring commissioner, and Lecturer-in-Attendance.
entries.literal: Day xinyou: Tang Situi was restored as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Culture, made commissioner of the Sweet Spring Abbey and concurrent Lecturer-in-Attendance.

entries.zh: 分行在官吏三之一扈從，餘留行遣常事。
entries.en: A third of capital officials would accompany the Emperor; the rest kept routine business.
entries.literal: One third of the mobile court's civil officials were to accompany the expedition; the rest remained to handle routine business.

entries.zh: 金人陷和州。
entries.en: The Jin took Hezhou.
entries.literal: Jin troops took Hezhou.

entries.zh: 壬戌，以將士勞於征討，避殿減膳。
entries.en: On renxu, Gaozong avoided the main hall and ate sparingly for the troops' sake.
entries.literal: Day renxu: because the troops were weary in campaign, the Emperor avoided the main hall and reduced his meals.

entries.zh: 劉錡退軍瓜州鎮，金人陷揚州，淮東安撫使劉澤棄城奔泰州。
entries.en: Liu Qi fell back to Guazhou; the Jin took Yangzhou; Liu Ze fled to Taizhou.
entries.literal: Liu Qi withdrew to Guazhou town; the Jin took Yangzhou; Huai East pacification commissioner Liu Ze abandoned the city and fled to Taizhou.

entries.zh: 以戶部侍郎劉岑為禦營隨軍都轉運使，李顯忠為禦營先鋒都統制屯蕪湖，主管步軍司李捧為前軍都統制。
entries.en: Liu Cen became campaign transport commissioner; Li Xianzhong vanguard commander at Wuhu; Li Peng forward-army commander.
entries.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Liu Cen was made Palace Guard campaign overall transport commissioner; Li Xianzhong was made Palace Guard vanguard overall commander and camped at Wuhu; director of the Infantry Bureau Li Peng was made forward-army overall commander.

entries.zh: 趙撙復新蔡縣。
entries.en: Zhao Zan retook Xincai.
entries.literal: Zhao Zan recovered Xincai county.

entries.zh: 癸亥，募諸州豪民招槍杖、弓箭手赴 行在。
entries.en: On guihai, wealthy prefectural households were recruited to raise pikes and bows for court.
entries.literal: Day guihai: wealthy men of the prefectures were recruited to raise pike and bowmen for the mobile court.

entries.zh: 金人入揚州。
entries.en: The Jin entered Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Jin troops entered Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 王權自採石夜還建康，
entries.en: Wang Quan slipped back from Caishi to Jiankang by night,
entries.literal: Wang Quan by night returned from Caishi to Jiankang,

entries.zh: 十一月己巳朔，邵宏淵遣統領崔皋及金人戰於定山，敗之。
entries.en: Eleventh month, jisi new moon: Shao Hongyuan's Cui Gao beat the Jin at Dingshan.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, day jisi new moon: Shao Hongyuan sent commander Cui Gao to fight the Jin at Dingshan and defeated them.

entries.zh: 任天錫復虢州，守將蕭信遁去。
entries.en: Ren Tiansi retook Guozhou; Xiao Xin fled.
entries.literal: Ren Tiansi recovered Guozhou; the Jin prefect Xiao Xin fled.

entries.zh: 庚午，通州守臣崔邦弼棄城去。
entries.en: On gengwu, Tongzhou's Cui Bangbi abandoned his post.
entries.literal: Day gengwu: Tongzhou prefect Cui Bangbi abandoned the city and left.

entries.zh: 辛未，成閔引兵發應城縣，援淮西。
entries.en: On xinwei, Cheng Min marched from Yingcheng to aid Huai West.
entries.literal: Day xinwei: Cheng Min led troops from Yingcheng county to aid Huai West.

entries.zh: 遣權吏部侍郎汪應辰詣浙東措置海道。
entries.en: Wang Yingchen was sent to organize the Zhe East sea route.
entries.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Personnel Wang Yingchen was sent to arrange the sea route in Zhe East.

entries.zh: 壬申，以張浚判建康府。
entries.en: On renshen, Zhang Jun was assigned Jiankang.
entries.literal: Day renshen: Zhang Jun was made to judge Jiankang prefecture.

entries.zh: 召王權赴行在，以李顯忠代將。
entries.en: Wang Quan was recalled; Li Xianzhong took his command.
entries.literal: Wang Quan was summoned to the mobile court; Li Xianzhong replaced him in command.

entries.zh: 邵宏淵為池州都統制。
entries.en: Shao Hongyuan became Chizhou overall commander.
entries.literal: Shao Hongyuan was made Chizhou overall commander.

entries.zh: 金人犯瓜州，鎮江中軍統制劉汜戰敗走，權都統制李橫亦遁。
entries.en: The Jin hit Guazhou; Liu Si fled in defeat and Li Heng with him.
entries.literal: Jin troops attacked Guazhou; Zhenjiang central-army controller Liu Si was defeated and fled; acting overall commander Li Heng also fled.

entries.zh: 金人鐵騎奄至江上，統制魏俊、王方死之。
entries.en: Jin iron cavalry swept to the riverbank; Wei Jun and Wang Fang fell.
entries.literal: Jin iron cavalry suddenly reached the river; controllers Wei Jun and Wang Fang died.

entries.zh: 葉義問惶怖欲退走，復趨建康。
entries.en: Ye Yiwen nearly fled in panic, then rushed to Jiankang.
entries.literal: Ye Yiwen in panic wished to withdraw but then hurried to Jiankang.

entries.zh: 金人游騎至無為軍，守臣韓髦棄城走。
entries.en: Jin raiders reached Wuwei; Han Mao fled.
entries.literal: Jin raiders reached Wuwei Army; prefect Han Mao abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 癸酉，淮甯府民陳亨祖執同知完顏耶魯，以其城來歸。
entries.en: On guiyou, Chen Hengzu of Huaining seized Wanyan Yelu and surrendered the city.
entries.literal: Day guiyou: Huaining prefecture commoner Chen Hengzu seized Vice Prefect Wanyan Yelu and brought the city in.

entries.zh: 趙撙引兵去，蔡州復陷。
entries.en: Zhao Zan withdrew and Caizhou fell again.
entries.literal: Zhao Zan led troops away; Caizhou again fell.

entries.zh: 甲戌，池州統制官崔定等復入無為軍。
entries.en: On jiaxu, Cui Ding of Chizhou re-entered Wuwei Army.
entries.literal: Day jiaxu: Chizhou controller Cui Ding and others re-entered Wuwei Army.

entries.zh: 乙亥，金主亮臨江築壇，刑馬祭天，期以翌日南渡。
entries.en: On yihai, Hailing sacrificed a horse by the river and vowed to cross the next day.
entries.literal: Day yihai: the Jin ruler Hailing built an altar by the river, slaughtered a horse to sacrifice to Heaven, and set the next day to cross south.

entries.zh: 丙子，虞允文督建康諸軍統制官張振、王琪、時俊、戴皋等以舟師拒金主亮於東採石，戰勝，卻之。
entries.en: On bingzi, Yu Yunwen's fleet met Hailing at East Caishi, won, and drove him back.
entries.literal: Day bingzi: Yu Yunwen directed Jiankang fleet controllers Zhang Zhen, Wang Qi, Shi Jun, and Dai Gao and others with warships to meet Hailing at East Caishi, fought, won, and drove him back.

entries.zh: 崔定復巢縣，任天錫復上津、商洛二縣。
entries.en: Cui Ding retook Chao; Ren Tiansi retook Shangjin and Shangluo.
entries.literal: Cui Ding recovered Chao county; Ren Tiansi recovered Shangjin and Shangluo counties.

entries.zh: 丁丑，虞允文遣水軍統制盛新以舟師擊金人于楊林河口，又敗之。
entries.en: On dingchou, Yu Yunwen's Sheng Xin beat the Jin again at Yanglin mouth.
entries.literal: Day dingchou: Yu Yunwen sent naval controller Sheng Xin with warships to strike the Jin at Yanglin River mouth and again defeated them.

entries.zh: 金主亮焚其舟而去。
entries.en: Hailing burned his boats and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing burned his boats and left.

entries.zh: 戊寅，王彥遣將楊堅復欒川縣。
entries.en: On wuyin, Wang Yan's Yang Jian retook Luanchuan.
entries.literal: Day wuyin: Wang Yan sent General Yang Jian to recover Luanchuan county.

entries.zh: 己卯，以湯思退為行宮留守。
entries.en: On jimao, Tang Situi was made mobile-court resident.
entries.literal: Day jimao: Tang Situi was made mobile-court resident.

entries.zh: 虛恨蠻犯嘉州籠蓬堡，官軍大敗，副將鄭祥等為所殺。
entries.en: The Xuhuaiman struck Longpeng fort in Jiazhou; government troops were routed and deputy commander Zheng Xiang and others were killed.
entries.literal: The Xuhuaiman attacked Jiazhou's Longpeng fort; government troops were badly beaten and deputy commander Zheng Xiang and others were killed.

entries.zh: 庚辰，金主亮引軍趨淮東。
entries.en: On gengchen, Jin Emperor Hailing marched toward Huai east.
entries.literal: Day gengchen: the Jin ruler Hailing led his army toward Huai east.

entries.zh: 癸未，吳璘病，自仙人原還興州，留姚仲節制軍事，虞允文自採石率李捧一軍及戈船如鎮江備敵。
entries.en: On guimao, Wu Lin fell ill, left Xianrenyuan for Xing, put Yao Zhong in charge of the army, and Yu Yunwen from Caishi sent Li Peng's force and war junks to Zhenjiang.
entries.literal: Day guimao: Wu Lin fell ill, returned from Xianrenyuan to Xing prefecture, left Yao Zhong to control the army, and Yu Yunwen from Caishi led Li Peng's army and war junks to Zhenjiang against the enemy.

entries.zh: 甲申，贈姚興、魏俊、王方官。
entries.en: On jiashen, Yao Xing, Wei Jun, and Wang Fang received posthumous enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Day jiashen: Yao Xing, Wei Jun, and Wang Fang were posthumously enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 金主亮至揚州。
entries.en: Jin Emperor Hailing reached Yangzhou.
entries.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing reached Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 乙酉，貸劉汜死、英州編管。
entries.en: On yiyou, Liu Si was spared execution and banished to Ying supervision.
entries.literal: Day yiyou: Liu Si was spared death and banished to registered supervision at Ying prefecture.

entries.zh: 江州統制李貴、忠義首領孟俊復順昌府，金州將邢進復華州。
entries.en: Jiangzhou commander Li Gui and loyalist Meng Jun retook Shunchang; Jin officer Xing Jin retook Hua prefecture.
entries.literal: Jiangzhou overall commander Li Gui and loyalist leader Meng Jun recovered Shunchang prefecture; Jin prefecture commander Xing Jin recovered Hua prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙戌，賜戰士帛，給其家薪炭。
entries.en: On bingxu, warriors received silk grants and their families were given fuel.
entries.literal: Day bingxu: silk was granted to fighting men and fuel given their families.

entries.zh: 任天錫復陝州。
entries.en: Ren Tiansi retook Shan prefecture.
entries.literal: Ren Tiansi recovered Shan prefecture.

entries.zh: 丁亥，劉錡以疾罷，以禦營宿衛中軍統制劉銳權鎮江都統制。
entries.en: On dinghai, Liu Qi left office for illness; central-army controller Liu Rui became acting Zhenjiang commander.
entries.literal: Day dinghai: Liu Qi was dismissed for illness; Imperial Guard central-army controller Liu Rui was made acting Zhenjiang overall commander.

entries.zh: 成閔自京西還建康，遂如鎮江。
entries.en: Cheng Min came back from Jing west to Jiankang and then to Zhenjiang.
entries.literal: Cheng Min returned from Jing west to Jiankang and then went to Zhenjiang.

entries.zh: 戊子，吳璘復力疾上仙人原。
entries.en: On wuzi, Wu Lin dragged himself back to Xianrenyuan despite illness.
entries.literal: Day wuzi: Wu Lin again forced himself up to Xianrenyuan despite illness.

entries.zh: 己丑，王權貸死、瓊州編管。
entries.en: On jichou, Wang Quan was spared execution and banished to Qiong supervision.
entries.literal: Day jichou: Wang Quan was spared death and banished to registered supervision at Qiong prefecture.

entries.zh: 李寶泛海南歸。
entries.en: Li Bao returned by sea from the south.
entries.literal: Li Bao sailed the sea south and returned.

entries.zh: 金人復攻陝州，任天錫破走之。
entries.en: The Jin struck Shan again; Ren Tiansi beat them back.
entries.literal: The Jin again attacked Shan prefecture; Ren Tiansi routed and drove them off.

entries.zh: 復犯襄陽，統制官李勝等拒卻之，復通化軍。
entries.en: They struck Xiangyang again; controller Li Sheng and others drove them off and restored Tonghua army.
entries.literal: They again attacked Xiangyang; controller Li Sheng and others repelled them and restored Tonghua army.

entries.zh: 王彥遣將楊堅、黨清至西京長水縣及金人戰，敗之。
entries.en: Wang Yan sent Yang Jian and Dang Qing to Changshui west of the Western Capital, fought the Jin, and won.
entries.literal: Wang Yan sent generals Yang Jian and Dang Qing to Changshui county west of the Western Capital and fought the Jin, defeating them.

entries.zh: 庚寅，復長水縣。
entries.en: On gengyin, Changshui county was restored.
entries.literal: Day gengyin: Changshui county was restored.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以成閔為鎮江都統制、淮東制置使、京東西路河北東路淮北泗宿州招討使，李顯忠為淮西制置使、京畿河北西路淮北壽亳州招討使，吳拱為湖北京西制置使、京西北路招討使。
entries.en: On guisi, Cheng Min became Zhenjiang commander, Huai east commissioner, and reconquest commissioner for Jing west and east, Hebei east, and Huai-north Si and Su; Li Xianzhong became Huai west commissioner and reconquest commissioner for Jingji, Hebei west, and Huai-north Shou and Bo; Wu Gong became Hubei–Jing west commissioner and Jing northwest reconquest commissioner.
entries.literal: Day guisi: Cheng Min was made Zhenjiang overall commander, Huai east commissioner, and commissioner for pacification and reconquest of Jing west, Jing east, Hebei east, and north of the Huai including Si and Su prefectures; Li Xianzhong Huai west commissioner and commissioner for Jingji, Hebei west, and north of the Huai including Shou and Bo prefectures; Wu Gong Hubei and Jing west commissioner and commissioner for Jing northwest.

entries.zh: 甲午，武钜遣鄉兵總轄杜隱等復嵩州。
entries.en: On jiawu, Wu Ju's militia commander Du Yin and others retook Song prefecture.
entries.literal: Day jiawu: Wu Ju sent militia commander Du Yin and others to recover Song prefecture.

entries.zh: 乙未，金人陷泰州。
entries.en: On yiwei, the Jin captured Taizhou.
entries.literal: Day yiwei: the Jin took Taizhou.

entries.zh: 是日，金人弑其主亮於揚州龜山寺。
entries.en: That day the Jin killed Emperor Hailing at Guishan Temple in Yangzhou.
entries.literal: That day the Jin slew their ruler Hailing at Guishan Temple in Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 戊戌，金都督府遣人持檄詣鎮江軍中議和。
entries.en: On wuxu, the Jin command sent envoys with a peace proclamation to the Zhenjiang army.
entries.literal: Day wuxu: the Jin command headquarters sent men with a proclamation to the Zhenjiang army to discuss peace.

entries.zh: 十二月己亥朔，趙撙夜襲蔡州，復入其城。
entries.en: Twelfth month, jihai new moon: Zhao Zong night-raided Cai prefecture and re-entered the city.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, day jihai new moon: Zhao Zong by night raided Cai prefecture and re-entered its walls.

entries.zh: 王彥遣兵復福昌縣。
entries.en: Wang Yan sent troops to retake Fuchang county.
entries.literal: Wang Yan sent troops to recover Fuchang county.

entries.zh: 庚子，楊存中及虞允文渡江至瓜州察金兵。
entries.en: On gengzi, Yang Cunzhong and Yu Yunwen crossed to Guazhou to scout the Jin.
entries.literal: Day gengzi: Yang Cunzhong and Yu Yunwen crossed the river to Guazhou to inspect Jin troops.

entries.zh: 金人犯漢南之茨湖，鄂州軍士史俊登其舟，獲一將，諸軍繼進，遂擊卻之。
entries.en: The Jin struck Cihu in south Han; Ezhou soldier Shi Jun boarded a boat, captured a general, the armies followed up, and beat them back.
entries.literal: The Jin attacked Cihu in south Han; Ezhou soldier Shi Jun boarded their boat, seized a general, the armies pressed on, and drove them back.

entries.zh: 楊椿夜攻金人，殺其帥高定山，復廬州。
entries.en: Yang Chun night-attacked the Jin, killed commander Gao Dingshan, and retook Luzhou.
entries.literal: Yang Chun by night attacked the Jin, killed their commander Gao Dingshan, and recovered Luzhou.

entries.zh: 辛丑，以李寶為靖海軍節度使、浙西通泰海州沿海制置使、京東東路招討使。
entries.en: On xinchou, Li Bao became Jinghai military commissioner, Zhe-west coastal commissioner for Tong, Tai, and Hai, and Jing-east reconquest commissioner.
entries.literal: Day xinchou: Li Bao was made military commissioner of the Jinghai Army, coastal commissioner for Zhe west and Tong, Tai, and Haizhou, and reconquest commissioner for Jing east.

entries.zh: 金統軍劉萼聞茨湖敗，亦退師。
entries.en: Jin commander Liu E, hearing of Cihu's defeat, also withdrew.
entries.literal: Jin overall commander Liu E, hearing of the defeat at Cihu, also withdrew his army.

entries.zh: 王彥遣將閻玘復澠池縣。
entries.en: Wang Yan sent Yan Qi to retake Mianchi county.
entries.literal: Wang Yan sent general Yan Qi to recover Mianchi county.

entries.zh: 壬寅，天有白氣。
entries.en: On renyin, white vapor appeared in the sky.
entries.literal: Day renyin: white vapor appeared in the sky.

entries.zh: 以趙密為行宮在城都總管。
entries.en: Zhao Mi was made in-city traveling-palace overall commander.
entries.literal: Zhao Mi was made overall commander of the traveling palace within the city.

entries.zh: 成閔渡江之揚州。
entries.en: Cheng Min crossed the river to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Cheng Min crossed the river to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 癸卯，命諸路招討司率兵進討，互相應援，沿江諸大帥條陳恢復事宜。
entries.en: On guimao, every reconquest office was told to advance in mutual support; Yangtze commanders were to submit recovery plans.
entries.literal: Day guimao: reconquest offices on every route were ordered to advance together with mutual support; great commanders along the river were to submit plans for recovery.

entries.zh: 復岳州舊名。
entries.en: Yue prefecture's former name was restored.
entries.literal: Yue prefecture's old name was restored.

entries.zh: 右軍統領沙世堅入泰州。
entries.en: Right-army controller Sha Shijian entered Taizhou.
entries.literal: Right-army controller Sha Shijian entered Taizhou.

entries.zh: 甲辰，虞允文自鎮江入見。
entries.en: On jiachen, Yu Yunwen came from Zhenjiang for audience.
entries.literal: Day jiachen: Yu Yunwen from Zhenjiang had audience.

entries.zh: 均州統領昝朝復鄧州。
entries.en: Jun controller Zan Chao retook Deng prefecture.
entries.literal: Jun prefecture controller Zan Chao recovered Deng prefecture.

entries.zh: 乙巳，張浚至慈湖，命李顯忠引兵渡江。
entries.en: On yisi, Zhang Jun reached Cihu and told Li Xianzhong to cross the river.
entries.literal: Day yisi: Zhang Jun reached Cihu and ordered Li Xianzhong to lead troops across the river.

entries.zh: 丙午，淮東統制王選復楚州。
entries.en: On bingwu, Huai east controller Wang Xuan retook Chu prefecture.
entries.literal: Day bingwu: Huai east controller Wang Xuan recovered Chu prefecture.

entries.zh: 丁未，杜隱等入河南府。
entries.en: On dingwei, Du Yin and others entered Henan prefecture.
entries.literal: Day dingwei: Du Yin and others entered Henan prefecture.

entries.zh: 吳拱遣統制牛宏入汝州。
entries.en: Wu Gong sent controller Niu Hong into Ru prefecture.
entries.literal: Wu Gong sent controller Niu Hong into Ru prefecture.

entries.zh: 戊申，帝發臨安，建王從行。
entries.en: On wushen, the emperor left Lin'an with the Prince of Jian.
entries.literal: Day wushen: the Emperor set out from Lin'an; the Prince of Jian accompanied him.

entries.zh: 庚戌，金人渡淮北去。
entries.en: On gengxu, the Jin crossed north of the Huai and withdrew.
entries.literal: Day gengxu: the Jin crossed north of the Huai and departed.

entries.zh: 壬子，次平江。
entries.en: On renzi, he stopped at Pingjiang.
entries.literal: Day renzi: he halted at Pingjiang.

entries.zh: 罷督視府。
entries.en: The Supervisory Office was abolished.
entries.literal: The Supervisory Office was abolished.

entries.zh: 虞允文還至鎮江。
entries.en: Yu Yunwen returned to Zhenjiang.
entries.literal: Yu Yunwen returned to Zhenjiang.

entries.zh: 癸丑，淮東統制劉銳、陳敏引兵入泗州。
entries.en: On guichou, Huai east controllers Liu Rui and Chen Min entered Si prefecture.
entries.literal: Day guichou: Huai east controllers Liu Rui and Chen Min led troops into Si prefecture.

entries.zh: 鄂州統制楊欽以舟師追敗金人于洪澤鎮。
entries.en: Ezhou controller Yang Qin's fleet pursued and beat the Jin at Hongze town.
entries.literal: Ezhou controller Yang Qin with a fleet pursued and defeated the Jin at Hongze town.

entries.zh: 乙卯，江北金兵盡去，李顯忠復入和州。
entries.en: On yimao, north-of-river Jin forces were gone; Li Xianzhong re-entered He prefecture.
entries.literal: Day yimao: Jin troops north of the river were all gone; Li Xianzhong re-entered He prefecture.

entries.zh: 吳璘遣將復水洛城。
entries.en: Wu Lin sent generals to retake Shuiluo city.
entries.literal: Wu Lin sent generals to recover Shuiluo city.

entries.zh: 金人復破汝州，牛宏敗走。
entries.en: The Jin retook Ru prefecture; Niu Hong was routed and fled.
entries.literal: The Jin again took Ru prefecture; Niu Hong was beaten and fled.

entries.zh: 戊午，次鎮江府。
entries.en: On wuwu, he stopped at Zhenjiang.
entries.literal: Day wuwu: he halted at Zhenjiang prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚申，吳璘遣將拔金人治平砦。
entries.en: On gengshen, Wu Lin's generals stormed the Jin Zhiping fort.
entries.literal: Day gengshen: Wu Lin sent generals to storm the Jin's Zhiping fort.

entries.zh: 壬戌，曲赦新復州軍。
entries.en: On renxu, newly recovered prefectures and armies received a partial pardon.
entries.literal: Day renxu: newly recovered prefectures and armies received a partial amnesty.

entries.zh: 甲子，降淮南、京西、湖北雜犯死罪以下囚。
entries.en: On jiazi, death sentences and lesser crimes in Huainan, Jing west, and Hubei were commuted.
entries.literal: Day jiazi: death sentences and below for miscellaneous offenses in Huainan, Jing west, and Hubei were reduced.

entries.zh: 賞採石功，進統制張振、時俊等官。
entries.en: Caishi victors were rewarded; controllers Zhang Zhen, Shi Jun, and others were promoted.
entries.literal: Caishi merit was rewarded; controllers Zhang Zhen, Shi Jun, and others were advanced in rank.

entries.zh: 金潁、壽二州巡檢高顯以壽春府來降。
entries.en: Jin patrol inspectors Gao Xian of Ying and Shou surrendered Shouchun prefecture.
entries.literal: Jin patrol inspectors Gao Xian of Ying and Shou prefectures surrendered Shouchun prefecture.

entries.zh: 丁卯，命諸道籍鄉兵。
entries.en: On dingmao, every route was told to register militia.
entries.literal: Day dingmao: every route was ordered to register militia.

entries.zh: 初，王友直、王任聚兵，嘗命友直為天雄軍節度使，任為天平軍節度使。
entries.en: Earlier Wang Youzhi and Wang Ren had raised forces; Youzhi was made Tianxiong commissioner and Ren Tianping commissioner.
entries.literal: Earlier Wang Youzhi and Wang Ren had gathered troops; Youzhi had been made military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army and Ren of the Tianping Army.

entries.zh: 金主褒既立，下令散其眾，友直等自壽春來歸。
entries.en: After Jin Emperor Shizong enthroned, he ordered their bands broken up; Youzhi and others came in from Shouchun.
entries.literal: After Jin Emperor Shizong took the throne, he ordered their bands dispersed; Youzhi and the rest came in from Shouchun.

entries.zh: 是月，金主知亮已死，遂趨燕京。
entries.en: That month, learning Hailing was dead, the Jin emperor hurried to Yanjing.
entries.literal: That month, learning Hailing was dead, the Jin ruler hurried to Yanjing.

entries.zh: 二月戊戌朔，罷借兩浙、江、淮坊場淨利錢。
entries.en: Second month, wuxu new moon: borrowing against Zhe, Jiang, and Huai licensed-shop profits was ended.
entries.literal: Second month, day wuxu new moon: borrowing against licensed-shop net profits in the two Zhe, Jiang, and Huai circuits was ended.

entries.zh: 以虞允文為兵部尚書、川陝宣諭使，措置招軍市馬及與吳璘議事。
entries.en: Yu Yunwen became Minister of War and Sichuan-Shaanxi commissioner to handle recruiting, horse buying, and affairs with Wu Lin.
entries.literal: Yu Yunwen was made Minister of War and Sichuan-Shaanxi commissioner for pacification, to handle recruiting, horse purchase, and affairs with Wu Lin.

entries.zh: 庚子，興州統領惠逢等復河州。
entries.en: On gengzi, Xing controller Hui Feng and others retook He prefecture.
entries.literal: Day gengzi: Xing prefecture controller Hui Feng and others recovered He prefecture.

entries.zh: 振兩淮饑民。
entries.en: Two-Huai famine victims were relieved.
entries.literal: Famine victims in the two Huai were relieved.

entries.zh: 壬寅，金人犯汝州，守將王宣逆戰，敗之。
entries.en: On renyin, the Jin struck Ru; defender Wang Xuan met them and won.
entries.literal: Day renyin: the Jin attacked Ru prefecture; defending commander Wang Xuan met them and defeated them.

entries.zh: 癸卯，帝發建康。
entries.en: On guimao, the emperor left Jiankang.
entries.literal: Day guimao: the Emperor set out from Jiankang.

entries.zh: 惠逢復積石軍，又克來羌城。
entries.en: Hui Feng retook Jishi army and also captured Laicang city.
entries.literal: Hui Feng recovered Jishi army and also took Laicang city.

entries.zh: 丁未，劉錡薨。
entries.en: On dingwei, Liu Qi died.
entries.literal: Day dingwei: Liu Qi died.

entries.zh: 己酉，王宣及金人再戰於汝州。
entries.en: On jiyou, Wang Xuan and the Jin fought again at Ru.
entries.literal: Day jiyou: Wang Xuan and the Jin fought again at Ru prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚戌，金人全師來攻，宣敗績，棄去。
entries.en: On gengxu, the Jin came in full strength; Xuan was routed and withdrew.
entries.literal: Day gengxu: the Jin came in full force; Xuan was beaten and withdrew.

entries.zh: 辛亥，金人復犯順昌府，孟新拒卻之，尋亦棄去。
entries.en: On xinhai, the Jin struck Shunchang again; Meng Xin beat them back and soon withdrew too.
entries.literal: Day xinhai: the Jin again attacked Shunchang prefecture; Meng Xin repelled them and soon withdrew as well.

entries.zh: 壬子，賞蔡州功，趙撙等進官有差。
entries.en: On renzi, Cai victors were rewarded; Zhao Zong and others were promoted by degrees.
entries.literal: Day renzi: Cai prefecture merit was rewarded; Zhao Zong and others were advanced in rank by degrees.

entries.zh: 乙卯，至臨安府。
entries.en: On yimao, he reached Lin'an.
entries.literal: Day yimao: he reached Lin'an prefecture.

entries.zh: 興元都統制姚仲攻鞏州不下，退守甘穀城，遂引兵圍德順軍。
entries.en: Xingyuan commander Yao Zhong failed to take Gong, fell back to Gangu city, and besieged Deshun army.
entries.literal: Xingyuan overall commander Yao Zhong attacked Gong prefecture without success, fell back to Gangu city, and then led troops to besiege Deshun army.

entries.zh: 丙辰，金人犯蔡州。
entries.en: On bingchen, the Jin attacked Cai prefecture.
entries.literal: Day bingchen: the Jin attacked Cai prefecture.

entries.zh: 趙撙擊卻之。
entries.en: Zhao Zong beat them back.
entries.literal: Zhao Zong struck and drove them off.

entries.zh: 戊午，復引兵來攻，撙又敗之，金兵遁去。
entries.en: On wuwu, they returned; Zong defeated them again and the Jin fled.
entries.literal: Day wuwu: they came again; Zong again defeated them and the Jin fled.

entries.zh: 王彥遣將馬貴斷河中南橋，金兵來攻，貴戰敗之。
entries.en: Wang Yan sent Ma Gui to cut the Yellow River's south bridge; the Jin attacked and Gui defeated them.
entries.literal: Wang Yan sent general Ma Gui to cut the south bridge on the Yellow River; the Jin came to attack and Gui defeated them.

entries.zh: 壬戌，詔軍士戰死者祿其家一年，傷重而死于營者半之。
entries.en: On renxu, families of soldiers killed in battle received one year's salary; half for those who died in camp of severe wounds.
entries.literal: Day renxu: an edict granted one year's salary to families of soldiers killed in battle; half for those who died in camp of severe wounds.

entries.zh: 乙丑，王宣及右軍副將汲靖敗金人于蔡州確山縣。
entries.en: On yichou, Wang Xuan and right-army deputy Ji Jing beat the Jin at Queshan in Cai.
entries.literal: Day yichou: Wang Xuan and right-army deputy Ji Jing defeated the Jin at Queshan county in Cai prefecture.

entries.zh: 趙撙棄蔡州。
entries.en: Zhao Zong abandoned Cai prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhao Zong abandoned Cai prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙寅，金人復取之。
entries.en: On bingyin, the Jin retook it.
entries.literal: Day bingyin: the Jin took it again.

entries.zh: 姚仲遣副將趙銓攻下鎮戎軍，金同知渭州秦弼及其子嵩來歸。
entries.en: Yao Zhong's deputy Zhao Quan took Zhenrong army; Jin acting Wei commissioner Qin Bi and his son Song defected.
entries.literal: Yao Zhong sent deputy Zhao Quan to take Zhenrong army; Jin acting Wei prefecture commissioner Qin Bi and his son Song came over.

entries.zh: 王彥遣兵救陝州，遇金人於虢州東，敗之，金兵引去。
entries.en: Wang Yan sent relief to Shan, met the Jin east of Guo, defeated them, and the Jin withdrew.
entries.literal: Wang Yan sent troops to relieve Shan prefecture, met the Jin east of Guo prefecture, defeated them, and the Jin withdrew.

entries.zh: 丁卯，吳珙遣將復永安軍、永寧、福昌、長水三縣。
entries.en: On dingmao, Wu Gong's generals retook Yong'an army and Yongning, Fuchang, and Changshui counties.
entries.literal: Day dingmao: Wu Gong sent generals to recover Yong'an army and the three counties Yongning, Fuchang, and Changshui.

entries.zh: 三月壬寅，更定金使入境接伴、館伴舊儀。
entries.en: Third month, renyin: the court revised the old protocol for welcoming and hosting Jin envoys on entry.
entries.literal: Third month, day renyin: the former protocol for welcoming and hosting Jin envoys entering the realm was revised.

entries.zh: 癸卯，成閔遣統制杜彥救淮甯，擊敗金人于項城縣。
entries.en: On guimao, Cheng Min sent Du Yan to relieve Huai'ning and beat the Jin at Xiangcheng.
entries.literal: Day guimao: Cheng Min sent controller Du Yan to relieve Huai'ning and defeated the Jin at Xiangcheng county.

entries.zh: 甲辰，罷扈從官吏賞典。
entries.en: On jiachen, reward grants to retinue officials were abolished.
entries.literal: Day jiachen: reward grants to officials of the imperial retinue were abolished.

entries.zh: 乙巳，錄商、虢之功，加吳璘少傅、王彥為保平軍節度使。
entries.en: On yisi, merits at Shang and Guo were recorded; Wu Lin was made junior mentor and Wang Yan Baoping military commissioner.
entries.literal: Day yisi: the merits at Shang and Guo were recorded; Wu Lin was advanced to junior mentor and Wang Yan was made Baoping military commissioner.

entries.zh: 戊申，吳璘復德順軍，又遣將嚴忠取環州。
entries.en: On wushen, Wu Lin recovered Deshun and sent Yan Zhong to take Huanzhou.
entries.literal: Day wushen: Wu Lin recovered Deshun army and also sent general Yan Zhong to take Huanzhou.

entries.zh: 辛亥，命兵部侍郎陳俊卿、工部侍郎許尹經畫兩淮堡砦屯田。
entries.en: On xinhai, Chen Junqing and Xu Yin were ordered to plan fortresses and garrison farms on both sides of the Huai.
entries.literal: Day xinhai: Vice Minister of War Chen Junqing and Vice Minister of Works Xu Yin were ordered to plan fortresses, stockades, and garrison farms on both sides of the Huai.

entries.zh: 癸丑，金人圍淮寧府，守臣陳亨祖死之。
entries.en: On guichou, the Jin besieged Huaining; defender Chen Hengzu was killed.
entries.literal: Day guichou: the Jin besieged Huaining prefecture; defender Chen Hengzu died in the defense.

entries.zh: 甲寅，吳璘自德順軍復還河池。
entries.en: On jiayin, Wu Lin returned from Deshun to Hechi.
entries.literal: Day jiayin: Wu Lin returned from Deshun army to Hechi.

entries.zh: 金人犯鎮戎軍。
entries.en: The Jin attacked Zhenrong.
entries.literal: The Jin attacked Zhenrong army.

entries.zh: 丁巳，遣洪邁等賀金主即位。
entries.en: On dingsi, Hong Mai and others were sent to congratulate the new Jin emperor on his accession.
entries.literal: Day dingsi: Hong Mai and others were sent to congratulate the Jin ruler on his accession.

entries.zh: 戊午，忠義軍統制、知蘭州王宏拔會州。
entries.en: On wuwu, Loyal-and-Righteous Army controller Wang Hong, prefect of Lanzhou, took Huizhou.
entries.literal: Day wuwu: Loyal-and-Righteous Army controller and Lanzhou prefect Wang Hong captured Huizhou.

entries.zh: 金人陷淮寧府，統領戴規戰死。
entries.en: The Jin took Huaining; commander Dai Gui was killed in battle.
entries.literal: The Jin took Huaining prefecture; commander Dai Gui died in battle.

entries.zh: 成閔歸自淮東。
entries.en: Cheng Min returned from east of the Huai.
entries.literal: Cheng Min returned from east of the Huai.

entries.zh: 辛酉，金人攻原州。
entries.en: On xinyou, the Jin attacked Yuan prefecture.
entries.literal: Day xinyou: the Jin attacked Yuan prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙寅，詔舉賢良。
entries.en: On bingyin, the court called for men of worth and excellence.
entries.literal: Day bingyin: an edict summoned men of worth and excellence.

entries.zh: 三十一年春正月甲戌朔，以日食，不受朝。
entries.en: Year 31, spring, jiaxu new moon: Gaozong canceled audience for the eclipse.
entries.literal: Thirty-first year, spring, first month, day jiaxu new moon: because of a solar eclipse, court audience was not held.

entries.zh: 丁丑，雷。
entries.en: On dingchou, thunder rolled.
entries.literal: Day dingchou: thunder.

entries.zh: 丁亥，免湖州增丁所輸絹。
entries.en: On dinghai, Huzhou was freed from added-household silk levies.
entries.literal: Day dinghai: the silk paid by Huzhou for added registered households was remitted.

entries.zh: 夜，風雷雨雪交作。
entries.en: That night wind, thunder, snow, and rain came together.
entries.literal: At night, wind, thunder, snow, and rain struck together.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔江、浙官民戶均輸和市絁帛。
entries.en: On xinmao, Jiang and Zhe were told to share silk transport and market purchases equally among official and common households.
entries.literal: Day xinmao: an edict ordered official and common households of Jiang and Zhe to share equally in transport and market purchase of silk.

entries.zh: 壬辰，劉寶落節鉞、福建路居住。
entries.en: On renchen, Liu Bao lost his command tally and was sent to live on the Fujian circuit.
entries.literal: Day renchen: Liu Bao was stripped of his command tally and made to reside on the Fujian circuit.

entries.zh: 丙申，大雨雪，給三衙衛士、行在貧民錢及薪炭，命常平振給輔郡細民，諸路監司決獄。
entries.en: On bingchen, heavy snow brought cash and charcoal to palace guards and capital poor; Ever-Normal stores fed nearby counties; commissioners judged cases.
entries.literal: Day bingchen: in great rain and snow, money and fuel were given to the Three Yamaz guards and poor people at the mobile court; the Ever-Normal Granaries were ordered to relieve needy folk in auxiliary commanderies; circuit commissioners were to decide cases.

entries.zh: 己亥，放張浚、胡銓自便。
entries.en: On jihai, Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were freed to their own devices.
entries.literal: Day jihai: Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were released to go as they pleased.

entries.zh: 庚子，禁淮南拘籍戶馬。
entries.en: On gengzi, Huainan could no longer seize and register civilian horses.
entries.literal: Day gengzi: Huainan was forbidden to seize and register household horses.

entries.zh: 至道六年，修昭应宫，有木断之，文如点漆，贯彻上下，体若梵书。
entries.en: In Zhidao 6 (1000), during repairs to Zhaoying Palace, workers split a timber whose grain appeared as jet-black lacquer tracery running the full length of the log, shaped like Indic script.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhidao, while repairing Zhaoying Palace, a piece of wood was cut; its markings were like dots of lacquer, running through it top to bottom, in form like Brahmi script.

entries.zh: 十一月，襄州民刘士家生木。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, timber sprouted inside the house of Liu Shi, a man of Xiang Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, wood grew at the home of the commoner Liu Shi in Xiang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 有文如龙、鱼、凤、鹤之状。
entries.en: The grain formed patterns resembling dragons, fish, phoenixes, and cranes.
entries.literal: It bore markings in the shapes of dragons, fish, phoenixes, and cranes.

entries.zh: 七年五月，抚州修天庆观，解木有文如墨画云气、峰峦、人物、衣冠之状。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the seventh year (1001), as Tianqing Abbey in Fuzhou was being restored, a log that was split open showed markings like ink-wash clouds, mountain ranges, figures, and court dress.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, while repairing Tianqing Abbey in Fuzhou, split wood bore markings like ink paintings of clouds, peaks, human figures, and caps and robes.

entries.zh: 七月，彰明县崇仙观柱有文为道士形及北斗七星象。
entries.en: In the seventh month, a column at Chongxian Abbey in Zhangming County displayed grain patterns shaped like a Daoist adept and the Big Dipper.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, a pillar at Chongxian Abbey in Zhangming County bore markings in the form of a Daoist priest and the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper.

entries.zh: 文章還沒有進行過校對和格式化，或文章還不全，不能保證任何部分可靠。
entries.en: This text has not been proofread or fully formatted, and portions may still be missing; nothing in it should be treated as authoritative.
entries.literal: The article has not yet undergone proofreading and formatting, or the article is still incomplete; no part can be guaranteed reliable.

entries.zh: 堯敕羲和制橫簫以考察星度，其機衡用玉，欲其燥濕不變，運動有常，堅久而不能廢也。
entries.en: Yao charged Xihe with fashioning transverse sight-tubes to measure the stars, and had the mechanisms and pivots made of jade so they would not warp with damp or dryness, would move evenly, and would endure firm and unchanging for long use.
entries.literal: Yao commanded Xihe to make transverse sight-tubes to examine the degrees of the stars; its mechanisms and pivots used jade, wishing that dryness and moisture would not alter it, that motion would have constancy, and that it would be firm and long-lasting and could not be discarded.

entries.zh: 至於後世，鑄銅為圓儀，以法天體。
entries.en: In later ages, bronze was cast into a spherical instrument to represent the celestial sphere.
entries.literal: As for later generations, they cast copper into a spherical instrument to model the heavenly body.

entries.zh: 自洛下閎造《太初曆》，用渾儀，及東漢孝和帝時，太史惟有赤道儀，歲時測候，頗有進退。
entries.en: From Luoxia Hong's compilation of the Taichu Calendar with the armillary sphere down to the Eastern Han Emperor He, the Grand Astrologer's office possessed only an equatorial instrument, and its seasonal observations drifted noticeably.
entries.literal: From when Luoxia Hong made the Taichu Calendar and used the armillary sphere, until the time of Emperor Xiaohe of the Eastern Han, the Grand Astrologer had only an equatorial instrument; seasonal measurements and observations had considerable advance and retreat.

entries.zh: 帝以問典星待詔姚崇等，皆曰：「星圖有規法，日月實從黃道，今無其器，是以失之。」
entries.en: The emperor asked the awaited-edict astrologers Yao Chong and others, and they all replied: "The star chart follows fixed rules, and the sun and moon truly travel the ecliptic; because we lack the proper instrument today, our readings go astray."
entries.literal: The emperor inquired of the Palace Star Awaited-Edict Yao Chong and others; all said: "The star chart has regulated methods; sun and moon in fact follow the Yellow Path; now we lack its instrument, and for this reason we have missed it."

entries.zh: 至永元十五年，賈逵始設黃道儀。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year of Yongyuan (103 CE), Jia Kui first installed an ecliptic instrument.
entries.literal: By the fifteenth year of Yongyuan, Jia Kui first set up an ecliptic instrument.

entries.zh: 桓帝延熹七年，張衡更制之，以四分為度。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yanxi (164 CE) under Emperor Huan, Zhang Heng redesigned it, using quarter-degrees as the unit.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yanxi under Emperor Huan, Zhang Heng remade it, taking one quarter as a degree.

entries.zh: 其後，陸績、王蕃、孔挺、斛蘭、梁令瓚、李淳風並嘗製作。
entries.en: Later, Lu Ji, Wang Fan, Kong Ting, Hu Lan, Liang Lingzan, and Li Chunfeng each produced instruments of their own.
entries.literal: Afterward, Lu Ji, Wang Fan, Kong Ting, Hu Lan, Liang Lingzan, and Li Chunfeng all at times made versions.

entries.zh: 五代亂亡，遺法蕩然矣。
entries.en: The turmoil and collapse of the Five Dynasties swept away the transmitted methods entirely.
entries.literal: The Five Dynasties fell in disorder and ruin, and the transmitted methods were utterly swept away.

entries.zh: 真宗祥符初，韓顯符作渾儀，但遊儀雙環夾望筒旋轉，而黃、赤道相固不動。
entries.en: Early in the Xiangfu era under Emperor Zhenzong, Han Xianfu built an armillary sphere in which only the pivoting rings gripping the sight-tube could turn, while the ecliptic and equatorial rings remained fixed.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiangfu under Emperor Zhenzong, Han Xianfu made an armillary sphere, but only the pivoting instrument's double rings clamping the sight-tube rotated, while the Yellow Path and equator rings were fixed and did not move.

entries.zh: 皇祐初，又命日官舒易簡、于淵、周琮等參用淳風、令瓚之制，改鑄黃道渾儀，又為漏刻、圭表，詔翰林學士錢明逸詳其法，內侍麥允言總其工。
entries.en: Early in the Huangyou era, the court again ordered the solar officials Shu Yijian, Yu Yuan, and Zhou Cong to draw on the designs of Li Chunfeng and Liang Lingzan, recast an ecliptic armillary sphere, and also build clepsydra graduations and a gnomon table; Hanlin Academician Qian Mingyi was directed to work out the methods, and Inner Attendant Mai Yunyan to supervise construction.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou, the court again ordered the solar officials Shu Yijian, Yu Yuan, Zhou Cong, and others to consult the designs of Chunfeng and Lingzan, recast an ecliptic armillary sphere, and also make clepsydra graduations and a gnomon table; an edict directed Hanlin Academician Qian Mingyi to elaborate the methods, and Inner Attendant Mai Yunyan to oversee the work.

entries.zh: 既成，置渾儀于翰林天文院之候台，漏刻於文德殿之鐘鼓樓，圭表于司天監。
entries.en: When they were finished, the armillary sphere was installed on the observation terrace of the Hanlin Astronomical Bureau, the clepsydra in the bell-and-drum tower of Wende Hall, and the gnomon table at the Directorate of Astronomy.
entries.literal: When completed, the armillary sphere was placed on the observation terrace of the Hanlin Astronomical Bureau, the clepsydra graduations in the bell-and-drum tower of Wende Hall, and the gnomon table at the Directorate of Astronomy.

entries.zh: 帝為制《渾儀總要》十卷，論前代得失，已而留中不出。
entries.en: The emperor drafted Essentials of the Armillary Sphere in ten scrolls, reviewing what earlier ages had done well or poorly, but afterward kept the work in the palace archives and never published it.
entries.literal: The emperor composed Essentials of the Armillary Sphere in ten scrolls, discussing the gains and losses of former ages, but afterward kept it within the palace and did not release it.

entries.zh: 今具黃道遊儀之法，著於此焉。
entries.en: The methods of the ecliptic pivoting instrument are set forth in full below.
entries.literal: Now the methods of the ecliptic pivoting instrument are set forth in full and recorded here.

entries.zh: 皇祐渾儀
entries.en: The Huangyou Armillary Sphere
entries.literal: Huangyou Armillary Sphere

entries.zh: 詔令禮官再議。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the ritual officials to deliberate again.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the ritual officials to deliberate again.

entries.zh: 禮官言：「按《祭統》曰：『祭有昭、穆者，所以別父子遠近長幼親疏之序而無亂也。』
entries.en: The ritual officials replied: "The Record of Sacrifices states that sacrifices employ zhao and mu to distinguish the order of father and son, near and far, elder and younger, close and distant, without confusion.
entries.literal: The ritual officials stated: "According to the Record of Sacrifices: 'Sacrifices have zhao and mu in order to distinguish the order of father and son, near and far, elder and younger, close and distant, without confusion.

entries.zh: 《公羊傳》，公孫嬰齊為兄歸父之後，《春秋》謂之仲嬰 齊。
entries.en: The Gongyang Commentary notes that Gongsun Yingqi became heir to his elder brother Gui Fu; the Spring and Autumn Annals calls him Zhong Yingqi.
entries.literal: The Gongyang Commentary: Gongsun Yingqi became heir to his elder brother Gui Fu; the Spring and Autumn Annals calls him Zhong Yingqi.

entries.zh: 何休云：『弟無後兄之義，為亂昭穆之序，失父子之親，故不言仲孫，明不以子為父孫。』
entries.en: He Xiu explains that a younger brother has no right to succeed an elder brother—it disrupts zhao-mu and loses the father-son bond; hence the text does not say Zhongsun, making clear that a son is not treated as father and grandson."
entries.literal: He Xiu says: 'A younger brother has no right to succeed an elder brother—it disrupts the zhao-mu order and loses the intimacy of father and son; hence it does not say Zhong Sun, making clear that one does not treat a son as father and grandson.'"

entries.zh: 晉賀循議兄弟不合繼位昭穆云：『商人六廟，親廟四，並契、湯而 六，比有兄弟四人相襲為君者，便當上毀四廟乎？
entries.en: Jin He Xun argued that brothers should not succeed in zhao-mu positions: 'The Shang had six temples—four direct-line plus Qi and Tang. If four brothers ruled in succession, should the four upper temples be destroyed?
entries.literal: Jin He Xun, deliberating that brothers should not succeed in zhao-mu positions, said: 'The Shang had six temples, four direct-line temples together with Qi and Tang—six in all. If four brothers succeeded one another as rulers, should the four temples above be destroyed?

entries.zh: 如此，四世之親盡，無復祖禰之神矣。』
entries.en: If so, affection for four generations would be exhausted and the spirits of ancestors and fathers would be lost.
entries.literal: If so, affection for four generations would be exhausted, and there would be no more spirits of ancestors and fathers.

entries.zh: 溫嶠議兄弟相繼、藏主夾室之事云：『若以一帝為一世，則當不得祭於 禰，乃不及庶人之祭也。』
entries.en: Wen Qiao, on brotherly succession and storing tablets in flanking chambers, argued: 'If each emperor counts as one generation, one could not sacrifice to one's father—falling short even of a commoner's rites.'"
entries.literal: Wen Jiao, deliberating on brotherly succession and storing tablets in flanking chambers, said: 'If each emperor counts as one generation, then one could not sacrifice to one's father—falling short even of a commoner's sacrifices.'"

entries.zh: 夫兄弟同世，於恩既順，於義無否。
entries.en: Brothers in the same generation accord with affection and violate no principle of right.
entries.literal: Brothers in the same generation accord with affection and violate no principle of right.

entries.zh: 玄宗朝禘袷，皇伯考中宗、皇考睿宗同列於穆位。
entries.en: At the di and xia sacrifices under Xuanzong, Imperial Elder Uncle Zhongzong and Imperial Father Ruizong were ranked together in the mu position.
entries.literal: At the di and xia sacrifices in Xuanzong's reign, Imperial Elder Uncle Zhongzong and Imperial Father Ruizong were ranked together in the mu position.

entries.zh: 德宗亦以中宗為高伯祖。
entries.en: Dezong likewise addressed Zhongzong as great-great-grand elder uncle.
entries.literal: Dezong likewise addressed Zhongzong as great-great-grand elder uncle.

entries.zh: 晉王導、荀崧議『大宗無 子，則立支子』，又曰『為人後者為之子』，無兄弟相為之文。
entries.en: Jin Wang Dao and Xun Song held that if the major line has no son, a branch son is established, and that an heir is treated as a son—nowhere do they authorize brother succeeding brother.
entries.literal: Jin Wang Dao and Xun Song deliberated: 'If the major line has no son, establish a branch son,' and also said 'one who becomes another's heir is considered his son'—there is no text on brothers succeeding one another.

entries.zh: 所以舍至親取遠屬者，蓋以兄弟一體，無父子之道故也。
entries.en: They set aside the closest kin for a distant collateral because brothers are one body and lack the father-son bond.
entries.literal: The reason for setting aside the closest kin and taking a distant collateral was that brothers are one body and lack the way of father and son.

entries.zh: 竊以七廟之制，百王是尊。
entries.en: The seven-temple system has been honored by a hundred kings.
entries.literal: We hold that the system of seven temples is honored by a hundred kings.

entries.zh: 至於祖有功，宗 有德，則百世不遷之廟也；
entries.en: Zu honors merit and zong honors virtue—these are shrines never moved for a hundred generations;
entries.literal: As for 'zu honors merit, zong honors virtue'—these are temples never moved for a hundred generations;

entries.zh: 父為昭，子為穆，則千古不刊之典也。
entries.en: father as zhao, son as mu—this is the canon never altered for a thousand ages.
entries.literal: father as zhao, son as mu—this is the canon never altered for a thousand ages.

entries.zh: 今議者引《漢書》曰：『為人後者為之子。』
entries.en: Those who argue now cite the Book of Han: 'One who becomes another's heir is considered his son.'
entries.literal: Those who deliberate now cite the Book of Han: 'One who becomes another's heir is considered his son.'

entries.zh: 殊不知弟不為兄後，子不為父孫，《春秋》之深旨。
entries.en: They overlook the Spring and Autumn Annals' deep teaching: a younger brother does not succeed an elder brother, and a son is not father and grandson.
entries.literal: They do not realize that a younger brother does not succeed an elder brother, and a son is not father and grandson—the deep purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

entries.zh: 父謂之昭，子謂之穆，《禮記》之明文也。
entries.en: Father is called zhao, son is called mu—the explicit text of the Record of Rites.
entries.literal: Father is called zhao, son is called mu—the explicit text of the Record of Rites.

entries.zh: 又按太宗享祀太祖二十有二載，稱曰『孝弟』，此不易之制，又安可追改乎？
entries.en: Moreover, Taizong sacrificed to Taizu for twenty-two years as 'Filial Younger Brother'—an established institution that cannot be retroactively altered.
entries.literal: Moreover, Taizong sacrificed to Taizu for twenty-two years, styled 'Filial Younger Brother'—this is an unchanging institution; how can it be retroactively altered?

entries.zh: 唐玄宗謂中宗為皇伯考，德宗謂中宗為高伯 祖，則伯氏之稱，復何不可？
entries.en: Tang Xuanzong called Zhongzong Imperial Elder Uncle; Dezong called him great-great-grand elder uncle—why then cannot the address of elder uncle be used?
entries.literal: Tang Xuanzong called Zhongzong Imperial Elder Uncle; Dezong called Zhongzong great-great-grand elder uncle—why then cannot the address of elder uncle be used?

entries.zh: 臣等參議：自今合祭日，太祖、太宗依典禮同位異坐，皇帝於太祖仍稱孝子，餘並遵舊制。」
entries.en: We jointly recommend: at combined sacrifices from this day forward, Taizu and Taizong shall share the same position with separate seats per canonical ritual; the emperor before Taizu shall still be styled Filial Son; all else shall follow former regulations."
entries.literal: We ministers jointly deliberate: from this day at combined sacrifices, Taizu and Taizong shall follow canonical ritual in the same position with separate seats; the emperor before Taizu shall still be styled Filial Son; all else shall follow the former regulations."

entries.zh: 景德元年，有司詳定明德皇太后李氏升祔之禮：「按唐睿宗昭成、肅明二後，先天初，以昭成配；開元末，以肅明祔。
entries.en: In the first year of Jingde, the responsible offices carefully fixed the rite for raising and enshrining Empress Dowager Mingde, Lady Li: “Examining the Tang case of Emperor Ruizong’s two empresses, Zhaocheng and Suming, at the beginning of Xiantian Zhaocheng was made consort; at the end of Kaiyuan, Suming was enshrined.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingde, the responsible offices carefully fixed the rite for raising and enshrining Empress Dowager Mingde, Lady Li: “Examining the Tang case of Emperor Ruizong’s two empresses, Zhaocheng and Suming, at the beginning of Xiantian Zhaocheng was made consort; at the end of Kaiyuan, Suming was enshrined.

entries.zh: 此時儒官名臣，步武相接，宗廟重事，必有據依。
entries.en: At that time Confucian officials and eminent ministers followed one another closely; in such a weighty matter of the ancestral temple, there must have been grounds and precedent.
entries.literal: At that time Confucian officials and eminent ministers followed one another closely; in such a weighty matter of the ancestral temple, there must have been grounds and precedent.

entries.zh: 推之閨門，亦可擬議。
entries.en: Extending this to matters of the inner chambers, it may also be used for deliberation.
entries.literal: Extending this to matters of the inner chambers, it may also be used for deliberation.

entries.zh: 晉驃騎將軍溫嶠有三夫人，嶠薨，詔問學官陳舒。
entries.en: Jin General of Agile Cavalry Wen Qiao had three wives; when Qiao died, an edict asked the scholar-official Chen Shu.
entries.literal: Jin General of Agile Cavalry Wen Qiao had three wives; when Qiao died, an edict asked the scholar-official Chen Shu.

entries.zh: 舒謂秦、漢之後，廢一娶九女之制，妻卒更娶，無復繼室，生既加禮，亡不應貶。
entries.en: Shu said that after Qin and Han, the system by which one marriage took nine women had been abolished; when a wife died and another was married, there was no longer a “successor wife.” Since rites had been added for her in life, she should not be demoted in death.
entries.literal: Shu said that after Qin and Han, the system by which one marriage took nine women had been abolished; when a wife died and another was married, there was no longer a “successor wife.” Since rites had been added for her in life, she should not be demoted in death.

entries.zh: 朝旨以李氏卒於嶠之微時，不沾贈典；王、何二氏追加章綬。
entries.en: The court decision held that Lady Li had died when Qiao was still humble and so did not receive the statutes of posthumous grant; Ladies Wang and He were later additionally granted insignia and ribbons.
entries.literal: The court decision held that Lady Li had died when Qiao was still humble and so did not receive the statutes of posthumous grant; Ladies Wang and He were later additionally granted insignia and ribbons.

entries.zh: 唐太子少傅鄭餘慶將立家廟，祖有二夫人。
entries.en: When Tang Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Zheng Yuqing was about to establish a family temple, his ancestor had two wives.
entries.literal: When Tang Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Zheng Yuqing was about to establish a family temple, his ancestor had two wives.

entries.zh: 禮官韋公肅議與舒同。
entries.en: The ritual official Wei Gongsu’s opinion was the same as Shu’s.
entries.literal: The ritual official Wei Gongsu’s opinion was the same as Shu’s.

entries.zh: 略稽禮文，參諸故事，二夫人並祔，於理為宜。
entries.en: Briefly examining the ritual texts and comparing the precedents, joint enshrinement of the two wives is appropriate in principle.
entries.literal: Briefly examining the ritual texts and comparing the precedents, joint enshrinement of the two wives is appropriate in principle.

entries.zh: 恭惟懿德皇后久從升祔，雖先後有殊，在尊親則一，請同列太宗室，以先後次之。」
entries.en: We reverently consider that Empress Yide has long been raised and enshrined; although there is a distinction of earlier and later, in honoring kin they are one. We request that she be placed together in Taizong’s chamber, ordered by earlier and later.”
entries.literal: We reverently consider that Empress Yide has long been raised and enshrined; although there is a distinction of earlier and later, in honoring kin they are one. We request that she be placed together in Taizong’s chamber, ordered by earlier and later.”

entries.zh: 詔尚書省集議，咸如禮官之請，祔神主於太廟。
entries.en: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene deliberation; all agreed with the ritual officials’ request, and the spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene deliberation; all agreed with the ritual officials’ request, and the spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 嘉祐年，仁宗將 祔廟，修奉太廟使蔡襄上八室圖，為十八間。
entries.en: During the Jiayou period, as Renzong was about to be enshrined, Cai Xiang, commissioner for the ancestral temple, submitted a plan for eight chambers in eighteen bays.
entries.literal: In the Jiayou period, when Renzong was about to be enshrined in the temple, Cai Xiang, commissioner for maintaining the Imperial Ancestral Temple, submitted a diagram of eight chambers totaling eighteen bays.

entries.zh: 初，禮院請增廟室，孫抃等以為：「七世之廟，據父子而言，兄弟則昭、穆同，不得以世數之。
entries.en: Initially the Court of Ritual requested additional chambers. Sun Bian and others argued: "The seven-generation temple is reckoned by father and son; brothers share zhao and mu and should not be reckoned by generation number.
entries.literal: Initially the Court of Ritual requested additional temple chambers. Sun Bian and others held: "The temple of seven generations is reckoned by father and son; brothers share the same zhao and mu and should not be reckoned by generation number.

entries.zh: 廟有始祖、有太祖、有 太宗、有中宗。
entries.en: Temples distinguish a founding ancestor, a Grand Ancestor, a Great Ancestor, and a Central Ancestor.
entries.literal: Temples have a founding ancestor, a Grand Ancestor, a Great Ancestor, and a Central Ancestor.

entries.zh: 若以一君為一世，則小乙之祭不及其父。
entries.en: If each ruler counts as one generation, Xiao Yi's sacrifices would not reach his father.
entries.literal: If each ruler counts as one generation, then Xiao Yi's sacrifices would not reach his father.

entries.zh: 故晉之廟十一室而六世，唐之廟十一室而九世。
entries.en: Hence Jin's temple had eleven chambers spanning six generations; Tang's had eleven chambers spanning nine.
entries.literal: Hence Jin's temple had eleven chambers for six generations; Tang's temple had eleven chambers for nine generations.

entries.zh: 國朝太祖之室，太宗稱孝弟，真宗稱孝子，大行稱孝孫。
entries.en: In our dynasty, at Taizu's shrine Taizong was styled Filial Younger Brother, Zhenzong Filial Son, and the late emperor Filial Grandson.
entries.literal: In our dynasty's Taizu shrine, Taizong was styled Filial Younger Brother, Zhenzong Filial Son, and the late emperor Filial Grandson.

entries.zh: 而 《禘袷圖》：太祖、太宗同居昭位，南向；
entries.en: Yet the Diagram of Di and Xia Sacrifices shows Taizu and Taizong sharing the zhao position, facing south;
entries.literal: Yet the Diagram of Di and Xia Sacrifices shows Taizu and Taizong sharing the zhao position, facing south;

entries.zh: 真宗居穆位，北向。
entries.en: with Zhenzong in the mu position, facing north.
entries.literal: Zhenzong in the mu position, facing north.

entries.zh: 蓋先朝稽用古禮，著之祀典。
entries.en: The former court had examined ancient ritual and recorded it in the sacrificial canon.
entries.literal: The former court examined and applied ancient ritual, recording it in the sacrificial canon.

entries.zh: 大行神主祔廟，請增為八室，以備天子事七世之禮。」
entries.en: When the late emperor's tablet is installed, we request expansion to eight chambers to fulfill the Son of Heaven's rite of seven generations."
entries.literal: When the late emperor's spirit tablet is installed in the temple, we request expansion to eight chambers to fulfill the Son of Heaven's rite of serving seven generations."

entries.zh: 盧士宗、司馬光 以為：「太祖已上之主，雖屬尊於太祖，親盡則遷。
entries.en: Lu Shizong and Sima Guang argued: "Lords above Taizu, though senior in rank, are moved when affection is exhausted.
entries.literal: Lu Shizong and Sima Guang held: "The lords above Taizu, though senior to Taizu in rank, are moved when affection is exhausted.

entries.zh: 故漢元之世，太上廟主瘞於寢園；
entries.en: In Emperor Yuan of Han's time, Supreme Temple tablets were buried in the rest-hall garden;
entries.literal: Hence in Emperor Yuan of Han's time, the Supreme Temple tablets were buried in the rest-hall garden;

entries.zh: 魏明之世，處士廟主遷於園邑；
entries.en: in Emperor Ming of Wei's time, Commoner Temple tablets were moved to the garden settlement;
entries.literal: in Emperor Ming of Wei's time, the Commoner Temple tablets were moved to the garden settlement;

entries.zh: 晉武祔廟，遷征西府君；
entries.en: when Emperor Wu of Jin enshrined tablets, the Lord of the Western Campaign was moved;
entries.literal: when Emperor Wu of Jin enshrined tablets, Lord of the Western Campaign was moved;

entries.zh: 惠帝祔廟，遷豫章府 君。
entries.en: when Emperor Hui enshrined tablets, the Lord of Yuzhang was moved.
entries.literal: when Emperor Hui enshrined tablets, Lord of Yuzhang Prefecture was moved.

entries.zh: 自是以下，大抵過六世則遷。
entries.en: From this point onward, generally beyond six generations tablets were moved.
entries.literal: From this downward, generally beyond six generations there was movement.

entries.zh: 蓋太祖未正東向，故上祀三昭三穆；
entries.en: Because the Grand Ancestor had not yet faced east, three zhao and three mu were sacrificed above;
entries.literal: Because the Grand Ancestor had not yet faced east, three zhao and three mu were sacrificed to above;

entries.zh: 巳正東向，則並昭、穆為七世。
entries.en: once he faced east, zhao and mu together constituted seven generations.
entries.literal: once he faced east, zhao and mu together made seven generations.

entries.zh: 唐初祀四世，太宗增祀六世。
entries.en: Early Tang sacrificed to four generations; Taizong increased it to six.
entries.literal: Early Tang sacrificed to four generations; Taizong increased sacrifice to six generations.

entries.zh: 及太宗祔廟，則遷弘農府君，高 宗祔廟，又遷宣帝，皆祀六世，前世成法也。
entries.en: When Taizong was enshrined, the Lord of Hongnong was moved; when Gaozong was enshrined, Emperor Xuan was moved again—all sacrificing to six generations, the established law of former ages.
entries.literal: When Taizong was enshrined, Lord of Hongnong was moved; when Gaozong was enshrined, Emperor Xuan was moved again—all sacrificing to six generations, the established law of former ages.

entries.zh: 玄宗立九室祀八世，事不經見。
entries.en: Xuanzong established nine chambers for eight generations—a practice without precedent.
entries.literal: Xuanzong established nine chambers to sacrifice to eight generations—a practice without precedent.

entries.zh: 若以太祖、太宗為一世，則大行祔廟，僖祖親盡，當遷夾室，祀三昭三穆，於先王典禮 及近世之制，無不符合。」
entries.en: If Taizu and Taizong count as one generation, when the late emperor is enshrined Xizu's affection is exhausted and he should move to a flanking chamber, sacrificing to three zhao and three mu—in full accord with ancient canonical ritual and recent practice."
entries.literal: If Taizu and Taizong count as one generation, then when the late emperor is enshrined, Xizu's affection is exhausted and he should be moved to a flanking chamber, sacrificing to three zhao and three mu—in ancient kings' canonical ritual and recent practice, nothing would fail to accord."

entries.zh: 抃等復議曰：「自唐至周，廟製不同，而皆七世。
entries.en: Bian and others rebutted: "From the Tang to the Later Zhou, temple systems differed, yet all maintained seven generations.
entries.literal: Bian and others rebutted: "From the Tang to the Later Zhou, temple systems differed, yet all had seven generations.

entries.zh: 自周以上，所謂太祖，非始受命之主，特始封之君而已。
entries.en: Before Zhou, Grand Ancestor meant not the first to receive the Mandate but merely the first enfeoffed lord.
entries.literal: Before Zhou, what was called Grand Ancestor was not the first to receive the Mandate but merely the first enfeoffed lord.

entries.zh: 今僖祖雖非始封之君，要為立 廟之祖，方廟數未過七世，遂毀其廟，遷其主，考之三代，禮未有此。
entries.en: Although Xizu was not the first enfeoffed lord, he is the ancestor who established the temple. The count has not yet exceeded seven generations, yet his temple would be destroyed and his tablet moved—nothing like this appears in the Three Dynasties.
entries.literal: Now although Xizu was not the first enfeoffed lord, he is nonetheless the ancestor who established the temple. The temple count has not yet exceeded seven generations, yet his temple is destroyed and his tablet moved—examining the Three Dynasties, ritual never had this.

entries.zh: 漢、魏及唐一時之議，恐未合先王制禮之意。」
entries.en: The deliberations of Han, Wei, and Tang at particular moments likely do not accord with the former kings' intent in establishing ritual."
entries.literal: The deliberations of Han, Wei, and Tang at particular moments likely do not accord with the former kings' intent in establishing ritual."

entries.zh: 乃存僖祖室以備七室。
entries.en: Xizu's chamber was therefore retained to complete seven chambers.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xizu's chamber was retained to complete seven chambers.

entries.zh: 宗廟之制
entries.en: Regulations Governing the Imperial Ancestral Temples
entries.literal: Regulations on the Ancestral Temples

entries.zh: 禮官張洞、韓維言：「國朝每遇禘祫，奉別廟四後之主合食 太廟。
entries.en: Ritual officials Zhang Dong and Han Wei argued: "At each dì and xiá sacrifice, our dynasty brings the spirit tablets of the four empresses from their separate temples to share the communal feast in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: The ritual officials Zhang Dong and Han Wei stated: "Whenever our dynasty performs the dì or xiá offerings, the spirit tablets of the four empresses from the separate temples are brought to share the feast at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 唐《郊祀志》載禘祫祝文，自獻祖至肅宗所配皆一後，惟睿宗二後，蓋昭成，明皇母也。
entries.en: The Tang Record of Suburban Sacrifices lists the prayer texts for dì and xiá sacrifices: from Emperor Xianzu through Emperor Suzong, each emperor was paired with only one empress—Emperor Ruizong alone had two, Zhaocheng being the mother of Emperor Xuanzong.
entries.literal: The Tang Record of Suburban Sacrifices records the prayer texts for dì and xiá offerings: from Emperor Xianzu through Emperor Suzong, each was paired with a single empress—only Emperor Ruizong had two empresses, namely Zhaocheng, mother of Emperor Ming.

entries.zh: 《續曲台禮》有別廟皇后合食之文，蓋未有本室，遇祫享即祔祖姑 下。
entries.en: The Continued Rites of the Qu Terrace includes provisions for empresses of separate temples to share the communal feast—when they lacked their own shrine, they were placed below the founding ancestress at the xiá sacrifice.
entries.literal: The Continued Rites of the Qu Terrace contains passages on empresses from separate temples sharing the feast—because they had no shrine of their own, when a xiá offering occurred they were enshrined below the founding ancestress.

entries.zh: 所以大順中，三太后配列禘祭，議者議其非禮。
entries.en: When three empress dowagers were ranked together in a dì sacrifice during the Dashun era, critics condemned the practice as improper.
entries.literal: Therefore in the Dashun era, when three empress dowagers were ranked together in the dì sacrifice, deliberators criticized this as contrary to ritual.

entries.zh: 臣謂每室既有定配，則餘後不當參列，義當革正。」
entries.en: We hold that since each imperial shrine already has its designated consort, additional empresses should not be included in the array, and the practice ought to be corrected."
entries.literal: Your subjects hold that since each shrine already has its fixed pairing, the remaining empresses ought not to be included in the array—it is right to correct this."

entries.zh: 五年，吏部員外郎董弅言：「臣聞戎、祀，國之大事，而宗廟之祭，又祀之大者也。
entries.en: In the fifth year, Dong Bian, supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, stated: "I have heard that military affairs and sacrifices are great affairs of state, and ancestral temple sacrifice is the greatest among sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel Dong Bian stated: "I have heard that military affairs and sacrifices are great affairs of state, and sacrifice at the ancestral temple is the greatest among sacrifices.

entries.zh: 大祀，禘祫為重，祫大禘小，則袷為莫大焉。
entries.en: Among great sacrifices, dì and xiá are paramount; xiá is greater than dì, so the xiá is supreme.
entries.literal: Among great sacrifices, dì and xiá are paramount; xiá is greater than dì, so the xiá is the greatest of all.

entries.zh: 今戎事方殷，祭祀之禮未暇遍 舉，然事有違經戾古，上不當天地神祇之意，下未合億兆黎庶之心，特出於一時大臣好勝之臆說，而行之六十年未有知其非者。
entries.en: Now military affairs are pressing and sacrifices cannot all be performed; yet some practices violate the classics and antiquity, failing to satisfy Heaven, Earth, and the spirits above or the people below—arising solely from presumptuous theories of rival ministers, practiced for sixty years without recognition of error.
entries.literal: Now military affairs are pressing and the full round of sacrifices cannot be performed everywhere; yet there are matters that violate the classics and depart from antiquity, failing to satisfy Heaven, Earth, and the spirits above or the hearts of the myriad people below—arising solely from the presumptuous theories of chief ministers eager to prevail, practiced for sixty years without anyone recognizing their error.

entries.zh: 顧雖治兵禦戎之際，正厥違誤，宜不 可緩。
entries.en: Even while organizing armies and repelling invaders, correcting these errors ought not be delayed.
entries.literal: Even amid organizing armies and repelling invaders, to correct these errors ought not be delayed.

entries.zh: 仰惟太祖受天明命，混一區宇，即其功德所起，宜祇享以正東向之尊。
entries.en: Taizu received the Mandate of Heaven and unified the realm; considering where his merit began, he ought to receive the due dignity of the east-facing seat.
entries.literal: Reflect that Taizu received the Mandate of Heaven and unified the realm; considering where his merit began, he ought to be honored with the due dignity of the east-facing seat.

entries.zh: 逮至仁宗，親行祫享，嘗議太祖東向，用昭正統之緒。
entries.en: By Emperor Renzong's time, when he personally performed the xiá sacrifice, it was debated that Taizu should face east to clarify the legitimate succession.
entries.literal: By the time of Emperor Renzong, who personally performed the xiá sacrifice, it was once debated that Taizu should face east, thereby clarifying the legitimate succession.

entries.zh: 當時在廷之臣，僉謂自古必以受 命之祖乃居東向之位，本朝太祖乃受命之君，若論七廟之次，有僖祖以降四廟在上，當時大祫，止列昭穆而虛東向，蓋終不敢以非受命之祖而居之也。
entries.en: Court ministers then unanimously held that since antiquity only the ancestor who received the Mandate occupies the east-facing seat, and Taizu was our dynasty's recipient of the Mandate; yet with four temples above him from Emperor Xi onward, at the great xiá only zhao and mu were arrayed while the east-facing seat was left vacant—because they dared not seat one who had not received the Mandate there.
entries.literal: The ministers at court then unanimously said that since antiquity the ancestor who received the Mandate must occupy the east-facing seat; in our dynasty Taizu was the ruler who received the Mandate. If one considers the order of the seven temples, four temples from Emperor Xi upward stood above him; at the great xiá of that time, only the zhao and mu were arrayed while the east-facing seat was left vacant—because in the end they did not dare place one who had not received the Mandate in that seat.

entries.zh: 暨熙寧之初， 僖祖以世次當祧，禮官韓維等據經有請，適王安石用事，奮其臆說，乃俾章衡建議，尊僖祖為始祖，肇居東向。
entries.en: By the beginning of Xining, when Emperor Xi was due for removal by generational order, ritual officials including Han Wei petitioned on canonical grounds; Wang Anshi was then in power and pressed his private theory, causing Zhang Heng to propose honoring Emperor Xi as founding ancestor in the east-facing seat.
entries.literal: By the beginning of Xining, when Emperor Xi by generational order was due for removal, ritual officials such as Han Wei petitioned on canonical grounds; just then Wang Anshi was in power and pressed his private theory, causing Zhang Heng to propose honoring Emperor Xi as founding ancestor and placing him first in the east-facing seat.

entries.zh: 馮京奏謂士大夫以太祖不得東向為恨，安石肆言以折 之。
entries.en: Feng Jing memorialized that scholar-officials resented Taizu's inability to face east; Anshi spoke boldly to refute them.
entries.literal: Feng Jing memorialized that scholar-officials resented that Taizu could not face east; Anshi spoke boldly to refute them.

entries.zh: 已而又欲罷太祖郊配，神宗以太祖開基受命，不許，安石終不以為然。
entries.en: Later he also wished to abolish Taizu's pairing at the suburban sacrifice; Shenzong, holding that Taizu founded the dynasty and received the Mandate, refused, yet Anshi never accepted this.
entries.literal: Later he also wished to abolish Taizu's pairing at the suburban sacrifice; Emperor Shenzong, holding that Taizu founded the dynasty and received the Mandate, did not permit it, yet Anshi never accepted this.

entries.zh: 元祐之初，翼祖既祧，正合典禮。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yuanyou, when Emperor Yi was removed, this accorded with canonical ritual.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, when Emperor Yi was removed, this accorded with canonical ritual.

entries.zh: 至於崇寧，宣祖當祧，適蔡京用事，一遵安石之術，乃 建言請立九廟，自我作古，其已祧翼祖、宣祖並即依舊。
entries.en: By Chongning, when Emperor Xuan was due for removal, Cai Jing followed Anshi's method entirely, proposing nine temples and creating antiquity anew, while restoring the removed Emperors Yi and Xuan.
entries.literal: By Chongning, when Emperor Xuan was due for removal, Cai Jing was in power and followed Anshi's method entirely; he proposed establishing nine temples, creating antiquity anew, and restored the removed Emperors Yi and Xuan as before.

entries.zh: 循沿至今，太祖尚居第四室，遇大祫處昭穆之列。
entries.en: Down to the present Taizu still occupies the fourth shrine and at the great xiá is placed among the zhao and mu.
entries.literal: Down to the present, Taizu still occupies the fourth shrine; at the great xiá he is placed among the zhao and mu.

entries.zh: 今若正太祖東向之尊，委合《禮經》。」
entries.en: If Taizu's east-facing dignity is now rectified, it will accord with the Ritual Canon."
entries.literal: If Taizu's east-facing dignity is now rectified, it will accord with the Ritual Canon."

entries.zh: 太 常寺丞王普又言：「弅所奏深得禮意，而其言尚有未盡。
entries.en: Assistant Director Wang Pu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices further stated: "Bian's memorial deeply accords with ritual intent, yet does not go far enough.
entries.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Pu further stated: "Bian's memorial deeply accords with ritual intent, yet his words do not go far enough.

entries.zh: 臣竊以古者廟製異宮，則太祖居中，而群廟列其左右；
entries.en: I consider that in antiquity, when temples were separate structures, Taizu stood at the center with the group of temples to his left and right;
entries.literal: Your subject considers that in antiquity when temples were separate structures, Taizu stood in the center and the group of temples were arrayed to his left and right;

entries.zh: 後世廟製同堂，則太祖居右，而諸室皆列其左。
entries.en: in later ages, when temples shared one hall, Taizu stood on the right with all shrines to his left.
entries.literal: in later ages when temples shared one hall, Taizu stood on the right and all shrines were arrayed to his left.

entries.zh: 古者 祫享，朝踐於堂，則太祖南向，而昭穆位於東西；
entries.en: In antiquity at the xiá, the morning presentation was in the hall, with Taizu facing south and zhao and mu east and west;
entries.literal: In antiquity at the xiá offering, the morning presentation was in the hall, with Taizu facing south and the zhao and mu placed east and west;

entries.zh: 饋食於室，則太祖東向，而昭穆位於南北。
entries.en: the feeding rite was in the chamber, with Taizu facing east and zhao and mu north and south.
entries.literal: the feeding rite was in the chamber, with Taizu facing east and the zhao and mu placed north and south.

entries.zh: 後世祫享一於堂上，而用室中之位，故唯以東向為太祖之尊焉。
entries.en: In later ages the xiá was performed entirely in the hall using chamber positions; only the east-facing seat expressed Taizu's dignity.
entries.literal: In later ages the xiá was performed entirely in the hall using chamber positions; therefore only the east-facing seat expressed Taizu's dignity.

entries.zh: 若夫群 廟迭毀，而太祖不遷，則其禮尚矣。
entries.en: As for the successive removal of other temples while Taizu was not moved, that rite was still honored.
entries.literal: As for the successive removal of the group of temples while Taizu was not moved, that rite was still honored.

entries.zh: 臣故知太祖即廟之始祖，是為廟號，非諡號也。
entries.en: I therefore know that Taizu is the temple's founding ancestor—this is a temple title, not a posthumous title.
entries.literal: Your subject therefore knows that Taizu is the founding ancestor of the temple—this is a temple title, not a posthumous title.

entries.zh: 惟我太宗嗣服之初，太祖廟號已定，雖更累朝，世次猶近，每於祫享，必虛東向 之位，以其非太祖必不可居也。
entries.en: When Taizong first succeeded, Taizu's temple title was already fixed; though generations passed, at each xiá the east-facing seat was left vacant, because only Taizu could occupy it.
