entries.literal: When our Taizong first succeeded to the throne, Taizu's temple title was already fixed; though many reigns passed and the generations were still near, at each xiá the east-facing seat was always left vacant, because he was not Taizu and certainly could not occupy it.

entries.zh: 迨至熙寧，又尊僖祖為廟之始祖，百世不遷，祫享東向，而太祖常居穆位，則名實舛矣。
entries.en: By Xining, Emperor Xi was again honored as founding ancestor, never removed, facing east at the xiá while Taizu occupied the mu position—then name and reality diverged.
entries.literal: By Xining, Emperor Xi was again honored as the temple's founding ancestor, never to be removed, and at the xiá faced east while Taizu constantly occupied the mu position—then name and reality were at odds.

entries.zh: 倘以熙寧之禮為是，僖祖當稱太祖，而太祖 當改廟號。
entries.en: If the Xining rite were correct, Emperor Xi should be called Taizu and Taizu's temple title changed.
entries.literal: If the Xining rite were correct, Emperor Xi should be called Taizu and Taizu's temple title should be changed.

entries.zh: 然則太祖之名不正，前日之失大矣。
entries.en: Then Taizu's name would be incorrect and the former error would be grave.
entries.literal: Then Taizu's name would not be correct, and the error of former days would be great.

entries.zh: 今宜奉太祖神主居第一室，永為廟之始祖。
entries.en: Taizu's spirit tablet should now be placed in the first shrine as the temple's permanent founding ancestor.
entries.literal: Now Taizu's spirit tablet should be placed in the first shrine, permanently the temple's founding ancestor.

entries.zh: 每歲五享、告朔、薦新，止於七廟。
entries.en: The five annual offerings, new- and full-moon reports, and new-harvest presentations should be limited to the seven temples.
entries.literal: The five annual offerings, new-moon and full-moon reports, and new-harvest presentations should be limited to the seven temples.

entries.zh: 三年一祫，則太祖正東向之位。
entries.en: Once every three years at the xiá, Taizu should occupy the correct east-facing seat.
entries.literal: Once every three years at the xiá, Taizu should occupy the correct east-facing seat.

entries.zh: 太 宗、仁宗、神宗南向為昭，真宗、英宗、哲宗北向為穆。
entries.en: Taizong, Renzong, and Shenzong should face south as zhao; Zhenzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong north as mu.
entries.literal: Taizong, Renzong, and Shenzong should face south as zhao; Zhenzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong should face north as mu.

entries.zh: 五年一禘，則迎宣祖神主享於太廟，而以太祖配焉。
entries.en: Once every five years at the dì, Emperor Xuan's tablet should be brought to the Imperial Ancestral Temple with Taizu as paired ancestor.
entries.literal: Once every five years at the dì, Emperor Xuan's spirit tablet should be brought to the Imperial Ancestral Temple with Taizu as his paired ancestor.

entries.zh: 如是，則宗廟之事盡合《禮經》，無復前日之失矣。」
entries.en: Thus ancestral temple affairs would fully accord with the Ritual Canon and former errors undone."
entries.literal: In this way, ancestral temple affairs would fully accord with the Ritual Canon and the errors of former days would be undone."

entries.zh: 上曰：「太祖皇帝開基創業，始受天命，祫享宜居東向之位。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Emperor Taizu founded the dynasty and first received the Mandate; at the xiá he ought to occupy the east-facing seat."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Taizu founded the dynasty and first received the Mandate; at the xiá he ought to occupy the east-facing seat."

entries.zh: 宰相趙鼎等奏曰：「三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七，載在《禮經》，無可疑者。」
entries.en: Chief Councilor Zhao Ding and others memorialized: "Three zhao and three mu together with Taizu's temple make seven, as recorded in the Ritual Canon—there is no doubt."
entries.literal: Chief Councilor Zhao Ding and others memorialized: "Three zhao and three mu, together with Taizu's temple making seven, are recorded in the Ritual Canon—there is no doubt."

entries.zh: 紹熙五 年九月，太常少卿曾三復亦言：請祧宣祖，就正太祖東向之位，其言甚切。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, Vice Director Zeng Sanfu also petitioned to remove Emperor Xuan and rectify Taizu's east-facing seat in earnest terms.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zeng Sanfu also petitioned to remove Emperor Xuan and rectify Taizu's east-facing seat; his words were very earnest.

entries.zh: 既而吏部尚書鄭僑等亦乞因大行祔廟之際，定宗廟萬世之禮，慰太祖在天之靈，破熙寧不 經之論。
entries.en: Shortly afterward Minister Zheng Qiao and others begged that at installation of the new spirit tablet during great mourning, the eternal ancestral temple rite be settled to comfort Taizu in Heaven and refute Xining's uncanonical theory.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward, Minister of Personnel Zheng Qiao and others also begged that at the installation of the new spirit tablet during the great mourning, the ancestral temple rite for ten thousand generations be settled to comfort Taizu in Heaven and refute the uncanonical theory of Xining.

entries.zh: 今太祖為始祖，則太宗為昭，真宗為穆，自是而下以至孝宗，四昭四穆與太祖之廟而九。
entries.en: With Taizu as founding ancestor, Taizong is zhao, Zhenzong mu, and down to Xiaozong—four zhao and four mu with Taizu's temple make nine.
entries.literal: Now with Taizu as founding ancestor, Taizong is zhao, Zhenzong is mu, and from there down to Xiaozong—four zhao and four mu together with Taizu's temple make nine.

entries.zh: 上參古禮，而不廢崇寧九廟之制，於義為允。
entries.en: The emperor consulted ancient ritual yet did not abolish Chongning's nine-temple system—in principle this was acceptable.
entries.literal: The emperor consulted ancient ritual yet did not abolish the nine-temple system of Chongning—in principle this was acceptable.

entries.zh: 又言：「治平四年， 僖祖祧遷，藏在西夾室。
entries.en: They further stated: "In the fourth year of Zhiping, Emperor Xi was removed and stored in the western side chamber.
entries.literal: They further stated: "In the fourth year of Zhiping, Emperor Xi was removed and his tablet stored in the western side chamber.

entries.zh: 至熙寧五年，王安石以私意使章衡等議，乃復祔僖祖以為始祖，又將推以配天，欲罷太祖郊配。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Xining, Wang Anshi had Zhang Heng and others restore Emperor Xi as founding ancestor by private intent and wished to promote him to pair with Heaven and abolish Taizu's suburban pairing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, Wang Anshi by private intent had Zhang Heng and others deliberate and restored Emperor Xi as founding ancestor; he also wished to promote him to pair with Heaven and abolish Taizu's pairing at the suburban sacrifice.

entries.zh: 韓維、司馬光等力爭，而安石主其說愈堅。
entries.en: Han Wei, Sima Guang, and others strove against this while Anshi held ever more firmly to his view.
entries.literal: Han Wei, Sima Guang, and others strove against this, while Anshi held to his view ever more firmly.

entries.zh: 孫固慮其罷太祖配天，建議以僖祖權居東向之位。
entries.en: Sun Gu, fearing abolition of Taizu's heavenly pairing, proposed that Emperor Xi provisionally occupy the east-facing seat.
entries.literal: Sun Gu, fearing abolition of Taizu's heavenly pairing, proposed that Emperor Xi provisionally occupy the east-facing seat.

entries.zh: 既曰權居，則當厘正明矣。」
entries.en: Since it was called provisional, rectification should have been clear."
entries.literal: Since it was called provisional, rectification should have been clear."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: An edict approved this.
entries.literal: An edict approved this.

entries.zh: 閏十月，權禮部侍郎許及之言：「僖、順、翼、宣四祖，為太 祖之祖考，所遷之主，恐不得藏於子孫之廟。
entries.en: In the intercalary tenth month, Acting Vice Minister Xu Jizhi stated: "Emperors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan, as Taizu's forebears—their removed tablets probably ought not be stored in descendants' temples.
entries.literal: In the intercalary tenth month, Acting Vice Minister of Rites Xu Jizhi stated: "Emperors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan, as Taizu's forebears—the removed tablets probably ought not be stored in descendants' temples.

entries.zh: 今順、翼二祖藏於西夾室，實居太廟太祖之右。
entries.en: Emperors Shun and Yi are now stored in the western side chamber, actually to Taizu's right in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Now the tablets of Emperors Shun and Yi are stored in the western side chamber, actually to the right of Taizu in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 遇祫享，則於夾室之前，設位以昭穆焉。」
entries.en: At the xiá, seats are set before the side chamber according to zhao and mu."
entries.literal: When a xiá is performed, seats are set before the side chamber according to zhao and mu."

entries.zh: 於是詔有司集議，吏部尚書 兼侍讀鄭僑等言：「僖祖當用唐興聖之制，立為別廟，順祖、翼祖、宣祖之主皆祔藏焉。
entries.en: An edict ordered deliberation. Zheng Qiao, Minister of Personnel and Imperial Reader, and others stated: "Emperor Xi should follow the Tang system for Emperor Xingsheng as a separate temple, with Emperors Shun, Yi, and Xuan enshrined there.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered officials to assemble for deliberation. Zheng Qiao, Minister of Personnel and Imperial Reader, and others stated: "Emperor Xi should follow the Tang system for Emperor Xingsheng, established as a separate temple, with the tablets of Emperors Shun, Yi, and Xuan enshrined there.

entries.zh: 如此，則僖祖自居別廟之尊，三祖不祔子孫之廟。
entries.en: Thus Emperor Xi would hold separate-temple dignity while the three ancestors would not be enshrined in descendants' temples.
entries.literal: In this way Emperor Xi would hold the dignity of a separate temple while the three ancestors would not be enshrined in descendants' temples.

entries.zh: 自漢、魏以來，太祖而 上，毀廟之主皆不合食，今遇祫，則即廟而享，於禮尤稱。」
entries.en: Since Han and Wei, dismantled ancestors above Taizu have not shared the feast; now at the xiá they would be honored at their own temple—especially fitting."
entries.literal: Since Han and Wei, tablets of ancestors above Taizu whose temples were dismantled have not shared the feast; now at the xiá they would be honored at their own temple—this is especially fitting in ritual.

entries.zh: 諸儒如樓鑰、陳傅良皆以為可，詔從之。
entries.en: Scholars Lou Yue and Chen Fuliang approved, and an edict followed.
entries.literal: Confucian scholars such as Lou Yue and Chen Fuliang all considered this acceptable, and an edict approved it.

entries.zh: 時宰臣趙汝愚既以安石之論為非，異議者懼其軋己，藉以求勝，事竟不行。
entries.en: Chief Councilor Zhao Ruyu already held Anshi's theory wrong; dissenters, fearing overpowering, seized on this to win, and the matter failed.
entries.literal: Chief Councilor Zhao Ruyu already held Anshi's theory wrong; those of differing views, fearing he would overpower them, seized on this to seek victory, and in the end the matter was not carried out.

entries.zh: 熹時以得罪，遺汝愚書曰：「相公以宗子入輔王室，而無故輕納妄議，拆祖宗之廟以快 其私，欲望神靈降歆，垂休錫羨，以永國祚於無窮，其可得乎？」
entries.en: Xi, then under censure, wrote Ruyu: "You entered as an imperial clansman to assist the throne, yet lightly accepted reckless deliberation, dismantling ancestral temples for private ends—can spirits descend and extend the nation's fortune forever?"
entries.literal: Xi, then under censure, sent Ruyu a letter saying: "The chief minister entered as an imperial clansman to assist the royal house, yet without cause lightly accepted reckless deliberation, dismantling the temples of the ancestors to gratify private desire—can one expect the spirits to descend, bestow blessing, and extend the nation's fortune forever?"

entries.zh: 時太廟殿已為十二室，故孝宗升祔，而東室尚虛。
entries.en: The temple hall already had twelve shrines; when Xiaozong was installed, the eastern shrine remained vacant.
entries.literal: At that time the Imperial Ancestral Temple hall already had twelve shrines; therefore when Xiaozong was installed, the eastern shrine was still vacant.

entries.zh: 熹以為非所以祝延壽康之意，深不然之，因自劾 不堪言語侍從之選，乞追奪待制，不許。
entries.en: Xi held this not conducive to prayers for longevity, deeply disapproved, and requested removal from attendance—asking revocation of his academician title; this was refused.
entries.literal: Xi held that this was not conducive to prayers for longevity and health, deeply disapproved, and therefore memorialized himself requesting removal from attendance on the emperor—asking that his academician title be revoked; this was not granted.

entries.zh: 及光宗祔廟，遂復為九世十二室。
entries.en: When Guangzong's tablet was installed, it again became nine generations and twelve shrines.
entries.literal: When Guangzong's tablet was installed, it again became nine generations and twelve shrines.

entries.zh: 蓋自昌陵祔廟，逾二百年而後正太祖之位。
entries.en: In all, more than two hundred years passed from installation at Changling until Taizu's seat was finally rectified.
entries.literal: In general, from the installation at Changling until the rectification of Taizu's seat, more than two hundred years passed.

entries.zh: 慶元二年四月，禮部太常寺言：「已於太廟之 西，別建僖祖廟，及告遷僖、順、翼、宣帝後神主詣僖祖廟奉安。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the second year of Qingyuan, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "A separate temple for Emperor Xi has been built west of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the tablets of Emperors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan have been escorted there for installation.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Qingyuan, the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "A separate temple for Emperor Xi has already been built west of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the spirit tablets of Emperors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan have been escorted to the temple of Emperor Xi for installation.

entries.zh: 所有今年孟冬祫享，先詣四祖廟室行禮，次詣太廟，逐幄次行禮。」
entries.en: For this year's winter xiá offering, rites shall first be performed at the four ancestral shrines, then at the Imperial Ancestral Temple in sequence at each enclosure."
entries.literal: For this year's first-month-of-winter xiá offering, rites shall first be performed at the four ancestral temple shrines, then at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with rites performed in sequence at each enclosure."

entries.zh: 時朱熹在講筵，獨入議狀，條其不可者四，大略 云：「準尚書吏部牒，集議四祖祧主宜有所歸。
entries.en: Zhu Xi, then at the lecture throne, alone submitted objections in four points, stating in substance: "According to the Ministry dispatch, deliberation is sought on where the four removed ancestral tablets should be placed.
entries.literal: At that time Zhu Xi was at the lecture throne and alone submitted a deliberation listing four objections, in substance stating: "According to the Ministry of Personnel dispatch, deliberation is sought on where the four removed ancestral tablets should be placed.

entries.zh: 今詳群議雖多，而皆有可疑。
entries.en: Though deliberations are many, all have doubtful points.
entries.literal: Now though the many deliberations are numerous, all have doubtful points.

entries.zh: 若曰藏之夾室，則是以祖宗之主下藏於子孫之夾室。
entries.en: Storing them in the side chamber places ancestors' tablets below in descendants' side chambers.
entries.literal: If they are stored in the side chamber, then ancestors' tablets are stored below in descendants' side chambers.

entries.zh: 至於祫祭，設幄於夾室之前，則亦 不得謂之祫。
entries.en: Setting enclosures before the side chamber at the xiá still cannot be called a xiá.
entries.literal: When at the xiá sacrifice enclosures are set before the side chamber, it still cannot be called a xiá.

entries.zh: 欲別立一廟，則喪事即遠，有毀無立。
entries.en: Building a separate temple fails because mourning is remote—there is dismantling without establishment.
entries.literal: If a separate temple is built, the mourning is already remote and there is dismantling without establishment.

entries.zh: 欲藏之天興殿，則宗廟、原廟不可相雜。
entries.en: Storing them in the Hall of Heavenly Prosperity mixes ancestral and original temples improperly.
entries.literal: If they are stored in the Hall of Heavenly Prosperity, then the ancestral temple and the original temple must not be mixed.

entries.zh: 議者皆知其不安，特以其心欲尊奉太祖三年一袷時暫東向之故，其實無 益於太祖之尊，而徒使僖祖、太祖兩朝威靈，相與校強弱於冥冥之中。
entries.en: Deliberators know this is unsound, yet wish Taizu to face east temporarily every three years—this does not enhance Taizu's dignity but sets Emperors Xi and Taizu against each other in the unseen realm.
entries.literal: Deliberators all know this is unsound, yet because they wish to honor Taizu by having him temporarily face east once every three years at the xiá, in fact this does not enhance Taizu's dignity but only sets the majesty of Emperors Xi and Taizu against each other in the unseen realm.

entries.zh: 今但以太祖當日追尊帝號之令而默推之，則知今日太祖在天之靈，必有所不忍而不敢當矣。
entries.en: Inferring from the day Taizu received his posthumous imperial title, his spirit in Heaven today would surely be unable to bear this.
entries.literal: If one silently infers from the day Taizu was posthumously ennobled with an imperial title, then Taizu's spirit in Heaven today would surely be unable to bear and dare not accept this.

entries.zh: 又 況僖祖祧主遷於治平，不過數年，神宗復奉以為始祖，已為得禮之正而合於人心，所謂『有其舉之，莫敢廢者』。」
entries.en: Emperor Xi's tablet was removed in Zhiping, yet Shenzong soon restored him as founding ancestor—already correct ritual accordant with hearts; 'when someone undertakes it, none dare abolish it.'"
entries.literal: Moreover, Emperor Xi's tablet was removed in Zhiping, yet within a few years Shenzong again honored him as founding ancestor—this was already the correct ritual and accorded with human hearts; as the saying goes, 'When someone undertakes it, none dare abolish it.'

entries.zh: 又言：「當以僖祖為始祖，如周之後稷，太祖如 周之文王，太宗如周之武王，與仁宗之廟，皆萬世不祧；
entries.en: He further stated: "Emperor Xi should be founding ancestor like Zhou's Hou Ji; Taizu like King Wen; Taizong like King Wu; with Renzong's temple—all never removed;
entries.literal: He further stated: "Emperor Xi should be taken as founding ancestor, like Hou Ji of Zhou; Taizu like King Wen of Zhou; Taizong like King Wu; together with Renzong's temple—all never to be removed;

entries.zh: 昭穆而次，以至高宗之廟亦萬世不祧。」
entries.en: zhao and mu in sequence down to Gaozong's temple also never removed."
entries.literal: the zhao and mu in sequence down to Gaozong's temple also never to be removed."

entries.zh: 又言：「元祐大儒程頤以為王安石言『僖祖不當祧』，復立廟為得 禮。
entries.en: He further stated: "Great scholar Cheng Yi of Yuanyou held that Anshi's view that Emperor Xi ought not be removed and restoring a temple obtained ritual.
entries.literal: He further stated: "The great Ru scholar Cheng Yi of Yuanyou held that Wang Anshi's saying 'Emperor Xi ought not be removed' and restoring a temple was obtaining ritual.

entries.zh: 竊詳頤之議論與安石不同，至論此事則深服之，足以見義理人心之所同，固有不約而合者。
entries.en: Yi differed from Anshi on most matters yet deeply approved this—showing principle and human hearts converge.
entries.literal: Your subject finds that Yi's deliberations differed from Anshi's, yet on this matter he deeply approved it—showing that principle and human hearts agree and can converge without prior arrangement.

entries.zh: 特以司馬光、韓維之徒皆是大賢，人所敬信，其議偶不出此，而安石 乃以變亂穿鑿得罪於公議，故欲堅守二賢之說，並安石所當取者而盡廢之。
entries.en: Because Guang, Wei, and others were trusted worthies whose view happened not to take this course, while Anshi was condemned for forced interpretation, one wishes to adhere to the worthies and abolish even what Anshi rightly held.
entries.literal: Only because Sima Guang, Han Wei, and others were all great worthies whom people trusted, and their deliberation happened not to take this course, while Anshi was condemned in public opinion for perverse change and forced interpretation, one wishes to adhere to the two worthies' views and abolish even what Anshi rightly held.

entries.zh: 今以程頤之說考之，則是非可判矣。」
entries.en: Examined by Cheng Yi's view, right and wrong can be judged."
entries.literal: Examined by Cheng Yi's view, right and wrong can be judged."

entries.zh: 宗廟之禮。
entries.en: Rites of the Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Rites of the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 每歲以四孟月及季冬，凡五享，朔、望則上食、薦新。
entries.en: Each year there were five regular offerings, held in the first month of each season and in the last month of winter; on the new and full moons, additional food offerings and presentations of the new harvest were made.
entries.literal: Each year, in the four first months of the seasons and the last month of winter, there were five offerings in all; on the new and full moons, food was presented and new harvests were offered.

entries.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬；
entries.en: A great xiá merging sacrifice was held once every three years, in the first month of winter;
entries.literal: Once every three years there was a xiá offering, held in the first month of winter;

entries.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏，唯親郊、封祀。
entries.en: and a great dì sacrifice once every five years, in the first month of summer—unless the emperor was personally conducting suburban rites or a fengshan ceremony.
entries.literal: once every five years there was a dì offering, held in the first month of summer—except when the emperor personally performed suburban or feng sacrifices.

entries.zh: 又有朝享、告謝及新主祔謁，皆大祀也。
entries.en: Morning offerings, thanksgiving ceremonies, and rites when a new ancestral tablet was installed were also counted among the major sacrifices.
entries.literal: There were also morning offerings, thanksgiving rites, and visits when a new spirit tablet was enshrined—all major sacrifices.

entries.zh: 二薦，則行一獻禮。
entries.en: For the two seasonal presentation offerings, a simplified single-presentation rite was used.
entries.literal: For the two seasonal presentations, a single-offering rite was performed.

entries.zh: 其祔祭，春祀司命及戶，夏祀灶，季夏祀中霤，秋祀門及厲，冬祀行，惟臘享、禘祫則遍祀焉。
entries.en: Associated household spirits received seasonal worship: the Director of Fate and the Door in spring, the Stove in summer, the Central Drain in the last month of summer, the Gate and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, and the Path in winter; only at the year-end la offering and at the great dì and xiá ceremonies were they all worshiped together.
entries.literal: For the associated sacrifices: in spring, the Director of Fate and the Door were worshiped; in summer, the Stove; in the last month of summer, the Central Drain; in autumn, the Gate and the Pestilence Spirit; in winter, the Path—only at the la offering and at the dì and xiá rites were all of them worshiped together.

entries.zh: 熙寧元年，宰臣曾公亮等上表請加尊號，詔不允。
entries.en: In Xining 1, 1068, Chief Minister Zeng Gongliang and others submitted a memorial requesting an additional honorific title; an edict refused.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xining, chief ministers Zeng Gongliang and others submitted a memorial requesting an additional honorific title; an edict did not grant it.

entries.zh: 先是，翰林學士司馬 光言：“尊號起唐武後、中宗之世，遂為故事。
entries.en: Earlier, Hanlin Academician Sima Guang had written: "Honorific titles began in the reigns of Empress Wu and Emperor Zhongzong of Tang and thereafter became precedent.
entries.literal: Earlier, Hanlin academician Sima Guang had said: "Honorific titles began in the eras of Empress Wu and Emperor Zhongzong of Tang, and thereafter became precedent.

entries.zh: 先帝治平二年，辭尊號不受，天下莫不稱頌聖德。
entries.en: The late emperor in Zhiping 2, 1065, declined an honorific title, and the whole realm praised his sagely virtue.
entries.literal: The late emperor in the second year of Zhiping declined the honorific title and did not accept it; throughout the realm none failed to praise his sagely virtue.

entries.zh: 其後佞臣建言，國家與契丹常有往來書，彼有尊號而中國獨無，足 為深恥。
entries.en: Later, sycophantic ministers argued that because the court and the Khitan regularly exchanged letters, and they bore honorific titles while China alone did not, this was a profound disgrace.
entries.literal: Afterward sycophantic ministers offered advice that the state and the Khitan often exchanged letters, that they had honorific titles while China alone had none—sufficient to be a deep shame.

entries.zh: 於是群臣復以非時上尊號，論者甚為朝廷惜之。
entries.en: The ministers then again requested an honorific title at an inopportune time, which commentators deeply regretted on the court's behalf.
entries.literal: Thereupon the ministers again requested an honorific title at an inopportune time; commentators greatly regretted it for the court.

entries.zh: 今群臣以故事上尊號，臣愚以為陛下聰明睿知，雖宜享有鴻名，然踐祚未久，又在亮陰之中，考之事體，似 未宜受。
entries.en: Now the ministers are requesting an honorific title by precedent. Your servant is foolish enough to think that although Your Majesty's intelligence and wisdom certainly merit a great name, you have not long been on the throne and are still in mourning; considering the circumstances, it seems premature to accept.
entries.literal: Now the ministers request an honorific title by precedent; this subject is foolish and considers that Your Majesty is intelligent and wise and, though you ought to bear a great name, yet you have not long been on the throne and are moreover in the period of bright mourning; considering the circumstances of the matter, it seems not yet appropriate to accept.

entries.zh: 陛下誠能斷以聖意，推而不居，仍令更不得上表請，則頌歎之聲將洋溢四海矣。”
entries.en: If Your Majesty can decide by your own sagely judgment, decline the title, and order that no further memorials be submitted, praise will resound throughout the realm."
entries.literal: If Your Majesty can truly decide by sagely intent, decline and not occupy it, and moreover order that no further memorials requesting it be submitted, then sounds of praise will overflow the four seas."

entries.zh: 詔賜光曰：“覽卿來奏，深諒忠誠。
entries.en: An edict to Guang read: "Having read your memorial, I deeply appreciate your loyalty.
entries.literal: An edict bestowed on Guang said: "Having read your submitted memorial, I deeply appreciate your loyalty.

entries.zh: 朕方以頻日淫雨，甲申地震，天威彰 著，日虞傾禍。
entries.en: I am facing days of incessant heavy rain and an earthquake on the jiashen day; Heaven's majesty is clearly manifest, and I daily fear impending disaster.
entries.literal: I am just now facing days of incessant heavy rain and an earthquake on the jiashen day; Heaven's majesty is clearly manifest, and daily I fear impending disaster.

entries.zh: 被此鴻名，有慚面目，況在亮陰，亦難當是盛典。
entries.en: To bear this great name would shame me; moreover, while in mourning it would be difficult to undertake such a grand ceremony.
entries.literal: To bear this great name shames my face; moreover, while in bright mourning, it is also difficult to undertake such a grand ceremony.

entries.zh: 今已批降指揮，可善為答辭，使中外知朕至誠慚懼，非欺眾邀名。”
entries.en: I have now issued orders. Craft an appropriate reply so that court and country alike know my sincere shame and fear, and that I am not deceiving the people to win renown."
entries.literal: I have now issued and transmitted orders; you may craft a good reply so that within and without all know my utmost sincerity, shame, and fear, and that I am not deceiving the multitude to seek a name."

entries.zh: 其後，宰臣數上表請，終不 允。
entries.en: Thereafter the chief ministers submitted several more memorials, but in the end the request was never granted.
entries.literal: Afterward the chief ministers several times submitted memorials requesting it, but in the end it was not granted.

entries.zh: 十二日，帝詣德壽宮，以雨，百僚免入見，上就宮中行禮。
entries.en: On the twelfth day the emperor proceeded to Deshou Palace. Because of rain, officials were excused from entering, and the emperor performed the rites within the palace.
entries.literal: On the twelfth day, the emperor proceeded to Deshou Palace; because of rain, the hundred officials were excused from entering for audience; the emperor above performed the rites within the palace.

entries.zh: 自後詣宮，若行宮中禮，即不集百官陪位。
entries.en: Thereafter, when the emperor went to the palace to perform inner-palace rites, officials were not assembled to attend.
entries.literal: From then on, when proceeding to the palace, if performing inner-palace rites, the hundred officials were not assembled to attend in place.

entries.zh: 十三 日，詔令宰臣率百官於初二日、十六日詣德壽宮起居。
entries.en: On the thirteenth day an edict ordered the chief ministers to lead all officials to Deshou Palace on the second and sixteenth of each month to report on the Supreme Emperor's health.
entries.literal: On the thirteenth day, an edict ordered chief ministers to lead the hundred officials on the second and sixteenth days of each month to proceed to Deshou Palace to report on health.

entries.zh: 又詔：“朕欲每日一朝德壽宮，修晨昏之禮。
entries.en: Another edict read: "I wish to visit Deshou Palace every day and observe the rites of morning and evening attendance.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "I wish daily to hold court once at Deshou Palace and observe the rites of morning and evening.

entries.zh: 麵奉慈訓，恐廢萬機，勞煩群下，不蒙賜許。
entries.en: To receive my father's instruction in person would, I fear, neglect the myriad affairs of state and burden my ministers, and this was not permitted.
entries.literal: To receive kind instruction face to face—I fear neglecting the myriad affairs, troubling and wearying the multitude below—and this was not granted permission.

entries.zh: 禮官宜重定其期， 如前代朝朔望，甚為疏闊，朕不敢取。”
entries.en: The ritual officers should set a new schedule. The practice of former dynasties, attending only on the new and full moons, is far too infrequent, and I dare not adopt it."
entries.literal: Ritual officers should redetermine the schedule; as in former dynasties attending on the new and full moons—it is very lax and broad, and I dare not adopt it."

entries.zh: 於是禮部、太常寺言：“《漢書》高皇帝五日一朝太上皇，乞依此故事，每五日一次詣德壽宮朝見，如宮中禮。”
entries.en: The Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites then reported: "The 《Book of Han》 records that Emperor Gaozu of Han attended the Supreme Emperor once every five days. We request following this precedent and visiting Deshou Palace once every five days, using inner-palace ceremony."
entries.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites said: "The 《Book of Han》 records that the High Emperor attended the Supreme Emperor once every five days; we request following this precedent, once every five days proceeding to Deshou Palace for audience, as in inner-palace ceremony."

entries.zh: 高宗內禪。
entries.en: Gaozong's Abdication.
entries.literal: Gaozong's abdication.

entries.zh: 紹興三十二年六月十日禦劄：“皇太子可即皇帝位，朕稱太上皇帝，退處德壽宮，皇后稱太上皇后。
entries.en: On the tenth day of the sixth month of Shaoxing 32, 1162, an imperial note read: "The crown prince may immediately ascend the throne. I shall be styled Supreme Emperor and retire to Deshou Palace; the empress shall be styled Supreme Empress.
entries.literal: On the tenth day of the sixth month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, an imperial note: "The crown prince may immediately take the emperor's throne; I shall be styled Supreme Emperor and retire to Deshou Palace; the empress shall be styled Supreme Empress.

entries.zh: 應軍國事並聽嗣君處分。”
entries.en: All military and state affairs shall be left to the disposition of the succeeding ruler."
entries.literal: All military and state affairs shall be left to the disposition of the succeeding ruler."

entries.zh: 禮十三
entries.en: Rites 13
entries.literal: Rites Thirteen

entries.zh: 〈（嘉禮一）〉
entries.en: (Auspicious Rites 1)
entries.literal: (Auspicious Rites One)

entries.zh: ○上尊號儀高宗內禪儀上皇太后皇太妃冊寶儀
entries.en: ○ Ceremonies for conferring honorific titles, for Gaozong's abdication, and for presenting seals and regalia to the empress dowager and imperial consort dowager
entries.literal: ○ The ceremony for conferring an honorific title; the ceremony for Gaozong's abdication; the ceremony for presenting seals and regalia to the empress dowager and the imperial consort dowager

entries.zh: 堯傳舜，盛事千古難並。
entries.en: Yao passed the throne to Shun—a grand event unmatched through the ages.
entries.literal: Yao passed to Shun—a grand event hard to match through a thousand ages.

entries.zh: 回龍馭，辭鳳掖，北內別有蓬、瀛。
entries.en: The dragon team returns, the phoenix chamber is left—the Northern Inner Palace holds its own Penglai and Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Returning the dragon team; leaving the phoenix side-chamber—within the Northern Inner Palace, separately there is Peng and Ying.

entries.zh: 為天子父，冊鴻名，萬年千歲福康寧，春秋不說楚冥靈。
entries.en: As the emperor's father, honored with a magnificent title—for ten thousand years, may he enjoy fortune, health, and peace; let none speak of Chu's long-lived Mingling tree.
entries.literal: As the Son of Heaven's father, he is registered under a magnificent name—for ten thousand years, a thousand years of fortune, peace, and ease; speak no more of Chu's long-lived Mingling tree.

entries.zh: 萊衣彩戲，漢殿玉卮輕，宸遊今不見，煙外落霞明。
entries.en: Motley dress and joyful play—jade goblets in the Han halls; imperial outings are seen no more—beyond the mist, sunset glows.
entries.literal: Garden-joy motley play; Han hall jade goblet light; imperial outings now unseen—beyond mist, setting sun bright.

entries.zh: 前回丁未，霧塞神京。
entries.en: Before, in the dingwei year—fog blocked the divine capital.
entries.literal: The previous time, in the dingwei year—fog blocked the divine capital.

entries.zh: 正同符光武中興，擎天獨力扶傾。
entries.en: Just like Guangwu's restoration—alone he held up heaven and righted the leaning realm.
entries.literal: Just matching the tally of Guangwu's restoration—holding up heaven, alone with strength righting the leaning.

entries.zh: 定宗廟，保河山，乾坤整頓庚庚。
entries.en: He fixed the ancestral temple, guarded rivers and mountains—the cosmos set in bright order.
entries.literal: Set the ancestral temple, protect rivers and mountains—the universe set in order, bright and clear.

entries.zh: 功成了，脫屣遺榮。
entries.en: Merit complete—he shed his shoes and left glory behind.
entries.literal: Merit accomplished—shedding shoes, leaving glory behind.

entries.zh: 訪崆峒，容與丹庭。
entries.en: He visited Kongtong, wandered at ease in the cinnabar court.
entries.literal: Visiting Kongtong; leisurely roaming the cinnabar court.

entries.zh: 笑挹塵寰，不留行。
entries.en: Smiling he lifted a cup to the dusty world—and would not stay.
entries.literal: Laughing, scooping the dusty realm—not staying behind.

entries.zh: 吾皇哀戀，淚血灑神旌。
entries.en: Our emperor, mourning in love—tears and blood sprinkled on the spirit banners.
entries.literal: Our emperor's mournful attachment—tears and blood sprinkled on the spirit banners.

entries.zh: 腸斷濤江渡，明日稽山，暮雲東望元陵。
entries.en: Hearts break at the Ta River crossing—tomorrow Mount Kuaiji; at dusk, eastward gazing toward the primal tomb.
entries.literal: Bowels broken at Taojiang crossing; tomorrow Mount Kuaiji—dusk clouds, eastward gazing at the primal mausoleum.

entries.zh: 龜書畀姒，曆數在皇躬，揖遜仰高風。
entries.en: The tortoise book bestowed on Si—the tally of succession in the emperor's hands; abdication yielding, looking up to lofty virtue.
entries.literal: Tortoise book bestowed on Si; the tally of succession on the emperor's person; yielding abdication, looking up to lofty wind.

entries.zh: 鼎湖龍去遺弓墮，冠劍鎖深宮。
entries.en: The Ding Lake dragon is gone—the bow fallen; crown and sword locked in the deep palace.
entries.literal: Ding Lake dragon gone—the fallen bow; crown and sword locked in the deep palace.

entries.zh: 塗山齊德翊成功，仙魄蚤賓空。
entries.en: At Mount Tu, virtue matched to aid success—the spirit soul departed early, leaving emptiness.
entries.literal: Mount Tu equal in virtue aiding success; spirit soul early guest, empty.

entries.zh: 珍台閑館棲神地，獻饗永無窮。
entries.en: Rare terrace and quiet hall—the spirit's dwelling; offerings presented forever without end.
entries.literal: Rare terrace and idle hall—the spirit's dwelling; offerings presented forever without end.

entries.zh: 寧宗皇帝發引三首
entries.en: Three pieces: Emperor Ningzong's funeral procession departure.
entries.literal: Three pieces for the departure of Emperor Ningzong's funeral procession.

entries.zh: 中興四葉，休德繼昭清，王度日熙平。
entries.en: The restoration's fourth generation—bright virtue succeeding brilliant clarity; royal measures passing in prosperity and peace.
entries.literal: Restoration's fourth leaf; bright virtue succeeding to brilliant clarity; royal measures passing in prosperity and peace.

entries.zh: 氣調玉燭金穰應，八表頌聲騰。
entries.en: Vital essence harmonized—jade candles match, golden harvest answers; praise soars from the eight directions.
entries.literal: Vital essence harmonized—jade candles, golden harvest answered; eight directions praising, voices soaring.

entries.zh: 中原圖籍入宸廷，列聖慰真靈。
entries.en: Central Plain registers and maps enter the imperial court—successive sages comfort the true spirit.
entries.literal: Central Plain registers and maps enter the imperial court; successive sages comforting the true spirit.

entries.zh: 袞龍登廟遊仙闕，億萬載尊承。
entries.en: Brocade dragon ascends the temple, roaming the immortal gate—honored and received for ten thousand myriad loads.
entries.literal: Brocade dragon ascending the temple, roaming immortal gate; ten thousand myriad loads honored and received.

entries.zh: 寶慶三年奉上寧宗徽號《導引》一首
entries.en: Baoqing year 3: one Processional for presenting Emperor Ningzong's posthumous honorific title.
entries.literal: Baoqing year 3: one piece of 《Processional》 for presenting Emperor Ningzong's posthumous honorific title.

entries.zh: 中興五葉，天子肇明禋，一德格高旻。
entries.en: The restoration's fifth generation—the Son of Heaven inaugurates bright sacrifice; one virtue attaining the lofty heavens.
entries.literal: Restoration's fifth leaf; Son of Heaven inaugurates bright sacrifice; one virtue attaining the lofty vault.

entries.zh: 寧皇至聖功超古，萬國慕深仁。
entries.en: Emperor Ning supremely sage—merit surpassing antiquity; ten thousand states admire deep benevolence.
entries.literal: Ning Emperor supremely sage—merit surpassing antiquity; ten thousand states admiring deep benevolence.

entries.zh: 徽稱顯號又還新，功德粲雕瑉。
entries.en: Honorific title and manifest designation renewed again—merit and virtue brilliant, carved in jade.
entries.literal: Honorific title and manifest designation again renewed; merit and virtue brilliant, carved in jade.

entries.zh: 乾坤繪畫終難盡，遺澤在斯民。
entries.en: Heaven and Earth painted—hard to exhaust; remaining grace rests in these people.
entries.literal: Heaven and Earth painted—hard to exhaust completely; remaining grace in these people.

entries.zh: 莊文太子薨《導引》一首
entries.en: One Processional for Crown Prince Zhuangwen's death.
entries.literal: One piece of 《Processional》 for Crown Prince Zhuangwen's death.

entries.zh: 明天子，昔日丕纂鴻圖。
entries.en: The bright Son of Heaven—once grandly inherited the vast design.
entries.literal: Bright Son of Heaven—in former days grandly inherited the vast design.

entries.zh: 躬道德，崇學問，稽古訓，訪群儒。
entries.en: He personally cultivated virtue, esteemed learning, examined ancient teachings, and visited the learned.
entries.literal: Personally cultivating virtue; esteeming learning; examining ancient instructions; visiting the scholar-multitude.

entries.zh: 日親廣廈論唐、虞，講求政治想都俞，君臣一德誌交孚。
entries.en: Daily in the broad hall he discussed Tang and Yu—seeking good governance, thinking of that ancient harmony; ruler and ministers one in virtue, mutual trust fulfilled.
entries.literal: Daily in the broad hall discussing Tang and Yu; seeking good governance, thinking of the 'du-yu' assent; ruler and ministers one in virtue, aspirations mutually trusting.

entries.zh: 外夷效順，猶自選車徒。
entries.en: Outer tribes showed obedience—yet he still personally selected chariot troops.
entries.literal: Outer barbarians showing obedience—still he personally selected chariot troops.

entries.zh: 仁恩沾四國，固結滿寰區。
entries.en: Benevolent grace soaked the four states—solid bonds filled the whole realm.
entries.literal: Benevolent grace soaked the four states; solid bonds filled the whole realm.

entries.zh: 千年宗社，萬歲規摹。
entries.en: A thousand years for the ancestral temple; ten thousand years for plan and model.
entries.literal: A thousand years' ancestral temple; ten thousand years' plan and model.

entries.zh: 重新天命出乾符，老癃策杖相扶，願觀德化遍方隅。
entries.en: Anew Heaven's mandate issued the Qian tally—the old and feeble lean on staffs and support each other, wishing to see virtuous transformation everywhere.
entries.literal: Anew Heaven's mandate issued the Qian tally; old and feeble, leaning on staffs, mutually supporting—wishing to see virtuous transformation everywhere.

entries.zh: 幸無死須臾，謂宜聖壽等嵩呼。
entries.en: Fortunate not to die in a moment—we thought his sacred longevity would match Mount Song's acclamation.
entries.literal: Fortunate not to die in a moment—we thought sacred longevity would equal Song's acclamation.

entries.zh: 遽登雲輿上龍湖，宸居幽寂紫雲孤。
entries.en: Suddenly he ascended cloud carriage to Dragon Lake—the imperial residence lonely under solitary purple clouds.
entries.literal: Suddenly ascending cloud carriage to Dragon Lake; imperial residence lonely, purple clouds solitary.

entries.zh: 宸章寶畫，但與日星俱。
entries.en: Imperial writings and precious paintings remain only with the sun and stars.
entries.literal: Imperial writings and precious paintings—only together with sun and stars.

entries.zh: 龍帷鳳翣已載途，忍聽笳鼓嗟籲！
entries.en: Dragon curtain and phoenix fan already loaded on the road—how can we bear the reed horns and drums sighing and lamenting!
entries.literal: Dragon curtain and phoenix fan already loaded on the road—how bear to hear reed horns and drums sigh and lament!

entries.zh: 弋綈革舄最仁賢，儉德自躬全。
entries.en: Hunting cloth and straw sandals—most benevolent and worthy; frugal virtue personally upheld, complete.
entries.literal: Hunting cloth and straw sandals most benevolent and worthy; frugal virtue personally practiced, complete.

entries.zh: 憂勤庶政，三十餘年。
entries.en: Anxious toil over common governance—for thirty-plus years.
entries.literal: Anxious toil over common governance; thirty-plus years.

entries.zh: 金風肅，秋漸老，攝調愆。
entries.en: Golden wind turns stern—autumn grows old; his vital tone falls out of balance.
entries.literal: Golden wind stern; autumn gradually aging; vital tone out of balance.

entries.zh: 忱恂遍群祀，號泣訴旻天。
entries.en: Sincere and earnest at every sacrifice—crying and appealing to heaven.
entries.literal: Sincere and earnest throughout all sacrifices; crying and weeping appealing to Heaven.

entries.zh: 綴衣將出，神凝玉幾，一夜登仙，弓墮隔蒼煙。
entries.en: Final garments about to be laid out—the spirit congealed at the jade frame; one night he ascended to immortality, the bow fallen beyond azure smoke.
entries.literal: Final garments about to go out; spirit congealed at the jade frame; one night ascending immortality—the bow fallen, separated by azure smoke.

entries.zh: 七月有來同軌，引綍動靈輇。
entries.en: In the seventh month mourners come on the same track—pulling the pall moves the spirit carriage.
entries.literal: In the seventh month mourners come on the same track; pulling the pall moves the spirit carriage.

entries.zh: 淒愴淚潸然，行號巷哭，《薤露》聲傳。
entries.en: Desolate, tears stream—walking, wailing in the lanes, Thoroughwort Dew's sound passes on.
entries.literal: Desolate, tears streaming; walking, wailing in lanes, 《Thoroughwort Dew》 sound passing.

entries.zh: 東城去路，驚濤忍見江船！
entries.en: East city departing road—surging waves; how can we bear to see the river boat!
entries.literal: East city departing road—surging waves, how bear to see the river boat!

entries.zh: 憔悴山川，不禁簫鼓咽。
entries.en: Haggard mountains and rivers—reed pipes and drums choke unbearably.
entries.literal: Haggard mountains and rivers—cannot bear reed pipes and drums choking.

entries.zh: 山陰處，茂林修竹芊芊。
entries.en: At Shanyin—luxuriant forests and cultivated bamboo lush.
entries.literal: At Shanyin place—luxuriant forests, cultivated bamboo lush.

entries.zh: 望陵宮，應弗遠，金粟堆前。
entries.en: Gazing at the mausoleum palace—it cannot be far, before the Golden Millet mound.
entries.literal: Gazing at the mausoleum palace—surely not far; before the Golden Millet mound.

entries.zh: 人徒慕戀，百神警侍，盤翥驅先。
entries.en: People yearn and long—the hundred spirits stand alert attending, coiling and hovering to drive ahead.
entries.literal: People only yearning and longing; hundred spirits alert attending; coiling and hovering drive ahead.

entries.zh: 戴鴻恩，空痛慕，淚珠連。
entries.en: Bearing vast favor—empty grief and longing, teardrops linking.
entries.literal: Bearing vast favor, empty grief and longing—teardrops linking.

entries.zh: 千秋歲，功德寄華編。
entries.en: A thousand years—merit and virtue entrusted to splendid annals.
entries.literal: A thousand autumns' years; merit and virtue entrusted to splendid annals.

entries.zh: 神主祔廟《導引》一首
entries.en: One Processional for the soul tablet's temple installation.
entries.literal: One piece of 《Processional》 for the soul tablet's temple installation.

entries.zh: 三弄曉，雲黯天低。
entries.en: Three stanzas at dawn—clouds darken, the sky hangs low.
entries.literal: Three stanzas at dawn; clouds dark, sky low.

entries.zh: 攀六引，轉悲淒。
entries.en: Climbing the Six Prefectures' lament—growing ever more mournful and desolate.
entries.literal: Climbing the Six Prefectures' lament—turning ever more mournful and desolate.

entries.zh: 儉慈孝哲鍾天性，深仁厚澤遍群黎。
entries.en: Frugal, benevolent, wise, and sagacious by nature—deep kindness and ample grace reaching all the people.
entries.literal: Frugal, benevolent, wise, and sagacious—nature's gift; deep kindness and thick grace throughout the multitudes.

entries.zh: 東西南北傒商霓。
entries.en: East, west, south, north—all await the merchant rainbow.
entries.literal: East, west, south, north—waiting for the merchant rainbow.

entries.zh: 功甫就，別宸閨。
entries.en: Merit just achieved—parting from the imperial chambers.
entries.literal: Merit just achieved; parting from the imperial boudoir.

entries.zh: 臣民千古恨，幾時羽衛帶潮歸！
entries.en: Officials and people grieve for a thousand ages—when will the feathered guards return with the tide!
entries.literal: Officials and people, grief through a thousand ages—when will feathered guards return with the tide!

entries.zh: 《六州》
entries.en: Six Prefectures
entries.literal: 《Six Prefectures》

entries.zh: 樂十六
entries.en: Music 16
entries.literal: Music 16

entries.zh: 〈（鼓吹下）〉
entries.en: (Drumming and Blowing: Lower)
entries.literal: (Drumming and Blowing: Lower)

entries.zh: ○高宗郊祀大禮五首《導引》
entries.en: ○ Five pieces for Emperor Gaozong's suburban sacrifice: 《Processional》
entries.literal: ○ Five pieces for Emperor Gaozong's suburban sacrifice great rite: 《Processional》

entries.zh: 先是舊制，大理寺讞天下奏案而不治獄。
entries.en: Under the earlier system, the Court of Judicial Review ruled on cases reported from across the empire but did not run its own prison.
entries.literal: Earlier, under the old system, the Court of Judicial Review judged memorial cases from throughout the realm but did not manage prisons.

entries.zh: 熙寧五年，增詳斷官二為十員。
entries.en: In 1072, two detailed-adjudication officers were added, bringing the total to ten.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, two detailed-adjudication officers were added, making ten posts.

entries.zh: 七年，置詳斷習學官十四，詳覆習學官六。
entries.en: In 1074, fourteen trainees in detailed adjudication and six trainees in detailed review were appointed.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, fourteen trainee detailed-adjudication officers and six trainee detailed-review officers were established.

entries.zh: 九年，詔以「京師官寺，凡有獄皆係開封府司錄司及左右軍巡三院，囚逮猥多，難於隔訊，又暑多瘐死，因緣流滯，動涉歲時。
entries.en: In 1076, an edict declared: "In the capital, every office with a prison funnels detainees through the Kaifeng recorder's office and the three military patrol wards. The numbers held are so large that proper separate interrogation is impossible, and in summer many prisoners suffocate. Cases linger and often take more than a year to resolve.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, an edict stated: "In the capital, all offices with prisons are tied to the Kaifeng prefectural recorder's office and the three wards of the Left and Right Military Patrol. Prisoners detained are excessively numerous, making separate interrogation difficult; moreover, in summer many die of suffocation. Because of delays, cases often drag on for a year or more.

entries.zh: 稽參故事，宜屬理官，可復置大理獄。」
entries.en: Precedent shows that such cases should fall to the judicial offices; the Court of Judicial Review's prison should be restored."
entries.literal: Consulting precedents, these should belong to the judicial officials; the Dali prison may be re-established."

entries.zh: 始命崔臺符爲知卿事，蹇周輔、楊汲爲少卿，各舉丞及檢法官。
entries.en: Cui Taifu was first appointed acting director, with Jian Zhoufu and Yang Ji as vice-directors; each recommended assistants and examining judges.
entries.literal: Cui Taifu was first appointed to manage director affairs, Jian Zhoufu and Yang Ji as vice-directors; each recommended assistants and examining judges.

entries.zh: 初，神宗謂國初廢大理獄非是，以問孫洙，洙對合旨，至是，命官起寺，十七日而成。
entries.en: Earlier, Emperor Shenzong had said that abolishing the court's prison at the dynasty's founding was a mistake and had questioned Sun Zhu, whose answer matched the emperor's view. Now officials were ordered to rebuild the court, and the work was finished in seventeen days.
entries.literal: Earlier, Emperor Shenzong had said that abolishing the Dali prison at the founding of the dynasty was wrong, and asked Sun Zhu; Zhu's reply accorded with the emperor's intent. At this time officials were ordered to rebuild the court, and it was completed in seventeen days.

entries.zh: 元豐二年手詔：「大理寺近舉墜典，俾治獄事，推輪規摹，皆以義起，不少寬假，必懷顧忌，稽留弊害，無異前日。
entries.en: In 1079, the emperor wrote in his own hand: "The Court of Judicial Review has lately revived abandoned institutions and been put in charge of prison affairs. Its investigative standards are strict and allow little latitude; officials are bound to hesitate, and the delays and abuses of detention are no better than before.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, an autograph edict stated: "The Court of Judicial Review has recently revived fallen institutions and been charged with managing prison affairs. Its investigative standards and models are all raised on principle, with little leniency; officials must harbor scruples, and the delays and harms of detention are no different from before.

entries.zh: 宜依推製院及御史臺例，不供報糾察司。」
entries.en: It should follow the precedent of the Investigation and Adjudication Office and the Censorate and not file reports with the Inspection Office."
entries.literal: It should follow the precedent of the Investigation and Adjudication Office and the Censorate, and not supply reports to the Inspection Office."

entries.zh: 三年，詔依舊供報。
entries.en: In 1080, an edict restored the former reporting requirement.
entries.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered reporting as before.

entries.zh: 凡官屬依御史臺例，謁有禁。
entries.en: All court officials were subject, like censors, to restrictions on outside visits.
entries.literal: All officials followed the Censorate precedent; visiting was prohibited.

entries.zh: 又詔糾察司察訪本寺斷徒以上出入不當者，索案點檢。
entries.en: The Inspection Office was also ordered to investigate improper admissions and releases in penal-servitude cases and above, and to demand the files for review.
entries.literal: It was further ordered that the Inspection Office investigate this court's improper admissions and releases in cases of penal servitude and above, and demand the files for inspection.

entries.zh: 五年，詔毋以大理寺官為試官。
entries.en: In 1082, an edict forbade appointing court officials as examination officers.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, an edict forbade using Court of Judicial Review officials as examination officers.

entries.zh: 六年，又詔：「凡斷公案，先上正看詳當否，論難改正，簽印注日，然後過議司覆議；
entries.en: In 1083, another edict ordered: "For every decided case, the ruling is first sent to the rectifier to check whether it is sound; after debate, correction, signature, seal, and dating, it passes to the deliberation office for review;
entries.literal: In the sixth year, another edict stated: "For all decided public cases, they are first sent up to the rectifier to examine whether the ruling is appropriate; after debate and correction, signature, seal, and date notation, they then pass to the deliberation office for re-deliberation;

entries.zh: 如有批難，具記改正，長貳更加審定，然後判成錄奏。」
entries.en: any objections are recorded and corrected, the chief and vice officials conduct a further review, and only then is the judgment finalized and memorialized."
entries.literal: if there are objections, these are fully recorded and corrected, the chief and vice officials further examine and fix, and only then is judgment completed and recorded for memorial.

entries.zh: 又刑部言：「應吏部補授大理寺左斷刑官，先與刑部、大理寺長貳同議可否，然後注擬。
entries.en: The Ministry of Justice also proposed: "Before the Ministry of Personnel appoints Left Division adjudication officers, the Ministry of Justice and the court's chief and vice officials should jointly assess the candidate's fitness, and only then should the appointment proceed.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Justice also stated: "For appointments by the Ministry of Personnel to Left Division adjudication officers of the Court of Judicial Review, the Ministry of Justice and the chief and vice officials of the Court of Judicial Review should first jointly discuss whether the candidate is suitable, and only then make the nomination.

entries.zh: 仍取經試得循資以上人充，正闕以丞補，丞闕以評事補。」
entries.en: Only candidates who had passed examinations and qualified for routine promotion should be used; rectifier vacancies were to be filled from assistants, and assistant vacancies from reviewers."
entries.literal: Still only persons who had passed examinations and attained qualification for routine promotion and above should fill the posts; vacancies for rectifiers were filled from assistants, and vacancies for assistants from reviewers."

entries.zh: 詔刑部、吏部同著為令。
entries.en: An edict ordered the ministries of Justice and Personnel to codify these rules jointly.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Personnel jointly to codify this as a statute.

entries.zh: 八年，詔大理寺推斷事應奏及上尚書省者，更不先申本曹。
entries.en: In 1085, an edict ruled that court investigations and rulings requiring memorialization or submission to the Secretariat no longer needed prior approval from the home bureau.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered that for Court of Judicial Review investigation and adjudication matters that should be memorialized or submitted to the Secretariat, there was no longer a prior report to the home bureau.

entries.zh: 建炎詔罷太府寺，以其所掌職務撥隸金部。
entries.en: In 1127 an edict abolished the Court of the Imperial Treasury and transferred its functions to the Gold Bureau.
entries.literal: In Jianyan an edict abolished the Court of the Imperial Treasury and transferred its duties to the Gold Bureau.

entries.zh: 紹興元年，復以章億守太府寺丞，措置印給茶鹽鈔引，續添置丞二員。
entries.en: In 1131 Zhang Yi was again appointed assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury to organize printing and issuance of tea and salt notes, and two more assistant posts were added.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, Zhang Yi was again appointed to serve as assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury to arrange printing and issuance of tea and salt note certificates; two assistant posts were subsequently added.

entries.zh: 四年，復置卿、少各一員。
entries.en: In 1134 the director and vice-director were restored.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, one director and one vice-director were re-established.

entries.zh: 十年，復置主簿。
entries.en: In 1140 the registrar post was restored.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, the registrar was re-established.

entries.zh: 十一年，詔交引庫書押鈔引寺丞兩員。
entries.en: In 1141 an edict assigned two court assistant directors to sign note certificates at the Exchange Note Store.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ordered two assistant directors of the court to sign and seal note certificates at the Exchange Note Store.

entries.zh: 遇合推賞。
entries.en: When promotions were recommended,
entries.literal: When promotions were recommended,

entries.zh: 各與減磨勘二年。
entries.en: each received a two-year reduction in tenure review.
entries.literal: each received a two-year reduction in tenure review.

entries.zh: 尋詔三丞一體行之。
entries.en: An edict soon extended the same benefit to all three assistants.
entries.literal: Soon an edict ordered all three assistants to receive this equally.

entries.zh: 隆興元年，並省主簿一員，明年如舊制，設案七，以序次分管。
entries.en: In 1163 one registrar post was cut; the following year the former staffing was restored with seven case sections dividing duties in order.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longxing, one registrar post was cut in consolidation; the next year the old system was restored and seven case sections were established for sequential division of duties.

entries.zh: 監交案，隨逐丞簿赴左藏庫監交看驗綱運錢物。
entries.en: The Supervised Handover Section accompanied assistants and registrars to the Left Treasury to inspect incoming cord shipments of funds and goods.
entries.literal: The Supervised Handover Section accompanied assistants and registrars to the Left Treasury stores to supervise handover and inspect cord-transported funds and goods.

entries.zh: 中興後，所隸惟有糧料院、審計司、左藏東西庫、交引庫、祗候庫、和劑局、惠民局如前製所置。
entries.en: After the Restoration its subordinates were only the Grain Rations Office, Audit Office, Eastern and Western Left Treasury stores, Exchange Note Store, Attendant Service Store, and the Compounding and Beneficent Bureaus, as under the earlier system.
entries.literal: After the Restoration, subordinate offices were only the Grain Rations Office, Audit Office, Eastern and Western Left Treasury stores, Exchange Note Store, Attendant Service Store, Compounding Bureau, and Beneficent Bureau, established as in the former system.

entries.zh: 左藏南庫，
entries.en: The Left Treasury Southern Store,
entries.literal: The Left Treasury Southern Store,

entries.en: (sealed reserve)
entries.literal: (sealed reserve)

entries.zh: 管御前激賞庫改。
entries.en: was renamed from the Imperial Reward Store.
entries.literal: was changed from managing the Imperial Reward Store.

entries.zh: 以侍從官提領，又置提轄檢察官一員，編估局、打套局，
entries.en: It was led by an attendant official, with an inspector-in-charge and the Appraisal Bureau and Packing Bureau,
entries.literal: It was led by an attendant official, and one inspector-in-charge was also established, together with the Appraisal Bureau and the Packing Bureau,

entries.zh: 〈（二局係揀選市舶香藥雜物等第，會其直以待貿易。）〉
entries.en: (The two bureaus graded maritime spices and miscellaneous goods and assessed their value for trade.)
entries.literal: (The two bureaus sorted maritime-trade spices, drugs, and miscellaneous goods by grade and assessed their value to await trade.)

entries.zh: 寄樁庫，掌發賣香藥、匹帛，拘其直歸於左藏南庫。
entries.en: The Deposited Reserve Store sold spices and silk, remitting the proceeds to the Left Treasury Southern Store.
entries.literal: The Deposited Reserve Store sold spices and drugs and bolts of silk and cloth, collecting payment and returning it to the Left Treasury Southern Store.

entries.zh: 置監官提領二人。
entries.en: Two supervising officials were appointed to oversee it.
entries.literal: Two supervising officials were established to lead it.

entries.zh: 職官五
entries.en: Official Posts, Part Five
entries.literal: Official Posts 5

entries.zh: 時帝欲利戎器，而患有司苟簡。
entries.en: The emperor then sought better arms but worried that officials would be slipshod.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor wished to improve military gear but feared the responsible offices would be perfunctory.

entries.zh: 王雱上疏曰：「漢宣帝號中興賢主，而史稱技巧工匠，獨精於元、成之時。
entries.en: Wang Pang submitted a memorial: "Emperor Xuan of Han is hailed as a restorative ruler, yet histories say skilled artisans flourished only under Emperors Yuan and Cheng.
entries.literal: Wang Pang submitted a memorial saying: "Emperor Xuan of Han was called a worthy ruler of restoration, yet the histories say that skilled craftsmen excelled only in the times of Emperors Yuan and Cheng.

entries.zh: 是雖有司之事，而上係朝廷之政。
entries.en: Though this is ostensibly an administrative matter, it reflects court policy from above.
entries.literal: Though this is the affair of responsible offices, above it is tied to court policy.

entries.zh: 方今外禦邊患，內虞盜賊，而天下歲課弓弩、甲胄入充武庫者以千萬數，乃無一堅好精利實可為備者。
entries.en: Today the empire faces border threats abroad and bandits within, yet millions of bows, crossbows, and armor enter the arsenal each year without a single piece stout, keen, and truly serviceable.
entries.literal: Now we defend the frontier without and guard against bandits within, yet the annual quota of bows, crossbows, and armor entering the arsenal runs to tens of millions—yet not one piece is stout, fine, sharp, and truly fit to be kept in reserve.

entries.zh: 臣嘗觀諸州作院兵匠乏少，至拘市人以備役，所作之器，但形質而已。
entries.en: I have seen prefectural workshops short of armorer-soldiers, conscripting townspeople to meet quotas and turning out mere shells of weapons.
entries.literal: Your servant has observed that in many prefectures the manufacturing offices lack armorer-soldiers and even seize townspeople to fill quotas; what they make is mere outward form.

entries.zh: 武庫之吏，計其多寡之數而藏之，未嘗責其實用，故所積雖多，大抵敝惡。
entries.en: Arsenal clerks count pieces for the ledger and never test them; stores are vast but mostly worthless.
entries.literal: Arsenal clerks count numbers for storage and never demand practical use; thus though accumulated stores are many, they are mostly worn and bad.

entries.zh: 夫為政如此，而欲抗威決勝，外攘內修，未見其可也。
entries.en: With governance like this, to project power, win battles, and secure the realm inside and out seems impossible.
entries.literal: To govern thus yet hope to display might, decide victory, repel outsiders and repair within—this is not yet seen as possible.

entries.zh: 儻欲弛武備，示天下以無事，則金木、絲枲、筋膠、角羽之材，皆民力也，無故聚工以毀之，甚可惜也。
entries.en: If the court means to relax defenses and signal peace, the gold, timber, silk, sinew, glue, horn, and feather that go into arms are all drawn from the people's labor; gathering craftsmen only to ruin the product is a grievous waste.
entries.literal: If one wishes to relax military preparedness and show the realm there is no trouble, then gold, wood, silk, hemp, sinew, glue, horn, and feather materials are all the people's labor; to gather craftsmen without cause to destroy them is deeply regrettable.

entries.zh: 莫若更製法度，斂數州之作聚為一處，若今錢監之比，擇知工事之臣使專其職；
entries.en: Better to revise the rules, consolidate several prefectures' workshops as with mints, and appoint officials who understand craft to oversee them;
entries.literal: Better to remake regulations, gather several prefectures' production into one place as with coin foundries today, select officials who understand the work to specialize in it;

entries.zh: 且募天下良工散為匠師，而朝廷內置工官以總制其事，察其精窳而賞罰之，則人人務勝，不加責而皆精矣。
entries.en: recruit skilled artisans from across the empire as masters while inner craft officials supervise, rewarding excellence and punishing shoddy work—then all will strive for quality without further coercion.
entries.literal: and recruit the realm's fine craftsmen as master artisans while the court places craft officials within to oversee, inspecting fineness and coarseness for reward and punishment—then each will strive to excel, and without extra demands all will be refined.

entries.zh: 聞今武庫太祖時弓尚有如新者，而近世所造往往不可用，此可見法禁之張弛矣。」
entries.en: Bows from Taizu's reign in the arsenal are said to remain like new, while recent products often fail—proof of how discipline has slackened."
entries.literal: It is heard that in the arsenal bows from Taizu's time are still like new, while those made in recent times are often unusable—this shows how tight or loose the regulations have been."

entries.zh: 大抵雱為此言，以迎逢上意，欲妄更舊制也。
entries.en: In sum, Pang's argument catered to the emperor's mood and sought rashly to overturn established practice.
entries.literal: In general An spoke thus to court the emperor's wishes, wishing rashly to overturn the old system.

entries.zh: 器甲之制，其工署則有南北作坊，有弓弩院，諸州皆有作院，皆役工徒而限其常課。
entries.en: Under the regulations governing weapons and armor, craft offices included the Northern and Southern Workshops and the Bow and Crossbow Court, and every prefecture maintained its own manufacturing office, all employing artisans and laborers subject to fixed annual quotas.
entries.literal: As for regulations for weapons and armor, the craft offices had the Northern and Southern Workshops and the Bow and Crossbow Court; every prefecture also had manufacturing offices, all employing artisans and laborers while fixing their regular quotas.

entries.zh: 南北作坊歲造塗金脊鐵甲等凡三萬二千，弓弩院歲造角巴弓等凡千六百五十餘萬，諸州歲造黃樺、黑漆弓弩等凡六百二十餘萬。
entries.en: Each year the Northern and Southern Workshops turned out thirty-two thousand pieces of gold-plated spine iron armor and similar gear; the Bow and Crossbow Court produced more than sixteen and a half million horn-backed bows and the like; and the prefectures produced more than six million two hundred thousand yellow birch and black-lacquered bows, crossbows, and similar items.
entries.literal: The Northern and Southern Workshops annually produced thirty-two thousand gold-plated spine iron armor and the like; the Bow and Crossbow Court annually produced horn-backed bows and the like totaling more than sixteen million five hundred thousand; the prefectures annually produced yellow birch and black-lacquered bows, crossbows, and the like totaling more than six million two hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 又南北作坊及諸州別造兵幕、甲袋、梭衫等什物，以備軍行之用。
entries.en: The Northern and Southern Workshops and the prefectures also manufactured campaign gear such as military tents, armor bags, and padded armor shirts for use in the field.
entries.literal: Moreover the Northern and Southern Workshops and the various prefectures separately made military tents, armor bags, padded armor shirts, and other sundries to supply use on campaign.

entries.zh: 京師所造，十日一進，謂之「旬課」。
entries.en: Products made in the capital were delivered every ten days in what was called the "ten-day quota."
entries.literal: What was made in the capital was submitted every ten days, called the "ten-day quota."

entries.zh: 上親閱視，置五庫以貯之。
entries.en: The emperor personally inspected the output and established five storehouses to hold it.
entries.literal: The emperor personally inspected them and established five storehouses to store them.

entries.zh: 嘗令試床子弩於郊外，矢及七百步，又令別造步弩以試。
entries.en: He once had a bed crossbow tested outside the city; its bolt flew seven hundred paces, and also ordered a separate foot crossbow built for trial.
entries.literal: He once ordered a bed crossbow tested in the suburbs; the arrow reached seven hundred paces, and also ordered a separate foot crossbow made for trial.

entries.zh: 戎具精致犀利，近代未有。
entries.en: The arms and armor were exquisitely wrought and keen—unmatched in recent times.
entries.literal: The military equipment was exquisitely refined and sharp; nothing like it in recent times.

entries.zh: 開寶三年五月，詔：「京都士庶之家，不得私蓄兵器。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the third year of Kaibao (970), an edict declared: "Households of scholars and commoners in the capital may not keep weapons in private stores.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Kaibao, an edict: "Households of gentry and commoners in the capital may not privately store weapons.

entries.zh: 軍士素能自備技擊之器者，寄掌本軍之司；
entries.en: Soldiers who habitually provided their own close-combat weapons were to lodge them with their unit's office;
entries.literal: Soldiers who were accustomed to supplying their own skill-and-strike weapons were to deposit them with their army's office;

entries.zh: 俟出征，則陳牒以請。
entries.en: and when a campaign was imminent, they filed a petition to retrieve them.
entries.literal: when about to go on campaign, they submitted a petition to request them.

entries.zh: 品官準法聽得置隨身器械。」
entries.en: Officials of rank were allowed by statute to keep personal arms on their persons."
entries.literal: Ranked officials were permitted by regulation to keep personal sidearms."

entries.zh: 時兵部令史馮繼升等進火箭法，命試驗，且賜衣物、束帛。
entries.en: At that time Feng Jisheng and other clerks of the Ministry of War presented a method for fire arrows; they were ordered to demonstrate it and were rewarded with clothing and silks.
entries.literal: At that time Ministry of War clerks Feng Jisheng and others presented the fire-arrow method; they were ordered to test it and were also granted clothing and silks.

entries.zh: 慶曆元年，知并州楊偕遣陽曲縣主簿楊拯獻《龍虎八陣圖》及所製神盾、劈陣刀、手刀、鐵連槌、鐵簡，且言《龍虎八陣圖》有奇有正，有進有止，遠則射，近則擊以刀盾。
entries.en: In the first year of Qingli (1041), Yang Jie, prefect of Bingzhou, sent Yang Zheng, registrar of Yangqu County, to present the Dragon-Tiger Eight Formations Diagram together with his inventions—the divine shield, formation-splitting saber, hand saber, iron linked mace, and iron rod—and argued that the formation combined orthodox and unorthodox movements, advance and halt: shoot at range, strike with blade and shield at close quarters.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingli, Yang Jie, prefect of Bingzhou, sent Yangqu County Registrar Yang Zheng to present the "Dragon-Tiger Eight Formations Diagram" and his inventions—the divine shield, formation-splitting blade, hand blade, iron linked mace, and iron rod—and stated that the diagram had odd and even, advance and halt; at distance shoot, at close strike with blade and shield.

entries.zh: 彼蕃騎雖眾，見神盾之異，必遽奔潰，然後以驍騎夾擊，無不勝者。
entries.en: Though enemy cavalry might be numerous, once they saw the divine shield they would break and flee; crack horsemen could then strike from both flanks and victory would be assured.
entries.literal: Though the barbarian cavalry were many, seeing the divine shield's strangeness they would surely flee in rout; then use crack cavalry to strike from both sides—none could fail to win.

entries.zh: 歷代用兵，未有經慮及此。
entries.en: No previous age of warfare, he claimed, had ever been planned with such care.
entries.literal: In warfare through the ages, none had ever planned to this degree.

entries.zh: 帝閱於崇政殿，降詔獎諭。
entries.en: The emperor reviewed the designs in Chongzheng Hall and issued a commendatory edict.
entries.literal: The emperor reviewed them in Chongzheng Hall and issued an edict of commendation.

entries.zh: 其後，言者以為其器重大，緩急難用云。
entries.en: Later critics judged the gear too heavy to be practical in a crisis.
entries.literal: Later, critics said the weapons were heavy and hard to use in emergencies.

entries.zh: 隆興元年，御降木羽弩箭式，每路依式製箭百萬。
entries.en: In Longxing 1 each circuit was ordered to make one million wooden-feathered bolts to imperial pattern.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longxing, an imperially sent wooden-feathered crossbow bolt pattern; each circuit made one million bolts according to the pattern.

entries.zh: 淳熙九年，衢州守臣製到木鶴觜弩二千、箭十萬。
entries.en: In Chunxi 9 Quzhou produced 2,000 wooden crane-beak crossbows and 100,000 arrows.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Chunxi, the Quzhou prefectural official made two thousand wooden crane-beak crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows.

entries.zh: 又湖北、京西造納無羽箭。
entries.en: Hubei and Jingxi also presented featherless arrows.
entries.literal: Also Hubei and Jingxi delivered featherless arrows.

entries.zh: 上曰：「箭不用羽，可謂精巧，其屋藏之。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Arrows without feathers can be called ingenious; store them in the armory."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Arrows without feathers can be called ingenious; store them in the armory."

entries.zh: 淮東總領朱佺言：「鎮江一軍，乃韓世忠部曲。
entries.en: Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian reported: "The Zhenjiang army is Han Shizhong's old command.
entries.literal: Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian said: "The Zhenjiang army is Han Shizhong's old command.

entries.zh: 世忠造克敵弓，以當敵騎衝突，其發可至百步，其勁可穿重甲，最為利器。
entries.en: Shizhong's enemy-defeating bow, designed to stop cavalry charges, shot one hundred paces and pierced heavy armor.
entries.literal: Shizhong made the enemy-defeating bow to counter enemy cavalry charges; its shot can reach one hundred paces, its force can pierce heavy armor—it is the sharpest tool.

entries.zh: 往歲調發，弓不免損失，存者歲久亦漸弛壞。
entries.en: Past deployments had depleted and damaged the bows.
entries.literal: In former years when mobilized, bows could not avoid loss; those remaining after years gradually also loosened and broke.

entries.zh: 今考諸軍見弩手八千八百四十二人，人合用兩弓，一弓一日上教，一弓備出戰，合用弓萬七千六百八十有四，僅存六千五百七十有四，餘皆不堪施教，乞下鎮江都統司足其額。」
entries.en: He counted 8,842 crossbowmen needing 17,684 bows but found only 6,574 serviceable and asked Zhenjiang headquarters to fill the gap."
entries.literal: Now examining the various armies' present crossbowmen eight thousand eight hundred forty-two men, each man should use two bows—one bow for daily drill, one bow prepared for battle—altogether should use seventeen thousand six hundred eighty-four bows; only six thousand five hundred seventy-four remain, the rest all unfit for drill instruction; we beg the Zhenjiang command headquarters fill the quota."

entries.zh: 十五年，工部侍郎李昌圖言：「弓矢之利，貴於便疾。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year Li Changtu, vice minister of works, said: "The advantage of bow and arrow lies in convenience and swiftness.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, Vice Minister of Works Li Changtu said: "The advantage of bow and arrow lies in being convenient and swift.

entries.zh: 神臂弓鬥力及遠，屢獲其用。
entries.en: The divine-arm crossbow's range had repeatedly proved valuable.
entries.literal: The divine-arm crossbow's draw strength reaches far and has repeatedly proved useful.

entries.zh: 後又又造神勁弓，及遠雖在神臂弓上，軍中多言其發遲，每神臂三矢而神勁方能一發，若臨敵之際，便疾反出神臂下。」
entries.en: The newer divine-power bow shot farther but slower—three divine-arm shots per one divine-power shot—making it inferior in combat."
entries.literal: Later they also made the divine-power bow; though its range exceeded the divine-arm crossbow, many in the army said its release was slow—every three divine-arm shots the divine-power could fire once; if facing the enemy, swiftness in fact fell below the divine-arm."

entries.zh: 上曰：「平原曠野宜用神勁弓，西蜀崇山峻嶺，未知孰利。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Open plains suit the divine-power bow; western Shu has lofty mountains and steep ridges—which is more advantageous is unknown."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Open plains and broad fields suit the divine-power bow; western Shu has lofty mountains and steep ridges—which is advantageous is unknown."

entries.zh: 詔金州都統司詳議以聞。
entries.en: Jinzhou headquarters was ordered to investigate and report.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Jinzhou command headquarters to deliberate in detail and report.

entries.zh: 既而都統製吳挺奏：「神勁弓並彈子頭箭，諸軍用之誠便疾，神臂不及也。」
entries.en: Wu Ting of Jinzhou then reported: "The divine-power bow with pellet-headed arrows is truly swift in army use; the divine-arm cannot match it."
entries.literal: Before long Overall Commander Wu Ting memorialized: "The divine-power bow with pellet-head arrows—in the armies' use it is truly convenient and swift; the divine-arm cannot match it."

entries.zh: 詔從其便。
entries.en: The court approved local preference.
entries.literal: An edict followed their convenience.

entries.zh: 楚州兵馬鈐轄言：「弩之力，勁者三十石，次者十五石，矢之鏃狀若鍬，所發何啻數百步，洞穿數人。
entries.en: Chuzhou's military commissioner said: "Crossbow power—the strong draws thirty stone, the next fifteen; the arrowheads are shaped like spades; their shots fly hundreds of paces and pierce several men through.
entries.literal: The Chuzhou military commissioner said: "Crossbow power—the strong draws thirty stone, the next fifteen stone; the arrowheads shaped like spades; what they shoot is no less than several hundred paces, piercing several men through.

entries.zh: 江上諸軍有弩式，皆廢不修。」
entries.en: Yangzi armies had crossbow patterns but left them unmaintained."
entries.literal: Armies along the river have crossbow patterns, all abandoned and unrepaired."

entries.zh: 詔兩淮、荊襄沿邊城守，各製二十枝，御前軍器所亦如之。
entries.en: Two Huai and Jing-Xiang garrisons and the Imperial Arms Office were each ordered to build twenty.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the two Huai and Jing-Xiang frontier garrisons each to make twenty; the Imperial Military Equipment Office likewise.

entries.zh: 紹熙而後，日造器械，數目山積。
entries.en: After Shaoxi arms production piled up endlessly.
entries.literal: After Shaoxi, daily manufacture of gear piled numbers like mountains.

entries.zh: 器甲之制
entries.en: Regulations for Weapons and Armor
entries.literal: Regulations for weapons and armor.

entries.zh: 六月朔，日食既，太后削「聖福」以應天變。
entries.en: On the first day of the sixth month, when a solar eclipse reached totality, the empress dowager dropped "Shengfu" from her title to answer the heavenly warning.
entries.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, at the completion of a solar eclipse, the empress dowager removed "Shengfu" from her title to respond to the heavenly omen.

entries.zh: 丞相王爚老病，陳宜中、留夢炎庸懦無所長，日坐朝堂相爭戾。
entries.en: Chief Councilor Wang Yan was old and ill. Chen Yizhong and Liu Mengyan were mediocre and timid men of no special talent, and day after day they quarreled in court.
entries.literal: Chief Councilor Wang Yan was old and ill; Chen Yizhong and Liu Mengyan were mediocre, timid, and without special ability; day after day they sat in court quarreling bitterly.

entries.zh: 而張世傑兵敗于焦山，宜中棄官去。
entries.en: Zhang Shijie's army was defeated at Jiaoshan, and Yizhong abandoned his post and fled.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Zhang Shijie's army was defeated at Jiaoshan and Yizhong abandoned his office and fled.

entries.zh: 太后累召不至，遺書宜中母，使勉之。
entries.en: The empress dowager summoned him repeatedly, but he would not return. She sent a letter to Yizhong's mother urging her to persuade him.
entries.literal: The empress dowager repeatedly summoned him but he did not come; she sent a letter to Yizhong's mother to urge him on.

entries.zh: 十月，始還朝。
entries.en: In the tenth month he finally returned to court.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he at last returned to court.

entries.zh: 太后又親為書召夏貴等兵，曰：「吾母子不足念，獨不報先帝德乎？」
entries.en: The empress dowager personally wrote again to summon the forces under Xia Gui and others, saying, "My son and I are not worth your concern—but will you not repay the kindness of the late emperor?"
entries.literal: The empress dowager again personally wrote to summon the troops of Xia Gui and others, saying: "My son and I are not worth considering—but will you not repay the late emperor's kindness?"

entries.zh: 貴等亦罕有至者。
entries.en: Few of Xia Gui's troops came either.
entries.literal: Few of Xia Gui's men came either.

entries.zh: 神宗欽聖獻肅向皇后、欽成朱皇后、欽慈陳皇后、林賢妃、武賢妃 哲宗昭慈孟皇后、昭懷劉皇后 徽宗顯恭王皇后、鄭皇后、王貴妃、韋賢妃、喬貴妃、劉貴妃 欽宗朱皇后 高宗憲節邢皇后、憲聖慈烈吳皇后、潘賢妃、張賢妃、劉貴妃、劉婉儀、張貴妃 孝宗成穆郭皇后、成恭夏皇后、成肅謝皇后、蔡貴妃、李賢妃 光宗慈懿李皇后、黃貴妃 甯宗恭淑韓皇后、恭聖仁烈楊皇后 理宗謝皇后 度宗全皇后、楊淑妃
entries.en: The empresses and consorts treated in this volume are: for Shenzong, Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, Empress Qincheng Zhu, Empress Qinci Chen, and the Worthy Consorts Lin and Wu; for Zhezong, Empress Zhaoci Meng and Empress Zhaohuai Liu; for Huizong, Empress Xiangong Wang, Empress Zheng, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, and the Worthy Consorts Wei and Qiao, together with Imperial Consort Liu; for Qinzong, Empress Zhu; for Gaozong, Empress Xianjie Xing, Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu, the Worthy Consorts Pan and Zhang, Imperial Consort Liu, Honored Lady Liu, and Imperial Noble Consort Zhang; for Xiaozong, Empresses Chengmu Guo, Chenggong Xia, and Chengsu Xie, Imperial Consort Cai, and Worthy Consort Li; for Guangzong, Empress Ciyi Li and Imperial Consort Huang; for Ningzong, Empress Gongshu Han and Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang; for Lizong, Empress Xie; and for Duzong, Empress Quan and Imperial Concubine Yang Shu.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Shenzong: Empress Qinxian Xiansu Xiang, Empress Qincheng Zhu, Empress Qinci Chen, Worthy Consort Lin, Worthy Consort Wu. Under Emperor Zhezong: Empress Zhaoci Meng, Empress Zhaohuai Liu. Under Emperor Huizong: Empress Xiangong Wang, Empress Zheng, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, Worthy Consort Wei, Worthy Consort Qiao, Imperial Consort Liu. Under Emperor Qinzong: Empress Zhu. Under Emperor Gaozong: Empress Xianjie Xing, Empress Xiansheng Cilie Wu, Worthy Consort Pan, Worthy Consort Zhang, Imperial Consort Liu, Honored Lady Liu, Imperial Noble Consort Zhang. Under Emperor Xiaozong: Empress Chengmu Guo, Empress Chenggong Xia, Empress Chengsu Xie, Imperial Consort Cai, Worthy Consort Li. Under Emperor Guangzong: Empress Ciyi Li, Imperial Consort Huang. Under Emperor Ningzong: Empress Gongshu Han, Empress Gongsheng Renlie Yang. Under Emperor Lizong: Empress Xie. Under Emperor Duzong: Empress Quan, Imperial Concubine Yang Shu.

entries.zh: 六年，春，命令坤以汴、亳民導汴水入於蔡。
entries.en: In the sixth year, in spring, the court ordered Lingkun to use laborers from Bian and Bo to divert the Bian River into the Cai canal.
