entries.literal: In the sixth year, in spring, [the court] ordered Lingkun to use laborers from Bian and Bo to divert the Bian River into the Cai [canal].

entries.zh: 三月，世宗將北征，命率龍捷、虎捷、驍武兵先赴大名，又副王晏為益津關一路都部署，俄為霸州都部署，率所部兵戍之。
entries.en: In the third month, as Emperor Shizong prepared the northern campaign, Lingkun was ordered to lead Dragon Swift, Tiger Swift, and Valiant Martial troops to Daming ahead of the main force. He then served as deputy to Wang Yan as overall commander of the Yijin Pass route, and soon became overall commander of Bazhou, leading his troops to garrison the post.
entries.literal: In the third month, as Emperor Shizong prepared the northern campaign, [Lingkun] was ordered to lead Dragon Swift, Tiger Swift, and Valiant Martial troops first to Daming; he then served as deputy to Wang Yan as overall commander of the Yijin Pass route, and soon became overall commander of Bazhou, leading his command to garrison it.

entries.zh: 恭帝即位，加檢校太尉、侍衛馬步軍都虞候。
entries.en: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, Lingkun was additionally made honorary grand marshal and chief adjutant of the palace guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, [Lingkun] was additionally made honorary grand marshal and chief adjutant of the palace horse-and-foot guard.

entries.zh: 冬，詔防北邊。
entries.en: That winter an edict ordered him to defend the northern frontier.
entries.literal: In winter, an edict ordered him to defend the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 韓令坤
entries.en: Han Lingkun
entries.literal: Han Lingkun

entries.zh: 王晏，徐州滕人，家世力田。
entries.en: Wang Yan came from Teng in Xuzhou. His family had farmed for generations.
entries.literal: Wang Yan was a native of Teng in Xuzhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.

entries.zh: 晏少壯勇無賴，嘗率群寇行攻劫。
entries.en: In youth Yan was fierce and lawless and led gangs in robbery and pillage.
entries.literal: When young Yan was bold, fierce, and unruly; he once led a band of robbers in raids and plunder.

entries.zh: 梁末，徐方大亂，屬邑皆為他盜所剽，惟晏鄉里恃晏獲全。
entries.en: Late in the Liang, chaos engulfed Xu. Neighboring districts were looted by other bandits, but Yan's home village alone was spared because of him.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang, the Xu region was greatly disturbed; subordinate districts were all plundered by other bandits, but only Yan's home village, relying on Yan, was kept intact.

entries.zh: 後唐同光中，應募隸禁軍，累遷奉國小校。
entries.en: Under Later Tang in the Tongguang era he enlisted in the palace army and rose to junior officer of the Fengguo Guard.
entries.literal: In the Later Tang Tongguang era he answered the levy and joined the palace army, rising through posts to junior officer of the Fengguo Guard.

entries.zh: 晉開運末，與本軍都校趙暉、忠衛都校侯章等戍陜州。
entries.en: Late in the Jin Kaiyun reign he garrisoned Shaanzhou with his colonel Zhao Hui, Zhongwei colonel Hou Zhang, and others.
entries.literal: At the end of Jin Kaiyun, together with his army's colonel Zhao Hui, the Zhongwei Guard's colonel Hou Zhang, and others, he garrisoned Shaanzhou.

entries.zh: 會契丹至汴，遣其將劉愿據陜，恣行暴虐，晏與暉等謀曰：「今契丹南侵，天下洶洶，英雄豪傑固當乘時自奮。
entries.en: When the Khitan took Bian they sent Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, where he ruled with savage cruelty. Yan and Hui plotted together: "The Khitan are south, the realm is in chaos—this is the hour for a true man to rise.
entries.literal: When the Khitan reached Bian, they sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan and wantonly practiced cruelty and oppression. Yan and Hui and the others plotted, saying: "Now the Khitan invade south and the realm is in turmoil; heroes and great men ought surely to seize the moment and rouse themselves.

entries.zh: 且聞太原劉公威德遠被，人心歸服，若殺愿送款河東，為天下倡首，則取富貴如反掌耳。」
entries.en: We hear that Liu of Taiyuan's fame reaches far and men flock to him. Kill Yuan, open the gates to Hedong, and lead the realm—fortune and rank would be ours in a stroke."
entries.literal: Moreover we hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's prestige and virtue extend far and men's hearts submit to him. If we kill Yuan and send allegiance to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, then gaining wealth and rank would be like turning the palm."

entries.zh: 暉等然之。
entries.en: Hui and the rest agreed.
entries.literal: Hui and the others agreed.

entries.zh: 晏乃率敢死士數人夜踰城，入府署，劫庫兵給其徒，遲明，斬愿首級府門外。
entries.en: Yan led a handful of daredevils over the wall by night into the yamen, seized arms from the arsenal for his men, and at dawn cut off Yuan's head and hung it outside the gate.
entries.literal: Yan then led several dare-to-die men by night over the wall, entered the prefectural compound, seized weapons from the arsenal for his followers, and at dawn beheaded Yuan and displayed his head outside the prefectural gate.

entries.zh: 眾請暉為帥，章為本城副指揮使、內外巡檢使兼都虞候；
entries.en: The troops made Hui their commander. Zhang became deputy garrison commander, patrol commissioner inside and out, and commandant as well;
entries.literal: The multitude asked Hui to be commander; Zhang was made deputy commander of the local garrison, inner and outer patrol commissioner, and concurrent commandant.

entries.zh: 遣其子漢倫奉表晉陽。
entries.en: and Yan sent his son Hanlun to Jinyang with a letter of submission.
entries.literal: they sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 時漢祖雖建號，威聲未振，得晏等來歸，甚喜，即日以暉為保平軍節度，章為鎮國軍節度，晏為絳州防禦使，仍領舊職。
entries.en: The Han emperor had taken the throne but his name still rang small. Yan's defection delighted him. That same day he made Hui governor of Baoping, Zhang of Zhenguo, and Yan defender of Jiangzhou while keeping their old posts.
entries.literal: At that time though the Han founding emperor had established his title, his prestige was not yet strong; receiving Yan and the others coming over, he was greatly pleased. That very day he made Hui military governor of Baoping, Zhang military governor of Zhenguo, and Yan defender of Jiangzhou, each retaining former duties.

entries.zh: 既而暉等表晏始謀功為第一，遷建雄軍節度。
entries.en: Hui and the others then reported that Yan had conceived the plot and deserved first credit. He was promoted to military governor of Jianxiong.
entries.literal: Soon Hui and the others memorialized that Yan's merit in initiating the plot was foremost, and he was transferred to military governor of Jianxiong.

entries.zh: 漢祖入汴，加同平章事。
entries.en: When the Han emperor entered Bian, Yan was made co-equal chief councilor.
entries.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered Bian, Yan was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.

entries.zh: 初，晏至鎮，悉召故時同為盜者遺以金帛，從容置酒語之曰：「吾鄉素多盜，我與諸君昔嘗為之。
entries.en: When Yan first took his post he summoned his old bandit comrades, gave them gold and silk, and over wine said gently, "Our country has always had its thieves—you and I were among them once.
entries.literal: When Yan first reached his command, he summoned all who had formerly been robbers with him, gave them gold and silk, and over wine said at ease: "Our district has always had many bandits; you and I once did this together.

entries.zh: 後來者固當出諸君之下，為我告諭，令不復為，若不能改，吾必盡滅其族。」
entries.en: Anyone who comes after you must stay beneath you. Tell them to stop—or I will wipe out their families to the last man."
entries.literal: Those who come later should surely rank below you; convey this for me and tell them not to do it again. If they cannot reform, I will exterminate their clans to the last."

entries.zh: 由是境內安靜，吏民詣闕舉留，請為晏立衣錦碑。
entries.en: The district grew quiet. Officials and commoners petitioned the throne to keep him and asked for a "glorious return" stele in his honor.
entries.literal: Thereby the territory within became peaceful and quiet; officials and people went to court to petition to retain him and asked to erect for Yan a "return in glory" stele.

entries.zh: 世宗初，復請立德政碑。
entries.en: Early in Shizong's reign they asked again for a stele praising his rule.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign they again asked to erect a stele of virtuous administration.

entries.zh: 世宗命比部郎中、知制誥張正撰文賜之，詔改其鄉里為使相鄉勳德里，私門立戟。
entries.en: Shizong had Zhang Zheng compose the inscription, renamed his home village Xunde Lane in Ministers' Township, and ordered halberds set before his gate.
entries.literal: Shizong ordered Zhang Zheng, director of the Ministry of Revenue's comparisons bureau and drafter of edicts, to compose the text and bestow it; an edict changed his home village to Xunde Lane in the Xiangxiang of chief ministers, and halberds were set up at his private gate.

entries.zh: 未幾，改河南尹、西京留守。
entries.en: Soon he was made metropolitan magistrate of Henan and regent of the western capital.
entries.literal: Before long he was made metropolitan magistrate of Henan and western capital regent.

entries.zh: 顯德三年，移鳳翔節度。
entries.en: In the third Xiande year he was transferred to Fengxiang as military governor.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to military governor of Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 六年，從世宗北征，為益津關一路馬軍都部署，韓令坤副焉，遂平三關。
entries.en: In the sixth year he joined Shizong's northern campaign as cavalry commander on the Yijin route with Han Lingkun as deputy, and helped secure the three frontier passes.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he followed Shizong on the northern campaign as overall commander of cavalry on the Yijin Pass route, with Han Lingkun as deputy, and thereby pacified the three passes.

entries.zh: 初，晏為軍校，與平陸人王興善，其妻亦相為娣姒。
entries.en: When Yan was still a junior officer he was close to Wang Xing of Pinglu, and their wives were sisters-in-law.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yan was an army officer, he was on good terms with Wang Xing of Pinglu; their wives were also sisters-in-law to each other.

entries.zh: 晏既貴，乃薄興，興不能平。
entries.en: Once Yan rose high he snubbed Xing, who could not bear the slight.
entries.literal: After Yan became eminent he treated Xing coldly; Xing could not accept this.

entries.zh: 晏妻病，興語人曰：「吾能治之。」
entries.en: When Yan's wife fell ill, Xing told people, "I can cure her."
entries.literal: When Yan's wife fell ill, Xing told others: "I can cure her."

entries.zh: 晏遽訪興，興曰：「我非能醫，但以公在陜時止一妻，今妓妾甚眾，得非待糟糠之薄，致夫人怏怏成疾耶？
entries.en: Yan rushed to see him. Xing said, "I am no physician—but in Shaan you had one wife and now a houseful of concubines. Have you neglected the woman who stood by you in poverty and made your lady sick with grief?
entries.literal: Yan hurried to visit Xing. Xing said: "I am not able to practice medicine, but when you were at Shaan you had only one wife; now your singing girls and concubines are very many—could it not be that treating your wife of humble days too lightly has made the lady displeased and brought on illness?

entries.zh: 若能斥去女侍，夫人之疾可立愈。」
entries.en: Send the concubines away and your wife will recover at once."
entries.literal: If you can drive away the female attendants, the lady's illness can be cured at once."

entries.zh: 晏以為謗己，乃誣以他事，悉案誅其夫妻。
entries.en: Yan took this for slander, trumped up other charges, and had husband and wife executed together.
entries.literal: Yan thought Xing was slandering him, so he fabricated other charges and had husband and wife investigated and executed together.

entries.zh: 守西洛日，白重贊鎮河陽，時世宗征淮南，重贊慮幷人乘間為寇，因葺城壘，且約晏為援。
entries.en: While Yan held the western capital, Bai Chongzan held Heyang. Shizong was campaigning in Huainan, and Chongzan feared the Bingzhou forces might strike while he was weak, so he strengthened his walls and asked Yan for support.
entries.literal: While holding the western capital, Bai Chongzan garrisoned Heyang. At that time Shizong was campaigning in Huainan; Chongzan feared the Bing people would seize the interval to raid, so he repaired walls and ramparts and also arranged with Yan as reinforcement.

entries.zh: 晏意欲兼有三城，即與漢倫同率兵赴之。
entries.en: Yan meant to seize all three cities for himself and marched with Hanlun to Heyang.
entries.literal: Yan intended to take all three cities for himself and immediately led troops with Hanlun to go to his aid.

entries.zh: 重贊聞其來，拒不納，遣人語之曰：「公在陜州已立大功，河陽小城不煩枉駕。」
entries.en: Chongzan heard he was coming and shut the gates, sending word: "You won great glory at Shaanzhou. This little town of Heyang hardly needs your presence."
entries.literal: Chongzan heard he was coming, refused to admit him, and sent someone to say: "Your Lordship already achieved great merit at Shaanzhou; this small city of Heyang does not trouble you to come in person."

entries.zh: 慚不能對，遂引兵還。
entries.en: Yan, shamed, had no answer and marched home.
entries.literal: Ashamed, Yan could not reply and thereupon led his troops back.

entries.zh: 周祖即位，加兼侍中。
entries.en: When the Zhou founder acceded, Yan was made concurrent Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When the Zhou founder acceded, [Yan] was given the additional title of concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 廣順元年，劉崇侵晉州，晏閉關不出，設伏城上。
entries.en: In the first Guangshun year, Liu Chong invaded Jinzhou. Yan shut the gates and refused to emerge, posting ambushes on the walls.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangshun, Liu Chong invaded Jinzhou; Yan closed the passes and would not come out, setting ambushes atop the walls.

entries.zh: 幷人以為怯，競攀堞而登，晏麾伏兵擊之，顛死者甚眾，遂焚橋遁。
entries.en: The Bing troops thought him cowardly and swarmed the battlements. Yan signaled his ambush, and many fell to their deaths. He then burned the bridge and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Bing men thought him cowardly and scrambled up the battlements to climb; Yan waved his hidden troops to strike them, and very many fell headlong to their deaths. He then burned the bridge and fled.

entries.zh: 遣漢倫追北數十里，斬首百餘級，擢漢倫濱州刺史。
entries.en: He sent Hanlun in pursuit for dozens of li, took more than a hundred heads, and promoted Hanlun to prefect of Binzhou.
entries.literal: He sent Hanlun in pursuit north for several tens of li, beheaded more than a hundred heads, and promoted Hanlun to prefect of Binzhou.

entries.zh: 八月來朝，周祖以晏家彭城，授武寧軍節度，俾榮其鄉里。
entries.en: He came to court in the eighth month. Because Yan's family came from Pengcheng, the Zhou founder made him military governor of Wuning so his homeland might share in the honor.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he came to court; because Yan's family was from Pengcheng, the Zhou founder appointed him military governor of the Wuning army so that his home district might be honored.

entries.zh: 三年，周祖征兗州，次張康鎮，晏來朝，獻馬七匹，賜襲衣、金帶。
entries.en: In the third year, while the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou and halted at Zhangkang, Yan came to court with seven horses and received ceremonial robes and a gold belt.
entries.literal: In the third year, as the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou and halted at Zhangkang town, Yan came to court, presented seven horses, and was granted ceremonial robes and a gold belt.

entries.zh: 親郊畢，封滕國公，加開府階。
entries.en: After the suburban sacrifice he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng and given Ministerial rank.
entries.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng and given Ministerial rank.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，加兼中書令。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Yan was made concurrent Chief Secretary.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Yan] was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，進封趙國公。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, Yan was advanced to Duke of Zhao.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Yan was advanced to Duke of Zhao.

entries.zh: 從征李筠，師還，改安遠軍節度。
entries.en: He joined the campaign against Li Yun and, on the army's return, was made military governor of Anyuan.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Li Yun; when the army returned he was made military governor of Anyuan.

entries.zh: 乾德元年，進封韓國公，上章請老，拜太子太師致仕。
entries.en: In the first Qiande year he was raised to Duke of Han, asked to retire, and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with permission to leave office.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qiande he was advanced to Duke of Han, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement from office.

entries.zh: 每朝會，令綴中書門下班。
entries.en: At court assemblies he was placed in the row just after the chief ministers.
entries.literal: At each court assembly he was ordered to take place in the row after the Zhongshu Gate class.

entries.zh: 俄歸洛陽別墅。
entries.en: Before long he withdrew to his villa at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Soon he returned to his villa at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 四年冬，卒，年七十七。
entries.en: He died in the winter of the fourth year, at seventy-seven.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he died, aged seventy-seven.

entries.zh: 廢朝三日，贈中書令。
entries.en: Court mourned three days and posthumously made him Chief Secretary.
entries.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously made Chief Secretary.

entries.zh: 顯德初，加開府階，進封譙國公。
entries.en: Early in Xiande he received Ministerial rank and was advanced to Duke of Qiao.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was given Ministerial rank and advanced to Duke of Qiao.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，兼中書令。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Xingde was made concurrent Chief Secretary.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Xingde] was made concurrent Chief Secretary.

entries.zh: 初，世宗處河東還，次河陽，以洛陽城頭缺，令葺之。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong had settled Hedong and was returning, he halted at Heyang. Finding Luoyang's battlements in disrepair, he ordered them restored.
entries.literal: At first, when Emperor Shizong had settled Hedong and was returning, he halted at Heyang. Because the battlements of Luoyang were deficient, he ordered them repaired.

entries.zh: 行德率部民萬餘完其城，封邢國公。
entries.en: Xingde led more than ten thousand local people to complete the walls and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
entries.literal: Xingde led more than ten thousand local people to complete the city and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.

entries.zh: 是秋，代王晏為武寧軍節度，與晏兩換其任。
entries.en: That autumn he and Wang Yan exchanged posts, Xingde taking the Wuning governorship.
entries.literal: That autumn he replaced Wang Yan as military governor of the Wuning army, the two exchanging their posts.

entries.zh: 先是，唐末楊氏據淮甸，自甬橋東南決汴，匯為汙澤。
entries.en: Earlier, late in Tang the Yang clan held the Huai region. Southeast of Yongqiao they breached the Bian River, turning it into a foul marsh.
entries.literal: Earlier, late in Tang the Yang clan held the Huai region; from Yongqiao southeast they breached the Bian River, which pooled into a foul marsh.

entries.zh: 二年，將議南征，遣行德率所部丁壯於古堤疏導之，東達於泗上。
entries.en: In the second year, as a southern campaign was planned, Xingde was sent to lead his able-bodied men in dredging the old embankment east to the Si River.
entries.literal: In the second year, as a southern campaign was being planned, [the court] sent Xingde to lead the able-bodied men of his command in dredging and channeling it along the old embankment east as far as the Si River.

entries.zh: 及親征，以行德為濠州行營都部署，破淮軍二千餘人於郡境。
entries.en: On the personal campaign, Xingde was made overall commander at Haozhou and defeated more than two thousand Huai troops in the prefecture.
entries.literal: When the emperor campaigned in person, Xingde was made overall commander of the Haozhou field headquarters and defeated more than two thousand Huai troops within the prefecture.

entries.zh: 俄遣率師屯定遠以逼其城，為吳所敗，死者數百人，行德以身免，左授右衛上將軍。
entries.en: Soon he led troops to garrison Dingyuan and press the city, but Wu defeated him and several hundred died. Xingde escaped alive and was demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: Soon he was sent to lead troops garrisoned at Dingyuan to press the city; he was defeated by Wu, several hundred died, and Xingde escaped with his life. He was demoted and appointed Grand General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 五年，下淮南，復授行德保大軍節度兼中書令。
entries.en: In the fifth year, after Huainan fell, Xingde was again made military governor of Baoda and concurrent Chief Secretary.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Huainan was taken; Xingde was again appointed military governor of the Baoda army and concurrent Chief Secretary.

entries.zh: 恭帝嗣位，進封宋國公。
entries.en: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, Xingde was advanced to Duke of Song.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, [Xingde] was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Song.

entries.zh: 會契丹入中原，與趙暉、王晏謀斬契丹將劉愿，送款於漢祖。
entries.en: When the Khitan overran the central plains, he joined Zhao Hui and Wang Yan in killing the Khitan general Liu Yuan and submitting to the Han emperor.
entries.literal: When the Khitan entered the central plains, together with Zhao Hui and Wang Yan he plotted to behead the Khitan general Liu Yuan and sent allegiance to the Han founding emperor.

entries.zh: 漢祖入汴，擢為鎮國軍節度。
entries.en: When the Han emperor entered Bian, Zhang was made military governor of Zhenguo.
entries.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered Bian, Zhang was promoted to military governor of Zhenguo.

entries.zh: 乾祐初，加同平章事，尋移鎮邠州。
entries.en: Early in Ganyou he was made co-equal chief councilor and soon transferred to Binzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Ganyou he was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor; soon he was transferred to garrison Binzhou.

entries.zh: 章居鎮無善政，傲上剝下，以貪猥聞，用見戶為逃，擅其租賦，乃矯奏貧民數千戶負稅租，久禁繫不能輸，願以己俸代。
entries.en: In his command Zhang governed badly—arrogant to superiors, harsh on subordinates, notorious for greed. He treated taxpayers as fugitives, seized their dues, then falsely reported that thousands of poor households owed back taxes, had been imprisoned unable to pay, and offered to cover the debt from his own salary.
entries.literal: While holding his command Zhang had no good administration; he was arrogant toward superiors and exploited subordinates, and was known for greed and baseness. He treated registered households as fugitives and seized their rents and taxes, then falsely memorialized that several thousand poor households owed tax and rent, had long been imprisoned unable to pay, and asked to substitute his own salary.

entries.zh: 時方姑息，詔褒之。
entries.en: The court was in an indulgent mood and issued an edict praising him.
entries.literal: The times were ones of indulgence and forbearance; an edict praised him.

entries.zh: 副使趙彥鐸有良馬，章欲之不與，誣彥鐸謀逆之，殺之，亦置而不問。
entries.en: Deputy Zhao Yanduo owned a fine horse. Zhang demanded it, was refused, falsely accused Zhao of treason, and killed him—with no consequences.
entries.literal: Deputy commissioner Zhao Yanduo had a fine horse; Zhang wanted it but Yanduo would not give it. Zhang falsely accused Yanduo of plotting rebellion and killed him; this too was set aside without inquiry.

entries.zh: 俄加檢校太師。
entries.en: Soon he was made Inspector Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Soon he was given the additional title of Inspector Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 論曰：王景輩微時，或至為盜、負薪，遭五代之亂，奮身戎功，重據邊要。
entries.en: The commentators observe: Men like Wang Jing, in their youth, were sometimes bandits or woodcutters. In the chaos of the Five Dynasties they threw themselves into military service and came to hold weighty frontier commands.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Men like Wang Jing, in humble times, sometimes became bandits or carried firewood; encountering the chaos of the Five Dynasties, they threw themselves into military merit and heavily held frontier posts of importance.

entries.zh: 宋興，稽顙北嚮，太祖待以誠信，宜無不自安者。
entries.en: When the Song rose, they kowtowed to the north and Taizu treated them with sincerity. They should have had nothing to fear.
entries.literal: When Song arose, they bowed their foreheads and turned north; Taizu treated them with sincerity and trust, and they ought all to have felt secure.

entries.zh: 景趨利改圖，乃至滅族。
entries.en: Yet Jing, chasing profit, changed course—and brought his clan to ruin.
entries.literal: Jing, pursuing profit, changed his course, even to the extermination of his clan.

entries.zh: 王晏、郭從義遷怒肆忿，誣人以死。
entries.en: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi vented their rage on others and framed innocent men to death.
entries.literal: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi shifted anger and vented wrath, framing men to death.

entries.zh: 侯章在藩邸有剝下之名，李洪義狃於肺腑之戚，而無外凜之志，咎孰甚焉！
entries.en: Hou Zhang was known for exploiting his subjects. Li Hongyi rested on family ties and lacked the outward sternness a commander needs—who was more to blame?
entries.literal: Hou Zhang had a reputation at his regional command for stripping subordinates; Li Hongyi was accustomed to kinship of flesh and blood yet lacked outward awe-inspiring resolve—whose fault was the greater!

entries.zh: 斯皆亂世之習，有不能盡去之者。
entries.en: All of this was the habit of a chaotic age—habits not easily shed.
entries.literal: These were all habits of a chaotic age; there were some that could not be entirely cast off.

entries.zh: 武行德守洛邑，辯究欺罔，民用畏服，顧不優於諸人耶？
entries.en: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, exposed fraud, and made the people fear and obey—was he not the better of them all?
entries.literal: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, investigated and exposed deception, and the people in consequence feared and submitted—was he not rather superior to the others?

entries.zh: 王景，萊州掖人，家世力田。
entries.en: Wang Jing came from Ye in Laizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.
entries.literal: Wang Jing was a native of Ye in Laizhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.

entries.zh: 景少倜儻，善騎射，不事生業，結里中惡少為群盜。
entries.en: In youth he was daring and free-spirited, an excellent horseman and archer who shunned honest work and banded with neighborhood troublemakers as outlaws.
entries.literal: When young, Jing was bold and unconventional, skilled at mounted archery, did not pursue a livelihood, and joined local ruffians as a band of robbers.

entries.zh: 梁大將王檀鎮滑臺，以景隸麾下，與後唐莊宗戰河上，檀有功，景嘗左右之。
entries.en: Liang general Wang Tan held Huatai and took Jing into his service. In the river battles against Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, Tan earned distinction, and Jing was often at his side.
entries.literal: The Liang general Wang Tan garrisoned Huatai and placed Jing under his command; when fighting Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River, Tan won merit and Jing often assisted at his side.

entries.zh: 莊宗入汴，景來降，累遷奉聖都虞候。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong took Bian, Jing submitted and rose through successive posts to commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Jing came to surrender and was repeatedly promoted to commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.

entries.zh: 清泰末，從張敬達圍晉陽，會契丹來援，景以所部歸晉祖。
entries.en: Late in the Qingtai reign he joined Zhang Jingda's siege of Jinyang. When Khitan forces marched to relieve the city, Jing defected with his troops to the future Jin emperor.
entries.literal: At the end of the Qingtai era he followed Zhang Jingda in besieging Jinyang; when the Khitan came to relieve the city, Jing brought his command over to the Jin founding emperor.

entries.zh: 周顯德初，永興軍節度劉詞辟為從事，詞卒，遺表薦普於朝。
entries.en: In the early Xiande era of Zhou, Liu Ci, military commissioner of Yongxing Circuit, took him on as a staff officer; when Liu Ci died, his death memorial recommended Pu to the throne.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, Liu Ci, military commissioner of Yongxing Circuit, recruited him as a staff member; when Ci died, his final memorial recommended Pu to the court.

entries.zh: 世宗用兵淮上，太祖拔滁州，宰相范質奏普為軍事判官。
entries.en: While Emperor Shizong was campaigning on the Huai, Taizu took Chuzhou, and Grand Councillor Fan Zhi recommended Pu for the post of military affairs adjudicator.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned on the Huai, Taizu captured Chuzhou, and Grand Councillor Fan Zhi memorialized to appoint Pu military affairs adjudicator.

entries.zh: 宣祖臥疾滁州，普朝夕奉藥餌，宣祖由是待以宗分。
entries.en: When Xuanzu fell ill at Chuzhou, Pu brought him medicines morning and evening; Xuanzu thereafter treated him as one of the family.
entries.literal: When Xuanzu lay ill at Chuzhou, Pu attended him morning and evening with medicines; Xuanzu therefore treated him with the closeness of kin.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗與語，奇之。
entries.en: Taizu once conversed with him and was struck by his ability.
entries.literal: Taizu once spoke with him and marveled at him.

entries.zh: 時獲盜百餘，當棄市，普疑有無辜者，啟太祖訊鞫之，獲全活者眾。
entries.en: When more than a hundred captured robbers were about to be executed in the marketplace, Pu suspected that some were innocent; he appealed to Taizu to have them questioned, and many lives were saved.
entries.literal: At the time more than a hundred bandits had been captured and were to be executed in the marketplace; Pu suspected that some were innocent, and reported this to Taizu to have them interrogated, and many were spared and kept alive.

entries.zh: 淮南平，調補渭州軍事判官。
entries.en: After the Huainan region was pacified, he was reassigned as military affairs adjudicator at Weizhou.
entries.literal: When the Huainan region was pacified, he was transferred and appointed military affairs adjudicator of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 太祖領同州節度，辟為推官；
entries.en: When Taizu served as military commissioner of Tongzhou, he recruited Pu as investigating officer;
entries.literal: When Taizu held the Tongzhou military commission, he recruited Pu as investigating officer;

entries.zh: 移鎮宋州，表為掌書記。
entries.en: when Taizu transferred his command to Songzhou, he recommended Pu as chief secretary.
entries.literal: when he moved his headquarters to Songzhou, he memorialized to appoint Pu chief secretary.

entries.zh: 伏念陛下自翦平太原，懷徠閩、浙，混一諸夏，大振英聲，十年之間，遂臻廣濟。
entries.en: I recall that since Your Majesty subdued Taiyuan, won over Min and Zhe, and unified the central lands, your fame has thundered abroad; within a decade you have brought wide relief to the realm.
entries.literal: I humbly recall that since Your Majesty cut down Taiyuan, embraced Min and Zhe, and unified the lands of Xia, your glorious renown has resounded greatly; within ten years you have reached broad relief and succor.

entries.zh: 遠人不服，自古聖王置之度外，何足介意。
entries.en: That distant peoples refuse submission is something sage kings since antiquity have placed beyond concern; it is not worth fretting over.
entries.literal: That distant peoples do not submit—from antiquity sage kings have set this outside their concern; it is not worth troubling over.

entries.zh: 竊慮邪諂之輩，蒙蔽睿聰，致興無名之師，深蹈不測之地。
entries.en: I fear flatterers have clouded Your Majesty's judgment, provoking an unjust war and leading us deep into uncertain territory.
entries.literal: I privately fear that flatterers and sycophants have blinded Your Majesty's clear hearing and led you to raise an army without just cause and plunge deep into unpredictable ground.

entries.zh: 臣載披典籍，頗識前言，竊見漢武時主父偃、徐樂、嚴安所上書及唐相姚元崇獻明皇十事，忠言至論，可舉而行。
entries.en: I have studied the classics and know the precedents: the memorials of Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, and the ten counsels Chancellor Yao Yuanchong offered Emperor Ming of Tang—loyal, penetrating arguments fit to be enacted.
entries.literal: Your servant has repeatedly consulted the classics and knows something of earlier words; I see the memorials submitted in Han Wudi's time by Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An, and the ten matters presented by Tang chancellor Yao Yuanchong to Emperor Ming—loyal words and perfect arguments that could be put into practice.

entries.zh: 伏望萬機之暇，一賜觀覽，其失未遠，雖悔可追。
entries.en: I beg that amid the myriad affairs of state Your Majesty will read them once; the mistake is not yet beyond repair, and repentance can still avail.
entries.literal: I humbly hope that in the intervals of your myriad duties Your Majesty will once grant them your reading; the error is not yet far gone, and though you repent it can still be remedied.

entries.zh: 「臣伏見唐太宗有魏玄成、房玄齡、杜如晦，明皇有姚崇、宋璟、魏知古，皆任以輔弼，委之心膂，財成帝道，康濟九區，宗祀延洪，史策昭煥，良由登用得其人也。
entries.en: "I observe that Emperor Taizong of Tang had Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui; Emperor Xuanzong had Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wei Zhigu. Each entrusted his ministers as true counselors, relying on them as his very heart and sinew. They perfected the imperial Way, brought peace to the realm, ensured enduring ancestral rites, and left histories that shine, all because the right men were appointed.
entries.literal: Your servant has seen that Tang Taizong had Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui; Ming Huang had Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wei Zhigu—all entrusted as assistants, confided to as heart and backbone, completing the imperial Way, bringing ease to the nine regions, extending ancestral sacrifice in abundance, histories shining bright—truly because in appointing them he obtained the right men.

entries.zh: 今陛下君臨萬方，焦勞庶政，宵衣旰食，以民為心。
entries.en: Your Majesty now rules all under Heaven, laboring over every affair, rising before dawn and dining after dusk, with the people's welfare always at heart.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty rules the myriad regions, toiling over all affairs, rising before dawn and eating after dusk, taking the people as your heart.

entries.zh: 歷考前王，誠無所讓，而輔相之重，未偕曩賢。
entries.en: Compared with the kings of old, Your Majesty yields to none—yet the weight borne by your chief ministers falls short of those former worthies.
entries.literal: Examining former kings, truly there is nothing to yield; yet the weight of the chief minister does not match those former worthies.

entries.zh: 況為邦在於任人，任人在乎公正，公正之道莫先於賞罰，斯為政之大柄也。
entries.en: Governing a state depends on appointing the right men; appointing men depends on fairness—and fairness begins with rewards and punishments. This is the sovereign lever of rule.
entries.literal: Moreover governing a state lies in appointing men; appointing men lies in fairness; in the way of fairness nothing comes before rewards and punishments—this is the great handle of government.

entries.zh: 茍賞罰匪當，淑慝莫分，朝廷紀綱，漸致隳紊。
entries.en: When rewards and punishments miscarry, good and evil blur, and the court's discipline gradually unravels.
entries.literal: If rewards and punishments are not proper, good and evil cannot be distinguished, and the court's laws and discipline gradually fall into disorder.

entries.zh: 必須公正之人典衡軸，直躬敢言，以辨得失，然後彝倫式序，庶務用康。
entries.en: Fair-minded men must hold the levers of power, stand upright, and speak boldly to distinguish right from wrong—only then will moral order prevail and all affairs prosper.
entries.literal: One must have fair men hold the pivot of power, stand upright and dare to speak, to distinguish gain and loss—then the moral order is set in array and all affairs find ease.

entries.zh: 伏見山南東道節度使趙普，開國元老，參謀締構，厚重有識，不妄希求恩顧以全祿位，不私徇人情以邀名望，此真聖朝之良臣也。
entries.en: I see Zhao Pu, military governor of Shannan East Circuit—a founding elder who helped shape the dynasty, stolid and wise. He does not seek favor to preserve his salary, nor indulge private ties to chase reputation. He is a true minister of this court.
entries.literal: I humbly see Zhao Pu, military governor of Shannan East Circuit—founding elder, counselor in founding and construction, stolid and perceptive, not rashly seeking favor to preserve salary and rank, not privately indulging personal ties to chase reputation—truly a good minister of this sage court.

entries.zh: 竊聞憸巧之輩，朋黨比周，眾口嗷嗷，惡直醜正，恨不斥逐遐徼，以快其心。
entries.en: I hear that the crafty and cunning band together in factions, their voices raised in clamor, hating the upright and reviling the honest—they long to banish such men to distant frontiers to satisfy themselves.
entries.literal: I secretly hear that crafty and artful sorts form factions and band together, mouths clamoring together, hating the upright and uglifying the correct, hating that they are not driven off to distant frontiers to satisfy their hearts.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why is this?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 蓋慮陛下之再用普也。
entries.en: Because they fear Your Majesty will restore Pu to power.
entries.literal: Because they fear Your Majesty will employ Pu again.

entries.zh: 然公讜之人，咸願陛下復委以政，啟沃君心，羽翼聖化。
entries.en: Yet honorable men everywhere wish Your Majesty would restore him to office—to nourish your judgment and strengthen your sage rule.
entries.literal: Yet men of public reputation all wish Your Majesty would again entrust him with government, to nourish your heart and wing the sage transformation.

entries.zh: 國有大事，使之謀之；
entries.en: When the state faces great affairs, let him plan them;
entries.literal: When the state has great affairs, let him plan them;

entries.zh: 朝有宏綱，使之舉之；
entries.en: when the court has great principles, let him uphold them;
entries.literal: when the court has great principles, let him uphold them;

entries.zh: 四目未察，使之明之；
entries.en: where your four eyes have not seen, let him make clear;
entries.literal: where the four eyes have not seen, let him make clear;

entries.zh: 四聰未至，使之達之。
entries.en: where your four ears have not reached, let him convey it.
entries.literal: where the four ears have not reached, let him convey it.

entries.zh: 官人以材，則無竊祿，致君以道，則無苟容。
entries.en: Appoint men by talent and none will hold office undeserved; guide the ruler by the Way and none will gain favor unworthily.
entries.literal: Appoint men by talent, then none steal salary; lead the ruler by the Way, then none indulge recklessly.

entries.zh: 賢愚洞分，玉石殊致，當使結朋黨以馳驁聲勢者氣索，縱巧佞以援引儕類者道消。
entries.en: When worthy and unworthy are clearly told apart, jade from common stone, those who parade in factions will lose their swagger, and the crafty flatterers who pull in their own kind will find their path blocked.
entries.literal: The worthy and foolish clearly divided, jade and stone differently displayed—then those who form factions to parade their power should lose breath, those who indulge craft and flattery to pull in their kind should see their path vanish.

entries.zh: 沈冥廢滯得以進，名儒懿行得以顯，大政何患乎不舉，生民何患乎不康，匪窬期月之間，可臻清靜之治。
entries.en: The obscure and overlooked may rise, eminent scholars and exemplary conduct may shine forth—then why fear that great affairs will not succeed, or that the people will not prosper? Within a month, tranquil order may be achieved.
entries.literal: The obscure and stalled may advance, famous scholars and fine conduct may shine forth—what worry that great governance is not uplifted, what worry that the people are not at ease? Within not a full month, one may reach quiet and clean rule.

entries.zh: 臣知慮庸淺，發言魯直。
entries.en: My understanding is shallow and my words blunt.
entries.literal: Your servant's knowledge and thought are shallow and mean; my words are blunt and straight.

entries.zh: 伏望陛下旁采群議，俯察物情，苟用不失，實邦國大幸。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to heed counsel from every quarter and discern the people's wishes. If you appoint him, the state will be greatly fortunate."
entries.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will gather opinions from all sides, look down and observe the people's sentiment—if employment is not mistaken, truly it is the state's great fortune.

entries.zh: 趙普，字則平，幽州薊人。
entries.en: Zhao Pu, whose style name was Zeping, came from Ji in Youzhou.
entries.literal: Zhao Pu, style name Zeping, was a native of Ji in Youzhou.

entries.zh: 後唐幽帥趙德鈞連年用兵，民力疲弊。
entries.en: Under the Later Tang, Zhao Dejun, military governor of You, fought year after year until the people were worn down and impoverished.
entries.literal: In the Later Tang, Zhao Dejun, military governor of You, waged war year after year, and the people's strength was exhausted.

entries.zh: 普父廻舉族徙常山，又徙河南洛陽。
entries.en: Pu's father Hui relocated the entire clan first to Changshan and then to Luoyang in Henan.
entries.literal: Pu's father Hui moved the whole clan to Changshan, and then again to Luoyang in Henan.

entries.zh: 普沈厚寡言，鎮陽豪族魏氏以女妻之。
entries.en: Pu was grave, steady, and taciturn; the prominent Wei clan of Zhenyang married a daughter to him.
entries.literal: Pu was deep and steady and sparing of speech; the powerful Wei clan of Zhenyang gave him their daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 王祜，字景叔，大名莘人。
entries.en: Wang Hu, styled Jingshu, came from Shen in Daming Prefecture.
entries.literal: Wang Hu, courtesy name Jingshu, was a native of Shen in Daming.

entries.zh: 祖言，仕唐黎陽令。
entries.en: His grandfather Yan had served as magistrate of Liyang under the Tang.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yan served as magistrate of Liyang under Tang.

entries.zh: 父徹，舉後唐進士，至左拾遺。
entries.en: His father Che passed the jinshi examination under Later Tang and rose to left remonstrator.
entries.literal: His father Che passed the jinshi examination under Later Tang and rose to Left Reminder.

entries.zh: 高錫，字天福，河中虞鄉人。
entries.en: Gao Xi, styled Tianfu, came from Yuxiang in Hezhong.
entries.literal: Gao Xi, style name Tianfu, was a native of Yuxiang in Hezhong.

entries.zh: 家世業儒，幼潁悟，能屬文。
entries.en: His family had long been devoted to learning; bright from childhood, he could already write essays.
entries.literal: His family for generations pursued Confucian studies; from youth he was quick-witted and could compose essays.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐中，舉進士。
entries.en: During the Qianyou era of Later Han he sat for the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: In Han's Qianyou era he was recommended for the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 王晏鎮徐州，辟掌書記；
entries.en: When Wang Yan governed Xuzhou he recruited Xi as his chief secretary;
entries.literal: When Wang Yan commanded Xuzhou he recruited him as chief secretary;

entries.zh: 留守西洛，又辟河南府推官。
entries.en: and when Wang held the western capital he also appointed Xi investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
entries.literal: when stationed at Western Luoyang he again recruited him as investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 坐按獄失實奪官，遷置涇州，會赦得歸。
entries.en: He lost his post when a criminal case he handled proved unfounded; after being reassigned to Jing Prefecture he was able to return home when an amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: He was stripped of office for investigating a case that did not accord with facts, was transferred and assigned to Jing Prefecture, and upon a general amnesty was allowed to return.

entries.zh: 周顯德初，劉崇入寇，宰相請選將拒之，世宗銳意親征，破崇高平，誅敗將樊愛能等，由是政無大小悉親決之，不復責成有司。
entries.en: Early in the Xiande era, when Liu Chong raided the border, the chief minister urged sending a general against him; Emperor Shizong insisted on taking the field himself, won at Gaoping, and executed the failed generals Fan Aineng and others. From then on he decided every matter himself, great or small, and no longer held the regular offices accountable.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhou's Xiande era, Liu Chong invaded; the chief minister requested selecting a general to resist him; Shizong was keen to campaign in person, crushed the enemy at Gaoping, executed the defeated generals Fan Aineng and others; from this all affairs great and small he decided in person, no longer charging the responsible offices.

entries.zh: 錫徒步詣招諫匭上書，請擇賢任官，分治眾職，疏奏不報。
entries.en: Xi walked to the public suggestion box and submitted a memorial urging the appointment of worthy men and a proper division of duties among offices; it went unanswered.
entries.literal: Xi went on foot to the suggestion and remonstrance box and submitted a memorial requesting selecting the worthy for office and dividing governance of many duties; the memorial received no response.

entries.zh: 世宗嘗令翰林學士及兩省官分撰俳優詞，付教坊肄習，以奉遊宴。
entries.en: Shizong once ordered Hanlin academicians and Secretariat officials to compose lyrics for variety players, have them rehearsed at the Court Entertainment Office, and perform them at his banquets and outings.
entries.literal: Shizong once ordered Hanlin academicians and officials of the two secretariats separately to compose variety-player lyrics, delivered to the Court Entertainment Office for drill, to serve banquets and excursions.

entries.zh: 錫復上疏諫。
entries.en: Xi submitted another memorial in protest.
entries.literal: Xi again submitted a memorial remonstrating.

entries.zh: 後為蔡州防禦推官。
entries.en: He later served as investigating officer on the defense staff of Cai Prefecture.
entries.literal: Later he served as investigating officer on the Cai Prefecture defense staff.

entries.zh: 陶穀，字秀實，邠州新平人。
entries.en: Tao Gu, styled Xiushi, came from Xinping in Bin Prefecture.
entries.literal: Tao Gu, courtesy name Xiushi, was a native of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 本姓唐，避晉祖諱改焉。
entries.en: The family had originally borne the surname Tang but changed it to evade the imperial taboo of the Jin founder.
entries.literal: His original surname was Tang; he changed it to avoid the taboo name of the Jin founding emperor.

entries.zh: 歷北齊、隋、唐為名族。
entries.en: For generations under the Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang they had ranked among the great families.
entries.literal: Through Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang they were a distinguished clan.

entries.zh: 祖彥謙，歷慈、絳、澧三州刺史，有詩名，自號鹿門先生。
entries.en: His grandfather Yanqian had served as prefect of Ci, Jiang, and Li, won renown as a poet, and took the sobriquet Master of Deer Gate.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yanqian served as prefect of Ci, Jiang, and Li prefectures, had a reputation in poetry, and styled himself Master of Deer Gate.

entries.zh: 父渙，領夷州刺史，唐季之亂，為邠帥楊崇本所害。
entries.en: His father Huan had governed Yi Prefecture, but during the chaos at the close of the Tang he was slain by Yang Chongben, the military governor of Bin.
entries.literal: His father Huan held the post of prefect of Yi Prefecture; in the turmoil at the end of Tang he was killed by the Bin military commissioner Yang Chongben.

entries.zh: 時穀尚幼，隨母柳氏育崇本家。
entries.en: Gu was still a child then and grew up in Chongben's house with his mother, Lady Liu.
entries.literal: At that time Gu was still young; he followed his mother the Lady Liu and was raised in Chongben's household.

entries.zh: 謙溥少通《左氏春秋》。
entries.en: Qianpu mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals in youth.
entries.literal: Qianpu in youth mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

entries.zh: 從晉祖入汴，補殿直，奉使契丹。
entries.en: Following the Jin founder into Bian, he became palace attendant and served as envoy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: Following the Jin ancestor into Bian, he was appointed palace attendant and sent on mission to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，改西頭供奉官，漢初，遷東頭。
entries.en: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne he became western head tribute officer; early in Later Han he was transferred to eastern head.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shaodi acceded, he was changed to western head tribute officer; at the beginning of Han he was transferred to eastern head.

entries.zh: 周祖討三叛及守鄴都，謙溥往來宣密命，周祖愛之。
entries.en: When Zhou's founding emperor campaigned against the Three Rebellions and held Ye capital, Qianpu carried secret orders back and forth and won his favor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Zhou campaigned against the Three Rebellions and guarded Ye capital, Qianpu went back and forth conveying secret orders; the Zhou founder favored him.

entries.zh: 廣順初，遷供備庫副使。
entries.en: Early in the Guangshun era he became deputy commissioner of the supply depot.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the supply depot.

entries.zh: 世宗征劉崇，遼州刺史張乙堅壁不下，遣謙溥單騎說之，乙以城降，以功改閑廄使。
entries.en: Campaigning against Liu Chong, Emperor Shizong sent Qianpu alone on horseback to persuade Zhang Yi, prefect of Liao, who held the walls; Yi surrendered, and Qianpu was made commissioner of the idle stables.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Liu Chong, Zhang Yi, prefect of Liao prefecture, held the walls and would not surrender; Qianpu was sent alone on horseback to persuade him, and Yi surrendered the city; for merit he was changed to commissioner of the idle stables.

entries.zh: 師還，留為晉州兵馬都監。
entries.en: When the army returned he was kept on as Jinzhou horse and foot supervisor.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was retained as Jinzhou horse and foot army supervisor.

entries.zh: 以偏師入河東境，頻致克捷，世宗詔褒美之。
entries.en: Leading a detached force into Hedong he won repeated victories, and Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.
entries.literal: With a detached force he entered Hedong territory and repeatedly achieved victories; Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.

entries.zh: 會隰州刺史孫義卒，時世宗親征淮南，謙溥謂節帥楊廷璋曰：「大寧，咽喉要地，不可闕守。
entries.en: When Xi prefect Sun Yi died while Emperor Shizong was campaigning in Huainan, Qianpu told military governor Yang Tingzhang, "Daning is a vital choke point and must not be left undefended.
entries.literal: When Sun Yi, prefect of Xi prefecture, died, at the time Emperor Shizong was personally campaigning in Huainan; Qianpu said to military governor Yang Tingzhang: "Daning is a vital throat-point and must not be left undefended.

entries.zh: 且車駕出征，若俟報，則孤城陷矣。」
entries.en: With the emperor on campaign, waiting for orders would mean the isolated city falls."
entries.literal: Moreover, with the imperial carriage on campaign, if we wait for a report, the isolated city will fall."

entries.zh: 廷璋即署謙溥權隰州事。
entries.en: Tingzhang immediately put Qianpu in provisional charge of Xi prefecture.
entries.literal: Tingzhang immediately appointed Qianpu to provisional charge of Xi prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 至郡，亟命浚城隍，嚴兵備，凡八日，幷人果以數千騎來寇。
entries.en: On reaching the prefecture he urgently dredged the moat, strengthened defenses, and within eight days Jin forces raided with several thousand cavalry.
entries.literal: Reaching the prefecture, he urgently ordered the moat and walls dredged and defenses tightened; within eight days the men of Bing indeed came to raid with several thousand cavalry.

entries.zh: 時盛暑，謙溥單衣持扇，從二小吏登城，徐步按視戰具。
entries.en: In peak summer heat Qianpu mounted the wall in light clothing with a fan, followed by two clerks, and slowly inspected the battle equipment.
entries.literal: It was peak summer heat; Qianpu in light clothing holding a fan, followed by two junior clerks, mounted the wall and slowly walked inspecting battle equipment.

entries.zh: 幷人退舍，後旬餘，大發衝車攻城。
entries.en: The Jin forces withdrew; more than ten days later they returned with battering rams.
entries.literal: The men of Bing withdrew; after more than ten days they launched battering rams on a large scale to attack the city.

entries.zh: 謙溥募敢死士，得百餘人，短兵堅甲，銜枚夜縋出城。
entries.en: Qianpu recruited more than a hundred dare-to-die soldiers with short weapons and strong armor, gagged and lowered from the wall by rope at night.
entries.literal: Qianpu recruited dare-to-die soldiers, obtaining more than a hundred men with short weapons and strong armor, gagged and lowered by rope from the wall at night.

entries.zh: 會廷璋兵至，合勢夾攻，掩其不及。
entries.en: When Tingzhang's troops arrived they pincered the enemy and caught them unprepared.
entries.literal: When Tingzhang's troops arrived, they combined forces in a pincer attack and caught them unprepared.

entries.zh: 幷人大擾，悉眾遁去。
entries.en: The Jin forces were thrown into disorder and fled with their entire army.
entries.literal: The men of Bing were greatly thrown into disorder and fled with their entire force.

entries.zh: 追北數十里，斬首千餘級，時顯德四年也。
entries.en: Pursuing north for tens of li they counted more than a thousand heads; this was Xiande year four.
entries.literal: Pursuing north for several tens of li, more than a thousand heads were cut off; this was in year four of Xiande.

entries.zh: 明年五月，攻破孝義縣，以功領衢州刺史、監軍如故。
entries.en: The following fifth month he captured Xiaoyi county and for his service held the post of Qu prefecture prefect while retaining army supervision.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the next year, he captured Xiaoyi county; for merit he held the post of prefect of Qu prefecture while retaining army supervision as before.

entries.zh: 世宗北征，召赴行在。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong marched north he was summoned to the imperial camp.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned north, he was summoned to the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 恭帝即位，為澶州巡檢使，詔城莫州，數旬而就。
entries.en: When Emperor Gongdi took the throne he became Danzhou patrol inspector; ordered to build Mo prefecture's walls, he finished in several weeks.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, he became Danzhou patrol inspector; an edict ordered the building of Mo prefecture's walls, completed within several tens of days.

entries.zh: 改丹州刺史。
entries.en: He was made prefect of Dan prefecture.
entries.literal: He was changed to prefect of Dan prefecture.

entries.zh: 李進卿
entries.en: Li Jinqing
entries.literal: Li Jinqing

entries.zh: 端拱初，遷龍衛都指揮使，領長州團練使，出鎮真定。
entries.en: At the start of the Duan Gong era he was made commander of the Longwei guard and regimental commissioner of Changzhou, and posted to garrison Zhending.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was transferred to commander of Longwei, concurrently regimental commissioner of Changzhou, and went out to garrison Zhending.

entries.zh: 是年秋，出為潁州防禦使。
entries.en: That autumn he was posted as defense commissioner of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: That autumn he went out as defense commissioner of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 未幾，太宗以其練習戎旅，特置龍衛、神衛四廂都指揮使以授之。
entries.en: Soon afterward Taizong, recognizing his mastery of military affairs, specially created the four-division commands of Longwei and Shenwei and appointed him to lead them.
entries.literal: Before long Taizong, because of his mastery of military affairs, specially created the four-division commanders of Longwei and Shenwei and invested him with the post.

entries.zh: 改領振州防禦使。
entries.en: He was concurrently made defense commissioner of Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: He was changed to concurrently defense commissioner of Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 明年，拜殿前都虞候，領容州觀察使。
entries.en: The following year he was made chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.

entries.zh: 一日，侍宴北苑，上入玄武門，守正大醉，與王榮論邊功於駕前，忿爭失儀，侍臣請以屬吏，上弗許。
entries.en: One day at a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor passed through the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng, very drunk, argued with Wang Rong over frontier exploits before the imperial carriage, quarreling loudly and forgetting decorum; attendants asked that they be turned over to the judicial authorities, but the emperor refused.
entries.literal: One day, while attending a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor entered the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng was greatly drunk and with Wang Rong disputed frontier merit before the imperial carriage, quarreling in anger and losing propriety; attendants asked that they be handed to the judicial officers, but the emperor would not permit it.

entries.zh: 翌日，俱詣殿廷請罪，上曰：「朕亦大醉，漫不復省。」
entries.en: The next day both came to court to apologize; the emperor said, "I was drunk myself and scarcely remember it."
entries.literal: The next day they both came to the palace hall to plead guilty; the emperor said, "I too was greatly drunk and scarcely remember it."

entries.zh: 遂釋不問。
entries.en: He dismissed the matter without further inquiry.
entries.literal: He then released them without inquiry.

entries.zh: 俄命為定州行營副部署，受詔詣保州軍開道，遇敵於曹河，與戰數合，梟首三十餘，獲馬五十匹，上聞而壯之。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made deputy commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters and, by imperial order, sent to Ba prefecture to open a route. At Cao River he met the enemy and fought several engagements, taking more than thirty heads and fifty horses. When the emperor heard the report, he praised his martial spirit.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed deputy commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters, received an edict to proceed to Ba prefecture army to open a route, encountered the enemy at Cao River, fought several engagements, took more than thirty heads, captured fifty horses; when the emperor heard of it he applauded his valor.

entries.zh: 劉福，徐州下邳人。
entries.en: Liu Fu was from Xiapi in Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Fu was a native of Xiapi in Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 少倜儻，魁岸有膂力。
entries.en: As a young man he was bold and unconventional, tall and powerfully built.
entries.literal: In youth he was unrestrained and free-spirited, with a towering frame and great physical strength.

entries.zh: 周顯德中，世宗征淮南，福徒步謁見於壽春。
entries.en: During the Xiande reign of the Later Zhou, when Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Fu walked to Shouchun to seek an audience.
entries.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, when the Shizong Emperor campaigned against Huainan, Fu went on foot to present himself at Shouchun.

entries.zh: 世宗奇之，因留麾下。
entries.en: The emperor was struck by him and kept him in his retinue.
entries.literal: The Shizong Emperor regarded him as extraordinary and therefore kept him in his personal following.

entries.zh: 每出戰，則令福率衛士為先鋒，與破紫金山砦。
entries.en: On every campaign he had Fu lead the imperial guards as vanguard; together they took the Zijin Mountain fort.
entries.literal: Whenever he went out to battle, he would have Fu lead the bodyguard as vanguard, and together they captured the Zijin Mountain stockade.

entries.zh: 淮南平，錄功授懷德指揮使。
entries.en: After Huainan was pacified, his service was recognized with appointment as commander of the Huaide regiment.
entries.literal: When Huainan was pacified, his merit was recorded and he was appointed commander of the Huaide command.

entries.zh: 張鑒，字德明，瀛州團練使藏英之孫。
entries.en: Zhang Jian, whose courtesy name was Deming, was the grandson of Zang Ying, the regimental commander of Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhang Jian, courtesy name Deming, was a grandson of Zang Ying, regimental commander of Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父裔，以蔭補供奉官。
entries.en: His father Yi received appointment as a palace attendant through hereditary privilege.
entries.literal: His father Yi entered service as a palace attendant through yin privilege.

entries.zh: 鑒本將家，幼能嗜學，入衛州霖落山肄業，凡十餘年。
entries.en: Though from a military family, Jian loved learning from childhood. He went to Linluo Mountain in Weizhou to pursue his studies, spending more than ten years there in all.
entries.literal: Jian came from a military family yet loved learning from youth; he entered Linluo Mountain in Weizhou to study, for more than ten years in all.

entries.zh: 太平興國三年，擢進士第，釋褐大理評事、監泰州紫墟榷務。
entries.en: In the third year of the Taiping Xingguo era (978), he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering official service he was appointed assessor of the Court of Judicial Review and superintendent of the Zixu monopoly office in Taizhou.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was elevated to jinshi rank; upon leaving office robes he became an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review and superintendent of the Zixu monopoly office in Taizhou.

entries.zh: 升朝，為太子右讚善大夫、知婺州，就遷著作郎。
entries.en: Once he entered court attendance, he served as Right Supporter-in-Attendance to the Heir Apparent and prefect of Wuzhou, and was then transferred in place to the post of Secretary of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: Upon entering court attendance he served as Right Supporter-in-Attendance to the Heir Apparent and prefect of Wuzhou, then was transferred in place to Secretary of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 還，拜監察御史。
entries.en: After returning to the capital, he was appointed investigating censor.
entries.literal: Upon return he was appointed investigating censor.

entries.zh: 奉詔決獄江左，頗雪冤滯。
entries.en: By imperial order he adjudicated cases in the lower Yangtze region, clearing many long-standing injustices.
entries.literal: By imperial order he adjudicated cases in the Jiangzuo region, clearing many long-standing injustices.

entries.zh: 曆殿中侍御史。
entries.en: He subsequently served as palace censor.
entries.literal: He served successively as palace censor.

entries.zh: 淳化中，盜起西蜀，王繼恩討平之，而御軍無政，其下恃功暴橫。
entries.en: During the Chunhua era, rebels rose in western Shu. Wang Jien suppressed them, but he governed his troops poorly, and his subordinates relied on their military merit to act with violence and arrogance.
entries.literal: During the Chunhua era, rebels rose in western Shu; Wang Jien suppressed them, but he governed his troops poorly and his subordinates relied on their merit to act with violence and arrogance.

entries.zh: 益州張詠密奏，請命近臣分屯師旅，即遣鑒與西京作坊使馮守規偕往。
entries.en: Zhang Yong of Yizhou secretly memorialized, requesting that close ministers be sent to station troops in separate camps. Jian was immediately dispatched together with Feng Shougui, commissioner of the Western Capital Workshop Office.
entries.literal: Zhang Yong of Yizhou secretly memorialized, requesting that close ministers be sent to station troops in separate camps; Jian was immediately dispatched together with Feng Shougui, commissioner of the Western Capital Workshop Office.

entries.zh: 召對後苑門，面授方略。
entries.en: He was summoned for audience at the Rear Garden Gate and personally instructed in strategy.
entries.literal: He was summoned for audience at the Rear Garden Gate and personally instructed in strategy.

entries.zh: 鑒曰：“益部新復，軍旅不和，若聞使命驟至，易其戎伍，慮或猜懼，變生不測。
entries.en: Jian said, "The Yi region has only recently been recovered, and the army is ill at ease. If the troops hear that envoys have suddenly arrived to reorganize their units, they may grow suspicious and fearful, and unforeseen trouble may arise.
entries.literal: Jian said: "The Yi region has only recently been recovered and the army is ill at ease. If they hear that envoys have suddenly arrived to change their military units, they may grow suspicious and fearful, and unforeseen trouble may arise.

entries.zh: 請假臣安撫之名。”
entries.en: I ask that I be granted the title of pacification commissioner."
entries.literal: I ask that I be granted the title of pacification commissioner."

entries.zh: 太宗稱善。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong praised the proposal.
entries.literal: Taizong praised the proposal.

entries.zh: 鑒至蜀，繼恩猶偃蹇，不意朝廷聞其縱肆。
entries.en: When Jian reached Shu, Wang Jien remained insolent and did not expect the court to have heard of his excesses.
entries.literal: When Jian reached Shu, Jien was still insolent and did not expect the court to have heard of his excesses.

entries.zh: 鑒之行，付以空名宣頭及廷臣數人，鑒與詠即遣部戍卒出境，繼恩麾下使臣亦多遣東還，督繼恩輩分路討捕殘寇，而鑒等招輯反側。
entries.en: Before Jian's departure he was given blank commission documents and several court officials. Jian and Yong immediately sent garrison troops out of the province, sent many of Wang Jien's staff envoys back east, and supervised Jien and his men in pursuing remnant bandits by separate routes, while Jian and the others won over those who were wavering.
entries.literal: Before Jian's departure he was given blank commission documents and several court officials; Jian and Yong immediately sent garrison troops out of the province, also sent many of Jien's staff envoys back east, supervised Jien and his men in pursuing remnant bandits by separate routes, and Jian and the others won over the wavering.

entries.zh: 事平歸朝，未至，拜左諫議大夫、戶部使。
entries.en: When the affair was settled and he was returning to court, he was appointed Left Remonstrance Councillor and commissioner of the Household Bureau before he even arrived.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled and he returned to court, before he arrived he was appointed Left Remonstrance Councillor and commissioner of the Household Bureau.

entries.zh: 初，鑒在南海，李夷庚為通判，謝德權為巡檢，皆與之不協。
entries.en: Earlier, when Jian was in the South Sea region, Li Yigeng served as vice prefect and Xie Dequan as inspector; both were at odds with him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Jian was in the South Sea region, Li Yigeng served as vice prefect and Xie Dequan as inspector; both were at odds with him.

entries.zh: 二人密言鑒以貲付海賈，往來貿市，故徙小郡。
entries.en: The two secretly reported that Jian had entrusted capital to maritime traders for commerce back and forth, and for this reason was transferred to a smaller prefecture.
entries.literal: The two secretly reported that Jian had entrusted capital to maritime traders for commerce back and forth, and for this reason was transferred to a smaller prefecture.

entries.zh: 至是，鑒自陳有親故謫瓊州，每以奉米附商舶寄贍之，又言夷庚、德權憸人貪凶之狀，上意稍釋。
entries.en: At this time Jian explained himself, saying he had relatives and friends exiled to Qiongzhou whom he regularly supplied with stipend grain sent by merchant ships. He also reported the treacherous and greedy conduct of Yigeng and Dequan, and the emperor's suspicions were somewhat eased.
entries.literal: At this time Jian explained himself, saying he had relatives and friends exiled to Qiongzhou whom he regularly supplied with stipend grain sent by merchant ships; he also reported the treacherous and greedy conduct of Yigeng and Dequan, and the emperor's mind was somewhat eased.

entries.zh: 召還，以疾徙知相州。
entries.en: Recalled to court, he was transferred to Xiangzhou on account of illness.
entries.literal: Recalled to court, he was transferred to Xiangzhou on account of illness.

entries.zh: 有芝草生於監牧之室，鑒表其祥異，以為河朔弭兵款附之兆。
entries.en: An auspicious fungus grew in the room of the pasture office. Jian memorialized the marvel, taking it as a sign that the north would lay down arms and submit.
entries.literal: An auspicious fungus grew in the room of the pasture office; Jian memorialized the marvel, taking it as a sign that the north would lay down arms and submit.

entries.zh: 優詔答之。
entries.en: A gracious edict replied to him.
entries.literal: A gracious edict replied to him.

entries.zh: 景德初，卒，年五十八。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Jingde era he died, aged fifty-eight.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era he died, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 淳化三年，召訪以邊事，稱旨，面賜緋魚，令授清資官。
entries.en: In the third year of Chunhua summoned to consult on frontier affairs. Pleasing the emperor he was personally granted the red fish badge and ordered granted a clear-rank office.
entries.literal: In the third year of Chunhua summoned to consult on frontier affairs; pleasing the emperor he was personally granted the red fish badge and ordered granted a clear-rank office.

entries.zh: 翌日，拜監察御史、荊湖南路轉運使。
entries.en: The next day appointed investigating censor and transport commissioner of the Jinghu South Circuit.
entries.literal: The next day appointed investigating censor and transport commissioner of the Jinghu South Circuit.

entries.zh: 未行，改三司鹽鐵判官。
entries.en: Before departing changed to salt and iron administrator of the Three Offices.
entries.literal: Before departing changed to salt and iron administrator of the Three Offices.

entries.zh: 上疏請給兩省官諫紙，又引故事，禁屠月勿報重刑。
entries.en: He memorialized requesting remonstrance paper for officials of the two provinces and also cited precedent forbidding heavy punishments in the slaughter month.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting remonstrance paper for officials of the two provinces and also cited precedent forbidding heavy punishments in the slaughter month.

entries.zh: 會劉式建議請廢緣江榷務，莊力言其非便。
entries.en: When Liu Shi proposed abolishing river-bank monopoly offices Zhuang forcefully said it was not advantageous.
entries.literal: When Liu Shi proposed abolishing river-bank monopoly offices Zhuang forcefully said it was not advantageous.

entries.zh: 出為荊湖北路轉運使。
entries.en: Sent out as transport commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.
entries.literal: Sent out as transport commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.

entries.zh: 五年，李順亂蜀，命與雷有終並兼峽路隨軍轉運、同知兵馬事。
entries.en: In the fifth year when Li Shun rebelled in Shu he was ordered together with Lei Youzhong to concurrently serve as accompanying army transport commissioner of the Gorges route and jointly manage military affairs.
entries.literal: In the fifth year when Li Shun rebelled in Shu he was ordered together with Lei Youzhong to concurrently serve as accompanying army transport commissioner of the Gorges route and jointly manage military affairs.

entries.zh: 或言莊本蜀人，不宜此任，上益倚信之，許以便宜。
entries.en: Some said Zhuang was originally a man of Shu and unsuited to this post. The emperor trusted him all the more and permitted expedient action.
entries.literal: Some said Zhuang was originally a man of Shu and unsuited to this post; the emperor trusted him all the more and permitted expedient action.

entries.zh: 事平，轉殿中侍御史，歷工部、司封二員外郎，特召問討賊方略。
entries.en: When the affair was settled he was transferred to palace censor, served successively as vice minister of works and director of the Ministry of Seals, and was specially summoned to ask strategy for suppressing bandits.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled he was transferred to palace censor, served successively as vice minister of works and director of the Ministry of Seals, and was specially summoned to ask strategy for suppressing bandits.

entries.zh: 薛奎，字宿藝，絳州正平人。
entries.en: Xue Kui, whose courtesy name was Suyi, came from Zhengping in Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Xue Kui, styled Suyi, was a native of Zhengping in Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 父化光，善數術，嘗以平晉策幹太宗行在，召見不用，罷歸。
entries.en: His father Huaguang was skilled in numerology and once offered Taizong a plan for pacifying Jin at the emperor's field headquarters; summoned but not employed, he went home.
entries.literal: His father Huaguang was skilled in numerology and once presented a strategy for pacifying Jin at the emperor's traveling camp of Emperor Taizong; summoned and not employed, he returned home.

entries.zh: 適奎始生，撫其首曰：“是子必至公輔。”
entries.en: Just as Kui was born, he stroked the infant's head and said: "This child will surely rise to chief minister."
entries.literal: Just as Kui was born, he stroked the child's head and said: "This boy will surely reach the rank of chief minister."

entries.zh: 奎舉進士，為州第一，乃推與裏人王嚴，而處嚴下。
entries.en: Kui took the jinshi examination and ranked first in the prefecture, yet yielded first place to his fellow townsman Wang Yan and placed himself below him.
entries.literal: Kui passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the prefecture, yet yielded the place to his fellow townsman Wang Yan and placed himself below Yan.

entries.zh: 進士及第，為隰州軍事推官。
entries.en: After passing the jinshi examination, he became military judicial officer of Xizhou.
entries.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became military judicial officer of Xizhou.

entries.zh: 州民常聚博僧舍，一日，盜殺寺奴取財去，博者適至，血偶涴衣，邏卒捕送州，考訊誣伏。
entries.en: The people of the prefecture often gambled in a Buddhist monastery. One day a thief killed a temple servant and made off with the goods. Gamblers arrived just then, and blood happened to stain their clothes. Patrolmen seized them and sent them to the prefecture, where interrogation forced false confessions.
entries.literal: The people of the prefecture often gathered to gamble in a Buddhist monastery. One day a thief killed a temple slave and took the goods away; gamblers happened to arrive, and blood happened to stain their clothes. Patrol soldiers seized and sent them to the prefecture; under interrogation they falsely confessed.

entries.zh: 奎獨疑之，白州緩其獄，後果得殺人者。
entries.en: Kui alone doubted the case, persuaded the prefect to delay judgment, and later found the real killer.
entries.literal: Kui alone doubted the case, reported to the prefecture to slow the trial, and later indeed obtained the real murderer.

entries.zh: 徙儀州推官，嘗部丁夫運糧至鹽州，會久雨，粟麥漬腐，奎白轉運盧之翰，請縱民還州而償所失。
entries.en: Transferred to judicial officer of Yizhou, he once led corvée laborers hauling grain to Yanzhou. After long rains the grain and wheat rotted. Kui reported to transport commissioner Lu Zhihan and asked to send the laborers home while making good the loss.
entries.literal: Transferred to judicial officer of Yizhou, he once led corvée laborers transporting grain to Yanzhou. Prolonged rain caused the grain and wheat to soak and rot. Kui reported to the transport commissioner Lu Zhihan, requesting to release the people back to the prefecture while compensating the loss.

entries.zh: 之翰怒，欲劾奏之。
entries.en: Zhihan was angry and wanted to impeach him.
entries.literal: Zhihan was angry and wished to memorialize and impeach him.

entries.zh: 奎徐曰：“用兵久，人疲轉餉，今幸兵食有餘，安用此陳腐以困民哉！”
entries.en: Kui said calmly: "The army has been at war for years and the people are exhausted hauling supplies. We are fortunate that military stores are ample—why trouble them with rotten grain?"
entries.literal: Kui said calmly: "The army has been employed a long time and the people are weary of transporting provisions. Now fortunately military food is abundant—why use this stale grain to trouble the people!"

entries.zh: 之翰意解，凡民所失，悉奏除之。
entries.en: Zhihan relented, and all losses borne by the people were memorialized for remission.
entries.literal: Zhihan's mind was eased, and all the people's losses were memorialized for remission.

entries.zh: 改大理寺丞、知莆田縣。
entries.en: He was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Putian County.
entries.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Putian County.

entries.zh: 請蠲南閩時稅鹹魚、蒲草錢。
entries.en: He petitioned to abolish the wartime taxes on salted fish and sedge grass in southern Fujian.
entries.literal: He requested remission of the wartime taxes on salted fish and sedge in southern Min.

entries.zh: 魯宗道
entries.en: Lu Zongdao
entries.literal: Lu Zongdao

entries.zh: 未幾，以足疾請告，上取名藥以賜。
entries.en: Before long, citing foot ailment he requested leave; the emperor selected famous medicines and granted them.
entries.literal: Before long, citing foot ailment he requested leave; the sovereign selected famous medicines and granted them.

entries.zh: 郊祀不及扈從，錫齎如侍祠之例。
entries.en: Unable to accompany the suburban sacrifice, he received gifts according to the precedent for those attending the rites.
entries.literal: Unable to accompany the suburban sacrifice, he received gifts according to the precedent for those attending the rites.

entries.zh: 車駕北巡，徽之力疾辭於苑中。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage toured north, Huizhi, though ill, declined in the palace garden.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage toured north, Huizhi, though ill, declined in the palace garden.

entries.zh: 上顧謂曰：「卿勉進醫藥，比見，當不久也。」
entries.en: The emperor turning to him said, "Sir, take your medicines diligently; when we next meet, it should not be long."
entries.literal: The sovereign turning to him said: "Sir, take your medicines diligently; when we next meet, it should not be long."

entries.zh: 及駐蹕大名，特降手詔存諭。
entries.en: When the halt was made at Daming, a special handwritten edict was sent down to comfort and reassure him.
entries.literal: When the halt was made at Daming, a special handwritten edict was sent down to comfort and reassure him.

entries.zh: 明年春正月，車駕還，又遣使臨問。
entries.en: In the first month of the following spring, when the imperial carriage returned, another envoy was sent to inquire after him.
entries.literal: In the first month of the following spring, when the imperial carriage returned, another envoy was sent to inquire after him.

entries.zh: 卒，年八十。
entries.en: He died, aged eighty.
entries.literal: He died, aged eighty.

entries.zh: 贈兵部尚書，賜其家錢五十萬，絹五百匹。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Minister of War; his family was granted five hundred thousand cash and five hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: He was posthumously honored as Minister of War; his family was granted five hundred thousand in cash and five hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 錄其外孫宋綬太常寺太祝，侄孫偃、集並同學究出身。
entries.en: His grandson by a daughter Song Shou was recorded as Director of Solemnity in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grand-nephews Yan and Ji were both given the jinshi-by-study status.
entries.literal: His grandson by a daughter Song Shou was recorded as Director of Solemnity in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grand-nephews Yan and Ji were both given the jinshi-by-study status.

entries.zh: 韓丕，字太簡，華州鄭人。
entries.en: Han Pi, courtesy name Taejian, was from Zheng in Hua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Han Pi, style name Taejian, was a native of Zheng in Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父杲，晉開運中，為曲陽主簿，契丹攻城，陷沒焉。
entries.en: His father Gao had been registrar of Quyang in the Kaiyun era of Jin; when the Khitans besieged the city, he was taken captive and never returned.
entries.literal: His father Gao, during the Kaiyun era of Jin, served as registrar of Quyang; when the Khitans attacked the city, he was captured and lost.

entries.zh: 母改適他氏。
entries.en: His mother remarried elsewhere.
entries.literal: His mother remarried into another family.

entries.zh: 丕幼孤貧，有志操，讀書於驪山、嵩陽，通《周易》、《禮記》，為人講說。
entries.en: Orphaned and poor from childhood, Pi nevertheless held firm principles. He studied at Lishan and Songyang, mastered the Book of Changes and the Book of Rites, and taught others by lecturing on the classics.
entries.literal: Pi was orphaned young and poor, yet possessed resolve and integrity; he studied at Lishan and Songyang, mastered the Book of Changes and the Book of Rites, and lectured for others.

entries.zh: 常有山林之志，家雖甚貧，處之晏如。
entries.en: He often yearned for a life in the hills, and though his family was desperately poor, he remained entirely at ease.
entries.literal: He often harbored the will to dwell in mountains and forests; though his household was very poor, he remained at ease.

entries.zh: 年長，始學文。
entries.en: He did not take up formal literary study until he was already grown.
entries.literal: Only when he was older did he begin to study letters.

entries.zh: 開寶中，鄭牧知文州，與之偕行，遂薄遊兩川。
entries.en: In the Kaibao era, when Zheng Mu was prefect of Wen, Pi accompanied him on his travels and so made a brief tour through the Two Shu.
entries.literal: During the Kaibao era, Zheng Mu governed Wen Prefecture; Pi traveled with him and so made a brief tour of the Two Shu regions.

entries.zh: 及牧知成都，劉熙古延置門下，掌書奏，以孫女妻之。
entries.en: When Mu became prefect of Chengdu, Liu Xigu took Pi into his household to manage documents and memorials, and married him to his granddaughter.
entries.literal: When Mu became prefect of Chengdu, Liu Xigu invited Pi into his household, put him in charge of documents and memorials, and gave him his granddaughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 「臣嘗讀史，見漢武北築朔方之郡，平津侯諫，以為罷敝中國，以奉無用之地，願罷之。
entries.en: "I have read in the histories that when Emperor Wu of Han established the northern commandery of Shuofang, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, arguing that it would exhaust the empire to sustain a worthless region and urging that the project be abandoned.
entries.literal: "Your servant has read history and seen that when Emperor Wu of Han built the northern commandery of Shuofang, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, holding that it would exhaust China to supply a useless region and asking that it be abandoned.

entries.zh: 上使辯士朱買臣等發十策以難平津，平津不能對。
entries.en: The emperor had the debater Zhu Maichen and others raise ten counterarguments to confound the marquis, and he could not answer them.
entries.literal: The emperor had the debater Zhu Maichen and others raise ten objections to confound Pingjin, and Pingjin could not reply.

entries.zh: 臣以為平津為賢相，非不能折買臣之舌，蓋所以將順人君之意爾。
entries.en: I believe Pingjin was a worthy minister. It was not that he could not refute Zhu Maichen's arguments, but that he chose to align himself with the emperor's wishes.
entries.literal: Your servant holds that Pingjin was a worthy minister and was not unable to refute Maichen's tongue; he was simply accommodating the ruler's intent.

entries.zh: 舊稱朔方，地在要荒之外，聲教不及。
entries.en: Shuofang, as it was known in antiquity, lay beyond the outer marches, where the court's civilizing influence did not reach.
entries.literal: Shuofang was so called of old; its land lay beyond the outer marches, where civilizing influence did not reach.

entries.zh: 元朔中，大將軍衛青奮兵掠地，列置郡縣。
entries.en: During the Yuanshuo reign period the Grand General Wei Qing campaigned vigorously, seized territory, and established a network of commanderies and counties.
entries.literal: In the Yuanshuo era the Grand General Wei Qing took the field vigorously, seized territory, and set up commanderies and counties in array.

entries.zh: 今靈州蓋朔方之故墟，僻介西鄙，數百里間無有水草，烽火亭障不相望。
