entries.en: Lingzhou today occupies roughly the old ground of Shuofang. It stands remote on the western frontier, and for hundreds of li there is neither water nor pasture; beacon towers and frontier posts cannot even see one another.
entries.literal: Present-day Lingzhou is roughly the old site of Shuofang, remote on the western border; for several hundred li there is no water or grass, and beacon towers and frontier posts cannot see one another.

entries.zh: 當其道路不壅，饢饋無虞，猶足以張大國之威聲，為中原之扞蔽。
entries.en: When its roads were open and supply lines secure, it could still magnify the empire's prestige and serve as a bulwark for the heartland.
entries.literal: When its roads were not blocked and supply trains were secure, it could still magnify the great state's prestige and serve as a shield for the central plain.

entries.zh: 自邊境屢驚，凶黨猖熾，爵賞之而不恭，討罰之而無獲。
entries.en: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown ever bolder. Honors and rewards win no deference from them, and punitive campaigns yield no captives.
entries.literal: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown rampant; ennobled and rewarded, they show no deference; punished in campaigns, they are not taken.

entries.zh: 自曹光實、白守榮、馬紹忠及王榮之敗，資糧屝屨，所失至多，將士丁夫，相枕而死。
entries.en: Since the defeats suffered by Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost on a vast scale, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died in heaps upon the roads.
entries.literal: Since the defeats of Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost in great measure, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died piled upon one another.

entries.zh: 以至募商人輸帛入穀，償價數倍；
entries.en: Matters have reached the point where merchants are recruited to deliver grain in exchange for silk, with reimbursement several times the market price;
entries.literal: Matters have reached the point of recruiting merchants to bring silk in exchange for grain, with reimbursement several times the cost;

entries.zh: 孤壤築城，邊民繹騷，國帑匱乏，不能制邊人之命，及濟靈武之急。
entries.en: fortresses are raised on barren ground, frontier populations are in constant uproar, the national treasury is exhausted, and the court can neither command the border peoples nor relieve the crisis at Lingwu.
entries.literal: fortresses are built on barren soil, frontier people are in constant turmoil, the national treasury is depleted, and the court cannot command the border peoples or relieve the crisis at Lingwu.

entries.zh: 數年之間，凶黨逾盛。
entries.en: Within a few years the hostile bands have grown stronger still.
entries.literal: Within a few years the hostile bands have grown ever stronger.

entries.zh: 靈武危堞，巋然僅存，河外五城，繼聞陷沒。
entries.en: Lingwu's perilous walls stand alone, barely intact, while the five cities beyond the river have fallen one after another.
entries.literal: Lingwu's perilous walls stand alone, barely surviving; the five cities beyond the river have fallen one after another.

entries.zh: 但堅壁清野，坐食糗糧，閉壘枕戈，苟度朝夕，未粕出一兵，馳一騎，敢與之角。
entries.en: The garrison merely fortifies its walls and clears the countryside, consumes stored grain, closes the forts and sleeps on its weapons, barely surviving from day to day, never venturing forth with a single soldier or rider to contest the enemy.
entries.literal: They only fortify walls and clear the countryside, sit consuming dried grain, close the forts and sleep on their weapons, barely passing day and night, never sending forth a single soldier or rider to dare contest the enemy.

entries.zh: 此靈武之存無益，明矣。
entries.en: It is plain that holding Lingwu serves no purpose.
entries.literal: That holding Lingwu is of no benefit is clear.

entries.zh: 平津所言罷敝中國以奉無用之地，正今日謂也。
entries.en: What the Marquis of Pingjin said about exhausting the empire to sustain a worthless region applies exactly to our situation today.
entries.literal: What Pingjin said about exhausting China to supply a useless region is precisely what applies today.

entries.zh: 楊億，字大年，建州浦城人。
entries.en: Yang Yi, styled Danian, came from Pucheng in Jianzhou.
entries.literal: Yang Yi, courtesy name Danian, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 祖文逸，南唐玉山令。
entries.en: His grandfather Yang Wenyi had served as magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.
entries.literal: His grandfather Wenyi was magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.

entries.zh: 億將生，文逸夢一道士，自稱懷玉山人來謁，未幾，億生，有毛被體，長尺餘，經月乃落。
entries.en: Shortly before Yi's birth, Wenyi dreamed of a Daoist who introduced himself as the Hermit of Mount Huaiyu coming to call. Soon afterward Yi was born with hair covering his body, more than a foot in length, which did not fall away until a month had passed.
entries.literal: Before Yi was to be born, Wenyi dreamed that a Daoist who called himself the Hermit of Huaiyu came to pay a visit; before long Yi was born, his body covered with hair more than a foot long, which fell off only after a month.

entries.zh: 能言，母以小經口授，隨即成誦。
entries.en: Once he could speak, his mother taught him the Minor Classics by recitation, and he mastered each passage as soon as he heard it.
entries.literal: When he could speak, his mother orally taught him the Minor Classics, and he could recite them at once.

entries.zh: 七歲，能屬文，對客談論，有老成風。
entries.en: At seven he could already draft compositions, and when he conversed with guests he carried himself with uncanny maturity.
entries.literal: At age seven he could compose prose; in conversation with guests he had the bearing of a seasoned man.

entries.zh: 雍熙初，年十一，太宗聞其名，詔江南轉運使張去華就試詞藝，送闕下。
entries.en: Early in the Yongxi era, when he was eleven, Emperor Taizong heard of him and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to examine his literary gifts locally and escort him to court.
entries.literal: Early in the Yongxi reign, at age eleven, Taizong heard his name and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to test his literary skill on the spot and send him to the capital.

entries.zh: 連三日得對，試詩賦五篇，下筆立成。
entries.en: He was granted audience three days running and asked to produce five poems and fu compositions, each finished the moment he set brush to paper.
entries.literal: For three days in succession he was granted audience; he was tested with five poems and rhapsodies, each completed as soon as his brush touched the paper.

entries.zh: 太宗深加賞異，命內侍都知王仁睿送至中書，又賦詩一章，宰相驚其俊異，削章為賀。
entries.en: Taizong was deeply impressed and had the chief eunuch Wang Renrui escort him to the Secretariat. Yi also composed a poem of his own, and the chief ministers, astonished at his brilliance, reshaped their memorials into letters of congratulation.
entries.literal: Taizong was deeply impressed and ordered the chief eunuch Wang Renrui to escort him to the Secretariat; he also composed a poem, and the chief ministers, astonished at his brilliance, trimmed their memorials into congratulations.

entries.zh: 翌日，下制曰：「汝方髫齔，不由師訓，精爽神助，文字生知。
entries.en: The next day an edict declared: "You are still a child, yet without formal schooling your mind is keen—as if heaven itself assisted you—and you know the written word as if born to it.
entries.literal: The next day an edict was issued: "You are still in childhood, yet without instruction from teachers your spirit is keen and divinely aided, and you know writing by innate gift.

entries.zh: 越景絕塵，一日千里，予有望於汝也。」
entries.en: You leave the common herd far behind, advancing a thousand li in a single day. I place great hope in you."
entries.literal: You outstrip the scene and leave the dust behind, a thousand li in a day; I have high hopes for you."

entries.zh: 即授秘書省正字，特賜袍笏。
entries.en: He was immediately appointed corrector in the Secretariat and was specially granted court robe and tablet.
entries.literal: He was at once appointed corrector in the Secretariat and specially granted robe and tablet.

entries.zh: 俄丁外艱，服除，會從祖徽之知許州，億往依焉。
entries.en: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father. When the mourning period ended, his father's cousin Yang Huizhi was serving as prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to stay with him.
entries.literal: Before long he mourned his father's death; when the mourning ended, his father's cousin Huizhi was prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to live with him.

entries.zh: 務學，晝夜不息，徽之間與語，歎曰：「興吾門者在汝矣。」
entries.en: He applied himself to study without pause by day or night. When Huizhi spoke with him privately he sighed and said, "You are the one who will restore our family's fortunes."
entries.literal: He devoted himself to study day and night without rest; when Huizhi spoke with him in private he sighed and said, "The one who will raise our house is you."

entries.zh: 蘇轍論殿試策問，引漢昭變武帝法度事。
entries.en: Su Zhe, in discussing the palace examination questions, cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing the institutions of Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: Su Zhe, discussing palace examination questions, cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing Emperor Wu's institutions.

entries.zh: 哲宗震怒曰：「安得以漢武比先帝？」
entries.en: Emperor Zhezong erupted in anger: "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?"
entries.literal: Zhezong erupted: "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?"

entries.zh: 轍下殿待罪，眾不敢仰視。
entries.en: Su Zhe left the hall to await punishment; no one dared raise his eyes.
entries.literal: Zhe left the hall awaiting punishment; none dared look up.

entries.zh: 純仁從容言：「武帝雄才大略，史無貶辭。
entries.en: Chunren said calmly, "Emperor Wu was heroic in talent and grand in design—the histories carry no word of blame against him.
entries.literal: Chunren said calmly: "Emperor Wu was heroic in talent and grand in design—the histories carry no word of blame.

entries.zh: 轍以比先帝，非謗也。
entries.en: Su Zhe's comparison with the late emperor is not slander.
entries.literal: Zhe's comparison with the late emperor is not slander.

entries.zh: 陛下親事之始，進退大臣，不當如訶叱奴僕。」
entries.en: At the beginning of Your Majesty's personal rule, advancing or dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding servants."
entries.literal: At the start of Your Majesty's personal governance, advancing or dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding servants."

entries.zh: 右丞鄧潤甫越次曰：「先帝法度，為司馬光、蘇轍壞盡。」
entries.en: Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted out of turn, "The late emperor's institutions were ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe."
entries.literal: Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted: "The late emperor's institutions were ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe."

entries.zh: 純仁曰：「不然，法本無弊，弊則當改。」
entries.en: Chunren said, "Not so—law by nature has no flaw; when a law proves flawed, it should be changed."
entries.literal: Chunren said: "Not so—law by nature has no flaw; when flawed, it should be changed."

entries.zh: 哲宗曰：「人謂秦皇、漢武。」
entries.en: Emperor Zhezong said, "People speak of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han."
entries.literal: Zhezong said: "People speak of Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi."

entries.zh: 純仁曰：「轍所論，事與時也，非人也。」
entries.en: Chunren said, "What Su Zhe discussed was the matter and its time—not the man himself."
entries.literal: Chunren said: "What Zhe discussed was the matter and its time—not the man."

entries.zh: 哲宗為之少霽。
entries.en: Emperor Zhezong's anger eased somewhat.
entries.literal: Zhezong's anger eased somewhat.

entries.zh: 轍平日與純仁多異，至是乃服謝純仁曰：「公佛地位中人也。」
entries.en: Su Zhe had often differed from Chunren, but now submitted and thanked him, saying, "Sir, you are a man midway to Buddhahood."
entries.literal: Zhe had often differed from Chunren, but now submitted and thanked him: "Sir, you are a man midway to Buddhahood."

entries.zh: 轍竟落職知汝州。
entries.en: Su Zhe was ultimately stripped of office and made prefect of Ru Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhe was ultimately stripped of office and made prefect of Ru Prefecture.

entries.zh: 范仲淹
entries.en: Fan Zhongyan
entries.literal: Fan Zhongyan

entries.zh: 初，世衡在青澗城，元昊未臣，其貴人野利剛浪㖫、遇乞兄弟有材謀，皆號大王。
entries.en: Earlier, while Shiheng held Qingjian, Yuan Hao had not yet submitted to the Song. Yuan's chief advisers, the brothers Yeli Ganglangrang and Yuji, were men of talent and strategy, and each was called a Great King.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Shiheng was at Qingjian Fort, Yuan Hao had not yet submitted; his nobles Yeli Ganglangrang and the brothers Yuji were talented in strategy and all were styled Great Kings.

entries.zh: 親信用事，邊臣欲以謀間之。
entries.en: They were Yuan's trusted inner circle, and the border officials hoped to drive a wedge between them.
entries.literal: They were trusted intimates in power, and border officials wished to estrange them by stratagem.

entries.zh: 慶曆二年，鄜延經略使龐籍，兩為保安軍守劉拯書，賂蕃部破醜以達野利兄弟，而涇原路王沿、葛懷敏亦遣人持書及金寶以遣遇乞。
entries.en: In Qingli year 2, Pang Ji, commissioner of the Fuyan frontier, twice had Liu Zheng, defender of Bao'an Army, write letters and bribe the tribesman Pochou to reach the Yeli brothers. Wang Yan and Ge Huaimin of Jingyuan circuit also sent envoys with letters and gold and jewels to Yuji.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qingli, Fuyan Frontier Commissioner Pang Ji twice had Bao'an Army defender Liu Zheng write, bribing the tribal people Pochou to reach the Yeli brothers, while Jingyuan Circuit's Wang Yan and Ge Huaimin also sent men bearing letters and gold and jewels to present to Yuji.

entries.zh: 會剛浪㖫令浪埋、賞乞、媚娘等三人詣世衡請降，世衡知其詐，曰：「與其殺之，不若因以為間。」
entries.en: Just then Ganglangrang sent three men—Langmai, Shangqi, and Meiniang—to Shiheng offering surrender. Shiheng saw through the ruse and said, "Better to turn them into a wedge than to kill them."
entries.literal: It happened that Ganglangrang sent Langmai, Shangqi, Meiniang, and three others to Shiheng to request surrender; Shiheng knew it was deceit and said, "Rather than kill them, better use them for estrangement."

entries.zh: 留使監商稅，出入騎從甚寵。
entries.en: He kept them to supervise trade taxes and treated them with conspicuous honor whenever they went abroad.
entries.literal: He retained them to supervise commercial taxes, and in going out and in they were greatly favored in mounted escort.

entries.zh: 有僧王光信者，趫勇善騎射，習知蕃部山川道路。
entries.en: A monk named Wang Guangxin was swift, brave, and expert with bow and horse, and knew every trail in the tribal country.
entries.literal: There was a monk Wang Guangxin, nimble and brave, skilled in mounted archery, thoroughly knowing the mountains, rivers, and roads of the tribal lands.

entries.zh: 世衡出兵，常使為鄉導，數蕩族帳，奏以為三班借職，改名嵩。
entries.en: Shiheng often used him as guide on campaign and sent him repeatedly against tribal camps. He memorialized for him a third-class attendant post on probation and gave him the name Song.
entries.literal: When Shiheng sent troops he often used him as guide, repeatedly raiding tribal camps; he memorialized appointing him Acting Third Class Attendant and changed his name to Song.

entries.zh: 世衡為蠟書，遣嵩遺剛浪㖫，言浪埋等已至，朝廷知王有向漢心，命為夏州節度使，奉錢月萬緡，旌節已至，趣其歸附，以棗綴畫龜，喻其早歸之意。
entries.en: Shiheng wrote a secret letter in wax, sent Song to deliver it to Ganglangrang, and claimed that Langmai and the others had already arrived, that the court knew the king favored the Song, that he had been appointed military commissioner of Xia with ten thousand strings of cash each month, and that the imperial commission was already on its way. He urged quick submission and sketched a tortoise with jujube stems to suggest "return soon."
entries.literal: Shiheng made a wax-sealed letter and sent Song to present it to Ganglangrang, saying Langmai and the others had already arrived, the court knew the king had a heart inclined toward Han, appointed him Military Commissioner of Xia Prefecture with ten thousand strings monthly, insignia of office had arrived, urging his submission, and with jujube strings drew a tortoise to suggest the meaning of early return.

entries.zh: 剛浪㖫得書大懼，自所治執嵩歸元昊。
entries.en: Ganglangrang was terrified, seized Song in his own territory, and handed him over to Yuan Hao.
entries.literal: Ganglangrang received the letter and was greatly afraid; from his own domain he seized Song and returned him to Yuan Hao.

entries.zh: 元昊疑剛浪㖫貳己，不得還所治，且錮嵩穽中。
entries.en: Yuan Hao suspected Ganglangrang of treachery, refused to let him return to his domain, and threw Song into a dungeon.
entries.literal: Yuan Hao suspected Ganglangrang of disloyalty to himself, would not let him return to his domain, and moreover imprisoned Song in a pit.

entries.zh: 使其臣李文貴以剛浪㖫旨報世衡，且言不達所遺書意，或許通和，願賜一言。
entries.en: He sent his minister Li Wengui to Shiheng in Ganglangrang's name, saying he had not understood the letter and that peace might be possible if the Song would send a reply.
entries.literal: He sent his minister Li Wengui to report to Shiheng in Ganglangrang's name, and added he did not grasp the meaning of the letter sent, perhaps peace might be allowed, and begged a word be granted.

entries.zh: 世衡以白籍。
entries.en: Shiheng reported this to Pang Ji.
entries.literal: Shiheng reported this to Pang Ji.

entries.zh: 時朝廷已欲招拊，籍召文貴至，諭以國家寬大開納意，縱使還報。
entries.en: The court was already seeking reconciliation. Pang Ji summoned Wengui, explained the empire's willingness to receive them generously, and sent him back with a reply.
entries.literal: The court already wished to win them over; Ji summoned Wengui, instructed him in the state's broad and open acceptance, and released him to return with report.

entries.zh: 元昊得報，出嵩，禮之甚厚，使與文貴偕來。
entries.en: Yuan Hao received the answer, freed Song, treated him with great honor, and sent him back with Wengui.
entries.literal: Yuan Hao received the reply, released Song, treated him with great honor, and had him come together with Wengui.

entries.zh: 自是繼遣使者請降，遂稱臣如舊。
entries.en: Envoys requesting peace followed in succession, and Yuan Hao submitted as a vassal as he had once done.
entries.literal: From this he successively sent envoys requesting surrender and at last submitted as vassal as before.

entries.zh: 世衡聞野利兄弟已誅，為文越境祭之。
entries.en: When Shiheng learned that the Yeli brothers had been executed, he wrote a memorial text and crossed the border to offer sacrifice for them.
entries.literal: Shiheng heard the Yeli brothers had been executed and composed a text to cross the border and sacrifice to them.

entries.zh: 籍疏嵩勞，具言元昊未通時，世衡畫策遣嵩冒艱險間其君臣，遂成猜貳，因此與中國通，請優進嵩官。
entries.en: Pang Ji memorialized to reward Song, explaining that before Yuan Hao submitted, Shiheng had plotted to send Song through great danger to sow distrust between ruler and ministers, which had opened the way to peace with the Song, and asked that Song be promoted.
entries.literal: Ji memorialized to reward Song, fully stating that before Yuan Hao had submitted, Shiheng had devised the plan and sent Song through hardship and peril to estrange ruler and ministers, thereby achieving suspicion and division, and through this communication with China was opened; he requested preferential advancement of Song's office.

entries.zh: 遷三班奉職。
entries.en: Song was promoted to third-class service attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Third Class Service Attendant.

entries.zh: 後嵩因對自陳，又進侍禁、閤門祗候。
entries.en: Later, when Song appeared at court in person, he was advanced again to palace guard attendant and gatehouse attendant.
entries.literal: Later Song on audience stated his own case and was further advanced to Palace Attendant Guard and Gatehouse Attendant.

entries.zh: 种世衡
entries.en: Zhong Shiheng
entries.literal: Zhong Shiheng

entries.zh: 漢武帝外事四征，內興宮室，財用匱竭，於是修鹽鐵、榷酤、均輸之政，民不堪命，幾至大亂。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned on four fronts and built palaces within until the treasury was drained; he then imposed salt-iron monopolies, wine franchises, and equal-transport levies until the people could hardly endure it and the realm nearly collapsed.
entries.literal: Han Emperor Wu on external affairs campaigned in four directions; within he raised palaces; fiscal resources were exhausted—thereupon he repaired salt-iron, monopoly wine, and equal-transport policies; the people could not bear the command and nearly reached great disorder.

entries.zh: 昭帝委任霍光，罷去煩苛，漢室乃定。
entries.en: Emperor Zhao entrusted Huo Guang, who abolished harsh measures, and the Han house was stabilized.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhao entrusted Huo Guang, abolished troublesome severity, and the Han house was then settled.

entries.zh: 光武、顯宗以察為明，以讖決事，上下恐懼，人懷不安。
entries.en: Guangwu and Mingzong prized minute scrutiny and decided affairs by omens; court and country lived in fear and unease.
entries.literal: Guangwu and Mingzong took scrutiny as clarity and used prognostic texts to decide affairs; above and below were in fear, people harbored unrest.

entries.zh: 章帝即位，深鑒其失，代之以寬厚、愷悌之政，後世稱焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhang came to the throne he deeply reflected on those errors and replaced them with generous and humane government, which later ages praised.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhang acceded, deeply mirrored their errors, and replaced them with generous, mild, and kind government—later ages praise it.

entries.zh: 本朝真宗右文偃武，號稱太平，而群臣因其極盛，為天書之說。
entries.en: Our Zhenzong honored culture over arms and was hailed for Great Peace, yet ministers at the height of prosperity preached the Heavenly Writings.
entries.literal: In our dynasty Zhenzong honored culture and rested arms, called Great Peace, yet the various ministers because of its extreme flourishing made the Heavenly Writings doctrine.

entries.zh: 章獻臨御，攬大臣之議，藏書梓宮，以泯其跡；
entries.en: Empress Zhangxian took power, accepted ministers' counsel, and buried the texts in the spirit palace to erase the episode;
entries.literal: Zhangxian held the throne, gathered great ministers' deliberation, stored the books in the spirit palace to erase their traces;

entries.zh: 及仁宗聽政，絕口不言。
entries.en: when Renzong began to rule, he never spoke of it again.
entries.literal: when Renzong heard government, he closed his mouth and did not speak of it.

entries.zh: 英宗自藩邸入繼，大臣創濮廟之議。
entries.en: Yingzong succeeded from the princely establishment, and ministers raised the Pu Temple controversy.
entries.literal: Yingzong from the princely residence entered to succeed; great ministers created the Pu Temple deliberation.

entries.zh: 及先帝嗣位，或請復舉其事，寢而不答，遂以安靜。
entries.en: When the late emperor succeeded, some asked to revive the issue; he ignored it, and the court remained calm.
entries.literal: When the former emperor succeeded the throne, some asked to revive the affair; he laid it aside without answer, and thereby there was quiet.

entries.zh: 夫以漢昭、章之賢，與吾仁宗、神宗之聖，豈其薄於孝敬而輕事變易也哉？
entries.en: Were Han Zhao and Zhang, or our Renzong and Shenzong, deficient in filial piety or careless about change?
entries.literal: Considering the worth of Han Zhao and Zhang, and our Renzong and Shenzong's sagehood—how could they be thin in filial respect and light in changing affairs?

entries.zh: 臣不勝區區，願陛下反覆臣言，慎勿輕事改易。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to weigh my words again and not lightly overturn established policy.
entries.literal: Your subject cannot bear his slight portion; I wish Your Majesty to turn over your subject's words again and carefully not lightly change affairs.

entries.zh: 若輕變九年已行之事，擢任累歲不用之人，人懷私忿，而以先帝為辭，大事去矣。」
entries.en: If you lightly overturn nine years of settled policy and elevate men long out of favor, men will nurse private grudges under the late emperor's name, and the great cause will be lost."
entries.literal: If one lightly changes what has been practiced nine years, promotes and employs men unused for accumulated years—people harbor private resentment and take the former emperor as pretext—the great affair is lost."

entries.zh: 元老外和內勁，不妄與人交。
entries.en: Yuanlao was outwardly mild and inwardly firm and did not make friends lightly.
entries.literal: Yuanlao outwardly was mild and inwardly was firm; he did not rashly associate with people.

entries.zh: 梁師成方用事，自言為軾外子，因緣欲見之，且求其文，拒不答。
entries.en: Liang Shicheng was then in power and claimed to be Shi's son by a concubine; he sought a meeting and asked for writings, but Yuanlao refused.
entries.literal: Liang Shicheng was then in power, saying himself he was Shi's son by a concubine; by connection he wished to see him and also asked for his writings—he refused and did not answer.

entries.zh: 言者遂論元老蘇軾從孫，且為元祐邪說，其學術議論，頗仿軾、轍，不宜在中朝。
entries.en: Critics then argued that Yuanlao, as Su Shi's collateral grandson, held Yuanyou heterodoxy and imitated Shi and Zhe in learning and opinion, and should not serve at court.
entries.literal: Memorializers thereupon argued Yuanlao was Su Shi's collateral grandson and moreover held Yuanyou perverse talk; his learning and deliberation largely imitated Shi and Zhe—he was not fitting in the central court.

entries.zh: 罷為提點明道宮。
entries.en: He was dismissed to serve as intendant of the Mingdao Palace.
entries.literal: He was dismissed to be Intendant of the Mingdao Palace.

entries.zh: 元老歎曰：「昔顏子附驥尾而名顯，吾今以家世坐累，榮矣。」
entries.en: Yuanlao sighed, "Yan Hui once rode a thoroughbred's tail to fame; I am now honored to suffer for my family name."
entries.literal: Yuanlao sighed: "Formerly Yanzi attached to a thoroughbred's tail and his name was displayed; I today sit in trouble because of family and generation—honored indeed."

entries.zh: 未幾卒，年四十七。
entries.en: He died soon after, at forty-seven.
entries.literal: Before long he died, age forty-seven.

entries.zh: 有詩文行于時。
entries.en: His poetry and prose circulated in his day.
entries.literal: He had poetry and prose circulating in his time.

entries.zh: 蘇轍，字子由，年十九，與兄軾同登進士科，又同策制舉。
entries.en: Su Zhe, courtesy name Ziyou, was nineteen when he and his elder brother Shi both passed the jinshi examination and were examined together in the policy test as well.
entries.literal: Su Zhe, style name Ziyou, at nineteen years of age passed the jinshi examination together with his elder brother Shi, and together also sat the policy examination.

entries.zh: 仁宗春秋高，轍慮或倦於勤，因極言得失，而於禁廷之事，尤為切至。
entries.en: Renzong was growing old, and Zhe worried that the emperor might slacken in his diligence. He therefore spoke at length about what had gone right and wrong, and was especially blunt about matters within the inner court.
entries.literal: Emperor Renzong was advanced in years; Zhe feared he might grow weary of diligence, and therefore spoke to the utmost of gains and losses, while on affairs within the forbidden court he was especially penetrating.

entries.zh: 曰：
entries.en: He said:
entries.literal: He said:

entries.zh: 頌宴客有美堂，或告將兵欲亂，頌密使捕渠領十輩，荷校付獄中，迨夕會散，坐客不知也。
entries.en: While entertaining guests at the Hall of Beauty, Su Song learned that soldiers were plotting a riot; he secretly had ten ringleaders arrested and shackled in prison, and when the banquet ended that evening his guests never knew.
entries.literal: Song entertained guests at the Hall of Beauty; someone reported that soldiers were about to riot. Song secretly had ten ringleaders arrested, shackled, and delivered to prison; when evening came the gathering dispersed, and seated guests did not know.

entries.zh: 及修兩朝正史，轉右諫議大夫。
entries.en: While compiling the standard histories of the two reigns he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee.
entries.literal: When the standard histories of the two reigns were compiled, he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Grandee.

entries.zh: 使契丹，遇冬至，其國曆後宋曆一日。
entries.en: On a mission to the Khitan he encountered the winter solstice; their calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day.
entries.literal: On mission to the Khitan, he encountered the winter solstice; their state's calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day.

entries.zh: 北人問孰為是，頌曰：「曆家算術小異，遲速不同，如亥時節氣交，猶是今夕；
entries.en: The northerners asked which was correct; Su Song said: "Calendar calculations differ slightly in timing. If a solar term arrives in the hour of hai, it is still this evening;
entries.literal: Northerners asked which was correct; Song said: "Calendar experts' arithmetic differs slightly; slowness and speed are not the same. If a solar term crosses in the hour of hai, it is still this evening;

entries.zh: 若逾數刻，則屬子時，為明日矣。
entries.en: but if it passes by several quarters, it falls in the hour of zi and belongs to the next day.
entries.literal: if it passes several quarters, then it belongs to the hour of zi and is tomorrow.

entries.zh: 或先或後，各從其歷可也。」
entries.en: Whether one calendar is ahead or behind, each side may follow its own—that is sufficient."
entries.literal: Whether earlier or later, each may follow his own calendar—that will do."

entries.zh: 北人以為然。
entries.en: The northerners accepted his explanation.
entries.literal: The northerners took this as right.

entries.zh: 使還以奏，神宗嘉曰：「朕嘗思之，此最難處，卿所對殊善。」
entries.en: On his return he reported to the throne; Emperor Shenzong praised him, saying: "I have often pondered this—it is the hardest point to handle, and your answer was excellent."
entries.literal: Returning from his mission he memorialized; Emperor Shenzong commended him, saying: "I have pondered this—it is the hardest point to handle; your reply was especially good."

entries.zh: 因問其山川、人情向背，對曰：「彼講和日久，頗竊中國典章禮義，以維持其政，上下相安，未有離貳之意。
entries.en: He then asked about their terrain and the people's loyalties. Su Song replied: "They have been at peace with us for a long time and have largely adopted Chinese institutions and ritual to sustain their rule; high and low are content, and there is no sign of disaffection.
entries.literal: He then asked about their mountains and rivers and the people's inclinations. He replied: "They have been at peace through treaty for a long time and have largely appropriated China's statutes, ritual, and righteousness to sustain their government; above and below are at ease, and there is no intent of division or defection.

entries.zh: 昔漢武帝自謂：『高皇帝遺朕平城之憂，雖久勤征討，而匈奴終不服。』
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han once said: 'The High Emperor left me the shame of Pingcheng; though I campaigned for years, the Xiongnu never submitted.'
entries.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han said of himself: 'The High Emperor left me the worry of Pingcheng; though I long labored in campaigns and attacks, the Xiongnu in the end did not submit.'

entries.zh: 至宣帝，呼韓單于稽首稱藩。
entries.en: Yet by Emperor Xuan's reign Chanyu Huhanye bowed his head and declared himself a vassal.
entries.literal: By Emperor Xuan's time, Chanyu Huhanye bowed his head and called himself a vassal state.

entries.zh: 唐自中葉以後，河湟陷於吐蕃，憲宗每讀《貞觀政要》，慨然有收復意。
entries.en: From mid-Tang onward the Hehuang region fell to Tibet; whenever Emperor Xianzong read the 《Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Era》 he sighed with longing to recover it.
entries.literal: Tang from the mid-dynasty onward, the Hehuang region fell to the Tibetans; Emperor Xianzong whenever he read the 《Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Era》 would sigh with intent to recover it.

entries.zh: 至宣宗時，乃以三關、七州歸於有司。
entries.en: By Emperor Xuanzong's reign the Three Passes and Seven Prefectures were restored to imperial control.
entries.literal: By Emperor Xuanzong's time, the Three Passes and Seven Prefectures were returned to the regular administration.

entries.zh: 由此觀之，外國之叛服不常，不繫中國之盛衰也。」
entries.en: From this one sees that foreign peoples submit or rebel regardless of whether China is strong or weak."
entries.literal: Viewed from this, foreign states' rebellion and submission are not constant—they are not tied to China's flourishing and decline."

entries.zh: 頌意蓋有所諷，神宗然之。
entries.en: Su Song's meaning was plainly admonitory, and Emperor Shenzong agreed.
entries.literal: Song's meaning probably carried indirect admonition; Emperor Shenzong approved of it.

entries.zh: 呂大防
entries.en: Lu Dafang
entries.literal: Lu Dafang

entries.zh: 熙寧三年，召為岐王侍講。
entries.en: In the third year of Xining he was summoned as lecturer to the Prince of Qi's household.
entries.literal: In Xining year three he was summoned as lecturer to the Prince of Qi's household.

entries.zh: 嘉王出閣，改諸王侍講。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jia left the inner palace school, Mu was reassigned as lecturer to the princes.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jia left the palace school, Mu was changed to lecturer for the princes.

entries.zh: 府僚闕員，御史陳襄請擇人，神宗曰：「如鄭穆德行，乃宜左右王者。」
entries.en: When a post in the princely household fell vacant, Remonstrance Officer Chen Xiang asked that someone be chosen; Shenzong said, "One of Zheng Mu's character is fit to attend a prince."
entries.literal: When a staff post in the princely mansion fell vacant, Remonstrance Officer Chen Xiang asked that a man be chosen; Shenzong said, "A man of Zheng Mu's conduct is fit to stand beside a king."

entries.zh: 凡居館閣三十年，而在王邸一紀，非公事不及執政之門。
entries.en: He spent thirty years in the palace library and twelve years in the princely mansions, never calling at the chief ministers' gates except on public business.
entries.literal: In all he spent thirty years in the palace library, and twelve years in the princely mansions, never visiting the chief ministers' doors except on public business.

entries.zh: 講說有法，可為勸戒者，必反復擿誦，岐、喜二王咸敬禮焉。
entries.en: His teaching had method; whatever could warn or admonish he would repeat and recite again and again, and the Princes of Qi and Xi both honored him.
entries.literal: His lecturing had method; whatever could serve as warning or admonition he would repeat and recite again and again, and the Princes of Qi and Xi both treated him with respect.

entries.zh: 元祐初，召拜國子祭酒。
entries.en: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he was summoned and made Director of the Directorate of Education.
entries.literal: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Education.

entries.zh: 每講益，無問寒暑，雖童子必朝服廷接，以禮送迎。
entries.en: Whenever he lectured on the Book of Changes he did so in heat or cold alike; even boys he received in court dress in the hall and sent away with ritual courtesy.
entries.literal: Whenever he lectured on the Book of Changes he did so regardless of heat or cold; even boys he received in court dress in the hall, seeing them off with ritual courtesy.

entries.zh: 諸生皆尊其經術，服其教訓。
entries.en: The students all revered his classical learning and submitted to his instruction.
entries.literal: The students all honored his classical learning and submitted to his instruction.

entries.zh: 故人張景晟者死，遣白金五百兩，託其孤，穆曰：「恤孤，吾事也，金於何有？」
entries.en: His old friend Zhang Jingsheng, on dying, left five hundred taels of silver, entrusting his orphan to Mu; Mu said, "To comfort the orphan is my duty—what need is there for gold?"
entries.literal: An old friend, Zhang Jingsheng, on dying left five hundred taels of white silver, entrusting his orphan to Mu; Mu said, "To comfort the orphan is my affair—what need is there for gold?"

entries.zh: 反金而收其子，長之。
entries.en: He returned the gold and took in the boy, raising him to adulthood.
entries.literal: He returned the gold and took in the son, raising him to adulthood.

entries.zh: 三年，揚王、荊王請為侍講，罷祭酒，除直集賢院，復入王府。
entries.en: In the third year the Princes of Yang and Jing asked that he lecture for them; he was removed as Director, made drafter in the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and returned to the princely mansions.
entries.literal: In the third year the Princes of Yang and Jing asked that he serve as their lecturer; he was removed as Director and made drafter in the Hall for Assembling Worthies, returning to the princely mansions.

entries.zh: 荊王薨，為揚王翊善。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jing died, he became tutor to the Prince of Yang.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jing died, he served as tutor to the Prince of Yang.

entries.zh: 太學生乞為師，復除祭酒，兼徐王翊善。
entries.en: Students of the Imperial University petitioned that he be their teacher; he was again made Director and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Xu.
entries.literal: Students of the Imperial University begged that he be their teacher; he was again made Director and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Xu.

entries.zh: 四年，拜給事中兼祭酒；
entries.en: In the fourth year he was appointed Supervising Secretary and concurrently Director;
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was made Supervising Secretary and concurrently Director;

entries.zh: 五年，除寶文閣待制，仍祭酒。
entries.en: in the fifth year he was made Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature while still serving as Director.
entries.literal: in the fifth year he was made Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature, still serving as Director.

entries.zh: 孫鼛，字叔靜，錢塘人。
entries.en: Sun Gao, courtesy name Shujing, was from Qiantang.
entries.literal: Sun Gao, style name Shujing, was a man of Qiantang.

entries.zh: 父直官，徙揚之江都。
entries.en: His father, surnamed Zhi, served in office and later relocated to Jiangdu in Yang Prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Zhi held office; the family moved to Jiangdu in Yang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 鼛年十五，遊太學，蘇洵、滕甫稱之。
entries.en: When Gao was fifteen he entered the Imperial University, where Su Xun and Teng Fu spoke highly of him.
entries.literal: At age fifteen Gao entered the Imperial University; Su Xun and Teng Fu praised him.

entries.zh: 用父任，調武平尉，捕獲名盜數十，謝賞不受。
entries.en: Through his father's yin privilege he was appointed commandant of Wuping, where he captured dozens of notorious bandits but refused any reward offered him.
entries.literal: Using his father's privilege, he was appointed Commandant of Wuping, captured several tens of notorious bandits, and declined reward, refusing to accept it.

entries.zh: 再調越州司法參軍，守趙抃薦其材。
entries.en: He was next assigned as judicial aide in Yue Prefecture, and the prefect Zhao Bian commended his abilities.
entries.literal: Transferred again to judicial military aide in Yue Prefecture; the prefect Zhao Bian recommended his ability.

entries.zh: 知偃師縣，蒲中優人詭僧服隱民間，以不語惑眾，相傳有異法，奔湊其門。
entries.en: While serving as magistrate of Yanshi, he found that entertainers from the Pu region were dressing as monks and living among the populace, mesmerizing crowds with vows of silence and rumors of supernatural powers until people thronged their doors.
entries.literal: As magistrate of Yanshi County, actors from Pu in monk's garb feigned and hid among the people, beguiling the crowd by not speaking, with talk passing around of strange methods, rushing to gather at their gate.

entries.zh: 鼛收按姦狀，立伏辜。
entries.en: Gao investigated the case, uncovered the fraud, and swiftly brought the culprits to justice.
entries.literal: Gao investigated and pressed the criminal facts; they immediately submitted to punishment.

entries.zh: 韓縝鎮長安，辟入府；
entries.en: When Han Zong served as military commissioner at Chang'an, he brought Gao onto his staff.
entries.literal: Han Zong was stationed at Chang'an and recruited him into the administration.

entries.zh: 縝去，後來者仍挽之使留，居五年，簽書西川判官。
entries.en: Though Han Zong departed, his successor pressed Gao to remain; he stayed five years before being appointed recorder under the West Sichuan judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zong left, the one who came after still held him back to make him stay; he dwelt five years, then was Recorder of the West Sichuan circuit judge.

entries.zh: 或薦於朝，召對，擢提舉廣東常平。
entries.en: On recommendation to the court he was called for an imperial audience and promoted to intendant of the Guangdong Ever-Normal Granary circuit.
entries.literal: Someone recommended him at court; he was summoned for audience and promoted to intendant of the Guangdong Ever-Normal Granary circuit.

entries.zh: 徽宗初，徙兩浙。
entries.en: Early in the Huizong reign he was transferred to the Two Zhe circuits.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huizong, he was transferred to the Two Zhes.

entries.zh: 由福建轉運判官召為屯田員外。
entries.en: He was summoned from the post of Fujian transport vice-commissioner to become Clerk of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: From Fujian transport vice-commissioner he was summoned as Clerk of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 論曰：賈易初以剛直名，觀其再劾文彥博、范純仁，而斥蘇軾、蘇轍尤甚，何以剛直為哉？
entries.en: Commentary: Jia Yi was first known for blunt integrity—yet when one sees him twice impeach Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren, and attack Su Shi and Su Zhe with special venom, how can he be called upright?
entries.literal: Commentary: Jia Yi was first known for blunt uprightness—yet seeing him twice impeach Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren, and especially reproach Su Shi and Su Zhe, how can this be called uprightness?

entries.zh: 董敦逸於元祐末與黃慶基誣二蘇，以開紹聖之禍，及紹聖則肆詆元祐諸臣，甚至瑤華之冤不能持正，雖終悔而諫，亦何及焉。
entries.en: At the end of Yuanyou, Dong Dunyi and Huang Qingji falsely accused the two Su brothers, opening the calamity of Shaosheng; when Shaosheng arrived he wantonly reviled the Yuanyou ministers, and even in the injustice done to Princess Yaohua could not stand for what was right; though he finally repented and remonstrated, what good did that do?
entries.literal: Dong Dunyi at the end of Yuanyou together with Huang Qingji falsely accused the two Su brothers, opening the calamity of Shaosheng; when Shaosheng came he wantonly vilified Yuanyou ministers, and even in the injustice of Yaohua could not hold to what was right; though he finally repented and remonstrated, what good was it?

entries.zh: 及見蔡京、蔡卞稔惡，乃論其過惡以自文，杯水不足以救車薪之火也。
entries.en: Only when he saw Cai Jing and Cai Bian's accumulated evil did he denounce their crimes to clear himself—a cup of water cannot quench a cartload of burning kindling.
entries.literal: Only when he saw Cai Jing and Cai Bian's accumulated wickedness did he discuss their faults to exculpate himself—a cup of water cannot save a cartload of burning firewood.

entries.zh: 上官均諫切中時事，及不從紹述之議，其為人若可觀，然論呂大防、蘇轍，以之再黜，是亦助紹述者也。
entries.en: Shang Guanjun's remonstrances cut to the heart of current affairs, and in refusing the "continuation" agenda he seemed a man of substance; yet in securing a second demotion for Lü Dafang and Su Zhe, he too served the "continuation" cause.
entries.literal: Shang Guanjun's remonstrances keenly hit the affairs of the time, and in not following the "continuation" program his conduct seemed admirable; yet in getting Lü Dafang and Su Zhe demoted a second time, he too aided the "continuation."

entries.zh: 楊畏傾危反覆，周流不窮，雖儀、秦縱橫，無以尚之，豈徒有三變而已。
entries.en: Yang Wei's treacherous reversals flowed on without end—even the coalition masters Yi and Qin could not surpass him; was it merely three changes?
entries.literal: Yang Wei's subversive reversals flowed on without end—even Yi and Qin in coalition tactics could not surpass him; was it only three changes?

entries.zh: 至於倡紹述以取信哲宗，又謂王安石之學有聖人意，可謂小人無忌憚也哉。
entries.en: To promote "continuation" in order to win Zhezong's trust, and to declare that Wang Anshi's learning captured the sage's intent—such a man may truly be called utterly shameless.
entries.literal: As for advocating "continuation" to win Zhezong's trust, and also saying Wang Anshi's learning had the sage's intent, one could call this a petty man utterly without scruple.

entries.zh: 來之邵盡擊時賢而進章惇、安燾、呂惠卿，又請加美諡於安石，其流惡不已，乃誣人非其子而欲掩其貲，亦何所不至焉。
entries.en: Lai Zhi Shao attacked every worthy man of the age while pushing Zhang Dun, An Tao, and Lü Huiqing forward, and even sought a posthumous honorific for Anshi; his stream of wickedness never ceased—he would falsely deny a man's paternity to seize his property; what would he stop at?
entries.literal: Lai Zhi Shao attacked all worthy men of the time while advancing Zhang Dun, An Tao, and Lü Huiqing, and also asked to add a posthumous honorific to Anshi; his stream of wickedness did not cease—he even falsely claimed a man was not his father's son to seize his property; what would he not do?

entries.zh: 葉濤在太學，已著汙跡，擢第之後，諂安石而從之學，後得曾布之薦，凡元祐名賢貶責制辭，肆筆醜詆，雖有善猶不能自滌，況無可述者乎！
entries.en: Ye Tao had already stained his name at the Imperial University; after passing the examination he flattered Anshi and followed his learning; later, through Zeng Bu's patronage, he drafted every edict demoting a Yuanyou worthy in language of vile abuse—even had he possessed virtue he could not have cleansed himself, much less when there was nothing worth recounting!
entries.literal: Ye Tao at the Imperial University already left filthy traces; after passing the examination he flattered Anshi and followed his learning; later through Zeng Bu's recommendation, for every demotion edict of a Yuanyou worthy he wielded the brush in vile abuse—even if he had virtue he still could not cleanse himself, much less when there was nothing to recount!

entries.zh: 崔台符，字平叔，蒲陰人。
entries.en: Cui Taifu, courtesy name Pingshu, came from Puyin.
entries.literal: Cui Taifu, styled Pingshu, was a native of Puyin.

entries.zh: 中明法科，為大理詳斷官，校試殿帷，仁宗賜以「盡美」二字。
entries.en: He passed the Mingfa examination and became detailed adjudication officer in the Court of Imperial Appeals; examined before the palace curtain, Renzong bestowed on him the two characters "Perfect in Beauty."
entries.literal: He passed the Mingfa branch and became detailed adjudication officer in the Court of Imperial Appeals; he was examined in the palace curtain and Renzong bestowed on him the two characters "Perfect in Beauty."

entries.zh: 熙寧中，文彥博薦為群牧判官，除河北監牧使，入判大理寺。
entries.en: During Xining, Wen Yanbo recommended him as aide in the Office of Herds; he was made Commissioner of Herds for Hebei and entered service as vice-director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.
entries.literal: In the Xining era Wen Yanbo recommended him as aide in the Office of Herds; he was made Commissioner of Herds for Hebei and entered as vice-director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.

entries.zh: 初，王安石定按問欲舉法，舉朝以為非，台符獨舉手加額曰：「數百年誤用刑名，今乃得正。」
entries.en: When Wang Anshi first established the interrogation-to-expose law, the whole court thought it wrong; Taifu alone raised his hands to his forehead and exclaimed: "For centuries penal law was misapplied; now it is finally set right."
entries.literal: At first Wang Anshi established the interrogation-to-expose law; the whole court thought it wrong; Taifu alone raised his hands to his forehead and said: "For hundreds of years penal names were wrongly applied; now it is finally set right."

entries.zh: 安石喜其附己，故用之。
entries.en: Anshi was pleased that Taifu sided with him and accordingly gave him office.
entries.literal: Anshi was pleased he sided with him and therefore used him.

entries.zh: 歷知審刑院，判少府監。
entries.en: He served in turn as director of the Office of Review and vice-director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
entries.literal: He successively served as director of the Office of Review and vice-director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

entries.zh: 復置大理獄，拜右諫議大夫，為大理卿。
entries.en: When the Court of Imperial Appeals prison was reinstated, he was made Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee and Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.
entries.literal: When the Court of Imperial Appeals prison was restored, he was made Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee and Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals.

entries.zh: 時中官石得一以皇城偵邏為獄，台符與少卿楊汲輒迎伺其意，所在以鍛煉笞掠成之，都人惴栗，至不敢偶語。
entries.en: At the time the eunuch Shi Deyi turned imperial-city patrol duty into a criminal investigation; Taifu and Vice Director Yang Ji at once catered to his wishes, manufacturing convictions through torture and beating wherever they went; the people of the capital were terrified—even pairs dared not speak together.
entries.literal: At the time the eunuch Shi Deyi used surveillance patrol of the imperial city as a prison case; Taifu and Vice Director Yang Ji at once welcomed and awaited his intent, everywhere forging cases through torture and beating; the capital people were fearful, to the point they dared not speak even in pairs.

entries.zh: 數年間，麗文法者且萬人。
entries.en: Within a few years nearly ten thousand people were caught up in charges under the letter of the law.
entries.literal: Within several years those entangled in textual law numbered nearly ten thousand.

entries.zh: 官制行，遷刑部侍郎，官至光祿大夫。
entries.en: When the new official system took effect, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and rose to Grandee of Splendid Brightness.
entries.literal: When the new official system was implemented, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and reached the rank of Grandee of Splendid Brightness.

entries.zh: 元祐初，御史林旦、上官均發其惡，出知潞州，又貶秩徙相州。
entries.en: Early in Yuanyou, censors Lin Dan and Shang Guanjun exposed his crimes; he was sent out as prefect of Luzhou, then demoted again and transferred to Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, censors Lin Dan and Shang Guanjun exposed his wickedness; he was sent out as prefect of Luzhou and again demoted in rank and moved to Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 後兼監牧使。
entries.en: He later also served concurrently as Commissioner of Herds.
entries.literal: Later he also served concurrently as Commissioner of Herds.

entries.zh: 卒，年六十四。
entries.en: He died at the age of sixty-four.
entries.literal: He died at sixty-four.

entries.zh: 楊汲，字潛古，泉州晉江人。
entries.en: Yang Ji, courtesy name Qian'gu, came from Jinjiang in Quanzhou.
entries.literal: Yang Ji, styled Qian'gu, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

entries.zh: 登進士第，調趙州司法參軍。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned judicial adjutant in Zhao prefecture.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial adjutant in Zhao prefecture.

entries.zh: 州民曹潯者，兄遇之不善，兄子亦加侮焉。
entries.en: A townsman named Cao Xun was mistreated by his elder brother, and his nephew insulted him as well.
entries.literal: A man of the prefecture named Cao Xun—his elder brother treated him badly, and the elder brother's son also added insult.

entries.zh: 潯持刀逐兄子，兄挾之以走，潯曰：「兄勿避，自為侄爾。」
entries.en: Xun took a knife and chased his nephew; his elder brother grabbed him and fled; Xun cried: "Brother, do not run—I was after the nephew alone."
entries.literal: Xun took a knife and chased the elder brother's son; the elder brother seized him and fled; Xun said: "Elder brother, do not flee—I meant it for the nephew alone."

entries.zh: 既就吏，兄子云：「叔欲紿吾父，止而殺之。」
entries.en: Before the magistrate, the nephew said: "My uncle meant to trick my father into stopping, then kill him."
entries.literal: Once before the officials, the elder brother's son said: "Uncle wanted to deceive my father, stop him, and kill him."

entries.zh: 吏當潯謀殺兄，汲曰：「潯呼兄使勿避，何謂謀？
entries.en: The clerks judged Xun guilty of plotting to kill his elder brother; Ji objected: "Xun shouted for his brother not to flee—how is that a plot?
entries.literal: The clerks judged Xun guilty of plotting to kill his elder brother; Ji said: "Xun called to his elder brother not to flee—how is that plotting?

entries.zh: 若以意為獄，民無所措手足矣。」
entries.en: If courts try cases by inferred intent rather than evidence, the people will have nowhere to stand."
entries.literal: If one judges by intent rather than the case, the people will have nowhere to put hand or foot."

entries.zh: 州用其言，讞上，潯得不死。
entries.en: The prefecture accepted his reasoning; the report went up, and Xun was spared execution.
entries.literal: The prefecture accepted his view; the report went up and Xun escaped death.

entries.zh: 主管開封府界常平，權都水丞，與侯叔獻行汴水淤田法，遂釃汴流漲潦以溉西部，瘠土皆為良田。
entries.en: He superintended the Kaifeng metropolitan Ever-Normal Granary, served as acting Director of the Bureau of Waterways, and with Hou Shuxian implemented the Bian River silt-farming method; they diverted floodwaters from the Bian to irrigate the western districts, turning poor soil into good farmland.
entries.literal: He superintended the Kaifeng metropolitan belt Ever-Normal Granary, held acting appointment as Director of the Bureau of Waterways, and with Hou Shuxian implemented the Bian River silt-farming method; they then diverted the Bian's flood to irrigate the western region and poor soil all became good fields.

entries.zh: 神宗嘉之，賜以所淤田千畝。
entries.en: Shenzong praised the work and granted him a thousand mu of the newly reclaimed land.
entries.literal: Shenzong praised this and granted him a thousand mu of the silted land.

entries.zh: 提點淮西刑獄，提舉西路常平，修古芍陂，引漢泉灌田萬頃。
entries.en: He served as judicial intendant for Huai West Circuit, superintendent of the Western Route Ever-Normal Granary, restored the ancient Shao Marsh, and channeled Han spring water to irrigate ten thousand qing of fields.
entries.literal: He was judicial intendant for Huai West Circuit, superintendent of the Western Route Ever-Normal Granary, restored the ancient Shao Marsh, and channeled Han spring water to irrigate ten thousand qing of fields.

entries.zh: 召判都水監，為大理卿，遷刑部、戶部侍郎。
entries.en: He was recalled to serve as vice-director of the Directorate of Waterways, became Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: He was summoned to serve as vice-director of the Directorate of Waterways, became Director of the Court of Imperial Appeals, and was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 元祐初，以寶文閣待制知廬州。
entries.en: Early in Yuanyou he was made Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Luz.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was made Academician-Awaiting Orders of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Luz prefecture.

entries.zh: 崔台符被劾，汲亦落職知黃州。
entries.en: When Cui Taifu was impeached, Ji was demoted as well and appointed prefect of Huangzhou.
entries.literal: When Cui Taifu was impeached, Ji also was demoted and made prefect of Huangzhou.

entries.zh: 歷徐、襄、越州。
entries.en: He served in turn as prefect of Xuzhou, Xiangzhou, and Yuezhou.
entries.literal: He successively served in Xuzhou, Xiangzhou, and Yuezhou.

entries.zh: 紹聖中，復為戶部侍郎，卒。
entries.en: During Shaosheng he was again made Vice Minister of Revenue, then died.
entries.literal: In the Shaosheng era he again served as Vice Minister of Revenue and died.

entries.zh: 論曰：神宗好大喜功之資，王安石、呂惠卿出而與之遇合，流毒不能止也。
entries.en: Commentary: Emperor Shenzong had a temperament inclined toward grandeur and great deeds. When Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing emerged and found favor with him, the poison spread and could not be checked.
entries.literal: Commentary: Emperor Shenzong had the character to love grandeur and merit; Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing emerged and met with his favor—the poison spread and could not be stopped.

entries.zh: 哲、徽之世，一變而為蔡確、章惇、曾布，又變而為蔡京、蔡卞，日有甚之，而天下亡矣。
entries.en: In the reigns of Zhezong and Huizong, power passed first to Cai Que, Zhang Dun, and Zeng Bu, then to Cai Jing and Cai Bian. Day by day the evil deepened, until the empire was lost.
entries.literal: In the eras of Zhezong and Huizong, it changed once to Cai Que, Zhang Dun, and Zeng Bu, changed again to Cai Jing and Cai Bian—daily growing worse—and the empire was lost.

entries.zh: 乘時起而附之者甚眾，若崔台符、楊汲以獄殺民；
entries.en: Many rose with the times and attached themselves to power—Cui Taifu and Yang Ji, who killed people through lawsuits;
entries.literal: Many rose with the times and attached themselves—such as Cui Taifu and Yang Ji, who killed people through lawsuits;

entries.zh: 呂嘉問以均輸困民；
entries.en: Lü Jiawen, who burdened the people with equalized transport;
entries.literal: Lü Jiawen, who burdened the people with equalized transport;

entries.zh: 董必肆酷，欲害流人以取悅；
entries.en: Dong Bi, who indulged in cruelty and sought to harm exiles in order to please his superiors;
entries.literal: Dong Bi, who wantonly cruel, wished to harm exiles to win favor;

entries.zh: 李南公以反覆詭隨；
entries.en: Li Nangong, with his shifting and opportunistic ways;
entries.literal: Li Nangong, with shifting duplicity;

entries.zh: 虞策以心持兩端；
entries.en: Yu Ce, who kept a foot in both camps;
entries.literal: Yu Ce, who held two hearts;

entries.zh: 郭知章迎合時好，且發實錄之誣。
entries.en: Guo Zhizhang catered to the tastes of the time and moreover exposed the falsehoods in the Veritable Records.
entries.literal: Guo Zhizhang catered to the tastes of the time and moreover exposed the deception in the Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 觀諸人所學與其從政，已多可尚，何樂而為此惡哉？
entries.en: Judging by what these men had studied and how they had governed, much in them was already admirable. Why then did they take pleasure in such wickedness?
entries.literal: Looking at what these men studied and how they governed, much was already admirable—why take pleasure in such evil?

entries.zh: 不過視一時君相之好尚，將以取富貴而已。
entries.en: They did nothing but read the preferences of the ruler and chief minister of the moment, seeking wealth and rank and nothing more.
entries.literal: Nothing but reading the preferences of the ruler and minister of the moment, intending only to obtain wealth and honor.

entries.zh: 設使神宗如仁宗之治，哲、徽承之，必無紹述之禍，雖安石輩亦將有所薰陶，而未必肆其情以至是，況此諸人乎？
entries.en: Had Shenzong ruled as Renzong had, and had Zhezong and Huizong inherited that example, there would have been no calamity of "continuation." Even men like Wang Anshi would have been shaped by such an example and might not have indulged their inclinations so far—much less these lesser figures.
entries.literal: If Shenzong had ruled like Renzong, and Zhezong and Huizong had inherited that, there would certainly have been no calamity of "continuation"; even Wang Anshi and his kind would have been molded by it and might not have indulged their inclinations to such a degree—much less these men.

entries.zh: 世道汙隆，士習升降，係於人主一念慮之趣向，可不戒哉！
entries.en: Whether the age's moral tide ebbs or flows, whether the habits of the scholar-official class rise or fall—all this hangs on the direction of a single thought in the sovereign's mind. Should this not give us pause!
entries.literal: Whether the age's ways sink or rise, whether scholar-official habits fall or ascend, depends on the direction of the sovereign's single thought—should this not be guarded against!

entries.zh: 可不懼哉！
entries.en: Should this not give us dread!
entries.literal: Should this not be feared!

entries.zh: 賈易，字明叔，無為人。
entries.en: Jia Yi, courtesy name Mingshu, came from Wuwei.
entries.literal: Jia Yi, styled Mingshu, was a native of Wuwei.

entries.zh: 七歲而孤。
entries.en: He lost his father when he was seven.
entries.literal: At seven he was orphaned.

entries.zh: 母彭，以紡績自給，日與易十錢，使從學。
entries.en: His mother Peng earned their living by spinning and weaving, giving Yi ten copper cash a day for his schooling.
entries.literal: His mother Peng supported herself by spinning and weaving, giving Yi ten cash each day so he could study.

entries.zh: 易不忍使一錢，每浹旬，輒復歸之。
entries.en: Yi hated to spend even one coin; every ten days or so he would bring the money back to her.
entries.literal: Yi could not bear to spend a single cash; every ten days he would return them.

entries.zh: 年逾冠，中進士甲科，調常州司法參軍。
entries.en: After he came of age, he placed in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial adjutant in Changzhou.
entries.literal: After coming of age he passed the jinshi in the top class and was appointed judicial adjutant in Changzhou.

entries.zh: 自以儒者不閑法令，歲議獄，唯求合於人情，曰：「人情所在，法亦在焉。」
entries.en: He regarded himself as a scholar of the classics, not versed in penal law; when he heard cases each year he looked only for what matched common human feeling, saying, "Where human feeling is, the law is as well."
entries.literal: Considering himself a Confucian scholar unfamiliar with statutes, when he reviewed cases each year he sought only what accorded with human feeling, saying: "Where human feeling lies, the law lies there too."

entries.zh: 訖去，郡中稱平。
entries.en: By the time he left office, the prefecture praised his judgments as even-handed.
entries.literal: When he left at the end of his term, the prefecture called his judgments fair.

entries.zh: 議者或謂敵馬既退，當遂用兵為大舉之計，臣竊以為不然。
entries.en: Some advisers argue that since the enemy cavalry has withdrawn, we should immediately launch a major military campaign. I respectfully disagree.
entries.literal: Some commentators say that since the enemy cavalry has withdrawn, we should immediately use troops for a major campaign. I privately think this is not so.

entries.zh: 生理未固，而欲浪戰以僥倖，非制勝之術也。
entries.en: When our foundations are not yet secure, to gamble on reckless battle is not the way to victory.
entries.literal: When our livelihood is not yet secure, to seek reckless battle for a lucky break is not the art of achieving victory.

entries.zh: 高祖先保關中，故能東向與項籍爭。
entries.en: Gaozu of Han first secured Guanzhong, and only then was able to turn east and contend with Xiang Yu.
entries.literal: The Founder of Han first secured Guanzhong, and thus was able to turn east and contend with Xiang Yu.

entries.zh: 光武先保河內，故能降赤眉、銅馬之屬。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu first secured Henei, and only then was able to subdue the Red Eyebrows, Bronze Horses, and their like.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu first secured Henei, and thus was able to subdue the Red Eyebrows, Bronze Horses, and the like.

entries.zh: 肅宗先保靈武，故能破安、史而復兩京。
entries.en: Emperor Suzong first secured Lingwu, and only then was able to defeat An Lushan and Shi Siming and recover the two capitals.
entries.literal: Emperor Suzong first secured Lingwu, and thus was able to break An Lushan and Shi Siming and recover the two capitals.

entries.zh: 今朝廷以東南為根本，將士暴露之久，財用調度之煩，民力科取之困，苟不大修守備，痛自料理，先為自固之計，何以能萬全而制敵？
entries.en: Today the court takes the southeast as its foundation. Officers and soldiers have long endured hardship in the field; finances are hard to manage; and the people are exhausted by levies. Unless we greatly strengthen our defenses and put our house in order first, how can we be secure and overcome the enemy?
entries.literal: Now the court takes the southeast as its foundation. Officers and soldiers have long been exposed to the elements; finances are troublesome to allocate; the people's strength is strained by levies. If we do not greatly strengthen defenses and painstakingly put our house in order, first planning for self-consolidation—how can we be fully secure and overcome the enemy?

entries.zh: 議者又謂敵人既退，當且保據一隅，以苟目前之安，臣又以為不然。
entries.en: Others argue that since the enemy has withdrawn, we should simply hold one corner of the realm and settle for present security. I disagree with that as well.
entries.literal: Commentators also say that since the enemy has withdrawn, we should for now hold to one corner and scrape by for present security. I again think this is not so.

entries.zh: 秦師三伐晉，以報殽之師；
entries.en: The armies of Qin attacked Jin three times to avenge the defeat at Xiao;
entries.literal: The troops of Qin thrice attacked Jin to avenge the defeat at Xiao;

entries.zh: 諸葛亮佐蜀，連年出師以圖中原，不如是，不足以立國。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang served Shu and sent armies out year after year to recover the Central Plain; without that, the state could not endure.
entries.literal: Zhuge Liang assisted Shu, sending out armies year after year to plan for the Central Plain. Without this, it would not suffice to establish the state.

entries.zh: 高祖在漢中，謂蕭何曰：'吾亦欲東。
entries.en: While still in Hanzhong, Gaozu said to Xiao He, "I too mean to turn east."
entries.literal: The Founder in Hanzhong said to Xiao He: "I too wish to go east."

entries.zh: '光武破隗囂，既平隴，復望蜀。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu, after defeating Wei Xiao and pacifying Long, turned his gaze toward Shu.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu, having defeated Wei Xiao and pacified Long, again looked toward Shu.

entries.zh: 此皆以天下為度，不如是，不足以混一區宇，戡定禍亂。
entries.en: All of them measured affairs by the whole realm; without that outlook, one cannot unify the empire and quell chaos.
entries.literal: All measured the realm as a whole; without this, it would not suffice to unify the land and quell disorder.

entries.zh: 況祖宗境土，豈可坐視淪陷，不務恢復乎？
entries.en: How much more so for the lands of our ancestors—can we sit by and watch them fall without striving for recovery?
entries.literal: Moreover, the lands of our ancestors—how can we sit and watch them fall without striving for recovery?

entries.zh: 今歲不征，明年不戰，使敵勢益張，而吾之所糾合精銳士馬，日以損耗，何以圖敵？
entries.en: If we neither campaign this year nor fight next, the enemy will grow stronger while the elite troops and horses we have assembled are worn down day by day—how then can we hope to defeat them?
entries.literal: If we do not campaign this year or fight next year, the enemy's power will only grow, while the elite troops and horses we have gathered will daily diminish—how then can we plan against the enemy?

entries.zh: 謂宜於防守既固、軍政既修之後，即議攻討，乃為得計。
entries.en: I hold that once defenses are secure and military administration restored, we should then discuss offensive action—that is the sound course.
entries.literal: I say that once defenses are secure and military administration is restored, we should then deliberate on attack—that is the proper plan.

entries.zh: 此二者，守備、攻戰之序也。
entries.en: These two points define the proper order of defense and attack.
entries.literal: These two are the sequence of defense and attack.

entries.zh: 臣聞自昔用兵以成大業者，必先固人心，作士氣，據地利而不肯先退，盡人事而不肯先屈。
entries.en: I have heard that from ancient times those who used armies to accomplish great enterprises first secured the people's loyalty, roused morale, held advantageous ground and refused to retreat first, and did all that human effort required without yielding first.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that from of old those who used troops to accomplish great enterprises first solidified popular resolve, roused the spirit of scholars, held advantageous ground and would not retreat first, exerted all human effort and would not yield first.

entries.zh: 是以楚、漢相距于滎陽、成皋間，高祖雖屢敗，不退尺寸之地；
entries.en: Thus when Chu and Han faced each other between Xingyang and Chenggao, though Emperor Gaozu suffered repeated defeats, he did not yield an inch of ground.
entries.literal: Therefore when Chu and Han faced each other between Xingyang and Chenggao, though Gaozu was repeatedly defeated, he did not retreat a fraction of an inch of territory.

entries.zh: 既割鴻溝，羽引而東，遂有垓下之亡。
entries.en: Once the Hong Canal agreement was drawn and Xiang Yu withdrew eastward, he met destruction at Gaixia.
entries.literal: Once the Hong Canal was divided, Xiang Yu withdrew eastward, and then came the destruction at Gaixia.

entries.zh: 曹操、袁紹戰於官渡，操雖兵弱糧乏，荀彧止其退避；
entries.en: When Cao Cao and Yuan Shao fought at Guandu, though Cao's army was weak and supplies short, Xun Yu dissuaded him from retreat.
entries.literal: Cao Cao and Yuan Shao fought at Guandu; though Cao's troops were weak and supplies scant, Xun Yu stopped his retreat.

entries.zh: 既焚紹輜重，紹引而歸，遂喪河北。
entries.en: Once Yuan Shao's supply train was burned and he withdrew homeward, he lost all of Hebei.
entries.literal: Once Yuan Shao's baggage train was burned, Yuan withdrew homeward and then lost Hebei.

entries.zh: 由是觀之，今日之事，豈可因一叛將之故，望風怯敵，遽自退屈？
entries.en: From this it follows: how can today's crisis be met by watching which way the wind blows, fearing the enemy because one general defected, and hastily retreating?
entries.literal: Viewed thus, in today's affair, how can one, because of a single defecting general, watch the wind and fear the enemy, hastily retreat and yield of oneself?

entries.zh: 果出此謀，六飛回馭之後，人情動搖，莫有固志，士氣銷縮，莫有鬥心。
entries.en: If this plan is adopted, once the imperial carriage turns back popular resolve will waver and no one will stand firm; morale will collapse and no one will want to fight.
entries.literal: If this plan is truly adopted, after the imperial carriage turns back, popular sentiment will waver and none will hold firm resolve; morale will shrink and none will have fighting spirit.

entries.zh: 我退彼進，使敵馬南渡，得一邑則守一邑，得一州則守一州，得一路則守一路；
entries.en: We retreat while they advance, allowing enemy cavalry to cross south — they will take each district and hold it, each prefecture and hold it, each circuit and hold it.
entries.literal: We retreat, they advance — letting enemy horsemen cross south: gain one district and hold one district, gain one prefecture and hold one prefecture, gain one circuit and hold one circuit.

entries.zh: 亂臣賊子，黠吏奸氓，從而附之，虎踞鴟張，雖欲如前日返駕還轅，復立朝廷於荊棘瓦礫之中，不可得也。
entries.en: Rebels and traitors, cunning officials and rogues will flock to them; perched like tigers and spreading like birds of prey, they will make it impossible to turn the court around as before and re-establish government amid thorns and rubble.
entries.literal: Rebels and traitors, cunning clerks and wicked rabble will follow and attach to them, crouching like tigers and spreading like owls — even if one wished as before to turn the carriage and return, re-establishing the court amid thorns and rubble would be impossible.

entries.zh: 至於守備之宜，則當科理淮南、荊襄，以為東南遮罩。
entries.en: As for proper defense, Huainan and Jing-Xiang should be organized as a protective screen for the southeast.
entries.literal: As for what is appropriate in defense, we should organize Huainan and Jing-Xiang as a protective screen for the southeast.

entries.zh: 夫六朝之所以能保有江左者，以強兵巨鎮，盡在淮南、荊襄間。
entries.en: The reason the Six Dynasties were able to hold the lands south of the Yangzi was that their strongest armies and greatest garrisons lay in Huainan and Jing-Xiang.
entries.literal: The reason the Six Dynasties could hold the lands south of the Yangzi was that their strongest armies and greatest garrisons were all in the Huainan and Jing-Xiang regions.

entries.zh: 故以魏武之雄，苻堅、石勒之眾，宇文、拓拔之盛，卒不能窺江表。
entries.en: Thus even the prowess of Cao Cao, the vast hosts of Fu Jian and Shi Le, and the power of the Yuwen and Tuoba clans could not in the end threaten the lands south of the Yangzi.
entries.literal: Thus despite Cao Cao's prowess, the multitudes of Fu Jian and Shi Le, and the might of the Yuwen and Tuoba—none in the end could gaze covetously upon the lands south of the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 後唐李氏有淮南，則可以都金陵，其後淮南為周世宗所取，遂以削弱。
entries.en: When the Later Tang Li house held Huainan, it could make Jinling its capital; once Huainan was taken by Emperor Shizong of Zhou, the dynasty was weakened.
entries.literal: When the Later Tang Li clan held Huainan, they could make Jinling their capital. Afterward Huainan was taken by Emperor Shizong of Zhou, and they were consequently weakened.

entries.zh: 近年以來，大將擁重兵于江南，官吏守空城於江北，雖有天險而無戰艦水軍之制，故敵人得以侵擾窺伺。
entries.en: In recent years great generals have hoarded heavy forces south of the Yangzi while officials hold empty cities north of the river. Though natural barriers exist, there is no proper system of warships and naval forces, so the enemy has been able to raid and probe at will.
entries.literal: In recent years, great generals have hoarded heavy troops south of the Yangzi while officials hold empty cities north of the river. Though there are natural barriers, there is no system of warships and naval forces—hence the enemy has been able to harass and probe.

entries.zh: 今當於淮之東西及荊襄置三大帥，屯重兵以臨之，分遣偏師，進守支郡，加以戰艦水軍，上運下接，自為防守。
entries.en: We should now appoint three supreme commanders east and west of the Huai and in Jing-Xiang, station heavy forces to face the enemy, dispatch detached columns to hold subsidiary prefectures, and build a linked system of warships and naval forces upstream and downstream to defend ourselves.
entries.literal: Now we should establish three supreme commanders east and west of the Huai and in Jing-Xiang, station heavy troops to face the enemy, dispatch detached columns to advance and hold subsidiary prefectures, add warships and naval forces linking upstream and downstream, and thus provide our own defense.

entries.zh: 敵馬雖多，不敢輕犯，則藩籬之勢盛而無窮之利也。
entries.en: Even if enemy cavalry is numerous, it will not dare lightly attack, and the strength of our outer defenses will grow with lasting benefit.
entries.literal: Though enemy cavalry is numerous, they will not dare lightly transgress—then the strength of our outer defenses will flourish, with endless benefit.

entries.zh: 有守備矣，然後議攻戰之利，分責諸路，因利乘便，收復京畿，以及故都。
entries.en: Once defenses are in place, we can then discuss the gains of offensive action, assign responsibility to each route, seize opportunities as they arise, and recover the capital region and the former capital.
entries.literal: Once there is defense, then discuss the benefits of attack—assign responsibility to each route, seize advantage and opportunity, recover the capital region and the former capital.

entries.zh: 斷以必為之志而勿失機會，則以弱為強，取威定亂於一勝之間，逆臣可誅，強敵可滅，攻戰之利，莫大於是。
entries.en: With resolute purpose and without missing the moment, weakness can be turned into strength, authority established and chaos settled in a single victory—traitors can be punished and powerful enemies destroyed. No gain from offensive action is greater than this.
entries.literal: With resolute will and without missing opportunity, we transform weakness into strength, establishing authority and quelling chaos in a single victory—rebellious ministers can be executed, powerful enemies can be destroyed. No benefit of attack is greater than this.

entries.zh: 臣又觀古者敵國善鄰，則有和親，仇讎之邦，鮮復遣使。
entries.en: Your minister further observes that in antiquity friendly neighboring states exchanged marriage alliances, while sworn enemies rarely sent envoys to one another.
entries.literal: Your minister further observes that in antiquity, when neighboring states were friendly, there was marriage alliance; between sworn enemies, envoys were rarely sent.

entries.zh: 豈不以釁隙既深，終無講好修睦之理故耶？
entries.en: Was this not because once enmity runs so deep, there is ultimately no basis for peace and good relations?
entries.literal: Is this not because enmity runs so deep that reconciliation and neighborly harmony are ultimately impossible?

entries.zh: 東晉渡江，石勒遣使于晉，元帝命焚其幣而卻其使。
entries.en: When Eastern Jin crossed the Yangzi, Shi Le sent envoys to Jin, and Emperor Yuan ordered the gifts burned and the envoys turned away.
entries.literal: When Eastern Jin crossed the Yangzi, Shi Le sent envoys to Jin; Emperor Yuan ordered the gifts burned and the envoys rejected.

entries.zh: 彼遣使來，且猶卻之，此何可往？
entries.en: When they came as envoys, they were still turned away—how then can we go to them?
entries.literal: When they sent envoys, those were still rejected—how then can we go to them?

entries.zh: 假道僭偽之國，其自取辱，無補於事，祗傷國體。
entries.en: To pass through a usurping puppet state is to invite humiliation, accomplish nothing, and only injure the dignity of the realm.
entries.literal: Passing through a usurping false state—we invite humiliation ourselves, accomplish nothing, and only injure the dignity of the state.

entries.zh: 金人造釁之深，知我必報，其措意為何如？
entries.en: The Jurchens' provocation runs deep; they know we must retaliate—what then do they intend?
entries.literal: The Jurchens' provocation runs deep; they know we must retaliate—what do they intend?

entries.zh: 而我方且卑辭厚幣，屈體以求之，其不推誠以見信，決矣。
entries.en: Yet we demean ourselves with humble words and rich gifts, bowing low to seek peace—they will assuredly not treat us with sincerity or trust.
entries.literal: Yet we demean ourselves with humble words and rich gifts, bowing our bodies to seek peace—they will assuredly not treat us with sincerity or trust.

entries.zh: 器幣禮物，所費不貲，使軺往來，坐索士氣，而又邀我以必不可從之事，制我以必不敢為之謀，是和卒不成，而徒為此擾擾也。
entries.en: Vessels, silks, and gifts cost incalculable sums; envoys shuttle back and forth, draining morale; and they impose terms we cannot accept and constrain plans we dare not pursue—peace will never be achieved, and all this bustle is for nothing.
entries.literal: Vessels, silks, and gifts cost incalculable sums; envoys shuttle back and forth, draining morale; and they impose on us what we absolutely cannot agree to, constraining us from plans we must dare not make—peace in the end will not be achieved, and all this bustle is for nothing.

entries.zh: 非特如此，于吾自治自強之計，動輒相妨，實有所害。
entries.en: Not only that—it constantly obstructs our plans for self-governance and self-strengthening and truly does harm.
entries.literal: Not only this—it actively obstructs our plans for self-governance and self-strengthening and truly does harm.

entries.zh: 金人二十餘年，以此策破契丹、困中國，而終莫之悟。
entries.en: For more than twenty years the Jurchens have used this strategy to break the Khitans and trap China, and we have never awakened to it.
entries.literal: For over twenty years the Jurchens have used this strategy to break the Khitans and trap China—and we have never awakened to it.

entries.zh: 夫辨是非利害者，人心所同，豈真不悟哉？
entries.en: Discerning right from wrong and benefit from harm is common to all hearts—are we truly unaware?
entries.literal: Discerning right from wrong and benefit from harm is what all hearts share—are we truly unaware?

entries.zh: 聊復用此以僥倖萬一，曾不知為吾害者甚大，此古人所謂幾何僥倖而不喪人之國者也。
entries.en: We simply employ it again hoping for one chance in ten thousand, never realizing how greatly it harms us—this is what the ancients meant by gambling on luck until one loses one's kingdom.
entries.literal: We simply employ it again hoping for one chance in ten thousand, never realizing how greatly it harms us—this is what the ancients called: how much luck before one loses one's kingdom?

entries.zh: 臣願自今以往，勿復遣和議之使，可乎？
entries.en: Your minister humbly asks that from this day forward no peace envoys be sent—is that acceptable?
entries.literal: Your minister humbly hopes that from this day forward no peace envoys will be sent—is this acceptable?

entries.zh: 淮西酈瓊以全軍叛歸劉豫，綱指陳朝廷有措置失當者、深可痛惜者及當監前失以圖方來者凡十有五事，奏之。
entries.en: When Li Qiong of Huai West defected to Liu Yu with his entire army, Li Gang identified fifteen problems — missteps in the court's handling, painful failures, and lessons to be drawn for the future — and submitted a memorial.
entries.literal: In Huai West, Li Qiong defected with his entire army to Liu Yu. Gang pointed out fifteen matters — where the court's arrangements were wrong, what was deeply regrettable, and what should be learned from past errors for the future — and memorialized them.

entries.zh: 張浚引咎去相位，言者引漢武誅王恢為比。
entries.en: Zhang Jun accepted blame and left the chancellorship; critics compared the case to Emperor Wu of Han executing Wang Hui.
entries.literal: Zhang Jun took blame and left the chancellorship; some memorialists compared this to Emperor Wu of Han executing Wang Hui.

entries.zh: 綱奏曰：「臣竊見張浚罷相，言者引武帝誅王恢事以為比。
entries.en: Li Gang memorialized: "I have seen Zhang Jun removed from office, with critics citing Emperor Wu's execution of Wang Hui as a parallel.
entries.literal: Gang memorialized: "Your subject has seen Zhang Jun removed from the chancellorship; memorialists cite Emperor Wu's execution of Wang Hui as a parallel.

entries.zh: 臣恐智謀之士捲舌而不談兵，忠義之士扼腕而無所發憤，將士解體而不用命，州郡望風而無堅城，陛下將誰與立國哉？
entries.en: I fear that strategists will fall silent and speak no more of war, loyal men will clench their fists with nowhere to vent their passion, troops will lose heart and refuse to obey, and prefectures will watch which way the wind blows and offer no stout defense — with whom then will Your Majesty sustain the state?
entries.literal: Your subject fears that men of strategy will roll up their tongues and speak no more of war, men of loyalty will wring their wrists with nowhere to vent their passion, troops will dissolve and obey no commands, prefectures and commanderies will watch the wind and have no stout walls — with whom will Your Majesty establish the state?

entries.zh: 張浚措置失當，誠為有罪，然其區區徇國之心，有可矜者。
entries.en: Zhang Jun's arrangements were indeed wrong and he was truly at fault, yet his sincere, if limited, devotion to the state deserves some compassion.
entries.literal: Zhang Jun's arrangements were indeed wrong and he is truly guilty, yet his petty heart devoted to the state has something worthy of pity.

entries.zh: 願少寬假，以責來效。」
entries.en: I pray he may be shown some leniency and held to future results."
entries.literal: I wish he may be given some leniency and held to future achievement."

entries.zh: 李綱 下
entries.en: Li Gang (continued)
entries.literal: Li Gang, Part Two

entries.zh: 所方招來豪傑，以王彥為都統制，岳飛為準備將，而李綱已罷相。
entries.en: Suo was just recruiting bold men, appointing Wang Yan overall commander and Yue Fei preparation general, when Li Gang was already removed from the chief ministership.
