entries.literal: Suo was just recruiting heroes, making Wang Yan overall commander and Yue Fei preparation general, but Li Gang had already been dismissed as chief minister.

entries.zh: 朝廷以王圭代之，所落直龍圖閣，嶺南安置。
entries.en: The court replaced him with Wang Gui; Suo lost his Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion title and was exiled to Lingnan.
entries.literal: The court replaced him with Wang Gui; Suo was stripped of Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion and settled in Lingnan.

entries.zh: 卒於貶所。
entries.en: He died in exile.
entries.literal: He died at his place of exile.

entries.zh: 子宗本，以岳飛奏補官。
entries.en: His son Zongben was given office on Yue Fei's recommendation.
entries.literal: His son Zongben received an official appointment through Yue Fei's memorial.

entries.zh: 李光 許翰 許景衡 張愨 張所 陳禾 蔣猷
entries.en: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, and Jiang You
entries.literal: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, Jiang You

entries.zh: 既而金專事殺戮，上意中悔，思退復密令孫造諭敵以重兵脅和。
entries.en: When the Jin turned to slaughter the emperor regretted it; Situi secretly had Sun Zao tell them to coerce peace with heavy troops.
entries.literal: Before long the Jin devoted themselves to slaughter; the emperor's heart midway regretted; Situi again secretly had Sun Zao tell the enemy to coerce peace with heavy troops.

entries.zh: 上聞有敵兵，命建康都統王彥等禦之，仍命思退督江、淮軍，辭不行。
entries.en: Hearing of enemy troops, the emperor ordered Wang Yan to resist and Situi to supervise Jiang and Huai armies; he declined.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of enemy troops he ordered Jiankang Commander Wang Yan and others to resist, and also ordered Situi to supervise Jiang and Huai armies; he declined and would not go.

entries.zh: 僕散忠義自清河口渡淮，言者極論思退急和撤備之罪，遂罷相，尋責居永州。
entries.en: Pusan Zhongyi crossed the Huai at Qinghekou; critics attacked Situi for rushing peace and withdrawing defenses; he was dismissed and banished to Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Pusan Zhongyi crossed the Huai at Qinghekou; remonstrators fiercely criticized Situi for urgently seeking peace and withdrawing defenses; he was dismissed as chancellor and soon banished to Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 於是太學生張觀等七十二人上書，論思退、王之望、尹穡等奸邪誤國，招致敵人，請斬之。
entries.en: Seventy-two Imperial Academy students led by Zhang Guan memorialized that Situi, Wang Zhiwang, and Yin Ji had misled the state and invited the enemy, begging their execution.
entries.literal: Thereupon seventy-two students of the Imperial Academy led by Zhang Guan memorialized that Situi, Wang Zhiwang, Yin Ji, and others were wicked and misled the state, inviting the enemy, and begged their execution.

entries.zh: 思退憂悸死。
entries.en: Situi died of fear and agitation.
entries.literal: Situi died of fear and agitation.

entries.zh: 白時中 徐處仁 馮澥 王倫 宇文虛中 湯思退
entries.en: Bai Shizhong, Xu Churen, Feng Xie, Wang Lun, Yu Wenxuzhong, and Tang Situi
entries.literal: Bai Shizhong, Xu Churen, Feng Xie, Wang Lun, Yu Wenxuzhong, Tang Situi

entries.zh: 兼侍講，兼中書舍人。
entries.en: He was also made lecturer-in-waiting and drafting officer of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was concurrently lecturer-in-waiting and drafting officer of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 未幾，辭直學士院，從之。
entries.en: Before long he resigned his Hanlin post, and the emperor assented.
entries.literal: Before long he resigned the Hanlin Academy post, and the emperor assented.

entries.zh: 張說再除簽書樞密院，給事中莫濟封還錄黃，必大奏曰：「昨舉朝以為不可，陛下亦自知其誤而止之矣。
entries.en: Zhang Yue was again appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs. The supervisory secretary Mo Ji returned the appointment record. Bida memorialized, "Yesterday the whole court held this impossible, and Your Majesty yourself knew it was a mistake and stopped it.
entries.literal: Zhang Yue was again appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs; the supervisory secretary Mo Ji returned the yellow record; Bida memorialized: "Yesterday the whole court held this impossible, and Your Majesty yourself knew it was a mistake and stopped it.

entries.zh: 曾未周歲，此命復出。
entries.en: Less than a year has passed, and the appointment has reappeared.
entries.literal: Not yet a full year has passed, and this appointment has reappeared.

entries.zh: 貴戚預政，公私兩失，臣不敢具草。」
entries.en: When imperial kin interfere in government, both public and private interest suffer. I dare not draft the document."
entries.literal: Imperial kin interfering in government — public and private both lose; your servant dares not draft the document."

entries.zh: 上批：「王嚴疾速撰入。
entries.en: The emperor annotated, "Wang Yan — draft it at once.
entries.literal: The emperor annotated: "Wang Yan — draft it immediately.

entries.zh: 濟、必大予宮觀，日下出國門。」
entries.en: Mo Ji and Bida were given palace-temple posts and ordered out of the capital gate that same day."
entries.literal: Mo Ji and Bida were given palace-temple posts and ordered to leave the capital gate that very day."

entries.zh: 說露章薦濟、必大，於是濟除溫州，必大除建寧府。
entries.en: Yue submitted an open memorial recommending Mo Ji and Bida. Mo Ji was then appointed to Wenzhou and Bida to Jianning Prefecture.
entries.literal: Yue submitted an open memorial recommending Mo Ji and Bida; thereupon Mo Ji was appointed to Wenzhou and Bida to Jianning Prefecture.

entries.zh: 濟被命即出，必大至豐城稱疾而歸，濟聞之大悔。
entries.en: Mo Ji left as soon as he received the order. Bida reached Fengcheng, pleaded illness, and returned home. When Mo Ji heard of this he was filled with regret.
entries.literal: Mo Ji, on receiving the order, departed at once; Bida reached Fengcheng, pleaded illness, and returned home; when Mo Ji heard of this he deeply regretted it.

entries.zh: 必大三請祠，以此名益重。
entries.en: Bida thrice requested a temple post, and his reputation grew all the greater for it.
entries.literal: Bida thrice requested a temple post, and by this his reputation grew heavier.

entries.zh: 周必大
entries.en: Zhou Bida
entries.literal: Zhou Bida

entries.zh: 王炎宣撫川、陝，辟為幹辦公事。
entries.en: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi and recruited him as administrative officer.
entries.literal: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Chuan and Shan and recruited him as administrative officer.

entries.zh: 游為炎陳進取之策，以為經略中原必自長安始，取長安必自隴右始。
entries.en: You presented Yan a strategy of advance: to recover the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.
entries.literal: You presented Yan a strategy of advance, holding that to plan the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.

entries.zh: 當積粟練兵，有釁則攻，無則守。
entries.en: Accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when opportunity opens, defend when it does not.
entries.literal: One should accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when there is an opening, defend when there is none.

entries.zh: 吳璘子挺代掌兵，頗驕恣，傾財結士，屢以過誤殺人，炎莫誰何。
entries.en: Wu Lin's son Ting took command, arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win scholars and repeatedly killing men through negligence — Yan could not restrain him.
entries.literal: Wu Lin's son Ting took command of the army, quite arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win over scholars, repeatedly killing men through errors — Yan could do nothing.

entries.zh: 游請以玠子拱代挺。
entries.en: You asked that Wu Jie's son Gong replace Ting.
entries.literal: You asked that Jie's son Gong replace Ting.

entries.zh: 炎曰：「拱怯而寡謀，遇敵必敗。」
entries.en: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; he will surely be defeated."
entries.literal: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; meeting the enemy he will surely be defeated."

entries.zh: 游曰：「使挺遇敵，安保其不敗。
entries.en: You replied: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?
entries.literal: You said: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?

entries.zh: 就令有功，愈不可駕馭。」
entries.en: Even if he won battles, he would be harder still to control."
entries.literal: Even if he had merit, he would be all the harder to control."

entries.zh: 及挺子曦僭叛，游言始驗。
entries.en: When Ting's son Xi rebelled, You's warning was vindicated.
entries.literal: When Ting's son Xi rebelled in usurpation, You's words were verified.

entries.zh: 樓鑰，字大防，明州鄞縣人。
entries.en: Lou Yao, courtesy name Dafang, came from Yin County in Mingzhou.
entries.literal: Lou Yao, styled Dafang, was a native of Yin County in Ming Prefecture.

entries.zh: 隆興元年，試南宮，有司偉其辭藝，欲以冠多士，策偶犯舊諱，知貢舉洪遵奏，得旨以冠末等。
entries.en: In Longxing 1 (1163), he sat for the metropolitan examination. The examiners admired his writing and intended to rank him first, but his policy essay inadvertently violated an old naming taboo. Chief examiner Hong Zun reported this, and by imperial order Lou was placed last among the highest tier of graduates.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he tested at the Southern Palace examination; the officials admired his literary skill and wished to place him first among the successful candidates, but his policy essay accidentally violated an old taboo name; Hong Zun, the chief examiner, memorialized, and he received the imperial decision to be ranked last among the top tier.

entries.zh: 投贄謝諸公，考官胡銓稱之曰：「此翰林才也。」
entries.en: When he submitted a letter of thanks to the examiners, Hu Quan, one of the examiners, praised him: "This man has the makings of a Hanlin academician."
entries.literal: Presenting a letter of thanks to the examiners, the examiner Hu Quan praised him, saying: "This is talent fit for the Hanlin Academy."

entries.zh: 試教官，調溫州教授，為敕令所刪定官，修《淳熙法》。
entries.en: He passed the instructor examination, was appointed professor at Wenzhou, served as a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and helped compile the Chunxi Code.
entries.literal: He passed the instructor examination, was assigned as professor at Wenzhou, served as a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and compiled the Chunxi Code.

entries.zh: 議者欲降太學釋奠為中祀，鑰曰：「乘輿臨幸，於先聖則拜，武成則肅揖，其禮異矣，可鈞敵乎？」
entries.en: Debaters proposed lowering the Imperial Academy's Confucian sacrifice from a major to a medium-grade rite. Lou objected: "When the emperor visits in person, he bows to Confucius but only performs a formal clasped-hand salute at the Wu Cheng shrine — the ceremonies are already unequal. How can they be treated as equivalent?"
entries.literal: Some in debate wished to downgrade the Imperial Academy's sacrifice to Confucius to a medium-grade rite; Yao said: "When the imperial carriage visits in person, one bows to the Former Sage but performs a solemn bow with hands clasped to Wu Cheng — the rites already differ; can they be made equal?"

entries.zh: 以淮西宣撫知廬州。
entries.en: As Huaixi pacification commissioner he governed Luzhou.
entries.literal: As Huaixi Pacification Commissioner he governed Luzhou.

entries.zh: 劉豫子麟合金兵大入，民情洶懼。
entries.en: Liu Yu's son Lin joined the Jin armies in a major invasion, and the people were greatly alarmed.
entries.literal: Liu Yu's son Lin joined Jin forces in a major invasion and popular sentiment was greatly alarmed.

entries.zh: 宣撫司統制張琦者，冀乘危為亂，驅居民越江南走。
entries.en: The pacification commission's controller Zhang Qi hoped to exploit the crisis to stir rebellion and drove the residents to flee south across the Yangzi.
entries.literal: The pacification commission's controller Zhang Qi hoped to take advantage of the crisis to create disorder and drove the residents to flee south across the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 欲先脅悆出，擁甲士數千突入，露刃登樓，揚白麾，左右驚潰，迫悆上馬。
entries.en: He meant first to force Chou Yu to flee, led several thousand armored men in a sudden assault, bared their blades and climbed the tower, waved a white banner, and as attendants fled in panic forced Yu onto a horse.
entries.literal: He wished first to coerce Yu to flee, led several thousand armored soldiers in a sudden entry, bared blades and ascended the tower, waved a white banner, attendants fled in alarm, and Yu was forced onto a horse.

entries.zh: 悆徐謂曰：「若輩無守土責，吾當以死徇國，寇未至而逃，人何賴焉。」
entries.en: Chou Yu said calmly, "You bear no duty to guard this territory. I shall die for the state. If we flee before the enemy even arrives, whom can the people rely on?"
entries.literal: Yu said calmly: "You have no responsibility to guard the territory; I shall die for the state. If we flee before the enemy arrives, whom can the people rely on?"

entries.zh: 堅不為動，神色無少異。
entries.en: He refused to budge, his expression unchanged.
entries.literal: He firmly would not move, his expression showing not the slightest change.

entries.zh: 琦等錯愕，遽散其徒，人心遂定。
entries.en: Zhang Qi and his men were abashed and hastily dispersed their followers, and popular sentiment settled.
entries.literal: Qi and the others were startled and abashed and hastily dispersed their followers; popular sentiment was thereby settled.

entries.zh: 時金人出入近境，悆求援於宣撫司，不報。
entries.en: Jin troops were then moving in and out of the nearby borderlands. Chou Yu requested aid from the pacification commission but received no reply.
entries.literal: At that time Jin troops moved in and out of the nearby borderlands; Yu requested aid from the pacification commission but received no reply.

entries.zh: 又遣其子自間道赴朝廷告急，雖旌其子以官，而援卒不至。
entries.en: He also sent his son by a secret route to report the emergency to the court. Though his son was rewarded with an office, relief troops never came.
entries.literal: He also sent his son by a secret route to the court to report the emergency; though the son was rewarded with an office, relief troops never arrived.

entries.zh: 帝方下詔親征，而詔亦不至淮甸，喧言將棄兩淮為保江計。
entries.en: The emperor had just issued an edict for a personal campaign, yet the edict never reached the Huai region, and rumor spread that the two Huai districts would be abandoned to secure the Yangzi.
entries.literal: The Emperor had just issued an edict for a personal campaign, yet the edict also did not reach the Huai region, and rumor spread that the two Huai districts would be abandoned to secure the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 悆錄詔語揭之郡縣，讀者至流涕，咸思自奮。
entries.en: Chou Yu copied the edict and posted it in the prefectures and counties. Readers wept, and all resolved to fight.
entries.literal: Yu copied the edict's words and posted them in prefectures and counties; readers wept, and all wished to rouse themselves.

entries.zh: 監押閻僅死於賊，餘眾來歸，州帑匱竭，無以為賞，悆悉引班坐，犒以酒食，慰勞之，眾皆感勵。
entries.en: Supervisor Yan Jin had died fighting bandits, and the survivors came in. The prefectural treasury was empty and there was nothing for rewards. Chou Yu had them all sit in ranks, feasted them with food and drink, and comforted them—and all were deeply moved.
entries.literal: Supervisor Yan Jin died at the hands of bandits; the remaining troops came to submit. The prefectural treasury was exhausted and there was nothing for rewards; Yu had them all sit in ranks, entertained them with food and drink, and comforted them—and all were moved and encouraged.

entries.zh: 募廬、壽兵得數百，益鄉兵二千，出奇直抵壽春城下，敵三戰皆北，卻走度淮。
entries.en: He recruited several hundred troops from Lu and Shou, added two thousand local militia, and launched a surprise attack straight to Shouchun. The enemy was defeated in three battles and retreated across the Huai.
entries.literal: He recruited several hundred troops from Lu and Shou, added two thousand local militia, made a surprise attack straight to the walls of Shouchun, the enemy was defeated in three battles and retreated across the Huai.

entries.zh: 其後麟復增兵來寇，悆復壽春，俘馘甚眾，獲旗械數千，焚糧船百餘艘，降渤海首領二人。
entries.en: Later Lin again reinforced his army to invade. Chou Yu recovered Shouchun, took many prisoners and heads, seized thousands of banners and weapons, burned more than a hundred grain boats, and received the surrender of two Bohai chieftains.
entries.literal: Later Lin again increased troops to invade; Yu recovered Shouchun, took many captives and heads, seized thousands of banners and weapons, burned more than a hundred grain boats, and received the surrender of two Bohai chieftains.

entries.zh: 麟復以步騎數千至合肥，諜言兀朮為之殿，人心怖駭，不知所為。
entries.en: Lin again advanced on Hefei with several thousand foot and horse. Spies reported that Wuzhu was covering the rear, and the people were terrified, not knowing what to do.
entries.literal: Lin again came to Hefei with several thousand infantry and cavalry; spies reported that Wuzhu was covering the rear, and people's hearts were terrified, not knowing what to do.

entries.zh: 會京西制置使遣牛皋統兵適至，悆顧左右曰：「召牛觀察來擊賊。」
entries.en: Just then the Jingxi commissioner sent Niu Gao with troops, who arrived in time. Chou Yu turned to his attendants and said, "Summon Commissioner Niu to attack the enemy."
entries.literal: It happened that the Jingxi Commissioner had sent Niu Gao leading troops just arriving; Yu turned to his attendants and said: "Summon Investigating Commissioner Niu to attack the bandits."

entries.zh: 皋既至，以忠義撼之，皋素勇甚，以二千餘騎馳出，短兵相接，所向披靡，敵稍懾，散而復集者三。
entries.en: When Niu Gao arrived, Yu stirred him with talk of loyalty and righteousness. Niu Gao was famously brave and charged out with more than two thousand cavalry in close combat, sweeping all before him. The enemy wavered and scattered and regathered three times.
entries.literal: When Gao arrived, Yu stirred him with talk of loyalty and righteousness; Gao was always very brave and charged out with more than two thousand cavalry, closed in hand-to-hand, swept all before him, the enemy was somewhat cowed, and scattered and regathered three times.

entries.zh: 其副徐慶忽墜馬，敵競赴之，皋掖以上，手刜數人，因免胄大呼曰：「我牛皋也，嘗四敗兀朮，可來決死。」
entries.en: His lieutenant Xu Qing suddenly fell from his horse and the enemy rushed at him. Gao pulled him up, cut down several men with his own hand, then removed his helmet and shouted, "I am Niu Gao! I have defeated Wuzhu four times—come and fight to the death!"
entries.literal: His lieutenant Xu Qing suddenly fell from his horse and the enemy rushed upon him; Gao hauled him up, with his own hand cut down several men, then removed his helmet and cried loudly: "I am Niu Gao—I have four times defeated Wuzhu; come and fight to the death."

entries.zh: 寇畏其名，遂自潰。
entries.en: The enemy feared his name and broke and fled.
entries.literal: The bandits feared his name and thereupon broke and fled of themselves.

entries.zh: 以悆克復守禦功，加徽猷閣待制。
entries.en: For his merit in recovering and defending the territory, Chou Yu was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Hall of Imperial Proclamations.
entries.literal: For Yu's merit in recovering and defending the territory, he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Imperial Proclamations.

entries.zh: 鄭瑴，字致剛，建州人。
entries.en: Zheng Jue, whose courtesy name was Zhigang, came from Jian Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zheng Jue, courtesy name Zhigang, was a native of Jian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 政和八年舉進士，授安陸府教授，權信陽縣尉，監南康酒稅。
entries.en: In 1118 he earned his jinshi degree and held successive posts as professor in Anlu Prefecture, acting sheriff of Xinyang County, and overseer of the wine tax at Nankang.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenghe he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Professor of Anlu Prefecture, acting Sheriff of Xinyang County, and Supervisor of the wine tax at Nankang.

entries.zh: 遂召為御史臺主簿。
entries.en: He was soon summoned to the Censorate as registrar.
entries.literal: He was then summoned to serve as Registrar of the Censorate.

entries.zh: 張邦昌之僭號也，挺身見高宗於濟州。
entries.en: When Zhang Bangchang seized the throne, he went in person to present himself to the future Emperor Gaozong at Jizhou.
entries.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne, he went forth boldly to meet Emperor Gaozong at Jizhou.

entries.zh: 既即位，擢監察御史，遷右司諫，升為諫議大夫。
entries.en: Once Gaozong had ascended the throne, Zheng was promoted to investigating censor, then right remonstrance officer, and finally remonstrance grandee.
entries.literal: After Gaozong took the throne, he was promoted to Investigating Censor, transferred to Right Remonstrance Officer, and advanced to Remonstrance Grandee.

entries.zh: 改知金壇縣，親嫌，更弋陽縣。
entries.en: He was appointed magistrate of Jintan County, but because of a kinship taboo was transferred to Yiyang County instead.
entries.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Jintan County; because of kinship taboo, he was moved to Yiyang County.

entries.zh: 父義和為侍御史主管佑神觀。
entries.en: His father Yihe had served as attendant censor assigned to manage Youshen Abbey.
entries.literal: His father Yihe was attendant censor assigned to manage Youshen Abbey.

entries.zh: 尋丁父喪，服除，知蘭溪縣，決擿如神。
entries.en: He soon mourned his father's death. When the mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Lanxi County, where his judgments seemed almost uncanny in their accuracy.
entries.literal: Soon he mourned his father's death; when mourning ended, he was magistrate of Lanxi County; his judgments and investigations were like a spirit's.

entries.zh: 歲旱，郡倚辦勸分，綱謂勸分所以助義倉，一切行之，非所謂安富恤貧也，願假常平錢為糶本，使得循環迭濟。
entries.en: In a drought year the prefecture relied on organizing mutual aid among the wealthy. Gang said mutual aid was meant to supplement the charity granaries, and applying it wholesale was not true relief for the poor. He asked to borrow Ever-Normal granary funds as capital for relief sales so that grain could circulate and aid the needy in turn.
entries.literal: In a drought year the prefecture relied on organizing mutual aid; Gang said mutual aid was to assist the charity granaries—carrying it out wholesale was not what is called enriching the secure and relieving the poor; he wished to borrow Ever-Normal granary funds as capital for relief sales so that circulation could aid in turn.

entries.zh: 又躬勸富民浚築塘堰，大興水利，餓者得食其力，全活甚眾。
entries.en: He also personally urged wealthy households to dredge ponds and build weirs, greatly expanding irrigation works. The hungry earned their food by labor, and very many lives were saved.
entries.literal: He also personally urged wealthy households to dredge and build ponds and weirs, greatly promoting waterworks; the hungry obtained food by their labor, and very many were wholly saved alive.

entries.zh: 郡守張抑及部使者列綱為一道荒政之冠。
entries.en: Prefect Zhang Yi and the circuit envoy ranked Gang the foremost in famine relief in the circuit.
entries.literal: Prefect Zhang Yi and the circuit envoy ranked Gang as the crown of famine administration in the circuit.

entries.zh: 以言去，邑人相率投軌直其事，綱力止之。
entries.en: He left office after speaking out on policy. The people of the district threw themselves before his carriage to plead his case, but Gang firmly stopped them.
entries.literal: He left because of remonstrance; the people of the district together cast themselves on the carriage tracks to state the facts directly; Gang forcefully stopped them.

entries.zh: 吳昌裔汪綱陳宓王霆
entries.en: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, and Wang Ting
entries.literal: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting

entries.zh: 應鈴開明磊落，守正不阿，別白是非，見義必為，不以得失利害動其心。
entries.en: Yingling was open and upright, steadfast and unyielding. He distinguished right from wrong, acted whenever justice required it, and was unmoved by gain, loss, or personal interest.
entries.literal: Yingling was open, bright, and upright, holding to the correct path without bending; he distinguished right from wrong, and when he saw righteousness he acted — gain, loss, benefit, and harm did not move his heart.

entries.zh: 書饋不交上官，薦舉不徇權門，當官而行，無敢撓以非義。
entries.en: He exchanged no letters or gifts with superiors and did not recommend people to please powerful families. He did his duty as an official, and no one dared interfere with improper pressure.
entries.literal: He did not exchange letters and gifts with superiors, nor did he curry favor with powerful families in recommendations; he acted according to office, and none dared obstruct him with improper means.

entries.zh: 所至無留訟，無滯獄，繩吏不少貸，亦未嚐沒其貲，曰：“彼之貨以悖入，官又從而悖入之，可乎？”
entries.en: Wherever he served, lawsuits did not linger and prisons did not backlog. He showed no leniency to corrupt clerks, yet he never seized their property, saying, “Their wealth was gained unjustly — should the government then take it unjustly too?”
entries.literal: Wherever he served there were no lingering lawsuits and no backlog in the prisons. He did not lightly pardon corrupt officials, yet he never confiscated their property, saying: “Their goods were gained by wrongdoing — should the state then take them by wrongdoing as well?”

entries.zh: 進修潔，案奸贓，振樹風聲，聞者興起。
entries.en: He upheld integrity, investigated corruption, and set a moral example that stirred those who heard of it.
entries.literal: He promoted integrity, investigated graft, and raised the standard of public conduct; those who heard of it were inspired.

entries.zh: 家居時，人有不平，不走官府，而走應鈴之門；
entries.en: While living at home, people with grievances did not go to the magistrates but came to Yingling’s door;
entries.literal: When at home, people with grievances did not go to the government but came to Yingling’s door;

entries.zh: 為不善者，輒相戒曰：“無使範公聞之。”
entries.en: and wrongdoers would warn one another, “Don’t let Master Fan find out.”
entries.literal: those who meant to do wrong would warn one another: “Do not let Master Fan hear of it.”

entries.zh: 讀書明大義，尤喜《左氏春秋》，所著有《西堂雜著》十卷，斷訟語曰《對越集》四十九卷。
entries.en: He read widely and grasped the larger moral principles, especially favoring the 《Zuo Tradition》. His works included ten juan of 《Miscellaneous Writings from the Western Hall》 and forty-nine juan of judicial remarks titled 《Facing the Supreme Collection》.
entries.literal: He read books and understood great principles, especially loving the 《Zuo Tradition》, and his writings included ten juan of 《Miscellaneous Writings from the Western Hall》 and forty-nine juan of judicial remarks titled 《Facing the Supreme Collection》.

entries.zh: 徐鹿卿曰：“應鈴經術似兒寬，決獄似雋不疑，治民似龔遂，風采似范滂，理財似劉晏，而正大過之。”
entries.en: Xu Luqing said, “In classical learning Yingling was like Er Kuan; in judging cases like Juan Buyi; in governing the people like Gong Sui; in moral bearing like Fan Pang; in managing revenue like Liu Yan — yet in uprightness and breadth he surpassed them all.”
entries.literal: Xu Luqing said: “Yingling’s mastery of the classics resembled Er Kuan, his adjudication of cases resembled Juan Buyi, his governance of the people resembled Gong Sui, his bearing resembled Fan Pang, his management of finances resembled Liu Yan — yet he surpassed them all in rectitude and greatness.”

entries.zh: 人以為名言。
entries.en: People took this for a memorable saying.
entries.literal: People regarded it as a celebrated remark.

entries.zh: 婁機沈煥
entries.en: Lou Ji and Shen Huan
entries.literal: Lou Ji, Shen Huan

entries.zh: 〈（舒璘附）〉
entries.en: (with appended biography of Shu Lin)
entries.literal: (with appended biography of Shu Lin)

entries.zh: 曹彥約範應鈴徐經孫
entries.en: Cao Yanyue, Fan Yingling, and Xu Jingsun
entries.literal: Cao Yanyue, Fan Yingling, Xu Jingsun

entries.zh: 〇陳靖張綸邵曄崔立魯有開張逸吳遵路趙尚寬高賦程師孟韓晉卿葉康直
entries.en: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, and Ye Kangzhi.
entries.literal: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, Ye Kangzhi.

entries.zh: 張逸，字大隱，鄭州滎陽人。
entries.en: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Dayin, came from Xingyang in Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Dayin, was a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.

entries.zh: 進士及第，為試秘書省校書郎。
entries.en: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became a probationary collator in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was made a probationary collator in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 知襄州鄧城縣，有能名。
entries.en: As magistrate of Dengcheng in Xiangzhou he earned a name for competence.
entries.literal: As magistrate of Dengcheng County in Xiangzhou he gained a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 積州謝泌將薦逸，先設几案，置章其上，望闕再拜曰：「老臣為朝廷得一良吏。」
entries.en: Xie Bi, the prefect, was about to recommend Yi; he set out a desk, laid the memorial on it, bowed twice toward the palace, and said, "Your old servant has secured a fine official for the dynasty."
entries.literal: Prefect Xie Bi was about to recommend Yi; he first set out a desk, placed the memorial upon it, bowed twice toward the palace, and said: "This old servant has found the court a worthy official."

entries.zh: 乃奏之。
entries.en: Then he sent in the memorial.
entries.literal: Then he submitted it.

entries.zh: 他日引對，真宗問所欲何官，逸對曰：「母老在家，願得近鄉一幕職官，歸奉甘旨足矣。」
entries.en: On a later audience day Emperor Zhenzong asked what post he wanted; Yi answered, "My mother is old and at home; I ask only for a county staff appointment near my native place so I can go back and support her—that is all I want."
entries.literal: On another day he was summoned for audience; Zhenzong asked what office he desired; Yi replied: "My mother is old at home; I wish only a local staff post near my home county so I may return and provide for her—that is enough."

entries.zh: 授澶州觀察推官，數日，以母喪去。
entries.en: He was given the post of investigating officer on the Chanzong observation commission; within days he resigned to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He was appointed investigating officer on the Chanzong observation commission; within days he left office on his mother's death.

entries.zh: 服除，引對，帝又固問之，對曰：「願得京官。」
entries.en: When the mourning period ended he was called in again; the emperor pressed him once more, and he replied, "I would like a capital appointment."
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned again; the emperor pressed the question once more, and he replied: "I wish to receive a capital appointment."

entries.zh: 特改大理寺丞。
entries.en: He was specially appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: He was specially made Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 帝雅賢泌，再召問逸者，用泌薦也。
entries.en: The emperor had always held Bi in high regard and questioned Yi again on Bi's recommendation.
entries.literal: The emperor had long esteemed Bi and summoned Yi again to question him because of Bi's recommendation.

entries.zh: 知長水縣，時王嗣宗留守西京，厚遇之，及徙青神縣，貧不自給，嗣宗假奉半年使辦裝。
entries.en: While magistrate of Changshui, he enjoyed the warm patronage of Wang Sizong, regent of the Western Capital; when he was moved to Qingshen he could barely support himself, and Sizong advanced him half a year's salary for travel expenses.
entries.literal: As magistrate of Changshui County, Wang Sizong was then regent at the Western Capital and treated him generously; when Yi was transferred to Qingshen County he was too poor to support himself, and Sizong lent him half a year's salary to prepare for the move.

entries.zh: 既至縣，興學校，教生徒。
entries.en: On reaching the county he founded schools and taught students.
entries.literal: Once he reached the county he established schools and instructed students.

entries.zh: 後邑人陳希亮、楊異相繼登科，逸改其居曰桂枝裏。
entries.en: Later two local men, Chen Xiliang and Yang Yi, passed the examinations in turn, and Yi renamed his home Gui Branch Lane.
entries.literal: Later townspeople Chen Xiliang and Yang Yi passed the examinations in succession, and Yi renamed his residence Gui Branch Lane.

entries.zh: 縣東南有松柏灘，夏秋暴漲多覆舟，逸禱江神，不逾月，灘為徙五里，時人異之。
entries.en: Southeast of the county lay Songbai Shoal, where summer and autumn floods often sank boats; Yi prayed to the river god, and within a month the shoal had shifted five li—a wonder to all who heard of it.
entries.literal: Southeast of the county was Songbai Shoal; in summer and autumn sudden floods often capsized boats; Yi prayed to the river god, and in less than a month the shoal shifted five li—people of the time marveled at it.

entries.zh: 再遷太常博士、知尉氏縣。
entries.en: He was promoted again to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed magistrate of Weishi County.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made magistrate of Weishi County.

entries.zh: 擢監察御史，提點益州路刑獄，開封府判官。
entries.en: He was raised to investigating censor, intendant of criminal cases on the Yizhou circuit, and judge in the Kaifeng prefectural office.
entries.literal: He was elevated to Investigating Censor, Intendant of Criminal Cases on the Yizhou Circuit, and judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.

entries.zh: 使契丹，為兩浙轉運使。
entries.en: He went on embassy to the Khitan and later became transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.
entries.literal: He served as envoy to the Khitan and became Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhes.

entries.zh: 徙陜西，未赴，又徙河東，居數月，復徙陜西。
entries.en: He was posted to Shaanxi, reassigned to Hedong before he could take up the post, and after a few months sent back to Shaanxi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Shaanxi; before he took up the post he was transferred again to Hedong; after several months he was transferred back to Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 以龍圖閣待制知梓州。
entries.en: With the title drafting attendant at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations he became prefect of Zizhou.
entries.literal: As Drafting Attendant at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations he was made prefect of Zizhou.

entries.zh: 累遷尚書兵部郎中，知開封府。
entries.en: He was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of War and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: He rose in stages to Director in the Ministry of War in the Ministry of Revenue and was made prefect of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 有僧求內降免田稅，而逸固執不許。
entries.en: A monk petitioned for an imperial exemption from land tax, but Yi steadfastly refused.
entries.literal: A monk sought an internal edict exempting him from field tax, but Yi firmly refused.

entries.zh: 仁宗曰：「有司能守法，朕何憂也。」
entries.en: Emperor Renzong said, "When the bureaucracy keeps the law, what need have I to worry?"
entries.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "When officials can uphold the law, what have I to worry about?"

entries.zh: 又言：「頃禁命婦幹禁中恩，比來稍通女謁，願令官司糾劾。」
entries.en: He also said, "Consorts of officials were recently barred from seeking favors inside the palace, yet lately such petitions have crept back in; I ask that the offices investigate and prosecute them."
entries.literal: He also said: "Recently consorts of officials were forbidden to solicit favors within the palace; of late women have again been gaining access through petitions—I ask that the offices investigate and punish this."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 以樞密直學士知益州。
entries.en: As direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he became prefect of Yizhou.
entries.literal: As Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was made prefect of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 逸凡四至蜀，諳其民風。
entries.en: Yi had been to Shu four times in all and knew its people and customs intimately.
entries.literal: Yi had gone to Shu four times in all and knew its customs well.

entries.zh: 華陽騶長殺人，誣道旁行者，縣吏受財，獄既具，乃使殺人者守囚。
entries.en: A stable chief in Huayang killed a man and framed a traveler on the road; county clerks took bribes, and when the case was closed they put the actual killer in charge of guarding the prisoner.
entries.literal: A Huayang stable chief murdered someone and framed a passerby on the road; county clerks took bribes; when the case was complete they even made the murderer guard the prisoner.

entries.zh: 逸曰：「囚色冤，守者氣不直，豈守者殺人乎？」
entries.en: Yi said, "The prisoner looks aggrieved, and the guard's manner is guilty—could the guard be the murderer?"
entries.literal: Yi said: "The prisoner looks wronged, and the guard's bearing is not upright—could the guard be the killer?"

entries.zh: 囚始敢言，而守者果服，立誅之，蜀人以為神。
entries.en: Only then did the prisoner dare speak out; the guard confessed, was executed at once, and the people of Shu thought Yi almost supernatural.
entries.literal: Only then did the prisoner dare speak; the guard indeed confessed, was immediately executed, and the people of Shu regarded Yi as divine.

entries.zh: 會歲旱，逸使作堰壅江水，溉民田，自出公租減價以振民。
entries.en: That year brought drought; Yi had a weir built to hold back river water and irrigate farmland, and from his own official income he sold grain at reduced prices to relieve the people.
entries.literal: When drought struck that year, Yi had a weir built to dam the river and irrigate the people's fields, and from his own official rent he cut prices to relieve the people.

entries.zh: 初，民饑多殺耕牛食之，犯者皆配關中。
entries.en: Earlier, in famine years many peasants had killed draft oxen for food, and offenders were all banished to Guanzhong.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the people were hungry many slaughtered plow oxen for food; offenders were all exiled to Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 逸奏：「民殺牛以活將死之命，與盜殺者異，若不禁之，又將廢穡事。
entries.en: Yi memorialized, "Peasants who slaughter oxen to stave off starvation are not the same as thieves who steal and kill cattle; yet if the practice is unchecked, agriculture will collapse.
entries.literal: Yi memorialized: "When people kill oxen to save lives on the verge of death, it differs from killing oxen by theft; if it is not forbidden, farming will again be ruined.

entries.zh: 今歲少稔，請一切放還，復其業。」
entries.en: This year the harvest is fair; I ask that all such exiles be pardoned and sent home to resume farming."
entries.literal: This year the harvest is somewhat good; I ask that all such offenders be released and restored to their occupations."

entries.zh: 報可。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒於官。
entries.en: Not long afterward he died in office.
entries.literal: Before long he died in office.

entries.zh: 張洽字元德，臨江之清江人。
entries.en: Zhang Qia, courtesy name Yuande, was from Qingjiang in Linjiang.
entries.literal: Zhang Qia, courtesy name Yuande, was a man of Qingjiang in Linjiang.

entries.zh: 父紱，第進士。
entries.en: His father Fu passed the jinshi.
entries.literal: His father Fu passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 洽少穎異，從朱熹學，自《六經》傳注而下，皆究其指歸，至於諸子百家、山經地誌、老子浮屠之說，無所不讀。
entries.en: Qia was precocious and studied under Zhu Xi; from the Six Classics down he traced every teaching; he read the hundred schools, geographies, Laozi, and Buddhist texts without exception.
entries.literal: Qia was precocious in youth and studied under Zhu Xi; from the Six Classics and their commentaries downward he traced all to their ends; as for the hundred schools, mountain classics, geographical records, Laozi, and Buddhist teachings, there was nothing he did not read.

entries.zh: 嘗取管子所謂「思之思之，又重思之，思之不通，鬼神將通之」之語，以為窮理之要。
entries.en: He took Guanzi's "Think, think; think again; if thought fails, spirits will aid" as the key to exhausting principle.
entries.literal: He once took Guanzi's words "Think, think; think again and weigh; if thinking does not penetrate, spirits will penetrate" as the key to exhausting principle.

entries.zh: 熹嘉其篤志，謂黃榦曰：「所望以永斯道之傳，如二三君者不數人也。」
entries.en: Xi praised his resolve and told Huang Gan, "Those who will perpetuate the Way—such men are few."
entries.literal: Xi praised his earnest will and said to Huang Gan, "The hope to perpetuate this Way's transmission—men like these two or three are not many."

entries.zh: 嘉定九年，待試中都，歸過嚴陵郡守鄭之悌，率僚屬延講郡庠。
entries.en: In Jiading year 9, awaiting capital examination, he passed Yanling; Prefect Zheng Zhitie and staff heard him lecture at the prefectural school.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Jiading, awaiting examination in the capital, returning he passed Yanling; Prefect Zheng Zhitie led his staff to invite him to lecture at the prefectural school.

entries.zh: 淳嘆陸、張、王，學問無源，全用禪家宗旨，認形氣之虛靈知覺為天理之妙，不由窮理格物，而欲徑造上達之境，反托聖門以自標榜。
entries.en: Chun lamented Lu, Zhang, and Wang: learning without source, using Chan aims, taking void spirit and awareness as heaven's principle, skipping investigation yet claiming the sage's gate.
entries.literal: Chun sighed over Lu, Zhang, and Wang: their learning had no source and wholly used Chanist aims, taking the void spirit and knowing awareness of form and qi as the wonder of heaven's principle, not by exhausting principle and investigating things yet wishing to reach upward directly, and in reverse borrowing the sage's gate to set up their signboard.

entries.zh: 遂發明吾道之體統，師友之淵源，用功之節目，讀書之次序，為四章以示學者。
entries.en: He set forth our Way's substance, teachers' source, effort's nodes, and reading's order in four chapters for learners.
entries.literal: He then set forth the substance of our Way, the deep source of teacher and friend, the nodes of effort, and the order of reading in four chapters to show learners.

entries.zh: 明年，以特奏恩授迪功郎、泉州安溪主簿，未上而沒，年六十五。
entries.en: Next year by special grace he was made probationary merit officer and Anxi recorder in Quanzhou; before reporting he died at sixty-five.
entries.literal: The next year by special memorial grace he was made probationary merit officer and recorder of Anxi in Quanzhou; before reporting he died at sixty-five.

entries.zh: 其所著有《語孟大學中庸》口義、字義、詳講，《禮》、《詩》、《女學》等書，門人錄其語，號《筠谷瀨口金山所聞》。
entries.en: He wrote oral exegeses on the Four Books, Rites, Odes, and Women's Learning; disciples recorded What Was Heard at Jun Valley, Lai Mouth, and Jin Mountain.
entries.literal: His writings include oral exegeses and character meanings with detailed commentary on the Analects, Mencius, Great Learning, and Doctrine of the Mean, and books on Rites, Odes, and Women's Learning; disciples recorded his words as What Was Heard at Jun Valley, Lai Mouth, and Jin Mountain.

entries.zh: 黃榦 李燔 張洽 陳淳 李方子 黃灝
entries.en: Huang Gan, Li Fan, Zhang Qia, Chen Chun, Li Fangzi, and Huang Hao
entries.literal: Huang Gan, Li Fan, Zhang Qia, Chen Chun, Li Fangzi, Huang Hao

entries.zh: 樞密使王炎薦於朝，召為大理寺主簿，未至，為書謝炎曰：“主上天資英特，群臣無將順緝熙之具，幸得遭時，不能格心正始，以建中興之業，徒僥幸功利，誇言以眩俗，雖復中夏，猶無益也。
entries.en: Wang Yan of the Privy Council recommended him to court; he was called up as chief clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, but before he arrived he wrote Yan a letter of refusal: "The Son of Heaven is gifted beyond the ordinary, yet his ministers have no way to guide and steady him; given the moment, they cannot set his heart straight at the start and build a true restoration—they chase quick results and bedazzle the world with empty boasts; even retaking the north would change little.
entries.literal: Privy Councilor Wang Yan recommended him to the court; he was summoned as chief clerk of the Court of Judicial Review but had not yet arrived when he wrote Yan to decline, saying: "Our ruler is talented and exceptional, yet the ministers lack the means to harmonize and brighten him; though fortune has placed him in office, they cannot rectify the heart and set a true beginning to build the enterprise of restoration—they merely grasp at expedient gain and dazzle the age with boastful words; even if the Central Plains were recovered, it would still be of no benefit.

entries.zh: 為今之計，莫若以仁義紀綱為本。
entries.en: The right course now is to take benevolence, righteousness, and the fundamental norms as the foundation.
entries.literal: For the policy of the present, nothing surpasses taking benevolence and righteousness and the great norms as the root.

entries.zh: 至於用兵，請俟十年之後可也。”
entries.en: As for going to war, that should wait ten years."
entries.literal: As for using troops, please wait until ten years have passed.

entries.zh: 改知嚴道縣，攝通判嘉定。
entries.en: He was reassigned to govern Yandao County and served as acting vice prefect of Jiading.
entries.literal: He was changed to govern Yandao County and acted as Vice Prefect of Jiading.

entries.zh: 白厓砦將王塤引蠻寇利店，刑獄使者置塤於法，又罥絓餘人當坐死。
entries.en: Baiya Fort commander Wang Kun led barbarian raiders against Lidian; the judicial envoy executed Kun and implicated others for death.
entries.literal: The Baiya Fort commander Wang Kun led barbarian raiders against Lidian; the judicial envoy punished Kun by law and also implicated others who should die.

entries.zh: 泰之訪知夷都實邇利店，夷都蠻稱亂，不需引導，固請釋之，不聽。
entries.en: Taizhi found the Yidu tribe lay next to Lidian and had been called rebels without needing a guide—he pleaded for their release in vain.
entries.literal: Taizhi investigated and learned that the Yidu tribe actually bordered Lidian; the Yidu barbarians were called rebels and needed no guide—he firmly requested release but was not heeded.

entries.zh: 乃去官。
entries.en: He resigned.
entries.literal: He thereupon left office.

entries.zh: 宣撫使安丙薦之曰：“蜀中名儒楊虞仲之子，當逆臣之變，勉有位者毋動。
entries.en: Pacification Commissioner An Bing recommended him: "Taizhi, son of the famed Shu scholar Yang Yuzhong, urged officials to hold firm when the rebel crisis came.
entries.literal: Pacification Commissioner An Bing recommended him, saying: "Taizhi, son of the famous Shu scholar Yang Yuzhong—when the rebellious minister's crisis came, he urged those in office not to stir.

entries.zh: 言不用，拂衣而去。
entries.en: When ignored he shook out his robes and left.
entries.literal: When his words were not used he shook out his robes and left.

entries.zh: 使得尺寸之柄，必能見危致命。”
entries.en: Given even a little authority he would meet danger and give his life."
entries.literal: If granted even a small measure of authority he would surely be able to meet peril and give his life."

entries.zh: 召泰之赴都堂審察，以親老辭。
entries.en: Taizhi was summoned to the Secretariat for review but declined, citing aged parents.
entries.literal: Taizhi was summoned to the Secretariat for examination; citing aged parents he declined.

entries.zh: 差知廣安軍，未上，丁父憂。
entries.en: He was assigned Guang'an Army but entered mourning for his father before taking up the post.
entries.literal: He was assigned to govern Guang'an Army; before he took up the post he entered mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 免喪，知富順監。
entries.en: After mourning he governed the Fushun salt monopoly.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he governed Fushun Salt Monopoly.

entries.zh: 去官，以祿稟數千緡予鄰裏，以千緡為義莊。
entries.en: On leaving office he gave thousands of strings of salary to neighbors and a thousand to a charity estate.
entries.literal: Leaving office he gave several thousand strings of his salary to neighbors and a thousand strings to a charity estate.

entries.zh: 知普州，以安居、安嶽二縣受禍尤慘，泰之力白丙盡蠲其賦。
entries.en: As prefect of Puzhou he persuaded An Bing to remit levies entirely for Anju and Anyue, which had suffered worst.
entries.literal: Governing Puzhou, because Anju and Anyue two counties had suffered especially cruel harm, Taizhi strongly told Bing to remit their levies entirely.

entries.zh: 丙復薦於朝，召赴行在，固辭。
entries.en: An Bing recommended him again; summoned to court he firmly declined.
entries.literal: Bing again recommended him to the court and he was summoned to the traveling palace; he firmly declined.

entries.zh: 知果州。
entries.en: He was appointed to govern Guozhou.
entries.literal: He was appointed to govern Guozhou.

entries.zh: 踦零錢病民，泰之以一年經費儲其贏為諸邑對減，上尚書省，按為定式。
entries.en: The qiling coin levy hurt the people; Taizhi saved a year's surplus to cut levies across prefectures, reported upward, and it became fixed practice.
entries.literal: The qiling coin levy harmed the people; Taizhi stored one year's surplus from routine expenses to reduce levies across prefectures in pairs, reported to the Ministry of Revenue, and it was adopted as a fixed pattern.

entries.zh: 民歌之曰：“前張後楊，惠我無疆。”
entries.en: The people sang: "First Zhang, then Yang—bless us without end."
entries.literal: The people sang: "First Zhang then Yang—bless us without end."

entries.zh: 張謂張義，實自發其端，而泰之踵行之。
entries.en: Zhang was Zhang Yi, who began the practice; Taizhi followed.
entries.literal: Zhang meant Zhang Yi—he actually began it, and Taizhi followed in his steps.

entries.zh: 儒林四
entries.en: Confucian Scholars 4
entries.literal: Confucian Scholars 4.

entries.zh: 世言唐所以亡，由諸侯之強，此未極於理。
entries.en: The age says Tang perished because the feudatories were strong—this does not reach the limit of reason.
entries.literal: The age says Tang perished because the feudatories were strong—this does not reach the limit of reason.

entries.zh: 夫弱唐者，諸侯也。
entries.en: What weakened Tang were the feudatories.
entries.literal: What weakened Tang were the feudatories.

entries.zh: 唐既弱矣，而久不亡者，諸侯維之也。
entries.en: Once Tang was weak, yet long did not perish because the feudatories sustained it.
entries.literal: Once Tang was weak, yet long did not perish because the feudatories sustained it.

entries.zh: 燕、趙、魏首亂唐製，專地而治，若古之建國，此諸侯之雄者，然皆恃唐為輕重。
entries.en: Yan, Zhao, and Wei first disturbed Tang's system, held territory and governed like ancient states—these were the mighty among feudatories, yet all relied on Tang for weight.
entries.literal: Yan, Zhao, and Wei first disturbed Tang's system, held territory and governed like ancient states—these were the mighty among feudatories, yet all relied on Tang for weight.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 假王命以相製則易而順，唐雖病之，亦不得而外焉。
entries.en: Borrowing the king's mandate to restrain one another was easy and orderly; though Tang was ill, it could not be cast aside.
entries.literal: Borrowing the king's mandate to restrain one another was easy and orderly; though Tang was ill, it could not be cast aside.

entries.zh: 故河北順而聽命，則天下為亂者不能遂其亂；
entries.en: Thus when Hebei was obedient and listened to orders, those who would make trouble in the realm could not complete their trouble;
entries.literal: Thus when Hebei was obedient and listened to orders, those who would make trouble in the realm could not complete their trouble;

entries.zh: 河北不順而變，則奸雄或附而起。
entries.en: when Hebei was disobedient and changed, then treacherous heroes might rise attached.
entries.literal: when Hebei was disobedient and changed, then treacherous heroes might rise attached.

entries.zh: 德宗世，朱泚、李希烈始遂其僭而終敗亡，田悅叛於前，武俊順於後也。
entries.en: In Emperor Dezong's time Zhu Ci and Li Xilie first achieved their usurpation yet finally were defeated; Tian Yue rebelled before, Wu Jun was obedient after.
entries.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time Zhu Ci and Li Xilie first achieved their usurpation yet finally were defeated and destroyed; Tian Yue rebelled before, Wu Jun was obedient after.

entries.zh: 憲宗討蜀、平夏、誅蔡、夷鄆，兵連四方而亂不生，卒成中興之功者，田氏稟命、王承宗歸國也。
entries.en: Emperor Xianzong attacked Shu, pacified Xia, executed Cai, and destroyed Yun; armies linked the four quarters yet disorder did not arise—mid-dynasty revival was because the Tian clan received orders and Wang Chengzong returned to the state.
entries.literal: Emperor Xianzong attacked Shu, pacified Xia, executed Cai, and destroyed Yun; armies linked the four quarters yet disorder did not arise—the merit of mid-dynasty revival was because the Tian clan received orders and Wang Chengzong returned to the state.

entries.zh: 武宗將討劉稹之叛，先正三鎮，絕其連衡之計，而王誅以成。
entries.en: When Emperor Wuzong was about to attack Liu Zhen's rebellion, he first rectified the three circuits, cut off their alliance plan, and Wang's execution succeeded.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wuzong was about to attack Liu Zhen's rebellion, he first rectified the three circuits, cut off their alliance plan, and Wang's execution succeeded.

entries.zh: 如是二百年，奸臣逆子專國命者有之，夷將相者有之，而不敢窺神器，非力不足，畏諸侯之勢也。
entries.en: Thus for two hundred years wicked ministers and rebellious sons monopolized state power, yet none dared peer at the throne—not from insufficient strength but from fear of the feudatories' power.
entries.literal: Thus for two hundred years there were wicked ministers and rebellious sons who monopolized state power and degraded generals and ministers, yet none dared peer at the sacred vessel—not from insufficient strength but from fear of the feudatories' power.

entries.zh: 及廣明之後，關東無復唐有，方鎮相侵伐者，猶以王室為名。
entries.en: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.
entries.literal: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.

entries.zh: 及梁祖舉河南，劉仁恭輕戰而敗，羅氏內附，王鎔請盟，於時河北之事去矣。
entries.en: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were settled.
entries.literal: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were gone.

entries.zh: 梁人一舉而代唐有國，諸侯莫能與之爭，其勢然也。
entries.en: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend—the trend was thus.
entries.literal: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend with them—the trend was thus.

entries.zh: 向使以僖、昭之弱，乘巢、蔡之亂，而田承嗣守魏，王武俊、朱滔據燕、趙，強相均，地相屬，其勢宜莫敢先動，況非義舉乎？
entries.en: Had Xizong and Zhaozong's weakness met Huang Chao and Cai Jing's turmoil, while Tian Chengsi held Wei and Wang Wujun and Zhu Tao held Yan and Zhao, strong and evenly matched—the trend should have been that none dared move first, how much less an unrighteous act?
entries.literal: Had the weakness of Xizong and Zhaozong met the turmoil of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, while Tian Chengsi held Wei and Wang Wujun and Zhu Tao held Yan and Zhao, strong and evenly matched, territory connected—the trend should have been that none dared move first, how much less an unrighteous act?

entries.zh: 如此雖梁祖之暴，不過取霸於一方耳，安能強禪天下？
entries.en: Thus even the Liang founder's violence would have taken hegemony in one region only—how could he forcibly yield the realm by Zen?
entries.literal: Thus even the Liang founder's violence would have taken hegemony in one region only—how could he forcibly yield the realm by Zen?

entries.zh: 故唐之弱者，以河北之強也；
entries.en: Thus Tang was weak because Hebei was strong;
entries.literal: Thus Tang was weak because Hebei was strong;

entries.zh: 唐之亡者，以河北之弱也。
entries.en: Tang perished because Hebei was weak.
entries.literal: Tang perished because Hebei was weak.

entries.zh: 文苑四
entries.en: Literary Grove, Part Four
entries.literal: Literary Grove Four

entries.zh: 朱娥張氏彭列女郝節娥朱氏崔氏趙氏丁氏項氏王氏二婦徐氏榮氏何氏董氏譚氏劉氏張氏師氏陳堂前節婦廖氏劉當可母曾氏婦王袤妻塗端友妻詹氏女劉生妻謝泌妻謝枋得妻王貞婦趙淮妾譚氏婦吳中孚妻呂仲洙女林老女童氏女韓氏女王氏婦劉仝子妻
entries.en: Zhu E, Zhang Shi, Peng Lienu, Hao Jiee, Zhu Shi, Cui Shi, Zhao Shi, Ding Shi, Xiang Shi, the two Wang wives, Xu Shi, Rong Shi, He Shi, Dong Shi, Tan Shi, Liu Shi, Zhang Shi, Shi Shi, Chen Tangqian, the chaste widow Liao, Liu Dangke's mother, the Zeng clanswoman, Wang Mao's wife, Tu Duanyou's wife, the Zhan family's daughter, Liu Sheng's wife, Xie Bi's wife, Xie Fangde's wife, the chaste widow Wang, Zhao Huai's concubine, the Tan clanswoman, Wu Zhongfu's wife, Lu Zhongzhu's daughter, old woman Lin, the Tong family's daughter, the Han family's daughter, the Wang clanswoman, and Liu Tongzi's wife
entries.literal: Zhu E, Zhang Shi, Peng Lienu, Hao Jiee, Zhu Shi, Cui Shi, Zhao Shi, Ding Shi, Xiang Shi, the two wives of the Wang family, Xu Shi, Rong Shi, He Shi, Dong Shi, Tan Shi, Liu Shi, Zhang Shi, Shi Shi, Chen Tangqian, the chaste wife Liao Shi, the mother of Liu Dangke, the wife of the Zeng clan, the wife of Wang Mao, the wife of Tu Duanyou, the daughter of the Zhan clan, the wife of Liu Sheng, the wife of Xie Bi, the wife of Xie Fangde, the chaste wife Wang, the concubine of Zhao Huai, the wife of the Tan clan, the wife of Wu Zhongfu, the daughter of Lu Zhongzhu, the old woman of the Lin family, the daughter of the Tong clan, the daughter of the Han clan, the wife of the Wang clan, the wife of Liu Tongzi

entries.zh: 〈（毛惜惜附）〉
entries.en: (with Mao Xixi appended)
entries.literal: (Mao Xixi appended)

entries.zh: 劉氏，海州朐山人，適同裏陳公緒。
entries.en: Liu Shi was from Qushan in Haizhou and married Chen Gongxu of the same neighborhood.
entries.literal: Liu Shi was a native of Qushan in Haizhou and married Chen Gongxu of the same lane.

entries.zh: 紹興末，金人犯山東，郡縣震響，公緒倡義來歸，偶劉歸寧，倉卒不得與偕，惟挈其子庚以行，宋授以八品官，後累功至正使。
entries.en: Near the end of the Shaoxing era the Jin invaded Shandong and the region was in turmoil. Gongxu raised a loyal force and submitted to the Song. Liu happened to be visiting her parents and could not leave with him in the haste—he took only their son Geng. The Song granted him an eighth-rank post; through accumulated merit he later rose to Regular Commissioner.
entries.literal: Near the end of the Shaoxing era the Jin invaded Shandong; prefectures and counties trembled. Gongxu raised righteous arms and came over to the Song; by chance Liu returned home to visit her parents and in the haste could not go with him—he took only their son Geng. The Song granted him an eighth-rank post; later, through accumulated merit, he rose to Regular Commissioner.

entries.zh: 劉留北方，音問不通。
entries.en: Liu remained in the north; no word could reach her.
entries.literal: Liu remained in the north; letters and inquiries could not pass.

entries.zh: 或語之曰：“人言‘貴易交，富易妻’。
entries.en: Some told her: "People say that when a man grows noble his friendships change, and when he grows rich he changes his wife.
entries.literal: Some said to her: "People say, 'When one grows noble, friendships change; when one grows rich, wives change.'

entries.zh: 今陳已貴，必他娶矣，盍改適？”
entries.en: Chen is now eminent—he must have remarried. Why not marry again?"
entries.literal: Now Chen has grown eminent—he must have taken another wife. Why not remarry?"

entries.zh: 曰：“吾知守吾誌而已，皇恤乎他？”
entries.en: She said: "I know only to keep my resolve—why should I fear anything else?"
entries.literal: She said: "I know only to keep to my resolve—why should I fear anything else?"

entries.zh: 公緒亦不他娶。
entries.en: Gongxu likewise never remarried.
entries.literal: Gongxu likewise did not take another wife.

entries.zh: 子庚浸長，輒思念涕泣，傾家貲，結任俠，奔走淮甸，險阻備嚐。
entries.en: As Geng grew older he often thought of her and wept; he spent the family fortune, joined with bold adventurers, and traveled the Huai region through every hardship and danger.
entries.literal: As Geng gradually grew, he often thought of her and wept; he spent the family fortune, joined with bold knights-errant, and rushed about the Huai region, tasting every hardship and danger.

entries.zh: 如是者十餘年，遂得迎母以歸。
entries.en: After more than ten years of this, he was finally able to bring his mother home.
entries.literal: Thus for more than ten years, he was finally able to bring his mother home.

entries.zh: 劉在北二十五年，嚐緯蕭以自給。
entries.en: Liu had been in the north for twenty-five years, weaving rush mats to support herself.
entries.literal: Liu had been in the north for twenty-five years and had always woven rush mats to support herself.

entries.zh: 同縣有朱雲孫妻劉氏，姑病，雲孫刲股肉作糜以進而愈。
entries.en: In the same county, Liu Shi, wife of Zhu Yunsun, when her mother-in-law fell ill, Yunsun cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel for her and she recovered.
entries.literal: In the same county, Liu Shi, wife of Zhu Yunsun, when her mother-in-law fell ill, Yunsun cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel and presented it; she recovered.

entries.zh: 姑復病，劉亦刲股以進，又愈。
entries.en: When her mother-in-law fell ill again, Liu also cut flesh from her thigh and presented it, and she recovered again.
entries.literal: When her mother-in-law fell ill again, Liu also cut flesh and presented it, and she recovered again.

entries.zh: 尚書謝諤為賦《孝婦詩》。
entries.en: Minister Xie E composed the Poem on the Filial Wife for them.
entries.literal: Minister Xie E composed the Poem on the Filial Wife for them.

entries.zh: 南漢劉鋹，其先蔡州上蔡人，高祖安仁，仕唐為潮州刺史，因家嶺表。
entries.en: Liu Chang of Southern Han came from a line originally of Shangcai in Cai Prefecture. His great-grandfather Anren had served the Tang as prefect of Chaozhou and settled his family in Lingnan.
entries.literal: Liu Chang of Southern Han — his ancestors were men of Shangcai in Cai Prefecture; his great-grandfather Anren served the Tang as prefect of Chaozhou and thereupon made his home in Lingnan.

entries.zh: 安仁生謙，為廣州牙校，累遷封州刺史、賀水鎮遏使。
entries.en: Anren's son Qian served as a military aide at Guangzhou and rose through successive appointments to prefect of Feng and commissioner at Hesui.
entries.literal: Anren begat Qian, who served as a military aide at Guangzhou and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Feng Prefecture and military commissioner of Hesui.

entries.zh: 謙生隱，謙卒，隱代領其任。
entries.en: Qian's son Yin succeeded him when Qian died and assumed his command.
entries.literal: Qian begat Yin; when Qian died, Yin took over his post in his stead.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗以薛王知柔鎮南海，辟為行軍司馬，委以兵柄。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhaozong posted the Prince of Xue, Zhi Rou, to the South Seas, Yin was made his chief of staff on campaign and given control of the army.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhaozong of Tang sent the Prince of Xue, Zhi Rou, to govern the South Seas and appointed Yin chief of staff on campaign, entrusting him with military authority.

entries.zh: 及宰相徐彥若代知柔，以為節度副使。
entries.en: When Chief Minister Xu Yanruo succeeded Zhi Rou, Yin was appointed deputy military commissioner.
entries.literal: When the chief minister Xu Yanruo replaced Zhi Rou, Yin was made deputy military commissioner.

entries.zh: 時唐室已季，彥若威令不振，事皆決於隱。
entries.en: The Tang dynasty was already in decline, and Yanruo's authority no longer commanded obedience; Yin decided everything.
entries.literal: The Tang house was already in its last days; Yanruo's prestige and orders did not carry weight, and all affairs were decided by Yin.

entries.zh: 彥若卒，遺表薦隱自代，昭宗不從，以崔遠代之。
entries.en: On Yanruo's death he recommended Yin to succeed him in a final memorial, but Zhaozong refused and appointed Cui Yuan instead.
entries.literal: When Yanruo died he left a memorial recommending Yin to succeed him; Zhaozong did not assent and sent Cui Yuan in his place.

entries.zh: 遠至江陵，遷延不進，乃以隱為留後，未幾，授以節旄。
entries.en: Cui Yuan reached Jiangling but lingered without advancing, so Yin was made acting commissioner; shortly afterward he received the full commission.
entries.literal: Yuan reached Jiangling but delayed and did not advance; Yin was then made acting commissioner, and before long he was granted the commissioner's insignia.

entries.zh: 梁開平初，兼靜海軍節度使，封南海王。
entries.en: Early in the Liang Kaiping period he was also made military commissioner of the Jinghai army and created Prince of the Southern Sea.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Liang dynasty's Kaiping era he additionally held the commission of the Jinghai army and was enfeoffed as Prince of the Southern Sea.

entries.zh: 隱卒，弟陟襲位。
entries.en: After Yin died, his younger brother Zhi took the throne.
entries.literal: When Yin died, his younger brother Zhi succeeded to the position.

entries.zh: 貞明三年，僭帝號，國稱大漢，改元乾亨，行郊祀禮。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhenming he took an imperial title, named his state Great Han, adopted the era Qianheng, and performed suburban sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he arrogated an imperial title; the state was called Great Han, the era name was Qianheng, and suburban sacrifices were performed.

entries.zh: 改名岩，又改龔，終改龑。
entries.en: He changed his name first to Yan, then to Gong, and at last to a character of his own devising.
entries.literal: He changed his name to Yan, then to Gong, and finally to a character of his own invention.

entries.zh: 「龑」讀為「儼」，字書不載，蓋其妄作也。
entries.en: The character 龑 was pronounced "yan," like the ordinary graph for that sound; it appears in no dictionary and was plainly his own fabrication.
entries.literal: The character 龑 is read as "yan," homophonous with the standard character for that sound; it does not appear in dictionaries — evidently he invented it himself.

entries.zh: 晉天福七年，卒，子玢嗣，為弟晟所殺。
entries.en: He died in the seventh year of Later Jin's Tianfu. His son Bin succeeded him but was killed by his younger brother Sheng.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Later Jin's Tianfu he died; his son Bin succeeded but was killed by his younger brother Sheng.

entries.zh: 晟遂自立，性尤酷暴，周顯德五年，卒，事具《五代史》。
entries.en: Sheng then seized power himself. He was exceptionally cruel and violent, and died in the fifth year of Later Zhou's Xiande; the full story is given in the History of the Five Dynasties.
entries.literal: Sheng then established himself in power; his nature was especially cruel and violent. In the fifth year of Later Zhou's Xiande he died; the full account is in the History of the Five Dynasties.

entries.zh: 初，龑雖寵任中官，其數裁三百餘，位不過掖庭諸局令丞。
entries.en: At first, even though that ruler favored eunuchs, their number was barely three hundred, and none rose above the chiefs and assistants of the palace bureaus.
entries.literal: At first, though the emperor with the invented name favored eunuchs, their number was limited to just over three hundred, and ranks did not exceed bureau chiefs and assistant commissioners of the palace domestic offices.

entries.zh: 至晟時千餘人，稍增內常侍、諸謁者之稱。
entries.en: Under Sheng they numbered more than a thousand, and titles such as inner regular attendant and various commissioners were gradually introduced.
entries.literal: By Sheng's time there were over a thousand, and titles of inner regular attendant and various commissioners were gradually added.

entries.zh: 至鋹漸至七千餘，有為三師、三公，但其上加「內」字，諸使名不翅二百，女官亦有師傅、令仆之號。
entries.en: Under Chang they eventually exceeded seven thousand. Some held the ranks of the Three Preceptors and Three Excellencies with only the prefix "inner" added; commissioner titles alone numbered no fewer than two hundred, and female officials too bore titles of tutor, steward, and chief steward.
entries.literal: Under Chang they gradually reached more than seven thousand; some held the ranks of the Three Preceptors and Three Excellencies, with only the prefix "inner" added; commissioner titles numbered no fewer than two hundred; female officials also had titles of tutor, steward, and chief steward.

entries.zh: 目百官為「門外人」，群臣小過及士人、釋、道有才略可備問者，皆下蠶室，令得出入宮闈。
entries.en: He called the civil officials "people outside the gate." Officials guilty of minor faults, and any scholar, Buddhist, or Daoist with talent worth consulting, were castrated and made to enter and leave the inner palace at will.
entries.literal: He regarded the hundred officials as "people outside the gate"; officials guilty of minor faults, and scholars, Buddhists, and Daoists with talent useful for consultation, were all sent to the silkworm chamber so they could come and go within the palace.

entries.zh: 作燒煮剝剔、刀山劍樹之刑，或令罪人鬥虎抵象。
entries.en: He invented punishments of boiling alive, flaying, dismemberment, and mountains of blades and forests of swords, or set criminals to fight tigers and elephants.
entries.literal: He devised punishments of boiling, flaying, cutting apart, mountains of knives and forests of swords, or made culprits fight tigers or elephants.

entries.zh: 又賦斂煩重，邕民入城者人輸一錢，瓊州米斗稅四五錢。
entries.en: His levies were oppressive as well: every person entering the capital at Yong paid one cash, and a peck of rice at Qiong Prefecture carried a tax of four or five cash.
entries.literal: Levies were also heavy and vexatious; people entering the city of Yong paid one cash per person; a peck of rice at Qiong Prefecture was taxed four or five cash.

entries.zh: 置媚川都，定其課，令入海五百尺采珠。
entries.en: He set up the Meichuan Command, fixed its levy, and ordered divers five hundred feet into the sea to collect pearls.
entries.literal: He established the Meichuan Command and fixed its quota, ordering men to dive five hundred feet into the sea to gather pearls.

entries.zh: 所居宮殿以珠、玳瑁飾之。
entries.en: The palaces where he lived were decorated with pearls and tortoise shell.
entries.literal: The palaces he dwelt in were adorned with pearls and tortoise shell.

entries.zh: 陳延壽作諸淫巧，日費數萬金。
entries.en: Chen Yanshou devised all manner of lewd contrivances, spending tens of thousands in gold every day.
entries.literal: Chen Yanshou made all manner of lewd clever devices, spending tens of thousands in gold daily.

entries.zh: 宮城左右離宮數十，鋹遊幸常至月餘或旬日。
entries.en: Dozens of detached palaces stood on either side of the capital, and Chang's pleasure tours often lasted a month or more, sometimes ten days at a stretch.
entries.literal: Several dozen detached palaces stood to left and right of the capital; Chang's excursions often lasted more than a month or ten days at a time.

entries.zh: 以豪民為課戶，供宴犒之費。
entries.en: Wealthy families were designated tax households to pay for banquets and rewards.
entries.literal: Wealthy households were made tax households to supply the costs of feasts and rewards.

entries.zh: 鋹即晟長子也，初名繼興，封衛王，襲父位，改今名，改元大寶。
entries.en: Chang was Sheng's eldest son, originally named Jixing and enfeoffed Prince of Wei. On succeeding his father he took his present name and proclaimed the era Dabao.
entries.literal: Chang was Sheng's eldest son; he was first named Jixing, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and on succeeding his father changed to his present name and era to Dabao.

entries.zh: 性昏懦，委政宦官龔澄樞及才人盧瓊仙，每詳覽可否，皆瓊仙指之。
entries.en: He was dull and timid by nature and left government to the eunuch Gong Chengshu and the talented concubine Lu Qiongxian; whenever he weighed what might be done, Qiongxian's finger decided it.
entries.literal: His character was dull and timid; he entrusted government to the eunuch Gong Chengshu and the talented concubine Lu Qiongxian; whenever he scrutinized what was permissible, it was Qiongxian who pointed it out.

entries.zh: 鋹日與宮人、波斯女等遊戲。
entries.en: Chang passed his days in games with palace women, Persian women, and the like.
entries.literal: Chang spent his days at play with palace women, Persian women, and the like.

entries.zh: 內官陳延壽引女巫樊胡入宮，言玉皇遣樊胡命鋹為太子皇帝，乃於宮中施帷幄，羅列珍玩，設玉皇坐。
entries.en: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou introduced the witch Fan Hu, who claimed the Jade Emperor had sent her to name Chang Crown Prince Emperor. Within the palace they hung silken curtains, displayed rare treasures, and set out a throne for the Jade Emperor.
entries.literal: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou brought the shamaness Fan Hu into the palace, saying the Jade Emperor had sent Fan Hu to appoint Chang as Crown Prince Emperor; in the palace silken curtains were hung, rare treasures arrayed, and a seat for the Jade Emperor set up.

entries.zh: 樊胡遠遊冠、紫衣、紫霞裙，坐宣禍福，令鋹再拜聽命；
entries.en: Fan Hu wore a traveling cap, purple robes, and a purple cloud skirt, sat proclaiming fortune and disaster, and made Chang bow twice to receive her commands;
entries.literal: Fan Hu wore a distant-traveling cap, purple robes, and a purple cloud skirt, sat announcing fortune and calamity, and ordered Chang to bow twice and heed commands;

entries.zh: 嘗雲瓊仙、澄樞、延壽皆玉皇遣輔太子皇帝，有過不得治。
entries.en: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou had all been sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor and that he must not punish them even if they erred.
entries.literal: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou were all sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor, and that if they erred he must not punish them.

entries.zh: 又有梁山師、馬媼、何擬之徒出入宮掖。
entries.en: Others such as Liang Shanshi, Old Woman Ma, and He Ni also moved freely through the inner palace.
entries.literal: Others such as Liang Shanshi, Old Woman Ma, and He Ni also came and went within the inner palace.

entries.zh: 宮中婦人皆具冠帶，領外事。
entries.en: Every woman in the palace wore official cap and sash and took charge of outside affairs.
entries.literal: All women in the palace wore caps and sashes and managed external affairs.

entries.zh: 先是，晟因湖南馬氏之亂，襲取桂、郴、賀等州。
entries.en: Earlier, Sheng had exploited the turmoil of Hunan's Ma clan to seize Gui, Chen, He, and other prefectures.
entries.literal: Earlier, Sheng had taken advantage of disorder in Hunan's Ma clan to seize Gui, Chen, He, and other prefectures.

entries.zh: 開寶初，鋹又舉兵侵道州，刺史王繼勳上言。
entries.en: Early in Kaibao, Chang again marched against Dao Prefecture, and Prefect Wang Jixun memorialized the throne.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Kaibao era Chang again raised troops to invade Dao Prefecture; prefect Wang Jixun memorialized the throne.

entries.zh: 鋹為政昏暴，民被其毒，請討之。
entries.en: Chang's rule was benighted and brutal, and the people were suffering under him; he asked that an expedition be launched.
entries.literal: Chang's governance was benighted and violent and the people suffered his poison; he asked that they be attacked.

entries.zh: 太祖難其事，令江南李煜遣使以書諭鋹使稱臣，歸湖南舊地。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor hesitated to act and ordered Li Yu of Jiangnan to send envoys with a letter urging Chang to submit as a vassal and restore the old Hunan territories.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor found the undertaking difficult and ordered Li Yu of Jiangnan to send envoys with a letter urging Chang to submit and return the old territories in Hunan.

entries.zh: 鋹不從。
entries.en: Chang refused.
entries.literal: Chang did not comply.

entries.zh: 煜又遣其給事中龔慎儀遺書曰：
entries.en: Yu then sent his Supervising Secretary, Gong Shenyi, with another letter that read:
entries.literal: Yu again sent his Supervising Secretary Gong Shenyi with a letter saying:

entries.zh: 四年正月，美等破英、雄二州，都統潘崇徹來降。
entries.en: In the first month of the fourth year Mei and the others took Ying and Xiong prefectures; Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche surrendered.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Mei and the others took Ying and Xiong prefectures; Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche came over in surrender.

entries.zh: 翌日，次瀧頭，鋹遣使請和，且求緩師。
entries.en: The next day they halted at Longtou; Chang sent envoys to sue for peace and ask that the advance be slowed.
entries.literal: The next day they halted at Longtou; Chang sent envoys to sue for peace and ask that the army be slowed.

entries.zh: 瀧頭山水險惡，美等疑有伏兵，乃挾鋹使速度諸險。
entries.en: Longtou's terrain was rugged and perilous; Mei and the others suspected ambush and forced Chang's envoy to hurry them through the dangerous passes.
entries.literal: Longtou's mountains and waters were perilous and harsh; Mei and the others suspected ambush and therefore forced Chang's envoy to speed them through the dangerous passes.

entries.zh: 二月，過馬逕，去廣城十里，砦於雙女山下。
entries.en: In the second month they passed Majing, ten li from the capital, and encamped below Shuangnv Mountain.
entries.literal: In the second month they passed Majing, ten li from Guang City, and encamped below Shuangnv Mountain.

entries.zh: 鋹聞之，取舶船十餘艘，載金寶、妃嬪欲入海。
entries.en: When Chang heard of it, he took more than ten ocean-going ships, loaded them with gold, treasures, and concubines, and prepared to flee to sea.
entries.literal: Chang heard of it, took more than ten ocean-going ships, loaded gold and treasures and concubines, intending to flee to sea.

entries.zh: 未及發，宦官樂範與衛兵千餘盜舶船走。
entries.en: Before they could depart, the eunuch Yue Fan and more than a thousand guards stole the ships and fled.
entries.literal: Before they could depart, the eunuch Yue Fan and over a thousand guards stole the ships and fled.

entries.zh: 美等將至城，鋹懼，遣其右僕射蕭漼奉表詣軍門乞降。
entries.en: As Mei and the others were about to reach the city, Chang in fear sent his Right Vice Director Xiao Hun to present a memorial at the army gate begging to surrender.
entries.literal: As Mei and the others were about to reach the city, Chang in fear sent his Right Vice Director Xiao Hun to present a memorial at the army gate begging surrender.

entries.zh: 美諭太祖意，語在《美傳》。
entries.en: Mei conveyed Taizu's intent — the account appears in Mei's biography.
entries.literal: Mei expounded Taizu's intent — the account is in the Biography of Mei.

entries.zh: 使者乞部送赴闕，師遂頓城外。
entries.en: The envoy asked to be escorted to the capital; the army thereupon halted outside the city.
entries.literal: The envoy asked to be escorted to court; the army thereupon halted outside the walls.

entries.zh: 鋹又遣其弟保興率百官奉迎，為郭崇嶽所遏。
entries.en: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the officials to welcome them, but Guo Chongyue blocked them.
entries.literal: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the hundred officials to welcome them, but they were blocked by Guo Chongyue.

entries.zh: 崇嶽無謀勇，但祈禱鬼神，復為拒捍之備。
entries.en: Chongyue lacked strategy and courage; he only prayed to spirits and gods and again prepared to resist.
entries.literal: Chongyue lacked strategy and courage; he only prayed to spirits and gods and again made preparations to resist.

entries.zh: 美等乃進攻，保興迎戰，大為所敗，美乘風縱火，煙埃坌起，崇嶽死於亂兵。
entries.en: Mei and the others then pressed the attack; Baoxing met them in battle and was utterly defeated. Mei took the wind to set fires; smoke and dust billowed up; Chongyue died in the melee.
entries.literal: Mei and the others then pressed the attack; Baoxing met them in battle and was utterly defeated. Mei took the wind to set fires; smoke and dust billowed up; Chongyue died among the disorderly troops.

entries.zh: 城既破，鋹盡焚其府庫。
entries.en: Once the city fell, Chang burned all the treasuries.
entries.literal: Once the city was broken, Chang burned all the treasuries.

entries.zh: 美擒鋹及龔澄樞、李托、薛崇譽與宗室文武九十七人，同縻於龍德宮。
entries.en: Mei captured Chang along with Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, and ninety-seven members of the imperial clan and the civil and military elite, all held together in Longde Palace.
entries.literal: Mei captured Chang together with Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, and ninety-seven members of the imperial clan and civil and military officials, all confined together in Longde Palace.

entries.zh: 保興逃於民家，亦獲之，悉部送闕下。
entries.en: Baoxing hid in a commoner's home but was also captured; all were escorted to court.
entries.literal: Baoxing hid in a commoner's home but was also taken; all were escorted to court.

entries.zh: 斬閹工五百餘人。
entries.en: More than five hundred eunuch craftsmen were beheaded.
entries.literal: More than five hundred castrated palace artisans were beheaded.

entries.zh: 凡得州六十、縣二百十四、戶十七萬。
entries.en: In all they took sixty prefectures, two hundred fourteen counties, and one hundred seventy thousand households.
entries.literal: In all they obtained sixty prefectures, two hundred fourteen counties, and one hundred seventy thousand households.

entries.zh: 鋹至江陵，邸吏龐師進迎謁，學士黃德昭侍鋹，鋹問師進何人，德昭曰：「本國人也。」
entries.en: When Chang reached Jiangling, lodge clerk Pang Shijin came to greet him; academician Huang Dezhao attended Chang, who asked who Shijin was; Dezhao said, "He is a man of our own state."
entries.literal: When Chang reached Jiangling, lodge clerk Pang Shijin came to greet and pay respects; academician Huang Dezhao attended Chang, who asked who Shijin was; Dezhao said: "He is a man of our own state."

entries.zh: 鋹曰：「何為在此？」
entries.en: Chang said, "Why is he here?"
entries.literal: Chang said: "Why is he here?"

entries.zh: 曰：「先主歲貢大朝，輜重比至荊州，乃令師進至邸，於此造車，以給饋運爾。」
entries.en: He said, "The former ruler sent yearly tribute to the Great Dynasty; when the baggage train reached Jingzhou, Shijin was posted to the lodge here to build carts for the supply transport — that is all."
entries.literal: He said: "The former ruler yearly sent tribute to the Great Dynasty; when the baggage train reached Jingzhou, Shijin was posted to the lodge here to build carts to supply the transport — that is all."

entries.zh: 鋹歎曰：「我在位十四年，未嘗聞此言，今日始知祖宗山河及大朝境土也。」
entries.en: Chang sighed, "In my fourteen years on the throne I never heard this — today I first learn the extent of our forebears' realm and the Great Dynasty's territory."
entries.literal: Chang sighed: "In my fourteen years on the throne I never heard this — today I first learn of our forebears' mountains and rivers and the Great Dynasty's territory."

entries.zh: 因泣涕久之。
entries.en: He wept for a long time.
entries.literal: Thereupon he wept for a long while.

entries.zh: 初，岩改名龔，有術者言不利，名龔，當敗國事，遂改名龑。
entries.en: Yan had first changed his name to Gong, but a diviner warned that the name Gong would bring ruin upon the state, so he adopted the invented character instead.
entries.literal: At first Yan changed his name to Gong; a diviner said it was unfavorable — the name Gong would ruin state affairs — so he changed his name to the invented character.

entries.zh: 後鋹用澄樞，以其姓卒亡其國，澄樞亦被誅。
