entries.en: Later Chang put Chengshu in power — and the Gong surname did indeed destroy his realm. Chengshu was executed as well.
entries.literal: Later Chang employed Chengshu; because of his surname he ultimately lost his state, and Chengshu was also executed.

entries.zh: 龔澄樞，廣州南海人。
entries.en: Gong Chengshu came from Nanhai in Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Gong Chengshu was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 性廉謹，不妄交遊。
entries.en: He was upright and cautious by nature and kept few companions.
entries.literal: His character was honest and careful; he did not socialize casually.

entries.zh: 幼事龑為內供奉官，累遷內給事。
entries.en: In his youth he entered service under the emperor with the invented name as an Inner Tribute Official and rose through successive posts to Inner Provisioner.
entries.literal: In youth he served the emperor with the invented name as Inner Tribute Official and was repeatedly promoted to Inner Provisioner.

entries.zh: 晟襲位，任閹人林延遇為甘泉宮使，頗預政事。
entries.en: When Shen took the throne, he made the eunuch Lin Yanyu Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, and Lin came to wield considerable influence over state affairs.
entries.literal: When Shen succeeded to the throne, he appointed the eunuch Lin Yanyu Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, and Yanyu took considerable part in government affairs.

entries.zh: 延遇病將死，言於晟曰：「臣死，惟龔澄樞可用。」
entries.en: On his deathbed Yanyu told Shen, "When I am gone, only Gong Chengshu is fit to serve you."
entries.literal: Yanyu, ill and near death, said to Shen: "When I die, only Gong Chengshu can be used."

entries.zh: 即日擢知承宣院兼內侍省，改德陵使兼龍德宮使。
entries.en: That same day Shen promoted him to head the Presentation Court while also serving in the Palace Domestic Service, then made him Commissioner of the Virtue Mausoleum and Commissioner of the Dragon Virtue Palace.
entries.literal: That same day he was promoted to administer the Presentation Court while also holding the Palace Domestic Service, then transferred to Commissioner of the Virtue Mausoleum together with Commissioner of the Dragon Virtue Palace.

entries.zh: 鋹嗣位，加特進、開府儀同三司、萬華宮使、驃騎大將軍，改上將軍、左龍虎軍觀軍容使、內太師，軍國之務皆決於澄樞。
entries.en: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General, then Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor. Every matter of war and state passed through his hands.
entries.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu was given Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General; he was then changed to Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor — all military and state affairs were decided by Chengshu.

entries.zh: 澄樞與李托、薛崇譽置酷法之具，民甚苦之。
entries.en: Chengshu, Li Tuo, and Xue Chongyu instituted instruments of torture, and the people endured terrible suffering.
entries.literal: Chengshu, together with Li Tuo and Xue Chongyu, set up instruments of cruel law, and the people suffered greatly.

entries.zh: 李托，封州封川人。
entries.en: Li Tuo came from Fengchuan in Feng Prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Tuo was a native of Fengchuan in Feng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少習騎射，以謹願事龑為內府局令。
entries.en: He trained in horsemanship and archery from youth and entered service under the emperor with the invented name as Director of an Inner Treasury Bureau, distinguished by his dutiful temperament.
entries.literal: In youth he practiced mounted archery and, with cautious compliance, served the emperor with the invented name as Director of an Inner Treasury Bureau.

entries.zh: 晟襲位，遷內侍省內侍，充宮闈諸衛押番兼秀華宮使。
entries.en: When Shen took the throne, Tuo was made a Palace Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, assigned to the palace guard rotation and Commissioner of the Splendid Beauty Palace.
entries.literal: When Shen succeeded to the throne, Tuo was transferred to Palace Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, filling the palace guard rotation duty together with Commissioner of the Splendid Beauty Palace.

entries.zh: 鋹立，改玩華宮使、內侍監兼列聖、景陽二宮使。
entries.en: When Chang took the throne, Tuo became Commissioner of the Playful Splendor Palace and Superintendent of the Palace Domestic Service, while also overseeing the Liesheng and Jingyang ancestral palaces.
entries.literal: When Chang established himself on the throne, Tuo was changed to Commissioner of the Playful Splendor Palace and Superintendent of the Palace Domestic Service, together with Commissioner of the Two Ancestor Palaces of Liesheng and Jingyang.

entries.zh: 托納二女於鋹，鋹以其長為貴妃，次為美人，政事皆訪托而後行。
entries.en: Tuo gave two daughters to Chang in marriage; the elder became Honored Consort and the younger a Beauty. No policy moved forward until Tuo had been consulted.
entries.literal: Tuo presented two daughters to Chang; Chang made the elder Honored Consort and the younger a Beauty, and all government affairs were consulted with Tuo before being carried out.

entries.zh: 加特進、開府儀同三司、甘泉宮使兼六軍觀軍容使、行內中尉，遷驃騎上將軍、內太師。
entries.en: He received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, Army Observer of the Six Armies, and Acting Inner Captain, then rose to Cavalry Grand General and Inner Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He was given the special advancement of Grand Mentor, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace together with Army Observer of the Six Armies, and Acting Inner Captain; he was then promoted to Cavalry Grand General and Inner Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 潘崇徹，廣州南海人。
entries.en: Pan Chongche came from Nanhai in Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Pan Chongche was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 事龑為內侍省局丞。
entries.en: He entered service under the emperor with the invented name as a Bureau Assistant in the Palace Domestic Service.
entries.literal: He served the emperor with the invented name as Bureau Assistant in the Palace Domestic Service.

entries.zh: 頗讀兵書，立戰功。
entries.en: He studied military texts and won distinction in battle.
entries.literal: He read military books extensively and established battle merit.

entries.zh: 晟嘗遣大將吳懷恩伐桂州平之，懷恩為部下所殺，命崇徹代之。
entries.en: Shen once sent the general Wu Huai'en to conquer Gui Prefecture. When Wu was killed by his own men, Shen put Chongche in command.
entries.literal: Shen once dispatched the great general Wu Huai'en to attack Gui Prefecture and pacify it; Huai'en was killed by his subordinates, and Shen ordered Chongche to replace him.

entries.zh: 鋹襲位，加西北面都統。
entries.en: When Chang took the throne, Chongche was made Commander-in-Chief of the Northwest Area.
entries.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chongche was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of the Northwest Area.

entries.zh: 歲餘，鋹頗疑崇徹，遣薛宗譽使其軍以察之。
entries.en: After a year Chang grew suspicious of Chongche and sent Xue Chongyu to his camp to investigate.
entries.literal: After more than a year Chang grew quite suspicious of Chongche and dispatched Xue Chongyu to his army to inspect him.

entries.zh: 崇譽還，遂白崇徹日以伶人百餘衣錦繡、吹玉笛，為長夜之飲，不恤軍政。
entries.en: On his return Chongyu reported that Chongche spent his days with more than a hundred performers in brocade robes, playing jade flutes and feasting through the night while neglecting military affairs.
entries.literal: Chongyu returned and reported that Chongche daily had more than a hundred actors clad in brocade, blowing jade flutes, holding all-night drinking revels, and not caring for military government.

entries.zh: 鋹怒，召歸，奪其兵柄，自是居常怏怏。
entries.en: Enraged, Chang recalled him and stripped him of command. Thereafter Chongche lived in perpetual resentment.
entries.literal: Chang was angry, summoned him back, and stripped him of military authority; from then on he lived in constant discontent.

entries.zh: 太祖命師度嶺，鋹復命崇徹領兵五萬戍賀江，崇徹不為效命。
entries.en: When Taizu's army crossed the mountains, Chang again put Chongche in charge of fifty thousand troops to guard the He River, but Chongche refused to fight with any zeal.
entries.literal: When Taizu ordered the army to cross the mountains, Chang again ordered Chongche to lead fifty thousand troops to garrison the He River; Chongche did not exert himself in service.

entries.zh: 鋹敗，至京，太祖知其事，特赦之，授汝州別駕，卒。
entries.en: After Chang's defeat Chongche was brought to the capital. Taizu, knowing what had transpired, granted him a special pardon and appointed him Vice-Governor of Ru Prefecture, where he later died.
entries.literal: When Chang was defeated and reached the capital, Taizu knew the circumstances, specially pardoned him, appointed him Vice-Governor of Ru Prefecture, and he died.

entries.zh: 世家四○南漢劉氏
entries.en: Hereditary Houses 4: The Southern Han Liu.
entries.literal: Hereditary Houses 4 — The Liu Clan of Southern Han.

entries.zh: 北漢劉繼元，并州太原人。
entries.en: Liu Jiyuan of the Northern Han state came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Jiyuan of Northern Han was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Province.

entries.zh: 祖崇，漢祖之弟，漢初為太原尹、北京留守。
entries.en: His grandfather Liu Chong was the Later Han founder's younger brother; in the early Han reign he was made Taiyuan governor and northern-capital commissioner.
entries.literal: His grandfather Chong was the younger brother of the founder of Later Han; at the beginning of the Han reign he served as governor of Taiyuan and as commissioner for the northern capital.

entries.zh: 隱帝嗣位，周祖為樞密使，崇謂判官鄭珙曰：“吾與郭樞密素不協，朝廷幼弱，郭得誌，吾無類矣。”
entries.en: After Emperor Yinyou came to the throne, Guo Wei of Later Zhou held the post of Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner. Liu Chong told his registrar Zheng Gong, "Guo and I have never gotten along. The throne is held by a boy. Once Guo has his way, my whole line is finished."
entries.literal: When Emperor Yinyou succeeded to the throne, the Later Zhou founder served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Chong said to his registrar Zheng Gong: "I have never been on good terms with Commissioner Guo. The court is ruled by a child. If Guo gets his way, there will be none of my kind left."

entries.zh: 因泣下。
entries.en: As he said this, he broke down in tears.
entries.literal: He wept as he spoke.

entries.zh: 珙遂勸繕完甲兵，招集亡命，為自全計。
entries.en: Gong then urged him to put arms and armor in order, recruit outlaws and fugitives, and plan how to save himself.
entries.literal: Gong thereupon urged him to repair weapons and armor, gather fugitives, and make plans to preserve himself.

entries.zh: 及聞隱帝遇害，崇欲率兵南向，會漢太后下令遣馮道詣徐州迎崇子贇為漢嗣，崇信之，謂賓佐曰：“吾兒為帝矣，復何慮哉？”
entries.en: On hearing that Emperor Yinyou had been murdered, Chong prepared to march south with his army. Just then the Han empress dowager sent Feng Dao to Xuzhou to bring back Chong's son Yun as heir to the throne. Chong took this at face value and told his advisers, "My son is going to be emperor—what is left to fear?"
entries.literal: When he heard that Emperor Yinyou had been killed, Chong wished to lead his troops south. It happened that the Han empress dowager ordered Feng Dao to go to Xuzhou to welcome Chong's son Yun as heir to Han. Chong believed this and said to his staff: "My son will be emperor—what more is there to worry about?"

entries.zh: 少尹李驤曰：“知幾其神，時不可失。
entries.en: Junior prefect Li Xiang said, "To read the moment is almost uncanny—and this moment will not wait.
entries.literal: The junior prefect Li Xiang said: "To know the turning point is divine; the moment must not be lost.

entries.zh: 揣郭公之心，必不以天下與人，不如領精騎疾度太行，控孟津，以觀其變，徐州位定，然後歸晉陽，即郭公不敢動矣。”
entries.en: Read Guo Wei's mind and you will see he will never hand the empire to anyone else. Take your best horsemen, cross the Taihang fast, seize Mengjin, and watch how things unfold. Once the succession at Xuzhou is settled, return to Jinyang—then even Guo Wei will not dare touch you."
entries.literal: Judging Lord Guo's heart, he will surely not yield the realm to another. Better to lead picked cavalry swiftly across the Taihang range, hold Mengjin, and watch how events unfold. Once the succession at Xuzhou is settled, then return to Jinyang—even Lord Guo would not dare move against you."

entries.zh: 崇大怒，罵曰：“腐儒敢離間我父子！”
entries.en: Chong erupted in fury. "You spineless pedant," he shouted, "how dare you set father against son!"
entries.literal: Chong flew into a rage and cursed: "You rotten scholar—how dare you drive a wedge between father and son!"

entries.zh: 遽令左右曳出斬之。
entries.en: He had his men drag Xiang out at once and cut off his head.
entries.literal: He immediately ordered his attendants to drag him out and behead him.

entries.zh: 驤曰：“仆負王佐才，今日為愚人畫計，死固甘心，但家有病妻，願同戮於市。”
entries.en: Xiang said, "I have the makings of a king's right hand. Today I gave advice to a fool, and I accept death—but my wife is ill at home. Let her be killed with me in the market square."
entries.literal: Xiang said: "I possess the talent to aid a true king. Today I offered counsel to a fool and death is acceptable—but I have an ailing wife at home; I ask that she be executed with me in the marketplace."

entries.zh: 崇並殺之，表其事於太后，明無他誌。
entries.en: Chong had them both killed, then reported the affair to the empress dowager to show he harbored no other ambition.
entries.literal: Chong killed them both and reported the matter to the empress dowager, making clear that he had no other design.

entries.zh: 俄周祖為眾所推，降封贇湘陰公。
entries.en: Soon afterward Guo Wei was elevated by popular acclaim; Yun was reduced in rank and made Duke of Xiangyin.
entries.literal: Before long the Later Zhou founder was raised up by the multitude; Yun was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyin.

entries.zh: 崇遣使奉書周祖，乞贇歸藩。
entries.en: Chong sent envoys with a letter to Guo Wei, asking that Yun be sent back to his own territory.
entries.literal: Chong sent an envoy with a letter to the Later Zhou founder, begging that Yun be returned to his domain.

entries.zh: 使還，知贇已死，崇慟哭，為驤立祠。
entries.en: When the envoy came back, he learned Yun was already dead. Chong wept bitterly and built a shrine in Li Xiang's honor.
entries.literal: When the envoy returned, he learned that Yun was already dead. Chong wailed in grief and erected a shrine to Xiang.

entries.zh: 遂即皇帝位，國仍號漢，仍稱乾祐年，改名旻。
entries.en: He thereupon took the throne. The state still bore the name Han and still used the Qianyou era, and he changed his name to Min.
entries.literal: He thereupon took the imperial throne; the state still bore the name Han and still used the Qianyou era, and he changed his name to Min.

entries.zh: 以子鈞為太原尹，判官趙華、鄭珙為宰相，陳光裕為宣徽使。
entries.en: He made his son Liu Jun governor of Taiyuan, appointed his registrars Zhao Hua and Zheng Gong as chancellors, and made Chen Guangyu commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: He made his son Jun governor of Taiyuan, and his registrars Zhao Hua and Zheng Gong chancellors, with Chen Guangyu as commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 齎重幣結契丹，自言與周有隙，願如晉祖故事，約為父子。
entries.en: He sent lavish gifts to court the Khitans, saying he and the Zhou were enemies and asking, on the Jin founder's precedent, to be bound in a father-and-son pact.
entries.literal: He sent heavy gifts to court the Khitans, saying that he and Zhou were at odds and that, following the precedent of the Jin founder, he wished to enter a father-and-son pact.

entries.zh: 契丹主許之，遣政事令燕王耶律述軋、上樞使高勳，策崇為大漢神武皇帝。
entries.en: The Khitan ruler agreed and sent Administrative Commissioner Prince of Yan Yelü Shuzha and Senior Palace Secretariat Commissioner Gao Xun to invest Liu Chong as Emperor Shenwu of Great Han.
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler agreed and sent Administrative Commissioner Prince of Yan Yelü Shuzha and Senior Palace Secretariat Commissioner Gao Xun to invest Chong as Emperor Shenwu of Great Han.

entries.zh: 自是數侵晉、絳。
entries.en: From then on he repeatedly raided Jin and Jiang.
entries.literal: From then on he repeatedly raided Jin and Jiang.

entries.zh: 高平之敗，崇單騎遁歸，由此喪氣，不敢復出師。
entries.en: After the defeat at Gaoping, Liu Chong fled home alone on horseback, lost heart, and dared not take the field again.
entries.literal: After the defeat at Gaoping, Chong fled home alone on horseback; from this he lost heart and dared not campaign again.

entries.zh: 顯德元年，崇卒，鈞襲位。
entries.en: In Xiande 1, Liu Chong died and Liu Jun succeeded him.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiande, Chong died and Jun succeeded to the throne.

entries.zh: 鈞舊名承鈞，後止名鈞。
entries.en: Jun had formerly been named Chengjun, but later used only the name Jun.
entries.literal: Jun had formerly been named Chengjun, but later used only the name Jun.

entries.zh: 改元天會，以衛融為相，段常為樞密使，蔚進掌親軍，子繼恩為太原尹。
entries.en: He changed the era name to Tianhui, made Wei Rong chancellor, Duan Chang commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wei Jin commander of the personal army, and his son Ji'en governor of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: He changed the era name to Tianhui, made Wei Rong chancellor, Duan Chang commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wei Jin commander of the personal army, and his son Ji'en governor of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 始建七廟於漢祖舊第，號顯聖宮。
entries.en: He first built seven ancestral temples at the Later Han founder's old residence and named the site Xiansheng Palace.
entries.literal: He first built seven ancestral temples at the old residence of the Han founder and named it Xiansheng Palace.

entries.zh: 潛結江南、西川為外援。
entries.en: He secretly allied with Jiangnan and Xichuan as outside support.
entries.literal: He secretly allied with Jiangnan and Xichuan as external support.

entries.zh: 六年冬，鈞結契丹侵周。
entries.en: In the winter of the sixth year, Liu Jun allied with the Khitans and invaded Zhou.
entries.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, Jun allied with the Khitans to invade Zhou.

entries.zh: 明年正月，周恭帝命太祖北征，至陳橋驛，眾推戴太祖即位。
entries.en: The next first month, Emperor Gong of Zhou ordered Taizu north. At Chenqiao Post the army acclaimed Taizu and raised him to the throne.
entries.literal: In the first month of the following year, Emperor Gong of Zhou ordered Taizu on a northern campaign; at Chenqiao Post the troops acclaimed Taizu and raised him to the throne.

entries.zh: 鈞與契丹兵皆遁去。
entries.en: Liu Jun and the Khitan army both withdrew.
entries.literal: Jun and the Khitan army both fled away.

entries.zh: 繼恩本姓薛。
entries.en: Ji'en had originally borne the surname Xue.
entries.literal: Ji'en was originally surnamed Xue.

entries.zh: 父釗，娶崇女，晉初為護聖營卒。
entries.en: His father Xue Zhao married Chong's daughter and, in the early Jin years, served as a soldier in the Imperial Guard camp.
entries.literal: His father Zhao married Chong's daughter; at the beginning of Jin he was a soldier in the Imperial Guard camp.

entries.zh: 漢祖典禁兵，以釗崇婿，釋其籍，館門下。
entries.en: When the Later Han founder took command of the palace guard, he freed Zhao from the rolls as Chong's son-in-law and housed him at his residence.
entries.literal: When the Han founder took charge of the forbidden troops, because Zhao was Chong's son-in-law he released him from the registers and lodged him at his gate.

entries.zh: 漢祖後領方鎮，爵位通顯，釗罕得見其妻，居常怏怏。
entries.en: Later, as the Han founder rose to a frontier command and high rank, Zhao seldom saw his wife and brooded in resentment.
entries.literal: Later the Han founder held a frontier command and his rank became eminent; Zhao rarely saw his wife and was habitually discontent.

entries.zh: 一日乘醉求見，即引佩刀刺妻，妻奮衣得脫，釗乃自剄。
entries.en: One day he came drunk to demand an audience, drew his belt knife, and lunged at his wife; she tore free of her robe and fled, and Zhao cut his own throat.
entries.literal: One day, drunk, he demanded an audience and at once drew his girdle knife to stab his wife; she tore free of her robe and escaped, and Zhao then cut his own throat.

entries.zh: 繼恩時尚幼，漢祖令鈞養為子，遂冒姓劉。
entries.en: Ji'en was still a child; the Han founder had Jun adopt him, and he took the Liu surname.
entries.literal: Ji'en was still young; the Han founder ordered Jun to raise him as a son, and he thereupon took the surname Liu.

entries.zh: 郭無為，青州千乘人。
entries.en: Guo Wuwei was a native of Qiansheng in Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Guo Wuwei was a native of Qiansheng in Qing Province.

entries.zh: 少博學有辭辯，為道士，隱武當山。
entries.en: In youth he was widely learned and eloquent; he became a Daoist priest and lived in seclusion on Mount Wudang.
entries.literal: In youth he was broadly learned and eloquent in debate; he became a Daoist priest and lived in seclusion on Mount Wudang.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐中，周祖征河中，無為杖策謁於軍門，周祖一見大奇之，將留館門下。
entries.en: During the Later Han Qianyou era, when Guo Wei campaigned in the Hezhong region, Wuwei came staff in hand to the army gate. Guo Wei was greatly impressed at first sight and was about to keep him at his residence.
entries.literal: During the Qianyou era of Han, when the Later Zhou founder campaigned in the Hezhong region, Wuwei came with staff in hand to present himself at the army gate; at first sight the Zhou founder was greatly struck by him and was about to keep him as a guest at his residence.

entries.zh: 左右曰：“無為縱橫家流，今公握重兵，不宜親之。”
entries.en: His advisers said, "Wuwei is a coalition strategist. You now command a great army—it is not wise to draw close to him."
entries.literal: Those around him said: "Wuwei is of the coalition strategist school; now you hold heavy troops—it is not fitting to draw close to him."

entries.zh: 無為遂拂衣去，隱太原抱腹山。
entries.en: Wuwei shook out his robe and left, living in seclusion on Baofu Mountain near Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Wuwei thereupon shook out his robe and left, living in seclusion on Baofu Mountain near Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 世家五○北漢劉氏
entries.en: Hereditary Houses, 5 — The Liu Clan of Northern Han
entries.literal: Hereditary Houses 5: The Liu Clan of Northern Han

entries.zh: 是時，天下久安，嶺南州縣無備，一旦兵起倉卒，不知所為，守將多棄城遁。
entries.en: The empire had been at peace for years, and Lingnan had no defenses. When rebellion erupted overnight, local commanders panicked and many fled their posts.
entries.literal: At this time, the realm had long been at peace; Lingnan prefectures and counties had no preparedness. Suddenly troops rose in haste, not knowing what to do—the defending generals mostly abandoned cities and fled.

entries.zh: 故智高所向得志，相繼破橫、貴、龔、潯、藤、梧、封、康、端九州，害曹覲於封州、趙師旦馬貴於康州，餘殺官吏甚眾。
entries.en: Zhigao swept through Heng, Gui, Gong, Xun, Teng, Wu, Feng, Kang, and Duan, killing Cao Jin at Fengzhou and Zhao Shidan and Ma Gui at Kangzhou along with countless other officials.
entries.literal: Therefore wherever Zhigao went he got his wish; in succession he broke the nine prefectures of Heng, Gui, Gong, Xun, Teng, Wu, Feng, Kang, and Duan, killed Cao Jin at Feng Prefecture and Zhao Shidan and Ma Gui at Kang Prefecture; besides these he killed very many officials.

entries.zh: 所過焚府庫，進圍廣州。
entries.en: His army burned treasuries along the way and pushed on to besiege Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Where he passed he burned government storehouses, advancing to besiege Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 初，智高將至，守將仲簡不許民入保城中，民不得入者皆附智高，智高勢益張。
entries.en: When Zhigao approached, Defender Zhong Jian refused to let civilians into the city. Those left outside joined the rebels, and Zhigao's forces swelled.
entries.literal: Initially, as Zhigao was about to arrive, the defending general Zhong Jian did not permit the people to enter and take refuge within the city; those who could not enter all attached to Zhigao, and Zhigao's power grew ever greater.

entries.zh: 先是，魏瓘築州城，鑿井畜水，作大弩為守備。
entries.en: Earlier, Wei Guan had fortified the city with walls, wells, and giant crossbows.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wei Guan had built the prefectural city wall, dug wells to store water, and made large crossbows for defensive preparation.

entries.zh: 至是，智高為雲梯土山，攻城甚急，又斷流水，而城堅，井飲不竭，弩發，中輒洞潰，智高力屈。
entries.en: Zhigao built siege towers and ramparts and cut off the water supply, but the walls held, the wells never ran dry, and Wei Guan's crossbows punched clean holes through his ranks until Zhigao's army was spent.
entries.literal: At this time, Zhigao made cloud-ladders and earthen mounds, attacking the city very urgently; he also cut off the flowing water, but the walls were strong, well water for drinking did not run dry, crossbows fired, and hits immediately pierced through and burst; Zhigao's strength was exhausted.

entries.zh: 會知英州蘇緘屯兵邊渡村，扼其歸路；
entries.en: Meanwhile Yingzhou Prefect Su Jian blocked the retreat at Biandu Village;
entries.literal: It happened that Ying Prefecture prefect Su Jian stationed troops at Biandu Village, blocking his route of return;

entries.zh: 番禺縣令蕭注募土丁及海上強壯二千餘人，與智高眾格鬥，焚其戰艦；
entries.en: Panyu Magistrate Xiao Zhu rallied over two thousand local militiamen and sailors, fought Zhigao's troops, and burned his fleet;
entries.literal: Panyu county magistrate Xiao Zhu recruited more than two thousand local militia and strong men from the sea, grappled with Zhigao's masses, and burned his warships;

entries.zh: 轉運使王罕亦自外至，益修守備。
entries.en: Transport Commissioner Wang Han arrived from outside and tightened the defenses.
entries.literal: Transport commissioner Wang Han also arrived from outside, further repairing defensive preparations.

entries.zh: 智高知不可拔，圍五十七日，七月壬戌，解去。
entries.en: After fifty-seven days, seeing Guangzhou could not be taken, Zhigao withdrew on the renxu day of the seventh month.
entries.literal: Zhigao knew it could not be taken; he besieged for fifty-seven days; on the renxu day of the seventh month, he lifted the siege and departed.

entries.zh: 由清遠濟江，擁婦女作樂而行，遇張忠戰於白田，忠死之。
entries.en: He crossed the river near Qingyuan, marching to music with captive women until Zhang Zhong intercepted him at Baitian and was killed.
entries.literal: By Qingyuan he crossed the river, embracing women and making music as he went; he encountered Zhang Zhong and fought at Baitian; Zhong died in it.

entries.zh: 去攻賀州，不克，夜害蔣偕於太平場。
entries.en: Failing to take Hezhou, he ambushed and killed Jiang Xie at Taiping that night.
entries.literal: He went on to attack He Prefecture, did not overcome it; at night he harmed Jiang Xie at Taiping Ground.

entries.zh: 九月庚申，破昭州，害王正倫等於館門驛。
entries.en: On the gengshen day of the ninth month he seized Zhaozhou and murdered Wang Zhenglun and others at Guanmen Post Station.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day of the ninth month, he broke Zhao Prefecture, harming Wang Zhenglun and others at Guanmen Post Station.

entries.zh: 州之山有數穴，大可容數百千人，民聞兵至，走匿其中，智高知之，縱火，皆焚死。
entries.en: Locals fled into mountain caves that could shelter thousands. Zhigao found them and set the caves ablaze, burning everyone inside.
entries.literal: The prefecture's mountains had several caves, large enough to hold several hundred or thousand people; when the people heard troops arrive, they ran and hid within them; Zhigao knew this, set fire, and all were burned to death.

entries.zh: 十月丁丑，破賓州。
entries.en: On the dingchou day of the tenth month he captured Binzhou.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day of the tenth month, he broke Bin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 甲申，復據邕州，日夜伐木治舟楫，揚言復趨廣州。
entries.en: On the jiashen day he retook Yongzhou, cutting timber day and night to build boats while boasting he would strike Guangzhou again.
entries.literal: On the jiashen day, he again occupied Yong Prefecture, day and night felling trees to build boats and oars, proclaiming he would again rush toward Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 十二月壬申，又敗陳曙於金城驛。
entries.en: On the renshen day of the twelfth month he routed Chen Shu at Jincheng Post Station.
entries.literal: On the renshen day of the twelfth month, he again defeated Chen Shu at Jincheng Post Station.

entries.zh: 初，智高以反聞，朝廷命曙就擊之，既而楊畋、曹修、張忠、蔣偕相繼出，又以余靖、孫沔為安撫使。
entries.en: Zhigao's disinformation first drew Chen Shu, then Yang Tian, Cao Xiu, Zhang Zhong, and Jiang Xie; the court also appointed Yu Jing and Sun Mian as pacification commissioners.
entries.literal: Initially, Zhigao by false intelligence misled the court to order Shu to go and strike him; afterward Yang Tian, Cao Xiu, Zhang Zhong, and Jiang Xie successively went out; again Yu Jing and Sun Mian were made pacification commissioners.

entries.zh: 畋、修聞智高至，退軍避之。
entries.en: Yang Tian and Cao Xiu retreated as soon as they heard Zhigao was near.
entries.literal: Tian and Xiu, hearing Zhigao had arrived, withdrew their armies to avoid him.

entries.zh: 忠、偕勇而無謀，皆死。
entries.en: Zhang Zhong and Jiang Xie fought boldly but recklessly, and both were killed.
entries.literal: Zhong and Xie were brave but without strategy; both died.

entries.zh: 智高益自恣，南土騷然。
entries.en: Zhigao grew bolder still, and the south was in turmoil.
entries.literal: Zhigao grew ever more self-indulgent; the southern lands were in uproar.

entries.zh: 仁宗以為憂，命狄青為宣撫使，諸將皆受青節制。
entries.en: Alarmed, Emperor Renzong put Di Qing in overall command, with every general under his authority.
entries.literal: Emperor Renzong regarded it as a worry, and ordered Di Qing as pacification commissioner; all generals were under Qing's command and control.

entries.zh: 曙恐青至有功，亟挑戰，故敗。
entries.en: Chen Shu, afraid Di Qing would win the glory, rashly offered battle and was defeated.
entries.literal: Shu feared that when Qing arrived there would be merit, and urgently challenged battle; therefore he was defeated.

entries.zh: 撫水州 廣源州 黎洞 環州
entries.en: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, the Li Dong, and Huan Zhou.
entries.literal: Fu Shuizhou, Guang Yuanzhou, Li Dong, and Huan Zhou.

entries.zh: 竊惟周公念先業之艱難，《七月》之詩是作；
entries.en: We venture to reflect that the Duke of Zhou, recalling the hardships of his forefathers' labors, composed the "Seventh Month";
entries.literal: We venture to consider that the Duke of Zhou, mindful of the hardships of his forefathers' enterprise, therefore composed the poem "Seventh Month";

entries.zh: 孔子論前王之文獻，二代之禮可言。
entries.en: and that Confucius, expounding the records of former kings, showed that the rites of the Two Dynasties could still be set forth.
entries.literal: Confucius discussed the documents of former kings, and the rites of the Two Dynasties could be spoken of.

entries.zh: 故觀趙氏隆替之由，足見皇元混一之績。
entries.en: Thus in tracing the rise and fall of the House of Zhao one may fully discern the achievement of the Great Yuan in unifying the realm.
entries.literal: Therefore, observing the causes of the rise and fall of the House of Zhao suffices to show the achievement of the Great Yuan in unifying all.

entries.zh: 欽惟世祖聖德神功文武皇帝，初由宗邸親總大軍，龍旂出指於離方，羽葆歸登於乾御，櫛風沐雨，詎辭跋履之勞；
entries.en: We respectfully consider Emperor Shizu, Sagely in Virtue and Divine in Merit, Martial and Civil, who at first from his princely residence personally took command of the great army, sent the dragon banner forth toward the south, and with the feather canopy returned to ascend the northern throne—braving wind and rain and never shrinking from the hardship of long campaigns;
entries.literal: We respectfully consider the Sagely Virtue, Divine Merit, Martial and Civil Emperor Shizu, who at first from his princely residence personally commanded the great army; the dragon banner went forth pointing toward the south; the feather canopy returned to mount the northern throne; he combed the wind and bathed in rain, how could he decline the toil of long marches;

entries.zh: 略地攻城，咸遵禀授之算。
entries.en: in seizing territory and storming cities, all followed the strategies Heaven had entrusted to him.
entries.literal: in seizing territory and storming cities, all followed the plans received from above.

entries.zh: 揚舲而平江、漢，卷甲而克襄、樊。
entries.en: With sails raised he pacified the Yangtze and Han regions; with armies gathered he captured Xiangyang and Fancheng.
entries.literal: Raising sails, he pacified the Yangtze and Han; rolling up armor, he conquered Xiang and Fan.

entries.zh: 龔行吊伐之師，昭受寵綏之寄。
entries.en: He marched as Heaven's avenger on a punitive campaign and plainly received the charge to secure the realm in imperial grace and peace.
entries.literal: He righteously marched punitive forces and clearly received the charge of securing imperial favor and peace.

entries.zh: 及夫收圖書於勝國，輯黼冔於神京，拔宋臣而列政塗，載《宋史》而歸秘府。
entries.en: Then he gathered books from the conquered state, assembled ceremonial regalia in the sacred capital, raised Song officials to posts on the paths of government, and brought the History of Song into the imperial archives.
entries.literal: When he had gathered books from the conquered state, collected ceremonial caps in the sacred capital, elevated Song officials to the roads of governance, and deposited the History of Song in the secret archives.

entries.zh: 然後告成郊廟，錫慶臣民，推大賚以惟均，示一統之無外。
entries.en: Thereafter he reported completion to the suburban altars, bestowed blessings on officials and people, extended great largess with impartial generosity, and showed that under unification nothing lay beyond the realm.
entries.literal: Then he reported completion at the suburban altars, bestowed blessings on officials and people, extended great largess equitably, and showed that unification left nothing outside.

entries.zh: 樞庭偃武，既編戡定之勳；
entries.en: The Bureau of Military Affairs laid down arms and already compiled the record of pacification;
entries.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs rested arms and already compiled the records of pacification and settlement;

entries.zh: 翰苑摛文，尋奉纂修之旨。
entries.en: the Hanlin Academy took up its literary charge and soon received the imperial order to compile and revise.
entries.literal: the Hanlin Academy unfolded its writings and soon received the decree for compilation and revision.

entries.zh: 事幾有待，歲月易遷。
entries.en: Affairs still awaited their proper moment, and the years slipped quickly by.
entries.literal: Matters had to await their moment, and years easily passed.

entries.zh: 累朝每切於繼承，多務未遑於制作。
entries.en: Reign after reign urgently attended to succession, and amid pressing duties found no leisure for such compilation.
entries.literal: Successive reigns each urgently attended to succession, and amid many affairs had no leisure for compilation.

entries.zh: 臣阿魯圖等，誠惶誠恐，頓首頓首，欽惟皇帝陛下恢弘至道，紹述丕謨。
entries.en: We, your servants Aruqtai and others, in deepest awe and reverence bow our heads repeatedly, respectfully considering that Your Majesty expands the utmost Way and carries forward the great design.
entries.literal: Your servants Aruqtai and others, in sincere awe and sincere fear, bow our heads repeatedly, respectfully considering that Your Majesty expands the utmost Way and continues the great plan.

entries.zh: 往行前言，樂討論於古訓；
entries.en: You delight in the words of antiquity and take pleasure in debating the teachings of old;
entries.literal: You delight in examining the words of antiquity and take pleasure in discussing ancient teachings;

entries.zh: 祖宗功德，思揚厲於耿光。
entries.en: and you seek to exalt and display the brilliant glory of your ancestors' merit and virtue.
entries.literal: the merit and virtue of your ancestors, thinking to exalt and display their brilliant glory.

entries.zh: 惟我朝大啟基圖，彼吳會後歸版籍。
entries.en: Our dynasty greatly opened its founding design, and the Wu region at last returned to the imperial registers.
entries.literal: Our dynasty greatly opened its founding design, and that Wu region later returned to the registers.

entries.zh: 視金源其未遠，紬石室以具存，及茲累洽之時，成此彌文之典。
entries.en: The Jin dynasty lies not far behind us, the stone archives remain fully preserved, and at this time of accumulated harmony we complete this enriched literary canon.
entries.literal: Viewing the Jin source as not yet distant, drawing together the stone chamber so that all is preserved, and at this time of accumulated harmony completing this enriched literary canon.

entries.zh: 命臣阿魯圖、左丞相臣別兒怯不花領史事，前右丞相臣脫脫為都總裁，平章政事臣帖穆爾達世、御史大夫臣惟一、翰林學士承旨臣起巖、臣玄、治書御史臣好文、禮部尚書臣沂、崇文大監臣宗瑞為總裁官，平章政事臣納麟、臣顏、前中書右丞 臣達世睦邇、左丞 臣守簡、參議 臣岳柱、臣住、臣思謙、郎中 臣斡欒、臣思立等協恭董治，史官工部侍郎 臣斡玉倫徒，秘書卿 臣泰不華、太常僉院 臣杜秉彝、翰林直學士 臣宋褧，國子司業 臣王思誠、臣澤民、集賢待制 臣干文傳、翰林待制 臣張瑾、臣師道、宣文閣鑒書博士 臣麥文貴、監察御史 臣余闕、太常博士 臣李齊、翰林修撰 臣劉聞、太醫院都事 臣賈魯、國子助教 臣馮福可、太廟署令 臣陳祖仁、西臺御史 臣趙中、翰林應奉 臣王儀、臣貞、秘書著作左郎 臣譚慥、翰林編修 臣張翥、國子助教 臣吳當、經筵檢討 臣危素編劘分局，彙粹為書。
entries.en: Your Majesty appointed Aruqtai and Left Chancellor Bayan Qutlugh to direct the history project, with former Right Chancellor Toqto'a as chief director-in-chief, and Chief Directors including Chief Councillors Temür Dash, Censor-in-Chief Weiyi, Hanlin Academicians Expositor Qiyan and Xuan, Investigating Censor Haowen, Minister of Rites Yi, and Director of the Directorate of Education Zongrui; together with Chief Councillors Nalin and Yan, former Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Dashimur, Left Vice Director Shoujian, Counsellors Yuezhu, Zhu, and Siqian, Bureau Directors Olon and Sili, and others to assist in reverent supervision; and history officers including Vice Minister of Works Oluntur, Secretary Director Taibuhua, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Du Bingyi, Hanlin Academician Song Jiong, Rectors of the Directorate of Education Wang Sicheng and Zemin, Awaiting Editor-in-Chief of the Hall of Gathered Worthies Gan Wenchuan, Hanlin Awaiting Editors Zhang Jin and Shidao, Doctor of the Xuanwen Pavilion Mai Wengui, Investigating Censor Yu Que, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Qi, Hanlin Compiler Liu Wen, Chief Administrator of the Imperial Medical Institute Jia Lu, Instructors of the Directorate of Education Feng Fuke, Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office Chen Zuren, Western Censor Zhao Zhong, Hanlin Attendants Wang Yi and Zhen, Left Secretary Compiler Tan Zao, Hanlin Compiler Zhang Zhu, Instructor of the Directorate of Education Wu Dang, and Classics Lectures Reviewer Wei Su to edit in separate bureaus and gather the whole into a book.
entries.literal: Your Majesty ordered your servant Aruqtai and Left Chancellor Bayan Qutlugh to direct the history project, former Right Chancellor Toqto'a as chief director-in-chief, and Chief Directors including Chief Councillors Temür Dash, Censor-in-Chief Weiyi, Hanlin Academician Expositor Qiyan, Xuan, Investigating Censor Haowen, Minister of Rites Yi, and Director of the Directorate of Education Zongrui; Chief Councillors Nalin and Yan, former Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Dashimur, Left Vice Director Shoujian, Counsellors Yuezhu, Zhu, and Siqian, Bureau Directors Olon and Sili, and others to assist in reverent supervision; history officers including Vice Minister of Works Oluntur, Secretary Director Taibuhua, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Du Bingyi, Hanlin Academician Song Jiong, Rectors of the Directorate of Education Wang Sicheng and Zemin, Awaiting Editor-in-Chief of the Hall of Gathered Worthies Gan Wenchuan, Hanlin Awaiting Editors Zhang Jin and Shidao, Doctor of the Xuanwen Pavilion Mai Wengui, Investigating Censor Yu Que, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Qi, Hanlin Compiler Liu Wen, Chief Administrator of the Imperial Medical Institute Jia Lu, Instructor of the Directorate of Education Feng Fuke, Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office Chen Zuren, Western Censor Zhao Zhong, Hanlin Attendants Wang Yi and Zhen, Left Secretary Compiler Tan Zao, Hanlin Compiler Zhang Zhu, Instructor of the Directorate of Education Wu Dang, and Classics Lectures Reviewer Wei Su to edit in separate bureaus and gather the essence into a book.

entries.zh: 進《宋史》表
entries.en: Memorial Presenting the History of Song
entries.literal: Memorial presenting the History of Song.

entries.zh: 永初元年夏六月丁卯，設壇於南郊，即皇帝位，柴燎告天。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer of the inaugural year Yongchu, on the day dingmao, an altar was raised at the southern suburb. Liu Yu took the imperial throne and burned firewood to announce his accession to Heaven.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of summer of the first year of Yongchu, on the day dingmao, an altar was set up at the southern suburb; he took the imperial throne and burned firewood to announce to Heaven.

entries.zh: 策曰：
entries.en: The accession proclamation read:
entries.literal: The mandate text reads:

entries.zh: 皇帝臣裕，敢用玄牡，昭告皇天后帝。
entries.en: The Emperor, your subject Yu, ventures to offer a black bull and proclaim plainly to August Heaven and Sovereign Earth.
entries.literal: The Emperor, your subject Yu, ventures to use a black bull to proclaim clearly to August Heaven and Sovereign Earth.

entries.zh: 晉帝以卜世告終，歷數有歸，欽若景運，以命于裕。
entries.en: The Jin emperor, because divination showed his dynasty's term had ended and the mandate had passed to its rightful holder, reverently followed the age's flourishing fortune and entrusted the mandate to Yu.
entries.literal: The Jin Emperor, because divination showed his dynasty's allotted span had ended and the mandate had found its destination, reverently followed the flourishing fortune and entrusted the mandate to Yu.

entries.zh: 夫樹君宰世，天下為公，德充帝王，樂推攸集。
entries.en: To set up a ruler and govern the world: the realm belongs to all; when virtue matches that of emperors and kings, the people's willing endorsement gathers of itself.
entries.literal: To establish a ruler and govern the age—under Heaven all is public; when virtue fills the place of emperor or king, willing abdication gathers of itself.

entries.zh: 越俶唐、虞，降暨漢、魏，靡不以上哲格文祖，元勳陟帝位，故能大拯黔首，垂訓無窮。
entries.en: From Yao and Shun down through Han and Wei, none failed to have a supreme sage align with the founding ancestor of civilization and a chief merit-holder ascend the throne, thereby greatly rescuing the common people and handing down instruction without end.
entries.literal: Tracing from Yao and Shun down through Han and Wei, none failed to have a supreme sage align with the culture-founding ancestor and a chief merit-holder ascend the imperial seat, thereby able greatly to rescue the black-headed people and hand down instruction without end.

entries.zh: 晉自東遷，四維不振，宰輔焉依，為日巳久。
entries.en: After the Jin moved south, the four pillars of order no longer held firm, and the court had long depended on chief ministers.
entries.literal: Since the Jin moved east, the four bonds were not secured; reliance on chief ministers had already lasted a long time.

entries.zh: 難棘隆安，禍成元興，遂至帝主遷播，宗祀堙滅。
entries.en: Hardship piled up in the Long'an era, catastrophe took shape under Yuanxing, until emperors were driven from the capital and the ancestral rites were cut off.
entries.literal: Distress piled up in the Long'an reign, disaster took shape in the Yuanxing era, until sovereigns were driven to wander and ancestral sacrifices were buried and extinguished.

entries.zh: 裕雖地非齊、晉，眾無一旅，仰憤時難，俯悼橫流，投袂一麾，[1]則皇祀克復。
entries.en: Though Yu's domain was no match for Qi or Jin and his forces scarcely amounted to a regiment, he looked up in anger at the age's calamities and down in grief at the flood of ruin; with a shake of his sleeve and one command, [1] the imperial sacrifices were restored.
entries.literal: Though Yu's territory was not like Qi or Jin and his forces lacked a full regiment, looking up he was stirred by the age's hardship, looking down he grieved the flood of ruin; with a shake of his sleeve and one command, [1] the imperial sacrifices were restored.

entries.zh: 及危而能持，顛而能扶，姦宄具殲，僭偽必滅。
entries.en: In peril he could hold firm; when the order was overturned he could set it right; treacherous evildoers were wiped out, and usurping pretenders were destroyed.
entries.literal: In danger he could hold fast; when overturned he could set upright; treacherous evildoers were entirely exterminated; usurping pretenders were certainly destroyed.

entries.zh: 誠興廢有期，否終有數。
entries.en: Truly, the revival of what had been cast down has its season, and the end of decline has its reckoning.
entries.literal: Truly, revival of what was abolished has its season; the end of obstruction has its count.

entries.zh: 至於大造晉室，撥亂濟民，因藉時來，實尸其重。
entries.en: As for greatly rebuilding the Jin house, quelling chaos and succoring the people—riding the tide of the times, he truly bore the heaviest burden.
entries.literal: As to greatly rebuilding the Jin house, putting down disorder and aiding the people—riding the tide of the times, he truly bore its weight.

entries.zh: 加以殊俗慕義，重譯來庭，正朔所暨，咸服聲教。
entries.en: Moreover, distant peoples admired righteousness, envoys came again and again to court, and wherever the imperial calendar reached, all submitted to civilizing rule.
entries.literal: Moreover, distant peoples admired righteousness; repeated translators came to court; wherever the correct calendar reached, all submitted to transforming instruction.

entries.zh: 至乃三靈垂象，山川告祥，人神協祉，歲月滋著。
entries.en: Even the three luminaries sent down portents, mountains and rivers announced auspicious signs, and heaven and earth joined in blessing, so that the mandate grew clearer month by month and year by year.
entries.literal: Even the three luminous bodies sent down signs, mountains and rivers announced auspice, man and spirits joined in blessing—the months and years daily grew manifest.

entries.zh: 是以羣公卿士，億兆夷人，僉曰皇靈降鑒於上，晉朝款誠於下，天命不可以久淹，宸極不可以暫曠。
entries.en: Therefore the nobles, ministers, and officials, and the hundred million common people, all said that the August Spirit looked down from above while the Jin court showed sincerity below: the Mandate of Heaven could not long be delayed, and the imperial throne could not remain vacant.
entries.literal: Therefore dukes, ministers, and officials, the hundred million common folk, all said the August Spirit sent down inspection from above, the Jin court showed sincerity below—the Mandate of Heaven cannot long be delayed, the imperial pinnacle cannot briefly be vacant.

entries.zh: 遂逼羣議，恭茲大禮。
entries.en: They thereupon pressed him with collective counsel and respectfully performed this great ceremony.
entries.literal: They thereupon pressed him with collective counsel and respectfully performed this great rite.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：漢氏載祀四百，比祚隆周，雖復四海橫潰，而民繫劉氏，惵惵黔首，未有遷奉之心。
entries.en: The historian states: The Han house carried sacrifices for four hundred years, its fortune comparable to the flourishing Zhou; though the four seas collapsed in ruin, the people remained bound to the Liu clan—the common people had no heart to shift allegiance.
entries.literal: The historian states: The Han house carried sacrifices for four hundred years, its fortune comparable to the flourishing Zhou; though the four seas collapsed in ruin, the people were bound to the Liu clan—the trembling black-headed people had no heart to shift allegiance.

entries.zh: 魏武直以兵威服眾，故能坐移天曆，鼎運雖改，而民未忘漢。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Wei directly by military prestige made the masses submit, and so was able to sit and shift the heavenly calendar; though the mandate changed, the people had not forgotten Han.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei directly by military prestige made the masses submit, and so was able to sit and shift the heavenly calendar; though the tripod's fortune changed, the people had not forgotten Han.

entries.zh: 及魏室衰孤，怨非結下。
entries.en: When the Wei house declined and stood isolated, resentment was not tied to the lower ranks.
entries.literal: When the Wei house declined and was isolated, resentment was not tied to the lower ranks.

entries.zh: 晉藉宰輔之柄，因皇族之微，世擅重權，用基王業。
entries.en: Jin relied on the power of chief ministers; because the imperial clan was weak, generation after generation they monopolized heavy authority and thereby founded the royal enterprise.
entries.literal: Jin relied on the handle of chief ministers; because the imperial clan was slight, generation after generation monopolized heavy power and thereby founded the royal enterprise.

entries.zh: 至於宋祖受命，義越前模。
entries.en: As for the founding emperor of Song receiving the mandate, the righteousness surpassed former models.
entries.literal: As for the founding emperor of Song receiving the mandate, the righteousness surpassed former models.

entries.zh: 晉自社廟南遷，祿去王室，朝權國命，遞歸台輔。
entries.en: Since Jin's altars moved south, emolument departed from the royal house; court power and the state's mandate in succession returned to the terrace ministers.
entries.literal: Since Jin's altars moved south, emolument departed from the royal house; court power and the state's mandate in succession returned to the terrace ministers.

entries.zh: 君道雖存，主威久謝。
entries.en: The way of the ruler though it existed, the sovereign's prestige had long declined.
entries.literal: The way of the ruler though existed, the sovereign's prestige had long declined.

entries.zh: 桓溫雄才葢世，勳高一時，移鼎之業巳成，天人之望將改。
entries.en: Huan Wen's heroic talent covered the age and his merit stood highest for a time; the enterprise of shifting the mandate was already accomplished and Heaven and man's expectation was about to change.
entries.literal: Huan Wen's heroic talent covered the age and his merit was highest for a time; the enterprise of shifting the tripod was already accomplished and Heaven and man's expectation was about to change.

entries.zh: 自斯以後，晉道彌昏，道子開其禍端，元顯成其末釁，桓玄藉運乘時，加以先父之業，因基革命，人無異心。
entries.en: From then on Jin's way grew ever darker; Daozi opened the source of calamity and Yuanxian completed the final provocation; Huan Xuan rode fortune and seized the season, adding his father's former enterprise, and thereby founded revolution—among the people there was no divergent heart.
entries.literal: From then on Jin's way grew ever darker; Daozi opened the source of calamity and Yuanxian completed the final provocation; Huan Xuan rode fortune and seized the season, adding his father's former enterprise, and thereby founded revolution—among the people there was no divergent heart.

entries.zh: 高祖地非桓、文，眾無一旅，曾不浹旬，夷凶翦暴，祀晉配天，不失舊物，誅內清外，功格區宇。
entries.en: Gaozu's territory was not like Duke Huan or Duke Wen's, his forces scarcely amounted to a regiment; in less than ten days he extinguished the fierce and cut down the violent, sacrificed to Jin and matched Heaven, did not lose the old emblems, punished within and cleared without—merit reached the realm.
entries.literal: Gaozu's territory was not like Duke Huan or Duke Wen's, his forces lacked a full regiment; in less than ten days he extinguished the fierce and cut down the violent, sacrificed to Jin and matched Heaven, did not lose the old emblems, punished within and cleared without—merit reached the realm.

entries.zh: 至於鍾石變聲，柴天改物，民巳去晉，異於延康之初，功實靜亂，又殊咸熙之末。
entries.en: As to bells and stones changing their sound and burning firewood to Heaven to change the regime—the people had already departed from Jin, differing from the beginning of Yanxi; the achievement truly quieted disorder, again unlike the end of Xianxi.
entries.literal: As to bells and stones changing their sound and burning firewood to Heaven to change things—the people had already departed from Jin, differing from the beginning of Yanxi; the achievement truly quieted disorder, again unlike the end of Xianxi.

entries.zh: 所以恭皇高遜，殆均釋負。
entries.en: Therefore Emperor Gong's lofty abdication was nearly equal to laying down a burden.
entries.literal: Therefore Emperor Gong's lofty abdication was nearly equal to laying down a burden.

entries.zh: 若夫樂推所歸，謳歌所集，魏、晉采其名，高祖收其實矣。
entries.en: As for where willing abdication returns and songs of praise gather—Wei and Jin harvested the name, but Gaozu gathered the reality.
entries.literal: As for where willing abdication returns and songs of praise gather—Wei and Jin harvested the name, but Gaozu gathered the reality.

entries.zh: 盛哉！
entries.en: Magnificent!
entries.literal: Magnificent!

entries.zh: 猥以寡德，託於兆民之上，雖仰畏天威，略是小節，顧深永懷，[2]祗懼若霣。
entries.en: Humbly, with scant virtue, I rest upon the myriad people above; though in awe of Heaven's majesty this is a small matter, yet turning deeply to lasting recollection, [2] I am reverently fearful as though about to fall.
entries.literal: Humbly with scant virtue, resting on the myriad people above—though in awe of Heaven's majesty this is a small ceremony, yet turning deeply to lasting recollection, [2] reverent fear as though falling.

entries.zh: 敬簡元辰，升壇受禪，告類上帝，用酬萬國之情。
entries.en: Respectfully selecting this great day, I ascend the altar to receive the abdication, announce the succession to High God, and thereby answer the feeling of all under Heaven.
entries.literal: Respectfully selecting the great day, ascending the altar to receive the abdication, announcing the category to High God, thereby answering all under Heaven's feeling.

entries.zh: 克隆天保，永祚于有宋。
entries.en: May Heaven's blessing be magnified and everlasting fortune rest upon Song.
entries.literal: May Heaven's blessing be magnified, and everlasting fortune rest on Song.

entries.zh: 惟明靈是饗。
entries.en: May the luminous spirits accept this offering.
entries.literal: May the luminous spirits be satisfied.

entries.zh: 二年春正月辛酉，車駕祠南郊，大赦天下。
entries.en: In spring, the first month of the second year, on the day xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a great amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month of the second year, on the day xinyou, the imperial carriage sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 丙寅，斷金銀塗。
entries.en: On the day bingyin, gilding with gold and silver was prohibited.
entries.literal: On the day bingyin, gilding with gold and silver was prohibited.

entries.zh: 以揚州刺史廬陵王義真為司徒，以尚書僕射、鎮軍將軍徐羨之為尚書令、揚州刺史。
entries.en: The Prince of Luling, Yizhen, Governor of Yang Province, was made Minister over the Masses; Secretariat Director and General Who Stabilizes the Army Xu Xianzhi was made Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Yang Province.
entries.literal: The Prince of Luling, Yizhen, was made Governor of Yang Province; Secretariat Director and General Who Stabilizes the Army Xu Xianzhi was made Secretariat Director and Governor of Yang Province.

entries.zh: 丙子，南康揭陽蠻反，郡縣討破之。
entries.en: On the day bingzi, the Jieyang barbarians of Nankang rebelled; commanderies and counties attacked and defeated them.
entries.literal: On the day bingzi, the Jieyang barbarians of Nankang rebelled; commanderies and counties attacked and defeated them.

entries.zh: 己卯，禁喪事用銅釘。
entries.en: On the day jimao, the use of copper nails in funeral affairs was forbidden.
entries.literal: On the day jimao, the use of copper nails in funeral affairs was forbidden.

entries.zh: 罷會稽郡府。
entries.en: The prefectural headquarters of Kuaiji Commandery was abolished.
entries.literal: The prefectural headquarters of Kuaiji Commandery was abolished.

entries.zh: 三年春正月甲辰朔，詔刑罰無輕重，悉皆原降。
entries.en: In spring, the first month of the third year, on the first day jiachen, an edict stated that punishments, without regard to severity, were all pardoned and reduced.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month of the third year, on the first day jiachen, an edict stated that punishments, without regard to severity, were all pardoned and reduced.

entries.zh: 壬子，以前冀州刺史王仲德為徐州刺史。
entries.en: On the day renzi, the former Governor of Ji Province Wang Zhongde was made Governor of Xu Province.
entries.literal: On the day renzi, the former Governor of Ji Province Wang Zhongde was made Governor of Xu Province.

entries.zh: 癸丑，以尚書令、揚州刺史徐羨之為司空、錄尚書事，刺史如故。
entries.en: On the day guichou, Secretariat Director and Governor of Yang Province Xu Xianzhi was made Minister of Works and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, with his governorship unchanged.
entries.literal: On the day guichou, Secretariat Director and Governor of Yang Province Xu Xianzhi was made Minister of Works and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, with his governorship unchanged.

entries.zh: 撫軍將軍、江州刺史王弘進號衞將軍、開府儀同三司，太子詹事傅亮為尚書僕射，中領軍謝晦為領軍將軍。
entries.en: General Who Comforts the Army and Governor of Jiang Province Wang Hong was advanced to General of the Guards and Commissioner with the Golden Grandee's insignia and ceremonial staff equal to the Three Dukes; Household Mentor of the Heir Fu Liang was made Secretariat Director; Central Army Commander Xie Hui was made Commander-in-Chief.
entries.literal: General Who Comforts the Army and Governor of Jiang Province Wang Hong was advanced to General of the Guards and Commissioner with the Golden Grandee's insignia and ceremonial staff equal to the Three Dukes; Household Mentor of the Heir Fu Liang was made Secretariat Director; Central Army Commander Xie Hui was made Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 乙卯，以輔國將軍毛德祖為司州刺史。
entries.en: On the day yimao, General Who Assists the State Mao Dezu was made Governor of Si Province.
entries.literal: On the day yimao, General Who Assists the State Mao Dezu was made Governor of Si Province.

entries.zh: [11]乙丑，詔曰：「古之建國，教學為先，弘風訓世，莫尚於此，發蒙啟滯，咸必由之。
entries.en: [11] On the day yichou, an edict stated: "In establishing a state of antiquity, teaching came first; to spread transforming influence and instruct the age, nothing is more honored than this; to open the benighted and relieve stagnation, all must pass through it.
entries.literal: [11] On the day yichou, an edict stated: "In establishing a state of antiquity, teaching came first; to spread transforming influence and instruct the age, nothing is more honored than this; to open the benighted and relieve stagnation, all must pass through it.

entries.zh: 故爰自盛王，迄于近代，莫不敦崇學藝，修建庠序。
entries.en: Therefore from the flourishing kings down to recent ages, none failed to esteem learning and arts and to build and repair schools.
entries.literal: Therefore from the flourishing kings down to recent ages, none failed to esteem and honor learning and arts and to build and repair schools.

entries.zh: 自昔多故，戎馬在郊，旍旗卷舒，日不暇給。
entries.en: Formerly there were many troubles; war horses were in the suburbs; banners rolled and unfurled, and days allowed no rest.
entries.literal: Formerly many troubles; war horses were in the suburbs; banners rolled and unfurled, and days allowed no rest.

entries.zh: 遂令學校荒廢，講誦蔑聞，軍旅日陳，俎豆藏器，訓誘之風，將墜于地。
entries.en: Thus schools were left desolate and lectures and recitation went unheard; armies were arrayed daily while sacrificial vessels were stored away; the wind of instruction and guidance was about to fall to earth.
entries.literal: Thus schools were left desolate and lectures and recitation went unheard; armies were arrayed daily while sacrificial vessels were stored away; the wind of instruction and guidance was about to fall to earth.

entries.zh: 後生大懼於牆面，故老竊歎於子衿。
entries.en: The young greatly feared facing the wall in ignorance, and old men privately sighed over the collar-gem.
entries.literal: The young greatly feared facing the wall, and old men privately sighed over the collar-gem.

entries.zh: 此國風所以永思，小雅所以懷古。
entries.en: This is why the nation's manners forever yearn for it, and the Lesser Odes therefore cherish antiquity.
entries.literal: This is why the nation's wind forever thinks of it, and the Lesser Odes therefore cherish antiquity.

entries.zh: 今王略遠屆，華域載清，仰風之士，日月以冀。
entries.en: Now the royal design extends afar and the flowering realm is cleared; those who look up to transforming influence increase day by day in hope.
entries.literal: Now the royal design extends afar and the flowering realm is cleared; those who look up to transforming influence increase day by day in hope.

entries.zh: 便宜博延冑子，陶奬童蒙，選備儒官，弘振國學。
entries.en: It is fitting broadly to extend noble sons, cultivate and encourage the young, select and prepare Confucian officials, and grandly revive the state school.
entries.literal: It is fitting broadly to extend noble sons, cultivate and encourage the young, select and prepare Confucian officials, and grandly revive the state school.

entries.zh: 主者考詳舊典，以時施行。」
entries.en: The responsible officials were to examine the old canon in detail and implement it in due time."
entries.literal: The responsible officials should examine the old canon in detail and implement it in due time."

entries.zh: 五月，上疾甚，召太子誡之曰：「檀道濟雖有幹略，而無遠志，非如兄韶有難御之氣也。
entries.en: In the fifth month, the emperor was gravely ill and summoned the Crown Prince to admonish him: "Tan Daoji has capacity and plan, but no far-reaching aim; he is not like his elder brother Shao, who has a spirit hard to control.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, the Emperor was gravely ill and summoned the Crown Prince to admonish him: "Tan Daoji has capacity and plan, but no far-reaching aim; he is not like your brother Shao, who has a hard-to-control spirit.

entries.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮當無異圖。
entries.en: Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang should have no divergent designs.
entries.literal: Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang should have no divergent designs.

entries.zh: 謝晦數從征伐，頗識機變，若有同異，必此人也。
entries.en: Xie Hui has followed campaigns many times and knows well how opportunity shifts; if there is divergence, it will surely be this man.
entries.literal: Xie Hui has followed campaigns many times and knows well how opportunity shifts; if there is divergence, it will surely be this man.

entries.zh: 小卻，可以會稽、江州處之。」
entries.en: When he recovers a little, he may be placed at Kuaiji and Jiang Province."
entries.literal: When he is a little better, he may be placed at Kuaiji and Jiang Province."

entries.zh: 又為手詔曰：「朝廷不須復有別府，宰相帶揚州，可置甲士千人。
entries.en: He also made a hand edict: "The court need not again have a separate headquarters; the chief minister should hold Yang Province and may have one thousand armored soldiers.
entries.literal: He also made a hand edict: "The court need not again have a separate headquarters; the chief minister should hold Yang Province and may have one thousand armored soldiers.

entries.zh: 若大臣中任要，宜有爪牙以備不祥人者，可以臺見隊給之。
entries.en: If among great ministers one holds a key post and should have guards to ward against unlucky men, he may be given the Terrace Guard detachment.
entries.literal: If among great ministers one holds a key post and should have claws and teeth to guard against unlucky men, he may be given the Terrace Guard detachment.

entries.zh: 有征討悉配以臺見軍隊，行還復舊。
entries.en: Where there is campaigning, all are to be assigned the Terrace Guard army; when they return, the old arrangement is restored.
entries.literal: Where there is campaigning, all are to be assigned the Terrace Guard army; when they return, the old arrangement is restored.

entries.zh: 後世若有幼主，朝事一委宰相，母后不煩臨朝。
entries.en: If in later generations there is a young sovereign, court affairs are entirely entrusted to the chief minister; the empress dowager need not attend court.
entries.literal: If in later generations there is a young sovereign, court affairs are entirely entrusted to the chief minister; the empress dowager need not attend court.

entries.zh: 仗既不許入臺殿門，要重人可詳給班劍。」
entries.en: Weapons are not permitted to enter the terrace and palace gates; for important men, court swords may be granted in detail."
entries.literal: Weapons are not permitted to enter the terrace and palace gates; for important men, court swords may be granted in detail."

entries.zh: 癸亥，上崩于西殿，時年六十。
entries.en: On the day guihai, the emperor died in the Western Hall, aged sixty.
entries.literal: On the day guihai, the Emperor died in the Western Hall, aged sixty.

entries.en: Editorial note fourteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
entries.literal: Editorial note fourteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

entries.zh: 禮畢，備法駕幸建康宮，臨太極前殿。
entries.en: When the rite was concluded, with full imperial equipage he went to Jiankang Palace and took his seat in the front hall of the Grand Ultimate.
entries.literal: When the rite was concluded, with full imperial equipage he proceeded to Jiankang Palace and attended the front hall of the Grand Ultimate.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「夫世代迭興，承天統極，雖遭遇異塗，因革殊事，若乃功濟區宇，道振生民，興廢所階，異世一揆。
entries.en: An edict stated: "Dynasties rise in succession and inherit Heaven's mandate; though they meet different circumstances and institutions change with the times, when merit saves the realm and the Way stirs the living people, the stages of rise and fall differ in age yet follow one measure.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Generations in succession rise; inheriting Heaven's succession and reaching the pinnacle—though they meet different paths and institutions change with different affairs, if merit saves the realm and the Way stirs the living people, the stages of rise and fall differ in age but share one measure.

entries.zh: 朕以寡薄，屬當艱運，藉否終之期，因士民之力，用獲拯溺，匡世撥亂，安國寧民，業未半古，功參曩烈。
entries.en: I, of meager virtue, stand at a harsh turning in fate; relying on the season when decline was ending and on the strength of scholars and people, I rescued the realm from ruin, set the age right, and settled the state and quieted the people. The achievement is not yet half that of antiquity, yet the merit rivals past glories.
entries.literal: I, with meager thinness, stand at a hard fortune; relying on the season when obstruction ends, by the strength of scholars and people I obtained rescue from drowning, corrected the age and put down disorder, settled the state and quieted the people; the enterprise is not yet half of antiquity, yet the achievement rivals past glories.

entries.zh: 晉氏以多難仍遘，曆運巳移，欽若前王，憲章令軌，用集大命于朕躬。
entries.en: The Jin house, because hardship followed hardship, saw its mandate already shift; reverently following former kings and taking their statutes as the present norm, the great mandate was gathered upon my person.
entries.literal: The Jin clan, because many hardships followed in succession, saw its mandate already shift; reverently following former kings, taking their statutes and present norms, the great mandate was gathered upon my person.

entries.zh: 惟德匪嗣，辭不獲申，遂祗順三靈，饗茲景祚，燔柴于南郊，受終于文祖。
entries.en: My virtue does not match the succession; I could not decline further, and so reverently followed the three spirits, received this bright fortune, burned firewood at the southern suburb, and received the mandate's end from the culture-founding ancestor.
entries.literal: My virtue does not succeed; I could not decline further, and so reverently followed the three spirits and received this bright fortune; burned firewood at the southern suburb and received the end of the mandate from the culture-founding ancestor.

entries.zh: 猥當與能之期，爰集樂推之運，嘉祚肇開，隆慶惟始，思俾休嘉，惠茲兆庶。
entries.en: I unworthily stand at the season when the able are gathered and at the fortune when willing abdication assembles; auspicious fortune has newly opened and grand celebration has just begun; I wish to spread fine blessing and favor these myriad people.
entries.literal: I unworthily stand at the season when the able are gathered, and at the fortune when willing abdication assembles; auspicious fortune newly opens, grand celebration has just begun; I think to spread fine blessing and favor these myriad people.

entries.zh: 其大赦天下。
entries.en: Let there be a great amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Let there be a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 改晉元熙二年為永初元年。
entries.en: Change the second year of Yuanxi of Jin to the first year of Yongchu.
entries.literal: Change the second year of Yuanxi of Jin to the first year of Yongchu.

entries.zh: 賜民爵二級。
entries.en: Grant the people two ranks of noble status.
entries.literal: Grant the people two ranks of noble status.

entries.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，人穀五斛。
entries.en: For widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves, give five piculs of grain per person.
entries.literal: For widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves, give five piculs of grain per person.

entries.zh: 逋租宿債勿復收。
entries.en: Overdue rents and old debts shall not be collected again.
entries.literal: Overdue rents and old debts are not to be collected again.

entries.zh: 其有犯鄉論清議、贓汙淫盜，一皆蕩滌洗除，與之更始。
entries.en: Those who have violated village standards of conduct, or committed corruption, debauchery, or theft—all are to be cleared and given a fresh start.
entries.literal: Those who have violated village discourse and pure judgment, or committed corruption, debauchery, or theft—all are to be washed clean and removed, and given a new beginning.

entries.zh: 長徒之身，特皆原遣。
entries.en: Persons sentenced to long penal service are all specially pardoned and sent home.
entries.literal: Persons sentenced to long penal service are especially all pardoned and sent home.

entries.zh: 亡官失爵，禁錮奪勞，一依舊准。」
entries.en: Those who lost office or rank, were barred from office, or had labor levies taken—all follow the former standards."
entries.literal: Those who lost office or rank, were forbidden from office, or had labor levies taken—all follow the old standards."

entries.zh: 戊辰，詔曰：「彭、沛、下邳三郡，首事所基，情義繾綣，事由情奬，古今所同。
entries.en: On the day wuchen, an edict stated: "The three commanderies Peng, Pei, and Xiapi were the base of the first enterprise; affection and righteousness were close-knit—the matter proceeds from feeling and reward, the same in ancient and modern times.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen, an edict stated: "The three commanderies Peng, Pei, and Xiapi were the base of the first enterprise; affection and righteousness were close-knit—the matter proceeds from feeling and reward, the same in ancient and modern times.

entries.zh: 彭城桑梓本鄉，加隆攸在，優復之制，宜同豐、沛。
entries.en: Pengcheng is the native district of the homeland; where special favor is due, the preferential exemption system should be the same as Feng and Pei.
entries.literal: Pengcheng is the native district of the mulberry-and-catalpa homeland; where special favor is due, the preferential exemption system should be the same as Feng and Pei.

entries.zh: 其沛郡、下邳可復租布三十年。」
entries.en: Pei Commandery and Xiapi may have land cloth exempted for thirty years."
entries.literal: Pei Commandery and Xiapi may have land cloth exempted for thirty years."

entries.zh: 秋七月己酉，葬丹陽建康縣蔣山初寧陵。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jiyou, he was buried at Chuning Mausoleum on Mount Jiang in Jianye County, Danyang.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jiyou, he was buried at Chuning Mausoleum on Mount Jiang in Jianye County, Danyang.

entries.zh: 封晉帝為零陵王，全食一郡。
entries.en: The Jin emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Lingling, with the full revenue of one commandery.
entries.literal: The Jin Emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Lingling, with the full revenue of one commandery.

entries.zh: 載天子旍旗，乘五時副車，行晉正朔，郊祀天地禮樂制度，皆用晉典。
entries.en: He bore the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, rode the five-season secondary chariot, followed the Jin calendar, and in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, rites, music, and institutions—all followed Jin regulations.
entries.literal: He bore the Son of Heaven's banner and flags, rode the five-season secondary chariot, followed the Jin calendar, and in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, rites and music, and institutions—all used Jin regulations.

entries.zh: 上書不為表，答表勿稱詔。
entries.en: In memorials to the throne he did not use the form "memorial"; in replies to memorials the word "edict" was not used.
entries.literal: In memorials to the throne he did not use the form "memorial"; in replies to memorials the word "edict" was not used.

entries.zh: 追尊皇考為孝穆皇帝，皇妣為穆皇后，尊王太后為皇太后。
entries.en: He posthumously honored his late father as Emperor Xiaomu, his late mother as Empress Mu, and honored the Wang Empress Dowager as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Posthumously honored his late father as Emperor Xiaomu, his late mother as Empress Mu, and honored the Wang Empress Dowager as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「夫微禹之感，歎深後昆，盛德必祀，道隆百世。
entries.en: An edict stated: "The regret at slighting Yu runs deep for later generations; great virtue must receive sacrifice, and the Way is honored for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The feeling at Wei's slighting of Yu runs deep for later generations; great virtue must receive sacrifice, and the Way is exalted for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 晉氏封爵，咸隨運改，至於德參微管，勳濟蒼生，愛人懷樹，猶或勿翦，雖在異代，義無泯絕。
entries.en: Jin enfeoffments all changed with the shifting mandate; yet for those whose virtue matched Guan Zhong and whose merit aided the people—loving men cherish trees, and even when cut they may not be felled; though in a different age, righteousness does not permit their rites to be extinguished.
entries.literal: Jin enfeoffments all changed with the fortune; yet as to those whose virtue matched the slight Guan Zhong and whose merit aided the black-headed people—loving men cherish trees, and even if cut they may not be felled; though in a different age, righteousness does not permit extinction.

entries.zh: 降殺之宜，一依前典。
entries.en: The propriety of lowering and reducing ranks should wholly follow the former canon.
entries.literal: The propriety of lowering and reducing ranks should wholly follow the former canon.

entries.zh: 可降始興公封始興縣公，廬陵公封柴桑縣公，各千戶；
entries.en: The Duke of Shixing may be reduced and enfeoffed as Duke of Shixing County, the Duke of Luling as Duke of Chaisang County, each with one thousand households;
entries.literal: The Duke of Shixing may be reduced and enfeoffed as Duke of Shixing County, the Duke of Luling as Duke of Chaisang County, each with one thousand households;

entries.zh: 始安公封荔浦縣侯，長沙公封醴陵縣侯，康樂公可即封縣侯，各五百戶：以奉晉故丞相王導、太傅謝安、大將軍溫嶠、大司馬陶侃、車騎將軍謝玄之祀。
entries.en: the Duke of Shi'an enfeoffed as Marquis of Lipu County, the Duke of Changsha as Marquis of Liling County, the Duke of Kangle immediately enfeoffed as county marquis, each with five hundred households—to maintain the sacrifices to former Jin Chancellor Wang Dao, Grand Tutor Xie An, Grand General Wen Qiao, Grand Marshal Tao Kan, and Cavalry General Xie Xuan.
entries.literal: the Duke of Shi'an enfeoffed as Marquis of Lipu County, the Duke of Changsha as Marquis of Liling County, the Duke of Kangle immediately enfeoffed as county marquis, each with five hundred households: to maintain the sacrifices to former Jin Chancellor Wang Dao, Grand Tutor Xie An, Grand General Wen Qiao, Grand Marshal Tao Kan, and Cavalry General Xie Xuan.

entries.zh: 其宣力義熙，豫同艱難者，一仍本秩，無所減降。」
entries.en: Those who exerted strength in the Yixi era and shared hardship are to keep their original ranks without reduction."
entries.literal: Those who exerted strength in the Yixi era and shared hardship are to keep their original ranks without reduction."

entries.zh: 封晉臨川王司馬寶為西豐縣侯，食邑千戶。
entries.en: The Jin Prince of Linchuan, Sima Bao, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng, with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: The Jin Prince of Linchuan, Sima Bao, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng, with a fief of one thousand households."

entries.zh: 辛未，追諡妃臧氏為敬皇后。
entries.en: On the day xinwei, the late consort Lady Zang was posthumously titled Empress Jing.
entries.literal: On the day xinwei, the late consort Lady Zang was posthumously titled Empress Jing.

entries.zh: 癸酉，立王太子為皇太子。
entries.en: On the day guiyou, the domain heir apparent was established as Crown Prince.
entries.literal: On the day guiyou, the Wang heir apparent was established as Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「朕承曆受終，猥饗天命。
entries.en: On the day yihai, an edict stated: "I inherit the mandate and receive the succession, unworthily enjoying Heaven's mandate.
entries.literal: On the day yihai, an edict stated: "I inherit the mandate and receive the end, unworthily enjoying Heaven's mandate.

entries.zh: 荷積善之祚，藉士民之力，七廟備文，率由令範。
entries.en: Bearing the fortune of accumulated goodness and relying on scholars and people's strength, the seven temples' texts are complete and all follow the present norm.
entries.literal: Bearing the fortune of accumulated goodness and relying on scholars and people's strength, the seven temples' texts are complete and all follow the present norm.

entries.zh: 先后祗嚴，獲遂宣訓，蒸嘗肇建，[6]情敬無違。
entries.en: The former and later spirits were reverently honored; instruction was duly proclaimed; seasonal offerings were newly established, [6] with affection and respect unbroken.
entries.literal: The former and later spirits were reverently honored; instruction was duly proclaimed; seasonal offerings were newly established, [6] affection and respect without violation.

entries.zh: 加以儲宮備禮，皇基彌固，國慶家禮，爰集旬日，豈予一人，獨荷茲慶。
entries.en: Moreover the heir's palace rites are complete and the imperial foundation is firmer; state celebration and family rites gather within ten days—how could I alone bear this celebration?
entries.literal: Moreover the heir's palace rites are complete and the imperial foundation is firmer; state celebration and family rites gather within ten days—how could I alone bear this celebration?

entries.zh: 其見刑罪無輕重，可悉原赦。
entries.en: Those now under punishment, without regard to severity, may all be pardoned.
entries.literal: Those now under punishment, without regard to severity, may all be pardoned.

entries.zh: 限百日，以今為始。
entries.en: The limit is one hundred days, beginning from today.
entries.literal: The limit is one hundred days, beginning from today.

entries.zh: 先因軍事所發奴僮，各還本主；
entries.en: Bondservants previously levied for military affairs are each returned to their original masters;
entries.literal: Bondservants previously levied for military affairs are each returned to their original masters;

entries.zh: 若死亡及勳勞破免，亦依限還直。」
entries.en: if they died or merit and labor broke the levy, compensation is also returned according to the limit."
entries.literal: if they died or merit and labor broke the levy, compensation is also returned according to the limit."

entries.zh: 庚午，以司空道憐為太尉，封長沙王。
entries.en: On the day gengwu, the Minister of Works Dao Lin was appointed Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.
entries.literal: On the day gengwu, the Minister of Works Dao Lin was made Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.

entries.zh: 追封司徒道規為臨川王。
entries.en: The late Minister over the Masses Dao Gui was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.
entries.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed the late Minister of Works Dao Gui as Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 尚書僕射徐羨之加鎮軍將軍，右衞將軍謝晦為中領軍，宋國領軍檀道濟為護軍將軍，中領軍劉義欣為青州刺史。
entries.en: Secretariat Director Xu Xianzhi was additionally appointed General Who Stabilizes the Army; Right Guards General Xie Hui was made Central Army Commander; Song Domain Commander-in-Chief Tan Daoji was made Protector General; Central Army Commander Liu Yixin was made Governor of Qing Province.
entries.literal: Secretariat Director Xu Xianzhi was additionally made General Who Stabilizes the Army; Right Guards General Xie Hui was made Central Army Commander; Song Domain Commander-in-Chief Tan Daoji was made Protector General; Central Army Commander Liu Yixin was made Governor of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 立南郡公義慶為臨川王。
entries.en: The Duke of Nan Commandery, Yiqing, was established as Prince of Linchuan.
entries.literal: The Duke of Nan Commandery, Yiqing, was established as Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「夫銘功紀勞，有國之要典，慎終追舊，在心之所隆。
entries.en: Another edict stated: "Inscribing merit and recording labor is a vital canon of the state; honoring the dead and remembering the past is what the heart holds sacred.
entries.literal: Another edict stated: "Inscribing merit and recording labor is an important canon of the state; careful conclusion and pursuing the past is what the heart exalts.

entries.zh: 自大業創基，十有七載，世路迍邅，戎車歲動，自東徂西，靡有寧日。
entries.en: From the founding of the great enterprise for seventeen years, the world's road was obstructed and war chariots moved every year; from east to west there was scarcely a day of peace.
entries.literal: From the founding of the great enterprise for seventeen years, the world's road was obstructed and war chariots moved every year; from east to west there was no day of peace.

entries.zh: 實賴將帥竭心，文武盡効，寧內拓外，迄用有成。
entries.en: Truly relying on generals who gave their all and civil and military officials who exerted every effort, they pacified within and expanded without until success was achieved.
entries.literal: Truly relying on generals exhausting their hearts and civil and military officials exerting all effort, pacifying within and expanding without, they were used and achieved success.

entries.zh: 威靈遠著，寇逆消蕩，遂當揖讓之禮，猥饗天人之祚。
