entries.en: Prestige and spirit were displayed afar, bandits and rebels were swept away, and so at last came the ceremony of abdication; I unworthily received Heaven and the people's mandate.
entries.literal: Prestige and spirit were displayed afar, bandits and rebels were dissolved and swept away, and so at last came the ceremony of abdication; I unworthily received Heaven and man's fortune.

entries.zh: 念功簡勞，無忘鑒寐，凡厥誠勤，宜同國慶。
entries.en: Thinking of merit and honoring labor, do not forget them waking or sleeping; all who were sincere and diligent should share the state's celebration.
entries.literal: Thinking of merit and selecting labor, do not forget them waking or sleeping; all who were sincere and diligent should share the state's celebration.

entries.zh: 其酬賞復除之科，以時論舉。
entries.en: The categories of reward, compensation, and exemption should be discussed and raised in due time.
entries.literal: The categories of reward, compensation, and exemption should be discussed and raised in due time.

entries.zh: 戰亡之身，厚加復贈。」
entries.en: Those who died in battle should receive generous posthumous compensation."
entries.literal: Those who died in battle should receive generous posthumous compensation."

entries.zh: 乙亥，立桂陽公義真為廬陵王，彭城公義隆為宜都王，第四皇子義康為彭城王。
entries.en: On the day yihai, the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen, was established as Prince of Luling; the Duke of Pengcheng, Yilong, as Prince of Yidu; the fourth prince, Yikang, as Prince of Pengcheng.
entries.literal: On the day yihai, the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen, was established as Prince of Luling; the Duke of Pengcheng, Yilong, as Prince of Yidu; the fourth prince, Yikang, as Prince of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 上清簡寡欲，嚴整有法度，未嘗視珠玉輿馬之飾，後庭無紈綺絲竹之音。
entries.en: The emperor was pure and simple, with few desires, strict and orderly with laws and standards; he never looked at ornaments of pearls, jade, chariots, or horses, and the rear palace had no sound of silk damask or bamboo pipes.
entries.literal: The Emperor was pure and simple, with few desires, strict and orderly with laws and standards; he never looked at ornaments of pearls, jade, chariots, or horses, and the rear palace had no sound of silk damask or bamboo pipes.

entries.zh: 寧州嘗獻虎魄枕，光色甚麗。
entries.en: Ning Province once presented an amber pillow; its light and color were very beautiful.
entries.literal: Ning Province once presented an amber pillow; its light and color were very beautiful.

entries.zh: 時將北征，以虎魄治金創，上大悅，命擣碎分付諸將。
entries.en: At the time he was about to campaign north and used amber to treat metal wounds; the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it pounded and divided among the generals.
entries.literal: At the time he was about to campaign north and used amber to treat metal wounds; the Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it pounded and divided among the generals.

entries.zh: 平關中，得姚興從女，有盛寵，以之廢事。
entries.en: When Guanzhong was pacified, he obtained Yao Xing's niece by marriage; she received great favor and he neglected affairs because of her.
entries.literal: When Guanzhong was pacified, he obtained Yao Xing's niece by marriage; she received great favor and he neglected affairs because of her.

entries.zh: 謝晦諫，即時遣出。
entries.en: Xie Hui remonstrated, and he immediately sent her out.
entries.literal: Xie Hui remonstrated, and he immediately sent her out.

entries.zh: 財帛皆在外府，內無私藏。
entries.en: Wealth and silks were all in the outer treasury; within there was no private store.
entries.literal: Wealth and silks were all in the outer treasury; within there was no private store.

entries.zh: 宋臺既建，有司奏東西堂施局脚牀、銀塗釘，上不許；
entries.en: When the Song terrace was first established, the responsible officials memorialized that the eastern and western halls use cabriole-legged couches and silver-coated nails; the emperor did not permit it;
entries.literal: When the Song terrace was first established, the responsible officials memorialized that the eastern and western halls use cabriole-legged couches and silver-coated nails; the Emperor did not permit it;

entries.zh: 使用直脚牀，釘用鐵。
entries.en: straight-legged couches were used, and nails were of iron.
entries.literal: straight-legged couches were used, and nails were of iron.

entries.zh: 諸主出適，遣送不過二十萬，無錦繡金玉。
entries.en: When princesses married out, the send-off did not exceed two hundred thousand cash, and there were no brocades, embroideries, gold, or jade.
entries.literal: When princesses went out in marriage, the send-off did not exceed two hundred thousand, and there were no brocades, embroideries, gold, or jade.

entries.zh: 內外奉禁，莫不節儉。
entries.en: Within and without the palace, all observed the prohibition; everyone lived frugally.
entries.literal: Within and without, all observed the prohibition; none were not frugal.

entries.zh: 性尤簡易，常著連齒木屐，好出神虎門逍遙，左右從者不過十餘人。
entries.en: His nature was especially plain and unpretentious; he often wore wooden clogs with linked teeth, liked to stroll out the Spirit Tiger Gate, and those who followed him numbered no more than a dozen or so.
entries.literal: His nature was especially plain and easy; he often wore wooden clogs with linked teeth, liked to go out the Spirit Tiger Gate for leisurely roaming, and attendants following him did not exceed a dozen or so.

entries.zh: 時徐羨之住西州，嘗幸羨之，便步出西掖門，羽儀絡驛追隨，巳出西明門矣。
entries.en: At the time Xu Xianzhi lived in West Province; once when he visited Xianzhi, he simply walked out the Western Side Gate on foot; the guard of honor pursued in relays and had already passed the Western Bright Gate before catching up.
entries.literal: At the time Xu Xianzhi lived in West Province; once when he visited Xianzhi, he simply walked out the Western Side Gate; the guard of honor pursued in continuous relays and had already passed the Western Bright Gate.

entries.zh: 諸子旦問起居，入閤脫公服，止著裙帽，如家人之禮。
entries.en: When his sons came in the morning to inquire after his health, entering the inner apartments they removed their official robes and wore only skirts and caps, observing the manners of an ordinary family.
entries.literal: When his sons came in the morning to inquire after his health, entering the inner apartments they removed their official robes and wore only skirts and caps, like the rites of a family.

entries.zh: 孝武大明中，壞上所居陰室，於其處起玉燭殿，與羣臣觀之。
entries.en: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu, the dark chamber where the late emperor had lived was demolished, and on that site the Jade Candle Hall was raised; he viewed it with his ministers.
entries.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu, the dark chamber where the late Emperor had lived was demolished, and on that site the Jade Candle Hall was raised; he viewed it with the hundred officials.

entries.zh: 牀頭有土鄣，壁上挂葛燈籠、麻繩拂。
entries.en: At the head of the bed stood an earthen barrier; on the wall hung a kudzu lamp shade and a hemp-rope duster.
entries.literal: At the head of the bed there was an earthen barrier; on the wall was hung a kudzu lamp shade and a hemp-rope duster.

entries.zh: 侍中袁顗盛稱上儉素之德。
entries.en: Palace Attendant Yuan Yi greatly praised the late emperor's virtue of frugality and plainness.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Yi greatly praised the late Emperor's virtue of frugality and plainness.

entries.zh: 孝武不答，獨曰：「田舍公得此，以為過矣。」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu did not reply, but only said: "That rustic fellow got this far and thought it excessive."
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu did not reply, but only said: "That rustic fellow got this far and thought it excessive."

entries.zh: 故能光有天下，克成大業者焉。
entries.en: Thus he was able to spread his light over all under Heaven and achieve the great enterprise.
entries.literal: Thus he was able to spread his light over all under Heaven and achieve the great enterprise.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛卯，改晉所用王肅祥禫二十六月儀，依鄭玄二十七月而後除。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on the day xinmao, the Jin practice using Wang Su's auspicious mourning rite of twenty-six months was changed; following Zheng Xuan's twenty-seven months, mourning garments were then put aside.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day xinmao, the Jin practice using Wang Su's auspicious mourning rite of twenty-six months was changed; following Zheng Xuan's twenty-seven months, removal of mourning followed thereafter.

entries.zh: 九月己丑，零陵王薨。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, the Prince of Lingling died.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, the Prince of Lingling died.

entries.zh: 車駕三朝率百僚舉哀于朝堂，一依魏明帝服山陽公故事。
entries.en: For three days the emperor led all officials in mourning at the court hall, following entirely the precedent of Emperor Ming of Wei mourning the Duke of Shanyang.
entries.literal: For three days the emperor led all officials in mourning at the court hall, following entirely the precedent of Emperor Ming of Wei mourning the Duke of Shanyang.

entries.zh: 太尉持節監護，葬以晉禮。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant held imperial credentials to oversee the funeral, and burial followed Jin rites.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant held imperial credentials to oversee the funeral, and burial followed Jin rites.

entries.zh: 少帝諱義符，小字車兵，武帝長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Shao, taboo name Yifu, childhood name Chebing, was Emperor Wu's eldest son.
entries.literal: Emperor Shao's taboo name was Yifu; his childhood name was Chebing. He was the eldest son of Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 母曰張夫人。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Zhang.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Zhang.

entries.zh: 晉義熙二年，生於京口。
entries.en: He was born at Jingkou in the second year of Yixi of Jin.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yixi of Jin, he was born at Jingkou.

entries.zh: 武帝晚無男，及帝生，甚悅。
entries.en: Emperor Wu had long been without a son; when the emperor was born, he was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu had long been without a son; when the emperor was born, he was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 年十歲，拜豫章公世子。
entries.en: At age ten, he was invested as heir of the Duke of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: At age ten, he was invested as heir of the Duke of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 帝有旅力，善騎射，解音律。
entries.en: The emperor was strong and vigorous, excelled at horseback archery, and understood musical theory.
entries.literal: The emperor had strength and vigor, excelled at horseback archery, and understood musical theory.

entries.zh: 宋臺建，拜宋世子。
entries.en: When the Song regime was established, he was invested as Song heir.
entries.literal: When the Song regime was established, he was invested as Song heir.

entries.zh: 元熙元年，進為宋太子。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanxi, he was advanced to Song crown prince.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi, he was advanced to Song crown prince.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，立為皇太子。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 永初三年五月癸亥，武帝崩，是日，太子即皇帝位。
entries.en: On the guihai day of the fifth month of the third year of Yongchu, Emperor Wu died; that same day the crown prince ascended the throne.
entries.literal: On the guihai day of the fifth month of the third year of Yongchu, Emperor Wu died; on that same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 大赦。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后。
entries.en: The empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager.
entries.literal: The empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager.

entries.zh: 王室不造，天禍未悔，先帝創業弗永，棄世登遐。
entries.en: The royal house has suffered misfortune; Heaven's wrath has not yet lifted; the late emperor's founding work was cut short when he died and passed beyond.
entries.literal: The royal house has met with misfortune, Heaven's calamity has not yet relented, the late emperor's founding work did not last long, and he departed the world and ascended afar.

entries.zh: 義符長嗣，屬當天位，不謂窮凶極悖，一至於此。
entries.en: Yifu, as the eldest son, was meant to inherit the throne under Heaven; none could have foreseen that his vicious depravity would go so far.
entries.literal: Yifu, as the eldest son and heir, was entrusted with the position under Heaven, yet who would have thought his utter villainy and extreme depravity would reach this point.

entries.zh: 大行在殯，宇內哀惶，幸災肆於悖詞，喜容表於在慼。
entries.en: While the late emperor still lay in state and the realm mourned, he delighted in others' misfortune and spoke rebelliously, wearing a cheerful countenance even amid mourning.
entries.literal: While the late emperor lay in coffin, the realm mourned in grief, yet he took others' disaster as his pleasure and poured forth rebellious words, and showed joy upon his face even in the period of mourning.

entries.zh: 至乃徵召樂府，鳩集伶官，優倡管絃，靡不備奏，珍羞甘膳，有加平日。
entries.en: He even summoned the Music Bureau, gathered performers, and had singers, musicians, and string players perform without exception; delicacies and fine foods exceeded those of ordinary days.
entries.literal: He even summoned the Music Bureau, gathered actors, and had singers, musicians, and string players all perform without exception; rare delicacies and fine foods exceeded those of ordinary days.

entries.zh: 採擇媵御，產子就宮，靦然無怍，醜聲四達。
entries.en: He selected concubines, and when they bore children he brought them into the palace without the least shame; scandal spread in every direction.
entries.literal: He selected concubines, and when they bore children he brought them into the palace with perfect composure and no shame; foul reports spread in every direction.

entries.zh: 及懿后崩背，重加天罰，親與左右執紼歌呼，推排梓宮，抃掌笑謔，殿省備聞。
entries.en: When Empress Yi died, Heaven again punished him: he personally joined his attendants in grasping the mourning cords and singing aloud, pushed the inner coffin about, and clapped his hands in laughter and jest—the palace offices all heard of it.
entries.literal: When Empress Yi died, Heaven added a further punishment: he personally joined his attendants in grasping the mourning cords and singing aloud, pushed the inner coffin about, clapped his hands and laughed and jested—the palace offices all heard of it.

entries.zh: 加復日夜媟狎，羣小慢戲，興造千計，費用萬端，帑藏空虛，人力殫盡。
entries.en: Moreover, day and night he indulged in lewd sport; his petty followers treated him with disrespect; he launched a thousand projects and spent ten thousand sums; the treasury was emptied and manpower exhausted.
entries.literal: Moreover, day and night he indulged in lewd sport; his petty followers treated him with disrespect; he launched a thousand projects and spent ten thousand sums; the treasury was emptied and manpower exhausted.

entries.zh: 刑罰苛虐，幽囚日增。
entries.en: Punishments were harsh and cruel, and those imprisoned increased daily.
entries.literal: Punishments were harsh and cruel, and those imprisoned increased daily.

entries.zh: 居帝王之位，好皁隸之役，處萬乘之尊，悅廝養之事。
entries.en: Though he occupied the throne, he delighted in the tasks of menial servants; though he possessed imperial dignity, he took pleasure in groom and stable work.
entries.literal: Though he occupied the position of an emperor, he delighted in the tasks of black-clad servants; though he possessed the honor of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler, he took pleasure in groom and stable work.

entries.zh: 親執鞭撲，毆擊無辜，以為笑樂。
entries.en: He personally wielded the whip and flail, beat the innocent, and made this his amusement.
entries.literal: He personally wielded the whip and flail, beat the innocent, and made this his amusement.

entries.zh: 穿池築觀，朝成暮毀，徵發工匠，疲極兆民。
entries.en: He dug ponds and built towers, completing them in the morning and destroying them in the evening; he conscripted craftsmen until the people were exhausted to the utmost.
entries.literal: He dug ponds and built towers, completing them in the morning and destroying them in the evening; he conscripted craftsmen until the people were exhausted to the utmost.

entries.zh: 遠近歎嗟，人神怨怒，社稷將墜，豈可復嗣守洪業，君臨萬邦。
entries.en: Near and far sighed in lament; men and spirits were angered; the altars of soil and grain were about to fall—how could he again inherit and guard the great enterprise and rule the myriad states.
entries.literal: Near and far sighed in lament; men and spirits were angered; the altars of soil and grain were about to fall—how could he again inherit and guard the great enterprise and rule the myriad states.

entries.zh: 今廢為營陽王，一依漢昌邑、晉海西故事。
entries.en: He is now deposed as Prince of Yingyang, following entirely the precedents of the Han Prince of Changyi and the Jin Emperor Haixi.
entries.literal: He is now deposed as Prince of Yingyang, following entirely the precedents of the Han Prince of Changyi and the Jin Emperor Haixi.

entries.zh: 始徐羨之、傅亮將廢帝，諷王弘、檀道濟求赴國訃。
entries.en: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor; they hinted to Wang Hong and Tan Daoji that they should come for the state mourning.
entries.literal: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor; they hinted to Wang Hong and Tan Daoji that they should come for the state mourning.

entries.zh: 弘等來朝。
entries.en: Hong and the others came to court.
entries.literal: Hong and the others came to court.

entries.zh: 使中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為內應。
entries.en: They made the Attendant of the Masters of Writing Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their inside contacts.
entries.literal: They made the Attendant of the Masters of Writing Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their inside contacts.

entries.zh: 是旦，道濟、謝晦領兵居前，羨之等隨後，因東掖門開，入自雲龍門。
entries.en: That morning, Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front while Xu Xianzhi and the others followed; because the East Side Gate was open, they entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate.
entries.literal: That morning, Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front while Xu Xianzhi and the others followed; because the East Side Gate was open, they entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate.

entries.zh: 盛等先戒宿衞，莫有禦者。
entries.en: Sheng and the others had first warned the night guards, and none resisted.
entries.literal: Sheng and the others had first warned the night guards, and none resisted.

entries.zh: 時帝於華林園為列肆，親自酤賣。
entries.en: At the time the emperor was in the Hualin Garden setting up a row of shops and personally selling wine.
entries.literal: At the time the emperor was in the Hualin Garden setting up a row of shops and personally selling wine.

entries.zh: 又開瀆聚土，以象破岡埭，與左右引船唱呼，以為歡樂。
entries.en: He also opened a canal and piled earth to imitate the Pogang dam, and with his attendants pulled boats while shouting and calling—taking this as his pleasure.
entries.literal: He also opened a canal and piled earth to imitate the Pogang dam, and with his attendants pulled boats while shouting and calling—taking this as his pleasure.

entries.zh: 夕游天淵池，即龍舟而寢。
entries.en: In the evening he toured the Tianyuan Pool and slept on the dragon boat.
entries.literal: In the evening he toured the Tianyuan Pool and slept on the dragon boat.

entries.zh: 其朝未興，兵士進，殺二侍者於帝側，傷帝指。
entries.en: The court had not yet risen when soldiers entered, killed two attendants at the emperor's side, and wounded his finger.
entries.literal: The court had not yet risen when soldiers entered, killed two attendants at the emperor's side, and wounded his finger.

entries.zh: 夫出東閤，就收璽紱，羣臣拜辭，送於東宮，遂幽於吳郡。
entries.en: He was taken out through the East Gate Pavilion, the seals and cords were taken from him, the officials bowed in farewell, he was sent to the Eastern Palace, and then confined in Wu Commandery.
entries.literal: He was taken out through the East Gate Pavilion, the seals and cords were taken from him, the officials bowed in farewell, he was sent to the Eastern Palace, and then confined in Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 是日，赦死罪以下。
entries.en: That day, those sentenced to death and below were pardoned.
entries.literal: That day, those sentenced to death and below were pardoned.

entries.zh: 太后令奉還璽紱。
entries.en: The empress dowager ordered that the seals and cords be returned.
entries.literal: The empress dowager ordered that the seals and cords be returned.

entries.zh: 檀道濟入守朝堂。
entries.en: Tan Daoji entered to guard the court hall.
entries.literal: Tan Daoji entered to guard the court hall.

entries.zh: 六月癸丑，徐羨之等使中書舍人邢安泰弒帝於金昌亭。
entries.en: On the guichou day of the sixth month, Xu Xianzhi and the others had the Attendant of the Masters of Writing Xing Antai assassinate the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.
entries.literal: On the guichou day of the sixth month, Xu Xianzhi and the others had the Attendant of the Masters of Writing Xing Antai assassinate the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.

entries.zh: 帝有勇力，不即受制，突走出昌門，追以門關踣之，致殞。
entries.en: The emperor was strong and courageous and did not submit at once; he burst out through Chang Gate, and pursuers struck him down with the gate bar, killing him.
entries.literal: The emperor had strength and courage and did not submit at once; he burst out through Chang Gate, and pursuers struck him down with the gate bar, causing his death.

entries.zh: 時年十九。
entries.en: He was nineteen years old.
entries.literal: He was nineteen years old.

entries.en: [17] Editorial note seventeen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
entries.literal: [17] Editorial note seventeen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

entries.zh: 夏五月，江州刺史王弘、南兗州刺史檀道濟入朝。
entries.en: In summer, the fifth month, Wang Hong, Inspector of Jiangzhou, and Tan Daoji, Inspector of South Yanzhou, came to court.
entries.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Wang Hong, Inspector of Jiangzhou, and Tan Daoji, Inspector of South Yanzhou, came to court.

entries.zh: [15]帝居處所為多過失。
entries.en: [15] In his conduct the emperor committed many faults.
entries.literal: [15] In his conduct the emperor committed many faults.

entries.zh: 乙酉，皇太后令曰：
entries.en: On the yiyou day, the empress dowager issued an order, saying:
entries.literal: On the yiyou day, the empress dowager issued an order, saying:

entries.zh: 明年春正月己亥朔，大赦，改元為景平元年。
entries.en: On the new moon of the first month of spring of the following year, on the day jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jingping, year one.
entries.literal: On the new moon of the first month of spring of the following year, the day jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jingping, year one.

entries.zh: 文武進位二等。
entries.en: Civil and military officials were advanced two ranks in status.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.

entries.zh: 辛丑，祀南郊。
entries.en: On the xinchou day, the southern suburban sacrifice was performed.
entries.literal: On the xinchou day, sacrifice was offered at the southern suburb.

entries.zh: [3]虜將達奚卬破金墉，進圍虎牢。
entries.en: [3] The enemy general Daxi Ang took Jinyong and pressed on to besiege Hulao.
entries.literal: [3] The barbarian general Daxi Ang captured Jinyong and advanced to besiege Hulao.

entries.zh: [4]毛德祖擊虜敗之，虜退而復合。
entries.en: [4] Mao Dezu attacked the enemy and routed them; the enemy withdrew and then rallied again.
entries.literal: [4] Mao Dezu struck the barbarians and defeated them; the barbarians withdrew and then regrouped.

entries.zh: 拓跋木末又遣安平公涉歸寇青州。
entries.en: Tuoba Mumo again sent the Prince of Anping, Shegui, to invade Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Tuoba Mumo again sent the Prince of Anping, Shegui, to raid Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 癸卯，河南郡失守。
entries.en: On the guimao day, Henan Commandery fell.
entries.literal: On the guimao day, Henan Commandery was lost.

entries.zh: 乙卯，有星孛于東壁。
entries.en: On the yimao day, a broom star appeared in the Eastern Wall lodge.
entries.literal: On the yimao day, a comet appeared in the Eastern Wall mansion.

entries.zh: 秋九月丁未，有司奏武皇帝配南郊，武敬皇后配北郊。
entries.en: In autumn, on the dingwei day of the ninth month, the relevant offices submitted that Emperor Wu should receive joint sacrifice at the southern suburban altar and Empress Wu Jing at the northern suburban altar.
entries.literal: In autumn, on the dingwei day of the ninth month, the relevant offices memorialized that Emperor Wu should be paired at the southern suburb altar and Empress Wu Jing at the northern suburb altar.

entries.zh: 三月壬寅，孝懿皇后祔葬于興寧陵。
entries.en: On the renyin day of the third month, Empress Xiaoyi was enshrined and buried at Xingning Mausoleum.
entries.literal: On the renyin day of the third month, Empress Xiaoyi was enshrined and buried at Xingning Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 是月，高麗國遣使朝貢。
entries.en: That month, Goguryeo sent envoys to court with tribute.
entries.literal: That month, Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 甲子，豫州刺史劉粹遣軍襲許昌，殺虜潁川太守庾龍。
entries.en: On the jiazi day, Liu Cui, Inspector of Yuzhou, sent troops to raid Xuchang and killed the enemy Administrator of Yingchuan, Yu Long.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, Liu Cui, Inspector of Yuzhou, sent troops to raid Xuchang and killed the barbarian Administrator of Yingchuan, Yu Long.

entries.zh: 乙丑，虜騎寇高平。
entries.en: On the yichou day, enemy horsemen raided Gaoping.
entries.literal: On the yichou day, barbarian horsemen raided Gaoping.

entries.zh: 初虜自河北之敗，請修和親；
entries.en: Earlier, after their defeat north of the Yellow River, the enemy had sought a marriage alliance;
entries.literal: Earlier, after their defeat north of the Yellow River, the barbarians had requested a marriage alliance;

entries.zh: 及聞高祖崩，因復侵擾，河、洛之地騷然矣。
entries.en: when they learned that Emperor Gaozu had died, they resumed their incursions, and the Yellow and Luo region was thrown into turmoil.
entries.literal: when they heard that Emperor Gaozu had died, they again launched raids, and the lands along the Yellow and Luo rivers were thrown into turmoil.

entries.zh: 司徒領護軍八座：子業雖曰嫡長，少稟凶毒，不仁不孝，著自髫齔。
entries.en: To the Minister over the Masses, the concurrent General Who Protects the Army, and the Eight Dignitaries: Though Ziye was the eldest son of the proper wife, from childhood he showed a vicious and poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety was evident even in his earliest years.
entries.literal: To the Minister over the Masses, the concurrent General Who Protects the Army, and the Eight Dignitaries: Though Ziye was called the eldest son of the proper wife, from youth he received a vicious and poisonous nature; his lack of benevolence and filial piety were evident from his childhood locks.

entries.zh: 孝武棄世，屬當辰曆。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiao Wu died, the throne passed to him by right of succession.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiao Wu passed from the world, the throne fell to him by the calendar.

entries.zh: 自梓宮在殯，喜容靦然，天罰重離，歡恣滋甚。
entries.en: From the moment the imperial coffin lay in state, his face was bright and untroubled; though Heaven's punishment had struck the imperial house, his wanton joy only grew.
entries.literal: From the time the imperial coffin lay in temporary lodging, his countenance was bright and calm; Heaven's punishment struck the li trigram, yet his wanton joy grew ever greater.

entries.zh: 逼以內外維持，忍虐未露，而凶慘難抑，一旦肆禍，遂縱戮上宰，殄害輔臣。
entries.en: Forced by court and family to restrain himself, he had not yet shown his full cruelty; but his savage brutality could not be held back, and in a single day he unleashed catastrophe, slaughtering the chief ministers and destroying his own supporters.
entries.literal: Forced by inner and outer constraints to hold himself in check, his cruel and violent nature was not yet exposed; yet his savage brutality could not be restrained, and in a single day he unleashed disaster, wantonly slaughtering the chief ministers and annihilating his supporting officials.

entries.zh: 子鸞兄弟，先帝鍾愛，含怨既往，枉加屠酷。
entries.en: Ziluan and his brothers had been the late emperor's favorites; nursing old resentments, he had them savagely executed without cause.
entries.literal: Ziluan and his brothers had been beloved of the late emperor; nursing old resentments, he wrongly subjected them to savage execution.

entries.zh: 昶茂親作扞，橫相徵討。
entries.en: Chang, a close kinsman who should have been a bulwark of the throne, was attacked and punished without cause.
entries.literal: Chang, a close kinsman, served as a bulwark, yet was wantonly attacked and punished.

entries.zh: 新蔡公主逼離夫族，幽置深宮，詭云薨殞。
entries.en: Princess Xincai was torn from her husband's family and shut away in the inner palace, while a false report announced her death.
entries.literal: Princess Xincai was torn from her husband's clan and shut away in the deep palace; it was falsely announced that she had died.

entries.zh: 襄事甫爾，喪禮頓釋，昏酣長夜，庶事傾遺。
entries.en: Mourning had barely begun when its rites were cast aside; through long nights of drunkenness every affair of state was neglected.
entries.literal: The mourning rites had barely begun when they were abruptly set aside; through long drunken nights every affair of state was abandoned.

entries.zh: 朝賢舊勳，棄若遺土。
entries.en: Court worthies and old ministers he cast aside like rubbish.
entries.literal: Court worthies and old ministers he cast off like discarded earth.

entries.zh: 管絃不輟，珍羞備膳。
entries.en: Music never ceased; rare delicacies filled every table.
entries.literal: Pipes and strings never ceased; rare delicacies filled every board.

entries.zh: 詈辱祖考，以為戲謔。
entries.en: He reviled his ancestors and forebears for sport.
entries.literal: He reviled and insulted his ancestors and forebears, making them the butt of his sport.

entries.zh: 行游莫止，淫縱無度。
entries.en: His wanderings knew no limit; his lewdness and excess knew no bounds.
entries.literal: His travels knew no stopping; his lewdness and excess had no measure.

entries.zh: 肆宴園陵，規圖發掘。
entries.en: He feasted in the imperial tombs and plotted to open the graves.
entries.literal: He held feasts in the imperial tombs and plotted to open the graves.

entries.zh: 誅剪無辜，籍略婦女。
entries.en: He slaughtered the innocent and seized women by force.
entries.literal: He executed and cut down the innocent and seized women by force.

entries.zh: 建樹偽豎，莫知誰息。
entries.en: He raised up false charges, and no one knew who would be struck down next.
entries.literal: He raised false pillars, and no one knew whose turn would come next.

entries.zh: 拜嬪立后，慶過恒典。
entries.en: In taking concubines and installing an empress, his celebrations exceeded all precedent.
entries.literal: In appointing concubines and installing an empress, his celebrations exceeded the constant statutes.

entries.zh: 宗室密戚，遇若婢僕，鞭捶陵曳，無復尊卑。
entries.en: Imperial kinsmen and close relatives he treated like servants, beating and dragging them with no regard for rank.
entries.literal: Kinsmen of the imperial clan and close relatives he treated like maidservants and slaves, beating and dragging them with no regard for rank.

entries.zh: 南平一門，特鍾其酷。
entries.en: The house of Nanping alone he singled out for especial cruelty.
entries.literal: The house of Nanping alone he singled out for especial cruelty.

entries.zh: 反天滅理，顯暴萬端。
entries.en: He turned against Heaven and extinguished moral principle; his open violence took ten thousand forms.
entries.literal: He turned against Heaven and extinguished principle; his open violence had ten thousand faces.

entries.zh: 苛罰酷令，終無紀極，夏桀、殷辛，未足以譬。
entries.en: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; even Jie of Xia and Xin of Yin would not suffice for comparison.
entries.literal: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; Xia Jie and Yin Xin would not suffice for comparison.

entries.zh: 闔朝業業，人不自保，百姓遑遑，手足靡厝。
entries.en: Throughout the court everyone lived in dread and no one was safe; the people were in turmoil and did not know where to turn.
entries.literal: Throughout the court everyone was in dread and no one could protect himself; the common people were in turmoil and did not know where to set hand or foot.

entries.zh: 行穢禽獸，罪盈三千。
entries.en: His conduct was more beastly than a beast's; his crimes were beyond numbering.
entries.literal: His conduct was filthier than a beast's; his crimes filled three thousand.

entries.zh: 高祖之業將泯，七廟之享幾絕。
entries.en: The founding emperor's enterprise was on the verge of ruin; the offerings at the seven temples were nearly cut off.
entries.literal: The enterprise of the High Ancestor was on the verge of perishing; the offerings to the seven temples were nearly cut off.

entries.zh: 吾老疾沈篤，每規禍鴆，憂煎漏刻，氣命無幾。
entries.en: I am old and gravely ill; each day I foresee the poisoned cup; anxiety consumes me with every drip of the water clock, and my life will not long endure.
entries.literal: I am old and my illness deep and grave; each day I foresee the poisoned cup; my anxious torment drips with the clepsydra, and my breath and life will not long endure.

entries.zh: 開闢以降，所未嘗聞。
entries.en: Since the opening of the age, nothing like this has ever been heard of.
entries.literal: Since the opening of the age, such a thing has never been heard of.

entries.zh: 遠近思奮，十室而九。
entries.en: Near and far alike yearn to rise against him; nine houses in ten.
entries.literal: Near and far alike yearn to rise up; nine houses in ten.

entries.zh: 衞將軍湘東王體自太祖，天縱英聖，文皇鍾愛，寵冠列藩。
entries.en: General of the Guard Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, is descended from the dynastic founder; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity, and Emperor Wen cherished him above all other princes.
entries.literal: General of the Guard Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, is descended from the Great Ancestor; Heaven endowed him with heroic sagacity, and Emperor Wen cherished him—his favor surpassed all the other princes.

entries.zh: 吾早識神睿，特兼常禮。
entries.en: I recognized his keen intelligence early and treated him with especial honor.
entries.literal: I recognized his divine keenness early and treated him with especial courtesy.

entries.zh: 潛運宏規，義士投袂，獨夫既殞，懸首白旗，社稷再興，宗祏永固，人鬼屬心，大命允集。
entries.en: He carried out his great design in secret; men of righteousness rallied to him; the tyrant has fallen, his severed head on the white banner; the altars of state are renewed and the ancestral temple secured; the hearts of men and spirits alike turn to him, and the great mandate is duly his.
entries.literal: He secretly carried out a great design; men of righteousness rallied to him; the tyrant alone has now fallen, his severed head on the white banner; the altars of state are renewed, the ancestral temple secured forever; the hearts of men and ghosts alike turn to him, and the great mandate is duly gathered.

entries.zh: 且勳德高邈，大業攸歸，宜遵漢、晉，纂承皇極。
entries.en: His merit and virtue are lofty; the great enterprise is his to receive; let him follow the precedents of Han and Jin in ascending the throne.
entries.literal: Moreover his merit and virtue are lofty and far-reaching; the great enterprise is his to receive; he should follow Han and Jin in ascending the imperial apex.

entries.zh: 主者詳舊典以時奉行。
entries.en: Those in charge should examine the old statutes and carry them out without delay.
entries.literal: Those in charge should examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：廢帝之事行著于篇。
entries.en: The historian remarks: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.
entries.literal: The historian remarks: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.

entries.zh: 若夫武王數殷紂之釁，不能絓其萬一；
entries.en: When King Wu of Zhou counted the crimes of King Zhou of Yin, he could not exhaust one part in ten thousand;
entries.literal: When King Wu of Zhou counted the crimes of Zhou of Yin, he could not exhaust one part in ten thousand;

entries.zh: 霍光書昌邑之過，未足舉其毫釐。
entries.en: when Huo Guang set down the faults of the Marquis of Haihun, he could not list one hair's breadth in a thousand.
entries.literal: when Huo Guang wrote out the faults of the Marquis of Haihun, he could not list one hair's breadth in a thousand.

entries.zh: 假以中才之君，有一于此，足以霣社殘宗，汚宮瀦廟，況總斯惡以萃一人之體乎！
entries.en: An emperor of only middling talent who committed one such fault would suffice to destroy the altars of state and defile the ancestral shrines; how much more when all these evils were gathered in a single body!
entries.literal: Suppose an emperor of only middling talent had one of these faults— that alone would suffice to destroy the altars of state, ruin the ancestral temple, and defile the palace and shrine; how much more when all these evils are gathered in a single person's body!

entries.zh: 其得亡亦為幸矣。
entries.en: That he perished when he did was itself a mercy.
entries.literal: That he perished when he did was itself a mercy.

entries.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Fei I was named Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was Emperor Xiao Wu's eldest son.
entries.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was the eldest son of Emperor Xiao Wu.

entries.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。
entries.en: He was born on jiashen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.
entries.literal: He was born on jiashen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

entries.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，子業留京邑。
entries.en: While the future Emperor Xiao Wu held Xunyang, Ziye stayed behind in the capital.
entries.literal: When Shizu garrisoned Xunyang, Ziye remained in the capital.

entries.zh: 三十年，世祖入伐元凶，被囚侍中下省，將見害者數矣，卒得無恙。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year, when the emperor marched in to punish the assassin prince, Ziye was held prisoner in the attendants' sub-bureau; more than once he was nearly executed, yet in the end escaped unharmed.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu entered the capital to attack the prime culprit, he was imprisoned in the lower office of the Palace Attendants; he was several times on the point of being killed, yet in the end came to no harm.

entries.zh: 昇明元年，改元，大赦天下，賜文武位二等。
entries.en: In the first year of Shengming the era name was changed, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and civil and military officials were advanced two ranks in status.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shengming the era name was changed, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm, and civil and military officials were granted two ranks in status.

entries.zh: 甲午，鎮軍將軍齊王出鎮東城，輔政作相。
entries.en: On the jiawu day the Prince of Qi, General Who Pacifies the Army, went out to garrison the Eastern Fortress and took up regency as chancellor.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day the Prince of Qi, General Who Pacifies the Army, went out to garrison the Eastern Fortress and served as regent and chancellor.

entries.zh: 丙申，詔曰：「露臺息構，義光漢德；
entries.en: On the bingshen day an edict said: "Ceasing construction on the Terrace of Dew shed light on Han virtue;
entries.literal: On the bingshen day an edict said: "Ceasing construction on the Terrace of Dew shed light on Han virtue;

entries.zh: 雉裘焚制，事隆晉道。
entries.en: burning the pheasant-fur robe exalted the way of Jin.
entries.literal: burning the pheasant-fur robe exalted the way of Jin.

entries.zh: 故以檢奢軌化，敦儉馭俗。
entries.en: Thus extravagance is checked to transform customs, and thrift is honored to govern the people.
entries.literal: Thus extravagance is checked to transform customs, and thrift is honored to govern the people.

entries.zh: 頃甸服未靜，師旅連年，委蓄屢空，勞敝莫偃。
entries.en: Recently the realm has not been at peace; armies have campaigned year after year; granaries stand empty again and again, and exhaustion never lets up.
entries.literal: Recently the imperial domain has not been tranquil; armies have campaigned year after year; stored supplies are repeatedly depleted and toil and exhaustion never ease.

entries.zh: 而丹雘之飾，糜耗難訾，寶賂之費，徵賦靡計。
entries.en: Yet lacquer and cinnabar ornament consume resources beyond measure, and treasure levies cannot be reckoned.
entries.literal: Yet vermilion and cinnabar ornament wastes beyond reckoning, and treasure outlays for tribute levies cannot be calculated.

entries.zh: 今車服儀制，實宜約損，使徽章有序，勿得侈溢。
entries.en: Carriage dress and ritual regalia should now be pared back, so that ranks and insignia stay in order and excess is not permitted.
entries.literal: Now carriage robes and ritual regalia truly ought to be reduced in scale, so that emblems and insignia keep their order and excess not be allowed.

entries.zh: 可罷省御府二署。
entries.en: The two bureaus of the Inner Palace are to be abolished.
entries.literal: The two bureaus of the Inner Palace may be abolished.

entries.zh: 凡工麗彫鑴，傷風毀治，一皆禁斷。
entries.en: Every sort of ornate carving and fine chasing that harms custom and undermines good government is forbidden.
entries.literal: All ingenious carving and fine chasing that harm customs and ruin governance—every one is forbidden.

entries.zh: 庶永昭憲則，弘茲始政。」
entries.en: May the statutes shine forever and this new rule be broadly proclaimed."
entries.literal: Thus may the canonical law shine forever and this inaugural governance be enlarged."

entries.zh: 征西大將軍、荊州刺史沈攸之進號車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，尚書左僕射、中領軍、鎮軍將軍、南兗州刺史齊王為司空、錄尚書事、驃騎大將軍，刺史如故，中書令、衞將軍、開府儀同三司，撫軍將軍劉秉為尚書令，加中軍將軍，[2]安西將軍、郢州刺史晉熙王燮為撫軍將軍、揚州刺史，南陽王翽為郢州刺史。
entries.en: Shen Youzhi, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. The Prince of Qi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Central Army Commander, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was appointed Minister of Works, Recording Secretary, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, remaining Inspector as before. [2] The text is defective here; the collation note restores the missing appointments: Yuan Can became Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister over the Masses, while Chu Yuan became Guards General, and both were authorized to maintain their own offices with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. Liu Bing, General Who Pacifies the Army, became Director of the Masters of Writing and additionally Central Army Commander. Xie, Prince of Jinxi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, became General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou. Prince of Nanyang Hui became Inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Shen Youzhi, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and granted authority to establish an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. The Prince of Qi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Central Army Commander, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was made Minister of Works, Recording Secretary, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, remaining Inspector as before. [2] The text is defective here; the collation note restores that Yuan Can was made Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister over the Masses, while Chu Yuan was made Guards General, and both received authority to establish offices with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. Liu Bing, General Who Pacifies the Army, was made Director of the Masters of Writing and additionally Central Army Commander. Xie, Prince of Jinxi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou. Prince of Nanyang Hui was made Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 辛丑，尚書右僕射王僧虔為尚書僕射，右衞將軍劉韞為中領軍，金紫光祿大夫王琨為右光祿大夫。
entries.en: On the xinchou day Wang Sengqian, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Liu Yun, Right Guards General, was appointed Central Army Commander; Wang Kun, Grandee of Splendid Gold and Purple Guanglu, was appointed Right Grandee of Splendid Service.
entries.literal: On the xinchou day the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Sengqian was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; the Right Guards General Liu Yun was made Central Army Commander; the Grandee of Splendid Gold and Purple Guanglu Wang Kun was made Right Grandee of Splendid Service.

entries.zh: 給司空齊王錢五百萬，布五千匹。
entries.en: Five million cash and five thousand bolts of cloth were granted to the Prince of Qi, Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Five million cash and five thousand bolts of cloth were granted to the Prince of Qi, Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 癸卯，車駕謁太廟。
entries.en: On the guimao day the emperor visited the Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: On the guimao day the imperial carriage visited the Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 丙午，以安西參軍明慶符為青、冀二州刺史，武陵王贊為郢州刺史，新除郢州刺史南陽王翽為湘州刺史，司空、南兗州刺史齊王改領南徐州刺史，征虜將軍李安民為南兗州刺史。
entries.en: On the bingwu day Ming Qingfu, staff officer of Anxi, was appointed Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces; Prince of Wuling Zan was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou; Prince of Nanyang Hui, newly appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, was appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou; the Prince of Qi, Minister of Works and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was reassigned to hold concurrently Inspector of South Xuzhou; Li Anmin, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was appointed Inspector of South Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On the bingwu day the Anxi staff officer Ming Qingfu was made Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces; the Prince of Wuling Zan was made Inspector of Yingzhou; the newly appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, Prince of Nanyang Hui, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; the Prince of Qi, Minister of Works and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was changed to hold concurrently the post of Inspector of South Xuzhou; Li Anmin, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 雍州大水，八月壬子，遣使賑卹，蠲除稅調。
entries.en: Yongzhou suffered severe flooding; in the eighth month, on the renzi day, envoys were dispatched for relief, and taxes and levies were remitted.
entries.literal: Yongzhou suffered great flooding; in the eighth month, on the renzi day, envoys were dispatched for relief, and taxes and levies were remitted.

entries.zh: 以驃騎長史劉澄之為南豫州刺史。
entries.en: Liu Chengzhi, chief clerk of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of South Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Chengzhi, chief clerk of Agile Cavalry, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 山陽太守于天寶、新吳縣子秦立有罪，下獄死。
entries.en: Yu Tianbao, Governor of Shanyang, and Qin Li, Viscount of Xinwu County, were found guilty, imprisoned, and died.
entries.literal: Yu Tianbao, Governor of Shanyang, and Qin Li, Viscount of Xinwu County, were guilty; imprisoned, they died.

entries.zh: 戊午，改平準署。
entries.en: On the wuwu day the Bureau of Equitable Standards was reorganized.
entries.literal: On the wuwu day the Bureau of Equitable Standards was reorganized.

entries.zh: 辛酉，以宣城太守李靈謙為兗州刺史。
entries.en: On the xinyou day Li Lingqian, Governor of Xuancheng, was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day Li Lingqian, Governor of Xuancheng, was made Inspector of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 癸亥，司徒袁粲鎮石頭。
entries.en: On the guihai day Minister over the Masses Yuan Can garrisoned Stone City.
entries.literal: On the guihai day Minister over the Masses Yuan Can garrisoned Stone City.

entries.zh: 丁卯，原除元年以前逋調；
entries.en: On the dingmao day arrears in levies before the first year of the era were wholly remitted;
entries.literal: On the dingmao day arrears in levies before the first year of the era were wholly remitted;

entries.zh: 復郡縣祿田。
entries.en: Salary fields for commanderies and counties were restored.
entries.literal: Salary fields for commanderies and counties were restored.

entries.zh: 戊辰，崇拜帝所生陳昭華為皇太妃。
entries.en: On the wuchen day the emperor's birth mother, Consort Chen of the Zhaohua rank, was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.
entries.literal: On the wuchen day the emperor's birth mother, Lady Chen, who held the consort rank Zhaohua, was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.

entries.zh: 庚午，司空長史謝朏、衞軍長史江斅、中書侍郎褚炫、武陵王文學劉候入直殿省，參侍文義。
entries.en: On the gengwu day Xie Fei, chief clerk to the Minister of Works; Jiang Xiao, chief clerk of the Guards Army; Chu Xuan, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; and Liu Yu (the received text has Liu Hou), Literary Scholar to the Prince of Wuling, entered duty in the palace offices to advise on literary matters.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day Xie Fei, chief clerk to the Minister of Works; Jiang Xiao, chief clerk of the Guards Army; Chu Xuan, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; and Liu Yu (the received text has Liu Hou), Literary Scholar to the Prince of Wuling, entered duty in the palace offices to assist with literary matters.

entries.zh: 齊王固讓司空，庚辰，以為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: The Prince of Qi firmly declined the post of Minister of Works; on the gengchen day he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry and authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qi firmly declined the post of Minister of Works; on the gengchen day he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and granted authority to establish an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 十二月丁巳，以驍騎將軍王廣之為徐州刺史。
entries.en: On the dingsi day of the twelfth month Wang Guangzhi, General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day of the twelfth month Wang Guangzhi, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 車騎大將軍、荊州刺史沈攸之舉兵反。
entries.en: Shen Youzhi, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jingzhou, rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: Shen Youzhi, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jingzhou, raised troops in rebellion.

entries.zh: 丁卯，錄公齊王入守朝堂，侍中蕭嶷鎮東府。
entries.en: On the dingmao day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, entered to guard the court hall, and Palace Attendant Xiao Ni garrisoned the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: On the dingmao day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, entered to guard the court hall, and the Palace Attendant Xiao Ni garrisoned the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 戊辰，內外纂嚴。
entries.en: On the wuchen day martial law was imposed within and without the capital.
entries.literal: On the wuchen day martial law was imposed within and without.

entries.zh: 己巳，以郢州刺史武陵王贊為安西將軍、荊州刺史，征虜將軍、雍州刺史張敬兒進號鎮軍將軍。
entries.en: On the jisi day Prince of Wuling Zan, Inspector of Yingzhou, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Zhang Jinger, General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Yongzhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army.
entries.literal: On the jisi day the Prince of Wuling Zan, Inspector of Yingzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Zhang Jinger, General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Yongzhou, was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.

entries.zh: 右衞將軍黃回為平西將軍、郢州刺史，督諸軍前鋒南討。
entries.en: Huang Hui, Right Guards General, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, commanding the vanguard in the southern expedition.
entries.literal: Huang Hui, Right Guards General, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, commanding the vanguard armies in the southern campaign.

entries.zh: 征虜將軍呂安國為湘州刺史，都官尚書王寬加平西將軍。
entries.en: Lu Anguo, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou; Wang Kuan, Director of Judicial Affairs, was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
entries.literal: Lu Anguo, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; Wang Kuan, Director of Judicial Affairs, was additionally made General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 庚午，新除左衞將軍齊王世子奉新除撫軍將軍、揚州刺史晉熙王燮鎮尋陽之盆城。
entries.en: On the gengwu day the newly appointed Left Guards General, heir of the Prince of Qi, escorted the newly appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Jinxi Xie, to garrison Pencheng at Xunyang.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day the newly appointed Left Guards General, heir of the Prince of Qi, escorted the newly appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Jinxi Xie, to garrison Pencheng at Xunyang.

entries.zh: 壬申，以驍騎將軍周盤龍為廣州刺史。
entries.en: On the renshen day Zhou Panlong, General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: On the renshen day Zhou Panlong, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 是日，司徒袁粲據石頭反，尚書令劉秉、黃門侍郎劉述、冠軍王蘊率眾赴之。
entries.en: That same day Minister over the Masses Yuan Can seized Stone City in rebellion; Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Bing, Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate Liu Shu, and General Who Establishes Champions Wang Yun led troops to his side.
entries.literal: That day Minister over the Masses Yuan Can held Stone City in rebellion; the Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Bing, the Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate Liu Shu, and the General Who Establishes Champions Wang Yun led troops to join him.

entries.zh: 黃回及輔國將軍孫曇瓘、屯騎校尉王宜興、輔國將軍任候伯、左軍將軍彭文之密相響應。
entries.en: Huang Hui; Sun Tanguan, General Who Assists the State; Wang Yixing, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry; Ren Houbo, General Who Assists the State; and Peng Wenzhi, General of the Left Army, secretly acted in concert.
entries.literal: Huang Hui and the General Who Assists the State Sun Tanguan, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry Wang Yixing, General Who Assists the State Ren Houbo, and General of the Left Army Peng Wenzhi secretly responded in concert.

entries.zh: 中領軍劉韞、直閤將軍卜伯興在殿內同謀。
entries.en: Central Army Commander Liu Yun and Direct Attendant Bu Boxing plotted together inside the palace.
entries.literal: Central Army Commander Liu Yun and the Direct Attendant Bu Boxing plotted together inside the palace.

entries.zh: 錄公齊王誅韞等於省內。
entries.en: The Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, executed Yun and the others inside the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, executed Yun and the others inside the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 軍主蘇烈、王天生、薛道淵、戴僧靜等陷石頭，斬粲於城內。
entries.en: Army commanders Su Lie, Wang Tiansheng, Xue Daoyuan, and Dai Sengjing took Stone City and beheaded Can within the walls.
entries.literal: The army commanders Su Lie, Wang Tiansheng, Xue Daoyuan, Dai Sengjing, and others took Stone City and beheaded Can inside the walls.

entries.zh: 秉、述、蘊踰城走，追擒之，並伏誅。
entries.en: Bing, Shu, and Yun fled over the wall; pursued and captured, they were all executed.
entries.literal: Bing, Shu, and Yun fled over the wall; they were pursued and captured, and all were executed.

entries.zh: 其餘無所問。
entries.en: The rest were not prosecuted.
entries.literal: The rest were not prosecuted.

entries.zh: 豫州刺史劉懷珍、雍州刺史張敬兒、廣州刺史陳顯達並舉義兵。
entries.en: Liu Huaizhen, Inspector of Yuzhou; Zhang Jinger, Inspector of Yongzhou; and Chen Xianda, Inspector of Guangzhou, all raised loyal forces.
entries.literal: Liu Huaizhen, Inspector of Yuzhou; Zhang Jinger, Inspector of Yongzhou; and Chen Xianda, Inspector of Guangzhou, all raised righteous armies.

entries.zh: 司州刺史姚道和、梁州刺史范栢年、湘州行事庾佩玉擁眾懷貳。
entries.en: Yao Daohe, Inspector of Sizhou; Fan Bonian, Inspector of Liangzhou; and Yu Peiyu, acting for Xiangzhou, all raised forces with divided loyalties.
entries.literal: Yao Daohe, Inspector of Sizhou; Fan Bonian, Inspector of Liangzhou; and Yu Peiyu, acting for Xiangzhou, all mustered troops with divided loyalties.

entries.zh: 甲戌，大赦天下。
entries.en: On the jiaxu day a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 乙亥，以尚書僕射王僧虔為尚書左僕射，新除中書令王延之為尚書右僕射。
entries.en: On the yihai day Wang Sengqian, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wang Yanzhi, the newly appointed Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: On the yihai day Wang Sengqian, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wang Yanzhi, newly appointed Director of the Secretariat, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 吳郡太守劉遐據郡反，輔國將軍張瓌討斬之。
entries.en: Liu Xia, Governor of Wu Commandery, rebelled and held the commandery; Zhang Gui, General Who Assists the State, attacked and killed him.
entries.literal: Liu Xia, Governor of Wu Commandery, held the commandery in rebellion; Zhang Gui, General Who Assists the State, attacked and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 閏月辛巳，屯騎校尉王宜興有罪伏誅。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, on the xinsi day, Wang Yixing, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry, was found guilty and executed.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on the xinsi day, Wang Yixing, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry, was guilty and executed.

entries.zh: 癸巳，沈攸之攻圍郢城，前軍長史柳世隆固守。
entries.en: On the guisi day Shen Youzhi besieged Yingcheng; Liu Shilong, chief clerk of the vanguard, held firm in defense.
entries.literal: On the guisi day Shen Youzhi attacked and besieged Yingcheng; Liu Shilong, chief clerk of the vanguard, held firm in defense.

entries.zh: 攸之弟登之作亂於吳興，吳興太守沈文季討斬之。
entries.en: Youzhi's younger brother Dengzhi rose in revolt in Wuxing; Shen Wenji, Governor of Wuxing, attacked and killed him.
entries.literal: Youzhi's younger brother Dengzhi made trouble in Wuxing; Shen Wenji, Governor of Wuxing, attacked and beheaded him.

entries.zh: [5]己亥，內外戒嚴，假錄公齊王黃鉞。
entries.en: [5] On the jihai day martial law was imposed within and without the capital, and the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, was granted the yellow battle-axe.
entries.literal: [5] On the jihai day martial law was imposed within and without, and the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, was lent the yellow battle-axe.

entries.zh: 辛丑，寧朔將軍、北秦州刺史武都王楊文度進號征西將軍。
entries.en: On the xinchou day Yang Wendu, General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of North Qinzhou, Prince of Wudu, was promoted to General Who Conquers the West.
entries.literal: On the xinchou day Yang Wendu, General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of North Qinzhou, Prince of Wudu, was advanced to General Who Conquers the West.

entries.zh: [6]乙巳，錄公齊王出頓新亭。
entries.en: [6] On the yisi day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, went out and encamped at Xinting.
entries.literal: [6] On the yisi day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, went out and encamped at Xinting.

entries.zh: 二年春正月，沈攸之遣將公孫方平據西陽，辛酉，建寧太守張謨擊破之。
entries.en: In spring of the second year, the first month, Shen Youzhi sent the general Gongsun Fangping to hold Xiyang; on the xinyou day Zhang Mo, Governor of Jianning, attacked and defeated him.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year, the first month, Shen Youzhi sent the general Gongsun Fangping to hold Xiyang; on the xinyou day Zhang Mo, Governor of Jianning, attacked and defeated him.

entries.zh: 丁卯，沈攸之自郢城奔散。
entries.en: On the dingmao day Shen Youzhi fled in rout from Yingcheng.
entries.literal: On the dingmao day Shen Youzhi fled in rout from Yingcheng.

entries.zh: 己巳，華容縣民斬送之。
entries.en: On the jisi day the people of Huarong district killed him and sent his head.
entries.literal: On the jisi day the people of Huarong district beheaded him and sent his head.

entries.zh: 左將軍、豫州刺史劉懷珍進號平南將軍。
entries.en: Liu Huaizhen, General of the Left Army and Inspector of Yuzhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
entries.literal: Liu Huaizhen, General of the Left Army and Inspector of Yuzhou, was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 辛未，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史張敬兒克江陵，斬攸之子光琰，荊州平，同逆皆伏誅。
entries.en: On the xinwei day Zhang Jinger, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, took Jiangling, beheaded Youzhi's son Guangyan, pacified Jingzhou, and all fellow rebels were executed.
entries.literal: On the xinwei day Zhang Jinger, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, took Jiangling, beheaded Youzhi's son Guangyan, pacified Jingzhou, and all fellow rebels were executed.

entries.zh: 丙子，解嚴。
entries.en: On the bingzi day martial law was lifted.
entries.literal: On the bingzi day martial law was lifted.

entries.zh: 以新除侍中柳世隆為尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Liu Shilong, newly appointed Palace Attendant, was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: The newly appointed Palace Attendant Liu Shilong was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 是日，錄公齊王旋鎮東府。
entries.en: That same day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, returned to garrison the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: That day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, returned to garrison the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 丁丑，以江州刺史邵陵王友為安南將軍、南豫州刺史。
entries.en: On the dingchou day Prince of Shaoling You was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of South Yuzhou.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day the Prince of Shaoling You was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of South Yuzhou.

entries.zh: [7]左衞將軍齊王世子為江州刺史，侍中蕭嶷為領軍，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史張敬兒進號征西將軍，平西將軍、郢州刺史黃回進號鎮西將軍。
entries.en: [7] The Left Guards General, heir of the Prince of Qi, was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou; Palace Attendant Xiao Ni was appointed Commander of the Guards; Zhang Jinger, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, was promoted to General Who Conquers the West; Huang Hui, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
entries.literal: [7] The Left Guards General, heir of the Prince of Qi, was made Inspector of Jiangzhou; the Palace Attendant Xiao Ni was made Commander of the Guards; Zhang Jinger, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou, was advanced to General Who Conquers the West; Huang Hui, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 二月庚辰，以尚書左僕射王僧虔為尚書令，尚書右僕射王延之為尚書左僕射。
entries.en: On the gengchen day of the second month Wang Sengqian, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing; Wang Yanzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: On the gengchen day of the second month Wang Sengqian, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Wang Yanzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 癸未，錄公齊王加授太尉，衞將軍褚淵為中書監、司空。
entries.en: On the guiwei day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, was additionally appointed Grand Commandant; Chu Yuan, Guards General, was appointed Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On the guiwei day the Recording Secretary, the Prince of Qi, was additionally invested as Grand Commandant; Chu Yuan, Guards General, was made Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 甲申，曲赦荊州。
entries.en: On the jiashen day a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Jingzhou.
entries.literal: On the jiashen day a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 丙戌，撫軍將軍、揚州刺史晉熙王燮進號中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: On the bingxu day Prince of Jinxi Xie, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou, was promoted to Central Army Commander and authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: On the bingxu day Prince of Jinxi Xie, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou, was advanced to Central Army Commander and granted authority to establish an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 戊子，蠲雍州緣沔居民前被水災者租布三年。
entries.en: On the wuzi day grain tax and cloth levy were remitted for three years for residents along the Han in Yongzhou who had earlier suffered flooding.
entries.literal: On the wuzi day the grain tax and cloth levy for three years were remitted for residents along the Han in Yongzhou who had earlier suffered flood disaster.

entries.zh: 辛卯，郢州刺史、新除鎮南將軍黃回為鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史，南兗州刺史李安民為郢州刺史。
entries.en: On the xinmao day Huang Hui, Inspector of Yingzhou and newly appointed General Who Pacifies the South, was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of South Yanzhou; Li Anmin, Inspector of South Yanzhou, was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: On the xinmao day Huang Hui, Inspector of Yingzhou and newly appointed General Who Pacifies the South, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of South Yanzhou; Li Anmin, Inspector of South Yanzhou, was made Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以山陰令傅琰為益州刺史。
entries.en: On the guisi day Fu Yan, Magistrate of Shanyin, was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.
entries.literal: On the guisi day Fu Yan, Magistrate of Shanyin, was made Inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 丙申，左軍將軍彭文之有罪，下獄死。
entries.en: On the bingshen day Peng Wenzhi, General of the Left Army, was found guilty, imprisoned, and died.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day Peng Wenzhi, General of the Left Army, was guilty, imprisoned, and died.

entries.zh: 行湘州事任候伯殺前湘州行事庾佩玉，傳首京邑。
entries.en: Ren Houbo, acting for Xiangzhou, killed the former acting officer of Xiangzhou Yu Peiyu and sent his head to the capital.
entries.literal: Ren Houbo, acting for Xiangzhou, killed the former Xiangzhou acting officer Yu Peiyu and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 三月庚戌，以廣州刺史周盤龍為司州刺史，輔國將軍劉悛為廣州刺史。
entries.en: On the gengxu day of the third month Zhou Panlong, Inspector of Guangzhou, was appointed Inspector of Sizhou; Liu Quan, General Who Assists the State, was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: On the gengxu day of the third month Zhou Panlong, Inspector of Guangzhou, was made Inspector of Sizhou; Liu Quan, General Who Assists the State, was made Inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 丙子，給太尉齊王羽葆、鼓吹。
entries.en: On the bingzi day the canopy of feathers and martial pipes and drums were granted to the Prince of Qi, Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: On the bingzi day the canopy of feathers and martial pipes and drums were granted to the Prince of Qi, Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 八月辛卯，太尉齊王表斷奇飾麗服，凡十有四條。
entries.en: On the xinmao day of the eighth month the Prince of Qi, Grand Commandant, memorialized to forbid extravagant ornament and splendid dress, fourteen articles in all.
entries.literal: On the xinmao day of the eighth month the Prince of Qi, Grand Commandant, memorialized to forbid extravagant ornament and splendid dress, fourteen articles in all.

entries.zh: [8]乙未，以江州刺史齊王世子為領軍將軍、撫軍將軍。
entries.en: [8] On the yiwei day the heir of the Prince of Qi, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was appointed Commander of the Guards and General Who Pacifies the Army.
entries.literal: [8] On the yiwei day the heir of the Prince of Qi, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was made Commander of the Guards and General Who Pacifies the Army.

entries.zh: 丙申，以領軍蕭嶷為江州刺史。
entries.en: On the bingshen day Xiao Ni, Commander of the Guards, was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day Xiao Ni, Commander of the Guards, was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 三年春正月甲辰，以江州刺史蕭嶷為鎮西將軍、荊州刺史，尚書左僕射王延之為安南將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: In spring of the third year, on the jiachen day of the first month, Xiao Ni, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Wang Yanzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: In spring of the third year, on the jiachen day of the first month, Xiao Ni, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Wang Yanzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 安西長史蕭順之為郢州刺史。
entries.en: Xiao Shunzhi, chief clerk of Anxi, was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Xiao Shunzhi, chief clerk of Anxi, was made Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 乙卯，太傅齊王表諸負官物質役者，悉原除。
entries.en: On the yimao day the Prince of Qi, Grand Preceptor, memorialized that all who owed official goods or corvée labor should be wholly remitted.
entries.literal: On the yimao day the Prince of Qi, Grand Preceptor, memorialized that all who owed official goods or corvée labor should be wholly remitted.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以驍騎將軍王玄邈為梁、南秦二州刺史。
entries.en: On the xinhai day Wang Xuanmiao, General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day Wang Xuanmiao, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin provinces.

entries.zh: 領軍將軍、撫軍將軍齊王世子加尚書僕射，進號中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: The heir of the Prince of Qi, Commander of the Guards and General Who Pacifies the Army, was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, promoted to Grand Central Army Commander, and authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: The heir of the Prince of Qi, Commander of the Guards and General Who Pacifies the Army, was additionally made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced to Grand Central Army Commander, and granted authority to establish an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 丙辰，加太傅齊王前部羽葆、鼓吹。
entries.en: On the bingchen day the front canopy of feathers and martial pipes and drums were granted to the Prince of Qi, Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day the front canopy of feathers and martial pipes and drums were granted to the Prince of Qi, Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 丁巳，詔太傅府依舊辟召。
entries.en: On the dingsi day an edict ordered the Grand Preceptor's office to recruit staff as before.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day an edict ordered the Grand Preceptor's office to recruit as of old.

entries.zh: 以征西將軍、雍州刺史張敬兒為護軍將軍，新除給事黃門侍郎蕭長懋為雍州刺史。
entries.en: Zhang Jinger, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Yongzhou, was appointed General Who Protects the Army; Xiao Changmao, newly appointed Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate, was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Jinger, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Yongzhou, was made General Who Protects the Army; Xiao Changmao, newly appointed Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate, was made Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 九月乙巳朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: On the new moon of the ninth month, the day yisi, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, the day yisi, there was an eclipse of the sun.

entries.zh: 丙午，加太尉齊王黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、太傅，領揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。
entries.en: On the bingwu day the Prince of Qi, Grand Commandant, was additionally granted the yellow battle-axe, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, and appointed Grand Preceptor, holding concurrently the governorship of Yangzhou; he was permitted sword and shoes in the palace hall, not to quicken his step on entering court, and not to have his name spoken in congratulatory address.
entries.literal: On the bingwu day the Prince of Qi, Grand Commandant, was additionally granted the yellow battle-axe, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, and appointed Grand Preceptor, holding concurrently the governorship of Yangzhou; he was permitted sword and shoes in the palace hall, not to quicken his step on entering court, and not to have his name spoken in congratulatory address.

entries.zh: 置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人。
entries.en: Left and right chief clerks, marshals, attendants, aides, and subordinates were established, four of each.
entries.literal: Left and right chief clerks, marshals, attendants, aides, and subordinates were established, four of each.

entries.zh: 中軍將軍、揚州刺史晉熙王燮為司徒。
entries.en: Prince of Jinxi Xie, Central Army Commander and Inspector of Yangzhou, was appointed Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: Prince of Jinxi Xie, Central Army Commander and Inspector of Yangzhou, was made Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 戊申，行南兗州刺史蕭映為南兗州刺史。
entries.en: On the wushen day Xiao Ying, acting Inspector of South Yanzhou, was appointed Inspector of South Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On the wushen day Xiao Ying, acting Inspector of South Yanzhou, was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 甲寅，給太傅齊王三望車。
entries.en: On the jiayin day three imperial lookout chariots were granted to the Prince of Qi, Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On the jiayin day three imperial lookout chariots were granted to the Prince of Qi, Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 己未，芮芮國遣使獻方物。
entries.en: On the jiwei day Ruru sent envoys presenting tribute.
entries.literal: On the jiwei day Ruru sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 癸酉，武陵內史張澹有罪，下獄死。
entries.en: On the guiyou day Zhang Dan, Interior Secretary of Wuling, was found guilty, imprisoned, and died.
entries.literal: On the guiyou day Zhang Dan, Interior Secretary of Wuling, was guilty, imprisoned, and died.

entries.zh: 三月癸卯朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: On the new moon of the third month, the day guimao, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: On the new moon of the third month, the day guimao, there was an eclipse of the sun.

entries.zh: 甲辰，崇太傅為相國，總百揆，封十郡，為齊公，備九錫之禮，加璽紱遠游冠，位在諸王上，加相國綠綟綬，其驃騎大將軍、揚州牧、南徐州刺史如故。
entries.en: On the jiachen day the Grand Preceptor was elevated to Chancellor of State, directing all affairs of government, enfeoffed with ten commanderies as Duke of Qi, granted the full rites of the Nine Bestowals, additionally given the imperial seal-cord and the Far Roaming cap, ranking above all princes, with a green cord for the Chancellor of State; he remained Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Yangzhou, and Inspector of South Xuzhou as before.
entries.literal: On the jiachen day the Grand Preceptor was elevated to Chancellor of State, directing all affairs of government, enfeoffed with ten commanderies as Duke of Qi, granted the full rites of the Nine Bestowals, additionally given the imperial seal-cord and the Far Roaming cap, ranking above all princes, with a green cord for the Chancellor of State; he remained Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Yangzhou, and Inspector of South Xuzhou as before.

entries.zh: 丙午，以中軍大將軍蕭賾為南豫州刺史、齊公世子，副貳相國，綠綟綬。
entries.en: On the bingwu day Xiao Ze, Grand Central Army Commander, was appointed Inspector of South Yuzhou and heir of the Duke of Qi, deputy to the Chancellor of State, with a green cord.
entries.literal: On the bingwu day Xiao Ze, Grand Central Army Commander, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou and heir of the Duke of Qi, deputy to the Chancellor of State, with a green cord.

entries.zh: 庚戌，臨川王綽謀反，綽及黨與皆伏誅。
entries.en: On the gengxu day Prince of Linchuan Chuo plotted rebellion; Chuo and his associates were all executed.
entries.literal: On the gengxu day Prince of Linchuan Chuo plotted rebellion; Chuo and his partisans were all executed.

entries.zh: 丁巳，以齊國初建，給錢五百萬，布五千匹，絹千匹。
entries.en: On the dingsi day, because the State of Qi was newly established, five million cash, five thousand bolts of cloth, and one thousand bolts of silk were granted.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day, because the State of Qi was newly established, five million cash, five thousand bolts of cloth, and one thousand bolts of silk were granted.

entries.zh: 夏四月壬申，進齊公爵為齊王，增封十郡。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on the renshen day the Duke of Qi was promoted to Prince of Qi, with ten additional commanderies added to his fief.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the renshen day the Duke of Qi was advanced to Prince of Qi, with ten additional commanderies added to his fief.

entries.zh: 甲戌，安西將軍武陵王贊薨。
entries.en: On the jiaxu day Prince of Wuling Zan, General Who Pacifies the West, died.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu day Prince of Wuling Zan, General Who Pacifies the West, died.

entries.zh: 丙戌，命齊王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂儛八佾，設鐘簴宮縣。
entries.en: On the bingxu day the Prince of Qi was commanded to wear a twelve-tassel cap, establish the imperial banners and flags, clear the roads on exit and entry, ride the golden-root chariot drawn by six horses, equip five seasonal auxiliary carriages, install the maotou and yunhan banners, perform the eight ranks of dancers, and establish the bell frames and palace musical sets.
entries.literal: On the bingxu day the Prince of Qi was commanded to wear a twelve-tassel cap, establish the imperial banners and flags, clear the roads on exit and entry, ride the golden-root chariot drawn by six horses, equip five seasonal auxiliary carriages, install the maotou and yunhan banners, perform the eight ranks of dancers, and establish the bell frames and palace musical sets.

entries.zh: 進世子為太子，王子、王女、王孫爵命之號，壹如舊儀。
entries.en: The heir was promoted to Crown Prince; titles and ranks for princes, princesses, and royal grandchildren followed entirely the former protocols.
entries.literal: The heir was advanced to Crown Prince; titles and ranks for princes, princesses, and royal grandchildren followed entirely the former protocols.

entries.zh: 辛卯，天祿永終，禪位于齊。
entries.en: On the xinmao day the celestial mandate reached its end, and the throne was yielded to Qi.
entries.literal: On the xinmao day the celestial mandate reached its end, and the throne was yielded to Qi.

entries.zh: 壬辰，帝遜位于東邸。
entries.en: On the renchen day the emperor abdicated at the Eastern Residence.
entries.literal: On the renchen day the emperor abdicated at the Eastern Residence.

entries.zh: 既而遷居丹陽宮。
entries.en: Thereafter he moved to dwell in the Danyang Palace.
entries.literal: Thereafter he moved to dwell in the Danyang Palace.

entries.zh: 齊王踐阼，封帝為汝陰王，待以不臣之禮。
entries.en: The Prince of Qi ascended the throne, enfeoffed the emperor as Prince of Ruyin, and treated him with the rites due one not subject to court protocol.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qi ascended the throne, enfeoffed the emperor as Prince of Ruyin, and treated him with the rites due one not subject to court protocol.

entries.zh: 行宋正朔，上書不為表，答表不為詔。
entries.en: The Song calendar was maintained; memorials submitted were not styled as petitions, and replies to petitions were not styled as edicts.
entries.literal: The Song calendar was maintained; memorials submitted were not styled as petitions, and replies to petitions were not styled as edicts.

entries.zh: 夏四月己卯，以游擊將軍垣崇祖為兗州刺史。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on the jimao day Yuan Chongzu, General of the Mobile Corps, was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the jimao day Yuan Chongzu, General of the Mobile Corps, was made Inspector of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 辛卯，新除鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史黃回有罪賜死。
entries.en: On the xinmao day Huang Hui, newly appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was found guilty and ordered to die.
entries.literal: On the xinmao day Huang Hui, newly appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was guilty and ordered to die.

entries.zh: 甲午，輔國將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守蕭映行南兗州刺史。
entries.en: On the jiawu day Xiao Ying, General Who Assists the State and Governor of Huainan and Xuancheng, acted as Inspector of South Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day Xiao Ying, General Who Assists the State and Governor of Huainan and Xuancheng, acted as Inspector of South Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 順皇帝諱準，字仲謀，[1]小字智觀，明帝第三子也。
entries.en: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.
entries.literal: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.

entries.zh: 泰始五年七月癸丑生。
entries.en: He was born on the guichou day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taishi.
entries.literal: He was born on the guichou day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taishi.

entries.zh: 七年，封安成王，食邑三千戶。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was created Prince of Ancheng with a fief of three thousand households.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng with a fief of three thousand households.

entries.zh: 仍拜撫軍將軍，置佐史。
entries.en: He was at once appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, with aides and clerks assigned.
entries.literal: He was at once appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, with aides and clerks established.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，為揚州刺史。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, he became Inspector of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, he became Inspector of Yangzhou.
