entries.zh: 元徽二年，進號車騎將軍、都督揚南豫二州諸軍事，給鼓吹一部，刺史如故。
entries.en: In the second year of Yuanhui he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yang and South Yu provinces, granted one set of martial pipes and drums, and remained Inspector as before.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui he was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the two provinces of Yang and South Yu, granted one set of martial pipes and drums, and remained Inspector as before.

entries.zh: 四年，又進號驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，班劍三十人，都督、刺史如故。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was further promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and granted thirty ceremonial swordsmen; he remained Commander-in-Chief and Inspector as before.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was further advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, granted authority to establish his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and thirty ceremonial swordsmen, and remained Commander-in-Chief and Inspector as before.

entries.zh: 改易者，其一，以舊法一章十九歲有七閏，閏數為多，經二百年，輒差一日。
entries.en: First change: the old rule of seven intercalations in nineteen years inserts too many leap months; in two centuries it slips a full day.
entries.literal: Of the changes—first, the old method had seven intercalations in nineteen years, the intercalation count being too many; over two hundred years it would shift by one day.

entries.zh: 節閏既移，則應改法，曆紀屢遷，實由此條。
entries.en: Once seasons and intercalation drift, the calendar must be revised—and that, I argue, is why systems have been rewritten again and again.
entries.literal: Once the qi and intercalation shift, the method ought to be changed; calendars have been repeatedly altered—truly from this cause.

entries.zh: 今改章法，三百九十一年有一百四十四閏。
entries.en: My new intercalation rule yields 144 leap months in 391 years.
entries.literal: Now changing the intercalation rule: in three hundred ninety-one years there are one hundred forty-four intercalations.

entries.zh: 令卻合周、漢，則將來永用，無複差動。
entries.en: Aligned with Zhou and Han practice, it should serve indefinitely without further drift.
entries.literal: Making it accord with Zhou and Han, then in future use forever, without further deviation.

entries.zh: 其二，以《堯典》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。」
entries.en: Second: the Canon of Yao says, "The days are short and the star is Mao—thereby fix mid-winter."
entries.literal: Second, the 《Canon of Yao》 says: "The days are short and the star is Mao; thereby fix mid-winter."

entries.zh: 以此推之，唐代冬至，日在今宿之左五十許度。
entries.en: From that line, at the Tang dynasty midwinter the sun stood some fifty degrees west of its present lodge.
entries.literal: Inferring from this, at the Tang era midwinter the sun was at about fifty degrees to the left of today's lodge.

entries.zh: 漢代之初，即用秦曆，冬至日在牽牛六度。
entries.en: At the Han founding the Qin calendar placed midwinter at 6° in Ox.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Han they immediately used the Qin calendar; midwinter sun was at Ox six degrees.

entries.zh: 漢武改立《太初曆》，冬至日在牛初。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's Taichu Calendar moved it to the start of Ox.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu established the 《Taichu Calendar》; midwinter sun at the head of Ox.

entries.zh: 後漢《四分法》，冬至日在鬥二十二。
entries.en: The Later Han Quarter-Remainder system put it at Dipper 22.
entries.literal: Later Han Four Elements method: midwinter sun at Dipper twenty-two.

entries.zh: 晉時薑岌以月蝕檢日，知冬至在鬥十七。
entries.en: In Jin, Jiang Ji checked eclipses and found midwinter at Dipper 17.
entries.literal: In Jin times Jiang Ji used lunar eclipses to check the sun, knowing midwinter was at Dipper seventeen.

entries.zh: 今參以中星，課以蝕望，冬至之日，在鬥十一。
entries.en: Comparing culminating stars with eclipse and full-moon tests, midwinter now falls at Dipper 11.
entries.literal: Now comparing with culminating stars and testing by eclipses and full moons, on midwinter day the sun is at Dipper eleven.

entries.zh: 通而計之，未盈百載，所差二度。
entries.en: Taken together, the shift is two degrees in less than a century.
entries.literal: Comprehensively reckoning, within not yet a full hundred years the discrepancy is two degrees.

entries.zh: 舊法並令冬至日有定處，天數既差，則七曜宿度漸與曆舛。
entries.en: Older systems pinned midwinter to a fixed longitude; as the sky moves, the seven luminaries steadily part from the calendar.
entries.literal: The old methods all fixed the midwinter sun at a definite place; since the heavenly count has shifted, the seven luminaries' lodge degrees gradually diverge from the calendar.

entries.zh: 乖謬既著，輒應改制，僅合一時，莫能通遠，遷革不已，又由此條。
entries.en: Once the mismatch shows, reform is due; a fixed midwinter served one age but not the long term—and that too drove endless revisions.
entries.literal: Once the error is evident, the system ought to be changed; it suited only one period and could not extend far—constant change also stems from this cause.

entries.zh: 今令冬至所在，歲歲微差，卻檢漢注，並皆審密，將來久用，無煩屢改。
entries.en: I would let midwinter advance slightly year by year; checked against Han observations it holds closely, and long use should not require repeated overhauls.
entries.literal: Now making the midwinter position shift slightly each year, checking against Han annotations all are verified and precise; for long future use there will be no need for frequent changes.

entries.zh: 法興議曰：「戰國橫騖，史官喪紀，爰及漢初，格候莫審，後雜覘知在南斗二十二度，元和所用，即與古曆相符也。
entries.en: Dai Faxing submitted: "In the Warring States calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at Southern Dipper 22°; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.
entries.literal: Faxing submitted: "In the Warring States era calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at twenty-two degrees of Southern Dipper; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.

entries.zh: 逮至景初，終無毫忒。」
entries.en: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error."
entries.literal: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error."

entries.zh: 沖之曰：古術訛雜，其詳闕聞，乙卯之曆，秦代所用，必有效於當時，故其言可征也。
entries.en: Zu Chongzhi said: Ancient methods were wrong and mixed; details are missing from record; the yimao calendar was used in the Qin era and must have been effective in its time, so its words can be verified.
entries.literal: Chongzhi said: Ancient methods were wrong and mixed; details are missing from record; the yimao calendar was used in the Qin era and must have been effective in its time, so its words can be verified.

entries.zh: 漢武改創，檢課詳備，正儀審漏，事在前史，測星辨度，理無乖遠。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han reformed and created anew; testing and checking were detailed and complete, correcting instruments and examining clepsydra—the matter is in earlier histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees, the principle is not far wrong.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Han reformed and created anew; testing and checking were detailed and complete, correcting instruments and examining clepsydra—the matter is in earlier histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees, the principle is not far wrong.

entries.zh: 今議者所是不實見，所非徒為虛妄，辨彼駭此，既非通談，運今背古，所誣誠多，偏據一說，未若兼今之為長也。
entries.en: What the debaters approve is not real observation; what they reject is merely empty falsity; distinguishing that and rejecting this is not general discussion; applying the present while turning against antiquity, the distortions are indeed many—relying on one theory alone is not as good as combining the present.
entries.literal: What the debaters approve is not real observation; what they reject is merely empty falsity; distinguishing that and rejecting this is not general discussion; applying the present and turning against antiquity, the distortions are indeed many—relying on one theory alone is not as good as combining the present.

entries.zh: 《景初》之法，實錯五緯，今則在沖口，至曩已移日。
entries.en: The Jingchu method in fact mis-set the five planets; Dai Faxing now cites it, yet long ago its solar day had already shifted.
entries.literal: The Jingchu method in fact mis-set the five planets; now it is in Chongzhi's mouth, yet long ago the day had already shifted.

entries.zh: 蓋略治朔望，無事檢候，是以晷漏昏明，並即《元和》，二分異景，尚不知革，日度微差，宜其謬矣。
entries.en: It roughly handled new and full moons without testing observation; therefore gnomon, clepsydra, dusk and dawn all followed Yuanhe; at the two seasonal nodes the shadows differed, yet they still did not know to reform—a slight solar discrepancy was bound to go wrong.
entries.literal: It roughly handled new and full moons without testing observation; therefore gnomon, clepsydra, dusk and dawn all followed Yuanhe; at the two seasonal nodes the shadows differed, yet they still did not know to reform—solar degree's slight discrepancy ought to have been wrong.

entries.zh: 志第三 曆下
entries.en: Treatise 3: Calendar, Part 2.
entries.literal: Treatise 3, Calendar (Part 2).

entries.zh: 禮云：「共工氏之霸九州，其子句龍曰后土，能平九土，故祀以為社。」
entries.en: The Rites state: "When Gong Gong dominated the nine provinces, his son Gou Long was called Lord of Earth; he could level the nine lands—therefore he was sacrificed to as the altar of Earth."
entries.literal: The Rites state: "When Gong Gong dominated the nine provinces, his son Gou Long was called Lord of Earth; he could level the nine lands—therefore he was sacrificed to as the altar of Earth."

entries.zh: 周以甲日祭之，用日之始也。
entries.en: Zhou sacrificed on the jia day—using the beginning of the day.
entries.literal: Zhou sacrificed on the jia day— using the beginning of the day.

entries.zh: 「社所以神地之道。
entries.en: "The altar of Earth is how one spiritualizes the way of earth.
entries.literal: "The altar of Earth is how one spiritualizes the way of earth.

entries.zh: 地載萬物，天垂象。
entries.en: Earth carries the myriad things, and Heaven displays the signs.
entries.literal: Earth carries the myriad things; Heaven displays the signs.

entries.zh: 取財於地，取法於天。
entries.en: Take wealth from earth and law from heaven.
entries.literal: Take wealth from earth; take law from heaven.

entries.zh: 是以尊天而親地。
entries.en: Therefore one reveres heaven and draws close to earth.
entries.literal: Therefore revere heaven and be close to earth.

entries.zh: 故教民美報焉。
entries.en: Thus the people are taught to make beautiful recompense.
entries.literal: Thus the people are taught beautiful recompense.

entries.zh: 家主中霤而國主社，示本也。」
entries.en: The household takes the central rafter as lord; the state takes the altar of Earth as lord—showing the root."
entries.literal: The household takes the central rafter as lord; the state takes the altar of Earth as lord—showing the root."

entries.zh: 故言報本反始。
entries.en: Therefore it speaks of recompensing the root and returning to the beginning.
entries.literal: Therefore it speaks of recompensing the root and returning to the beginning.

entries.zh: 烈山氏之有天下，其子曰農，能殖百穀。
entries.en: When the Flame Emperor possessed the realm, his son was called Nong and could propagate the hundred kinds of grain.
entries.literal: When the Flame Emperor possessed the realm, his son was called Nong and could propagate the hundred grains.

entries.zh: 其裔曰柱，佐顓頊為稷官，主農事，周棄係之，法施於人，故祀以為稷。
entries.en: His descendant was called Zhu; he assisted Zhuanxu as officer of grain, presiding over agricultural affairs; Zhou's Hou Ji succeeded him; his method benefited the people—therefore he was sacrificed to as the god of grain.
entries.literal: His descendant was called Zhu; he assisted Zhuanxu as officer of grain, presiding over agricultural affairs; Zhou's Hou Ji succeeded him; his method benefited the people— therefore he was sacrificed to as the god of grain.

entries.zh: 禮：「王為羣姓立社曰太社，王自為立社曰王社。」
entries.en: The Rites: "The king establishes an altar of Earth for the clans—called the Grand Altar of Earth; the king establishes an altar of Earth for himself—called the King's Altar of Earth."
entries.literal: The Rites: "The king establishes an altar of Earth for the clans—called the Grand Altar of Earth; the king establishes an altar of Earth for himself—called the King's Altar of Earth."

entries.zh: 故國有二社，而稷亦有二也。
entries.en: Therefore the state has two altars of Earth, and the god of grain also has two.
entries.literal: Therefore the state has two altars of Earth, and the god of grain also has two.

entries.zh: 漢、魏則有官社，無稷，故常二社一稷也。
entries.en: Han and Wei had the official altar of Earth but no god of grain—therefore regularly two altars of Earth and one god of grain.
entries.literal: Han and Wei had the official altar of Earth but no god of grain— therefore regularly two altars of Earth and one god of grain.

entries.zh: 晉初仍魏，無所增損。
entries.en: Early Jin followed Wei without adding or subtracting anything.
entries.literal: Early Jin followed Wei without increase or decrease.

entries.zh: 至太康九年，改建宗廟，而社稷壇與廟俱徙。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Taikang the ancestral temple was rebuilt, and the altars of soil and grain were moved together with it.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang the ancestral temple was rebuilt; the altars of soil and grain were moved together with the temple.

entries.zh: 乃詔曰：「社實一神，其并二社之祀。」
entries.en: An edict then stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit—combine the sacrifice of the two altars of Earth."
entries.literal: An edict then stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit—combine the sacrifice of the two altars of Earth."

entries.zh: 於是車騎司馬傅咸表曰：「祭法二社各有其義。
entries.en: Thereupon General of Chariots and Cavalry Fu Xian submitted a memorial: "The Record of Sacrifice—the two altars of Earth each have their meaning.
entries.literal: Thereupon General of Chariots and Cavalry Fu Xian submitted a memorial: "The Record of Sacrifice— the two altars of Earth each have their meaning.

entries.zh: 天子尊事郊廟，故冕而躬耕。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven reverently serves the suburban altars and temples—therefore wears the sacrificial cap and personally plows.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven reverently serves the suburban altars and temples— therefore wears the sacrificial cap and personally plows.

entries.zh: 躬耕也者，所以重孝享之粢盛，致殷薦於上帝也。
entries.en: Personal plowing is to emphasize the sacrificial grain of filial offerings—rendering the yin offering to the Lord on High.
entries.literal: Personal plowing is to emphasize the sacrificial grain of filial offerings— rendering the yin offering to the Lord on High.

entries.zh: 穀梁傳曰：『天子親耕以供粢盛。』
entries.en: The Guliang Commentary says: 'The Son of Heaven personally plows in order to supply the sacrificial grain.'
entries.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: 'The Son of Heaven personally plows in order to supply the sacrificial grain.'

entries.zh: 親耕，謂自報，自為立社者，為籍而報也。
entries.en: Personal plowing means self-recompense; establishing an altar for oneself—for the field and recompense.
entries.literal: Personal plowing means self-recompense; establishing an altar for oneself— for the field and recompense.

entries.zh: 國以人為本，人以穀為命，故又為百姓立社而祈報焉。
entries.en: The state takes the people as foundation; people take grain as life—therefore also establish an altar of Earth for the hundred surnames and pray for recompense.
entries.literal: The state takes the people as foundation; people take grain as life— therefore also establish an altar of Earth for the hundred surnames and pray for recompense.

entries.zh: 事異報殊，此社之所以有二也。
entries.en: The affair differs and recompense differs—this is why there are two altars of Earth.
entries.literal: The affair differs and recompense differs— this is why there are two altars of Earth.

entries.zh: 王景侯之論王社，亦謂春祈籍田，秋而報之也。
entries.en: Wang Jinghou's discussion of the King's Altar of Earth also speaks of spring prayer at the field of sacrifice and autumn recompense.
entries.literal: Wang Jinghou's discussion of the King's Altar of Earth also says spring prayer at the field of sacrifice, autumn recompense.

entries.zh: 其論太社，則曰『王者布下圻內，為百姓立之，謂之太社，不自立之於京師也』。
entries.en: His discussion of the Grand Altar of Earth says: 'The king spreads within the inner domain; establishes it for the hundred surnames—called the Grand Altar of Earth; does not establish it for himself in the capital.'
entries.literal: His discussion of the Grand Altar of Earth says: 'The king spreads within the inner domain; establishes it for the hundred surnames—called the Grand Altar of Earth; does not establish it for himself in the capital.'

entries.zh: 景侯此論，據祭法『大夫以下，成羣立社，曰置社』。
entries.en: Jinghou's discussion cites the Record of Sacrifice: 'Grand officers and below—when a group is formed establish an altar of Earth—called establishing an altar.'
entries.literal: Jinghou's discussion cites the Record of Sacrifice: 'Grand officers and below—when a group is formed establish an altar of Earth—called establishing an altar.'

entries.zh: 景侯解曰：『今之里社是也。』
entries.en: Jinghou explains: 'The present neighborhood altar of Earth is of this kind.'
entries.literal: Jinghou explains: 'The present neighborhood altar of Earth is of this kind.'

entries.zh: 景侯解祭法，則以置社為人間之社矣。
entries.en: In Jinghou's explanation of the Record of Sacrifice, establishing an altar is taken as the people's altar of Earth.
entries.literal: Jinghou explaining the Record of Sacrifice takes establishing an altar as the people's altar of Earth.

entries.zh: 而別論復以太社為人間之社，未曉此旨也。
entries.en: Yet separately discussing takes the Grand Altar of Earth as the people's altar—the intent of this is not understood.
entries.literal: Yet separately discussing takes the Grand Altar of Earth as the people's altar— the intent of this is not understood.

entries.zh: 太社，天子為民而祀，故稱天子社。
entries.en: The Grand Altar of Earth—the Son of Heaven sacrifices for the people—therefore called the Son of Heaven's altar of Earth.
entries.literal: The Grand Altar of Earth— the Son of Heaven sacrifices for the people— therefore called the Son of Heaven's altar of Earth.

entries.zh: 郊特牲曰：『天子太社，必受霜露風雨。』
entries.en: Suburban Sacrifice states: 'The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Earth must be exposed to frost, dew, wind, and rain.'
entries.literal: Suburban Sacrifice states: 'The Son of Heaven's Grand Altar of Earth must be exposed to frost, dew, wind, and rain.'

entries.zh: 夫以羣姓之眾，王者通為立社，故稱太社。
entries.en: For the multitude of the clans the king universally establishes altars of Earth—therefore called Grand Altar of Earth.
entries.literal: For the multitude of the clans the king universally establishes altars of Earth— therefore called Grand Altar of Earth.

entries.zh: 若夫置社，其數不一，蓋以里所為名。
entries.en: As for establishing altars, their number is not one—generally named by the neighborhood.
entries.literal: As for establishing altars, their number is not one— generally named by the neighborhood.

entries.zh: 左氏傳盟于清丘之社是也。
entries.en: The Zuo Commentary's account of the covenant at Qingqiu's altar of Earth is such.
entries.literal: The Zuo Commentary's covenant at Qingqiu's altar of Earth is such.

entries.zh: 人間之社，既已不稱太矣。
entries.en: The people's altar of Earth—already not called Grand.
entries.literal: The people's altar of Earth— already not called Grand.

entries.zh: 若復不立之京都，當安所立乎？
entries.en: If again not established in the capital—where should it be established?
entries.literal: If again not established in the capital— where should it be established?

entries.zh: 祭法又曰：『王為羣姓立七祀。
entries.en: The Record of Sacrifice also says: 'The king establishes seven sacrifices on behalf of the clans.
entries.literal: The Record of Sacrifice also says: 'The king establishes seven sacrifices for the clans.

entries.zh: 自為立七祀。』
entries.en: He also establishes seven sacrifices for himself.'
entries.literal: He also establishes seven sacrifices for himself.'

entries.zh: 言自為者，自為而祀也。
entries.en: Speaking of "for himself"—sacrifice for oneself.
entries.literal: Speaking of "for himself"— sacrifice for oneself.

entries.zh: 為羣姓者，為羣姓而祀也。
entries.en: For the clans—sacrifice for the clans.
entries.literal: For the clans— sacrifice for the clans.

entries.zh: 太社與七祀，其文正等。
entries.en: The Grand Altar of Earth and the seven sacrifices—their texts are equally ranked.
entries.literal: The Grand Altar of Earth and the seven sacrifices— their texts are equally ranked.

entries.zh: 說者窮此，因云墳籍但有五祀無七祀也。
entries.en: Expositors exhaust this point and therefore say the canonical texts have only five sacrifices, not seven.
entries.literal: Expositors exhaust this and therefore say the canonical texts have only five sacrifices, not seven.

entries.zh: 按祭五祀，國之大祀，七者小祀。
entries.en: Examining sacrifice to the five sacrifices—great sacrifice of the state; the seven are lesser sacrifice.
entries.literal: Examining sacrifice to the five sacrifices— great sacrifice of the state; the seven are lesser sacrifice.

entries.zh: 周禮所云祭凡小祀，則墨冕之屬也。
entries.en: The Rites of Zhou speaks of sacrificing all lesser sacrifices—then black sacrificial cap and the like.
entries.literal: The Rites of Zhou speaks of sacrificing all lesser sacrifices— then black sacrificial cap and the like.

entries.zh: 景侯解大厲曰：『如周杜伯，鬼有所歸，乃不為厲。』
entries.en: Jinghou explaining great pestilence says: 'Like Zhou's Duke of Du—when the ghost has a place to return, then it does not become a pestilence.'
entries.literal: Jinghou explaining great pestilence says: 'Like Zhou's Duke of Du—when the ghost has a place to return, then it does not become a pestilence.'

entries.zh: 今云無二社者，稱景侯祭法不謂無二，則曰口傳無其文也。
entries.en: Now saying there are not two altars of Earth—citing Jinghou's Record of Sacrifice does not mean there are not two; it says oral tradition has no text.
entries.literal: Now saying there are not two altars of Earth— citing Jinghou's Record of Sacrifice does not mean there are not two; it says oral tradition has no text.

entries.zh: 夫以景侯之明，擬議而後為解，而欲以口論除明文。
entries.en: Given Jinghou's clarity—deliberating before making explanation—yet wishing to remove explicit text by oral argument.
entries.literal: Given Jinghou's clarity— deliberating before making explanation— yet wishing to remove explicit text by oral argument.

entries.zh: 如此，非但二社，當是思惟景侯之後解，亦未易除也。
entries.en: Thus not only the two altars of Earth—one should reflect on Jinghou's later explanations; they too are not easily removed.
entries.literal: Thus not only the two altars of Earth— one should reflect on Jinghou's later explanations; they too are not easily removed.

entries.zh: 前被敕，尚書召誥：『社于新邑，唯一太牢，』不立二社之明義也。
entries.en: Formerly receiving the edict—the Announcement of the Prince of Shao: 'Altar of Earth at the new city—only one Grand Victim'—the clear meaning of not establishing two altars of Earth.
entries.literal: Formerly receiving the edict— the Announcement of the Prince of Shao: 'Altar of Earth at the new city— only one Grand Victim'— the clear meaning of not establishing two altars of Earth.

entries.zh: 按郊特牲曰：『社稷太牢。』
entries.en: Examining Suburban Sacrifice: 'Altars of soil and grain—Grand Victim.'
entries.literal: Examining Suburban Sacrifice: 'Altars of soil and grain—Grand Victim.'

entries.zh: 必援一牢之文，以明社之無二，則稷無牲矣。
entries.en: Must cite the text of one victim to show the altar of Earth has not two—then the god of grain has no victim.
entries.literal: Must cite the text of one victim to show the altar of Earth has not two— then the god of grain has no victim.

entries.zh: 說者則曰，舉社以明稷。
entries.en: Expositors then say: one cites the altar of Earth in order to clarify the god of grain.
entries.literal: Expositors then say: cite the altar of Earth to clarify the god of grain.

entries.zh: 苟可舉社以明稷，何獨不可舉一以明二。
entries.en: If one may cite the altar of Earth to clarify the god of grain—why alone may one not cite one to clarify two?
entries.literal: If one may cite the altar of Earth to clarify the god of grain— why alone may one not cite one to clarify two?

entries.zh: 『國之大事，在祀與戎』。
entries.en: "The great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war."
entries.literal: "The great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war."

entries.zh: 若有過而除之，不若過而存之。
entries.en: If there is excess and one removes it—better excess and preserve it.
entries.literal: If there is excess and one removes it— better excess and preserve it.

entries.zh: 況存之有義，而除之無據乎。
entries.en: How much more so when preservation has principle and removal lacks evidence?
entries.literal: How much more when preservation has principle and removal lacks evidence?

entries.zh: 周禮封人『掌設社壝』。
entries.en: The Rites of Zhou, Border Officer, states: 'He presides over setting up the altar platform of Earth.'
entries.literal: The Rites of Zhou, Border Officer, states: 'He presides over setting up the altar platform of Earth.'

entries.zh: 無稷字。
entries.en: There is no character for the god of grain.
entries.literal: There is no character for god of grain.

entries.zh: 今帝社無稷，蓋出於此。
entries.en: Now the imperial altar of Earth has no god of grain—probably arising from this.
entries.literal: Now the imperial altar of Earth has no god of grain— probably arising from this.

entries.zh: 然國主社稷，故經傳動稱社稷。
entries.en: Yet the state takes lordship of the altars of soil and grain—therefore classics and commentaries often say altars of soil and grain together.
entries.literal: Yet the state takes lordship of the altars of soil and grain— therefore classics and commentaries often say altars of soil and grain together.

entries.zh: 周禮，王祭稷則絺冕。
entries.en: The Rites of Zhou: when the king sacrifices to the god of grain, he wears the xi sacrificial cap.
entries.literal: The Rites of Zhou: when the king sacrifices to the god of grain he wears the xi sacrificial cap.

entries.zh: 此王社有稷之文也。
entries.en: This is textual evidence that the King's Altar of Earth has a god of grain.
entries.literal: This is text that the King's Altar of Earth has a god of grain.

entries.zh: 封人設壝之無稷字，說者以為略文，從可知也。
entries.en: The Border Officer setting the platform lacking the character for god of grain—expositors hold this abbreviated text; from this it may be known.
entries.literal: The Border Officer setting the platform lacking the character for god of grain— expositors hold this abbreviated text; from this it may be known.

entries.zh: 謂宜仍舊立二社，而加立帝社之稷。」
entries.en: I hold that one should still establish two altars of Earth as before, and additionally establish the god of grain at the Imperial Altar of Earth."
entries.literal: I hold that one should still establish two altars of Earth as before, and additionally establish the god of grain at the Imperial Altar of Earth."

entries.zh: 時成粲議稱：「景侯論太社不立京都，欲破鄭氏學。」
entries.en: At that time Cheng Can deliberated: "Jinghou's discussion that the Grand Altar of Earth is not established in the capital—wishes to break Master Zheng's school."
entries.literal: At that time Cheng Can deliberated: "Jinghou's discussion that the Grand Altar of Earth is not established in the capital—wishes to break Master Zheng's school."

entries.zh: 咸重表以為：「如粲之論，景侯之解文以此壞。
entries.en: Xian resubmitted the memorial: "Following Can's discussion—Jinghou's exegesis is destroyed on this point.
entries.literal: Xian resubmitted the memorial: "Following Can's discussion— Jinghou's exegesis is destroyed on this point.

entries.zh: 大雅云：『乃立冢土。』
entries.en: The Great Odes state: 'Then he established the mound of earth.'
entries.literal: The Great Odes state: 'Then he established the mound of earth.'

entries.zh: 毛公解曰：『冢土，太社也。』
entries.en: Mao's commentary says: 'Mound of earth—the Grand Altar of Earth.'
entries.literal: Mao's commentary says: 'Mound of earth—the Grand Altar of Earth.'

entries.zh: 景侯解詩，即用此說。
entries.en: In Jinghou's explanation of the Odes, he uses this doctrine.
entries.literal: Jinghou explaining the Odes uses this doctrine.

entries.zh: 禹貢『惟土五色』。
entries.en: The Tribute of Yu states: 'Only the five colors of earth.'
entries.literal: The Tribute of Yu states: 'Only the five colors of earth.'

entries.zh: 景侯解曰：『王者取五色土為太社，封四方諸侯。
entries.en: Jinghou explains: 'The king takes five-colored earth for the Grand Altar of Earth and enfeoffs the feudal lords of the four directions with it.
entries.literal: Jinghou explains: 'The king takes five-colored earth for the Grand Altar of Earth and enfeoffs the feudal lords of the four directions.

entries.zh: 各割其方色土者覆四方也。』
entries.en: Each cuts earth of his direction's color in order to cover the four directions.'
entries.literal: Each cuts earth of his direction's color in order to cover the four directions.'

entries.zh: 如此，太社復為立京都也。
entries.en: Thus the Grand Altar of Earth is again established in the capital.
entries.literal: Thus the Grand Altar of Earth is again established in the capital.

entries.zh: 不知此論從何出而與解乖。
entries.en: I do not know whence this discussion arose, yet it contradicts the explanation.
entries.literal: I do not know whence this discussion arose yet it contradicts the explanation.

entries.zh: 上違經記明文，下壞景侯之解。
entries.en: Above it violates explicit text in the classics; below it undermines Jinghou's explanation.
entries.literal: Above it violates explicit text in the classics; below it destroys Jinghou's explanation.

entries.zh: 臣雖頑蔽，少長學問，不能默已，謹復續上。」
entries.en: Your subject, though dull and obscured, having studied from youth, cannot remain silent—respectfully resubmitting."
entries.literal: Your subject, though dull and obscured, having studied from youth, cannot remain silent—respectfully resubmitting."

entries.zh: 劉寔與咸議同。
entries.en: Liu Shi concurred with Xian's deliberation.
entries.literal: Liu Shi agreed with Xian's deliberation.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「社實一神，而相襲二位，眾議不同，何必改作，其便仍舊，一如魏制。」
entries.en: An edict stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit, yet two positions are inherited in succession; the collective deliberations differ—why must it be changed? For convenience retain the former practice, exactly as Wei regulations."
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The altar of Earth is truly one spirit, yet two positions are inherited in succession; the collective deliberations differ— why must it be changed? For convenience retain the former practice, exactly as Wei regulations."

entries.zh: 漢東海恭王薨，明帝出幸津門亭發哀。
entries.en: When Prince Gong of Donghai died in Han, Emperor Ming went out to Jinmen Pavilion to express mourning.
entries.literal: When Prince Gong of Donghai in Han died, Emperor Ming went out to Jinmen Pavilion to express mourning.

entries.zh: 魏時會喪及使者弔祭，用博士杜希議，皆去玄冠，加以布巾。
entries.en: In Wei times at assembly mourning and when envoys performed condolence sacrifice—following Erudite Du Xi's deliberation—all removed the black cap and added cloth headcloth.
entries.literal: In Wei times at assembly mourning and when envoys performed condolence sacrifice— following Erudite Du Xi's deliberation— all removed the black cap and added cloth headcloth.

entries.zh: 宋文帝元嘉三年五月庚午，以誅徐羨之等，讎恥已雪，幣告太廟。
entries.en: On the gengwu day of the fifth month in the third year of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen of Song announced to the Imperial Ancestral Temple that Xu Xianzhi and his associates had been executed and the blood-debt finally avenged.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day of the fifth month of the third year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, because Xu Xianzhi and others had been executed and the grievance and shame had been avenged, silk offerings were announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 漢末吳人陸績善天文，始推渾天意。
entries.en: Near the end of Han, Lu Ji of Wu, an expert in astronomy, was the first to work out the Huntian theory in full.
entries.literal: At the end of Han, Lu Ji of Wu was skilled in astronomy and was the first to develop the meaning of Huntian.

entries.zh: 王蕃者，盧江人，吳時為中常侍，善數術，傳劉洪《乾象曆》。
entries.en: Wang Fan came from Lujiang; under Wu he served as Regular Palace Attendant, excelled in mathematical astronomy, and carried on Liu Hong's Supernal Signs Calendar.
entries.literal: Wang Fan was a man of Lujiang; in Wu times he served as Regular Palace Attendant, was skilled in numerology, and transmitted Liu Hong's Supernal Signs Calendar.

entries.zh: 依《乾象法》而制渾儀，立論考度曰：
entries.en: On the Supernal Signs method he built an armillary sphere and drafted a treatise on measurement that begins:
entries.literal: Following the method of the Supernal Signs, he made a armillary sphere and set forth a treatise on measurement, saying:

entries.zh: 三光之行，不必有常，術家以算求之，各有同異，故諸家曆法參差不齊。
entries.en: Sun, moon, and stars do not move by fixed rules; mathematicians derive their paths by calculation, and schools disagree—hence calendars diverge.
entries.literal: The motion of the three luminaries is not necessarily constant; numerologists calculate them by computation, each with agreements and differences—hence the calendrical methods of the various schools are uneven and do not align.

entries.zh: 《洛書甄耀度》、《春秋考異郵》皆云周天一百七萬一千里，一度為二千九百三十二里七十一步二尺七寸四分四百八十七分分之三百六十二。
entries.en: The Radiance of Degrees and the Examination of Strange Correspondences both give Heaven's circuit as 1,071,000 li and one degree as 2,932 li plus 71 paces, 2 chi, 7 cun, 4 fen, and 362/487 of a fen.
entries.literal: The Luo shu Radiance of Degrees and Spring and Autumn Examination of Strange Correspondences both say the circuit of Heaven is 1,071,000 li; one degree is 2,932 li, 71 bu, 2 chi, 7 cun, 4 fen, and 362 parts in 487 fen.

entries.zh: 陸績云：天東西南北徑三十五萬七千里，此言周三徑一也。
entries.en: Lu Ji held that Heaven's diameter is 357,000 li, assuming the classic ratio of circumference three to diameter one.
entries.literal: Lu Ji said: Heaven's diameter east-west and north-south is 357,000 li—this speaks of circumference three, diameter one.

entries.zh: 考之徑一不啻周三，率周百四十二而徑四十五，則天徑三十三萬九千四百一里一百二十二步三尺二寸一分七十一分分之九。
entries.en: On examination, the ratio is not three to one; with circumference 142 to diameter 45, Heaven's diameter comes to 339,401 li, 122 paces, 3 chi, 2 cun, 1 fen, and 9/71 of a fen.
entries.literal: Examined, diameter one is not merely circumference three; with the ratio circumference 142 to diameter 45, Heaven's diameter is 339,401 li, 122 bu, 3 chi, 2 cun, 1 fen, and 9 parts in 71 fen.

entries.zh: 以句股法言之，傍萬五千里，句也；
entries.en: In right-triangle terms, the 15,000-li horizontal leg is the gou;
entries.literal: Speaking in terms of the gou-gu method, the side of 15,000 li is the gou;

entries.zh: 立八萬里，股也；
entries.en: the 80,000-li vertical leg is the gu;
entries.literal: the upright of 80,000 li is the gu;

entries.zh: 從日邪射陽城，弦也。
entries.en: the slanting ray to Yangcheng is the hypotenuse.
entries.literal: from the sun's oblique rays on Yangcheng is the xian.

entries.zh: 以句股求弦法入之，得八萬一千三百九十四里三十步五尺三寸六分，天徑之半，而地上去天之數也。
entries.en: By the Pythagorean method the hypotenuse comes to 81,394 li, 30 paces, 5 chi, 3 cun, 6 fen—half Heaven's diameter, the height from Earth to the sun.
entries.literal: Applying the gou-gu method to find the xian, one obtains 81,394 li, 30 bu, 5 chi, 3 cun, 6 fen—half Heaven's diameter, and the number of li from the ground up to Heaven.

entries.zh: 倍之，得十六萬二千七百八十八里六十一步四尺七寸二分，天徑之數也。
entries.en: Doubled, that gives 162,788 li, 61 paces, 4 chi, 7 cun, 2 fen for Heaven's full diameter.
entries.literal: Doubled, this yields 162,788 li, 61 bu, 4 chi, 7 cun, 2 fen—the number of Heaven's diameter.

entries.zh: 以周率乘之，徑率約之，得五十一萬三千六百八十七里六十八步一尺八寸二分，周天之數也。
entries.en: Multiplying by pi and reducing by the diameter ratio yields 513,687 li, 68 paces, 1 chi, 8 cun, 2 fen for Heaven's circumference.
entries.literal: Multiplying by the circumference ratio and reducing by the diameter ratio, one obtains 513,687 li, 68 bu, 1 chi, 8 cun, 2 fen—the number of Heaven's circuit.

entries.zh: 減《甄耀度》、《考異郵》五十五萬七千三百一十二里有奇。
entries.en: That is 557,312-odd li less than the figures in those two texts.
entries.literal: This is 557,312 and a fraction li less than the Radiance of Degrees and Examination of Strange Correspondences.

entries.zh: 一度凡千四百六里百二十四步六寸四分十萬七千五百六十五分分之萬九千三十九，減舊度千五百二十五里二百五十六步三尺三寸二十一萬五千一百三十分分之十六萬七百三十分。
entries.en: One degree equals 1,406 li, 124 paces, 6 cun, 4 fen, and 19,039/107,565 of a fen—1,525 li, 256 paces, 3 chi, 3 cun, and 167,030/215,130 of a fen shorter than the older reckoning.
entries.literal: One degree totals 1,406 li, 124 bu, 6 cun, 4 fen, and 19,039 parts in 107,565 fen—1,525 li, 256 bu, 3 chi, 3 cun, and 167,030 parts in 215,130 fen less than the old degree.

entries.zh: 黃赤二道，相與交錯，其間相去二十四度。
entries.en: The ecliptic and equator cross at an angle of 24 degrees.
entries.literal: The Yellow and Red roads cross each other; the distance between them is 24 degrees.

entries.zh: 以兩儀推之，二道俱三百六十五度有奇，是以知天體圓如彈丸。
entries.en: Both circles measure 365-odd degrees by the two-armillary method—proof that Heaven is a perfect sphere.
entries.literal: Deducing from the two markers, both roads are 365 and a fraction degrees—hence we know Heaven's body is round like a pellet.

entries.zh: 而陸績造渾象，其形如鳥卵，然則黃道應長於赤道矣。
entries.en: Yet Lu Ji's globe was egg-shaped, which would make the ecliptic longer than the equator.
entries.literal: Yet Lu Ji made a armillary globe whose form is like a bird's egg—then the Yellow Road ought to be longer than the Red Road.

entries.zh: 績云天東西南北徑三十五萬七千里，然則績亦以天形正圓也。
entries.en: Lu Ji gave Heaven a diameter of 357,000 li, so he too treated the sky as a true sphere.
entries.literal: Ji said Heaven's diameter east-west and north-south is 357,000 li—thus Ji also held Heaven's form to be perfectly round.

entries.zh: 而渾象為鳥卵，則為自相違背。
entries.en: An egg-shaped globe contradicts that assumption.
entries.literal: Yet the armillary globe is a bird's egg—this contradicts itself.

entries.zh: 史臣案：設器象，定其恆度，合之則吉，失之則凶，以之占察，有何不可。
entries.en: The historiographer notes: A model with fixed degrees that match heaven brings good fortune and mismatch brings ill—why should observation be impossible?
entries.literal: The historiographer comments: Set up an instrument's image, fix its constant degrees—when they match, auspicious; when they miss, inauspicious; to use it for observation and divination—what could be impossible?

entries.zh: 渾文廢絕，故有宣、蓋之論，其術並疏，故後人莫述。
entries.en: With Huntian texts lost, Xuanye and Gaitian theories survived, but both are crude and later scholars abandoned them.
entries.literal: Huntian texts were abandoned and lost, hence there are Xuanye and Gaitian theories; their methods are all loose, hence later men do not expound them.

entries.zh: 揚雄《法言》云：「或人問渾天於雄。
entries.en: Yang Xiong's Fayan records: "Someone asked him about Huntian.
entries.literal: Yang Xiong's Fayan says: "Someone asked Xiong about Huntian.

entries.zh: 雄曰：'落下閎營之，鮮于妄人度之，耿中丞象之，幾乎莫之違也'。」
entries.en: He answered: 'Luo Xiahong designed it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, Censor Geng modeled it—hardly a point of dispute.'"
entries.literal: Xiong said: 'Luo Xiahong planned it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, Censor-in-Chief Geng modeled it—almost nothing contradicts it.'"

entries.zh: 若問天形定體，渾儀疏密，則雄應以渾儀答之，而舉此三人以對者，則知此三人製造渾儀，以圖晷緯。
entries.en: Had the question been Heaven's shape or the instrument's scale, he would have described the armillary itself; naming these three men shows they built it to map the gnomon shadow and the celestial warp.
entries.literal: If one asked about Heaven's fixed form or the armillary's density, Xiong should have answered with the armillary; yet he named these three men in reply—hence we know these three made the armillary to chart the gnomon and the warp.

entries.zh: 問者蓋渾儀之疏密，非問渾儀之淺深也。
entries.en: The question concerned the instrument's precision, not cosmological depth.
entries.literal: The questioner was probably asking about the armillary's density, not the armillary's depth.

entries.zh: 以此而推，則西漢長安已有其器矣。
entries.en: On this basis the armillary existed in Western Han Chang'an.
entries.literal: Deducing from this, Western Han Chang'an already had this instrument.

entries.zh: 將由喪亂亡失，故衡復鑄之乎？
entries.en: Did Zhang Heng recast it only because war had destroyed the original?
entries.literal: Was it because turmoil and loss destroyed it, that Heng recast it?

entries.zh: 王蕃又記古渾儀尺度並張衡改制之文，則知斯器非衡始造，明矣。
entries.en: Wang Fan's record of earlier dimensions and Zhang Heng's redesign proves Heng did not invent the armillary.
entries.literal: Wang Fan also recorded the ancient armillary's dimensions and the text of Zhang Heng's remaking—hence we know clearly this instrument was not first made by Heng.

entries.zh: 衡所造渾儀，傳至魏、晉，中華覆敗，沈沒戎虜；
entries.en: Heng's armillary passed to Wei and Jin, then was lost when China fell to the barbarians;
entries.literal: The armillary Heng made was transmitted to Wei and Jin; China fell in ruin and sank among the barbarians;

entries.zh: 績、蕃舊器，亦不復存。
entries.en: and the globes of Lu Ji and Wang Fan vanished as well.
entries.literal: the old instruments of Ji and Fan also no longer survive.

entries.zh: 晉安帝義熙十四年，高祖平長安，得衡舊器，儀狀雖舉，不綴經星七曜。
entries.en: In Yixi year 14 the High Ancestor took Chang'an and recovered Heng's armillary, but its fixed stars and planets no longer aligned.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Emperor An's Yixi era, the High Ancestor pacified Chang'an and obtained Heng's old instrument; though its form was raised, it did not link the fixed stars and seven luminaries.

entries.zh: 黃初四年三月癸卯，月犯心大星。
entries.en: the fourth year of Huangchu, third month, day guimao: the moon crossed the great star of Heart.
entries.literal: Huangchu year 4, third month, day guimao: the moon encroached on the great star of Heart.

entries.zh: 十二月丙子，月又犯心大星。
entries.en: Twelfth month, day bingzi: the moon again crossed the great star of Heart.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, day bingzi: the moon again encroached on the great star of Heart.

entries.zh: 占曰：「心為天王，王者惡之。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Heart is the celestial king—rulers dread its violation."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Heart is the celestial king—rulers dread it."

entries.zh: 七年五月，文帝崩。
entries.en: In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died.

entries.zh: 黃初四年六月甲申，太白晝見。
entries.en: the fourth year of Huangchu, sixth month, day jiashen: Venus appeared in daylight.
entries.literal: Huangchu year 4, sixth month, day jiashen: Great White was seen in daylight.

entries.zh: 五年十一月辛卯，太白又晝見。
entries.en: In the fifth year, on the xinmao day of the eleventh month, Venus again appeared in daylight.
entries.literal: Year 5, eleventh month, day xinmao: Great White was again seen in daylight.

entries.zh: 案劉向《五紀論》曰：「太白少陰，弱，不得專行，故以己未為界，不得經天而行。
entries.en: Liu Xiang's Five Regulators Treatise explains: "Venus is lesser yin and weak, unable to travel alone; bounded by ji and wei it cannot cross the sky.
entries.literal: Examining Liu Xiang's Five Regulators Treatise: "Great White is lesser yin, weak, and cannot travel alone; hence with ji-wei as its boundary it cannot cross heaven and travel.

entries.zh: 經天則晝見，其占為兵，為喪，為不臣，為更王。
entries.en: When it crosses the sky it appears by day, portending war, mourning, treason, and dynastic change.
entries.literal: When it crosses heaven it is seen by day; its prognostication is war, mourning, disloyal ministers, and change of kings.

entries.zh: 強國弱，小國強。」
entries.en: Great powers weaken while lesser ones grow strong."
entries.literal: Strong states weaken; small states strengthen."

entries.zh: 是時，孫權受魏爵號，而稱兵距守。
entries.en: Sun Quan had accepted Wei titles yet took up arms and held his ground.
entries.literal: At that time Sun Quan had received Wei's enfeoffment and title, yet raised troops and held out in resistance.

entries.zh: 七年五月，文帝崩。
entries.en: In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died.

entries.zh: 八月，吳遂圍江夏，寇襄陽，魏江夏太守文聘固守得全。
entries.en: In the eighth month Wu besieged Jiangxia and raided Xiangyang; Wei's Wen Pin, Administrator of Jiangxia, held the city intact.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Wu then besieged Jiangxia and raided Xiangyang; Wei's Administrator of Jiangxia Wen Pin held firm and preserved the city.

entries.zh: 大將軍司馬懿救襄陽，斬吳將張霸。
entries.en: Grand General Sima Yi relieved Xiangyang and killed Wu's Zhang Ba.
entries.literal: Grand General Sima Yi relieved Xiangyang and beheaded Wu's general Zhang Ba.

entries.zh: 魏明帝太和四年十一月壬戌，太白犯歲星。
entries.en: Wei Emperor Ming, Taihe 4, eleventh month, day renxu: Venus crossed Jupiter.
entries.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Taihe year 4, eleventh month, day renxu: Great White encroached on the Year Star.

entries.zh: 占曰：「太白犯五星，有大兵；
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "When Venus crosses a planet, major war erupts;
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "When Great White encroaches on the five stars, there is great warfare;

entries.zh: 犯列宿，為小兵。」
entries.en: crossing a constellation lodge means lesser conflict."
entries.literal: encroaching on listed lodges means small warfare."

entries.zh: 五年三月，諸葛亮以大眾寇天水，遣大將軍司馬懿距退之。
entries.en: Taihe 5, third month: Zhuge Liang attacked Tianshui with a large force; Grand General Sima Yi was dispatched and drove him back.
entries.literal: Year 5, third month, Zhuge Liang with a great host raided Tianshui; Grand General Sima Yi was sent to repel and drive him back.

entries.zh: 太和五年五月，熒惑犯房。
entries.en: Taihe 5, fifth month: Mars crossed Encampment.
entries.literal: Taihe year 5, fifth month: Sparkling Deluder encroached on Encampment.

entries.zh: 占曰：「房四星，股肱臣將相位也。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Encampment's four stars govern the ruler's chief ministers and the posts of general and chancellor.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The four stars of Encampment are the limb-and-bone ministers and the rank of general and chancellor.

entries.zh: 月五星犯守之，將相有憂。」
entries.en: When the moon or planets cross or hold it, generals and chancellors face danger."
entries.literal: When the moon and five planets encroach on or guard it, generals and chancellors have anxiety."

entries.zh: 七月，車騎將軍張郃追諸葛亮，為其所害。
entries.en: In the seventh month Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was slain.
entries.literal: Seventh month, Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was killed by him.

entries.zh: 十二月，太尉華歆薨。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.

entries.zh: 太和五年十一月乙酉，月犯軒轅大星。
entries.en: Taihe 5, eleventh month, day yiyou: the moon crossed the great star of Chariot Pivot.
entries.literal: Taihe year 5, eleventh month, day yiyou: the moon encroached on the great star of Chariot Pivot.

entries.zh: 占曰：「女主憂。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The empress faces danger."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The chief consort has anxiety."

entries.zh: 十二月甲辰，月犯鎮星。
entries.en: Twelfth month, day jiachen: the moon crossed Saturn.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, day jiachen: the moon encroached on Quelling Star.

entries.zh: 占曰：「女主當之。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The empress will suffer the blow."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The chief consort will bear it."

entries.zh: 六年三月乙亥，月又犯軒轅大星。
entries.en: Taihe 6, third month, day yihai: the moon again crossed the great star of Chariot Pivot.
entries.literal: Year 6, third month, day yihai: the moon again encroached on the great star of Chariot Pivot.

entries.zh: 青龍二年十一月乙丑，月又犯鎮星。
entries.en: Qinglong 2, eleventh month, day yichou: the moon again crossed Saturn.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 2, eleventh month, day yichou: the moon again encroached on Quelling Star.

entries.zh: 三年正月，太后郭氏崩。
entries.en: Qinglong 3, first month: Empress Dowager Guo died.
entries.literal: Year 3, first month, Empress Dowager Guo died.

entries.zh: 太和六年十一月丙寅，太白晝見南斗，遂歷八十餘日恒見。
entries.en: Taihe 6, eleventh month, day bingyin: Venus appeared in daylight at Southern Dipper and stayed visible for more than eighty days.
entries.literal: Taihe year 6, eleventh month, day bingyin: Great White was seen in daylight at Southern Dipper and remained constantly visible for more than eighty days.

entries.zh: 占曰：「吳有兵。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Wu will see war".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Wu has warfare".

entries.zh: 明年，孫權遣張彌等將兵萬人，錫授公孫淵為燕王。
entries.en: The next year Sun Quan sent Zhang Mi and others with ten thousand men to enfeoff Gongsun Yuan as King of Yan.
entries.literal: " The next year Sun Quan sent Zhang Mi and others with ten thousand troops to invest Gongsun Yuan as King of Yan.

entries.zh: 淵斬彌等，虜其眾。
entries.en: Yuan killed Mi and his party and seized their troops.
entries.literal: Yuan beheaded Mi and the others and captured their forces.

entries.zh: 太和六年十一月丙寅，有星孛于翼，近太微上將星。
entries.en: Taihe 6, eleventh month, day bingyin: a comet appeared at Wings, near the General-in-Chief star of Supreme Subtlety.
entries.literal: Taihe year 6, eleventh month, day bingyin: a broom star appeared at Wings, near Supreme Subtlety's General-in-Chief star.

entries.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning".

entries.zh: 甘氏曰：「孛彗所當之國，是受其殃。」
entries.en: Master Gan says: "The state a comet strikes receives its calamity".
entries.literal: " Master Gan says: "The state struck by a broom or comet receives its calamity.

entries.zh: 翼又楚分，孫權封略也。
entries.en: Wings also marks Chu—Sun Quan's domain.
entries.literal: " Wings is also Chu's allotted field—Sun Quan's territorial domain.

entries.zh: 明年，權有遼東之敗。
entries.en: The next year Quan met defeat in Liaodong.
entries.literal: The next year Quan suffered defeat in Liaodong.

entries.zh: 權又自向合肥新城，遣全琮征六安，皆不克而還。
entries.en: Quan also marched on Hefei New City in person and sent Quan Cong against Lu'an; both failed and withdrew.
entries.literal: Quan also advanced in person toward Hefei New City and sent Quan Cong to campaign against Lu'an; neither succeeded and both returned.

entries.zh: 又明年，諸葛亮入秦川，據渭南，司馬懿距之。
entries.en: The following year Zhuge Liang entered Qinchuan, held the south Wei River, and Sima Yi opposed him.
entries.literal: The year after that Zhuge Liang entered Qinchuan, held the south bank of the Wei River, and Sima Yi opposed him.

entries.zh: 孫權遣陸議、諸葛瑾等屯江夏口，孫韶、張承等向廣陵淮陽，權以大眾圍新城以應亮。
entries.en: Sun Quan sent Lu Xun, Zhuge Jin, and others to hold Jiangxia Ford; Sun Shao, Zhang Cheng, and others toward Guangling and Huaiyang; and Quan himself besieged New City in support of Liang.
entries.literal: Sun Quan sent Lu Yi, Zhuge Jin, and others to encamp at Jiangxia Ford; Sun Shao, Zhang Cheng, and others advanced toward Guangling and Huaiyang; Quan with a great host besieged New City to support Liang.

entries.zh: 於是帝自東征，權及諸將乃退。
entries.en: The emperor then marched east in person, and Quan and his commanders withdrew.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor campaigned east in person, and Quan and his generals withdrew.

entries.zh: 太和六年十二月，陳王植薨。
entries.en: Taihe 6, twelfth month: Prince of Chen Zhi died.
entries.literal: Taihe year 6, twelfth month: Prince of Chen Zhi died.

entries.zh: 青龍元年夏，北海王蕤薨。
entries.en: Qinglong 1, summer: Prince of Beihai Rui died.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 1, summer: Prince of Beihai Rui died.

entries.zh: 三年正月，太后郭氏崩。
entries.en: Qinglong 3, first month: Empress Dowager Guo died.
entries.literal: Year 3, first month: Empress Dowager Guo died.

entries.zh: 明帝青龍二年二月己未，太白犯熒惑。
entries.en: Emperor Ming, Qinglong 2, second month, day jiwei: Venus crossed Mars.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming, Qinglong year 2, second month, day jiwei: Great White encroached on Sparkling Deluder.

entries.zh: 占曰：「大兵起，有大戰。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Major war erupts; a great battle follows."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Great warfare rises; there is a great battle."

entries.zh: 是年四月，諸葛亮據渭南，吳亦起兵應之，魏東西奔命。
entries.en: That year in the fourth month Zhuge Liang held the south Wei River; Wu mobilized in support, and Wei rushed troops east and west.
entries.literal: That year, fourth month, Zhuge Liang held the south bank of the Wei River; Wu also raised troops in response, and Wei raced east and west to answer both.

entries.zh: 九月，亮卒，軍退，將帥分爭，為魏所破。
entries.en: In the ninth month Liang died; the army retreated, its commanders turned on one another, and Wei crushed them.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Liang died; the army withdrew, commanders quarreled among themselves, and were defeated by Wei.

entries.zh: 案占，太白所犯在南，南國敗，在北，北國敗，此宜在熒惑南也。
entries.en: Per the texts, when Venus strikes a target in the south the southern state falls, in the north the northern state falls—and here Venus should have lain south of Mars.
entries.literal: Examining prognostication: wherever Great White encroaches, if in the south the southern state is defeated, if in the north the northern state is defeated—here it should have been south of Sparkling Deluder.

entries.zh: 青龍二年三月辛卯，月犯輿鬼。
entries.en: Qinglong 2, third month, day xinmao: the moon crossed Carriage Ghost.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 2, third month, day xinmao: the moon encroached on Carriage Ghost.

entries.zh: 輿鬼主斬殺。
entries.en: Carriage Ghost governs execution and slaughter.
entries.literal: Carriage Ghost governs beheading and slaying.

entries.zh: 占曰：「民多病，國有憂，又有大臣憂。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The people sicken widely; the state and its senior ministers face disaster."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The people have much illness; the state has anxiety, and great ministers have anxiety too."

entries.zh: 是年夏，大疫；
entries.en: That summer a great plague struck;
entries.literal: That year in summer, great pestilence;

entries.zh: 冬，又大病，至三年春乃止。
entries.en: in winter another wave of disease raged until it abated in the spring of year three.
entries.literal: in winter, again great illness, until spring of year 3 it ceased.

entries.zh: 正月，太后郭氏崩。
entries.en: In the first month Empress Dowager Guo died.
entries.literal: First month, Empress Dowager Guo died.

entries.zh: 四年五月，司徒董昭薨。
entries.en: Qinglong 4, fifth month: Minister of Works Dong Zhao died.
entries.literal: Year 4, fifth month, Minister of Works Dong Zhao died.

entries.zh: 青龍二年五月丁亥，太白晝見，積三十餘日。
entries.en: Qinglong 2, fifth month, day dinghai: Venus appeared in daylight for more than thirty days.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 2, fifth month, day dinghai: Great White was seen in daylight, lasting more than thirty days accumulated.

entries.zh: 以晷度推之，非秦、魏，則楚也。
entries.en: By gnomon reckoning the omen fell not on Qin or Wei but on Chu.
entries.literal: Calculating by gnomon and degree, if not Qin or Wei, then it is Chu.

entries.zh: 是時諸葛亮據渭南，司馬懿與相持。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang held the south Wei River while Sima Yi locked horns with him.
entries.literal: At that time Zhuge Liang held the south bank of the Wei River; Sima Yi faced him in stalemate.

entries.zh: 孫權寇合肥，又遣陸議、孫韶等入淮、沔，帝親東征。
entries.en: Sun Quan attacked Hefei and sent Lu Xun, Sun Shao, and others against the Huai and Han; the emperor marched east in person.
entries.literal: Sun Quan raided Hefei; he also sent Lu Yi, Sun Shao, and others into the Huai and Han rivers; the emperor personally campaigned east.

entries.zh: 蜀本秦地，則為秦、晉及楚兵悉起應占。
entries.en: Shu lay in the old Qin domain, and armies of Qin, Jin, and Chu all took the field in fulfillment of the omen.
entries.literal: Shu is originally Qin territory; thus the armies of Qin, Jin, and Chu all rose, answering the prognostication.

entries.zh: 青龍二年七月己巳，月犯楗閉。
entries.en: Qinglong 2, seventh month, day jisi: the moon crossed Door Bolt.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 2, seventh month, day jisi: the moon encroached on Door Bolt.

entries.zh: 占曰：「天子崩，又為火災。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The emperor dies; fire disaster follows."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The Son of Heaven dies; moreover there is fire disaster."

entries.zh: 三年七月，崇華殿災。
entries.en: Qinglong 3, seventh month: Chonghua Palace burned.
entries.literal: Year 3, seventh month, the Chonghua Palace suffered fire.

entries.zh: 景初三年正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 青龍二年十月戊寅，月犯太白。
entries.en: Qinglong 2, tenth month, day wuyin: the moon crossed Venus.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 2, tenth month, day wuyin: the moon encroached on Great White.

entries.zh: 占曰：「人君死，又為兵。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The ruler dies; war follows."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The ruler dies; moreover there is warfare."

entries.zh: 景初元年七月，公孫淵叛。
entries.en: Jingchu 1, seventh month: Gongsun Yuan rebelled.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 1, seventh month, Gongsun Yuan rebelled.

entries.zh: 二年正月，遣司馬懿討之。
entries.en: Jingchu 2, first month: Sima Yi was dispatched to suppress him.
entries.literal: Year 2, first month, Sima Yi was sent to attack him.

entries.zh: 三年正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: Year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年六月丁未，鎮星犯井鉞。
entries.en: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong 3, sixth month, day dingwei: Saturn crossed Well Axe.
entries.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong year 3, sixth month, day dingwei: Quelling Star encroached on Well Axe.

entries.zh: 四年閏四月乙巳，復犯。
entries.en: Qinglong 4, intercalary fourth month, day yisi: it crossed again.
entries.literal: Year 4, intercalary fourth month, day yisi: again encroached.

entries.zh: 戊戌，太白又犯。
entries.en: Day wuxu: Venus crossed it again.
entries.literal: Day wuxu, Great White again encroached.

entries.zh: 占曰：「凡月五星犯井鉞，悉為兵起。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Whenever the moon or planets cross Well Axe, war erupts."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Whenever the moon or five planets encroach on Well Axe, all signify warfare rising."

entries.zh: 一曰：「斧鉞用，大臣誅。」
entries.en: Another reading: "The axes are drawn; great ministers are put to death."
entries.literal: Another reading says: "Axe and halberd are deployed; great ministers are executed."

entries.zh: 景初元年，公孫淵叛，司馬懿討滅之。
entries.en: In Jingchu 1 Gongsun Yuan rebelled and Sima Yi crushed him.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 1, Gongsun Yuan rebelled; Sima Yi attacked and destroyed him.

entries.zh: 青龍三年七月己丑，鎮星犯東井。
entries.en: Qinglong 3, seventh month, day jichou: Saturn crossed Eastern Well.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 3, seventh month, day jichou: Quelling Star encroached on Eastern Well.

entries.zh: 四年三月癸卯，在參，又還犯之。
entries.en: Qinglong 4, third month, day guimao: while in Three Stars it swung back and crossed again.
entries.literal: Year 4, third month, day guimao: in Three Stars, again returned and encroached on it.

entries.zh: 占曰：「鎮星入井，大人憂。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "When Saturn enters the Well, exalted persons face disaster.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "When Quelling Star enters the Well, great persons have anxiety.

entries.zh: 行近距為行陰，其占大水，五穀不成。」
entries.en: Drawing near is called traveling in yin, portending great floods and failed harvests."
entries.literal: Traveling near and close is traveling yin; its prognostication is great flood, the five grains do not ripen."

entries.zh: 景初元年夏，大水，傷五穀。
entries.en: Jingchu 1 summer brought catastrophic floods that ruined the crops.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 1 summer, great flood, damaging the five grains.

entries.zh: 九月，皇后毛氏崩。
entries.en: In the ninth month Empress Mao died.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Empress Mao died.

entries.zh: 三年正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: Year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 青龍三年十月壬申，太白晝見在尾，曆二百餘日恆見。
entries.en: Qinglong 3, tenth month, day renshen: Venus appeared by day in Tail and remained visible for more than two hundred days.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 3, tenth month, day renshen: Great White was seen in daylight in Tail, passing more than two hundred days constantly visible.

entries.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，燕臣強，有兵。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Tail corresponds to Yan—Yan's ministers grow strong and war follows."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Tail is Yan; Yan's ministers are strong; there is warfare."

entries.zh: 青龍四年三月己巳，太白與月俱加丙，晝見。
entries.en: Qinglong 4, third month, day jisi: Venus and the moon both reached the bing quadrant and shone by day.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 4, third month, day jisi: Great White and the moon together reached bing, seen in daylight.

entries.zh: 月犯太白。
entries.en: The moon crossed Venus.
entries.literal: The moon encroached on Great White.

entries.zh: 景初元年七月辛卯，太白又晝見，積二百八十餘日。
entries.en: Jingchu 1, seventh month, day xinmao: Venus again appeared by day for more than 280 days.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 1, seventh month, day xinmao: Great White was again seen in daylight, accumulating more than 280 days.

entries.zh: 占悉同上。
entries.en: The prognostications matched those above.
entries.literal: All prognostications were the same as above.

entries.zh: 是時公孫淵自立為燕王，署置百官，發兵距守，遣司馬懿討滅之。
entries.en: Gongsun Yuan had declared himself King of Yan, installed a full court, and mobilized for defense until Sima Yi was sent and destroyed him.
entries.literal: At that time Gongsun Yuan declared himself King of Yan, appointed the hundred officials, raised troops to hold out in defense; Sima Yi was sent to attack and destroy him.

entries.zh: 青龍三年十二月戊辰，月犯鉤鈐。
entries.en: Qinglong 3, twelfth month, day wuchen: the moon crossed Hooked Halberd.
entries.literal: Qinglong year 3, twelfth month, day wuchen: the moon encroached on Hooked Halberd.

entries.zh: 占曰：「王者憂。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The ruler faces disaster."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The king has anxiety."

entries.zh: 景初三年正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 景初二年二月癸丑，月犯心距星，又犯中央大星。
entries.en: Jingchu 2, second month, day guichou: the moon crossed Heart's margin star and then crossed its central great star.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 2, second month, day guichou: the moon encroached on Heart's margin star, and again encroached on the central great star.

entries.zh: 五月己亥，又犯心距星及中央大星。
entries.en: Fifth month, day jihai: it crossed Heart's margin star and central great star again.
entries.literal: Fifth month, day jihai, again encroached on Heart's margin star and the central great star.

entries.zh: 閏月癸丑，月又犯心、中央大星。
entries.en: Intercalary month, day guichou: the moon again crossed Heart and its central great star.
entries.literal: Intercalary month, day guichou, the moon again encroached on Heart and the central great star.

entries.zh: 按占，「大星為天王，前為太子，後為皇子。
entries.en: Per the prognostications: "The central star is the celestial king; the star in front is the crown prince; the star behind is an imperial son.
entries.literal: Checking the prognostications: "The great star is the celestial king; the star before it is the heir apparent; the star behind is a prince.

entries.zh: 犯大星，王者惡之。
entries.en: Crossing the great star—rulers dread it.
entries.literal: Encroaching on the great star—rulers dread it.

entries.zh: 犯前星，太子有憂。
entries.en: Crossing the front star—the crown prince faces danger.
entries.literal: Encroaching on the front star—the heir apparent has anxiety.

entries.zh: 犯後星，庶子有憂。」
entries.en: Crossing the rear star—imperial sons face danger."
entries.literal: Encroaching on the rear star—lesser sons have anxiety."

entries.zh: 三年正月，帝崩，太子立，卒見廢為齊王。
entries.en: Jingchu 3, first month: the emperor died and the crown prince took the throne, only to be deposed as Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: Year 3, first month, the emperor died; the heir apparent was enthroned, but in the end was deposed as Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 正始四年，秦王詢薨。
entries.en: Zhengshi 4: Prince of Qin Xun died.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 4, Prince of Qin Xun died.

entries.zh: 景初二年八月彗星見張，長三尺，逆西行，四十一日滅。
entries.en: Jingchu 2, eighth month: a comet appeared in Extended Net, three feet long, moving retrograde westward; it faded after forty-one days.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 2, eighth month: a comet appeared in Extended Net, three chi long, traveling west against the stars, extinguished after forty-one days.

entries.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning.

entries.zh: 張，周分野，洛邑惡之。」
entries.en: Extended Net marks Zhou's domain—Luoyang bears the omen."
entries.literal: Extended Net is Zhou's allotted field—Luoyang is imperiled."

entries.zh: 其十月，斬公孫淵。
entries.en: That tenth month Gongsun Yuan was executed.
entries.literal: That tenth month, Gongsun Yuan was beheaded.

entries.zh: 明年正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: The following first month Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: The next year, first month, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 景初二年十月甲午，月犯箕。
entries.en: Jingchu 2, tenth month, day jiawu: the moon crossed Winnowing Basket.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 2, tenth month, day jiawu: the moon encroached on Winnowing Basket.

entries.zh: 占曰：「軍將死。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "An army commander will die."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Army generals die."

entries.zh: 正始元年四月，車騎將軍黃權薨。
entries.en: Zhengshi 1, fourth month: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huang Quan died.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 1, fourth month, General of Chariots and Cavalry Huang Quan died.

entries.zh: 景初二年，司馬懿圍公孫淵于襄平。
entries.en: Jingchu 2: Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 2, Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.

entries.zh: 八月丙寅夜，有大流星長數十丈，色白有芒鬣，從首山北流墜襄平城東南。
entries.en: On the night of the eighth month's day bingyin a great meteor tens of fathoms long—white, with blazing rays—swept north from Mount Shou and fell southeast of Xiangping.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day bingyin, night: there was a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with horned rays, flowing north from Shoushan and falling southeast of Xiangping city.

entries.zh: 占曰：「圍城而有流星來走城上及墜城中者破。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "When a city is under siege, a meteor racing over its walls or falling inside means the city will fall."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "When a city is besieged, if a meteor comes running over the wall or falls within the city, the city is broken."

entries.zh: 又曰：「星墜，當其下有戰場。」
entries.en: Also: "Where a star falls, a battlefield lies below."
entries.literal: It also says: "When a star falls, beneath it there will be a battlefield."

entries.zh: 又曰：「凡星所墜，國易姓。」
entries.en: Also: "Wherever a star falls, a dynasty changes hands."
entries.literal: It also says: "Whenever a star falls, the state's surname is changed."

entries.zh: 九月，淵突圍，走至星墜所被斬，屠城坑其眾。
entries.en: In the ninth month Yuan broke out, fled to the place where the star had fallen, and was killed; the city was sacked and its people put to the sword and buried in mass graves.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Yuan broke the siege and fled to where the star had fallen, where he was beheaded; the city was slaughtered and its people buried alive in pits.

entries.zh: 景初二年十月癸巳，客星見危，逆行在離宮北，騰蛇南。
entries.en: Jingchu 2, tenth month, day guisi: a guest star appeared in Rooftop, moving retrograde between Retirement Palace to the north and Coiled Serpent to the south.
entries.literal: Jingchu year 2, tenth month, day guisi: a guest star appeared in Rooftop, moving retrograde north of Retirement Palace, south of Coiled Serpent.

entries.zh: 甲辰，犯宗星。
entries.en: Day jiachen: it crossed the Ancestor star.
entries.literal: Day jiachen, it encroached on the Ancestor star.

entries.zh: 己酉，滅。
entries.en: Day jiyou: it vanished.
entries.literal: Day jiyou, it was extinguished.

entries.zh: 占曰：「客星所出有兵喪。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Where a guest star appears, war and mourning follow.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Where a guest star appears, there is warfare and mourning.

entries.zh: 虛危為宗廟，又為墳墓。
entries.en: Emptiness and Rooftop govern the ancestral temple—and also tombs.
entries.literal: Emptiness and Rooftop are the ancestral temple; they also signify graves.

entries.zh: 客星近離宮，則宮中將有大喪，就先君於宗廟，皆王者崩殞之象也。」
entries.en: A guest star near Retirement Palace foretells great mourning within the palace and rites for departed sovereigns at the ancestral temple—all omens of royal death."
entries.literal: A guest star near Retirement Palace means the palace will soon have great mourning, paying respects to former rulers at the ancestral temple—all signs of a king's death."

entries.zh: 三年正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: Year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 正始二年五月，吳將硃然圍樊城，司馬懿率眾距卻之。
entries.en: Zhengshi 2, fifth month: Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng; Sima Yi led an army and repulsed him.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 2, fifth month, Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng; Sima Yi led troops to repel and drive him back.

entries.zh: 魏齊王正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。
entries.en: Under Wei emperor Cao Fang, Zhengshi 1, fourth month, day wuwu: the moon crossed the first star at the eastern horn of Hairy Head.
entries.literal: Wei, Prince of Qi, Zhengshi year 1, fourth month, day wuwu: the moon encroached on the first star at the eastern end of Hairy Head.

entries.zh: 其年十月庚寅，月又犯昴北頭第四星。
entries.en: That year, tenth month, day gengyin: the moon again crossed the fourth star at the northern horn of Hairy Head.
entries.literal: That year, tenth month, day gengyin: the moon again encroached on the fourth star at the northern end of Hairy Head.

entries.zh: 占曰：「犯昴，胡不安。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Striking Hairy Head foretells unrest among the northern peoples".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Encroaching on Hairy Head means the northern tribes are unsettled".

entries.zh: 二年六月，鮮卑阿妙兒等寇西方，燉煌太守王延斬之，并二千餘級。
entries.en: In the sixth month of year two the Xianbei under Amiao'er raided the west; Dunhuang administrator Wang Yan killed them, taking more than two thousand heads.
entries.literal: " Year 2, sixth month: the Xianbei led by Amiao'er and others raided the west; Wang Yan, Administrator of Dunhuang, beheaded them, more than two thousand heads in all.

entries.zh: 三年，又斬鮮卑大帥及千餘級。
entries.en: In year three another Xianbei chieftain was killed, with more than a thousand heads taken.
entries.literal: Year 3: the Xianbei great chief was again beheaded, with more than a thousand heads.

entries.zh: 正始元年十月乙酉，彗星見西方，在尾，長三丈，拂牽牛，犯太白。
entries.en: Zhengshi 1, tenth month, day yiyou: a comet appeared in the west at Tail, three zhang long, sweeping Lead Ox and crossing Venus.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 1, tenth month, day yiyou: a comet appeared in the west, in Tail, three zhang long, brushing Lead Ox and encroaching on Great White.

entries.zh: 十一月甲子，進犯羽林。
entries.en: Eleventh month, day jiazi: it advanced to strike Feathered Forest.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, day jiazi: it advanced to encroach on Feathered Forest.

entries.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，又為吳，牛亦吳、越之分。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Tail governs Yan and also Wu; Lead Ox marks Wu and Yue as well.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Tail governs Yan and also Wu; Ox is likewise the allotted field of Wu and Yue.

entries.zh: 太白為上將，羽林中軍兵。
entries.en: Venus is the commander-in-chief; Feathered Forest is the central host.
entries.literal: Great White is the great general; Feathered Forest is the central army.

entries.zh: 吳、越有兵喪，中軍兵動。」
entries.en: Wu and Yue face war and mourning; the central army mobilizes."
entries.literal: Wu and Yue have warfare and mourning; the central army stirs."

entries.zh: 二年五月，吳將全琮寇芍陂，朱然圍樊城，諸葛瑾入沮中。
entries.en: In the fifth month of year two Wu general Quan Cong attacked Quebei; Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng; and Zhuge Jin entered Juzhong.
entries.literal: " Year 2, fifth month: Wu general Quan Cong raided Quebei; Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng; Zhuge Jin entered Juzhong.

entries.zh: 吳太子登卒。
entries.en: Wu crown prince Deng died.
entries.literal: Wu heir apparent Deng died.

entries.zh: 六月，司馬懿討諸葛恪於皖，恪焚積聚，棄城走。
entries.en: In the sixth month Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke at Wan; Ke burned his supplies and fled the city.
entries.literal: Sixth month: Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke at Wan; Ke burned his stores and abandoned the city in flight.

entries.zh: 三年，太尉滿寵薨。
entries.en: In year three Grand Commandant Man Chong died.
entries.literal: Year 3: Grand Commandant Man Chong died.

entries.zh: 正始九年七月癸丑，鎮星犯楗閉。
entries.en: Zhengshi 9, seventh month, day guichou: Saturn crossed Door Bolt.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 9, seventh month, day guichou: Quelling Star encroached on Door Bolt.

entries.zh: 占曰：「王者不宜出宮下殿。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The sovereign should not leave the palace or step down from the throne hall."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The king ought not leave the palace or descend from the hall."

entries.zh: 明年，車駕謁陵，司馬懿奏誅曹爽等，天子野宿，於是失勢。
entries.en: The next year the emperor went to pay respects at the tombs; Sima Yi moved to execute Cao Shuang and his faction; the emperor camped in the open—and from that moment lost all real power.
entries.literal: The next year, the imperial carriage visited the tombs; Sima Yi memorialized to execute Cao Shuang and others; the Son of Heaven lodged in the open wilds, and thus lost power.

entries.zh: 正始四年十月、十一月，月再犯井鉞。
entries.en: Zhengshi 4, tenth and eleventh months: the moon twice crossed Well's Halberd.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 4, tenth and eleventh months: the moon twice encroached on Well's Halberd.

entries.zh: 是月，司馬懿討諸葛恪，恪棄城走。
entries.en: That month Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke, who abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: That month Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke; Ke abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 五年三月，曹爽征蜀。
entries.en: Zhengshi 5, third month: Cao Shuang marched against Shu.
entries.literal: Year 5, third month: Cao Shuang campaigned against Shu.

entries.zh: 正始五年十一月癸巳，鎮星犯亢距星。
entries.en: Zhengshi 5, eleventh month, day guisi: Saturn crossed the margin star of Neck.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 5, eleventh month, day guisi: Quelling Star encroached on the margin star of Neck.

entries.zh: 占曰：「諸侯有失國者。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Some feudal lords will lose their states".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Among the feudal lords there are those who lose their states".

entries.zh: 嘉平元年，曹爽兄弟誅。
entries.en: In Jiaping 1 Cao Shuang and his brothers were executed.
entries.literal: " Jiaping year 1: Cao Shuang and his brothers were executed.

entries.zh: 正始六年八月戊午，彗星見七星，長二尺，色白，進至張，積二十三日滅。
entries.en: Zhengshi 6, eighth month, day wuwu: a white comet two chi long appeared at Seven Stars, advanced to Spread, and vanished after twenty-three days.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 6, eighth month, day wuwu: a comet appeared at Seven Stars, two chi long, white, advancing to Spread; it lasted twenty-three days and vanished.

entries.zh: 七年十一月癸亥，又見軫，長一尺，積百五十六日滅。
entries.en: In the seventh year, in the eleventh month, on guihai day, another comet one chi long appeared at Chariot Shaft and lasted one hundred fifty-six days.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, in the eleventh month, on guihai day, it again appeared at Chariot Shaft, one chi long, lasting one hundred fifty-six days before vanishing.

entries.zh: 九年三月，又見昴，長六尺，色青白，芒西南指。
entries.en: In the ninth year, in the third month, another comet six chi long, greenish-white, appeared at Hairy Head with rays pointing southwest.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, in the third month, it again appeared at Hairy Head, six chi long, greenish-white, its rays pointing southwest.

entries.zh: 七月，又見翼，長二尺，進至軫，積四十二日滅。
entries.en: Seventh month: another comet two chi long appeared at Wings, advanced to Chariot Shaft, and vanished after forty-two days.
entries.literal: Seventh month: it again appeared at Wings, two chi long, advancing to Chariot Shaft; it lasted forty-two days and vanished.

entries.zh: 按占，「七星、張，周分野，翼、軫為楚，昴為趙、魏，彗所以除舊布新，主兵喪也。」
entries.en: Per the texts: "Seven Stars and Spread mark Zhou; Wings and Chariot Shaft mark Chu; Hairy Head marks Zhao and Wei; comets remove the old and spread the new and preside over war and mourning".
entries.literal: Examining prognostication: "Seven Stars and Spread are Zhou's allotted field; Wings and Chariot Shaft are Chu; Hairy Head is Zhao and Wei; comets remove the old and spread the new and govern warfare and mourning".

entries.zh: 嘉平元年，司馬懿誅曹爽兄弟及其黨與，皆夷族，京師嚴兵，實始翦魏。
entries.en: In Jiaping 1 Sima Yi executed Cao Shuang, his brothers, and their faction, destroying their clans; the capital mobilized—Wei was truly cut back from that moment.
entries.literal: " Jiaping year 1: Sima Yi executed Cao Shuang, his brothers, and their faction, exterminating their clans; the capital tightened its guard—this was the true beginning of pruning Wei.

entries.zh: 三年，誅楚王彪，又襲王淩於淮南。
entries.en: In year three Prince of Chu Biao was executed and Wang Ling was struck at Huainan.
entries.literal: Year 3: Prince of Chu Biao was executed, and Wang Ling was attacked at Huainan.

entries.zh: 淮南，東楚也。
entries.en: Huainan is eastern Chu.
entries.literal: Huainan is eastern Chu.

entries.zh: 幽魏諸王于鄴。
entries.en: Wei princes were confined at Ye.
entries.literal: The princes of Wei were confined at Ye.

entries.zh: 正始七年七月丁丑，月犯左角。
entries.en: Zhengshi 7, seventh month, day dingchou: the moon crossed Left Horn.
entries.literal: Zhengshi year 7, seventh month, day dingchou: the moon encroached on Left Horn.

entries.zh: 占曰：「天下有兵，將軍死。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War will break out and a general will die".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Under Heaven there is warfare; a general dies".

entries.zh: 九年正月辛亥，月犯亢南星。
entries.en: In the ninth year, in the first month, on xinhai day, the moon crossed the southern star of Neck.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, in the first month, on xinhai day, the moon encroached on the southern star of Neck.

entries.zh: 占曰：「兵起。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Arms will be raised".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Warfare rises".

entries.zh: 一曰：「軍將死。」
entries.en: Alternatively: "An army commander will die".
entries.literal: " One reading says: "An army commander dies.

entries.zh: 七月乙亥，熒惑犯畢距星。
entries.en: Seventh month, day yihai: Mars crossed the margin star of Net.
entries.literal: " Seventh month, day yihai: Sparkling Deluder encroached on the margin star of Net.

entries.zh: 占曰：「有邊兵。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Frontier war will erupt".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "There is warfare on the frontier".

entries.zh: 一曰：「刑罰用。」
entries.en: Alternatively: "Punishments will be enforced".
entries.literal: " One reading says: "Punishments are applied.

entries.zh: 嘉平元年，曹爽等誅。
entries.en: In Jiaping 1 Cao Shuang and his faction were executed.
entries.literal: " Jiaping year 1: Cao Shuang and others were executed.

entries.zh: 三年，王淩等又誅。
entries.en: In year three Wang Ling and his associates were executed again.
entries.literal: Year 3: Wang Ling and others were again executed.

entries.zh: 魏高貴鄉公正元元年十一月，有白氣出斗側，廣數丈，長竟天。
entries.en: Under Wei emperor Cao Mao, Zhengyuan 1, eleventh month: white vapor rose beside the Dipper, several fathoms wide, streaking the length of the sky.
entries.literal: Wei, Duke of Gaoguixiang, Zhengyuan year 1, eleventh month: white vapor emerged from the side of Dipper, several zhang wide, stretching the length of the sky.

entries.zh: 王肅曰：「蚩尤之旗也，東南其有亂乎！」
entries.en: Wang Su said: "That is Chiyou's banner—surely the southeast will erupt in rebellion!"
entries.literal: Wang Su said: "This is the banner of Chiyou—is there rebellion in the southeast?"

entries.zh: 二年正月，毋丘儉等據淮南以叛，大將軍司馬師討平之。
entries.en: Zhengyuan 2, first month: Guanqiu Jian seized Huainan in revolt; Grand General Sima Shi crushed the rebellion.
entries.literal: Year 2, first month, Guanqiu Jian and others held Huainan in rebellion; Grand General Sima Shi suppressed and pacified them.

entries.zh: 案占，「蚩尤旗見，王者征伐四方。」
entries.en: Per the prognostications: "When Chiyou's banner appears, the sovereign marches to war on every front."
