entries.literal: Per astrological texts: "When Chiyou's banner appears, the king campaigns in all four directions."

entries.zh: 自後又征淮南，西平巴蜀。
entries.en: Thereafter the court campaigned again in Huainan and pacified Ba and Shu in the west.
entries.literal: Afterwards there were again campaigns against Huainan and the pacification of Ba-Shu in the west.

entries.zh: 是歲，吳主孫亮五鳳元年，斗牛，吳、越分。
entries.en: That same year Sun Liang of Wu entered his Wufeng reign: the Dipper and Ox govern Wu and Yue's domain.
entries.literal: That year, Wu ruler Sun Liang's Wufeng year 1: Dipper-Ox—Wu and Yue's allotted field.

entries.zh: 案占：「有兵喪，除舊佈新之象也。」
entries.en: Per the prognostications: "War and mourning follow—the omen of sweeping away the old and installing the new."
entries.literal: Checking the prognostications: "There is warfare and mourning—the sign of removing the old and spreading the new."

entries.zh: 太平三年，孫綝盛兵圍宮，廢亮為會稽王，孫休代立，是其應也。
entries.en: In Taiping 3, Sun Chen marched on the palace, deposed Sun Liang as King of Kuaiji, and installed Sun Xiu in his place—the omen fulfilled.
entries.literal: Taiping year 3, Sun Chen massed troops and besieged the palace, deposed Liang as King of Kuaiji, and Sun Xiu succeeded him—this was its fulfillment.

entries.zh: 故國志又書于吳。
entries.en: Hence the Records of the Three Kingdoms places the entry under Wu as well.
entries.literal: Therefore the Records of the Three Kingdoms also records it under Wu.

entries.zh: 由是淮南江東同揚州地，故于時變見吳、楚之分。
entries.en: Because Huainan and Jiangdong both lay within Yang Province, the portents of that era clustered in the Wu and Chu domains.
entries.literal: From this, Huainan and Jiangdong share Yang Province territory, so celestial anomalies of the time appeared in Wu and Chu's allotted fields.

entries.zh: 則魏之淮南，多與吳同災，是以毋丘儉以孛為己應，遂起兵而敗，又其應也。
entries.en: Wei's Huainan and Wu often suffered the same omens; Guanqiu Jian read the comet as his personal sign, rose in revolt, and was crushed—yet another fulfillment.
entries.literal: Thus Wei's Huainan often shared calamities with Wu; Guanqiu Jian took the broom star as his own omen, raised troops and was defeated—again its fulfillment.

entries.zh: 後三年，即魏甘露二年，諸葛誕又反淮南，吳遣硃異救之。
entries.en: Three years on—in Wei Ganlu 2—Zhuge Dan rebelled again in Huainan, and Wu dispatched Zhu Yi to his aid.
entries.literal: Three years later, Wei Ganlu year 2, Zhuge Dan again rebelled in Huainan; Wu sent Zhu Yi to rescue him.

entries.zh: 及城陷，誕眾吳兵死沒各數萬人，猶前長星之應也。
entries.en: When the city fell, tens of thousands on both sides—Dan's men and Wu's relief force—were killed, fulfilling the earlier comet's warning.
entries.literal: When the city fell, tens of thousands each among Dan's followers and Wu's soldiers died and perished—still the fulfillment of the earlier long star.

entries.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年二月戊午，熒惑犯東井北轅西頭第一星。
entries.en: Under Cao Mao, Zhengyuan 2, second month, day wuwu: Mars crossed the westernmost star at the northern yoke of Eastern Well.
entries.literal: Duke of Gaoguixiang, Zhengyuan year 2, second month, day wuwu: Sparkling Deluder encroached on Eastern Well's northern shaft, the first star at its western end.

entries.zh: 占曰：「群臣有家坐罪者。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Ministers will see their families punished for capital offenses."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Among the ministers, some will have their clans punished for crimes."

entries.zh: 甘露元年，諸葛誕族滅。
entries.en: In Ganlu 1, Zhuge Dan's entire clan was annihilated.
entries.literal: Ganlu year 1, Zhuge Dan's clan was exterminated.

entries.zh: 晉武帝泰始四年正月丙戌，彗星見軫，青白色，西北行，又轉東行。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Jin, the fourth year of Taishi, first month, day bingxu: a greenish-white comet appeared in Chariot Shaft, moving northwest before swinging eastward.
entries.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Taishi year 4, first month, day bingxu: a comet appeared in Chariot Shaft, greenish-white, traveling northwest, then turning to travel east.

entries.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning.

entries.zh: 軫又楚分也。」
entries.en: Chariot Shaft also marks Chu's domain."
entries.literal: Chariot Shaft is also Chu's allotted field."

entries.zh: 三月，皇太后王氏崩。
entries.en: In the third month Empress Dowager Wang passed away.
entries.literal: Third month, Empress Dowager Lady Wang died.

entries.zh: 十月，吳將施績寇江夏，萬彧寇襄陽，後將軍田璋、荊州刺史胡烈等破卻之。
entries.en: In the tenth month Wu generals Shi Ji attacked Jiangxia and Wan Yu attacked Xiangyang; Rear General Tian Zhang, Jing provincial inspector Hu Lie, and others drove them back.
entries.literal: Tenth month, Wu generals Shi Ji raided Jiangxia and Wan Yu raided Xiangyang; Rear General Tian Zhang, Jing Province Inspector Hu Lie, and others defeated and repelled them.

entries.zh: 泰始四年七月，星隕如雨，皆西流。
entries.en: the fourth year of Taishi, seventh month: stars showered down like rain, all streaking westward.
entries.literal: Taishi year 4, seventh month: stars fell like rain, all flowing westward.

entries.zh: 占曰：「星隕為民叛，西流，吳民歸晉之象也。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "A starfall marks popular defection; a westward drift foretells Wu's people submitting to Jin."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Falling stars signify the people's rebellion; flowing westward is the image of Wu's people returning to Jin."

entries.zh: 二年，吳夏口督孫秀率部曲二千餘人來降。
entries.en: Two years on Wu's Xiakou garrison commander Sun Xiu brought more than two thousand of his retainers over in surrender.
entries.literal: Two years later, Wu's Xiakou supervisor Sun Xiu led more than two thousand of his personal troops in surrender.

entries.zh: 泰始十年十二月，有星孛於軫。
entries.en: the tenth year of Taishi, twelfth month: a comet appeared in Chariot Shaft.
entries.literal: Taishi year 10, twelfth month: a broom star appeared at Chariot Shaft.

entries.zh: 占曰：「天下兵起。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War will erupt across the empire.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Warfare rises throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 軫又楚分也。」
entries.en: Chariot Shaft also marks Chu's domain."
entries.literal: Chariot Shaft is also Chu's allotted field."

entries.zh: 咸寧二年六月，星孛於氐。
entries.en: In Xianning 2, sixth month, a comet appeared at Root.
entries.literal: Xianning year 2, sixth month: a broom star appeared at Root.

entries.zh: 占曰：「天子失德易政。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The sovereign forfeits virtue and the throne changes hands.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The Son of Heaven loses virtue and the regime changes.

entries.zh: 氐又兗州分。」
entries.en: Root also marks Yanzhou's domain."
entries.literal: Root is also Yanzhou's allotted field."

entries.zh: 七月，星孛大角。
entries.en: In the seventh month a comet appeared at Great Horn.
entries.literal: Seventh month: a broom star appeared at Great Horn.

entries.zh: 大角為帝坐。
entries.en: Great Horn is the throne star of the sovereign.
entries.literal: Great Horn is the Emperor's Seat.

entries.zh: 八月，星孛太微，至翼、北斗、三台。
entries.en: In the eighth month a comet appeared in Supreme Subtlety and passed through Wings, the Northern Dipper, and the Three Steps.
entries.literal: Eighth month: a broom star appeared at Supreme Subtlety, reaching Wings, Northern Dipper, and Three Steps.

entries.zh: 占曰：「太微天子廷，大人惡之。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Supreme Subtlety is the imperial court—great men will suffer for it."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Supreme Subtlety is the Son of Heaven's court; great men dread it."

entries.zh: 一曰：「有徙王。
entries.en: Another reading says: "A deposed prince will be moved.
entries.literal: One account says: "There will be a transferred king.

entries.zh: 翼又楚分也。」
entries.en: Wings also marks Chu's domain."
entries.literal: Wings is also Chu's allotted field."

entries.zh: 「北斗主殺罰，三台為三公。」
entries.en: "The Northern Dipper presides over execution and judgment; the Three Steps represent the Three Dukes."
entries.literal: "Northern Dipper governs killing and punishment; Three Steps are the Three Dukes."

entries.zh: 三年，星孛於胃。
entries.en: In Xianning 3 a comet appeared at Stomach.
entries.literal: Year 3: a broom star appeared at Stomach.

entries.zh: 胃，徐州分。
entries.en: Stomach marks Xuzhou's domain.
entries.literal: Stomach is Xuzhou's allotted field.

entries.zh: 四月，星孛女御。
entries.en: In the fourth month a comet appeared at Female Charioteer.
entries.literal: Fourth month: a broom star appeared at Female Charioteer.

entries.zh: 女御為後宮。
entries.en: Female Charioteer governs the inner harem.
entries.literal: Female Charioteer is the rear palace.

entries.zh: 五月，又孛於東方。
entries.en: In the fifth month another comet appeared in the east.
entries.literal: Fifth month: a broom star again appeared in the east.

entries.zh: 七月，星孛紫宮。
entries.en: In the seventh month a comet appeared in Purple Palace.
entries.literal: Seventh month: a broom star appeared at Purple Palace.

entries.zh: 占曰：「天下易主。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The empire will change hands."
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The realm changes its ruler."

entries.zh: 五年三月，星孛于柳。
entries.en: In Xianning 5, third month, a comet appeared at Willow.
entries.literal: Year 5, third month: a broom star appeared at Willow.

entries.zh: 占曰：「外臣陵主。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "Outer vassals will overpower their lord.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "Outer ministers encroach upon the ruler.

entries.zh: 柳又三河分也。
entries.en: Willow also marks the Three Rivers domain.
entries.literal: Willow is also the Three Rivers' allotted field.

entries.zh: 大角、太微、紫宮、女御，並為王者。」
entries.en: Great Horn, Supreme Subtlety, Purple Palace, and Female Charioteer all stand for royal power."
entries.literal: Great Horn, Supreme Subtlety, Purple Palace, and Female Charioteer all represent the kingly ruler."

entries.zh: 明年吳亡，是其應也。
entries.en: The following year Wu fell—the omen fulfilled.
entries.literal: The next year Wu perished—this was its fulfillment.

entries.zh: 孛主兵喪，征吳之役，三河、徐、兗之兵悉出，交戰于吳、楚之地。
entries.en: Comets presage war and death; in the conquest of Wu, forces from the Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan all took the field and clashed in the Wu-Chu heartland.
entries.literal: Broom stars govern warfare and mourning; in the campaign against Wu, armies of the Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan all marched out and joined battle in Wu and Chu territory.

entries.zh: 吳丞相都督以下，梟戮十數，偏裨行陣之徒，馘斬萬計，皆其征也。
entries.en: More than a dozen Wu chancellors and commanders were executed and exposed; lieutenants and common soldiers fell by the tens of thousands—all of it the comet's doing.
entries.literal: Among Wu, from chancellors and area commanders downward, more than ten were decapitated and displayed; among lieutenants and rank-and-file in the battle lines, those beheaded and killed numbered in the tens of thousands—all signs of it.

entries.zh: 《春秋》星孛北方，則齊、魯、晉、鄭、陳、宋、莒之君，並受殺亂之禍。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals record that when a comet appeared in the north, the rulers of Qi, Lu, Jin, Zheng, Chen, Song, and Ju all met violent ruin.
entries.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a broom star appeared in the north, the rulers of Qi, Lu, Jin, Zheng, Chen, Song, and Ju all suffered the calamity of slaughter and disorder.

entries.zh: 星孛東方，則楚滅陳，三家、田氏分篡齊、晉。
entries.en: An eastern comet foretold Chu destroying Chen and the great houses of Jin and Qi carving up their states.
entries.literal: When a broom star appeared in the east, Chu destroyed Chen, and the Three Families and the Tian clan partitioned and usurped Qi and Jin.

entries.zh: 漢文帝末，星孛西方，後吳、楚七國誅滅。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Wen's reign a comet appeared in the west; soon after the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were crushed.
entries.literal: At the end of Emperor Wen of Han, a broom star appeared in the west; afterward the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were exterminated.

entries.zh: 案泰始末至太康初，災異數見，而晉氏隆盛，吳實滅，天變在吳可知矣。
entries.en: From late Taishi through early Taikang, omens multiplied even as Jin rose and Wu fell—clear proof that heaven's warnings were aimed at Wu, not Jin.
entries.literal: Examined: from the end of Taishi to the beginning of Taikang, calamities and anomalies appeared repeatedly, yet the Jin clan flourished and Wu was truly destroyed—heaven's changes targeted Wu, as can be known.

entries.zh: 昔漢三年，星孛大角，項籍以亡，漢氏無事，此項氏主命故也。
entries.en: In Han year 3 a comet struck Great Horn: Xiang Yu fell while the Han house stood untouched, for Great Horn governed Xiang's fate.
entries.literal: Formerly in Han year 3, a comet baleful at Great Horn—Xiang Yu perished thereby while the Han house was unharmed; this was because Great Horn was the star of Xiang's mandate.

entries.zh: 吳、晉之時，天下橫分，大角孛而吳亡，是與項氏同事。
entries.en: When Wu and Jin divided the realm, a comet at Great Horn preceded Wu's fall—the same pattern as Xiang Yu's doom.
entries.literal: In the age of Wu and Jin, the realm was split across; Great Horn was baleful and Wu perished—this is the same affair as the Xiang clan.

entries.zh: 後學皆以咸甯災為晉室，非也。
entries.en: Later scholars misread the Xianning omens as warnings to Jin; they are mistaken.
entries.literal: Later scholars all take the Xianning calamities as aimed at the Jin house—this is wrong.

entries.zh: 晉武帝咸寧四年四月，蚩尤旗見。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Jin, Xianning 4, fourth month: the Chiyou Banner appeared.
entries.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Xianning year 4, fourth month: the Chiyou Banner appeared.

entries.zh: 案星傳，蚩尤旗類彗，而後曲象旗。
entries.en: Star lore holds that the Chiyou Banner resembles a comet but curves backward like a banner.
entries.literal: Examining star lore: the Chiyou Banner resembles a comet, but curves backward like a banner.

entries.zh: 漢武帝時見，長竟天。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu of Han it appeared, spanning the entire sky.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Han it appeared, stretching across the whole sky.

entries.zh: 獻帝時又見，長十餘丈，皆長星也。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xian it appeared again, more than ten zhang long—both were long stars.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Xian it appeared again, more than ten zhang long—all were long stars.

entries.zh: 魏高貴時則為白氣。
entries.en: In Wei's Gaogui era it appeared as white vapor.
entries.literal: In the Gaogui era of Wei it was a white vapor.

entries.zh: 案校眾記，是歲無長星，宜又是異氣。
entries.en: Collating many records shows no long star that year; it was again an anomalous vapor.
entries.literal: Examining and collating many records, that year had no long star; it should again have been an anomalous vapor.

entries.zh: 後二年，傾三方伐吳，是其應。
entries.en: Two years later Jin mobilized on three fronts against Wu—the omen fulfilled.
entries.literal: Two years later the three fronts poured forth to attack Wu—this was its fulfillment.

entries.zh: 至武帝崩，天下兵又起，遂亡諸夏。
entries.en: By Emperor Wu's death war broke out again and the Central States fell into chaos.
entries.literal: By the time Emperor Wu died, warfare rose again under Heaven, and the Central States perished.

entries.zh: 咸寧四年九月，太白當見不見。
entries.en: Xianning 4, ninth month: Venus should have appeared but did not.
entries.literal: Xianning year 4, ninth month: Great White should have appeared but did not.

entries.zh: 占曰：「是謂失舍，不有破軍，必有死王之墓。
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "This is called losing one's station; if no army is shattered, a royal tomb will be opened.
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "This is called losing one's lodging; if there is no shattered army, there must be the tomb of a dead king.

entries.zh: 又有亡國。」
entries.en: A state may also perish."
entries.literal: Moreover there is loss of state."

entries.zh: 是時羊祜表求伐吳，上許之。
entries.en: At that time Yang Hu memorialized to attack Wu and the throne approved.
entries.literal: " At that time Yang Hu memorialized requesting an attack on Wu, and the throne approved.

entries.zh: 五年十一月，兵出，太白始夕見西方。
entries.en: In the fifth year, in the eleventh month, the army marched and Venus first appeared at dusk in the west.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, in the eleventh month, the army marched out, and Great White first appeared at dusk in the west.

entries.zh: 太康元年三月，大破吳軍，孫晧面縛請死，吳國遂亡。
entries.en: Taikang 1, third month: Wu's army was crushed; Sun Hao bound himself and begged for death; Wu fell.
entries.literal: Taikang year 1, third month: Wu's army was greatly defeated; Sun Hao bound himself and begged for death; the state of Wu perished.

entries.zh: 晉武帝太康二年八月，有星孛于張。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Jin, Taikang 2, eighth month: a comet appeared at Spread.
entries.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Taikang year 2, eighth month: a broom star appeared at Spread.

entries.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning".

entries.zh: 周分野，災在洛邑。
entries.en: Zhou's domain—the calamity struck Luoyang.
entries.literal: " Zhou's allotted field—the calamity falls on Luoyang.

entries.zh: 十一月，星孛軒轅。
entries.en: Eleventh month: a comet appeared at Chariot Shaft.
entries.literal: Eleventh month: a broom star baleful at Chariot Shaft.

entries.zh: 占曰：「後宮當之。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The inner palace will be struck".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The rear palace is struck".

entries.zh: 四年三月戊申，星孛于西南。
entries.en: In the fourth year, in the third month, on wushen day, a comet appeared in the southwest.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, in the third month, on wushen day, a broom star appeared in the southwest.

entries.zh: 四年三月癸丑，齊王攸薨。
entries.en: In the fourth year, in the third month, on guichou day, Prince Sima You of Qi died.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, in the third month, on guichou day, Prince You of Qi died.

entries.zh: 四月戊寅，任城王陵薨。
entries.en: Fourth month, day wuyin: Prince of Rencheng Ling died.
entries.literal: Fourth month, day wuyin: Prince of Rencheng Ling died.

entries.zh: 五月己亥，琅邪王伷薨。
entries.en: Fifth month, day jihai: Prince of Langye Xiu died.
entries.literal: Fifth month, day jihai: Prince of Langye Xiu died.

entries.zh: 十一月戊午，新都王該薨。
entries.en: Eleventh month, day wuwu: Prince of Xindu Gai died.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, day wuwu: Prince of Xindu Gai died.

entries.zh: 太康八年三月，熒惑守心。
entries.en: Taikang 8, third month: Mars held station in Heart.
entries.literal: Taikang year 8, third month: Sparkling Deluder guarded Heart.

entries.zh: 占曰：「王者惡之。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The sovereign faces ill omen".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The kingly ruler is ill-omened".

entries.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
entries.en: Taixi 1, fourth month, day jiyou: Emperor Wu died.
entries.literal: " Taixi year 1, fourth month, day jiyou: Emperor Wu died.

entries.zh: 太康八年九月，星孛于南斗，長數十丈，十餘日滅。
entries.en: Taikang 8, ninth month: a comet tens of zhang long appeared at Southern Dipper and vanished after more than ten days.
entries.literal: Taikang year 8, ninth month: a broom star appeared at Southern Dipper, several tens of zhang long; it vanished after more than ten days.

entries.zh: 占曰：「斗主爵祿，國有大憂。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "The Dipper governs rank and salary; the state faces grave danger".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "The Dipper governs rank and stipend; the state has great anxiety".

entries.zh: 一曰：「孛于斗，王者疾病，臣誅其父，天下易政，大亂兵起。」
entries.en: Alternatively: "A comet at the Dipper means royal illness, a minister kills his father, the realm changes hands, and great war erupts".
entries.literal: " One reading says: "A broom star at the Dipper means the kingly ruler falls ill, a minister executes his father, rule changes under Heaven, and great disorder and warfare rise.

entries.zh: 太熙元年四月，客星在紫宮。
entries.en: Taixi 1, fourth month: a guest star stood in Purple Palace.
entries.literal: " Taixi year 1, fourth month: a guest star was in Purple Palace.

entries.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
entries.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow".
entries.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning".

entries.zh: 太康末，武帝耽宴遊，多疾病。
entries.en: Near the end of Taikang Emperor Wu indulged in feasts and tours and grew seriously ill.
entries.literal: " At the end of Taikang Emperor Wu indulged in feasting and travel and suffered many illnesses.

entries.zh: 是月己酉，帝崩。
entries.en: That month, day jiyou: the emperor died.
entries.literal: That month, day jiyou: the emperor died.

entries.zh: 永平元年，賈后誅楊駿及其黨與，皆夷三族。
entries.en: Yongping 1: Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and his faction, destroying all three clans.
entries.literal: Yongping year 1: Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and his faction, exterminating all three clans.

entries.zh: 楊太后亦見殺。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Yang was also killed.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Yang was also killed.

entries.zh: 是年，又誅汝南王亮、太保衞瓘、楚王瑋，王室兵喪之應。
entries.en: That year Prince of Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and Prince of Chu Wei were also executed—fulfillment of the royal house's war and mourning.
entries.literal: That year Prince of Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and Prince of Chu Wei were also executed—the royal house's fulfillment of warfare and mourning.

entries.zh: 志第十三 天文一
entries.en: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One
entries.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1

entries.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，成都王穎使陸機率眾向京師，擊長沙王乂。
entries.en: In the second year of Tai'an, Emperor Hui of Jin's reign, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, ordered Lu Ji to march on the capital and strike the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tai'an of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, sent Lu Ji at the head of an army toward the capital to attack the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.

entries.zh: 軍始引而牙竿折，俄而戰敗，機被誅。
entries.en: The army had barely moved when the command pennant pole broke; shortly afterward the force was routed and Lu Ji was put to death.
entries.literal: As soon as the army set out the command pennant staff snapped; soon afterward they were defeated and Ji was executed.

entries.zh: 穎尋奔潰，卒賜死。
entries.en: Ying soon fled in defeat and was eventually compelled to commit suicide.
entries.literal: Ying soon fled in rout and in the end was ordered to take his own life.

entries.zh: 初，河間王顒謀先誅長沙，廢太子，立穎。
entries.en: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had planned to kill the Prince of Changsha first, depose the crown prince, and set up Ying in his place.
entries.literal: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had plotted first to kill the Prince of Changsha, depose the heir, and install Ying.

entries.zh: 長沙知之，誅其黨卞粹等，故穎來伐。
entries.en: The Prince of Changsha uncovered the plot and executed Yong's allies Bian Cui and the rest, which brought Ying's invasion.
entries.literal: The Prince of Changsha learned of it and executed his partisans Bian Cui and others; therefore Ying came to attack.

entries.zh: 機又以穎得遐邇心，將為漢之代王，遂委質於穎，為犯從之將。
entries.en: Lu Ji likewise believed Ying had won universal support and would replace the Han house as king; he therefore pledged himself to Ying and served as a general in the rebel host.
entries.literal: Ji also thought that because Ying had won the hearts of near and far he would become the Han dynasty's replacement king, and therefore submitted to Ying and served as a general who followed the rebel cause.

entries.zh: 此皆姦謀之罰，木不曲直也。
entries.en: All of this fell under the penalty for treacherous designs—wood failing to be straight or bent.
entries.literal: All these were punishments for treacherous plots—wood not straight or bent.

entries.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，賈謐親貴，數入二宮，與儲君遊戲，无降下心。
entries.en: During Yuankang, Jia Mi, riding on intimate favor, entered the inner palaces again and again to sport with the crown prince and showed no deference.
entries.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, Jia Mi enjoyed intimate favor and repeatedly entered the two palaces to play with the heir apparent, without a submissive heart.

entries.zh: 又嘗同弈棊爭道，成都王穎厲色曰：「皇太子，國之儲貳。
entries.en: Once, disputing a game of go, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sharply: "The crown prince is the heir of the realm.
entries.literal: Once when they played go and disputed the board, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sternly: "The crown prince is the state's heir.

entries.zh: 賈謐何敢無禮！」
entries.en: How dare Jia Mi behave without courtesy!"
entries.literal: How dare Jia Mi be discourteous!"

entries.zh: 謐猶不悛，故及於禍。
entries.en: Mi still would not mend his ways, and so brought disaster on himself.
entries.literal: Mi still did not reform himself; therefore he met with disaster.

entries.zh: 齊王冏既誅趙倫，因留輔政，坐拜百官，符敕臺府，淫醟專驕，不一朝覲。
entries.en: After Sima Jiong of Qi had killed Zhao Lun he stayed on as regent, accepted officials' bows while seated, issued Secretariat orders at will, and grew drunken, arrogant, and aloof—never attending court.
entries.literal: After the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, had executed Zhao Lun, he remained to assist in government, sat to receive the obeisance of all officials, issued orders in the name of the Secretariat, and was dissolute, arrogant, and exclusive—never once attending court audience.

entries.zh: 此狂恣不肅之容也。
entries.en: This was the deportment of reckless insolence without respect.
entries.literal: This was the bearing of mad presumption without reverence.

entries.zh: 天下莫不高其功，而慮其亡也。
entries.en: The empire applauded his success yet dreaded his fall.
entries.literal: Throughout the realm none failed to praise his achievement, yet all feared his ruin.

entries.zh: 冏終弗改，遂至夷滅。
entries.en: Jiong never reformed and was destroyed in the end.
entries.literal: Jiong in the end did not change and proceeded to extermination.

entries.zh: 吳婦人之修容者，急束其髮，而劘角過于耳。
entries.en: Wu women who dressed their hair bound it fiercely and trimmed the corners past the ears.
entries.literal: Among Wu women who dressed their appearance, they bound the hair urgently and cut the corners past the ears.

entries.zh: 蓋其俗自操束大急，而廉隅失中之謂也。
entries.en: Their custom of tight self-restraint overshot the mean of proper conduct.
entries.literal: Generally their custom of self-restraint was excessively tight, which is called losing the mean in integrity.

entries.zh: 故吳之風俗，相驅以急，言論彈射，以刻薄相尚。
entries.en: Wu folk drove one another to urgency, shot verbal barbs in debate, and prized harshness.
entries.literal: Therefore Wu's customs drove one another to haste; in speech they shot barbs and honored one another with harshness.

entries.zh: 居三年之喪者，往往有致毀以死。
entries.en: Mourners in the three-year rites often starved themselves to death.
entries.literal: Those in the three-year mourning often brought themselves to ruin by emaciation and died.

entries.zh: 諸葛患之，著正交論，雖不可以經訓整亂，蓋亦救時之作也。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang, troubled by this, wrote the Discourse on Correct Friendship—not enough to restore order by the classics, yet a timely remedy.
entries.literal: Zhuge Liang was troubled by this and wrote the Discourse on Correct Friendship; though it could not set chaos in order by canonical teaching, it was nevertheless a work to rescue the age.

entries.zh: 孫休後，衣服之制，上長下短，又積領五六而裳居一二。
entries.en: After Sun Xiu, garments grew long above and short below; collars piled five or six deep while the skirt shrank to a fraction.
entries.literal: After Sun Xiu, the system of dress was long above and short below, with collars stacked five or six deep while the skirt occupied only one or two parts.

entries.zh: 干寶曰：「上饒奢，下儉逼，上有餘下不足之妖也。」
entries.en: Gan Bao said: "Extravagance above and meanness below—an omen of plenty on top and want underneath."
entries.literal: Gan Bao said: "Luxury above and stinginess below pressing upward—this is the portent of surplus above and insufficiency below."

entries.zh: 至孫晧，果奢暴恣情於上，而百姓彫困於下，卒以亡國。
entries.en: Under Sun Hao the ruler grew wanton and cruel while the people were ground down, and the state fell.
entries.literal: By Sun Hao in the end he was extravagant and violent in feeling above while the common people were carved thin below, and in the end the state perished.

entries.zh: 是其應也。
entries.en: This was the omen fulfilled.
entries.literal: This was the fulfillment.

entries.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，洛陽南山有䖟作聲曰：「韓屍屍。」
entries.en: In Yuankang, flies on Luoyang's southern mountain buzzed “Han corpses, corpses.”
entries.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, on the southern mountain of Luoyang flies made a sound saying "Han corpse corpse."

entries.zh: 識者曰：「韓氏將死也。
entries.en: Observers said: "The Han clan will perish.
entries.literal: Observers said: "The Han clan is about to die.

entries.zh: 言屍屍者，盡死意也。」
entries.en: Corpse corpse means all are dead."
entries.literal: Saying corpse corpse means the meaning of all dead."

entries.zh: 其後韓謐誅而韓族殲焉。
entries.en: Soon Han Mi was executed and the Han clan wiped out.
entries.literal: Afterward Han Mi was executed and the Han clan was exterminated.

entries.zh: 此青祥也。
entries.en: This was a blue portent.
entries.literal: This was a blue omen.

entries.zh: 晉惠帝永熙初，衛瓘家人炊飯，墮地，盡化為螺，出足起行。
entries.en: Early in Yongxi, rice in Wei Guan's kitchen fell to the floor and turned into snails that sprouted feet and crawled away.
entries.literal: In the early Yongxi era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in the household of Wei Guan when cooking rice it fell to the ground and all turned into snails that put out feet, rose, and walked.

entries.zh: 螺，龜類，近龜孽也。
entries.en: Snails belong to the tortoise family and count as near tortoise omens.
entries.literal: Snails are of the tortoise kind and are near to tortoise portents.

entries.zh: 干寶曰：「螺被甲，兵象也。
entries.en: Gan Bao said: "Snails wear armor—the sign of war.
entries.literal: Gan Bao said: "Snails wear armor—the image of arms.

entries.zh: 於周易為離，離為戈兵。」
entries.en: In the Book of Changes this is Li, the trigram of weapons."
entries.literal: In the Book of Changes this is Li, and Li is spear and weapon."

entries.zh: 明年，瓘誅。
entries.en: The next year Guan was executed.
entries.literal: The next year Guan was executed.

entries.zh: 吳孫休永安五年二月，白虎門北樓災。
entries.en: In the second month of the fifth Yong'an year under Sun Xiu of Wu, fire destroyed the north tower of the White Tiger Gate.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, the north tower of the White Tiger Gate burned.

entries.zh: 六年十月，石頭小城火，燒西南百八十丈。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the sixth year fire swept the small citadel at Shitou, burning one hundred eighty zhang along the southwest.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year, the small fortress at Shitou burned, consuming one hundred eighty zhang of the southwest quarter.

entries.zh: 是時嬖人張布專擅國勢，多行無禮，而韋昭、盛冲終斥不用，兼遣察戰等為使，驚擾州郡，致使交趾反亂。
entries.en: At the time the favorite Zhang Bu dominated the government and behaved lawlessly, while Wei Zhao and Sheng Chong were kept from office; he also dispatched Cha Zhan and others as envoys, unsettling the provinces until Jiaozhi rose in revolt.
entries.literal: At that time the favorite Zhang Bu monopolized state power and often acted without propriety, while Wei Zhao and Sheng Chong were finally rejected and not employed; he also sent Cha Zhan and others as envoys, alarming and harassing commanderies and districts, causing Jiaozhi to rebel.

entries.zh: 是其咎也。
entries.en: That was the offense behind the omen.
entries.literal: This was its fault.

entries.zh: 十年四月癸丑，崇賢殿災。
entries.en: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year fire destroyed the Chongxian Hall.
entries.literal: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year, the Chongxian Hall burned.

entries.zh: 十月庚辰，含章鞠室、脩成堂前廡、丙坊東屋、煇章殿南閣火。
entries.en: On the gengchen day of the tenth month fire broke out in the Hanzhang kickball court, the front veranda of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern wing of the Huizhang Hall.
entries.literal: On the gengchen day of the tenth month, fire struck the Hanzhang cuju court, the front colonnade of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern gallery of the Huizhang Hall.

entries.zh: 時有上書者曰：「漢王氏五侯兄弟迭任，今楊氏三公並在大位。
entries.en: A memorialist wrote at the time, "Under Han the five Wang marquises held office in turn; now the three Yang dukes all stand at the summit of power together.
entries.literal: At the time a memorialist said: "Under Han the five marquises of the Wang clan held office in succession as brothers; now the three dukes of the Yang clan all hold high position together.

entries.zh: 天變屢見，竊為陛下憂之。」
entries.en: Heavenly omens keep appearing, and I cannot help fearing for Your Majesty."
entries.literal: Heavenly changes appear repeatedly; I venture to be anxious on Your Majesty's behalf."

entries.zh: 楊珧由是乞退。
entries.en: Yang Yao thereupon asked to withdraw from office.
entries.literal: Yang Yao therefore requested to retire.

entries.zh: 是時帝納馮紞之間，廢張華之功；
entries.en: At that time the emperor heeded Feng Dan's private advice and cast aside Zhang Hua's merits;
entries.literal: At that time the emperor accepted Feng Dan's private counsel and set aside Zhang Hua's achievements;

entries.zh: 聽楊駿之讒，離衞瓘之寵。
entries.en: listened to Yang Jun's slanders and turned away from Wei Guan's favor.
entries.literal: heeded Yang Jun's slanders and estranged himself from Wei Guan's favor.

entries.zh: 此逐功臣之罰也。
entries.en: This was the retribution for driving out worthy ministers.
entries.literal: This was the penalty for expelling meritorious ministers.

entries.zh: 明年，宮車晏駕。
entries.en: The following year the emperor died.
entries.literal: The next year the imperial carriage halted at dusk.

entries.zh: 其後楚王承竊發之旨，戮害二公，身亦不免。
entries.en: Later the Prince of Chu, acting on a clandestine order, killed the two chief ministers, yet could not save himself.
entries.literal: Afterward the Prince of Chu, acting on a secretly issued directive, slaughtered the two grandees, yet he himself did not escape punishment.

entries.zh: 震災其坊，又天意乎。
entries.en: Lightning had already struck his residence—was that not Heaven's intent as well?
entries.literal: Lightning had struck his ward—was this again Heaven's intent?

entries.zh: 晉惠帝元康五年閏月庚寅，武庫火。
entries.en: On the gengyin day of the intercalary fifth Yuankang year under Emperor Hui of Jin, fire destroyed the imperial armory.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day of the intercalary month of the fifth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the armory burned.

entries.zh: 張華疑有亂，先固守，然後救災。
entries.en: Zhang Hua, suspecting revolt, secured the site before turning to fight the blaze.
entries.literal: Zhang Hua suspected rebellion and first held the site under guard, only then fighting the fire.

entries.zh: 是以累代異寶，王莽頭，孔子履，漢高斷白蛇劍及二百萬人器械，一時蕩盡。
entries.en: Thus treasures hoarded for generations—the head of Wang Mang, Confucius's sandal, the sword with which Han Gaozu slew the white serpent, and arms for two million men—were destroyed in a single hour.
entries.literal: Thus rare treasures accumulated over generations—the head of Wang Mang, Confucius's shoe, the sword with which Gaozu of Han cut the white serpent, and arms for two million men—were swept away at once.

entries.zh: 是後愍懷見殺，殺太子之罰也。
entries.en: Later Prince Minhuai was murdered—the retribution for killing the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Afterward Prince Minhuai was killed—the penalty for slaying the crown prince.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，夫設險擊柝，所以固其國，儲積戎器，所以戒不虞。
entries.en: Heaven seemed to warn: ramparts and watch-clappers exist to secure the realm; arsenals are stocked to guard against surprise.
entries.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: defenses and night-watch clappers are set up to secure the state; stores of weapons are amassed to guard against the unforeseen.

entries.zh: 今冢嗣將傾，社稷將泯，禁兵無所復施，皇旅又將誰衞。
entries.en: Now the heir's house is collapsing, the altars are failing, the palace guard can no longer be used, and who will defend the throne?
entries.literal: Now the heir's line is about to topple, the altars of soil and grain about to perish; the palace guard can no longer be deployed, and who will guard the imperial host?

entries.zh: 帝后不悟，終喪四海，是其應也。
entries.en: Emperor and empress failed to understand, and in the end lost the realm—the omen fulfilled.
entries.literal: The emperor and empress did not understand; in the end they lost all within the four seas—this was the response.

entries.zh: 張華、閻纂皆曰，武庫火而氐、羌反，太子見廢，則四海可知矣。
entries.en: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said that when the armory burns, the Di and Qiang rise, and the heir is deposed, the fate of the empire is already clear.
entries.literal: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said: when the armory burns, the Di and Qiang rebel, and the crown prince is deposed—then the fate of all within the four seas can be known.

entries.zh: 元康八年十一月，高原陵火。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the eighth Yuankang year fire struck the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year of Yuankang, the Gaoyuan Mausoleum burned.

entries.zh: 是時賈后凶恣，賈謐擅朝，惡積罪稔，宜見誅絕。
entries.en: At the time Empress Jia was brutal and overbearing and Jia Mi dominated the court; their crimes had piled high and they ought to have been destroyed.
entries.literal: At that time Empress Jia was fierce and unrestrained, Jia Mi monopolized the court; evil had accumulated and guilt was ripe—they ought to have been executed.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，臣妾之不可者，雖親貴莫比，猶宜忍而誅之，如吾燔高原陵也。
entries.en: Heaven seemed to warn that even the closest and most exalted minister or consort, when intolerable, must be struck down—as it had burned the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.
entries.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: what must not be tolerated in ministers and consorts, though none be closer or nobler, should still be endured only long enough to execute them—as I have burned the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 帝既眊弱，而張華又不納裴頠、劉卞之謀，故后遂與謐誣殺太子也。
entries.en: The emperor was already feeble, and Zhang Hua refused the counsel of Pei Song and Liu Bian, so the empress and Mi conspired to destroy the heir apparent.
entries.literal: The emperor was already dim-eyed and weak, and Zhang Hua did not adopt the plans of Pei Song and Liu Bian, so the empress then joined with Mi to frame and kill the crown prince.

entries.zh: 干寶云：「高原陵火，太子廢，其應也。
entries.en: Gan Bao wrote, "Fire at the Gaoyuan Mausoleum and the heir's deposition were the same omen fulfilled.
entries.literal: Gan Bao said: "When the Gaoyuan Mausoleum burned, the crown prince was deposed—this was the response.

entries.zh: 漢武帝世，高園便殿火，董仲舒對與此占同。」
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu of Han the Gaoyuan side hall burned, and Dong Zhongshu's interpretation matched this reading."
entries.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu of Han, the side hall of the Gaoyuan burned; Dong Zhongshu's response used the same prognostication."

entries.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘；
entries.en: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth Yuankang year a mulberry sprouted in the western wing of the Eastern Palace and grew more than a chi a day;
entries.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, a mulberry tree grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, growing more than a chi a day;

entries.zh: 甲辰，枯死。
entries.en: by the jiachen day it had withered away.
entries.literal: on the jiachen day it withered and died.

entries.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖。
entries.en: This matched the prodigy of Emperor Taiwu of Yin.
entries.literal: This was the same prodigy as under Emperor Taiwu of Yin.

entries.zh: 太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。
entries.en: The crown prince failed to understand, and was deposed and killed.
entries.literal: The crown prince could not understand, and therefore came to deposition and execution.

entries.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危亡國家，象朝將為墟也」。
entries.en: Ban Gu wrote, "When wild trees spring up in the court and grow violently, petty men will seize the posts of great ministers, endanger the state, and the court itself will become a ruin."
entries.literal: Ban Gu said: "When wild trees grow in the court and shoot up violently, petty men will violently occupy the positions of great ministers, endangering and destroying the state—the court will become a ruin."

entries.zh: 是後孫秀、張林尋用事，遂至大亂。
entries.en: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon seized power, and the realm fell into great chaos.
entries.literal: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon held power, and great disorder followed.

entries.zh: 永康元年四月，壯武國有桑化為柏。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the first Yongkang year a mulberry in Zhuangwu Principality turned into a cypress.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongkang, in Zhuangwu Principality a mulberry tree transformed into a cypress.

entries.zh: 是月，張華遇害。
entries.en: That month Zhang Hua was killed.
entries.literal: That month, Zhang Hua met with murder.

entries.zh: 孟懷玉，平昌安丘人也。
entries.en: Meng Huaiyu was a native of Anqiu in Pingchang.
entries.literal: Meng Huaiyu was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang.

entries.zh: 高祖珩，晉河南尹。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's father Heng had been Jin administrator of Henan.
entries.literal: The Gaozu's father Heng was Jin Administrator of Henan.

entries.zh: 祖淵，右光祿大夫。
entries.en: His grandfather Yuan was right grand master for splendid happiness.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yuan was Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 父綽，義旗後為給事中，光祿勳，追贈金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Chuo, after the founding uprising, became palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness, and was posthumously made grand master for the palace with golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: His father Chuo, after the righteous banner was raised, became Palace Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was posthumously given Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 世居京口。
entries.en: The family had long lived at Jingkou.
entries.literal: For generations they dwelt at Jingkou.

entries.zh: 列傳第七 劉懷肅 孟懷玉
entries.en: Biographies 7: Liu Huaisu and Meng Huaiyu
entries.literal: Biographies 7: Liu Huaisu, Meng Huaiyu

entries.zh: 〈弟龍符〉
entries.en: 〈Younger brother Longfu〉
entries.literal: 〈Younger brother Longfu〉

entries.zh: 劉敬宣 檀祗
entries.en: Liu Jingxuan and Tan Zhi
entries.literal: Liu Jingxuan, Tan Zhi

entries.zh: 毛脩之
entries.en: Mao Xiuzhi
entries.literal: Mao Xiuzhi

entries.zh: 毛脩之，字敬文，滎陽陽武人也。
entries.en: Mao Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Jingwen, came from Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.
entries.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, courtesy name Jingwen, was a man of Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.

entries.zh: 祖虎生，伯父璩，並益州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Husheng and his uncle Quan had both been Inspectors of Yizhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Husheng and his paternal uncle Quan both served as Inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 父瑾，梁、秦二州刺史。
entries.en: His father Jin held the Liang and Qin inspectorates.
entries.literal: His father Jin was Inspector of Liang and of Qin.

entries.zh: 脩之有大志，頗讀史籍，荊州刺史殷仲堪以為寧遠參軍。
entries.en: He harbored large designs, steeped himself in historical works, and Yin Zhongkan appointed him Pacifying-the-Distant staff officer.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi had great ambitions, read histories widely, and Yin Zhongkan made him Pacifying-the-Distant staff officer.

entries.zh: 桓玄克荊州，仍為玄佐，歷後軍、太尉、相國參軍。
entries.en: Huan Xuan seized Jingzhou and kept him as aide, through the Rear Army, Grand Marshal, and Chancellor's offices in turn.
entries.literal: When Huan Xuan took Jingzhou, Xiuzhi remained on Xuan's staff, serving successively on the Rear Army, Grand Marshal, and Chancellor's staffs.

entries.zh: 解音律，能騎射，玄甚遇之。
entries.en: He mastered pitch and horsemanship; Xuan favored him greatly.
entries.literal: He understood music and could ride and shoot; Xuan treated him with exceptional favor.

entries.zh: 及篡位，以為屯騎校尉。
entries.en: At Xuan's usurpation he became Commandant of the Escort Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne, he was made Commandant of the Escort Cavalry.

entries.zh: 隨玄西奔，玄敗於崢嶸洲，復還江陵，人情離散，議欲西奔漢川。
entries.en: He fled west with Xuan; after defeat at Zhengrong Isle they returned to Jiangling, the host melting away, and some urged flight into Hanzhong.
entries.literal: He followed Xuan west in flight; when Xuan was defeated at Zhengrong Isle and returned to Jiangling, morale dissolved, and the court debated fleeing west to Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 脩之誘令入蜀，馮遷斬玄於枚回洲，脩之力也。
entries.en: Xiuzhi steered them into Shu; Feng Qian cut Xuan down at Meihui Isle on his counsel.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi persuaded them to enter Shu; Feng Qian beheaded Xuan at Meihui Isle—Xiuzhi's doing.

entries.zh: 晉安帝反正於江陵，除驍騎將軍。
entries.en: After Emperor An's restoration at Jiangling he was named General of Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor An was restored at Jiangling, Xiuzhi was made General of Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 下至京師，高祖以為鎮軍諮議參軍，加寧朔將軍。
entries.en: Downriver at the capital the Gaozu gave him consultative staff rank on the Pacifying Army and the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: When he reached the capital the Gaozu made him consultative staff officer of the Pacifying Army and added the title General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 旬月，遷右衛將軍。
entries.en: A month later he rose to General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: Within a month he was promoted to General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 既有斬玄之謀，又伯、父並在蜀土，高祖欲引為外助，故頻加榮爵。
entries.en: He had helped kill Xuan, and his father's and uncles' power still sat in Shu; the Gaozu courted him as a western lever and piled honors on him.
entries.literal: Because he had plotted Xuan's death and because his uncles and father still held lands in Shu, the Gaozu wished to win him as an outside ally and therefore repeatedly heaped honors upon him.

entries.zh: 及父瑾為譙縱所殺，高祖表為龍驤將軍，配給兵力，遣令奔赴。
entries.en: After Qiao Zong slew his father Jin, the Gaozu petitioned for Dragon-Prancing General, gave him troops, and sent him west.
entries.literal: When his father Jin was killed by Qiao Zong, the Gaozu memorialized him as Dragon-Prancing General, allotted troops, and ordered him to march west.

entries.zh: 又遣益州刺史司馬榮期及文處茂、時延祖等西討。
entries.en: He dispatched Sima Rongqi, Inspector of Yizhou, with Wen Chumao, Shi Yanzu, and others in the western expedition.
entries.literal: He also sent the Inspector of Yizhou Sima Rongqi with Wen Chumao, Shi Yanzu, and others on a western punitive campaign.

entries.zh: 脩之至宕渠，榮期為參軍楊承祖所殺，承祖自稱鎮軍將軍、巴州刺史。
entries.en: At Dangqu, Rongqi fell to his aide Yang Chengzu, who proclaimed himself Pacifying-Army general and Inspector of Ba.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi reached Dangqu, but Rongqi was killed by his staff officer Yang Chengzu, who styled himself General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Bazhou.

entries.zh: 脩之退還白帝，承祖自下攻之，不拔。
entries.en: Xiuzhi fell back to Baidi; Chengzu assailed from downstream and failed.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi withdrew to Baidi; Chengzu attacked from below but could not take it.

entries.zh: 脩之使參軍嚴綱等收兵眾，漢嘉太守馮遷率兵來會，討承祖斬之。
entries.en: He sent Yan Gang to rally the host; Feng Qian, Administrator of Hanjia, marched in, and they slew Chengzu.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi sent his staff officer Yan Gang and others to gather troops; the Administrator of Hanjia Feng Qian led soldiers to join him, and they attacked and beheaded Chengzu.

entries.zh: 時文處茂猶在巴郡，脩之遣振武將軍張季仁五百兵係處茂等。
entries.en: Chumao remained in Ba; Xiuzhi detached Zhang Jiren, General Who Quells Barbarians, with five hundred to coordinate with him.
entries.literal: Wen Chumao was still in Ba commandery; Xiuzhi sent the General Who Quells Barbarians Zhang Jiren with five hundred men to link with Chumao.

entries.zh: 荊州刺史道規又遣奮武將軍原導之領千人，受脩之節度。
entries.en: Inspector Daogui of Jingzhou added Yuan Daozhi, General Who Inspires Might, with a thousand men under Xiuzhi's command.
entries.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui also sent the General Who Inspires Might Yuan Daozhi with a thousand men to take orders from Xiuzhi.

entries.zh: 脩之遣原導之與季仁俱進。
entries.en: Xiuzhi pushed Daozhi and Jiren ahead in concert.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi sent Yuan Daozhi and Jiren forward together.

entries.zh: 時益州刺史鮑陋不肯進討，脩之下都上表曰：「臣聞在生所以重生，實有生理可保。
entries.en: Inspector Bao Lou refused to press the attack; Xiuzhi descended to the capital and memorialized: "I hear that the living may be reborn when a way to preserve life remains.
entries.literal: At that time the Inspector of Yizhou Bao Lou would not advance to attack; Xiuzhi went down to the capital and submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that while one lives one may be reborn because there is a path of life that can be preserved.

entries.zh: 臣之情地，生途已竭，所以未淪於泉壤，借命於朝露者，以日月貞照，有兼映之輝，庶憑天威，誅夷仇逆。
entries.en: My own road is spent; I linger above the grave only because the throne's light still falls on me, and I trust to imperial might to destroy the murderer.
entries.literal: In my own case the road of life is already spent; the reason I have not yet sunk into the yellow earth but borrow my life from the morning dew is that sun and moon shine with a radiance that can reflect upon me alike, and I hope by Heaven's majesty to exterminate my foe.

entries.zh: 自提戈西赴，備嘗時難，遂使齊斧停柯，狡豎假息。
entries.en: Since I marched west every trial of the campaign has left the axe idle and the traitor breathing still.
entries.literal: Since I took spear and went west I have tasted every hardship of the hour, yet the executioner's axe halted mid-stroke and the cunning rebel still breathes.

entries.zh: 誠由經路有暨，亦緣制不自己。
entries.en: The roads were barred—and I was not free to command.
entries.literal: Truly the route was blocked, yet it was also that I was not master of my own measures.

entries.zh: 撫影窮號，泣望西路。
entries.en: I clutch my shadow and cry toward the west.
entries.literal: I clutch my shadow and wail, weeping as I gaze west.

entries.zh: 益州刺史陋始以四月二十九日達巴東，頓白帝，以俟廟略。
entries.en: Inspector Lou reached Badong on the twenty-ninth of the fourth month and camped at Baidi awaiting the court's plan.
entries.literal: Inspector Lou of Yizhou first reached Badong on the twenty-ninth of the fourth month and halted at Baidi to await the court's grand design.

entries.zh: 可乘之機宜踐，投袂之會屢愆。
entries.en: Every chance to strike he let slip; every call to lash his sleeve he ignored.
entries.literal: Occasions that could be seized he let pass; moments that demanded a swift sleeve he missed again and again.

entries.zh: 臣雖效死寇庭，而理絕救援，是以束骸載馳，訴冤象魏。
entries.en: Though I would die in the enemy camp, no aid could reach me; I raced here with bound bones to cry injustice at the palace gate.
entries.literal: Though I would die in the rebels' court, rescue was cut off by reason; therefore I bound my bones and raced here to plead my grievance before the imperial gate.

entries.zh: 昔宋害申丹，楚莊有遺履之憤，況忘家殉國，尠有臣門，節冠風霜，人所矜悼。
entries.en: When Song killed Shen Dan, King Zhuang of Chu raged over a sandal left behind; how much more a house that gives family for the realm—a gate rare in its season, a loyalty that outlasts frost and draws every man's grief.
entries.literal: Of old Song harmed Shen Dan and King Zhuang of Chu nursed the fury of a sandal left behind; how much more when one forgets family to die for the state—few houses can show such a gate, a steadfastness that crowns the wind and frost and moves all who know it to pity.

entries.zh: 伍員不虧君義，而申包不忘國艱，俟會佇鋒，因時乃發。
entries.en: Wu Zixu kept faith with his prince; Shen Bao remembered the realm's peril—they waited the hour and struck when it came.
entries.literal: Wu Yuan did not fail his lord's righteousness, and Shen Bao did not forget the state's straits; they waited for the moment and struck when the hour came.

entries.zh: 今臣庸逾在昔，未蒙宵邁之旗，是以仰辰極以希照，眷西土以灑淚也。
entries.en: My deeds are meaner than theirs, and no night-marching banner has been raised for me; I look to the pole star for light and to the west for tears.
entries.literal: Today my merit falls short of those men of old, and I have not received the banner that marches by night; therefore I lift my face to the pole star hoping for light and turn my gaze to the western lands to shed tears.

entries.zh: 公私懷恥，仰望洪恩，豈宜遂享名器，比肩人伍。
entries.en: Shame grips court and camp; we beg imperial grace—how can I still wear golden purple and rank with the multitude?
entries.literal: Public and private alike burn with shame; we look up for great grace—how should I still enjoy famous offices and stand shoulder to shoulder with the common ranks?

entries.zh: 求情既所不容，即實又非所繼，但以方仗威靈，要須綜攝，乞解金紫寵私之榮，賜以鷹揚折衝之號。
entries.en: Feeling forbids it and fact cannot bear it; yet the campaign needs a single hand on the reins—I beg to shed gilded rank and take the hawk-banners of the shock commander.
entries.literal: Sentiment will not allow it, and the reality cannot sustain it; yet because I must wield authority in the field, command must be unified—I beg to lay aside the glory of gold and purple favor and be granted the title that soars like hawk and breaks the foe.

entries.zh: 臣之於國，理無虛請。
entries.en: Toward the throne my plea is not hollow.
entries.literal: Toward the state I have no empty request.

entries.zh: 自臣涉道，情慮荒越，疹毒交纏，常慮性命隕越，要當躬先士卒，身馳賊庭，手斬凶醜，以攄莫大之釁。
entries.en: On this path my mind reels and sickness knots me; I expect death daily, yet I will ride before the ranks, burst their camp, and with my own blade kill the arch-criminal to wash away the gravest stain.
entries.literal: Since I entered this road my thoughts have run wild and plagues entwine; I constantly fear my life will fail, yet I mean to lead the soldiers myself, charge the rebels' camp, and with my own hand cut down the chief villain to expiate the greatest guilt.

entries.zh: 然後就死之日，即化如歸，闔門靈爽，豈不謝先帝於玄宮。」
entries.en: Then when death comes I shall go as to my own hearth, and the shades of my line will thank the late emperor in the hidden court."
entries.literal: Then on the day I go to die I shall transform as though returning home, and every spirit of my house will thank the late emperor in the dark palace."

entries.zh: 高祖哀其情事，乃命冠軍將軍劉敬宣率文處茂、時延祖諸軍伐蜀。
entries.en: The Gaozu, grieving at his words, sent Champion General Liu Jingxuan with Chumao, Yanzu, and the host against Shu.
entries.literal: The Gaozu, moved by his plea, then ordered Champion General Liu Jingxuan to lead Wen Chumao, Shi Yanzu, and the armies to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 軍次黃虎，無功而退。
entries.en: The army camped at Huanghu and retreated empty-handed.
entries.literal: The army halted at Huanghu and withdrew without success.

entries.zh: 譙縱由此送脩之父、伯及中表喪，口累並得俱還。
entries.en: Qiao Zong returned Xiuzhi's father, uncles, and cousins in their coffins, every bier permitted home.
entries.literal: Qiao Zong thereupon sent back Xiuzhi's father, uncles, and maternal kin—all the coffins together were allowed to return.

entries.zh: 傅弘之，字仲度，北地泥陽人。
entries.en: Fu Hongzhi, whose courtesy name was Zhongdu, came from Niyang in Beidi.
entries.literal: Fu Hongzhi, courtesy name Zhongdu, was a man of Niyang in Beidi.

entries.zh: 傅氏舊屬靈州，漢末郡境為虜所侵，失土寄寓馮翊，置泥陽、富平二縣，靈州廢不立，故傅氏還屬泥陽。
entries.en: The Fu line once belonged to Lingzhou; at Han's end barbarians overran the district, they lost their lands and settled in Fengyi, where Niyang and Fuping were founded and Lingzhou abolished—so the Fu returned to Niyang.
entries.literal: The Fu clan had originally belonged to Lingzhou; in the chaos at the end of Han the commandery lands were overrun by barbarians, they lost their territory and lodged in Fengyi, where the counties Niyang and Fuping were established and Lingzhou was abolished and not re-established—therefore the Fu clan came again under Niyang.

entries.zh: 晉武帝太康三年，復立靈州縣，傅氏悉屬靈州。
entries.en: In Taikang year 3 of Emperor Wu, Lingzhou was restored and all the Fu reverted to it.
entries.literal: In the third year of Emperor Wu's Taikang era Lingzhou county was re-established, and the entire Fu clan again belonged to Lingzhou.

entries.zh: 弘之高祖晉司徒祗，後封靈州公，不欲封本縣，故祗一門還復泥陽。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Zhi, Jin Minister of Works, was later made Duke of Lingzhou but refused a fief in his home county, so that branch alone returned to Niyang.
entries.literal: Hongzhi's great-grandfather Zhi, Jin's Minister of Works, was later enfeoffed Duke of Lingzhou but did not wish to be enfeoffed in his native county—therefore Zhi's household alone returned again to Niyang.

entries.zh: 曾祖暢，秘書丞，沒胡，生子洪，晉穆帝永和中，胡亂得還。
entries.en: Grandfather Chang, Secretariat Director, died among the barbarians and left Hong; in Emperor Mu's Yonghe era he came back through the chaos.
entries.literal: His grandfather Chang, Secretariat Director, perished among the barbarians and begot Hong; in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, amid barbarian turmoil he was able to return.

entries.zh: 洪生韶，梁州刺史，散騎常侍。
entries.en: Hong fathered Shao, Inspector of Liang and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: Hong begot Shao, Inspector of Liangzhou and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 韶生弘之。
entries.en: Shao fathered Hongzhi.
entries.literal: Shao begot Hongzhi.

entries.zh: 列傳第八 朱齡石
entries.en: Biographies 8: Zhu Lingshi
entries.literal: Biographies 8: Zhu Lingshi

entries.zh: 〈弟超石〉
entries.en: 〈Younger brother Chaoshi〉
entries.literal: 〈Younger brother Chaoshi〉

entries.zh: 毛脩之 傅弘之
entries.en: Mao Xiuzhi and Fu Hongzhi
entries.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi

entries.zh: 孫處，字季高，會稽永興人也。
entries.en: Sun Chu, whose courtesy name was Jigao, was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji commandery.
entries.literal: Sun Chu, courtesy name Jigao, was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji commandery.

entries.zh: 籍注季高，故字行於世。
entries.en: His name was entered in the register as Jigao, and that courtesy name is the one by which he was known.
entries.literal: His household register recorded Jigao, so that courtesy name was used in the world.

entries.zh: 少任氣。
entries.en: As a young man he was quick to take offense and act on impulse.
entries.literal: In youth he was given to hot-tempered action.

entries.zh: 高祖東征孫恩，季高義樂隨。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor marched east against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed him out of loyalty.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned east against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed out of righteousness.

entries.zh: 高祖平定京邑，以為振武將軍，封新夷縣五等侯。
entries.en: After the Founding Emperor secured the capital, he appointed Sun Chu General Who Quells Martiality and enfeoffed him as a fifth-rank marquis of Xin'yi county.
entries.literal: After the Founding Emperor pacified the capital region, he made him General Who Quells Martiality and enfeoffed him as a five-rank marquis of Xin'yi county.

entries.zh: 廣固之役，先登有功。
entries.en: At the siege of Guanggu he was first over the wall and distinguished himself.
entries.literal: At the battle of Guanggu he was first to ascend and had merit.

entries.zh: 八年，除寧蠻護軍、尋陽太守，領文武二年從征劉毅。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was made Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang; leading two thousand civil and military personnel, he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang, holding civil and military authority; two years later he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.

entries.zh: 事平，補太尉行參軍，尋加振威將軍。
entries.en: After the campaign he was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff and soon promoted to General Who Quells Might.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and soon promoted to General Who Quells Might.

entries.zh: 九年，以前後功封望蔡縣男，食邑五百戶，加龍驤將軍。
entries.en: In the ninth year, for his accumulated service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of five hundred households and made General Who Leaps like a Dragon.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, for his accumulated merits he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of five hundred households and promoted to General Who Leaps like a Dragon.

entries.zh: 討司馬休之，又有戰功。
entries.en: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he again distinguished himself.
entries.literal: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he again had battle merit.

entries.zh: 軍還，除輔國將軍、山陽太守。
entries.en: When the army returned he was made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Shanyang.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Shanyang.

entries.zh: 宋臺令書除秦郡太守，督陳留郡事，將軍如故。
entries.en: An order from the Song administration appointed him Administrator of Qin commandery with supervisory authority over Chenliu, while his rank as general remained unchanged.
entries.literal: An order from the Song administration appointed him Administrator of Qin commandery with supervision over Chenliu commandery; his generalship remained as before.

entries.zh: 元熙二年，宋王令書以為高祖第四子義康右將軍司馬。
entries.en: In the second year of Yuanxi an order from the Prince of Song appointed him Major on the staff of Right General Yikang, the Founding Emperor's fourth son.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanxi, an order from the Prince of Song appointed him Major on the staff of the Right General for the Founding Emperor's fourth son Yikang.

entries.zh: 永初二年，遷太子右衛率。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongchu he was made Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he was transferred to Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

entries.zh: 明年，卒官。
entries.en: The following year he died in office.
entries.literal: The next year he died in office.

entries.zh: 時年六十。
entries.en: He was sixty years old.
entries.literal: He was then sixty years old.

entries.zh: 追論討司馬休之功，進爵為子，增邑三百戶。
entries.en: His service against Sima Xiuzhi was reviewed posthumously; his rank was raised to viscount and his fief increased by three hundred households.
entries.literal: His merit in the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi was reviewed posthumously; his rank was advanced to viscount and his fief increased by three hundred households.

entries.zh: 高祖西征劉毅，恩與王鎮惡輕軍襲江陵，事在鎮惡傳。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor marched west against Liu Yi, En and Wang Zhen'e led light troops in a surprise attack on Jiangling— the full account appears in Zhen'e's biography.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned west against Liu Yi, En with Wang Zhen'e led light troops in a surprise attack on Jiangling; the account is in Zhen'e's biography.

entries.zh: 以本官為太尉長兼行參軍，領眾二千，隨益州刺史朱齡石伐蜀。
entries.en: Retaining his original rank, he served as Clerk of the Grand Commandant with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant, leading two thousand men under Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Lingshi in the campaign against Shu.
entries.literal: Retaining his original office, he served as Clerk of the Grand Commandant with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant, leading two thousand troops following Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Lingshi to campaign against Shu.

entries.zh: 至彭模，恩所領居前，大戰，自朝至日昃，勇氣益奮，賊破走。
entries.en: At Pengmo his detachment led the van in a great battle that raged from morning until late afternoon; his courage only mounted, and the enemy was routed.
entries.literal: At Pengmo, the force En commanded was in the van; in a great battle from morning until the sun slanted west, his courage grew fiercer and the rebels were broken and fled.

entries.zh: 進平成都，擢為行參軍，改封北至縣五等男。
entries.en: After Chengdu was pacified he was promoted to Acting Adjutant and re-enfeoffed as a fifth-rank baron of Beizhi county.
entries.literal: Advancing to pacify Chengdu, he was promoted to Acting Adjutant and re-enfeoffed as a five-rank baron of Beizhi county.

entries.zh: 高祖伐司馬休之及魯宗之，恩與建威將軍徐逵之前進。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, En advanced with General Who Establishes Might Xu Dazhi.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, En advanced together with General Who Establishes Might Xu Dazhi.

entries.zh: 逵之敗沒，恩陳于堤下。
entries.en: When Dazhi was defeated and killed, En drew up his ranks below the dike.
entries.literal: Dazhi was defeated and lost; En formed ranks below the dike.

entries.zh: 宗之子軌乘勝擊恩，矢下如雨，呼聲震地，恩整厲將士，置陣堅嚴。
entries.en: Zongzhi's son Gui pressed his advantage and attacked En; arrows fell like rain and the battle cries shook the earth, but En rallied his men and held his formation firm.
entries.literal: Zongzhi's son Gui, seizing victory, attacked En; arrows fell like rain and shouts shook the earth. En rallied his officers and soldiers and set formations firm and strict.

entries.zh: 軌屢衝之不動，知不可攻，乃退。
entries.en: Gui charged again and again but could not break them; seeing that the attack would not succeed, he withdrew.
entries.literal: Gui charged repeatedly but could not move them; knowing he could not attack successfully, he withdrew.

entries.zh: 高祖善其能將軍持重。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor praised his ability to hold an army steady under pressure.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor praised his ability to command the army with weight and steadiness.

entries.zh: 江陵平定，復追魯軌於石城。
entries.en: After Jiangling was pacified he again pursued Lu Gui at Shicheng.
entries.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, he again pursued Lu Gui at Shicheng.

entries.zh: 軌棄城走，恩追至襄陽，宗之奔羌，恩與諸將追討，至魯陽關乃還。
entries.en: Gui abandoned the city and fled; En pursued him to Xiangyang. Zongzhi fled to the Qiang, and En with the other generals pursued as far as Luyang Pass before turning back.
entries.literal: Gui abandoned the city and fled; En pursued to Xiangyang. Zongzhi fled to the Qiang; En with the generals pursued and attacked to Luyang Pass and then returned.

entries.zh: 恩自從征討，每有危急，輒率先諸將，常陷堅破陣，不避艱嶮。
entries.en: From the time he first took the field, whenever danger arose En led the other generals, repeatedly breaking through strong positions and never shying from hardship or peril.
entries.literal: From the time En followed on campaigns, whenever there was danger he would take the lead among the generals, often breaking through hard positions and smashing formations, never shunning hardship and peril.

entries.zh: 凡百餘戰，身被重創。
entries.en: In more than a hundred battles he suffered grave wounds.
entries.literal: In more than a hundred battles altogether, he suffered grave wounds.

entries.zh: 高祖錄其前後功勞，封新寧縣男，食邑五百戶。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor recorded his accumulated service and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xining county with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor recorded his merits before and after and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xining county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 高祖世子為征虜將軍，恩以大府佐領中兵參軍，隨府轉中兵參軍。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor's heir was made General Who Pacifies Barbarians, En served as Central Army Adjutant on the grand headquarters staff, and when the headquarters moved he retained that post.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor's heir was General Who Pacifies Barbarians, En as grand headquarters aide served as Central Army Adjutant; when the headquarters transferred he became Central Army Adjutant.

entries.zh: 高祖北伐，留恩侍衛世子，命朝士與之交。
entries.en: On the Founding Emperor's northern campaign En was left to guard the heir, and was instructed to keep company with court gentlemen.
entries.literal: On the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, En was left to guard the heir; he was ordered to associate with court gentlemen.

entries.zh: 恩益自謙損，與人語常呼官位，而自稱為鄙人。
entries.en: En grew ever more modest; in conversation he always addressed others by their official titles and called himself "this humble man."
entries.literal: En became ever more humble; when speaking with others he always addressed them by their official titles and called himself "this lowly man."

entries.zh: 撫待士卒，甚有紀綱，眾咸親附之。
entries.en: He treated his soldiers with firm discipline, and they all drew close to him.
entries.literal: In managing soldiers he had strict discipline, and all drew close and attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 遷諮議參軍，轉輔國將軍、淮陵太守。
entries.en: He was promoted to Advisory Adjutant, then transferred to General Who Assists the State and made Administrator of Huailing.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Advisory Adjutant, then transferred to General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Huailing.

entries.zh: 世子開府，又為從事中郎，轉司馬，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: When the heir opened his own headquarters En served as Attendant Secretary, then as Major, while retaining his rank as general and his prefecture.
entries.literal: When the heir opened a headquarters, he again served as Attendant Secretary, then transferred to Major; his generalship and prefecture remained as before.

entries.zh: 入關迎桂陽公義真。
entries.en: He entered the passes to meet the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen.
entries.literal: He entered the passes to meet the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen.

entries.zh: 義真還至青泥，為佛佛虜所追，恩斷後，力戰連日。
entries.en: When Yizhen reached Qingni on his return, the Babao barbarians pursued him; En covered the rear and fought fiercely for days on end.
entries.literal: When Yizhen returned to Qingni, he was pursued by the Babao barbarians; En covered the rear and fought fiercely for days.

entries.zh: 義真前軍奔散，恩軍人亦盡，為虜所執，死於虜中。
entries.en: Yizhen's vanguard broke and fled; En's men were also spent, and he was captured by the enemy and died in captivity.
entries.literal: Yizhen's vanguard scattered and fled; En's soldiers were also exhausted; he was captured by the barbarians and died among them.

entries.zh: 子國才嗣。
entries.en: His son Guocai succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Guocai succeeded.

entries.zh: 國才卒，子慧度嗣。
entries.en: When Guocai died, his son Huidu succeeded.
entries.literal: Guocai died; his son Huidu succeeded.

entries.zh: 慧度卒，無子，國除。
entries.en: When Huidu died without an heir, the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Huidu died without a son; the fief was abolished.

entries.zh: 從平京城，進定京邑，以寧遠將軍領幢。
entries.en: He followed the pacification of the capital and the securing of the capital region, and was made General of Distant Pacification with command of the standard-bearer guard.
entries.literal: He followed in pacifying the capital and then securing the capital region, and was appointed General of Distant Pacification to command the standard-bearer guard.

entries.zh: 隨振武將軍道規西討，虜桓仙客，克偃月壘，遂平江陵。
entries.en: He followed General Who Quells Martiality Daogui on the western campaign, captured Huan Xianke, took Yanyue fortress, and pacified Jiangling.
entries.literal: Following General Who Quells Martiality Daogui west on campaign, he captured Huan Xianke, took Yanyue fortress, and pacified Jiangling.

entries.zh: 義熙二年，賊張堅據應城反，恩擊破之，封都鄉侯。
entries.en: In the second year of Yixi the rebel Zhang Jian seized Yingcheng and rose in revolt; En defeated him and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yixi, the rebel Zhang Jian held Yingcheng and rebelled; En defeated him and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.

entries.zh: 從伐廣固，又有戰功。
entries.en: He joined the campaign against Guanggu and again distinguished himself in battle.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Guanggu and again had battle merit.

entries.zh: 盧循逼京邑，恩戰於查浦，賊退走。
entries.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, En fought at Zhapu and drove the rebels back.
entries.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, En fought at Zhapu and the rebels retreated and fled.

entries.zh: 與王仲德等追破循別將范崇民於南陵。
entries.en: With Wang Zhongde and others he pursued and defeated Lu Xun's deputy commander Fan Chongmin at Nanling.
entries.literal: With Wang Zhongde and others he pursued and defeated Lu Xun's deputy commander Fan Chongmin at Nanling.

entries.zh: 循既走還廣州，恩又領千餘人隨劉藩追徐道覆於始興，斬之。
entries.en: After Xun fled back to Guangzhou, En led more than a thousand men under Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and killed him.
entries.literal: After Xun had fled back to Guangzhou, En again led more than a thousand men following Liu Fan to pursue Xu Daofu at Shixing and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、蘭陵太守。
entries.en: He was promoted to General Who Leaps like a Dragon and made Administrator of Lanling.
entries.literal: He was promoted to General Who Leaps like a Dragon and Administrator of Lanling.

entries.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，前軍將軍道憐留鎮東府，領屯兵。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor marched against Sima Xiuzhi, Vanguard Army General Daolian remained to guard the Eastern Palace and command the garrison troops.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Vanguard Army General Daolian remained to guard the Eastern Palace and command the garrison troops.

entries.zh: 冶亭羣盜數百夜襲鍾壘，距擊破之。
entries.en: Several hundred bandits at Yeting raided Zhong's camp by night; he fought them off and routed them.
entries.literal: Several hundred bandits at Yeting raided Zhong's camp by night; he held them off and defeated them.

entries.zh: 時大軍外討，京邑擾懼，鍾以不能鎮遏，降號建威將軍。
entries.en: While the main army was away on campaign the capital was thrown into alarm; because Zhong could not restore order, his title was reduced to General Who Establishes Might.
entries.literal: At the time the main army was campaigning abroad and the capital was thrown into alarm and fear; because Zhong could not keep order, his title was reduced to General Who Establishes Might.

entries.zh: 平蜀功，應封四百戶男，以先有封爵，減戶以賜次子敬順高昌縣男，食邑百戶。
entries.en: For his service in pacifying Shu he was due a barony of four hundred households; because he already held a title, the grant was reduced and his second son Jingshun was made Baron of Gaochang county with a fief of one hundred households.
entries.literal: For his merit in pacifying Shu he should have been enfeoffed as a baron with a fief of four hundred households; because he already held a title, households were reduced and his second son Jingshun was granted Baron of Gaochang county with a fief of one hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋復本號龍驤將軍。
entries.en: Soon his former rank of General Who Leaps like a Dragon was restored.
entries.literal: Soon his former title of General Who Leaps like a Dragon was restored.

entries.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，復留鎮居守，增其兵力，又命府置佐史。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, when the Founding Emperor marched north, Zhong was again left to guard the capital; his forces were increased, and he was ordered to appoint staff assistants and clerks for his headquarters.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, on the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, Zhong was again left to guard the capital; his military strength was increased, and he was ordered to appoint staff assistants and clerks for his headquarters.

entries.zh: 荊州刺史道憐獻名馬三匹，并精麗乘具，高祖悉以賜鍾三子。
entries.en: Inspector of Jingzhou Daolian presented three famous horses with fine harness and riding gear, and the Founding Emperor gave them all to Zhong's three sons.
entries.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Daolian presented three famous horses together with fine harness and riding gear; the Founding Emperor gave them all to Zhong's three sons.

entries.zh: 十四年，遷右衞將軍，龍驤將軍如故。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was made Right Guards General, while retaining his rank as General Who Leaps like a Dragon.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Right Guards General, while his rank as General Who Leaps like a Dragon remained unchanged.

entries.zh: 元熙元年卒，時年四十三。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanxi he died at the age of forty-three.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he died, aged forty-three.

entries.zh: 盧循之難，於石頭捍柵，戍越城、查浦，破賊於新亭。
entries.en: During Lu Xun's rebellion he held the palisade at Shitou, garrisoned Yuecheng and Zhapu, and routed the rebels at Xinting.
entries.literal: During the crisis of Lu Xun, he defended the palisade at Shitou, garrisoned Yuecheng and Zhapu, and defeated the rebels at Xinting.

entries.zh: 高祖謂季高曰：「此賊行破，應先傾其巢窟，令奔走之日，無所歸投，非卿莫能濟事。」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor told Jigao, "These rebels are on the verge of collapse. We must first destroy their base, so that when they flee they have nowhere to go. No one but you can see this through."
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor said to Jigao: "These rebels will soon be broken. We should first overturn their nest and stronghold, so that on the day they flee they will have nowhere to turn. No one but you can accomplish this."

entries.zh: 遣季高率眾三千，汎海襲番禺。
entries.en: He sent Jigao with three thousand men across the sea to strike Panyu.
entries.literal: He dispatched Jigao to lead three thousand men across the sea to strike Panyu.

entries.zh: 初，賊不以海道為防，季高至東衝，去城十餘里，城內猶未知。
entries.en: At first the rebels had not guarded the sea route. Jigao reached Dongchong, little more than ten li from the city, and those within still knew nothing of his approach.
entries.literal: At first the rebels did not guard against the sea route. Jigao reached Dongchong, more than ten li from the city, and those inside still did not know.

entries.zh: 循守戰士猶有數千人，城池甚固。
entries.en: Xun still had several thousand defenders, and the city was strongly fortified.
entries.literal: Xun's defending soldiers still numbered several thousand, and the city walls were very strong.

entries.zh: 季高先焚舟艦，悉力登岸，會天大霧，四面陵城，即日克拔。
entries.en: Jigao burned his ships, landed with all his strength, and— as a heavy fog rolled in— assaulted the city from every side and took it that same day.
entries.literal: Jigao first burned his boats and ships, then exerted all his strength to go ashore. Heaven sent a great fog; from all four sides he scaled the city and took it the same day.

entries.zh: 循父嘏、長史孫建之、司馬虞尪夫等，輕舟奔始興。
entries.en: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, Major Yu Wangfu, and others escaped in light boats to Shixing.
entries.literal: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, Major Yu Wangfu, and others fled in light boats to Shixing.

entries.zh: 即分遣振武將軍沈田子等討平始興、南康、臨賀、始安嶺表諸郡。
entries.en: He then sent General Who Quells Martiality Shen Tianzi and others to subdue Shixing, Nankang, Linhe, Shi'an, and the other commanderies beyond the Ling range.
entries.literal: He then dispatched General Who Quells Martiality Shen Tianzi and others to pacify Shixing, Nankang, Linhe, Shi'an, and the various commanderies south of the Ling mountains.

entries.zh: 循於左里奔走，而眾力猶盛，自嶺道還襲廣州。
entries.en: Xun was in flight at Zuoli, but his army was still formidable, and he came back over the mountain passes to strike Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Xun was in flight at Zuoli, but his forces were still strong; he returned by the Ling route to strike Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 季高距戰二十餘日，循乃破走，所殺萬餘人。
entries.en: Jigao fought him off for more than twenty days until Xun was routed and fled; more than ten thousand were killed.
entries.literal: Jigao held him off in battle for more than twenty days; Xun was then broken and fled, and more than ten thousand were slain.

entries.zh: 追奔至鬱林，會病，不得窮討，循遂得走向交州。
entries.en: He pursued the fugitives as far as Yulin, but fell ill and could not finish the hunt, and Xun escaped toward Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: Pursuing the fugitives to Yulin, he fell ill and could not pursue to the end, so Xun was able to flee toward Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 義熙七年四月，季高卒於晉康，時年五十三。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Yixi, Jigao died at Jinkang at the age of fifty-three.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Yixi, Jigao died at Jinkang, aged fifty-three.

entries.zh: 追贈龍驤將軍、南海太守，封侯官縣侯，食邑千戶。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made General Who Leaps like a Dragon and Administrator of Nanhai, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Houguan county with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Leaps like a Dragon and Administrator of Nanhai, enfeoffed as Marquis of Houguan county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 九年，高祖念季高之功，乃表曰：「孫季高嶺南之勳，已蒙褒贈。
entries.en: In the ninth year, remembering Jigao's service, the Founding Emperor submitted a memorial: "Sun Jigao's exploits in the Lingnan region have already been honored with posthumous rewards.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, the Founding Emperor, mindful of Jigao's merit, submitted a memorial saying: "Sun Jigao's achievements south of the Ling have already received honorable posthumous grants.

entries.zh: 臣更思惟盧循稔惡一紀，據有全域。
entries.en: Yet I further consider that Lu Xun had grown wicked over a full twelve-year cycle and held an entire region.
