entries.literal: Your subject further reflects that Lu Xun accumulated wickedness for a full twelve-year cycle and held an entire region.

entries.zh: 若令根本未拔，投奔有所，招合餘燼，猶能為虞；
entries.en: Had his base not been destroyed and he still had somewhere to flee, he could have rallied the remnants of his force and remained a threat;
entries.literal: If his root and trunk had not been uprooted and he had had somewhere to flee, gathering the embers of his force, he could still have caused trouble;

entries.zh: 縣師遠討，方勤廟筭。
entries.en: and the court would have had to dispatch armies on distant campaigns and labor over strategy in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: the imperial army would have had to campaign far away, and the court would have been busy with strategy in the temple.

entries.zh: 而季高汎海萬里，投命洪流，波激電邁，指日遄至，遂奄定南海，覆其巢窟，使循進退靡依，輕舟遠迸。
entries.en: Instead Jigao crossed ten thousand li of open sea, staking his life on the raging waters; riding wind and wave he arrived within days, swiftly secured Nanhai, and destroyed their stronghold, leaving Xun with nowhere to turn and driving him to flee in light boats.
entries.literal: But Jigao crossed ten thousand li of sea, risking his life in the surging flood; waves leaped and lightning flashed as he arrived within days, then swiftly secured Nanhai and overturned their nest, leaving Xun with nowhere to advance or retreat and forcing him to flee in light boats.

entries.zh: 曾不旬月，妖凶殲殄。
entries.en: In less than a month the rebel scourge was wiped out.
entries.literal: In less than a full month, the demonic rebels were utterly destroyed.

entries.zh: 蕩滌之功，實庸為大。
entries.en: The merit of clearing them away was truly great.
entries.literal: The merit of sweeping them away was truly great.

entries.zh: 往年所贈，猶為未優。
entries.en: The rewards granted in earlier years were still inadequate.
entries.literal: What was granted in previous years was still insufficient.

entries.zh: 愚謂宜更贈一州，即其本號，庶令忠勳不湮，勞臣增厲。」
entries.en: I humbly submit that one further prefecture should be granted posthumously under his former title, so that loyal service may not be forgotten and hardworking ministers may be further inspired."
entries.literal: I humbly propose that one further prefecture be granted posthumously, bearing his former title, so that loyal merit may not be lost and laboring ministers may be further encouraged."

entries.zh: 重贈交州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: Jigao was posthumously made Inspector of Jiaozhou, while his rank as general remained unchanged.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the post of Inspector of Jiaozhou; his generalship remained as before.

entries.zh: 子宗世卒，子欽公嗣。
entries.en: His son Zongshi died, and his grandson Qingong succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Zongshi died; his grandson Qingong succeeded.

entries.zh: 欽公卒，子彥祖嗣。
entries.en: When Qingong died, his son Yanzu succeeded.
entries.literal: Qingong died; his son Yanzu succeeded.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，國除。
entries.en: When Qi accepted the abdication, the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

entries.zh: 義旗將建，高祖版鍾為郡主簿。
entries.en: As the righteous banner was about to be raised, the Founding Emperor commissioned Zhong chief clerk of the commandery.
entries.literal: As the righteous banner was about to be raised, the Founding Emperor issued Zhong a commission as chief clerk of the commandery.

entries.zh: 明日，從入京城。
entries.en: The next day he entered the capital with the army.
entries.literal: The next day he followed into the capital.

entries.zh: 將向京邑，高祖命曰：「預是彭、沛鄉人赴義者，並可依劉主簿。」
entries.en: As they prepared to march on the capital, the Founding Emperor ordered, "All men of Peng and Pei who have risen in the cause may report to Chief Clerk Liu."
entries.literal: When about to march on the capital region, the Founding Emperor ordered: "All who from Peng and Pei country have come out in righteousness may attach themselves to Chief Clerk Liu."

entries.zh: 於是立為義隊，恆在左右，連戰皆捷。
entries.en: A volunteer unit was formed with Zhong always at the Founding Emperor's side, and battle after battle was won.
entries.literal: Thereupon a righteous-force unit was formed with Zhong always at his side; battle after battle was victorious.

entries.zh: 明日，桓謙屯於東陵，卞範之屯覆舟山西，高祖疑賊有伏兵，顧視左右，正見鍾，謂之曰：「此山下當有伏兵，卿可率部下稍往撲之。」
entries.en: The next day Huan Qian encamped at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou mountain. Suspecting an ambush, the Founding Emperor looked about and spotted Zhong. "There are likely hidden troops on this hillside," he said. "Take your men forward and flush them out."
entries.literal: The next day Huan Qian encamped at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi at west of Fuzhou mountain. The Founding Emperor suspected the enemy had hidden troops; looking left and right, he saw Zhong and said to him: "There ought to be hidden troops below this mountain. You may lead your subordinates a little ways forward to flush them out."

entries.zh: 鍾應聲馳進，果有伏兵數百，一時奔走。
entries.en: Zhong galloped forward at once; sure enough, several hundred hidden troops broke and fled.
entries.literal: Zhong at once galloped forward; indeed there were several hundred hidden troops who all fled at once.

entries.zh: 桓玄西奔，其夕，高祖止桓謙故營，遣鍾宿據東府，轉鎮軍參軍督護。
entries.en: Huan Xuan fled west; that evening the Founding Emperor camped at Huan Qian's former position and sent Zhong to hold the Eastern Palace. Zhong was then made Inspector-and-Protector on the Army Pacification General's staff.
entries.literal: Huan Xuan fled west; that evening the Founding Emperor halted at Huan Qian's former camp and sent Zhong to garrison the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to Inspector-and-Protector under the Army Pacification General.

entries.zh: 桓歆寇歷陽，遣鍾助豫州刺史魏詠之討之，歆即奔迸。
entries.en: When Huan Xin raided Liyang, the Founding Emperor sent Zhong to assist Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Yongzhi; Xin fled at once.
entries.literal: Huan Xin raided Liyang; he sent Zhong to assist Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Yongzhi to attack him; Xin at once fled in panic.

entries.zh: 除南齊國內史，封安丘縣五等侯。
entries.en: He was appointed Interior Minister of the principality of Nanqi and enfeoffed as a fifth-rank marquis of Anqiu county.
entries.literal: He was appointed Interior Minister of Nanqi kingdom and enfeoffed as a five-rank marquis of Anqiu county.

entries.zh: 自陳情事，改葬父祖及親屬十喪，高祖厚加資給。
entries.en: He petitioned to reinter his father, grandfather, and ten other relatives; the Founding Emperor generously provided the funds.
entries.literal: He stated his personal circumstances: reburial of his father, grandfather, and ten relatives' funerals; the Founding Emperor generously provided funds.

entries.zh: 轉車騎長史，兼行參軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of Chariots and Cavalry with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of Chariots and Cavalry with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant.

entries.zh: 司馬叔璠與彭城劉謐、劉懷玉等自蕃城攻鄒山，魯郡太守徐邕失守，鍾率軍討平之。
entries.en: Sima Shufan with Liu Mi and Liu Huaiyu of Pengcheng and others attacked Zou mountain from Fancheng; when Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong lost the city, Zhong led troops to suppress them.
entries.literal: Sima Shufan with Liu Mi and Liu Huaiyu of Pengcheng and others attacked Zou mountain from Fancheng; Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong lost the city; Zhong led troops to attack and pacify them.

entries.zh: 從征廣固。
entries.en: He joined the campaign against Guanggu.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Guanggu.

entries.zh: 孟龍符陷沒，鍾率左右直入，取其尸而反。
entries.en: When Meng Longfu was killed in action, Zhong led his personal guard straight into the enemy lines, recovered the body, and returned.
entries.literal: Meng Longfu was killed in action; Zhong led his personal guard straight in, recovered the corpse and returned.

entries.zh: 除振武將軍、中兵參軍，代龍符領廣川太守。
entries.en: He was made General Who Quells Martiality and Central Army Adjutant, succeeding Longfu as Administrator of Guangchuan.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Quells Martiality and Central Army Adjutant, succeeding Longfu as Administrator of Guangchuan.

entries.zh: 蒯恩，字道恩，蘭陵承人也。
entries.en: Kuai En, whose courtesy name was Daoen, was a native of Cheng in Lanling commandery.
entries.literal: Kuai En, courtesy name Daoen, was a man of Cheng in Lanling commandery.

entries.zh: 高祖征孫恩，縣差為征民，充乙士，使伐馬芻。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor marched against Sun En, the county drafted him for the campaign as a second-class soldier and set him to cutting horse fodder.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Sun En, the county conscripted him as campaign labor, assigning him as a second-class soldier to cut horse fodder.

entries.zh: 恩常負大束，兼倍餘人，每捨芻於地，歎曰：「大丈夫彎弓三石，柰何充馬士！」
entries.en: En often carried huge bundles— more than twice what the others could manage— and each time he dropped his load he would sigh, "A man who can draw a three-stone bow— and yet here I am cutting fodder like a stable hand!"
entries.literal: En often carried large bundles, more than twice what others carried; each time he set fodder on the ground he sighed: "A great man who can draw a three-stone bow— why am I serving as horse fodder labor!"

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，即給器仗，恩大喜。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor heard this, he immediately gave En weapons and armor, and En was overjoyed.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor heard this, he immediately gave him weapons and armor; En was greatly delighted.

entries.zh: 自征妖賊，常為先登，多斬首級。
entries.en: From the campaigns against the rebels he was often first over the wall and took many enemy heads.
entries.literal: From the campaigns against demonic rebels, he was often first to ascend and took many heads.

entries.zh: 既習戰陣，膽力過人，誠心忠謹，未嘗有過失，甚見愛信。
entries.en: Once seasoned in battle, his courage and strength surpassed those around him; he was sincerely loyal and careful, never once at fault, and won great trust and favor.
entries.literal: Once practiced in battle formations, his courage and strength exceeded others'; he was sincerely loyal and careful, never committing a fault, and was greatly trusted and favored.

entries.zh: 於婁縣戰，箭中左目。
entries.en: In the fighting at Lou county an arrow struck his left eye.
entries.literal: In battle at Lou county, an arrow struck his left eye.

entries.zh: 劉鍾，字世之，彭城彭城人也。
entries.en: Liu Zhong, whose courtesy name was Shizhi, was a native of Pengcheng in Pengcheng commandery.
entries.literal: Liu Zhong, courtesy name Shizhi, was a man of Pengcheng in Pengcheng commandery.

entries.zh: 少孤，依鄉人中山太守劉回共居。
entries.en: Orphaned in youth, he lived with his fellow townsman Liu Hui, Administrator of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Orphaned young, he lived together with his fellow townsman Liu Hui, Administrator of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 幼有志力，常慷慨於貧賤。
entries.en: Even as a boy he had strength of will, and often burned with ambition despite his poverty and low station.
entries.literal: As a child he had resolution and strength, and often felt passionate indignation in poverty and low station.

entries.zh: 隆安四年，高祖伐孫恩，鍾願從餘姚、浹口攻句章、海鹽、婁縣，皆摧堅陷陣，每有戰功。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Long'an the Founding Emperor marched against Sun En; Zhong volunteered and fought at Juzhang, Haiyan, and Lou county from Yuyao and Jiakou, breaking through every strong position and winning merit in every engagement.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, the Founding Emperor attacked Sun En; Zhong volunteered to follow, attacking Juzhang, Haiyan, and Lou county from Yuyao and Jiakou—all smashing hard positions and breaking formations, with merit in every battle.

entries.zh: 為劉牢之鎮北參軍督護。
entries.en: He served as Inspector-and-Protector under Liu Laozhi, General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: He served as Inspector-and-Protector under Liu Laozhi, General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 高祖每有戎事，鍾不辭艱劇，專心盡力，甚見愛信。
entries.en: Whenever the Founding Emperor took the field, Zhong never shrank from hardship, giving himself wholly to the task, and won great trust and favor.
entries.literal: Whenever the Founding Emperor had military affairs, Zhong never declined hardship and toil, devoting heart and strength; he was greatly trusted and favored.

entries.zh: 高祖討劉毅，鍾率軍繼王鎮惡。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor marched against Liu Yi, Zhong led an army in support of Wang Zhen'e.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Liu Yi, Zhong led troops following Wang Zhen'e.

entries.zh: 江陵平定，仍隨朱齡石伐蜀，為前鋒，由外水至于彭模，去成都二百里。
entries.en: After Jiangling was pacified he again followed Zhu Lingshi against Shu as vanguard, taking the outer water route to Pengmo, two hundred li from Chengdu.
entries.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, he again followed Zhu Lingshi to campaign against Shu as vanguard, going by the outer water route to Pengmo, two hundred li from Chengdu.

entries.zh: 偽冠軍征討督護譙亢等兩岸連營，曾樓重柵，眾號三萬。
entries.en: The enemy Champion General and Campaign Protector Qiao Kang and others had linked camps on both banks with layered towers and heavy palisades; their force was said to number thirty thousand.
entries.literal: The false regime's Champion General and Campaign Protector Qiao Kang and others had linked camps on both banks, with layered towers and heavy palisades, their force proclaimed at thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 鍾于時腳疾不能行，齡石乃詣鍾謀曰：「今天時盛熱，而賊嚴兵固險，攻之未必可拔，祗增疲困。
entries.en: Zhong was then afflicted with a foot ailment and could not walk; Lingshi came to consult him. "The weather is fiercely hot," he said, "and the enemy holds strong positions with a tight defense. An assault may not succeed and will only wear our men down.
entries.literal: Zhong at the time had a foot ailment and could not walk; Lingshi then went to Zhong to consult, saying: "Today the season is fiercely hot, and the enemy holds troops firm in strong positions; an attack may not necessarily succeed and will only increase exhaustion.

entries.zh: 計其人情恇撓，必不久安，且欲養銳息兵，以伺其隙；
entries.en: I reckon their troops are timid and restless and will not hold firm for long. We should conserve our strength, rest the army, and wait for an opening;
entries.literal: I calculate that their men's spirits are timid and unsettled and will not long remain steady; moreover we should nurture sharpness and rest the army to watch for an opening;

entries.zh: 隙而乘之，乃可捷事。
entries.en: and when the moment comes, strike— that is how we can win quickly.
entries.literal: when an opening appears, seize it, and then the affair can be swiftly concluded.

entries.zh: 然決機兩陳，公本有所委，卿意謂何？」
entries.en: Two plans are before us, and the lord originally entrusted this decision to you— what is your view?"
entries.literal: Yet two plans for decision are set forth; the lord originally had someone entrusted— what does your view say?"

entries.zh: 鍾曰：「不然。
entries.en: Zhong replied, "I disagree.
entries.literal: Zhong said: "Not so.

entries.zh: 前揚聲言大眾向內水，譙道福不敢舍涪城。
entries.en: We had spread word that the main army was advancing by the inner water route, so Qiao Daofu did not dare leave Fucheng.
entries.literal: Earlier we proclaimed that the main force was heading by the inner water route, so Qiao Daofu did not dare leave Fucheng.

entries.zh: 今重軍卒至，出其不意，蜀人已破膽矣。
entries.en: Now our main force has arrived unexpectedly, and the Shu troops have already lost their nerve.
entries.literal: Now our heavy army has suddenly arrived, catching them unawares; the men of Shu are already broken in courage.

entries.zh: 賊今阻兵守險，是其懼不敢戰，非能持久堅守也。
entries.en: The enemy holds the passes because they are afraid to fight, not because they can sustain a long defense.
entries.literal: The rebels now block with troops and hold strong positions because they fear and dare not fight; it is not that they can long hold firm.

entries.zh: 因其凶懼，盡銳攻之，其勢必克。
entries.en: Strike now, while they are still terrified, with every available man— we are sure to break them.
entries.literal: Taking advantage of their terror and fear, attack with all sharpness; the momentum will surely overcome them.

entries.zh: 鼓行而進，成都必不能守矣。
entries.en: March in with drums beating, and Chengdu will not be able to hold.
entries.literal: Advancing with drums beating, Chengdu will surely be unable to hold.

entries.zh: 今若緩兵相守，彼將知人虛實，涪軍忽并來力距我，人情既安，良將又集，此求戰不獲，軍食無資，當為蜀子虜耳。」
entries.en: If we hold back now, they will learn our true strength; the Fucheng army may suddenly unite against us. Once their troops regain confidence and their best commanders assemble, we will fail to bring them to battle and run out of provisions— and become prisoners of Shu."
entries.literal: If we now slow the army and stand in stalemate, they will learn our true strength and weakness; the Fucheng army may suddenly join and forcefully resist us. Once their men's spirits are settled and good generals gather, we will seek battle in vain and have no supplies for the army—we will become captives of the Shu people."

entries.zh: 齡石從之。
entries.en: Lingshi accepted his counsel.
entries.literal: Lingshi followed his advice.

entries.zh: 明日進攻，陷其二城，斬其大將侯輝、譙詵，逕平成都。
entries.en: The next day they attacked, took two cities, killed the enemy generals Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, and went on to pacify Chengdu.
entries.literal: The next day they advanced in attack, took two cities, beheaded the enemy generals Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, and straightway pacified Chengdu.

entries.zh: 以廣固功，封永新縣男，食邑五百戶。
entries.en: For his service at Guanggu he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongxin county with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: For merit at Guanggu he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongxin county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 遷給事中、太尉參軍事、龍驤將軍、高陽內史，領石頭戍事。
entries.en: He was promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Army Staff Officer on the Grand Commandant's staff, General Who Leaps like a Dragon, and Interior Minister of Gaoyang, while retaining command of the Shitou garrison.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Army Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant, General Who Leaps like a Dragon, and Interior Minister of Gaoyang, in charge of the garrison at Shitou.

entries.zh: 虞丘進字豫之，東海郯人也。
entries.en: Yu Qiujin, whose courtesy name was Yuzhi, was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.
entries.literal: Yu Qiujin, courtesy name Yuzhi, was a man of Tan in Donghai commandery.

entries.zh: 少時隨謝玄討苻堅，有功，封關內侯。
entries.en: As a young man he followed Xie Xuan against Fu Jian and distinguished himself; he was enfeoffed as Marquis Within the Passes.
entries.literal: In youth he followed Xie Xuan in the campaign against Fu Jian and had merit; he was enfeoffed as Marquis Within the Passes.

entries.zh: 隆安中，從高祖征孫恩，戍句章城，被圍數十日，無日不戰，身被數創。
entries.en: During Long'an he followed the Founding Emperor against Sun En, garrisoned Juzhang, and was besieged for several tens of days; he fought every day and suffered several wounds.
entries.literal: During Long'an he followed the Founding Emperor against Sun En, garrisoned Juzhang city, was besieged for several tens of days, fought every day without exception, and suffered several wounds.

entries.zh: 至餘姚呵浦，破賊張驃，追至海鹽故治及婁縣。
entries.en: At Yuyao Hapu he defeated the rebel Zhang Biao and pursued as far as the former seat of Haiyan and Lou county.
entries.literal: At Yuyao Hapu he defeated the rebel Zhang Biao and pursued to the former seat of Haiyan and Lou county.

entries.zh: 於蒲濤口與孫恩水戰，又被重創。
entries.en: At Putao Ford he fought Sun En on the water and again suffered grave wounds.
entries.literal: At Putao Ford he fought Sun En on the water and again suffered grave wounds.

entries.zh: 追恩至鬱洲，又至石鹿頭，還海鹽大柱，頻戰有功。
entries.en: He pursued En to Yuzhou and then to Shilutou, returned to Haiyan Dazhu, and won merit in repeated engagements.
entries.literal: Pursuing En to Yuzhou and then to Shilutou, he returned to Haiyan Dazhu and repeatedly fought with merit.

entries.zh: 元興元年，又從高祖東征臨海，於石步固與盧循相守二十餘日。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanxing he again followed the Founding Emperor east against Linhai and at Shibu fortress held Lu Xun at bay for more than twenty days.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing he again followed the Founding Emperor east against Linhai and at Shibu fortress faced Lu Xun for more than twenty days.

entries.zh: 二年，又從高祖至東陽，破徐道覆。
entries.en: In the second year he again followed the Founding Emperor to Dongyang and defeated Xu Daofu.
entries.literal: In the second year he again followed the Founding Emperor to Dongyang and defeated Xu Daofu.

entries.zh: 其年，又至臨松穴破賊，追至永嘉千江，又至安固，累戰皆有功。
entries.en: That year he again went to Linsong Pass, defeated the rebels, pursued to Yongjia Qianjiang and then to Angu, and distinguished himself in battle after battle.
entries.literal: That year he again went to Linsong Pass, defeated the rebels, pursued to Yongjia Qianjiang and then to Angu, and in repeated battles all had merit.

entries.zh: 三年，從平京城，定京邑，除燕國內史。
entries.en: In the third year he followed the pacification of the capital and the securing of the capital region, and was made Interior Minister of the principality of Yan.
entries.literal: In the third year he followed in pacifying the capital and securing the capital region, and was appointed Interior Minister of Yan principality.

entries.zh: 義熙二年，除龍驤將軍，封龍川縣五等侯。
entries.en: In the second year of Yixi he was made General Who Leaps like a Dragon and enfeoffed as a fifth-rank marquis of Longchuan county.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yixi he was appointed General Who Leaps like a Dragon and enfeoffed as a five-rank marquis of Longchuan county.

entries.zh: 從高祖伐廣固，於臨朐破賊。
entries.en: He joined the Founding Emperor's campaign against Guanggu and routed the enemy at Linqu.
entries.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor in the campaign against Guanggu and defeated the rebels at Linqu.

entries.zh: 盧循逼京邑，孟昶、諸葛長民等建議奉天子過江，進廷議不可，面折昶等，高祖甚嘉之。
entries.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed moving the emperor south across the Yangzi. Qiujin argued before the court that this was unacceptable and openly refuted Chang and his allies; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed escorting the Son of Heaven across the river; Jin argued in court that this was unacceptable and rebutted Chang and the others to their faces. The Founding Emperor greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 獻計伐樹，樹柵石頭。
entries.en: He proposed felling trees to build a palisade at Shitou.
entries.literal: He offered a plan to cut trees and build a palisade at Shitou.

entries.zh: 除鄱陽太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was made Administrator of Poyang while retaining his rank as general.
entries.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Poyang; his generalship remained as before.

entries.zh: 統馬步十八隊，於東道出鄱陽，至五畝嶠。
entries.en: He commanded eighteen cavalry and infantry detachments, advancing east from Poyang to Wumu Pass.
entries.literal: He commanded eighteen cavalry and infantry units, marching east from Poyang to Wumu Pass.

entries.zh: 循遣將英紏為上饒令。
entries.en: Xun sent the general Ying Gou to serve as magistrate of Shangrao.
entries.literal: Xun dispatched the general Ying Gou to serve as magistrate of Shangrao.

entries.zh: 千餘人守故城，進攻破之。
entries.en: More than a thousand men held the old city; Qiujin advanced, attacked, and captured it.
entries.literal: More than a thousand men held the old city; Jin advanced, attacked, and took it.

entries.zh: 循又遣童敏之為鄱陽太守，據郡，進從餘干步道趣鄱陽，敏之退走，追破之，斬首數百。
entries.en: Xun then sent Tong Minzhi as Administrator of Poyang to hold the commandery. Qiujin advanced overland from Yugan toward Poyang; Minzhi fled, and Qiujin pursued, defeated him, and took several hundred heads.
entries.literal: Xun again dispatched Tong Minzhi as Administrator of Poyang to hold the commandery; Jin advanced by the land route from Yugan toward Poyang; Minzhi retreated and fled; Jin pursued, defeated him, and took several hundred heads.

entries.zh: 復隨劉藩至始興，討斬徐道覆。
entries.en: He again followed Liu Fan to Shixing, where Xu Daofu was hunted down and killed.
entries.literal: He again followed Liu Fan to Shixing and attacked and beheaded Xu Daofu.

entries.zh: 列傳第九 孫處 蒯恩 劉鐘[1] 虞丘進
entries.en: Biographies 9: Sun Chu, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, and Yu Qiujin
entries.literal: Biographies 9: Sun Chu, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin

entries.zh: 孔靖字季恭，會稽山陰人也。
entries.en: Kong Jing, whose style name was Jigong, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.
entries.literal: Kong Jing, style name Jigong, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 名與高祖祖諱同，故稱字。
entries.en: Because his given name matched the taboo on Gaozu's grandfather's name, he was addressed by his style name instead.
entries.literal: His personal name matched the taboo of Gaozu's grandfather, so he was known by his style name.

entries.zh: 祖愉，晉車騎將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Yu had served Jin as Cavalry General-in-Chief.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yu had been Cavalry General-in-Chief under Jin.

entries.zh: 父誾，散騎常侍。
entries.en: His father Yin had been Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: His father Yin had been Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 季恭始察郡孝廉，功曹史，著作佐郎，太子舍人，鎮軍司馬，司徒左西掾。
entries.en: At the outset Jigong was nominated as a commandery Filial and Incorrupt candidate and held posts as chief clerk, aide in the Bureau of Composition, gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, army aide on the Pacification Army staff, and western clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: Jigong was first nominated as commandery Filial and Incorrupt, then served as chief clerk, aide in the Bureau of Composition, gentleman attendant of the heir apparent, army aide on the Pacification Army staff, and western clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 未拜，遭母憂。
entries.en: Before he could take up his appointment, he went into mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: Before he could take office, he entered mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 隆安五年，於喪中被起建威將軍、山陰令，不就。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Long'an he was recalled from mourning to serve as General Who Establishes Might and Magistrate of Shanyin, but he declined.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Long'an, while still in mourning he was summoned to the posts of General Who Establishes Might and Magistrate of Shanyin, but he did not accept.

entries.zh: 高祖東征孫恩，屢至會稽，季恭曲意禮接，贍給甚厚。
entries.en: When Gaozu campaigned east against Sun En and repeatedly passed through Kuaiji, Jigong treated him with elaborate courtesy and supported him very generously.
entries.literal: When Gaozu marched east against Sun En and repeatedly came to Kuaiji, Jigong received him with every courtesy and supplied him very generously.

entries.zh: 高祖後討孫恩，時桓玄篡形已著，欲於山陰建義討之。
entries.en: On a later campaign against Sun En, Huan Xuan's usurpation was already obvious, and Gaozu planned to raise a righteous force at Shanyin to overthrow him.
entries.literal: Later, when Gaozu campaigned again against Sun En, Huan Xuan's usurpation was already plain, and Gaozu wished to raise arms at Shanyin to punish him.

entries.zh: 季恭以為山陰去京邑路遠，且玄未居極位，不如待其篡逆事彰，釁成惡稔，徐於京口圖之，不憂不剋。
entries.en: Jigong argued that Shanyin was too far from the capital, and that since Xuan had not yet seized the throne outright, they should wait until his usurpation was fully exposed and his crimes fully ripened, then move deliberately from Jingkou—success would be assured.
entries.literal: Jigong held that Shanyin was far from the capital by road, and that since Xuan had not yet reached the supreme position, it would be better to wait until his treason was fully exposed, guilt ripened, and evil fully formed, then slowly plot at Jingkou—there would be no worry of failure.

entries.zh: 高祖亦謂為然。
entries.en: Gaozu agreed.
entries.literal: Gaozu also thought this correct.

entries.zh: 虞嘯父為征東將軍、會稽內史，季恭初求為府司馬，不得。
entries.en: Yu Xiaofu held the posts of General Who Conquers the East and Interior Governor of Kuaiji. Jigong had earlier sought a post as major on his staff but was turned down.
entries.literal: Yu Xiaofu was General Who Conquers the East and Interior Governor of Kuaiji; Jigong had first sought to become his staff major but was refused.

entries.zh: 及帝定桓玄，以季恭為內史，使齎封板拜授，正與季恭相值，季恭便回舟夜還。
entries.en: After the court had suppressed Huan Xuan, Jigong was appointed Interior Governor and an envoy was dispatched with sealed boards of appointment. He met Jigong on the route; Jigong at once turned his boat and returned by night.
entries.literal: When the emperor had settled Huan Xuan, Jigong was made Interior Governor; an envoy was sent bearing sealed appointment boards to invest him. He happened to meet Jigong on the way, and Jigong turned his boat about and returned that same night.

entries.zh: 至即叩扉告嘯父，并令掃拂別齋，即便入郡。
entries.en: As soon as he arrived he knocked at Xiaofu's gate to announce himself, had a separate lodging cleaned, and entered the commandery administration at once.
entries.literal: On arrival he knocked at the gate to inform Xiaofu, ordered a separate lodging swept, and immediately entered the commandery seat.

entries.zh: 嘯父本為桓玄所授，聞玄敗，震懼，開門請罪。
entries.en: Xiaofu had originally been appointed by Huan Xuan. When he heard of Xuan's defeat he was terrified and opened his gate to plead guilty.
entries.literal: Xiaofu had originally been appointed by Huan Xuan; hearing of Xuan's defeat, he was terrified and opened his gate to plead guilt.

entries.zh: 季恭慰勉，使且安所住，明旦乃移。
entries.en: Jigong comforted him and told him to stay where he was for the night and move only the next morning.
entries.literal: Jigong comforted and encouraged him, telling him to remain where he was for the time being and move only the next morning.

entries.zh: 季恭到任，務存治實，敕止浮華，翦罰遊惰，由是寇盜衰止，境內肅清。
entries.en: In office Jigong pursued practical administration, forbade ostentation, and punished idleness and vagrancy. Banditry declined and ceased, and the region was pacified.
entries.literal: Once in office, Jigong devoted himself to solid governance, forbade empty display, and punished idleness and wandering; banditry dwindled and stopped, and the district was brought to order.

entries.zh: 徵為右衞將軍，加給事中，不拜。
entries.en: He was summoned as General of the Right Guard with added status as Supernumerary Palace Attendant, but declined.
entries.literal: He was summoned as General of the Right Guard with added status as Supernumerary Palace Attendant, but did not accept.

entries.zh: 尋除侍中，領本國中正，徙琅邪王大司馬司馬。
entries.en: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and head of his native state's chief rectifier, then transferred as major on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langye.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant and head of his native state's chief rectifier, then transferred as major on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langye.

entries.zh: 尋出為吳興太守，加冠軍。
entries.en: He was soon posted as Administrator of Wuxing with the additional title Champion.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he went out as Administrator of Wuxing with the additional title Champion.

entries.zh: 先是，吳興頻喪太守，云項羽神為卞山王，居郡聽事，二千石至，常避之，季恭居聽事，竟無害也。
entries.en: Previously Wuxing had lost one administrator after another. People said the spirit of Xiang Yu, as King of Bianshan, dwelt in the commandery hall and that incoming two-thousand-bushel officials always avoided it. Jigong took up residence in the hall and came to no harm.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wuxing had repeatedly lost its administrators; it was said that the spirit of Xiang Yu, as King of Bianshan, dwelt in the commandery hall, and when a two-thousand-bushel official arrived he always avoided it. Jigong occupied the hall and suffered no harm.

entries.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，固讓。
entries.en: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing but firmly declined.

entries.zh: 義熙八年，復督五郡諸軍、征虜、會稽內史。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Yixi he again supervised military affairs in five commanderies and served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Interior Governor of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi he again supervised military affairs in five commanderies and served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Interior Governor of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 修飾學校，督課誦習。
entries.en: He refurbished the schools and supervised study and recitation.
entries.literal: He restored the schools and supervised study and recitation.

entries.zh: 十年，復為尚書右僕射，加散騎常侍，又讓不拜。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was again made Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and again declined.

entries.zh: 頃之，除領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，本州大中正。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Leads the Army with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of his home province.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Leads the Army with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and chief rectifier of his home province.

entries.zh: 十二年，致仕，拜金紫光錄大夫，常侍如故。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he retired and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, retaining his attendant status.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he retired from office and was granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, retaining his attendant status.

entries.zh: 是歲，高祖北伐，季恭求從，以為太尉軍諮祭酒、後將軍。
entries.en: That year, when Gaozu marched north, Jigong asked to join the campaign and was appointed consultation army aide on the Grand Commandant's staff and Rear General.
entries.literal: That year, when Gaozu marched north, Jigong asked to accompany the campaign and was made consultation army aide on the Grand Commandant's staff and Rear General.

entries.zh: 從平關、洛。
entries.en: He took part in pacifying Guanzhong and Luoyang.
entries.literal: He followed in the pacification of Guan and Luo.

entries.zh: 高祖為相國，又隨府遷。
entries.en: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Jigong transferred with the office.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Jigong moved with the office.

entries.zh: 宋臺初建，令書以為尚書令，加散騎常侍，又讓不受，乃拜侍中、特進、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: When the Song regime was first established, an imperial order named him Minister of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry. He declined again and was instead appointed Palace Attendant, Special Grand Master, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.
entries.literal: When the Song regime was first established, an imperial order named him Minister of the Masters of Writing with added Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry; he again declined and would not accept, and was then appointed Palace Attendant, Special Grand Master, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.

entries.zh: 辭事東歸，高祖餞之戲馬臺，百僚咸賦詩以述其美。
entries.en: He resigned and returned east. Gaozu gave him a farewell feast at the Terrace of the Sportive Horse, and the hundred officials all composed poems in praise of him.
entries.literal: He resigned his duties and returned east; Gaozu feasted him at Terrace of the Sportive Horse, and the hundred officials all composed poems to praise his merit.

entries.zh: 及受命，加開府儀同三司，辭讓累年，終以不受。
entries.en: When Gaozu received the Mandate, he was offered the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes. He declined for years and never accepted.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Jigong was offered the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes; he declined for years and in the end never accepted.

entries.zh: 永初三年，薨，時年七十六。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongchu he died, aged seventy-six.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died, aged seventy-six.

entries.zh: 追贈侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, and the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, and the Three Excellencies of opening an office with ritual equal to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: =弟靈符，元嘉末，為南譙王義宣司空長史、南郡太守，尚書吏部郎。
entries.en: His younger brother Lingfu, at the end of Yuanjia, served as chief administrator on the Minister of Works staff of the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, and as Administrator of Nan commandery and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: =His younger brother Lingfu, at the end of Yuanjia, served as chief administrator on the Minister of Works staff of the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, and as Administrator of Nan commandery and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 世祖大明初，自侍中為輔國將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Daming era under Shizu, he left the post of Palace Attendant to become General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Daming era under Shizu, he left the post of Palace Attendant to become General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 入為丹陽尹。
entries.en: He entered the capital as Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 山陰縣土境褊狹，民多田少，靈符表徙無貲之家於餘姚、鄞、鄮三縣界，墾起湖田。
entries.en: Shanyin county was cramped, with many people and little land. Lingfu memorialized to move impoverished households to the borders of Yuyao, Yin, and Mao counties and to open lake fields for cultivation.
entries.literal: The territory of Shanyin county was narrow and cramped, with many people and little land. Lingfu memorialized to move households without means to the borders of Yuyao, Yin, and Mao counties and to open lake fields for cultivation.

entries.zh: 上使公卿博議，太宰江夏王義恭議曰：「夫訓農修本，有國所同，土著之民，習翫日久，如京師無田，不聞徙居他縣。
entries.en: The emperor had the high ministers debate the proposal at length. Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, argued: "Teaching agriculture and strengthening the foundations are the same for every state. Long-settled natives grow attached to their ways over time; in the capital, when people lack fields, one never hears of relocating them to other counties.
entries.literal: The emperor had the high ministers debate the matter at length. Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, argued: "Training the people in agriculture and repairing the foundations are alike for every state. Natives long settled grow used to their ways over time; in the capital, when people have no fields, one does not hear of moving them to other counties.

entries.zh: 尋山陰豪族富室，頃畝不少，貧者肆力，非為無處，耕起空荒，無救災歉。
entries.en: Moreover, in Shanyin the great clans and wealthy houses hold considerable land; the poor can still work—they are not truly without a place. Opening empty waste land will not relieve famine and shortage.
entries.literal: Moreover, in Shanyin the great clans and wealthy houses hold no small acreage; the poor can exert their strength—there is not truly no place for them. Opening empty waste land will not relieve famine and shortage.

entries.zh: 又緣湖居民，魚鴨為業，及有居肆，理無樂徙。」
entries.en: Again, lakeside residents live by fish and ducks, and some keep shops; by rights they cannot welcome relocation."
entries.literal: Again, lakeside residents make their living from fish and ducks, and some keep shops; by reason they cannot be glad to move."

entries.zh: 尚書令柳元景、右僕射劉秀之、尚書王瓚之、顧凱之、顏師伯、嗣湘東王彧議曰：「富戶溫房，無假遷業；
entries.en: Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Vice Minister of the Right Liu Xiuzhi, and Ministers Wang Zanzhi, Gu Kaizhi, Yan Shibo, and the heir-designate Prince of Xiangdong, Yu, argued: "Wealthy households in warm rooms need not change their livelihood;
entries.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Vice Minister of the Right Liu Xiuzhi, and Ministers Wang Zanzhi, Gu Kaizhi, Yan Shibo, and the heir-designate Prince of Xiangdong, Yu, argued: "Wealthy households in warm rooms need not change their livelihood;

entries.zh: 窮身寒室，必應徙居。
entries.en: those in poor bodies and cold rooms must be moved.
entries.literal: those in poor bodies and cold rooms must be moved.

entries.zh: 葺宇疏臯，產粒無待，資公則公未易充，課私則私卒難具。
entries.en: They would build houses on sparse marshland and could not wait for grain. If the state must supply them, the state cannot easily meet the need; if private households must provide, private households can hardly furnish it.
entries.literal: They build houses on sparse marshland and cannot wait for grain; if the state must supply them, the state cannot easily fill the need; if private households must provide, private households can hardly furnish it.

entries.zh: 生計既完，畬功自息，宜募亡叛通卹及與樂田者，其往經創，須粗修立，然後徙居。」
entries.en: Once livelihoods are secure, the work of clearing fields will cease of itself. One should recruit fugitives and rebels under amnesty and those who delight in farming; where the land has suffered harm, it must first be roughly repaired, and only then should people be moved."
entries.literal: Once livelihoods are secure, the work of clearing fields will cease of itself. One should recruit fugitives and rebels under amnesty and those who delight in farming; where the land has suffered harm, it must first be roughly repaired, and only then should people be moved."

entries.zh: 侍中沈懷文、王景文、黃門侍郎劉敳、郄顒議曰：「百姓雖不親農，不無資生之路，若驅以就田，則坐相違奪。
entries.en: Palace Attendants Shen Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Liu Yi and Qie Yan argued: "Though common people do not personally farm, they are not without ways to make a living; if they are driven onto the fields, their livelihoods will simply be seized from them.
entries.literal: Palace Attendants Shen Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Liu Yi and Qie Yan argued: "Though the common people do not personally farm, they are not without ways to make a living; if they are driven onto the fields, their livelihoods will simply be seized from them.

entries.zh: 且鄞等三縣，去治並遠，既安之民，忽徙他邑，新垣未立，舊居已毀，去留兩困，無以自資。
entries.en: Moreover, Yin and the other three counties are far from the seat of government. People already settled, if suddenly moved to another district, will find new walls not yet built and old dwellings already destroyed—troubled whether to go or stay, with no means to support themselves.
entries.literal: Moreover, Yin and the other three counties are far from the seat of government. People already settled, if suddenly moved to another district, will find new walls not yet built and old dwellings already destroyed—troubled whether to go or stay, with no means to support themselves.

entries.zh: 謂宜適任民情，從其所樂，開宥逋亡，且令就業，若審成腴壤，然後議遷。」
entries.en: They held that one should suit the people's feelings, let them follow what they enjoy, pardon fugitives, and for the time being let them take up their trades; if the land is truly shown to be fertile, then one may discuss relocation."
entries.literal: They held that one should suit the people's feelings, let them follow what they enjoy, pardon fugitives, and for the time being let them take up their trades; if the land is truly shown to be fertile, then one may discuss relocation."

entries.zh: 太常王玄謨議曰：「小民貧匱，遠就荒疇，去舊即新，糧種俱闕，習之既難，勸之未易。
entries.en: Minister of Ceremonies Wang Xuanmo argued: "Small people are poor and destitute; sent far to waste land, leaving the old for the new, grain and seed alike lacking—hard to accustom them, and hard to encourage them.
entries.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Wang Xuanmo argued: "Small people are poor and destitute; sent far to waste land, leaving the old for the new, grain and seed alike lacking—hard to accustom them, and hard to encourage them.

entries.zh: 謂宜微加資給，使得肆勤，明力田之賞，申怠惰之罰。」
entries.en: They held that one should add a little support so that they could exert themselves, make clear rewards for diligent farming, and enforce penalties for idleness."
entries.literal: They held that one should add a little support so that they could exert themselves, make clear rewards for diligent farming, and enforce penalties for idleness."

entries.zh: 光祿勳王昇之議曰：「遠廢之疇，方翦荊棘，率課窮乏，其事彌難，資徙粗立，徐行無晚。」
entries.en: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wang Sheng argued: "On distant abandoned fields one is only now cutting brambles; to drive the poor to labor there is all the harder. Let support for relocation be roughly established first; there is no harm in proceeding slowly."
entries.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wang Sheng argued: "On distant abandoned fields one is only now cutting brambles; to drive the poor to labor there is all the harder. Let support for relocation be roughly established first; there is no harm in proceeding slowly."

entries.zh: 上違議，從其徙民，並成良業。
entries.en: The emperor rejected the debates and followed the plan to move the people; all became good cultivators.
entries.literal: The emperor rejected the debates and followed the plan to move the people; all became good cultivators.

entries.zh: 玄保起家楚臺太常博士，遭母憂，服闕，右將軍何無忌、前將軍諸葛長民俱板為參軍，並不就。
entries.en: Xuanbao began his career as erudite of the Grand Ceremonial on the Chu court. After mourning for his mother ended, General of the Right He Wuji and General of the Front Zhuge Changmin both summoned him as military aide, but he accepted neither.
entries.literal: Xuanbao began his career as erudite of the Grand Ceremonial on the Chu court; he entered mourning for his mother, and when mourning ended, General of the Right He Wuji and General of the Front Zhuge Changmin both summoned him as military aide, but he accepted neither.

entries.zh: 除臨安令。
entries.en: He was appointed Magistrate of Lin'an.
entries.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Lin'an.

entries.zh: 劉穆之舉為高祖鎮軍參軍，庫部郎，永世令。
entries.en: Liu Muzhi recommended him as military aide on Gaozu's Pacification Army staff, as Director of the Storehouses, and as Magistrate of Yongshi.
entries.literal: Liu Muzhi recommended him as military aide on Gaozu's Pacification Army staff, as Director of the Storehouses, and as Magistrate of Yongshi.

entries.zh: 復為高祖太尉參軍，轉主簿，丹陽丞。
entries.en: He again served as military aide on Gaozu's Grand Commandant staff, then became chief clerk and Assistant in Danyang.
entries.literal: He again served as military aide on Gaozu's Grand Commandant staff, then became chief clerk and Assistant in Danyang.

entries.zh: 少帝景平二年，入為尚書右丞，轉左丞，司徒右長史。
entries.en: In the second year of Jingping under Shaodi, he entered the Masters of Writing as Right Assistant, then Left Assistant, and Chief Clerk on the Right of the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jingping under Shaodi, he entered the Masters of Writing as Right Assistant, then Left Assistant, and Chief Clerk on the Right of the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 府公王弘甚知重之，謂左長史庾登之、吏部尚書王准之曰：「卿二賢明美朗識，會悟多通，然弘懿之望，故當共推羊也。」
entries.en: The Duke of the Domain, Wang Hong, valued him highly and said to Chief Clerk on the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi: "You two are brilliant, clear-sighted, and broadly capable, yet in the expectation of great virtue, it is Yang whom we should jointly advance."
entries.literal: The Duke of the Domain, Wang Hong, valued him highly and said to Chief Clerk on the Left Yu Dengzhi and Minister of Personnel Wang Zhunzhi: "You two are brilliant, clear-sighted, and broadly capable, yet in the expectation of great virtue, it is Yang whom we should jointly advance."

entries.zh: 頃之，入為黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he entered the palace as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he entered the palace as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 列傳第十五 臧燾徐廣傅隆
entries.en: Biography 15 — Zang Dao, Xu Guang, and Fu Long
entries.literal: Biography 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long

entries.zh: 臧燾，字德仁，東莞莒人，武敬皇后兄也。
entries.en: Zang Dao, whose courtesy name was De Ren, came from Ju in Dongguan and was the elder brother of Empress Wu Jing.
entries.literal: Zang Dao, styled De Ren, was a man of Ju in Dongguan and elder brother to Empress Wu Jing.

entries.zh: 少好學，善《三禮》，貧約自立，操行為鄉里所稱。
entries.en: From an early age he devoted himself to study and excelled in the Three Rites. Though poor, he made his own way, and his moral bearing won praise throughout his home district.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled in the Three Rites, supported himself in poverty and frugality, and his conduct was praised in his district.

entries.zh: 晉孝武帝太元中，衛將軍謝安始立國學，徐、兗二州刺史謝玄舉燾為助教。
entries.en: During the Taixuan reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-General Xie An founded the National Academy for the first time, and Xie Xuan, inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao to serve as an assistant instructor.
entries.literal: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-General Xie An first established the National Academy, and Xie Xuan, regional inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao as assistant instructor.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：選賢於野，則治身業弘；
entries.en: The historiographer writes: When worthies are chosen from the countryside, self-cultivation flourishes;
entries.literal: The historiographer says: When worthies are selected in the countryside, then self-cultivation and enterprise are broad;

entries.zh: 求士於朝，則飾智風起。
entries.en: when scholars are sought at court, the fashion of displaying cleverness takes hold.
entries.literal: when scholars are sought at court, then the fashion of displaying cleverness arises.

entries.zh: 《六經》奧遠，方軌之正路；
entries.en: The Six Classics are profound and remote — the straight path and correct road;
entries.literal: The Six Classics are profound and remote, the straight track and correct road;

entries.zh: 百家淺末，捷至之偏道。
entries.en: the hundred schools are shallow and marginal — the shortcut and side path.
entries.literal: the hundred schools are shallow and marginal, the side path of quick arrival.

entries.zh: 漢世登士，閭黨為先，崇本務學，不尚浮詭，然後可以俯拾青組，顧蔑籝金。
entries.en: In Han, advancement to office began with the local community; men honored fundamentals and devoted themselves to learning, scorning empty cleverness — only then could they win official rank with ease and disdain mere wealth.
entries.literal: In Han, when men entered office, the village community came first; they honored the root and devoted themselves to learning, did not esteem empty trickery — only then could they stoop to pick up blue cords and look down on casket gold.

entries.zh: 於是人厲從師之志，家競專門之術，藝重當時，所居一旦成市，黌舍暫啟，著錄或至萬人。
entries.en: Thus men sharpened their resolve to follow teachers, families competed in specialized learning, and scholarship weighed heavily in the age — a master's dwelling could become a marketplace overnight, and when the academy opened, enrollment sometimes reached ten thousand.
entries.literal: Thus men sharpened the will to follow teachers, families competed in specialized arts, learning was weighty in the age — where one dwelt became a market in a day; when the schoolhouse briefly opened, those registered sometimes reached ten thousand.

entries.zh: 是故仕以學成，身由義立。
entries.en: Thus office came through completed learning, and personal standing through moral principle.
entries.literal: Therefore office came through completion of learning, and the person was established through righteousness.

entries.zh: 自魏氏膺命，主愛雕蟲，家棄章句，人重異術。
entries.en: From the time Wei received the mandate, rulers loved ornamental prose, families abandoned classical exegesis, and men prized unorthodox arts.
entries.literal: From the time Wei received the mandate, lords loved ornamental writing, families abandoned exegetical clauses, and men prized strange arts.

entries.zh: 又選賢進士，不本鄉閭，銓衡之寄，任歸台閣。
entries.en: Again, in selecting worthies and advancing scholars, local roots were ignored, and the power of evaluation passed to the central offices.
entries.literal: Again, in selecting worthies and advancing scholars, they did not take the village lane as root; the charge of the balance-scale was entrusted to the terrace offices.

entries.zh: 以一人之耳目，究山川之險情，賢否臆斷，萬不值一。
entries.en: With one man's eyes and ears to judge the conditions of every region, worth and unworth were decided by guesswork — scarcely one judgment in ten thousand was correct.
entries.literal: With one man's eyes and ears to investigate the perilous conditions of mountains and rivers, worth and unworth were judged by guesswork — not one in ten thousand was correct.

entries.zh: 由是仕憑藉譽，學非為己，崇詭遇之巧速，鄙稅駕之遲難，士自此委笥植《經》，各從所務，早往晏退，以取世資。
entries.en: Hence office depended on borrowed reputation and learning was not pursued for its own sake; men honored quick cleverness and despised slow mastery; scholars set the Classics aside, each following his own pursuit, coming early and leaving late to gain worldly advantage.
entries.literal: Hence office relied on borrowed reputation, learning was not for oneself; they honored the clever speed of chance encounters and despised the slow difficulty of thorough mastery; scholars from this time set aside cases and planted the Classics, each following his own pursuit, going early and returning late to gain worldly capital.

entries.zh: 庠序黌校之士，傳經聚徒之業，自黃初至於晉末，百餘年中，儒教盡矣。
entries.en: The scholars of the academies and the profession of transmitting the classics and gathering disciples — from Huangchu to the end of Jin, for more than a hundred years, Confucian teaching was exhausted.
entries.literal: The scholars of the schools and academies, the profession of transmitting the classics and gathering disciples — from Huangchu to the end of Jin, for more than a hundred years, Confucian teaching was exhausted.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，議創國學，宮車早晏，道未及行。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, there was discussion of founding a National Academy, but he died before the plan could be carried out.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, there was discussion of founding a National Academy, but the imperial carriage departed early and the way had not yet been carried out.

entries.zh: 迄於元嘉，甫獲克就，雅風盛烈，未及曩時，而濟濟焉，頗有前王之遺典。
entries.en: By Yuanjia it was at last accomplished; its elegant culture did not match former ages, yet in abundance it preserved much of the former kings' legacy.
entries.literal: By Yuanjia it was at last accomplished; elegant wind and flourishing splendor did not reach former times, yet in abundance there was much of the former kings' surviving canon.

entries.zh: 天子鸞旗警蹕，清道而臨學館，儲後冕旒黼黻，北面而禮先師，後生所不嘗聞，黃發未之前睹，亦一代之盛也。
entries.en: The emperor, his procession clearing the way, came by the purified road to the academy; the heir apparent in full regalia faced north to honor the former master — what the young had never heard and the aged had never seen was truly the splendor of an age.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven with imperial banners clearing the way came by the purified road to the academy; the heir in cap-strings and embroidered robes faced north to pay rites to the former master — what the young had never heard and the gray-haired had never before seen was also the splendor of an age.

entries.zh: 臧燾、徐廣、傅隆、裴松之、何承天、雷次宗，並服膺聖哲，不為雅俗推移，立名於世，宜矣。
entries.en: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all devoted themselves to the sages, were not swayed by fashion, and won renown in their age — as was only fitting.
entries.literal: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sage and wise in their hearts, were not shifted by elegant fashion or vulgar custom, and established names in the world — as was fitting.

entries.zh: 潁川庾蔚之、雁門周野王、汝南周王子、河內向琰、會稽賀道養，皆托志經書，見稱於後學。
entries.en: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all devoted themselves to the classics and were praised by later scholars.
entries.literal: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all entrusted their aims to the classics and were praised by later students.

entries.zh: 蔚之略解《禮記》，並注賀循《喪服》，行於世雲。
entries.en: Weizhi had a partial understanding of the Record of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments, which circulated in his day.
entries.literal: Weizhi had a partial understanding of the Record of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments, which circulated in the world, it is said.

entries.zh: 遷通直郎，高祖鎮軍、車騎、中軍、太尉諮議參軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant and served as advisory aide on the staffs of the Founding Emperor as General Who Guards the Army, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army Commander, and Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, and served as advisory aide to the Founding Emperor when he was General Who Guards the Army, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army Commander, and Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 高祖北伐關、洛，大司馬琅邪王同行，除大司馬從事中郎，總留府事。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor marched north against Guanzhong and Luoyang, the Prince of Langye, serving as Grand Marshal, accompanied the campaign; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman on the Grand Marshal's staff and took charge of all affairs left behind at headquarters.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor marched north against Guan and Luo, the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal, accompanied him; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman of the Grand Marshal and oversaw all affairs left at headquarters.

entries.zh: 義熙十四年，除侍中。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 元熙元年，以腳疾去職。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanxi he resigned because of a foot ailment.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he left office because of foot ailment.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，征拜太常，雖外戚貴顯，而彌自沖約，茅屋蔬餐，不改其舊。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Dao was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies; though he was now a prominent imperial kinsman, he became only more restrained, keeping to his thatched dwelling and plain meals as before.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate he was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies; though a prominent maternal relative, he became only more self-restrained and modest, living in thatched huts on vegetable fare without changing his former ways.

entries.zh: 所得奉祿，與親戚共之。
entries.en: He shared his official salary with his relatives.
entries.literal: The salary he received he shared with his kin.

entries.zh: 永初三年，致仕，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple cord.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired from office, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and granted the golden seal and purple cord.

entries.zh: 其年卒，時年七十。
entries.en: He died the same year, at the age of seventy.
entries.literal: That year he died, aged seventy.

entries.zh: 少帝追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Emperor Shao posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: Emperor Shao posthumously awarded him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮京口，與燾書曰：「頃學尚廢弛，後進頹業，衡門之內，清風輟響。
entries.en: While stationed at Jingkou, the Founding Emperor wrote to Dao: "Learning has lately fallen into neglect, the younger generation's devotion to study has waned, and within humble households the voice of upright conduct has fallen silent.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor was stationed at Jingkou he wrote to Dao: "Recently learning has been neglected and slack, the younger generation's pursuit of study has declined, and within humble doorways the sound of pure conduct has ceased.

entries.zh: 良由戎車屢警，禮樂中息，浮夫恣志，情與事染，豈可不敷崇墳籍，敦厲風尚。
entries.en: This is surely because war has repeatedly broken out, rites and music have been interrupted, and restless men follow their whims until feeling is corrupted by circumstance — how can we fail to promote the classics and strengthen public morals?
entries.literal: Truly because war-chariots have repeatedly sounded the alarm and rites and music have halted midway, drifting men indulge their wills and sentiment is stained by affairs — how can we fail to spread reverence for the classics and urge refinement of custom?

entries.zh: 此境人士，子侄如林，明發搜訪，想聞令軌。
entries.en: Talented men in this region are as plentiful as trees in a forest; I intend to seek them out at once and hope to hear of exemplary conduct among them.
entries.literal: Men of talent in this region are as numerous as trees in a grove; at dawn I shall search them out, and I trust I shall hear of worthy models.

entries.zh: 然荊玉含寶，要俟開瑩，幽蘭懷馨，事資扇發，獨習寡悟，義著周典。
entries.en: Yet jade from Jing hides its luster until it is cut and polished, and orchids in the shade need stirring to release their fragrance; solitary study brings little enlightenment — the Zhou classics themselves teach as much.
entries.literal: Yet jade from Jing holds its treasure and must await polishing; orchids in the shade bear fragrance and depend on being fanned into bloom; solitary study yields little understanding — the principle is set forth in the Zhou canon.

entries.zh: 今經師不遠，而赴業無聞，非唯志學者鮮，或是勸誘未至邪。
entries.en: Masters of the classics are close at hand, yet we hear nothing of students flocking to study — is it only that aspiring scholars are few, or perhaps that encouragement has not yet been offered?
entries.literal: Now masters of the classics are not far away, yet no word is heard of students coming to study — is it not only that those who wish to learn are few, or perhaps encouragement has not yet reached them?

entries.zh: 想復弘之。」
entries.en: I trust you will take up this cause again."
entries.literal: I trust you will again extend this effort."

entries.zh: 參高祖中軍軍事，入補尚書度支郎，改掌祠部。
entries.en: He then served on the Founding Emperor's central army staff as military aide, entered the capital as Director of Revenue in the Secretariat, and was later transferred to head the Sacrifices Bureau.
entries.literal: He joined the Founding Emperor's central army as military aide, entered the capital to fill the post of Director of Revenue in the Secretariat, and was reassigned to head the Sacrifices Bureau.

entries.zh: 襲封高陵亭侯。
entries.en: He inherited the title Marquis of Gaoling district.
entries.literal: He inherited enfeoffment as Marquis of Gaoling district.

entries.zh: 頃之，去官。
entries.en: Before long he resigned his post.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he left office.

entries.zh: 以母老家貧，與弟熹俱棄人事，躬耕自業，約己養親者十餘載。
entries.en: His mother was old and the family poor, so he and his younger brother Xi withdrew from public life, worked the fields with their own hands, and for more than ten years lived frugally to support their parents.
entries.literal: Because his mother was aged and his family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together abandoned worldly affairs, tilled the fields themselves to make their living, and for more than ten years restrained themselves to support their kin.

entries.zh: 父母喪亡，居喪六年，以毀瘠著稱。
entries.en: After his parents died he mourned for six years and became famous for the wasting grief that marked his observance.
entries.literal: When his parents died he observed mourning for six years and became renowned for emaciation from grief.

entries.zh: 服闋，除臨沂令。
entries.en: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.

entries.zh: 義旗建，為太學博士，參右將軍何無忌軍事，隨府轉鎮南參軍。
entries.en: When the righteous armies rose, he was made an erudite of the Imperial Academy, joined General of the Right He Wuji's staff as military aide, and was later transferred with the headquarters to serve as aide of the Army of the South.
entries.literal: When the righteous banner was raised he became erudite of the Imperial Academy, served as aide on military affairs to General of the Right He Wuji, and followed the headquarters to become aide of the Army of the South.

entries.zh: 長子邃，護軍司馬，宜都太守。
entries.en: His eldest son Sui served as marshal of the Protector Army and as governor of Yidu.
entries.literal: His eldest son Sui was marshal of the Protector Army and governor of Yidu.

entries.zh: 少子綽，太子中舍人，新安太守。
entries.en: His younger son Chuo served as attendant in the heir apparent's household and as governor of Xin'an.
entries.literal: His younger son Chuo was attendant in the household of the Heir Apparent and governor of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 邃長子諶之，尚書都官郎，烏程令。
entries.en: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi served as a director in the Ministry of Justice and as magistrate of Wucheng.
entries.literal: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi was a director in the Ministry of Justice and magistrate of Wucheng.

entries.zh: 諶之弟凝之，學涉有當世才具，與司空徐湛之為異常之交。
entries.en: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was widely learned and gifted for his age; he formed an unusually close friendship with Xu Tanzhi, Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was broadly learned and possessed talent for the age; with Minister of Works Xu Tanzhi he formed an extraordinary friendship.

entries.zh: 年少時與北地傅僧祐俱以通家子始為太祖所引見，時上與何尚之論鑄錢事，凝之便幹其語，上因回與論之。
entries.en: In his youth he and Fu Shengyou of Beidi, both sons of allied families, were first presented to Emperor Taizu; when the emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi, Ningzhi interjected, and the emperor turned to debate the matter with him.
entries.literal: In youth he and Fu Shengyou of Beidi, both sons of families linked by marriage, were first introduced to Emperor Taizu; at the time the emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi, and Ningzhi at once joined their conversation, whereupon the emperor turned and debated with him.

entries.zh: 僧祐引凝之衣令止，凝之大言謂僧祐曰：「明主難再遇，便應正盡所懷。」
entries.en: Shengyou tugged at Ningzhi's robe to stop him, but Ningzhi said loudly: "A wise ruler is seldom met twice; one should speak one's mind fully while one can."
entries.literal: Shengyou pulled Ningzhi's robe to make him stop; Ningzhi spoke loudly to Shengyou: "A clear-sighted lord is hard to meet twice — one ought at once to set forth fully what is in one's heart."

entries.zh: 上與往復十餘反，凝之詞韻銓序，兼有理證，上甚賞焉。
entries.en: The emperor and he exchanged views more than ten times; Ningzhi's language was measured and orderly and supported by sound reasoning, and the emperor was greatly impressed.
entries.literal: The emperor and he went back and forth more than ten times; Ningzhi's phrasing was measured and orderly and combined reasoned proof — the emperor greatly admired him.

entries.zh: 曆隨王誕後軍記室錄事，欲以為青州，其事不果。
entries.en: He later served as recorder on the staff of Prince Dan of Sui's rear army; there was a plan to appoint him regional inspector of Qingzhou, but it did not come to pass.
entries.literal: He successively served as recorder in the secretariat of Prince Dan of Sui's rear army, and there was a plan to make him regional inspector of Qingzhou, but the matter did not come to pass.

entries.zh: 遷尚書右丞，以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。
entries.en: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director in the Secretariat and, as an associate of Xu Tanzhi, was executed by the prime culprit.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Right Assistant Director in the Secretariat and, as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.

entries.zh: 子夤，尚書主客郎，沈攸之征西功曹，為攸之盡節，事在《攸之傳》。
entries.en: His son Yin served as Master of Guests in the Secretariat and as merit officer on Shen Youzhi's western campaign staff; he gave his full loyalty to Youzhi, as recounted in Youzhi's biography.
entries.literal: His son Yin was Master of Guests in the Secretariat and merit officer on Shen Youzhi's western campaign staff; he gave full loyalty to Youzhi — the affair is in the biography of Youzhi.

entries.zh: 凝之弟潭之，亦有美譽。
entries.en: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi likewise enjoyed a fine reputation.
entries.literal: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi also had a fine reputation.

entries.zh: 太宗世，曆尚書吏部郎，禦史中丞。
entries.en: Under Emperor Taizong he served successively as director in the Ministry of Personnel and as Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong he successively served as director in the Ministry of Personnel and as Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，為左民尚書，卒官。
entries.en: Under the deposed emperor, during the Yuanhui era, he served as Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.
entries.literal: Under the deposed emperor, in the Yuanhui era, he was Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.

entries.zh: 潭之弟澄之，太子左積弩將軍。
entries.en: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi served as Left Master of Strong Crossbows in the heir apparent's household.
entries.literal: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi was Left Master of Strong Crossbows in the Heir Apparent's household.

entries.zh: 元嘉二十七年，領軍於盱眙，為索虜所破，見殺，追贈通直郎。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded troops at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern invaders, and was killed; he was posthumously awarded the title Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded troops at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern barbarians, and was killed; posthumously he was awarded Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 綽子煥，順帝升明中，為武昌太守。
entries.en: Chuo's son Huan served as governor of Wuchang during the Shengming era of Emperor Shun.
entries.literal: Chuo's son Huan, in the Shengming era of Emperor Shun, was governor of Wuchang.

entries.zh: 沈攸之攻郢城，煥棄郡赴之；
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his post and went to join him;
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his commandery and went to join him;

entries.zh: 攸之敗，伏誅。
entries.en: when Youzhi was defeated, Huan was executed.
entries.literal: when Youzhi was defeated, he was executed.

entries.zh: 傅僧祐，祖父弘仁，高祖外弟也。
entries.en: Fu Shengyou's grandfather Hongren was the Founding Emperor's brother-in-law.
entries.literal: Fu Shengyou — his grandfather Hongren was younger brother by marriage to the Founding Emperor.

entries.zh: 以中表曆顯官，征虜將軍、南譙太守，太常卿。
entries.en: Through family connections he rose through prominent posts, serving as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: Through maternal kin ties he successively held eminent offices: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 子邵，員外散騎侍郎，妻燾女也，生僧祐，有吏才，再為山陰令，甚有能名，末世令長莫及。
entries.en: His son Shao served as Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, married Dao's daughter, and fathered Shengyou. Shengyou had a gift for administration, served twice as magistrate of Shanyin with great renown, and in the dynasty's final years no district magistrate could rival him.
entries.literal: His son Shao was Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; he married Dao's daughter and fathered Shengyou, who had talent for administration, twice served as magistrate of Shanyin with a great reputation for competence, and at the end of the dynasty no district magistrate could match him.

entries.zh: 亦以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。
entries.en: He too, as an associate of Xu Tanzhi, was executed by the prime culprit.
entries.literal: He too, as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.

entries.zh: 孝武帝追崇庶祖母宣太后，議者或謂宜配食中宗。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu raised his father's concubine mother, Empress Dowager Xuan, to posthumous honor, some debaters argued that she ought to share sacrificial offerings in the temple of Emperor Zhongzong.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored his father's concubine mother, Empress Dowager Xuan, and some in the debate held that she should receive offerings alongside Emperor Zhongzong.

entries.zh: 燾議曰：「《陽秋》，之義，母以子貴，故仲子、成風，咸稱夫人。
entries.en: Dao argued in a memorial: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, a mother is elevated through her son's rank; that is why Zhong Zi and Cheng Feng were both addressed as Lady.
entries.literal: Dao submitted a memorial saying: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that a mother is ennobled through her son; therefore Zhong Zi and Cheng Feng were both styled Lady.

entries.zh: 《經》云'考仲子之宮'。
entries.en: The Classic states, 'Inspect the temple of Zhong Zi.'
entries.literal: The Classic says, 'Inspect the temple of Zhong Zi.'

entries.zh: 若配食惠廟，則宮無緣別築。
entries.en: If she were given a place in Emperor Hui's temple, there would be no occasion to erect a separate shrine.
entries.literal: If she were to share offerings in the temple of Emperor Hui, there would be no reason to build a separate temple.

entries.zh: 前漢孝文、孝昭太后，並系子為號，祭於寢園，不配于高祖、孝武之廟。
entries.en: In Former Han, the empress dowagers Wen and Zhao both bore titles tied to their sons, received sacrifice in the tomb-park shrines, and were not installed as consorts in the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: The empress dowagers Wen and Zhao of Former Han both took titles derived from their sons, were sacrificed to in the park shrines at their tombs, and were not paired in the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 後漢和帝之母曰恭懷皇所，安帝祖母曰敬隱皇后，順帝之母曰恭湣皇后，雖不系子為號，亦祭於陵寢。
entries.en: In Later Han, Emperor He's mother was known as Empress Gonghuai, Emperor An's grandmother as Empress Jingyin, and Emperor Shun's mother as Empress Gongmin; although their titles were not framed through their sons' reign names, they likewise received sacrifice at the tomb shrines.
entries.literal: In Later Han, the mother of Emperor He was called Empress Gonghuai, the grandmother of Emperor An was called Empress Jingyin, and the mother of Emperor Shun was called Empress Gongmin; though their titles were not derived from their sons, they too were sacrificed to at the tomb shrines.

entries.zh: 不配章、安二帝。
entries.en: None of them was paired with the temples of Emperors Zhang and An.
entries.literal: They were not paired with Emperors Zhang and An.

entries.zh: 此則二漢雖有太后、皇后之異，至於並不配食，義同《陽秋》。
entries.en: Thus, although Former and Later Han differed in whether the women were styled empress dowager or empress, in neither dynasty were they given shared temple offerings — a principle in keeping with the Spring and Autumn Annals.
entries.literal: Thus although the two Han differed as to empress dowager and empress, in neither case were they given shared offerings, in the same sense as the Spring and Autumn Annals.

entries.zh: 唯光武追廢呂後，故以薄後配高祖廟。
entries.en: Only under Guangwu, who posthumously deposed Empress Lü, was Empress Bo installed as consort in Gaozu's temple.
entries.literal: Only Guangwu, in posthumously deposing Empress Lü, therefore paired Empress Bo in the temple of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 又衛後既廢，霍光追尊李夫人為皇后，配孝武廟，此非母以子貴之例，直以高、武二廟無配故耳。
entries.en: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her with Emperor Wu's temple; that was not an instance of a mother elevated through her son, but merely because the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu had lacked consorts.
entries.literal: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her in the temple of Emperor Wu; this was not a case of a mother ennobled through her son, but simply because the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu lacked consorts.

entries.zh: 夫漢立寢於陵，自是晉制所異。
entries.en: Han practice of erecting tomb shrines at the mausoleums was in any case unlike Jin custom.
entries.literal: That Han established tomb shrines at the mausoleums was itself something Jin institutions differed from.

entries.zh: 謂宜遠准《陽秋》考宮之義，近摹二漢不配之典。
entries.en: I submit that we should take as our distant standard the Annals' principle of the separate temple, and as our near precedent the two Han rule against shared offerings.
entries.literal: I hold that one should take as distant standard the Annals' meaning of inspecting the temple, and as near model the two Han precedent of not pairing offerings.

entries.zh: 尊號既正，則罔極之情申，別建寢廟，則嚴禰之義顯，系子為稱，兼明母貴之所由，一舉而允三義，固哲王之高致也。」
entries.en: Once her title is properly fixed, the fullest measure of filial devotion is expressed; if a separate shrine is built, the solemn dignity of ancestral worship is preserved; and framing her title through her son's name makes clear the source of her elevation — to satisfy all three principles in a single measure is truly the mark of a sage ruler."
entries.literal: Once the honorific title is correct, boundless filial feeling is expressed; if a separate tomb shrine is built, the solemn meaning of ancestral sacrifice is displayed; taking the son's name in the title also clarifies whence the mother's nobility derives — one act satisfying three principles is indeed the lofty aim of a sage king."

entries.zh: 議者從之。
entries.en: The assembly adopted his view.
entries.literal: The debaters followed him.

entries.zh: 時太廟鴟尾災，燾謂著作郎徐廣曰：「昔孔子在齊，聞魯廟災，曰必桓、僖也。
entries.en: When fire broke out at the finials of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Dao said to Xu Guang of the Master of Writings office: "Long ago, when Confucius was in Qi and heard that Lu's ancestral temple had burned, he said the disaster must concern the shrines of Duke Huan and Duke Xi.
entries.literal: At that time the temple finials of the Imperial Ancestral Temple caught fire; Dao said to Xu Guang, Master of Writings: "Formerly when Confucius was in Qi and heard of fire in the Lu temple, he said it must concern Huan and Xi.

entries.zh: 今征西、京兆四府君，宜在毀落，而猶列廟饗，此其征乎？」
entries.en: Today the four ancestral lords of the Western Campaign and Jingzhao offices ought already to have been removed, yet they still receive temple sacrifice — is this not the same kind of sign?"
entries.literal: Now the four lords of the Western Campaign and Jingzhao offices ought to be among those removed, yet they still stand in the temple for sacrifice — is this not the omen?"

entries.zh: 乃上議曰：「臣聞國之大事，在祀與戎，將營宮室，宗廟為首。
entries.en: He then submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war, and that when palaces are to be built, the ancestral temple must come first.
entries.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war; when palace buildings are to be planned, the ancestral temple comes first.

entries.zh: 古先哲王，莫不致肅恭之誠心，盡崇嚴乎祖考，然後能流淳化于四海，通幽感於神明。
entries.en: The sage kings of antiquity all brought reverent sincerity to their rites and showed the utmost honor to their ancestors; only then could pure teaching spread through the realm and the unseen world respond to their devotion.
entries.literal: The sage kings of antiquity all devoted reverent and sincere hearts and showed the utmost honor to their forefathers, and only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits.

entries.zh: 固宜詳廢興於古典，循情禮以求中者也。
entries.en: One ought therefore to weigh abolition and establishment against the ancient canon and seek the mean in light of ritual and human feeling.
entries.literal: One should indeed examine abolition and establishment in the ancient canon and follow sentiment and ritual to seek the mean.

entries.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。
entries.en: According to ritual, the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples — three zhao and three mu, with the Great Ancestor, for a total of seven.
entries.literal: Ritual prescribes seven temples for the Son of Heaven: three zhao and three mu, with the Great Ancestor making seven.

entries.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之，遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。
