entries.en: From the temple of the immediate forebear down through the five temples of more distant ancestors, all receive monthly sacrifice; the most remote temples become tiao, and once there are two tiao, only the seasonal offerings remain.
entries.literal: From the temple of the father down to the five temples of the ancestors, all receive monthly sacrifice; distant temples become tiao, and when there are two tiao, only the seasonal offerings continue.

entries.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之。
entries.en: When the tiao are removed they become altars; when the altars are removed they become open ritual mounds; and sacrifice is offered only when prayer is required.
entries.literal: When the tiao are removed they become altars; when the altars are removed they become open mounds; sacrifice is made only when there is prayer.

entries.zh: 此宗廟之次，親疏之序也。
entries.en: Such is the order of the ancestral temples and the gradation of kinship from near to remote.
entries.literal: This is the order of the ancestral temples and the sequence of near and remote kinship.

entries.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王、武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。
entries.en: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of Kings Wen and Wu, whereas Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
entries.literal: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

entries.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。
entries.en: If we examine the phrase 'removing the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.
entries.literal: Examining the phrase 'removing the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.

entries.zh: 文、武周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？
entries.en: Wen and Wu were Zhou's founding ancestors — how could the rites speak of removing the tiao to make altars?
entries.literal: Wen and Wu were the founding ancestors of Zhou — how could one speak of removing the tiao to make altars?

entries.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。
entries.en: This makes clear that temples made tiao are ancestors beyond the range of mourning obligation.
entries.literal: This shows that distant temples made tiao are ancestors beyond the scope of mourning garments.

entries.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之禮，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者，其義彌疏也。
entries.en: Moreover, distant temples still receive seasonal offerings, whereas removed tiao are reduced to altars and open mounds — showing that the farther the generation, the more attenuated the ritual becomes.
entries.literal: Again, distant temples still have the seasonal offering rites, while removed tiao have the distinction of altars and mounds — showing that the more remote the generation, the more attenuated the rite.

entries.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。
entries.en: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought to receive monthly sacrifice together with the Great Ancestor; although Hou Ji was elevated to match Heaven, that was because merit began with him, not because the principle of honor allows no gradation.
entries.literal: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought likewise to receive monthly sacrifice with the Great Ancestor; although Hou Ji was elevated to match Heaven, that was because merit and virtue began with him, not because the meaning of honor admits no gradation.

entries.zh: 又禮有以多貴者，故傳稱德厚者流光，德薄者流卑。
entries.en: Ritual also holds that greater merit confers greater honor; hence the tradition says that abundant virtue casts its radiance far, while meager virtue casts it low.
entries.literal: Again, ritual has the principle that abundance confers honor; therefore the tradition says that thick virtue casts its light far, while thin virtue casts it low.

entries.zh: 又雲自上以下，降殺以兩，禮也。
entries.en: It also says that from higher to lower ranks, ritual diminishes by steps of two.
entries.literal: It also says that from above to below, diminution proceeds by twos — such is ritual.

entries.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。
entries.en: This is the canon governing rank and precedence, the written rule distinguishing higher from lower.
entries.literal: This is the canon of noble and base ranks and the text of distinction between higher and lower.

entries.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？
entries.en: Yet how can it be said that the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples?
entries.literal: Yet it says that Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — how so?

entries.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫，而上祀之禮，不過高祖。
entries.en: Again, the king may sacrifice for legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet the rite of ascending sacrifice goes no higher than the great-grandfather.
entries.literal: Again, the king sacrifices for legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet the rite of ascending sacrifice goes no higher than the great-grandfather.

entries.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊屬，亦非聖人制禮之意也。
entries.en: To extend lavish favor downward while displacing sincere reverence owed to honored forebears is not what the sages intended when they established ritual.
entries.literal: To extend exalted favor downstream while displacing sincere reverence for honored kin is also not the intent of the sages in establishing ritual.

entries.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。
entries.en: Therefore, when the Taishi temples were established, Wang's proposal was adopted: by ritual the father had been a common officer while the son became Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was performed with royal rites, but the impersonator wore an officer's garment.
entries.literal: Therefore when the Taishi temples were established, Wang's proposal was followed: by ritual the father was a common officer and the son became Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was offered as to Son of Heaven or feudal lord, but the impersonator's garment was the officer's robe.

entries.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數，宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。
entries.en: Sacrifice therefore extended up to the Western Campaign lord to complete six generations; although Emperor Xuan was the Great Ancestor, he still occupied the position of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east had not yet been accorded him — illustrating the rule that even a sage son does not take precedence over his father at the offering.
entries.literal: Thus sacrifice extended up to the Western Campaign lord to complete the count of six generations; although Emperor Xuan was the Great Ancestor, he still stood in the place of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east had not yet been performed for him — what is called 'though the son be equal to a sage, he does not take precedence over his father in eating.'

entries.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨。
entries.en: Now that the shrines above Jingzhao have been moved, the Great Ancestor can at last take the central position; some debaters, believing the zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Great Ancestor in a lower seat — I hold that this violates the intent of the ritual canon.
entries.literal: Now that those above Jingzhao have been moved, the Great Ancestor can at last take the central place; debaters, holding that the zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Great Ancestor in a lower seat — I hold that this is not the intent of the ritual canon.

entries.zh: 所與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太祖在六世之外，非為須滿七廟，乃得居太祖也。
entries.en: 'Seven temples with the Great Ancestor' means that the zhao and mu are already complete; the Great Ancestor stands beyond the sixth generation — he does not need seven temples to be filled before he may take the position of Great Ancestor.
entries.literal: 'With the Great Ancestor, seven' means that the zhao and mu are already complete; the Great Ancestor stands beyond the sixth generation — it is not that one must fill seven temples before he may occupy the place of Great Ancestor.

entries.zh: 議者又以四府君神主宜永同于殷祫，臣又以為不然。
entries.en: The debaters also argued that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice — I again held that this was wrong.
entries.literal: The debaters also held that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice — I again held that this was wrong.

entries.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。
entries.en: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of abolished temples displayed before the Great Ancestor' refers to the tablets of former lords below the Great Ancestor.
entries.literal: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of abolished temples displayed before the Great Ancestor' means the tablets of former lords below the Great Ancestor.

entries.zh: 故《白虎通》雲「禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。」
entries.en: Thus the Comprehensive Meaning states: 'The great seasonal sacrifices for moved temples are offered because those ancestors embodied succession to the lordship and preserved the line without break.'
entries.literal: Therefore the Comprehensive Meaning says: 'The great seasonal sacrifices for moved temples are because they embody succession to the lordship and maintain the line without break.'

entries.zh: 豈如四府君在太祖之前乎。
entries.en: How could the four lords stand before the Great Ancestor?
entries.literal: How could the four lords stand before the Great Ancestor?

entries.zh: 非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基，昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍，未見其可。
entries.en: They were not rulers who succeeded to the throne, bore no mandate confirmed by heavenly signs, and were not the foundation of the royal enterprise; they were included before only because the generations were near, but now feeling and ritual have grown remote, yet they are to receive the great seasonal sacrifice forever while the Great Ancestor's place remains empty — I find no approval for this in the ritual canon.
entries.literal: They were not lords who succeeded to the line, bore no auspicious mandate of the spirits, and were not the foundation of royal enterprise; formerly they were included because the generation was near, but now sentiment and ritual are remote, yet they are to receive the great seasonal sacrifice forever and leave the Great Ancestor's place eternally vacant — sought in the ritual records, I do not see how this can be approved.

entries.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以淵儒碩學，鹹謂四府君神主，無緣永存於百世。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound and accomplished scholars, agreed that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no grounds to endure for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: In the beginning of the Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound scholars of vast learning, all held that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no reason to endure for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所秉小異，而大歸是同。
entries.en: Some proposed burying the tablets between the temple steps, others storing them in the stone chamber, others rebuilding shrines for them; though their particular proposals differed, they agreed in principle.
entries.literal: Some wished to bury them between the steps, some to store them in the stone chamber, some to rebuild shrines for them; though their particular views differed slightly, the main conclusion was the same.

entries.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭，長無太祖之位矣。
entries.en: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the other temples while the four lords continue forever in the great seasonal sacrifice, then in Jin's great seasonal rites the Great Ancestor's place will remain permanently empty.
entries.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the mass of temples while the four lords continue in the great seasonal sacrifice without end, then in the great Jin seasonal rites the place of the Great Ancestor will forever be vacant.

entries.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚；
entries.en: Ritual principle values the mean and need not be excessive;
entries.literal: Principle values hitting the mean and need not be excessive;

entries.zh: 禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷！
entries.en: ritual changes with the times — how can one follow custom without ever drawing a line!
entries.literal: ritual shifts with the age — how can one follow it without making a break!

entries.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈厲之諡彌彰；
entries.en: Thus although a subject's devotion may run deep, the posthumous title of the departed grows ever more distinct;
entries.literal: Thus although the feeling of subject and son is deep, the posthumous title of the departed spirit grows ever more distinct;

entries.zh: 追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。
entries.en: and although longing for the distant past may be intense, the rite of moving and abolishing temples is what must govern.
entries.literal: although longing to reach the remote past is keen, the rite of moving and abolishing temples is what applies.

entries.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可逾爾。
entries.en: It is not that the heart lacks desire to show greater honor, but ritual cannot be overstepped.
entries.literal: Is it not that one has a mind to add still more honor, yet ritual institutions cannot be transgressed?

entries.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處，虞主所以依神，神移則有 瘞埋之禮。
entries.en: The stone chamber lies north of the temple; rebuilding would leave their resting place uncertain; the provisional tablet lodges the spirit, and when the spirit is transferred there is a rite of burial.
entries.literal: The stone chamber lies north of the temple; rebuilding would leave the place unknown; the provisional tablet exists to lodge the spirit — when the spirit moves, there is the rite of burial.

entries.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也，准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。
entries.en: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to cease, their spirits likewise have no further lodging; following parallel precedents, their tablets should be buried as provisional tablets are.
entries.literal: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to be abolished, the spirits likewise have no lodging; following parallel precedents, they should be buried like provisional tablets.

entries.zh: 然經典難詳，群言紛錯，非臣卑淺所能折中。」
entries.en: Yet the classics are difficult to pin down and opinions conflict; this is more than my limited learning can reconcile."
entries.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail fully and many opinions tangle and clash — this is not something my lowly shallowness can reconcile."

entries.zh: 時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。
entries.en: At the time most scholars sided with Dao, but in the end his proposal was not implemented.
entries.literal: At the time most scholars followed Dao's proposal, but in the end it was not carried out.

entries.zh: 義熙初，高祖使撰車服儀注，乃除鎮軍諮議參軍，領記室。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yixi the Founding Emperor commissioned him to compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial protocol, and appointed him advisory aide on the Army Who Guards the Army staff, with charge of the secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yixi the Founding Emperor had him compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial observances, and appointed him advisory aide of the Army Who Guards the Army, heading the secretariat.

entries.zh: 封樂成縣五等侯。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Lecheng county.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Lecheng county.

entries.zh: 轉員外散騎常侍，領著作郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed head of the Master of Writings office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and headed the office of Master of Writings.

entries.zh: 二年，尚書奏曰：「臣聞左史述言，右官書事，《乘》、《志》顯于晉、鄭，《陽秋》著乎魯史。
entries.en: In the second year the Secretariat memorialized: "We have heard that the left historiographer records speech and the right official records events; the Cheng and Zhi gained renown in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were preserved in Lu's chronicle.
entries.literal: In the second year the Secretariat memorialized: "I have heard that the left historiographer records speech and the right official records affairs; the Cheng and Zhi were displayed in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were set forth in Lu's chronicle.

entries.zh: 自皇代有造，中興晉祀，道風帝典，煥乎史策。
entries.en: Since the founding of the imperial house and the restoration of Jin's rites, the moral example of the imperial canon has shone brilliantly in the historical records.
entries.literal: Since the imperial age was founded and Jin's sacrifices were restored, the way-wind and imperial canon shine brilliantly in the historical records.

entries.zh: 而太和以降，世曆三朝，玄風聖跡，倏為疇古。
entries.en: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and the sage's legacy has swiftly receded into the distant past.
entries.literal: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and the mysterious wind and sage traces have suddenly become antiquity.

entries.zh: 臣等參詳，宜敕著作郎徐廣撰成國史。」
entries.en: We your subjects have reviewed the matter and submit that Xu Guang of the Master of Writings office should be ordered to complete the national history."
entries.literal: We your subjects have examined the matter and hold that Xu Guang, Master of Writings, should be ordered to complete the national history."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「先朝至德光被，未著方策，宜流風緬代，永貽將來者也。
entries.en: The edict replied: "The supreme virtue of the former court spread its radiance yet was not recorded in the annals; its influence should span generations and be preserved for posterity.
entries.literal: The edict said: "The supreme virtue of the former court spread its radiance but was not recorded in the registers; its flowing influence should span generations and be bequeathed forever to those who come after.

entries.zh: 便敕撰集。」
entries.en: Let the compilation proceed at once."
entries.literal: Let compilation be ordered at once."

entries.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，又領徐州大中正，轉正員常侍。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, also served as great rectifier of Xu province, and was later made a full regular attendant.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, also headed the great rectifier of Xu province, and was made full regular attendant.

entries.zh: 時有風雹為災，廣獻書高祖曰：「風雹變未必為災，古之聖賢輒懼而修己，所以興政化而隆德教也。
entries.en: When wind and hail brought disaster, Guang wrote to the Founding Emperor: "Such omens are not necessarily calamities; the sages of antiquity always took them as warnings to refine themselves — and thereby raised good government and exalted moral teaching.
entries.literal: At the time wind and hail caused disaster; Guang submitted a letter to the Founding Emperor: "Wind and hail changes are not necessarily calamities; the sages of antiquity always feared them and cultivated themselves — thereby they raised government and exalted moral teaching.

entries.zh: 嘗忝服事，宿眷未忘，思竭塵露，率誠于習。
entries.en: I once had the honor to serve you and have not forgotten your kindness; I wish to offer whatever humble strength remains and speak with all sincerity from my experience.
entries.literal: I once had the honor to serve you and have not forgotten your longstanding favor; I wish to exhaust the dust and dew of my strength and offer sincerity in what I have learned.

entries.zh: 明公初建義旗，匡複宗社，神武應運，信宿平夷。
entries.en: When you first raised the righteous banner and restored the ancestral altars, your divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, and peace was restored within days.
entries.literal: When you first raised the righteous banner, restored the ancestral altars, and with divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, peace was restored within a day or two.

entries.zh: 且恭儉謙約，虛心匪懈，來蘇之化，功用若神。
entries.en: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, and modest, never slack in self-cultivation; the relief you bring to the people works as if by divine power.
entries.literal: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, modest, and restrained, humble in mind and never slack; the transformation of those who awaken from suffering works with godlike effect.

entries.zh: 頃事故既多，刑德並用，戰功殷積，報敘難盡，萬機繁湊，固應難速，且小細煩密，群下多懼。
entries.en: Recently affairs have multiplied, punishment and reward are applied together, military merit has piled up and rewards are hard to dispense, and the myriad tasks are pressing — swift action is naturally difficult; moreover petty matters are intricate and many subordinates live in fear.
entries.literal: Recently affairs have multiplied, punishment and virtue are applied together, military merit has heaped up and rewards are hard to exhaust, and the myriad tasks are dense and pressing — naturally speed is difficult; moreover petty matters are intricate and many below are fearful.

entries.zh: 又谷帛豐賤，而民情不勸；
entries.en: Grain and cloth are abundant and cheap, yet the people are not encouraged to prosper;
entries.literal: Again, grain and cloth are abundant and cheap, yet the people's hearts are not encouraged;

entries.zh: 禁司互設，而劫盜多有，誠由俗弊未易整，而望深未易炳。
entries.en: prohibitory offices multiply upon one another, yet robbery remains common — truly because popular abuses are hard to correct and deep expectations are hard to satisfy at once.
entries.literal: prohibitory offices are set up in mutual overlap, yet banditry is frequent — truly because popular abuses are not easily rectified and expectations run deep and are not easily made clear.

entries.zh: 追思義熙之始，如有不同，何者？
entries.en: Looking back to the beginning of Yixi, if something has changed, what is it?
entries.literal: Reflecting on the beginning of Yixi, if there is something different, what is it?

entries.zh: 好安願逸，萬物之大趣，習舊駭新，凡識所不免。
entries.en: The love of ease is the great tendency of all things, and alarm at the new when accustomed to the old is what ordinary minds cannot avoid.
entries.literal: Loving rest and wishing for ease is the great tendency of all things; being startled by the old when facing the new is what ordinary understanding cannot avoid.

entries.zh: 要當俯順群情，抑揚隨俗，則朝野歡泰，具瞻允康矣。
entries.en: What matters is to heed the feelings of the people and adjust policy to custom — then court and countryside will rejoice in peace, and all who look to you will find true well-being.
entries.literal: The essential thing is to bow to the feelings of the multitude and moderate and elevate according to custom — then court and countryside will rejoice in peace, and all who look up will find true tranquility.

entries.zh: 言無可采，願矜其愚款之志。」
entries.en: My words may have little worth; I only ask that you regard the sincerity of my humble counsel."
entries.literal: My words have nothing worth adopting; I only ask that you regard the sincerity of my foolish loyalty."

entries.zh: 又轉大司農，領著作郎皆如故。
entries.en: He was then appointed Minister of Agriculture while continuing to head the Master of Writings as before.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of Agriculture, continuing as before to head the Master of Writings.

entries.zh: 十二年，《晉紀》成，凡四十六卷，表上之。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he completed the Annals of Jin in forty-six volumes and submitted them to the throne.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year the Annals of Jin were completed, forty-six volumes in all, and were submitted in memorial.

entries.zh: 遷秘書監。
entries.en: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 初，桓玄篡位，安帝出宮，廣陪列悲慟，哀動左右。
entries.en: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An was driven from the palace, Guang stood in attendance weeping so bitterly that he moved all those around him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An left the palace, Guang stood in attendance, grieved and sobbed, moving those on either side.

entries.zh: 及高祖受禪，恭帝遜位，廣又哀感，涕泗交流。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang was again overcome with grief, tears streaming down his face.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang again was moved to grief, tears and mucus streaming down.

entries.zh: 謝晦見之，謂之曰：「徐公將無小過？」
entries.en: Xie Hui saw this and said to him: "Master Xu, are you not going a little too far?"
entries.literal: Xie Hui saw this and said to him: "Master Xu, are you not being a little excessive?"

entries.zh: 廣收淚答曰：「身與君不同。
entries.en: Guang wiped away his tears and replied: "My situation and yours are not the same.
entries.literal: Guang wiped away his tears and replied: "My person and yours are not the same.

entries.zh: 君佐命興王，逢千載嘉運；
entries.en: You assisted the mandate and helped raise the new dynasty, meeting a once-in-a-millennium fortune;
entries.literal: You assisted the mandate and raised the royal house, meeting a thousand-year auspicious fortune;

entries.zh: 身世荷晉德，實眷戀故主。」
entries.en: my family and I received Jin's grace and truly remain attached to the former sovereign."
entries.literal: my person and family received Jin's grace and truly cherish attachment to the former lord."

entries.zh: 因更歔欷。
entries.en: He then sobbed afresh.
entries.literal: He then sobbed again.

entries.zh: 列傳第十六 謝瞻孔琳之
entries.en: Biography 16: Xie Zhan and Kong Linzhi
entries.literal: Biography 16: Xie Zhan, Kong Linzhi

entries.zh: 謝瞻，字宣遠，一名簷，字通遠，陳郡陽夏人，衛將軍晦第三兄也。
entries.en: Xie Zhan, whose courtesy name was Xuanyuan—he was also known as Yan, with the alternative courtesy name Tongyuan—came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery and was the third elder brother of Xie Hui, General of the Guard.
entries.literal: Xie Zhan, courtesy name Xuanyuan, also called Yan with the alternative courtesy name Tongyuan, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery and the third elder brother of General of the Guard Xie Hui.

entries.zh: 年六歲，能屬文，為《紫石英贊》、《果然詩》，當時才士，莫不歎異。
entries.en: At six he could already compose literary pieces, including "In Praise of Amethyst Quartz" and "The Guoran Poem," and every gifted writer of the time marveled at him.
entries.literal: At the age of six he could compose literary works, writing "In Praise of Amethyst Quartz" and "The Guoran Poem"; the talented men of the day all sighed in wonder.

entries.zh: 初為桓偉安西參軍，楚台秘書郎。
entries.en: He began his career as a staff officer under Huan Wei in the Anxi command and later became Secretary Gentleman in the Chu court.
entries.literal: He first served as staff officer to Huan Wei in the Anxi command, then as Secretary Gentleman in the Chu regime.

entries.zh: 瞻幼孤，叔母劉撫養有恩紀，兄弟事之，同於至親。
entries.en: Zhan was orphaned young; his aunt by marriage, the Liu lady, raised him with devoted care, and he and his brothers treated her exactly as they would their own parents.
entries.literal: Zhan lost his father in childhood; his aunt by marriage, Lady Liu, raised him with devoted kindness, and he and his brothers served her as they would their closest kin.

entries.zh: 劉弟柳為吳郡，將姊俱行，瞻不能違，解職隨從，為柳建威長史。
entries.en: When Lady Liu's brother Liu Liu was appointed governor of Wu and took their elder sister along, Zhan could not bring himself to stay behind; he resigned and went with them, serving Liu as chief clerk of the Jianwei command.
entries.literal: When Lady Liu's younger brother Liu Liu became governor of Wu Commandery and took their elder sister with him, Zhan could not refuse and resigned his post to follow, serving Liu as Chief Clerk of the Jianwei command.

entries.zh: 尋為高祖鎮軍、琅邪王大司馬參軍，轉主簿，安成相，中書侍郎，宋國中書、黃門侍郎，相國從事中郎。
entries.en: He was soon appointed staff officer to Emperor Gaozu's Zhenjun Army and to the Prince of Langye as Grand Marshal, then served successively as chief clerk, administrator of Ancheng, gentleman of the palace secretariat, secretariat and yellow gate gentleman of the Song state, and attendant of the chancellor of state.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he became a staff officer to the Zhenjun Army and to the Prince of Langye as Grand Marshal, then chief clerk, Administrator of Ancheng, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Secretariat and Yellow Gate Gentleman of the Song state, and Attendant of the Chancellor of State.

entries.zh: 瞻善於文章，辭采之美，與族叔混、族弟靈運相抗。
entries.en: Zhan was a gifted writer; the brilliance of his style rivaled that of his clansman Hun and his younger kinsman Lingyun.
entries.literal: Zhan excelled at literary composition; the beauty of his diction matched that of his clansman Hun and his younger clansman Lingyun.

entries.zh: 靈運父瑛，無才能。
entries.en: Lingyun's father Ying was a man of no particular talent.
entries.literal: Lingyun's father Ying had no talent or ability.

entries.zh: 為秘書郎，早年而亡。
entries.en: He had served as secretary gentleman and died young.
entries.literal: He served as Secretary Gentleman and died in early years.

entries.zh: 靈運好臧否人物，混患之，欲加裁折，未有方也。
entries.en: Lingyun loved to pass judgment on other people's merits and faults; Hun found this troubling and wanted to rein him in, but had not yet found a way.
entries.literal: Lingyun liked to pass judgment on people's merits and faults; Hun was troubled by this and wished to curb him, but had found no means.

entries.zh: 謂瞻曰：「非汝莫能。」
entries.en: He said to Zhan, "No one but you can manage this."
entries.literal: He said to Zhan, "No one but you can do it."

entries.zh: 乃與晦、曜、弘微等共遊戲，使瞻與靈運共車；
entries.en: He then arranged outings with Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and the others and had Zhan share a carriage with Lingyun.
entries.literal: He then joined Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and the others in shared outings and had Zhan ride in the same carriage as Lingyun.

entries.zh: 靈運登車，便商較人物，瞻謂之曰：「秘書早亡，談者亦互有同異。」
entries.en: The moment Lingyun got into the carriage he began ranking people's merits and faults. Zhan said to him, "The secretary gentleman died young, and even those who speak of him disagree among themselves."
entries.literal: As soon as Lingyun boarded the carriage he began comparing people's merits; Zhan said to him, "The Secretary Gentleman died young, and those who discuss him also differ among themselves."

entries.zh: 靈運默然，言論自此衰止。
entries.en: Lingyun fell silent, and from that day his habit of judging others faded away.
entries.literal: Lingyun fell silent, and from then on such talk dwindled and ceased.

entries.zh: 弟晦時為宋台右衛，權遇已重，于彭城還都迎家，賓客輻輳，門巷填咽。
entries.en: His younger brother Hui then held the post of Right Guard in the Song regime, and his influence was already formidable. When he returned from Pengcheng to the capital to bring the family home, guests thronged about him until the lanes before his gate were impassable.
entries.literal: His younger brother Hui was then Right Guard of the Song regime; his power and favor were already great. Returning from Pengcheng to the capital to fetch the family, guests converged like wheel spokes and the lanes before his gate were choked.

entries.zh: 時瞻在家，驚駭謂晦曰：「汝名位未多，而人歸趣乃爾。
entries.en: Zhan was at home at the time. Alarmed, he said to Hui, "Your rank and title are still modest, yet people are flocking to you like this.
entries.literal: Zhan was then at home and, startled and alarmed, said to Hui, "Your rank and title are not yet great, yet people flock to you like this.

entries.zh: 吾家以素退為業，不願干預時事，交遊不過親朋，而汝遂勢傾朝野，此豈門戶之福邪？」
entries.en: Our family has always made a virtue of modest retirement; we do not wish to meddle in public affairs, and our circle extends no farther than kin and friends—yet you have come to dominate court and countryside alike. Can this truly be a blessing for our house?"
entries.literal: Our family has made plain withdrawal its calling; we do not wish to meddle in the affairs of the age, and our acquaintances extend no farther than kin and friends—yet you have come to sway court and countryside. Is this really a blessing for our house?"

entries.zh: 乃籬隔門庭，曰：「吾不忍見此。」
entries.en: He then put up a hedge to screen off the courtyard, saying, "I cannot bear to look upon this."
entries.literal: He then fenced off the courtyard with a hedge, saying, "I cannot bear to see this."

entries.zh: 及還彭城，言于高祖曰：「臣本素士，父、祖位不過二千石。
entries.en: When he returned to Pengcheng he told Emperor Gaozu, "I was originally a man of no distinction; my father and grandfather never rose above the two-thousand-dan rank.
entries.literal: When he returned to Pengcheng he spoke to Emperor Gaozu, saying, "Your servant was originally a plain scholar; my father and grandfather held posts no higher than the two-thousand-dan rank.

entries.zh: 弟年始三十，志用凡近，榮冠台府，位任顯密，福過災生，其應無遠。
entries.en: My brother has only just turned thirty; his talents and ambitions are unremarkable, yet his honors outshine the whole regime and his offices are weighty and exposed. When fortune runs too high, disaster follows—and that day cannot be far off.
entries.literal: My brother has only just turned thirty; his aims and abilities are ordinary, yet his glory tops the regime and his office is conspicuous and weighty. When good fortune exceeds its measure, disaster is born—the consequence cannot be far off.

entries.zh: 特乞降黜，以保衰門。」
entries.en: I beg that he be demoted and removed from office, so that our declining house may be spared."
entries.literal: I beg especially that he be demoted and removed from office, to preserve our declining house."

entries.zh: 前後屢陳。
entries.en: He made this plea again and again.
entries.literal: He submitted such petitions repeatedly.

entries.zh: 高祖以瞻為吳興郡，又自陳請，乃為豫章太守。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhan to Wuxing Commandery, but Zhan petitioned again on his own behalf and was instead made administrator of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhan to Wuxing Commandery; he petitioned again on his own behalf and was then made Administrator of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 晦或以朝廷密事語瞻，瞻輒向親舊陳說，以為笑戲，以絕其言。
entries.en: When Hui confided court secrets to him, Zhan would promptly repeat them to relatives and old friends as a joke, so as to put an end to such disclosures.
entries.literal: Hui would sometimes tell Zhan confidential matters of the court; Zhan would at once repeat them to kin and old friends as a jest, to cut off such talk.

entries.zh: 晦遂建佐命之功，任寄隆重，瞻愈憂懼。
entries.en: Hui went on to earn merit in establishing the new dynasty, and the trust placed in him grew ever heavier; Zhan's anxiety only deepened.
entries.literal: Hui then achieved merit in aiding the founding mandate; his commission and trust grew weighty, and Zhan grew ever more anxious and afraid.

entries.zh: 永初二年，在郡遇疾，不肯自治，幸於不永。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongchu he fell ill while serving in his commandery; he refused medical care, hoping his life would not be prolonged.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, while in his commandery he fell ill; he refused to treat himself, hoping his life would not be long.

entries.zh: 晦聞疾奔往，瞻見之，曰：「汝為國大臣，又總戎重，萬里遠出，必生疑謗。」
entries.en: When Hui heard of his illness he rushed to his side. Zhan saw him and said, "You are a chief minister of state and hold supreme military authority; to travel a thousand li on such an errand is bound to invite suspicion and slander."
entries.literal: Hearing of the illness, Hui rushed to him; when Zhan saw him he said, "You are a great minister of state and also hold overall military authority; to travel a thousand li on such an errand is sure to breed suspicion and slander."

entries.zh: 時果有訴告晦反者。
entries.en: And indeed, at that very time petitions were filed accusing Hui of rebellion.
entries.literal: At that time there were indeed petitions accusing Hui of rebellion.

entries.zh: 瞻疾篤還都，高祖以晦禁旅，不得出宿，使瞻居於晉南郡公主婿羊賁故第，在領軍府東門。
entries.en: When Zhan's illness grew grave he returned to the capital. Because Hui commanded the palace guard and could not stay away overnight, Emperor Gaozu had Zhan lodged in the former residence of Yang Ben, son-in-law of the Jin Princess of Nan Commandery, east of the headquarters of the General of the Guards.
entries.literal: When Zhan's illness grew grave he returned to the capital. Because Hui commanded the palace guard and could not lodge outside, Emperor Gaozu had Zhan stay in the former residence of Yang Ben, son-in-law of the Jin Princess of Nan Commandery, east of the General of the Guards headquarters.

entries.zh: 瞻曰：「吾有先人弊廬，何為於此！」
entries.en: Zhan said, "I have my forefathers' humble house—why should I stay here?"
entries.literal: Zhan said, "I have my forefathers' humble dwelling—why should I be here!"

entries.zh: 臨終，遣晦書曰：「吾得啟體幸全，歸骨山足，亦何所多恨。
entries.en: On his deathbed he sent Hui a letter: "I have been fortunate to leave this world with my body whole and to return my bones to the hills—what more could I regret?
entries.literal: On his deathbed he sent Hui a letter saying, "I have been fortunate to leave my body whole and to return my bones to the foot of the hills—what more is there to regret?

entries.zh: 弟思自勉厲，為國為家。」
entries.en: Brother, strive to discipline yourself—for the sake of the state and our house."
entries.literal: Brother, strive to urge yourself on—for the state and for the family."

entries.zh: 遂卒，時年三十五。
entries.en: He died soon after, at the age of thirty-five.
entries.literal: He then died, at the age of thirty-five.

entries.zh: 弟㬭，字宣鏡，幼有殊行。
entries.en: His younger brother Jiao, whose courtesy name was Xuanjing, showed exceptional conduct from childhood.
entries.literal: His younger brother Jiao, courtesy name Xuanjing, showed extraordinary conduct from childhood.

entries.zh: 年數歲，所生母郭氏，久嬰痼疾，晨昏溫清，嘗藥捧膳，不闕一時，勤容戚顏，未嘗暫改。
entries.en: While still a small boy, he cared for his birth mother of the Guo clan, who had long suffered a chronic illness. Morning and evening he saw to her comfort, tasted her medicine, and brought her food without missing a single hour; his devoted manner and sorrowful face never changed, even for a moment.
entries.literal: When he was only a few years old, his birth mother, the Guo clan, suffered a chronic illness for a long time; morning and evening he attended her with warm and cool care, tasted her medicine and brought her meals, never missing an hour; his earnest bearing and sorrowful countenance never changed for a moment.

entries.zh: 恐僕役營疾懈倦，躬自執勞。
entries.en: Fearing the servants who nursed her would grow slack, he took on the work himself.
entries.literal: Fearing that the servants tending the sick would grow slack and weary, he personally took up the labor himself.

entries.zh: 母為病畏驚，微踐過甚，一家尊卑，感㬭至性，鹹納屢而行，屏氣而語，如此者十餘年。
entries.en: Because his mother feared being startled by noise in her illness, even the lightest footfall was too much; moved by Jiao's devotion, everyone in the household, high and low alike, removed their shoes and walked on tiptoe, speaking only in hushed breaths—for more than ten years.
entries.literal: Because his mother, in her illness, feared being startled, the slightest step was excessive; high and low in the household, moved by Jiao's utmost sincerity, all removed their shoes and walked softly, holding their breath when they spoke—thus for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 初為州主簿，中軍行參軍，太子舍人，俄遷秘書丞。
entries.en: He first served as provincial chief clerk, staff officer of the central army, and attendant of the heir apparent, and was soon promoted to secretary director.
entries.literal: He first served as chief clerk of the province, staff officer of the Central Army, and attendant of the heir apparent, and soon was promoted to Secretary Director.

entries.zh: 自以兄居權貴，己蒙超擢，固辭不就。
entries.en: Because his elder brother held power and rank and he himself had been promoted beyond his due, he firmly declined the appointment.
entries.literal: Considering that his elder brother held power and rank and that he himself had received extraordinary promotion, he firmly declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 徐羨之請為司空長史，黃門郎。
entries.en: Xu Xianzhi had him appointed chief clerk of the minister of works and gentleman of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: Xu Xianzhi had him appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 元嘉三年，從坐伏誅，時年三十一。
entries.en: In the third year of Yuanjia he was executed as an associate in the crime; he was thirty-one.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he was executed by association; he was thirty-one.

entries.zh: 有詔宥其子世平，又早卒，無後。
entries.en: An edict spared his son Shiping, but Shiping too died young, and the line came to an end.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned his son Shiping, but Shiping also died young and left no heirs.

entries.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to gentleman of the ministry of personnel in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 義熙六年，高祖領平西將軍，以為長史，大司馬琅邪王從事中郎。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yixi, when Emperor Gaozu held the post of general who pacifies the west, he appointed Linzhi chief clerk and attendant of the prince of Langye as grand marshal.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yixi, when Emperor Gaozu held the post of General Who Pacifies the West, he appointed Linzhi Chief Clerk and Attendant of the Prince of Langye as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 又除高祖平北、征西長史，遷侍中。
entries.en: He was also appointed chief clerk to Emperor Gaozu's pacify-the-north and campaign-the-west commands and promoted to palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was also appointed Chief Clerk to Emperor Gaozu's Pacify-the-North and Campaign-the-West commands and was promoted to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 宋台初建，除宋國侍中。
entries.en: When the Song regime was first established, he was appointed palace attendant of the Song state.
entries.literal: When the Song regime was first established, he was appointed Palace Attendant of the Song state.

entries.zh: 出為吳興太守，公事免。
entries.en: He was sent out as administrator of Wuxing Commandery and was dismissed for official misconduct.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Wuxing Commandery and was dismissed for official misconduct.

entries.zh: 永初二年，為禦史中丞。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongchu he became imperial censor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he became Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 明憲直法，無所屈橈。
entries.en: He was clear in statutes and upright in law, yielding to no pressure.
entries.literal: He was clear in statutes and upright in law, bending to nothing.

entries.zh: 奏劾尚書令徐羨之曰：「臣聞事上以奉憲為恭，臨下以威嚴為整。
entries.en: He memorialized to impeach the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xianzhi: "I have heard that serving superiors by upholding the law is respect, and governing subordinates with authority is order.
entries.literal: He memorialized to impeach the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xianzhi, saying, "Your servant has heard that serving superiors with observance of statutes is respect, and facing subordinates with awe and dignity is order.

entries.zh: 然後朝典惟明，蒞眾必肅。
entries.en: Only then are court statutes clear and the multitude governed with dignity.
entries.literal: Only then are court statutes clear and the multitude governed with dignity.

entries.zh: 斯道或替，則憲綱其頹。
entries.en: When this way is neglected, the net of law collapses.
entries.literal: When this way is neglected, the net of law collapses.

entries.zh: 臣以今月七日，預皇太子正會。
entries.en: On the seventh day of this month I attended the crown prince's regular assembly.
entries.literal: Your servant on the seventh day of this month attended the crown prince's regular assembly.

entries.zh: 會畢車去，並猥臣停門待闕。
entries.en: When the assembly ended the carriages departed, and I waited at the gate for the audience to close.
entries.literal: When the assembly ended the carriages departed, and I, unworthy as I am, waited at the gate for the audience to close.

entries.zh: 有何人乘馬，當臣車前，收捕驅遣命去。
entries.en: A man on horseback blocked my carriage; I had my officers seize him and ordered him driven away.
entries.literal: Some man on horseback blocked before my carriage; I had my officers seize him and ordered him driven away.

entries.zh: 何人罵詈收捕，咨審欲錄。
entries.en: The man cursed my officers; I questioned him and intended to take his name.
entries.literal: The man cursed my officers; I questioned him and intended to take a record.

entries.zh: 每有公事，臣常慮有紛紜，語令勿問，而何人獨罵不止，臣乃使錄。
entries.en: Whenever there is official business I always fear disorder and tell my men not to pursue it—but this man alone would not stop cursing, so I ordered his name taken.
entries.literal: Whenever there is official business I always fear disorder and tell them not to inquire—but this man alone would not stop cursing, so I ordered a record made.

entries.zh: 何人不肯下馬，連叫大喚，有兩威儀走來，擊臣收捕。
entries.en: The man would not dismount and kept shouting; two ceremonial attendants ran up and struck my officers.
entries.literal: The man would not dismount and kept shouting loudly; two ceremonial attendants ran up and struck my officers who had seized him.

entries.zh: 尚書令省事倪宗又牽威儀手力，擊臣下人。
entries.en: Ni Zong, clerk of the minister of works, also pulled the ceremonial attendants' men and struck my subordinates.
entries.literal: Ni Zong, clerk of the Minister of Works, also pulled the ceremonial attendants' strongmen and struck my subordinates.

entries.zh: 宗云：『中丞何得行凶，敢錄令公人。
entries.en: Zong said, 'How dare the censor commit violence and seize the minister's men!
entries.literal: Zong said, 'How dare the censor commit violence and seize the minister's men!

entries.zh: 凡是中丞收捕，威儀悉皆縛取。
entries.en: Every man the censor seizes, the ceremonial attendants bind and take away.'
entries.literal: Every man the censor seizes, the ceremonial attendants bind and take away.'

entries.zh: '臣敕下人一不得鬥，凶勢輈張，有頃乃散。
entries.en: I ordered my subordinates not to fight; the violence was overwhelming, and only after a while did it disperse.
entries.literal: I ordered my subordinates not to fight at all; the violent force was overwhelming, and only after a while did it disperse.

entries.zh: 又有群人就臣車側，錄收捕樊馬子，互行築馬子頓伏，不能還台。
entries.en: Another crowd gathered beside my carriage; my officers had seized Fan Mazi—they beat him until he collapsed and could not return to the censorate.
entries.literal: Another crowd gathered beside my carriage; I had Fan Mazi, whom my officers had seized, recorded—they beat Fan Mazi until he collapsed and could not return to the censorate.

entries.zh: 臣自錄非，本無對校，而宗敢乘勢凶恣，篡奪罪身。
entries.en: I was taking the record myself; there was no confrontation—yet Zong dared, riding the wave of violence, to seize the prisoner by force.
entries.literal: I was taking the record myself; there was originally no confrontation—yet Zong dared, riding the momentum of violence, to seize the guilty person by force.

entries.zh: 尚書令臣羨之，與臣列車，紛紜若此，或雲羨之不禁，或雲羨之禁而不止。
entries.en: The minister of works Xu Xianzhi was in the same row of carriages; with such disorder, some say he did not restrain it, others say he tried but could not stop it.
entries.literal: The Minister of Works, your servant Xianzhi, was in the same row of carriages; with such disorder, some say Xianzhi did not restrain it, others say he restrained but could not stop it.

entries.zh: 縱而不禁，既乖國憲；
entries.en: To indulge without restraint already violates the statutes of the state;
entries.literal: To indulge without restraint already violates the statutes of the state;

entries.zh: 禁而不止，又不經通。
entries.en: to restrain yet fail to stop is likewise without proper authority.
entries.literal: to restrain yet fail to stop is likewise without proper authority.

entries.zh: 陵犯監司，凶聲彰赫，容縱宗等，曾無糾問，虧損國威，無大臣之體，不有準繩，風裁何寄。
entries.en: He allowed assault on the censorate; his violent reputation was notorious; he indulged Zong and the rest without inquiry or correction—damaging the state's authority and lacking the bearing of a great minister; without standards, upon what can moral discipline rest?
entries.literal: He allowed assault on the supervising office; his violent reputation was glaring; he indulged Zong and the rest without ever inquiring or correcting—damaging the state's authority, lacking the bearing of a great minister; without standards and measures, upon what can moral discipline rest?

entries.zh: 羨之內居朝右，外司輦轂，位任隆重，百辟所瞻。
entries.en: Xianzhi holds the foremost position at court and administers the capital region; his office is weighty, and all officials look to him.
entries.literal: Xianzhi within holds the right hand of the court and without administers the capital region; his position and commission are weighty, and all the hundred officials look to him.

entries.zh: 而不能弘惜朝章，肅是風軌。
entries.en: Yet he could not uphold the court's statutes and enforce this standard of conduct.
entries.literal: Yet he could not broadly cherish the court's statutes and make this standard of conduct solemn.

entries.zh: 致使宇下縱肆，淩暴憲司，凶赫之聲，起自京邑，所謂己有短垣，而自逾之。
entries.en: The result was that subordinates ran wild and insulted the censorate; violence arose from the capital itself—what is called having a low wall and leaping over it oneself.
entries.literal: The result was that those below were unrestrained and insulted the censorate; the sound of violence arose from the capital itself—what is called having a low wall and leaping over it oneself.

entries.zh: 又宗為篡奪之主，縱不糾問，二三虧違，宜有裁貶。
entries.en: Moreover Zong led the forcible seizure; even if he is not prosecuted, these breaches warrant censure and demotion.
entries.literal: Moreover Zong was the chief of the forcible seizure; even if he is not inquired into, these two or three breaches warrant censure and demotion.

entries.zh: 請免羨之所居官，以公還第。
entries.en: I request that Xianzhi be removed from office and sent home with the title of duke.
entries.literal: I request that Xianzhi be removed from his office and sent home with the title of duke.

entries.zh: 宗等篡奪之愆，已屬掌故禦史隨事檢處。」
entries.en: The offense of Zong and the rest has already been referred to the clerical censor for investigation and disposition."
entries.literal: The offense of Zong and the rest in forcible seizure has already been referred to the clerical censor for investigation and disposition according to the facts."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「小人難可檢禦，司空無所問，餘如奏。」
entries.en: An edict said, "Petty men are hard to restrain; the minister of works is not to be questioned; the rest as memorialized."
entries.literal: An edict said, "Petty men are hard to restrain and control; the Minister of Works is not to be questioned; the rest as memorialized."

entries.zh: 羨之任居朝端，不欲以犯憲示物。
entries.en: Xianzhi, holding the foremost post at court, did not wish to display a violation of law before others.
entries.literal: Xianzhi, holding the foremost post at court, did not wish to display violation of the statutes before others.

entries.zh: 時羨之領揚州刺史，琳之弟璩之為治中，羨之使璩之解釋琳之，停寢其事。
entries.en: At that time Xianzhi also governed Yang Province; Linzhi's younger brother Qiong was attendant clerk, and Xianzhi had Qiong intercede with Linzhi to suspend the case.
entries.literal: At that time Xianzhi also held the post of Governor of Yang Province; Linzhi's younger brother Qiong was Attendant Clerk, and Xianzhi had Qiong explain matters to Linzhi and suspend the case.

entries.zh: 琳之不許。
entries.en: Linzhi would not agree.
entries.literal: Linzhi would not agree.

entries.zh: 璩之固陳，琳之謂曰：「我觸忤宰相，正當罪止一身爾，汝必不應從坐，何須勤勤邪！」
entries.en: Qiong pressed him repeatedly. Linzhi said, "I have offended the chancellor; the punishment should stop with me alone. You certainly ought not to suffer by association—why press so earnestly?"
entries.literal: Qiong pressed him repeatedly; Linzhi said to him, "I have offended the chancellor; the punishment should rightly stop with me alone. You certainly ought not to suffer by association—why press so earnestly!"

entries.zh: 自是百僚震肅莫敢犯禁。
entries.en: From then on the hundred officials were awed into dignity and none dared violate the prohibitions.
entries.literal: From then on the hundred officials were awed into dignity and none dared violate the prohibitions.

entries.zh: 高祖甚嘉之，行經蘭台，親加臨幸。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu greatly praised him; passing the Orchid Terrace, he paid a personal visit.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu greatly praised him; passing by the Orchid Terrace, he personally paid a visit.

entries.zh: 又領本州大中正，遷祠部尚書。
entries.en: He also served as grand rectifier of his native province and was promoted to minister of the imperial ancestral temple.
entries.literal: He also held the post of Grand Rectifier of his native province and was promoted to Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 不治產業，家尤貧素。
entries.en: He did not manage estates; his household was especially poor and plain.
entries.literal: He did not manage estates; his household was especially poor and plain.

entries.zh: 景平元年，卒，時年五十五。
entries.en: In the first year of Jingping he died, at the age of fifty-five.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingping he died, at the age of fifty-five.

entries.zh: 追贈太常。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of ceremonies.
entries.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 孔琳之，字彥琳，會稽山陰人。
entries.en: Kong Linzhi, whose courtesy name was Yanlin, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Kong Linzhi, courtesy name Yanlin, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 祖沈，晉丞相掾。
entries.en: His grandfather Shen had served as an aide to the Jin chancellor.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shen was an aide to the Jin chancellor.

entries.zh: 父廞，光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Yin had held the post of grand master of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: His father Yin was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 琳之強正有志力，好文義，解音律，能彈棋，妙善草隸。
entries.en: Linzhi was forceful and upright, a man of firm resolve; he loved letters and learning, understood music, played chess well, and was a master of cursive and clerical calligraphy.
entries.literal: Linzhi was forceful and upright, with resolve and strength; he loved literary learning, understood music, could play chess, and excelled at cursive and clerical script.

entries.zh: 郡命主簿，不就，後辟本國常侍。
entries.en: The commandery offered him the post of chief clerk, but he declined; he was later summoned as regular attendant of his native state.
entries.literal: The commandery appointed him chief clerk, but he did not accept; later he was summoned as Regular Attendant of his native state.

entries.zh: 桓玄輔政為太尉，以為西閣祭酒。
entries.en: When Huan Xuan held power as grand marshal, he appointed Linzhi libationer of the Western Pavilion.
entries.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted in government as Grand Marshal, he appointed Linzhi Libationer of the Western Pavilion.

entries.zh: 桓玄時議欲廢錢用穀帛，琳之議曰：「《洪範》八政，以貨次食，豈不以交易之所資，為用之至要者乎？
entries.en: At that time Huan Xuan proposed abolishing coin and using grain and cloth currency instead. Linzhi argued: "In the Eight Policies of the Hongfan, wealth ranks immediately after food—is this not because the medium of exchange is among the most essential instruments of government?
entries.literal: At that time Huan Xuan proposed abolishing coin and using grain and cloth instead; Linzhi argued, saying, "In the Eight Policies of the Hongfan, wealth comes next after food—is this not because what trade relies upon is among the most essential of uses?

entries.zh: 若使不以交易，百姓用力于為錢，則是妨其為生之業，禁之可也。
entries.en: If the people were not using coin for trade but were exhausting themselves minting money instead, that would indeed obstruct their livelihood—and forbidding it would be right.
entries.literal: If the people were not to use it for trade but were to exert their labor on making money, that would obstruct the livelihood by which they live—then forbidding it would be fitting.

entries.zh: 今農自務穀，工自務器，四民各肄其業，何嘗致勤于錢。
entries.en: Today farmers devote themselves to grain and artisans to tools; the four classes each pursue their own calling—when have they ever lavished their labor on coin?
entries.literal: Now farmers devote themselves to grain, artisans to tools; the four classes each pursue their own calling—when have they ever applied their diligence to coin?

entries.zh: 故聖王制無用之貨，以通有用之財，既無毀敗之費，又省運置之苦，此錢所以嗣功龜貝，歷代不廢者也。
entries.en: That is why the sage kings created a token of no intrinsic use to circulate goods of real value, avoiding spoilage and sparing the cost of transport—this is why coin succeeded tortoise shells and cowries and has never been abandoned across the ages.
entries.literal: Therefore the sage kings fashioned useless goods to circulate useful wealth, avoiding the cost of spoilage and sparing the hardship of transport and storage—this is why coin succeeded tortoise shells and cowries and has not been abandoned through the ages.

entries.zh: 穀帛為寶，本充衣食，今分以為貨，則致損甚多。
entries.en: Grain and cloth are treasures meant for food and clothing; if they are now parcelled out to serve as currency, the waste will be enormous.
entries.literal: Grain and cloth are treasures meant to supply food and clothing; if they are now divided off to serve as currency, the loss will be very great.

entries.zh: 又勞毀于商販之手，耗棄於割截之用，此之為敝，著於自曩。
entries.en: They are further worn down in merchants' hands and wasted in cutting and trimming—this harm has been plain since antiquity.
entries.literal: Moreover they are worn out in the hands of merchants and wasted in cutting and trimming—this harm has been evident since antiquity.

entries.zh: 故鐘繇曰：'巧偽之民，競蘊濕穀以要利，制薄絹以充資。
entries.en: As Zhong Yao said, "Crafty men compete to hoard damp grain for profit and weave thin silk to pass as currency."
entries.literal: Therefore Zhong Yao said, 'Crafty and deceitful men compete to hoard damp grain for profit and make thin silk to serve as currency.'

entries.zh: '魏世制以嚴刑，弗能禁也。
entries.en: In the Wei dynasty severe punishments were imposed, yet the practice could not be stopped.
entries.literal: In the Wei era severe punishments were imposed, yet it could not be stopped.

entries.zh: 是以司馬芝以為用錢非徒豐國，亦所以省刑。
entries.en: That is why Sima Zhi argued that using coin not only enriches the state but also reduces the need for harsh punishments.
entries.literal: Therefore Sima Zhi held that using coin not only enriches the state but also reduces punishments.

entries.zh: 錢之不用，由於兵亂積久，自至於廢，有由而然，漢末是也。
entries.en: Coin fell out of use because warfare and disorder persisted so long that it was abandoned of its own accord; there was a reason for it, as at the end of the Han.
entries.literal: The disuse of coin came from warfare and disorder accumulating over a long time until it fell into disuse of itself; there was a reason for it—such was the end of Han.

entries.zh: 今既用而廢之，則百姓頓亡其財。
entries.en: Now that coin is in use, to abolish it would be to strip the common people of their wealth overnight.
entries.literal: Now, having used it and then abolishing it, the common people would at once lose their wealth.

entries.zh: 今括囊天下之谷，以周天下之食，或倉庾充衍，或糧靡鬥儲，以相資通，則貧者仰富，致之之道，實假于錢。
entries.en: If one gathered all the grain in the realm to feed everyone, some granaries would overflow while others would lack even a peck in store; to move supplies between them so the poor could draw on the rich—the means to do this truly depends on coin.
entries.literal: If one were to gather all the grain under Heaven to supply all the food under Heaven, some granaries would overflow while others would lack even a peck in store; to aid and circulate between them so that the poor might rely on the rich—the way to achieve this truly depends on coin.

entries.zh: 一朝斷之，便為棄物，是有錢無糧之民，皆坐而饑困，此斷錢之立敝也。
entries.en: Abolish it overnight and it becomes worthless scrap; those who hold coin but no grain would all sit helpless and starve—this is the immediate harm of cutting off coin.
entries.literal: Cut it off in a single morning and it becomes worthless refuse; those who have coin but no grain would all sit idle and starve—this is the immediate harm of abolishing coin.

entries.zh: 且據今用錢之處不為貧，用穀之處不為富。
entries.en: Moreover, judging from present conditions, regions that use coin are not poor, and regions that use grain are not rich.
entries.literal: Moreover, judging from the present, places that use coin are not poor, and places that use grain are not rich.

entries.zh: 又民習來久，革之必惑。
entries.en: The people have long been accustomed to coin; to change the system would surely breed confusion.
entries.literal: The people have long been accustomed to it; to change it would surely breed confusion.

entries.zh: 語曰：'利不百，不易業。
entries.en: As the saying goes, "Unless the profit is a hundredfold, do not change your trade."
entries.literal: A saying runs, 'If the profit is not a hundredfold, do not change your occupation.'

entries.zh: '況又錢便於穀邪？
entries.en: How much more convenient is coin than grain?
entries.literal: How much more is coin more convenient than grain?

entries.zh: 魏明帝時，錢廢穀用，三十年矣。
entries.en: Under Emperor Ming of Wei, coin was abolished and grain used as currency—for thirty years.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Wei, coin was abolished and grain was used—for thirty years.

entries.zh: 以不便於民，乃舉朝大議。
entries.en: Because it proved inconvenient for the people, the whole court debated the matter at length.
entries.literal: Because it was inconvenient for the people, the whole court held a great debate.

entries.zh: 精才達治之士，莫不以為宜複用錢，民無異情，朝無異論。
entries.en: Talented statesmen all agreed that coin should be restored; the people had no objection, and the court had no dissent.
entries.literal: Men of refined talent versed in governance all held that coin should be used again; the people had no dissenting sentiment, and the court had no dissenting opinion.

entries.zh: 彼尚舍穀帛而用錢，足以明穀帛之弊，著於已試。
entries.en: They still abandoned grain and cloth in favor of coin—enough to show the defects of grain-and-cloth currency, as proven by experience.
entries.literal: They still set aside grain and cloth to use coin—enough to show the defects of grain and cloth, demonstrated by what had already been tried.

entries.zh: 世或謂魏氏不用錢久，積累巨萬，故欲行之，利公富國。
entries.en: Some say the Wei restored coin because they had long gone without it and accumulated vast stores, hoping thereby to enrich the public treasury and strengthen the state.
entries.literal: Some in the world say that because the Wei had long not used coin and had accumulated tens of thousands, they wished to restore it to benefit the public treasury and enrich the state.

entries.zh: 斯殆不然。
entries.en: That is almost certainly wrong.
entries.literal: That is probably not so.

entries.zh: 昔晉文後舅犯之謀，而先成季之信，以為雖有一時之勳，不如萬世之益。
entries.en: Long ago Duke Wen of Jin deferred Jiu Fan's counsel but honored Ji Zi's pledge first, holding that a moment's merit was nothing compared to benefit lasting ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: Formerly Duke Wen of Jin put Jiu Fan's counsel later but fulfilled Ji Zi's pledge first, holding that though there might be merit for a moment, it was not equal to benefit for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 于時名賢在列，君子盈朝，大謀天下之利害，將定經國之要術。
entries.en: At that time famous worthies sat in the ranks and gentlemen filled the court; they debated the welfare of the realm and were about to settle the essential methods of statecraft.
entries.literal: At that time famous worthies sat in the ranks and gentlemen filled the court; they deliberated greatly on the benefit and harm under Heaven, about to fix the essential methods for governing the state.

entries.zh: 若谷實便錢，義不昧當時之近利，而廢永用之通業，斷可知矣。
entries.en: If grain had truly been more convenient than coin, they would never, in good conscience, have sacrificed a lasting institution for a moment's gain—that much is certain.
entries.literal: If grain were truly more convenient than coin, they would not, in righteousness, have obscured the near profit of the moment and abandoned the enduring common enterprise—this can be known for certain.

entries.zh: 斯實由困而思革，改而更張耳。
entries.en: They acted from hardship and sought reform—changing course and starting anew.
entries.literal: This was truly a case of hardship prompting thought of reform, of changing and renewing the system.

entries.zh: 近孝武之末，天下無事，時和年豐，百姓樂業，便自谷帛殷阜，幾乎家給人足，驗之事實，錢又不妨民也。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu's reign the realm was at peace; seasons were mild and harvests abundant; the people were content in their work, and grain and cloth themselves grew plentiful, nearly to the point of abundance in every home—facts show that coin did the people no harm.
entries.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu, all under Heaven was at peace; the seasons were harmonious and the years abundant; the people were content in their occupations, and grain and cloth themselves grew plentiful, nearly to the point where every household had enough—verified by the facts, coin also did not harm the people.

entries.zh: 頃兵革屢興，荒饉薦及，饑寒未振，實此之由。
entries.en: Recently warfare has broken out again and again, famine has followed in its wake, and hunger and cold have not been relieved—that is the real cause.
entries.literal: Recently warfare has arisen repeatedly, famine and dearth have followed one upon another, and hunger and cold have not been relieved—this is truly the cause.

entries.zh: 公既援而拯之，大革視聽，弘敦本之教，明廣農之科，敬授民時，各順其業，遊蕩知反，務末自休，固以南畝競力，野無遺壤矣。
entries.en: Your Lordship has already come to the people's aid, transforming what they see and hear, promoting the teaching of agriculture, clarifying statutes to expand farming, granting the seasons to the people so each may follow his calling; the idle will return home, those chasing profit will cease—and the fields will be tilled with vigor until no land lies fallow.
entries.literal: Your Lordship has already aided and rescued the people, greatly renewing what they see and hear, broadly promoting the teaching of the root, clarifying statutes to expand agriculture, respectfully granting the seasons to the people, each following his occupation; the wandering know to return, those devoted to the secondary cease of themselves—surely the southern fields will compete in effort and the wilds will have no abandoned soil.

entries.zh: 於是以往，升平必至，何衣食之足恤。
entries.en: From this point on, peace and prosperity are sure to follow—why worry whether there will be enough food and clothing?
entries.literal: From this going forward, rising peace is sure to come—why worry about having enough food and clothing?

entries.zh: 愚謂救弊之術，無取于廢錢。」
entries.en: In my humble view, abolishing coin is no remedy for these ills."
entries.literal: I hold that among methods to remedy harm, there is nothing to be gained from abolishing coin."

entries.zh: 子邈，有父風，官至揚州治中從事史。
entries.en: His son Miao had his father's manner and rose to attendant clerk of Yang Province.
entries.literal: His son Miao had his father's manner and rose to Attendant Clerk of Yang Province.

entries.zh: 邈子覬，別有傳。
entries.en: Miao's son Ji has a separate biography.
entries.literal: Miao's son Ji has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 覬弟道存，世祖大明中，曆黃門吏部郎，臨海王子頊前軍長史、南郡太守。
entries.en: Ji's younger brother Daocun, in the Daming era of Emperor Shizu, served as gentleman of the yellow gate in the ministry of personnel, chief clerk of the vanguard army of the prince of Linhai Zixu, and administrator of Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: Ji's younger brother Daocun, in the Daming era of Emperor Shizu, successively held the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Ministry of Personnel, Chief Clerk of the Vanguard Army of the Prince of Linhai Zixu, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 晉安王子勳建偽號，為侍中，行雍州事。
entries.en: When the prince of Jin'an Zixun established a rival regime, Daocun became palace attendant and acted for Yong Province.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an Zixun established a false reign title, Daocun became Palace Attendant and acted for Yong Province.

entries.zh: 事敗自殺。
entries.en: When the affair failed he took his own life.
entries.literal: When the affair failed he killed himself.

entries.zh: 王惠，字令明，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘從祖弟也。
entries.en: Wang Hui, styled Lingming, came from Langya Linyi and was a distant cousin of Grand Tutor Wang Hong.
entries.literal: Wang Hui, style name Lingming, a man of Langya Linyi, was a paternal cousin once removed of Grand Tutor Hong.

entries.zh: 祖劭，車騎將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Wang Shao had served as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shao was General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 父默，左光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Wang Mo was Left Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall.
entries.literal: His father Mo was Left Household Grandee of the Luminous Hall.

entries.zh: 惠幼而夷簡，為叔父司徒謐所知。
entries.en: Hui was placid and unpretentious even as a boy, and his uncle Wang Mi, Minister over the Masses, took notice of him.
entries.literal: From youth Hui was serene and unadorned; he was appreciated by his uncle, Minister over the Masses Mi.

entries.zh: 恬靜不交遊，未嘗有雜事。
entries.en: He lived quietly and kept no company, and never busied himself with extraneous matters.
entries.literal: Quiet and still, he did not associate in social rounds and never had miscellaneous affairs.

entries.zh: 陳郡謝瞻才辯有風氣，嘗與兄弟群從造惠，談論鋒起，文史間發，惠時相酬應，言清理遠，瞻等慚而退。
entries.en: Xie Zhan of Chen Commandery was eloquent and commanding; once he and his brothers and cousins called on Hui, talk flared, history and literature poured forth, and Hui answered in measured turns with discourse so lucid and penetrating that Zhan and his party withdrew abashed.
entries.literal: Xie Zhan of Chen Commandery was talented in debate and possessed bearing; once he visited Hui with his brothers and kinsmen of his clan; thrusts of discussion rose sharp, and historical and literary remarks broke out in turn; Hui responded from time to time; his words were clear and reasoning far-reaching; Zhan and the others retired in shame.

entries.zh: 高祖聞其名，以問其從兄誕，誕曰：「惠後來秀令，鄙宗之美也。」
entries.en: When Gaozu heard of him, he asked his elder cousin Wang Dan, who said, "Hui is a late-blooming talent—the finest ornament of our house."
entries.literal: Gaozu heard his name and inquired of his elder cousin of his clan Dan; Dan said, "Hui is a late-blooming splendid fellow—the glory of our humble clan."

entries.zh: 即以為行太尉參軍事，府主簿，從事中郎。
entries.en: Hui was accordingly appointed Acting Retainer to the Grand Commandant, bureau chief clerk, and Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was made Acting Retainer to the Grand Commandant, chief clerk of the bureau, and Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 世子建府，以為征虜長史，仍轉中軍長史。
entries.en: When the heir apparent opened his staff, Hui became Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, then was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Central Army.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent established his bureau, he was made Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers Barbarians and shortly thereafter transferred to Chief Clerk of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 時會稽內使劉懷敬之郡，送者傾京師，惠亦造別，還過從弟球。
entries.en: When Liu Huaijing, Interior Attendant of Kuaiji, was leaving for his post, the whole capital turned out to see him off; Hui went as well, and on his way back stopped at his cousin Wang Qiu's.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Huaijing, Interior Attendant of Kuaiji, was going to his commandery; those who saw him off filled the capital; Hui also went to bid farewell, and on returning passed by his younger cousin of his clan Qiu.

entries.zh: 球問：「向何所見？」
entries.en: Qiu asked, "What did you see on your way back?"
entries.literal: Qiu asked, "What did you just see?"

entries.zh: 惠曰：「惟覺即時逢人耳。」
entries.en: Hui replied, "Only that I kept running into people at every turn."
entries.literal: Hui said, "Only that everywhere I met people at once."

entries.zh: 常臨曲水，風雨暴至，座者皆馳散，惠徐起，姿貌不異常日。
entries.en: Once at a gathering by the Winding Water, a sudden storm struck; everyone at the table bolted, but Hui rose unhurriedly, his composure unchanged from any ordinary day.
entries.literal: Once at the Winding Water gathering, a violent storm burst upon them; those seated all scattered in flight; Hui rose slowly, his bearing no different from an ordinary day.

entries.zh: 世子為荊州，惠長史如故。
entries.en: When the heir apparent went to Jingzhou, Hui continued as chief clerk as before.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent took charge of Jingzhou, Hui remained chief clerk as before.

entries.zh: 領南郡太守，不拜。
entries.en: He was offered the concurrent post of Administrator of Nan Commandery but declined to take office.
entries.literal: He was made concurrent Administrator of Nan Commandery but did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 宋國初建，當置郎中令，高祖難其人，謂傅亮曰：「今用郎中令，不可令減袁曜卿也。」
entries.en: When the Song state was first established and a Director of Palace Retainers had to be chosen, Gaozu found no one satisfactory and told Fu Liang, "Whoever fills this post now must not rank below Yuan Yaoqing."
entries.literal: When the Song state was first established and a Director of Palace Retainers was to be appointed, Gaozu found the choice difficult; he said to Fu Liang, "For Director of Palace Retainers today, one cannot let the post fall below Yuan Yaoqing."

entries.zh: 既而曰：「吾得其人矣。」
entries.en: Then he said, "I have my man."
entries.literal: Then he said, "I have found the man."

entries.zh: 乃以惠居之。
entries.en: He then appointed Hui to the post.
entries.literal: Thereupon he installed Hui in the office.

entries.zh: 遷世子詹事，轉尚書，吳興太守。
entries.en: He was promoted to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, then became Director of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, then transferred to be Director of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 混風格高峻，少所交納，唯與族子靈運、瞻、曜、弘微並以文義賞會。
entries.en: Hun's bearing was lofty and austere; he admitted few companions, and shared literary fellowship only with his kinsmen Lingyun, Zhan, Yao, and Hongwei.
entries.literal: Hun's manner was lofty and severe; he admitted few associations, associating in literary appreciation only with his clansmen Lingyun, Zhan, Yao, and Hongwei.

entries.zh: 嘗共宴處，居在烏衣巷，故謂之烏衣之遊。
entries.en: They often feasted together in Black Robe Lane, whence their gatherings came to be called the Black Robe company.
entries.literal: They once feasted together in residence in Black Robe Lane, hence it was called the Black Robe gatherings.

entries.zh: 混五言詩所云「昔為烏衣游，戚戚皆親姪」者也。
entries.en: This is the company Hun meant in his pentasyllabic lines: "Once we roamed Black Robe Lane—close kin, every one a nephew."
entries.literal: This is what Hun's pentasyllabic poem means by "Once we roamed Black Robe Lane—all kin, all nephews close at heart."

entries.zh: 其外雖復高流時譽，莫敢造門。
entries.en: Beyond this circle, however eminent the men of the day, none dared knock at his door.
entries.literal: Beyond them, though there were lofty figures of the age in repute, none dared call at his gate.

entries.zh: 瞻等才辭辯富，弘微每以約言服之，混特所敬貴，號曰微子。
entries.en: Zhan and the others were brilliant and argumentative, yet Hongwei regularly won them over with a few well-chosen words; Hun held him in special esteem and called him Master Wei.
entries.literal: Zhan and the others were rich in talent, eloquence, and debate; Hongwei each time won them over with brief words; Hun especially honored and prized him, calling him Master Wei.

entries.zh: 謂瞻等曰：「汝諸人雖才義豐辯，未必皆愜眾心；
entries.en: He told Zhan and the others, "You may be gifted and eloquent, yet you will not all win every heart;
entries.literal: He said to Zhan and the others, "You all, though rich in talent, righteousness, and debate, may not all satisfy the hearts of the multitude;

entries.zh: 至於領會機賞，言約理要，故當與我共推微子。」
entries.en: but in grasping what matters, judging the essential, and saying little yet striking the heart of things—you should join me in holding up Master Wei."
entries.literal: as for grasping the subtle and judging the essential, speaking briefly yet hitting the core of principle—for that you should join me in elevating Master Wei."

entries.zh: 常雲：「阿遠剛躁負氣；
entries.en: He often remarked, "A-Yuan is headstrong and quick to take offense;
entries.literal: He often said, "A-Yuan is harsh, impetuous, and full of proud spirit;

entries.zh: 阿客博而無檢；
entries.en: A-Ke is learned but unrestrained;
entries.literal: A-Ke is broad in learning but without restraint;

entries.zh: 曜恃才而持操不篤；
entries.en: Yao trusts in talent but lacks constancy of character;
entries.literal: Yao relies on talent yet holds his conduct without steadfastness;

entries.zh: 晦自知而納善不周，設復功濟三才，終亦以此為恨；
entries.en: Hui is self-aware yet does not fully take in what is good; even if his achievements were to match the worthiest of men, he would still be left with this flaw;
entries.literal: Hui knows himself yet does not fully embrace what is good; even if his merit were to aid the three capacities of talent, he would still in the end regret this;

entries.zh: 至如微子，吾無間然。」
entries.en: but as for Master Wei, I can find no fault in him."
entries.literal: as for Master Wei, I find no fault in him."

entries.zh: 又云：「微子異不傷物，同不害正，若年迨六十，必至公輔。」
entries.en: He also said, "Master Wei stands apart without wounding others, and joins with others without compromising what is right; if he lives to sixty, he will surely reach the highest offices of state."
entries.literal: He also said, "Master Wei in difference does not harm others; in sameness he does not injure what is right; if he lives to sixty, he will surely reach the rank of chief minister."

entries.zh: 嘗因酣宴之餘，為韻語以獎勸靈運、瞻等曰：「康樂誕通度，實有名家韻，若加繩染功，剖瑩乃瓊瑾。
entries.en: Once, over wine after a feast, he composed rhymed verses to encourage and warn Lingyun, Zhan, and the rest: "Kangle is born with breadth of mind and truly bears a great family's tone; add the finishing discipline, and the polished core within will prove jade.
entries.literal: Once, amid the warmth of a tipsy feast, he composed rhymed lines to encourage and admonish Lingyun, Zhan, and the others, saying, "Kangle is born with comprehensive measure; he truly has the tone of a great house; if the work of binding and dyeing be added, when the lustrous core is split open it will prove jade and gems.

entries.zh: 宣明體遠識，穎達且沈儁，若能去方執，穆穆三才順。
entries.en: Xuanming has far-reaching vision, sharp yet deep; shed stubborn fixity, and the three gifts of talent will follow him in harmony.
entries.literal: Xuanming embodies far-reaching insight; keen and penetrating, yet deep and distinguished; if he can cast off obstinate fixation, the three capacities will follow him in harmony.

entries.zh: 阿多標獨解，弱冠纂華胤，質勝誡無文，其尚又能峻。
entries.en: A-Duo stands apart in understanding; in early manhood he inherited a splendid line; substance outweighs show—mind that you do not neglect refinement; his aims can still rise high.
entries.literal: A-Duo bears a mark of singular understanding; in his weak-crown years he succeeded a splendid lineage; substance prevails—take warning not to lack ornament; his aspirations can yet be lofty.

entries.zh: 通遠懷清悟，采采摽蘭訊，直轡鮮不躓，抑用解偏吝。
entries.en: Tongyuan holds to lucid insight, radiant as orchids in bloom; the straight rein seldom falters—only ease it to loosen a narrow heart.
entries.literal: Tongyuan cherishes clear discernment; flourishing, flourishing he displays orchid fragrance; the straight reins rarely stumble—only restrain them to loosen partial narrowness.

entries.zh: 微子基微尚，無勌由慕藺，勿輕一簣少，進往將千仞。
entries.en: Master Wei rests on quiet excellence; tireless, he emulates Lin Xiangru; do not despise a single basket's lack—the climb ahead will reach a thousand ren.
entries.literal: Master Wei founds himself on subtle elevation; unwearied, he follows the model of Lin; do not slight a single basket's shortfall—the advance ahead will be a thousand ren.

entries.zh: 數子勉之哉，風流由爾振，如不犯所知，此外無所慎。」
entries.en: Strive on, all of you! The age's refinement will be renewed through you; if you do not violate what you already know, there is nothing else to fear."
entries.literal: You several, strive on! The current of refinement will be revived by you; if you do not transgress what you know, beyond that there is nothing to beware."

entries.zh: 靈運等並有誡厲之言，唯弘微獨盡褒美。
entries.en: Lingyun and the others each received admonition and warning; Hongwei alone was praised without reserve.
entries.literal: Lingyun and the others all received words of warning and stern urging; only Hongwei received unmixed praise.

entries.zh: 曜，弘微兄，多，其小字也。
entries.en: Yao was Hongwei's elder brother; Duo was his childhood name.
