entries.literal: Yao was Hongwei's elder brother; Duo was his childhood name.

entries.zh: 遠即瞻字。
entries.en: Yuan was Zhan's style name.
entries.literal: Yuan was Zhan's style name.

entries.zh: 靈運小名客兒。
entries.en: Lingyun's childhood name was Ke'er, "Guest Boy."
entries.literal: Lingyun's childhood name was Guest Boy.

entries.zh: 晉世名家身有國封者，起家多拜員外散騎侍郎，弘微亦拜員外散騎，琅邪王大司馬參軍。
entries.en: In Jin times, scions of great houses who held state fiefs usually began as Supernumerary Gentlemen of the Palace Cadet; Hongwei received the same appointment and became Military Assistant to the Prince of Langya's Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: In the Jin age, eminent families whose members held state fiefs generally began their careers as Supernumerary Gentlemen of the Palace Cadet, and Hongwei too was made Supernumerary Palace Cadet and Military Assistant to the Grand Marshal of Langya.

entries.zh: 義熙八年，混以劉毅黨見誅，妻晉陵公主改適琅邪王練，公主雖執意不行，而詔其與謝氏離絕，公主以混家事委之弘微。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as a partisan of Liu Yi; his wife, Princess Jinling, was ordered to marry Wang Lian of Langya; though she refused, an edict severed her ties to the Xie clan, and she entrusted the household to Hongwei.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as a partisan of Liu Yi; his wife Princess Jinling was remarried to Wang Lian of Langya; though the princess was resolute in refusing, an edict severed her from the Xie clan, and she entrusted Hun's household affairs to Hongwei.

entries.zh: 混仍世宰輔，一門兩封，田業十餘處，僮僕千人，唯有二女，年數歲。
entries.en: The Xie family had produced chief ministers for generations; Hun's household held two enfeoffments, estates in more than ten places, and a thousand servants—yet only two daughters, both still small children.
entries.literal: Hun's family had for generations been chief ministers; one household held two enfeoffments; estates in more than ten places; a thousand servants and bondsmen; only two daughters, a few years old.

entries.zh: 弘微經紀生業，事若在公，一錢尺帛出入，皆有文簿。
entries.en: Hongwei managed the estates as though they were public office; every coin and every foot of silk that passed in or out was entered in the ledgers.
entries.literal: Hongwei managed the livelihood and enterprises as if they were public affairs; every cash or foot of silk in or out had a written record.

entries.zh: 遷通直郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Direct Attendant.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，晉陵公主降為東鄉君，以混得罪前代，東鄉君節義可嘉，聽還謝氏。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Princess Jinling was demoted to Lady of Eastern District; because Hun had been condemned under the previous regime, yet her constancy was deemed admirable, she was allowed to rejoin the Xie household.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Princess Jinling was demoted to Lady of Eastern District; because Hun had offended the previous dynasty, yet the Lady of Eastern District's integrity and righteousness were admirable, she was permitted to return to the Xie clan.

entries.zh: 自混亡，至是九載，而室宇修整，倉廩充盈，門徒業使，不異平日，田疇墾闢，有加於舊。
entries.en: Nine years had passed since Hun's death, yet the house stood in good repair, the granaries were full, servants and tenants went about their work as on any ordinary day, and the fields under cultivation exceeded what there had been before.
entries.literal: From Hun's death to this time was nine years, yet the halls and chambers were in good repair, the granaries full, retainers and laborers no different from ordinary days, and fields opened to cultivation greater than before.

entries.zh: 東鄉君歎曰：「僕射平生重此子，可謂知人。
entries.en: The Lady of Eastern District sighed and said, "The Vice Director valued this boy all his life—he truly knew how to judge men.
entries.literal: The Lady of Eastern District sighed and said, "The Vice Director all his life prized this son—he may truly be said to have known men.

entries.zh: 僕射為不亡矣。」
entries.en: The Vice Director lives on in him."
entries.literal: The Vice Director is not dead."

entries.zh: 中外姻親，道俗義舊，見東鄉之歸者，入門莫不歎息，或為之涕流，感弘微之義也。
entries.en: Relatives near and far, lay friends and clerical acquaintances alike—whoever witnessed the Lady of Eastern District's return sighed at the threshold, and some wept, moved by Hongwei's devotion.
entries.literal: Kinsmen within and without, friends lay and clerical, seeing the Lady of Eastern District's return—all who entered the gate sighed without exception, and some wept for it, moved by Hongwei's righteousness.

entries.zh: 性嚴正，舉止必循禮度，事繼親之黨，恭謹過常。
entries.en: He was stern and upright by nature, conducted himself always within ritual bounds, and in serving his adoptive kin showed a respect exceeding the ordinary.
entries.literal: His nature was stern and upright; his bearing always followed ritual measure; in serving the kin of the family he had succeeded into, his respect and care exceeded the norm.

entries.zh: 伯叔二母，歸宗兩姑，晨夕瞻奉，盡其誠敬。
entries.en: His uncles' wives, his aunts who had returned to the clan—morning and evening he attended them with complete sincerity.
entries.literal: His paternal uncles' two wives, his aunts returned to the clan—morning and evening he attended them with full sincerity and reverence.

entries.zh: 內或傳語通訊，輒正其衣冠。
entries.en: Whenever a message was relayed from the inner quarters, he would straighten his cap and robes.
entries.literal: If within the inner quarters someone passed a message or communication, he would straighten his cap and robes.

entries.zh: 婢僕之前，不妄言笑，由是尊卑小大，敬之若神。
entries.en: Before servants he never spoke or laughed lightly; high and low alike revered him as though he were divine.
entries.literal: Before maidservants and bondsmen he did not speak or laugh at random; thereby great and small, high and low, revered him as a spirit.

entries.zh: 王球，字倩玉，琅邪臨沂人，太常惠從父弟也。
entries.en: Wang Qiu, styled Qianyu, came from Langya Linyi and was a paternal cousin of Grand Master of Sacrifices Wang Hui.
entries.literal: Wang Qiu, style name Qianyu, a man of Langya Linyi, was a paternal cousin once removed of Grand Tutor Hui.

entries.zh: 父謐，司徒。
entries.en: His father Wang Mi was Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: His father Mi was Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 球少與惠齊名，美容止。
entries.en: In youth Qiu was as renowned as Hui for his handsome bearing.
entries.literal: Qiu in youth was as famed as Hui for his fine appearance and bearing.

entries.zh: 除著作佐郎，不拜。
entries.en: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing but declined to take office.
entries.literal: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing but did not accept.

entries.zh: 尋除琅邪王大司馬行參軍，轉主簿，豫章公世子中軍功曹。
entries.en: Soon after he became Acting Military Assistant to the Prince of Langya's Grand Marshal, then chief clerk, then Merit Officer on the Central Army staff of the Duke of Yuzhang's heir.
entries.literal: Shortly he was made Acting Military Assistant to the Grand Marshal of the Prince of Langya, then chief clerk, then Merit Officer of the Central Army on the Heir Apparent of the Duke of Yuzhang's staff.

entries.zh: 宋國建，初拜世子中舍人。
entries.en: When the Song state was founded he was first appointed Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When the Song state was established he was first appointed Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，仍為太子中舍人，宜都王友，轉諮議參軍，以疾去職。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he remained Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the crown prince, became Friend to the Prince of Yidu, then Advising Military Assistant, and resigned on account of illness.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate he remained Gentleman of the Palace Suite to the Heir Apparent, Friend to the Prince of Yidu, transferred to Advising Military Assistant, and left office due to illness.

entries.zh: 元嘉四年，起為義興太守。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Yuanjia he was recalled to serve as Administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia he was raised to Administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 從兄弘為揚州，服親不得相臨，加宣威將軍，在郡有寬惠之美，徙太子右衛率。
entries.en: His cousin Wang Hong was in Yangzhou; as kin in mourning they could not govern one another's territory; Qiu was given the additional title General Who Proclaims Might; in the commandery he won praise for leniency and kindness, then was transferred to Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard.
entries.literal: His elder cousin of his clan Hong was in Yangzhou; as mourning kin they could not oversee one another; he was given the additional title General Who Proclaims Might; in the commandery he had the reputation of leniency and kindness; he was transferred to Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard.

entries.zh: 入為侍中，領冠軍將軍，又領本州大中正，徙中書令，侍中如故。
entries.en: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Champion General, also served as Senior Arbiter of his home province, then became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant, headed the Champion General, also headed the Senior Arbiter of his home province, was moved to Inspector of the Masters of Writing while remaining Palace Attendant as before.

entries.zh: 遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，以蔡廓為吏部尚書，不肯拜，乃以惠代焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Shao came to the throne, Cai Kuo was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel but declined the post; Hui was then appointed in his place.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shao came to the throne, Cai Kuo was made Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel but refused to accept; Hui was then appointed in his stead.

entries.zh: 惠被召即拜，未嘗接客，人有與書求官者，得輒聚置閣上，及去職，印封如初時。
entries.en: When summoned, Hui accepted at once and never received guests. Letters from those seeking office he would pile unopened on a shelf; when he left office, the seals were still intact as at the start.
entries.literal: When summoned, Hui accepted at once; he never received guests. When anyone sent a letter seeking office, on receiving it he would pile them on the shelf; by the time he left office, the seals were still as when first applied.

entries.zh: 談者以廓之不拜，惠之即拜，雖事異而意同也。
entries.en: Commentators held that although Kuo's refusal and Hui's immediate acceptance differed outwardly, their intent was the same.
entries.literal: Commentators held that though Kuo's refusal to accept and Hui's immediate acceptance were different in outward act, their intent was the same.

entries.zh: 兄鑒，頗好聚斂，廣營田業，惠意甚不同，謂鑒曰：「何用田為？」
entries.en: His elder brother Jian was fond of amassing wealth and greatly expanded his estates; Hui thought quite differently and said to him, "What need is there for fields?"
entries.literal: His elder brother Jian was fond of amassing wealth and greatly expanded his estates; Hui's mind was quite different. He said to Jian, "What need is there for fields?"

entries.zh: 鑒怒曰：「無田何由得食！」
entries.en: Jian said angrily, "Without fields, how can one get food!"
entries.literal: Jian said angrily, "Without fields, how can one get food!"

entries.zh: 惠又曰：「亦復何用食為。」
entries.en: Hui replied, "What need is there for food either?"
entries.literal: Hui replied, "What need is there for food either?"

entries.zh: 其標寄如此。
entries.en: Such was the character he held to.
entries.literal: Such was the character he held to.

entries.zh: 元嘉三年，卒，時年四十二。
entries.en: In the third year of Yuanjia he died, at the age of forty-two.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he died, aged forty-two.

entries.zh: 追贈太常。
entries.en: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Sacrifices.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was appointed Grand Master of Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He had no sons.
entries.literal: He had no sons.

entries.zh: 列傳第十八 王惠謝弘微王球
entries.en: Biographies 18: Wang Hui, Xie Hongwei, and Wang Qiu.
entries.literal: Biographies 18: Wang Hui, Xie Hongwei, Wang Qiu.

entries.zh: 張暢，字少微，吳郡吳人，吳興太守邵兄子也。
entries.en: Zhang Chang, styled Shaowei, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery and the nephew of Shao, governor of Wuxing, on his father's side.
entries.literal: Zhang Chang, style Shaowei, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery, nephew of Wuxing Governor Shao by his elder brother.

entries.zh: 父禕，少有孝行，歷宦州府，為琅邪王國郎中令。
entries.en: His father Zhang Yi was known for filial devotion from youth and served in regional government until he was appointed chief of gentlemen in the principality of Langye.
entries.literal: His father Yi in youth had filial conduct; he passed through offices in prefectures and provinces and served as Administrator of Gentlemen in the Kingdom of Langye.

entries.zh: 從琅邪王至洛。
entries.en: He accompanied the Prince of Langye to Luoyang.
entries.literal: He followed the Prince of Langye to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 還京都，高祖封藥酒一甖付褘，使密加酖毒。
entries.en: On the return journey to the capital, Emperor Gaozu gave Yi a sealed jar of medicinal wine with orders to lace it secretly with lethal poison.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, Emperor Gaozu sealed a jar of medicinal wine and entrusted it to Yi, ordering him secretly to add poison.

entries.zh: 褘受命，既還，於道自飲而卒。
entries.en: Yi accepted the charge, and on the way home he drank the wine himself and died.
entries.literal: Yi received the command; once returned, on the road he drank it himself and died.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：夫將帥者，御眾之名；
entries.en: The historian remarks: The term "commander" denotes one who governs troops;
entries.literal: The historian says: A commander is the name for one who governs the multitude;

entries.zh: 士卒者，一夫之用。
entries.en: soldiers are the instrument of a single man.
entries.literal: soldiers are the use of a single man.

entries.zh: 坐談兵機，制勝千里，安在乎蒙楯前驅，履腸涉血而已哉！
entries.en: To sit and discuss strategy and prevail a thousand li away — what need is there merely to bear a shield in the van and tread through blood and entrails!
entries.literal: To sit and discuss military stratagem, to overcome a thousand li away — how does that depend on bearing a shield and driving ahead, treading entrails and wading through blood alone!

entries.zh: 山濤之稱羊祜曰：「大將雖不須筋力，軍中猶宜強健。」
entries.en: Shan Tao said of Yang Hu, "A great general need not rely on brute strength, yet in the army robust health is still desirable."
entries.literal: Shan Tao's praise of Yang Hu said: "A great general may not need physical strength, yet in the army one should still be robust."

entries.zh: 以此為言，則叔子之幹力弱矣。
entries.en: By that standard, Shuzi's physical vigor was slight.
entries.literal: By this saying, then Shuzi's physical strength was weak.

entries.zh: 杜預文士儒生，身不能穿札，射未嘗跨馬，一朝統大眾二十餘萬，為平吳都督。
entries.en: Du Yu was a literati and Confucian scholar who could not pierce a target with an arrow and had never mounted a horse for archery — yet one morning he took command of more than two hundred thousand men as director-general for the conquest of Wu.
entries.literal: Du Yu was a literary scholar and Confucian student — his body could not pierce a target; in archery he had never straddled a horse — yet in a morning he commanded a great host of more than two hundred thousand as Director-General for the Pacification of Wu.

entries.zh: 王戎把臂入林，亦受專征之寄。
entries.en: Wang Rong, the man who linked arms with Ruan Ji in the bamboo grove, likewise received an independent military command.
entries.literal: Wang Rong, arm in arm entering the grove, also received the entrustment of independent campaign command.

entries.zh: 何必山西猛士，六郡良家，然後可受脤於朝堂，荷推轂之重。
entries.en: Why must one be a fierce warrior of Shanxi or a son of a good family from the six commanderies before receiving investiture at court and bearing the weight of supreme command?
entries.literal: Why must there be fierce warriors of Shanxi and good families of the six commanderies before one may receive sacrificial flesh in the court hall and bear the weight of the chariot-push?

entries.zh: 及虜兵深入，徐服恇震，非張暢正言，則彭、汴危矣。
entries.en: When the barbarian armies drove deep inland and Xu Province trembled with fear, had it not been for Zhang Chang's forthright counsel, Pengcheng and Bian would have been lost.
entries.literal: When the barbarian armies penetrated deep, Xu and the coastal regions were shaken with fear — had it not been for Zhang Chang's upright words, Peng and Bian would have been in peril.

entries.zh: 豈其身捍飛鏑，手折雲衝，方足使窮揲假命，危城載安乎？
entries.en: Was it only by catching flying bolts with his body or snapping siege engines with his hands that he saved a doomed city and a desperate garrison?
entries.literal: Was it only by his body blocking flying bolts and his hands breaking cloud-chariots that he could make the desperate divination gain life and the perilous city bear peace?

entries.zh: 仁者之有勇，非為臆說。
entries.en: That the benevolent can also be brave is no idle speculation.
entries.literal: That the benevolent also have courage is no fanciful doctrine.

entries.zh: 列傳第十九 殷淳子孚弟沖淡張暢何偃江智淵
entries.en: Biography 19: Yin Chun, Yin Fu, Yin Chong, Yin Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, and Jiang Zhiyuan
entries.literal: Biography 19: Yin Chun, his son Fu, younger brothers Chong and Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, Jiang Zhiyuan

entries.zh: 義熙九年，上表曰：「臣聞咎繇亡後，臧文以為深歎；
entries.en: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen lamented deeply;
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen deeply lamented;

entries.zh: 伯氏奪邑，管仲所以稱仁。
entries.en: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised the act as humane.
entries.literal: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised its humanity.

entries.zh: 功高可百世不泯，濫賞無崇朝宜許。
entries.en: Merit so high may endure for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.
entries.literal: Merit so high may be unextinguished for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.

entries.zh: 故太傅鉅平侯祜，明德通賢，宗臣莫二，勳參佐命，功成平吳，而後嗣闕然，烝嘗莫寄。
entries.en: The late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Hu, combined bright virtue with penetrating worth and stood second to none among the eminent ministers; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was done, still his later line was cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.
entries.literal: Thus the late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Huo, was of bright virtue and penetrating worth, second to none among the imperial clans; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was accomplished, yet his later descendants were cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.

entries.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒紹。
entries.en: Because of Xiao He's founding merit, Han whenever the line ended always continued the succession.
entries.literal: Han, because of Xiao He's founding merit, whenever the line ended always continued the succession.

entries.zh: 愚謂鉅平之封，宜同酇國。
entries.en: I humbly believe the enfeoffment of Juping should be treated like the state of Zan.
entries.literal: I humbly think the enfeoffment of Juping should be the same as the state of Zan.

entries.zh: 故太尉廣陵公陳淮，黨翼孫秀，禍加淮南，竊饗大國，因罪為利。
entries.en: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; when disaster struck Huainan he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.
entries.literal: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; disaster fell on Huainan; he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.

entries.zh: 值西朝政刑失裁，中興復因而不奪。
entries.en: It happened that the Western Court lost proper measure in government and punishments, and at the restoration they again followed precedent without revoking the grant.
entries.literal: It happened that the Western Court's government and punishments lost proper measure, and at the restoration they again followed precedent and did not revoke it.

entries.zh: 今王道惟新，豈可不大判臧否？
entries.en: Now that the royal way is newly renewed, how can one fail to judge good and ill on a grand scale?
entries.literal: Now the royal way is newly renewed—how can one not greatly distinguish good from ill?

entries.zh: 謂廣陵之國，宜在削除。
entries.en: I believe the state of Guangling ought to be abolished.
entries.literal: I hold that the state of Guangling should be abolished.

entries.zh: 故太保衛瓘，本爵蕭陽縣公，既被橫禍，及進弟秩，始贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。
entries.en: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan had originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; after he suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling and then transferred to Jiangxia.
entries.literal: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; having suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, then transferred to Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 中朝公輔，多非理終，瓘功德不殊，亦無緣獨受偏賞，宜復本封，以正國章。」
entries.en: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not meet a natural end; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should keep a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to set the state's regulations right."
entries.literal: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not die natural deaths; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should receive a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to rectify the state's regulations."

entries.zh: 詔付門下。
entries.en: An edict referred the memorial to the Gate Department.
entries.literal: An edict referred it to the Gate Department.

entries.zh: 前散騎常侍江夏公衛璵上表自陳曰：「臣乃祖故太保瓘，於魏咸熙之中，太祖文皇帝為元輔之日，封蕭陽侯；
entries.en: The former supernumerary palace attendant, Duke of Jiangxia Wei Yu, submitted a memorial in his own name, saying, "My founding ancestor, the late Grand Guardian Guan, in the middle of the Wei period of Xianxi, when the founding Emperor Wen was chief minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoyang;
entries.literal: The former Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Duke of Jiangxia Wei Yun, submitted a memorial in his own person, saying: "Your servant's founding ancestor, the late Grand Guardian Guan, in the middle of the Wei period of Xianxi, when the founding Emperor Wen was chief minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoyang;

entries.zh: 大晉受禪，進爵為公。
entries.en: After the Great Jin received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.
entries.literal: when the Great Jin received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 歷位太保，揔錄朝政。
entries.en: He successively held the post of grand guardian and oversaw the recording of court affairs.
entries.literal: He successively held the post of Grand Guardian and oversaw recording of court affairs.

entries.zh: 於時賈庶人及諸王用事，忌瓘忠節，故楚王瑋矯詔致禍。
entries.en: At that time the commoner Jia and the various princes held power; jealous of Guan's loyal integrity, Prince Wei of Chu forged an edict and brought disaster upon him.
entries.literal: At that time the commoner Jia and the various princes held power; jealous of Guan's loyal integrity, Prince Yun of Chu therefore forged an edict and brought disaster upon him.

entries.zh: 前朝以瓘秉心忠正，加以伐蜀之勳，故追封蘭陵郡公。
entries.en: The former court, seeing that Guan held his heart loyal and upright and added the merit of conquering Shu, therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.
entries.literal: The former court, because Guan held his heart loyal and upright and added the merit of conquering Shu, therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.

entries.zh: 永嘉之中，東海王越食蘭陵，換封江夏，戶邑如舊。
entries.en: In the middle of the Yongjia period, Prince Yue of Donghai took Lanling as his sustenance and exchanged the enfeoffment for Jiangxia, with households and fief left unchanged.
entries.literal: In the middle of the Yongjia period, Prince Yue of Donghai consumed Lanling and exchanged the enfeoffment for Jiangxia, with households and fief unchanged.

entries.zh: 臣高祖散騎侍郎璪，囗之嫡孫，纂承封爵。
entries.en: My founding ancestor, Supernumerary Palace Attendant Sao, was the legitimate grandson of [text damaged] and inherited the enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Your servant's founding ancestor the Supernumerary Palace Attendant Sao was Guan's legitimate grandson and inherited the enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 中宗元皇帝以曾祖故右衛將軍崇承襲，逮于臣身。
entries.en: The Central Ancestor, Emperor Yuan, because of my great-grandfather the late Right Colonel of the Guard Chong, continued the succession down to my own person.
entries.literal: The Central Ancestor, Emperor Yuan, because of his founding ancestor the Right Colonel of the Guard Chong, continued the succession down to your servant's person.

entries.zh: 伏聞祠部郎荀伯子表，欲貶降復封蕭陽。
entries.en: I have heard that gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized, wishing to demote and restore the enfeoffment to Xiaoyang.
entries.literal: I have heard that Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized, wishing to demote and restore the enfeoffment to Xiaoyang.

entries.zh: 夫趙氏之忠，寵延累葉，漢祖開封，誓以山河。
entries.en: Zhao's loyalty won favor through successive generations; when the Han founder opened enfeoffments, he bound them with oaths of mountains and rivers.
entries.literal: The loyalty of the Zhao clan extended favor through successive generations; when the Han founder opened enfeoffments, he swore them with mountains and rivers.

entries.zh: 伏願陛下錄既往之勳，垂罔極之施，乞出臣表，付外參詳。」
entries.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to record past merit and extend boundless favor, and to take my memorial out and refer it outside for joint deliberation."
entries.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to record past merit and extend immeasurable favor; I beg that my memorial be taken out and referred outside for joint deliberation."

entries.zh: 潁川陳茂先亦上表曰：「祠部郎荀伯子表臣七世祖太尉准禍加淮南，不應濫賞。
entries.en: Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan also submitted a memorial, saying, "Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized that my seventh-generation ancestor the Grand Marshal Huai suffered disaster in Huainan and should not have received a reckless reward.
entries.literal: Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan also submitted a memorial, saying: "Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized that your servant's seventh-generation ancestor the Grand Marshal Huai suffered disaster in Huainan and should not have received a reckless reward.

entries.zh: 尋先臣以剪除賈謐，封海陵公，事在淮南遇禍之前。
entries.en: I find that my founding ancestor, for cutting down Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing—this occurred before Huainan met with disaster.
entries.literal: I examine that my founding ancestor, for cutting down Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing—this occurred before Huainan met with disaster.

entries.zh: 後廣陵雖在擾攘之際，臣祖乃始蒙殊遇，歷位元、凱。
entries.en: Later, though Guangling was in a time of turmoil, my grandfather only then received special favor and successively held posts among the foremost.
entries.literal: Later, though Guangling was in a time of turmoil, your servant's grandfather only then received special favor and successively held posts among the foremost.

entries.zh: 後被遠外，乃作平州，而猶不至除國。
entries.en: Afterward he was sent far abroad and made governor of Ping Province, yet the state was still not abolished.
entries.literal: Afterward he was sent far abroad and became governor of Ping Province, yet the state was still not abolished.

entries.zh: 良以先勳深重，百世不泯故也。
entries.en: This was truly because the founding merit was weighty and could not be extinguished for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: Truly because the founding merit was weighty and could not be extinguished for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 聖明御世，英輔係興，曾無疑議，以為濫賞。
entries.en: Under sage clarity governing the age, worthy assistants arose in succession, and never was there doubt that the grant had been reckless.
entries.literal: Under sage clarity governing the age, worthy assistants arose in succession; never was there doubt that it was a reckless reward.

entries.zh: 臣以微弱，未齒人倫，加始勉視息，封爵兼嗣。
entries.en: I, being slight and weak, have not yet taken my place among men; moreover I have only just barely drawn breath and inherited the enfeoffment by succession.
entries.literal: Your servant, being slight and weak, has not yet taken his place among men; moreover he has only just barely drawn breath and inherited the enfeoffment by succession.

entries.zh: 伏願陛下遠錄舊勳，特垂矜察。」
entries.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to look back upon the old merit from afar and especially bestow compassionate scrutiny."
entries.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to record the old merit from afar and especially bestow compassionate scrutiny.

entries.zh: 詔皆付門下，並不施行。
entries.en: Edicts referred all memorials to the Gate Department, and none was implemented.
entries.literal: Edicts referred all to the Gate Department, and none was implemented.

entries.zh: 列傳第二十 范泰王淮之王韶之荀伯子
entries.en: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Zhunzhi, Wang Shaozhi, and Xun Bozi
entries.literal: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Huaizhi, Wang Shaozhi, Xun Bozi

entries.zh: 羊欣，字敬元，泰山南城人也。
entries.en: Yang Xin, whose courtesy name was Jingyuan, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.
entries.literal: Yang Xin, courtesy name Jingyuan, was a native of Nancheng in Taishan.

entries.zh: 曾祖忱，晉徐州刺史。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Chen had served as Inspector of Xu Province under the Jin.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Chen was Jin Inspector of Xu Province.

entries.zh: 祖權，黃門郎。
entries.en: His grandfather Quan had been a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: His grandfather Quan was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 父不疑，桂陽太守。
entries.en: His father Buyi had been Governor of Guiyang.
entries.literal: His father Buyi was Governor of Guiyang.

entries.zh: 欣少靖默，無競於人，美言笑，善容止。
entries.en: Xin had been quiet and unassuming since boyhood, never striving against others, with a pleasant wit and graceful bearing.
entries.literal: From youth Xin was quiet and restrained, not competing with others; he had a fine manner of speech and laughter and was skilled in deportment.

entries.zh: 汎覽經籍，尤長隸書。
entries.en: He read widely in the classics and was especially masterful in clerical script calligraphy.
entries.literal: He broadly read the classics and histories and was especially accomplished in clerical script.

entries.zh: 不疑初為烏程令，欣時年十二，時王獻之為吳興太守，甚知愛之。
entries.en: When Buyi first served as magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve; Wang Xianzhi was then Governor of Wuxing and took a great liking to him.
entries.literal: When Buyi was first magistrate of Wucheng, Xin was twelve; at the time Wang Xianzhi was Governor of Wuxing and greatly favored and cherished him.

entries.zh: 獻之嘗夏月入縣，欣著新絹裙晝寢，獻之書裙數幅而去。
entries.en: Once in midsummer Xianzhi came into the county seat; Xin was napping by day in a new silk gauze skirt, and Xianzhi wrote calligraphy across several panels of the skirt before departing.
entries.literal: Xianzhi once entered the county in midsummer; Xin was wearing a new silk gauze skirt and napping by day; Xianzhi wrote several sections on the skirt and left.

entries.zh: 欣本工書，因此彌善。
entries.en: Xin had already been adept at calligraphy, and this episode made him still better.
entries.literal: Xin was already skilled at writing; through this he became even more accomplished.

entries.zh: 起家輔國參軍，府解還家。
entries.en: He entered office as aide to the General Who Assists the State; when that post was abolished he went home.
entries.literal: He began his career as aide to the General Who Assists the State; when the office was dissolved he returned home.

entries.zh: 隆安中，朝廷漸亂，欣優遊私門，不復進仕。
entries.en: During the Long'an years, as the court slipped into disorder, Xin lived at ease in private life and sought no further advancement.
entries.literal: In the Long'an era the court grew increasingly turbulent; Xin enjoyed himself leisurely at home and did not advance in office again.

entries.zh: 會稽王世子元顯每使欣書，常辭不奉命，元顯怒，乃以為其後軍府舍人。
entries.en: Yuan Xian, heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, often pressed Xin to do calligraphy for him; Xin routinely refused, and in anger Yuan Xian made him registrar of his Rear Army staff.
entries.literal: Yuan Xian, heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, often had Xin write for him; Xin regularly declined and did not obey; Yuan Xian was angry and therefore appointed him registrar in his Rear Army headquarters.

entries.zh: 此職本用寒人，欣意貌恬然，不以高卑見色，論者稱焉。
entries.en: The post was normally given to men of humble origin, yet Xin remained serene in manner and never altered his demeanor with rank; men of judgment praised him for it.
entries.literal: This post was originally filled by men of low birth; Xin's bearing and expression were calm, and he showed no change of color according to rank high or low; commentators praised this.

entries.zh: 欣嘗詣領軍將軍謝混，混拂席改服，然後見之。
entries.en: Once when Xin called on General of the Guards Xie Hun, Hun first brushed the seat and changed his garments before receiving him.
entries.literal: Xin once visited General of the Guards Xie Hun; Hun brushed the mat and changed his dress before then receiving him.

entries.zh: 時混族子靈運在坐，退告族兄瞻曰：「望蔡見羊欣，遂易衣改席。」
entries.en: Xie Lingyun, a kinsman of Hun's, was present; afterward he told his elder kinsman Zhan, "When Wangcai received Yang Xin, he changed his clothes and brushed the mat."
entries.literal: At the time Hun's clansman Lingyun was seated there; he withdrew and told his clansman elder brother Zhan: "When Wangcai saw Yang Xin, he at once changed clothes and the mat."

entries.zh: 欣由此益知名。
entries.en: From that moment Xin's fame grew still greater.
entries.literal: Through this Xin became still more renowned.

entries.zh: 義熙中，弟徽被遇於高祖，高祖謂諮議參軍鄭鮮之曰：「羊徽一時美器，世論猶在兄後，恨不識之。」
entries.en: During the Yixi years Xin's younger brother Hui won favor with Gaozu, who said to Staff Aide Zheng Xianzhi, "Yang Hui is a rare talent of our time; opinion still ranks him below his brother—I regret never having met the elder."
entries.literal: In the Yixi era younger brother Hui received favor from Gaozu; Gaozu said to Consultation and Planning Staff Aide Zheng Xianzhi: "Yang Hui is for the age a fine vessel; public opinion still places him after his elder brother—I regret not knowing him."

entries.zh: 即板欣補右將軍劉藩司馬，轉長史，中軍將軍道憐諮議參軍。
entries.en: He at once commissioned Xin as Major on the staff of General of the Right Liu Fan, then chief clerk, and finally Consultation Staff Aide to General of the Central Army Daolian.
entries.literal: He thereupon issued a fiat appointing Xin to fill the post of Major under General of the Right Liu Fan, then transferred him to chief clerk and Staff Aide for Consultation and Planning under General of the Central Army Daolian.

entries.zh: 出為新安太守。
entries.en: He was sent out as Governor of Xin'an.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 在郡四年，簡惠著稱。
entries.en: He governed the prefecture four years and won renown for simple, humane rule.
entries.literal: In the commandery for four years, he was famed for simplicity and kind grace.

entries.zh: 除臨川王義慶輔國長史，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，並不就。
entries.en: Appointments followed as Chief Clerk on the staff of Prince of Linchuan Yiqing's Kingdom-Assisting command and as Consultation Aide on Prince of Luling Yizhen's Chariots and Cavalry staff, but he took neither post.
entries.literal: He was removed from office to become Chief Clerk for the Kingdom-Assisting Army under Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, and Consultation Staff Aide to the Chariots and Cavalry under Prince of Luling Yizhen—he accepted neither.

entries.zh: 太祖重之，以為新安太守，前後凡十三年，遊玩山水，甚得適性。
entries.en: Taizu esteemed him and again made him Governor of Xin'an; over thirteen years in all he wandered among hills and streams to his heart's content.
entries.literal: Taizu valued him and appointed him Governor of Xin'an; altogether before and after thirteen years, he toured mountains and waters and greatly suited his nature.

entries.zh: 轉在義興，非其好也。
entries.en: When he was transferred to Yixing, it was not what he wanted.
entries.literal: He was transferred to serve in Yixing—it was not to his liking.

entries.zh: 頃之，又稱病篤自免歸。
entries.en: Before long he again pleaded grave illness and resigned to go home.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he again claimed serious illness and resigned to return home.

entries.zh: 除中散大夫。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand Master of Leisurely Disposition.
entries.literal: He was removed from office and made Grand Master of Leisurely Disposition.

entries.zh: 張敷，字景胤，吳郡人，吳興太守邵子也。
entries.en: Zhang Fu, courtesy name Jingyin, was from Wu commandery and the son of Shao, Governor of Wuxing.
entries.literal: Zhang Fu, courtesy name Jingyin, a man of Wu commandery, was the son of Governor of Wuxing Shao.

entries.zh: 生而母沒。
entries.en: His mother died when he was born.
entries.literal: At birth his mother was gone.

entries.zh: 年數歲，問母所在，家人告以死生之分，敷雖童蒙，便有思慕之色。
entries.en: When he was only a few years old he asked where his mother was; the family explained that she had died; even as a small child Fu's face showed mourning and longing.
entries.literal: At several years of age he asked where his mother was; the household told him of the division between life and death; though still a child, Fu already showed the color of longing and grief.

entries.zh: 年十許歲，求母遺物，而散施已盡，唯得一畫扇，乃緘錄之，每至感思，輒開笥流涕。
entries.en: Around ten he searched for keepsakes of his mother, but nearly everything had been given away; only one painted fan remained, which he wrapped and stored; whenever grief overtook him he opened the case and wept.
entries.literal: At about ten he sought his mother's surviving objects, but what had been distributed was already exhausted; he obtained only one painted fan, which he sealed and kept; whenever moved to remembrance he would open the chest and weep.

entries.zh: 見從母，常悲感哽咽。
entries.en: Seeing his aunt by marriage always left him choked with sorrow.
entries.literal: When he saw his maternal aunt he was often moved to grief and choked with sobs.

entries.zh: 性整貴，風韻甚高，好讀玄書，兼屬文論，少有盛名。
entries.en: Upright and fastidious by nature, with a lofty air, he loved metaphysical texts and wrote literary essays as well; his reputation was great even while young.
entries.literal: By nature he was upright and noble; his bearing was very lofty; he loved reading arcane books and also composed literary disquisitions; from youth he had great fame.

entries.zh: 高祖見而愛之，以為世子中軍參軍，數見接引。
entries.en: Gaozu took him in at once and made him aide on the Heir Apparent's Central Army staff, summoning him often.
entries.literal: Gaozu saw him and cherished him, making him aide to the Heir Apparent's Central Army, and many times received and guided him.

entries.zh: 永初初，遷秘書郎。
entries.en: Early in the Yongchu reign he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu he was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 嘗在省直，中書令傅亮貴宿權要，聞其好學，過候之；
entries.en: Once while on duty in the Secretariat, Chief Palace Attendant Fu Liang, a senior wielder of power, heard of his devotion to study and paid a visit;
entries.literal: Once while on duty in the office, Palace Attendant Fu Liang, an elder of rank and power, heard of his love of learning and came calling;

entries.zh: 敷臥不即起，亮怪而去。
entries.en: Fu remained lying down and did not rise promptly; Liang took offense and withdrew.
entries.literal: Fu was lying down and did not rise at once; Liang thought it strange and left.

entries.zh: 弟徽，字敬猷，世譽多欣。
entries.en: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou; worldly praise mostly favored Xin.
entries.literal: Younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou; worldly praise mostly favored Xin.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮京口，以為記室參軍掌事。
entries.en: When Gaozu was stationed at Jingkou, he made Hui Record-House Staff Aide in charge of affairs.
entries.literal: When Gaozu held Jingkou, he made him Record-House Staff Aide in charge of affairs.

entries.zh: 八年，遷中書郎，直西省。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was promoted to Palace Gentleman on duty in the Western Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Palace Gentleman and attended the Western Office.

entries.zh: 後為太祖西中郎長史、河東太守。
entries.en: He later became Chief Clerk on Taizu's Western Center Army staff and Governor of Hedong.
entries.literal: Later he served as Chief Clerk of Taizu's Western Center Army and Governor of Hedong.

entries.zh: 子瞻，元嘉末為世祖南中郎長史、尋陽太守，卒官。
entries.en: His son Zhan, late in Yuanjia, was Chief Clerk on Shizu's Southern Center Army staff and Governor of Xunyang, and died in office.
entries.literal: His son Zhan, at the end of Yuanjia served as Chief Clerk of Shizu's Southern Center Army and Governor of Xunyang, and died in office.

entries.zh: 素好黃老，常手自書章，有病不服藥，飲符水而已。
entries.en: He had long favored Daoist teachings, copied ritual texts himself, and when ill refused medicine, drinking only consecrated talisman water.
entries.literal: He had long favored Huang-Lao teaching, often personally copying talismanic texts; when ill he did not take medicine but drank only talisman water.

entries.zh: 兼善醫術，撰《藥方》十卷。
entries.en: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled a ten-juan work titled Pharmaceutical Formulations.
entries.literal: He was also skilled in medicine and compiled ten juan of Pharmaceutical Formulations.

entries.zh: 欣以不堪拜伏，辭不朝覲，高祖、太祖並恨不識之。
entries.en: Unable to endure prostration, Xin declined court audiences; both Gaozu and Taizu regretted never having met him in person.
entries.literal: Because Xin could not bear to bow prostrate, he declined court audiences; both Gaozu and Taizu regretted never having met him.

entries.zh: 自非尋省近親，不妄行詣，行必由城外，未嘗入六關。
entries.en: Except for brief visits to near kin, he would not pay calls indiscriminately; when he traveled he always kept outside the city walls and never passed through the six inner gates.
entries.literal: Unless visiting close kin on brief family business, he did not go about paying calls rashly; when traveling he always went by way outside the city and never entered the six passes.

entries.zh: 元嘉十九年，卒，時年七十三。
entries.en: He died in the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, at the age of seventy-three.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia he died, aged seventy-three.

entries.zh: 子俊，早卒。
entries.en: His son Jun died young.
entries.literal: His son Jun died young.

entries.zh: 琅邪顏延之書弔茂度曰：「賢弟子少履貞規，長懷理要，清風素氣，得之天然。
entries.en: Yan Yanzhi of Langye wrote Maodu a letter of condolence: "Your worthy nephew practiced integrity from youth and held to essential truth in maturity; clarity of spirit was his by nature.
entries.literal: Yan Yanzhi of Langye wrote to condole with Maodu: "Your worthy nephew from youth trod the path of pure rule, in maturity cherished essential principle, clear wind and plain spirit—he gained these from Heaven's endowment.

entries.zh: 言面以來，便申忘年之好，比雖艱隔成阻，而情問無睽。
entries.en: From our first meeting we formed a friendship without regard to age; though distance has lately intervened, our bond has not cooled.
entries.literal: Since we spoke face to face he extended the friendship that forgets years; though recently hardship and separation have formed barriers, our emotional exchange has known no breach.

entries.zh: 薄莫之人，冀其方見慰說，豈謂中年，奄為長往，聞問悼心，有兼恆痛。
entries.en: I am a man in life's twilight and hoped soon to enjoy his company again—who dreamed that in his prime he would be gone so suddenly? The news fills me with grief beyond ordinary sorrow.
entries.literal: A man in the dusk of life, I hoped soon to see comfort and discourse—who would have thought that in midlife he would suddenly make the long journey? Hearing the news my grieving heart shares in constant pain.

entries.zh: 足下門教敦至，兼實家寶，一旦喪失，何可為懷。」
entries.en: Your family discipline is exemplary, and he was its jewel; to lose him in a day—how can the heart bear it?"
entries.literal: Your household instruction is thick and perfect, and he was moreover a true treasure of the family; in one morning lost—how can it be borne in the breast?"

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which men held him.
entries.literal: Thus was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「司徒故左長史張敷，貞心簡立，幼樹風規。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, an edict read: "The late Zhang Fu, former Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, bore a loyal heart and plain integrity and established his moral bearing from youth.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne an edict said: "Former Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works Zhang Fu—loyal heart, plain establishment; from youth he planted wind and rule.

entries.zh: 居哀毀滅，孝道淳至，宜在追甄，於以報美。
entries.en: In mourning he destroyed himself—filial devotion of the purest kind; let posthumous honors recall his excellence.
entries.literal: In mourning he destroyed himself—filial devotion pure and utmost; he should receive posthumous advancement, thereby to repay his excellence.

entries.zh: 可追贈侍中。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant."

entries.zh: 於是改其所居稱為孝張里。
entries.en: His former neighborhood was thereafter renamed Filial Zhang Lane.
entries.literal: Thereupon his former residence was renamed Filial Zhang Lane.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He left no sons.
entries.literal: He had no sons.

entries.zh: 常謂生遭太公，將即華士之戮；
entries.en: I have often said that had I lived in the age of the Grand Duke of Qi, I would soon have shared Hua Shi's fate;
entries.literal: I have often said that if born in the age of the Grand Duke, I would soon meet the execution of the Flower Gentleman;

entries.zh: 幸遇管叔，必蒙僻儒之養。
entries.en: had I met Uncle Guan instead, I would surely have been kept alive as an eccentric scholar.
entries.literal: fortunate to meet Uncle Guan, I would surely receive the fostering of an eccentric scholar.

entries.zh: 光武以馮衍才浮其實，故棄而不齒。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu found Feng Yan's talent greater than his substance and cast him aside without a place at court.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu, because Feng Yan's talent floated above his substance, cast him aside and did not rank him among his teeth.

entries.zh: 諸葛孔明云：「來敏亂郡，過於孔文舉。」
entries.en: Zhuge Liang said, "Lai Min throws a commandery into disorder—worse than Kong Rong."
entries.literal: Zhuge Kongming said: "Lai Min throws a commandery into disorder, exceeding Kong Wenju."

entries.zh: 況無古人之才槩，敢干周、漢之常刑。
entries.en: How much less do I possess the capacity of the ancients, yet dare to invite the ordinary penalties of Zhou and Han!
entries.literal: How much more when one lacks the capacity of the ancients yet dares to offend against the regular punishments of Zhou and Han!

entries.zh: 彼二三英賢，足為曉治與否？
entries.en: Do those two or three worthy men suffice to show whether one understands good government?
entries.literal: Are those two or three worthy men enough to show understanding of governance or not?

entries.zh: 恐君逄此時，或亦不免高閣，乃復假名不知己者，豈欲自比衛賜邪？
entries.en: I fear that in such a time you too may not escape disgrace in high office, yet you borrow the name of one who does not know you—do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?
entries.literal: I fear that when you meet such a time you likewise may not escape the high pavilion; yet you borrow a name from one who does not know you—do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?

entries.zh: 君欲高斅山公，而以仲容見處，徒以搥提禮學，本不參選，鄙夫瞻彼，固不任下走，未知新沓何如州陵耳。
entries.en: You wish to take Mount Gong as your model yet treat me like Ruan Zhongrong; raised on ritual learning, I was never on the selection rolls—a coarse man like me cannot serve as your runner, and I do not know how the new appointee compares with you, Zhouling.
entries.literal: You wish to imitate high Mount Gong, yet treat me as Zhongrong; merely because I was raised on ritual learning I was never in the selection lists—this coarse fellow looking on that naturally cannot serve as a runner; I do not know what the new entrant is like compared with Zhouling.

entries.zh: 而作不師古，坐亂官政，誣飾蚯蚓，冀招神龍，如復託以真素者，又不宜居華留名，有害風俗。
entries.en: Yet acting without antiquity as your guide you disturb official government, dressing up an earthworm and hoping to summon a dragon; if one truly relies on plain authenticity, one should not dwell in glory and leave a name—harmful to custom.
entries.literal: Yet acting without taking antiquity as teacher you disturb official government, bedecking an earthworm and hoping to summon a divine dragon; if one again relies on plain authenticity, one should not dwell in glory and leave a name—harmful to custom.

entries.zh: 君亦不至期人如此，若交以為人賜，舉未以己勞，則商販之事，又連所不忍聞也。
entries.en: You should not expect such a man either; if friendship is treated as a gift from others and promotion comes without one's own effort—that is merchant's business, and something I cannot bear to hear.
entries.literal: You also should not expect a man so; if association is taken as a gift from others, and promotion without one's own labor—then the affairs of merchants, again something one cannot bear to hear.

entries.zh: 豈謂不肖易擢，貪者可誘，凡此數者，君必居一焉。
entries.en: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be bought—of all these you must be guilty of at least one.
entries.literal: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be enticed—of all these several you must occupy one.

entries.zh: 雖假天口於齊駢，藉鬼說於周季，公孫碎毛髮之文，莊生縱漭瀁之極，終不能舉其契，為之辭矣。
entries.en: Though one had the eloquence of the Qi persuaders, the ghost lore of late Zhou, Gongsun Long's hair-splitting disputations, or Zhuangzi's boundless paradoxes, one still could not justify this appointment.
entries.literal: Though one borrow Heaven's mouth from the Qi persuader, borrow ghostly discourse from the Zhou season, Gongsun split the essay of hair and down, Zhuangzi let the vast flood to its extreme—still one cannot raise their bond and make excuse for it.

entries.zh: 子將明魂，必靈咍於萬里，汝、潁餘彥，將拂衣而不朝。
entries.en: Zizhan's bright spirit must laugh in the dark from afar; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will brush their robes and refuse court.
entries.literal: Zizhan's bright soul must laugh darkly at ten thousand li; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will brush their coats and not attend court.

entries.zh: 浮華一開，風俗或從此而爽。
entries.en: Once ostentation is unleashed, custom may slip away from this.
entries.literal: Once ostentation opens, custom may from this slip away.

entries.zh: 鬼谷以揣情為最難，何君忖度之輕謬。
entries.en: Guiguzi held gauging a man's heart the hardest art—how lightly and absurdly you judge!
entries.literal: Guiguzi held gauging sentiment the hardest—how lightly and absurdly you estimate!

entries.zh: 又前年優旨，自弟所宣，雖夏后撫辜人，周宣及鰥寡，不足過也。
entries.en: Moreover the favorable edict of two years ago was proclaimed by you; though Yu comforted the guilty and King Xuan of Zhou reached widows and orphans, they could not surpass it.
entries.literal: Moreover the favorable edict of the year before last was proclaimed by you, younger brother; though Xia Hou comforted the guilty man and Zhou Xuan reached widowers and widows, it is not enough to surpass this.

entries.zh: 語皆循檢校跡，不為虛飾也。
entries.en: The words all follow verified facts and are not empty adornment.
entries.literal: The words all follow inspected traces and are not empty adornment.

entries.zh: 作人不阿諛，無緣頭髮見白，稍學諂詐。
entries.en: By nature I do not flatter; without cause for my hair to turn white, I would slightly learn flattery and deceit.
entries.literal: Making a man I do not flatter and fawn; without cause for hair to show white, slightly learning flattery and deceit.

entries.zh: 且吾何以為，足不能行，自不得出戶；
entries.en: Moreover what can I do—my feet cannot walk, so I naturally cannot leave the house;
entries.literal: Moreover what can I do—feet cannot walk, naturally cannot go out the door;

entries.zh: 頭不耐風，故不可扶曳。
entries.en: my head cannot bear wind, so I cannot be supported and led along.
entries.literal: the head cannot bear wind, therefore cannot be supported and dragged.

entries.zh: 家本貧餧，至於惡衣蔬食，設使盜蹠居此，亦不能兩展其足，妄意珍藏也。
entries.en: Our family was originally poor, to the point of coarse clothes and plain food; even Robber Zhi dwelling here could not stretch both feet twice, vainly dreaming of hoarded treasure.
entries.literal: The family was originally poor and hungry, to the point of detestable clothes and vegetable food; suppose Robber Zhi dwelt here, he also could not stretch both feet twice, vainly intending treasured store.

entries.zh: 正令選官設作此舉，於吾亦無劍戟之傷，所以懃懃畏人之多言也。
entries.en: Even if the selection official made this appointment, it would not wound me like sword or halberd; what I earnestly fear is people's gossip.
entries.literal: Even if the selection official set up this action, for me there is also no wound of sword and halberd; therefore I earnestly fear people's much talk.

entries.zh: 管子晉賢，乃關人主之輕重，此何容易哉。
entries.en: Guanzi was a worthy man of Jin, yet concerned the ruler's weight in the balance—how is this easy!
entries.literal: Guanzi was Jin's worthy man, yet concerned the ruler's light and heavy—how is this easy!

entries.zh: 州陵亦自言視明聽聰，而返區區飾吾，何辯致而下英俊。
entries.en: Zhouling also claims clear sight and keen hearing, yet turns to petty flattery of me—what eloquence can bring down outstanding men?
entries.literal: Zhouling also himself says he sees clearly and hears keenly, yet returns to petty adorning me—what eloquence to bring down outstanding men.

entries.zh: 夫奇士必龍居深藏，與蛙蝦為伍，放勳其猶難之，林宗輩不足識也。
entries.en: Extraordinary men must dwell hidden like dragons, keeping company with frogs and shrimp; even Emperor Yao found it hard; men like Guo Linzong are not enough to recognize them.
entries.literal: Extraordinary men must like dragons dwell in deep hiding, keeping company with frogs and shrimp; even Fangxun still found it hard; Lin Zong's sort are not enough to recognize them.

entries.zh: 似不肯睠睠奉牋記，雕琢獻文章，居家近市廛，親戚滿城府，吾猶自知袁陽源輩當平此不？
entries.en: Seemingly unwilling to present polished memorials and carved compositions, dwelling near the market with kin filling the city offices—I still know whether men like Yuan Yangyuan would approve of this, do I not?
entries.literal: Seemingly unwilling attentively to present memorials, carving and polishing to offer literary compositions, dwelling near market stalls, kin filling city offices—I still know myself whether Yuan Yangyuan's sort ought to level this or not?

entries.zh: 飾詐之與直獨，兩不關吾心，又何所耿介。
entries.en: Adorning deceit and plain solitude—neither concerns my heart; what is there to be indignant about?
entries.literal: Adorning deceit and plain solitude—neither concerns my heart; what is there to be upright and aloof about?

entries.zh: 弟自宜以解塞群賢矣，兼悉怒此言自爾家任兄故能也。
entries.en: Younger brother, you yourself ought to use this to answer the worthy men; moreover I fully know that anger at these words comes from your Elder Brother Ren's influence.
entries.literal: Younger brother, you yourself ought to use this to answer and block the crowd of worthies; moreover I fully know anger at these words comes from your family's Elder Brother Ren's ability.

entries.zh: 元嘉三十年，卒，時年三十九。
entries.en: He died in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, at the age of thirty-nine.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia he died, aged thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 僧謙卒後四旬而微終。
entries.en: Wei died forty days after Sengqian.
entries.literal: Forty days after Sengqian's death Wei ended.

entries.zh: 遺令薄葬，不設轜旐鼓挽之屬，施五尺床，為靈二宿便毀。
entries.en: His final instructions were for a simple burial, without funeral carts, banners, drums, or processions; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights before the spirit, destroy it.
entries.literal: His final command was simple burial, not setting out funeral carts, banners, drums, or pulling teams; provide a five-foot couch; after two nights at the spirit, destroy it.

entries.zh: 以嘗所彈琴置床上，何長史來，以琴與之。
entries.en: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.
entries.literal: Place the zither he once played on the couch; when Chief Clerk He comes, give him the zither.

entries.zh: 何長史者，偃也。
entries.en: Chief Clerk He was He Yan.
entries.literal: Chief Clerk He was Yan.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He left no sons.
entries.literal: He had no sons.

entries.zh: 家人遵之。
entries.en: The family followed his instructions.
entries.literal: The family followed this.

entries.zh: 所著文集傳於世。
entries.en: His collected writings circulated in the world.
entries.literal: The collected writings he authored were transmitted in the world.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，詔曰：「微棲志貞深，文行惇洽，生自華宗，身安隱素，足以賁茲丘園，惇是薄俗。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, an edict read: "Wei dwelt with pure and deep intent, his literary conduct sincere and harmonious; born of a great clan, he lived at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and enrich this shallow age.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne an edict said: "Wei dwelt with intent pure and deep, literary conduct sincere and harmonious, born from a splendid clan, personally at ease in plain simplicity—enough to adorn these hills and gardens and thicken this thin custom.

entries.zh: 不幸蚤世，朕甚悼之。
entries.en: He died untimely, and I deeply mourn him.
entries.literal: Unfortunate early death—I deeply mourn him.

entries.zh: 可追贈秘書監。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Director of the Secretariat."

entries.zh: 列傳第二十二 羊欣張敷王微
entries.en: Biography 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei
entries.literal: Biography 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei

entries.zh: 少有志行，以父存亡不測，布衣蔬食不交遊，如此十餘年，為時人所稱美。
entries.en: From youth he showed purpose and integrity. With his father's fate still unknown, he dressed plainly, ate sparingly, and kept to himself for more than ten years, and people of the day praised him for it.
entries.literal: In youth he had aspiration and conduct. Because his father's fate was unknown, he wore plain clothes, ate simple food, and made no social visits—for more than ten years—and was praised by people of the time.

entries.zh: 高祖欲收其才用，乃發廞喪問，使華制服。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu wanted to make use of his abilities, so he announced Yin's death and had Hua put on mourning dress.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu wished to employ his talent and so had Yin's funeral proclaimed and had Hua enter mourning garb.

entries.zh: 服闋，高祖北伐長安，領鎮西將軍、北徐州刺史，辟華為州主簿，仍轉鎮西主簿，治中從事史，歷職著稱。
entries.en: When his mourning was over, Gaozu marched north against Chang'an as General Who Guards the West and governor of Northern Xuzhou. He took Hua on as chief clerk of the province, then as chief clerk of his western headquarters, then as attendant administrative officer, and in every post Hua distinguished himself.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, Gaozu on his northern campaign to Chang'an held the post of General Who Guards the West and Governor of Northern Xuzhou; he appointed Hua as Chief Clerk of the province, then transferred him to Chief Clerk of the General Who Guards the West, Attendant Administrative Officer of the Province, and in each office he was outstanding.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮江陵，以為西中郎主簿，遷諮議參軍，領錄事。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Wen was posted at Jiangling, he made Hua chief clerk of the western headquarters, then promoted him to advising colonel and put him in charge of recording affairs.
entries.literal: When the Taizu was stationed at Jiangling, he made him Chief Clerk of the General of the West, promoted him to Advising Colonel, and put him in charge of recording affairs.

entries.zh: 太祖進號鎮西，復隨府轉。
entries.en: When the prince took the title General Who Guards the West, Hua moved with the headquarters once again.
entries.literal: When the Taizu advanced to the title General Who Guards the West, Hua again transferred with the headquarters.

entries.zh: 太祖未親政，政事悉委司馬張邵。
entries.en: Before the prince took government into his own hands, he left all affairs to his adjutant Zhang Shao.
entries.literal: Before the Taizu personally administered government affairs, all administration was entrusted to Adjutant Zhang Shao.

entries.zh: 華性尚物，不欲人在己前；
entries.en: Hua was vain about appearances and could not bear anyone to outshine him.
entries.literal: Hua by nature prized status symbols and did not wish anyone to rank above him.

entries.zh: 邵性豪，每行來常引夾轂，華出入乘牽車，從者不過二三以矯之。
entries.en: Shao loved display and whenever he went abroad had paired carriages escort him. Hua, by contrast, went out in a hand-drawn cart with no more than two or three followers, deliberately playing the opposite part.
entries.literal: Shao was by nature ostentatious; whenever he went out he constantly had paired carriages flank his train. Hua when going out rode in a hand-drawn cart, with no more than two or three attendants, to make a contrast.

entries.zh: 嘗於城內相逢，華陽不知是邵，謂左右：「此鹵簿甚盛，必是殿下出行。」
entries.en: Once they met in the city. Hua pretended not to know it was Shao and told his attendants, "That procession is enormous—it must be the prince himself going out."
entries.literal: Once they met within the city. Hua pretended not to know it was Shao and said to his attendants, "That guard procession is very grand—it must be the Prince going out."

entries.zh: 乃下牽車，立於道側，及邵至乃驚。
entries.en: He stepped down from his cart and stood aside on the road; when Shao drew near, Hua was mortified.
entries.literal: So he left his hand-cart and stood by the roadside; when Shao arrived, he was startled.

entries.zh: 邵白服登城，為華所糾，坐被徵，華代為司馬、南郡太守，行府州事。
entries.en: Shao had gone up on the wall dressed in white mourning, and Hua denounced him for it; Shao was recalled and removed from office, and Hua took his place as chief clerk and governor of Nan Commandery, acting head of both headquarters and province.
entries.literal: Shao wearing white mourning dress mounted the city wall and was impeached by Hua; as a result he was summoned and dismissed, and Hua succeeded him as Chief Clerk, Governor of Nan Commandery, and acting chief of the headquarters and province.

entries.zh: 太祖入奉大統，以少帝見害，疑不敢下。
entries.en: When the Taizu entered to receive the grand succession, he hesitated to come down because the young emperor had been murdered.
entries.literal: The Taizu entered to receive the great succession. Because the young emperor had been killed, he was doubtful and dared not descend.

entries.zh: 華建議曰：「羨之等受寄崇重，未容便敢背德，廢主若存，慮其將來受禍，致此殺害。
entries.en: Hua advised: "Xu Xianzhi and the others had received a weighty charge and high honor; they could hardly have dared to rebel openly. If the deposed ruler had lived, they feared he would suffer harm later—that is why he was killed.
entries.literal: Hua advised, saying, "Xu Xianzhi and the others received a weighty charge and high honor; they could not lightly dare to turn against virtue. If the deposed ruler had lived, they feared he would suffer harm in the future—this led to the killing.

entries.zh: 蓋由每生情多，寧敢一朝頓懷逆志。
entries.en: Feelings arise at every turn; they could hardly have suddenly harbored rebellious intent overnight.
entries.literal: It was because feelings arise at every turn; how could they in one morning suddenly harbor rebellious intent?

entries.zh: 且三人勢均，莫相推伏，不過欲握權自固，以少主仰待耳。
entries.en: Moreover, the three were evenly matched and none would yield; they only wished to hold power and secure themselves, counting on the young ruler's dependence on them.
entries.literal: Moreover, the three men were equal in power and none would yield to another; they only wished to grasp authority to secure themselves, relying on the young ruler's dependence on them.

entries.zh: 今日就徵，萬無所慮。」
entries.en: If you answer the summons today, there is absolutely nothing to fear."
entries.literal: If you go to the summons today, there is absolutely nothing to fear."

entries.zh: 太祖從之，留華總後任。
entries.en: The Taizu followed his advice and left Hua in overall charge of the rear.
entries.literal: The Taizu followed his advice and left Hua in overall charge of the rear duties.

entries.zh: 上即位，以華為侍中，領驍騎將軍，未拜，轉右衞將軍，侍中如故。
entries.en: When the emperor took the throne, he made Hua palace attendant and concurrently general of agile cavalry; before the appointment was taken up, he was transferred to general of the right guards while keeping his post as palace attendant.
entries.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, he made Hua Palace Attendant and concurrently General of Agile Cavalry; before the appointment was taken up, he was transferred to General of the Right Guards, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 先是，會稽孔甯子為太祖鎮西諮議參軍，以文義見賞，至是為黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉。
entries.en: Earlier, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had served the prince as advising colonel when he was General Who Guards the West and had won praise for his literary learning. By now he was a gentleman at the Yellow Gate and commandant of foot soldiers.
entries.literal: Earlier, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had been Advising Colonel of the General Who Guards the West under the Taizu and was admired for literary excellence; by this time he was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

entries.zh: 甯子先為高祖太尉主簿，陳損益曰：「隆化之道，莫先於官得其才；
entries.en: Ningzi had once been chief clerk to Gaozu when he was grand marshal, and he submitted a memorial on what to cut and what to add, saying, "In the path of great transformation, nothing comes before putting the right men in office;
entries.literal: Ningzi had earlier been Chief Clerk to Gaozu as Grand Marshal and submitted a statement on what should be cut and what added, saying: "In the way of grand transformation, nothing comes before offices obtaining fit men;

entries.zh: 枚卜之方，莫若人慎其舉。
entries.en: and in the method of selection, nothing surpasses men being careful in whom they recommend.
entries.literal: In the method of casting lots, nothing surpasses men being strict in their nominations.

entries.zh: 雖復因革不同，損益有物，求賢審官，未之或改。
entries.en: Systems of reform may differ and what is cut or added may change, but seeking the worthy and scrutinizing officeholders has never gone out of date.
entries.literal: Though the systems of reform differ and cuttings and additions have their objects, seeking the worthy and scrutinizing offices have never been altered.

entries.zh: 師錫僉曰，煥乎欽明之誥，拔茅徵吉，著於幽《賁》之爻。
entries.en: When the Master took counsel and all assented—how radiant is the charge of reverent clarity; when pulling up grass foretells good fortune—it is written in the humble Bi hexagram of the Changes.
entries.literal: When the Master consulted and all assented—the radiant charge of reverent clarity; when pulling up grass foretold good fortune—it is set forth in the humble Bi hexagram of the Changes.

entries.zh: 晉師有成，瓜衍作賞，楚乘無入，蔿賈不賀。
entries.en: When Jin's army prevailed, rewards were handed out at Guayan; when Chu had no worthy man to bring in, Wei Jia offered no congratulations.
entries.literal: When Jin's army had success, rewards were made at Guayan; when Chu had no worthy to enter, Wei Jia did not congratulate.

entries.zh: 今舊命惟新，幽人引領，《韶》之盡美，已備於振綱；
entries.en: Now the old mandate is made new and recluses stretch their necks in hope—the perfection of the Shao is already complete in restoring the norms;
entries.literal: Now with the old mandate renewed, recluses crane their necks—the perfection of the Shao is already complete in restoring norms;

entries.zh: 《武》之未盡，或存於理目。
entries.en: what the Wu did not finish may still remain in statutes and regulations.
entries.literal: The imperfection of the Wu perhaps still remains in statutes and regulations.

entries.zh: 雖九官之職，未可備舉，親民之選，尤宜在先。
entries.en: Though not every post among the nine officers can be filled at once, choosing those who govern close to the people should come first.
entries.literal: Though the nine officers cannot all be appointed at once, the choice of those who draw near the people should especially come first.

entries.zh: 愚欲使天朝四品官，外及守牧，各舉一人堪為二千石長吏者，以付選官，隨缺敘用，得賢受賞，失舉任罰。
entries.en: I would have every fourth-rank official at court, and every governor and prefect in the provinces, each recommend one man fit to serve as a two-thousand-shi chief magistrate, hand the name to the selection office, and let appointments follow vacancies. Reward the nominator when the man proves worthy; punish him when the choice fails.
entries.literal: I foolishly wish that every official of the fourth rank at court, and outside them governors and prefects, each nominate one person fit to be chief official at the two-thousand-shi level and deliver him to the selection office to be assigned as vacancies arise; if worthy, the nominator receives reward—if mistaken, the nominator bears punishment.

entries.zh: 夫惟帝之難，豈庸識所易，然舉爾所知，非求多人，因百官之明，孰與一識之見，執咎在己，豈容徇物之私。
entries.en: Finding the right men is hard even for an emperor—how could shallow minds grasp it easily? Yet to recommend those you know is not to seek a crowd. Which is sharper—the judgment of a hundred offices or the knowledge of one man who must answer for his choice? The blame rests on the recommender; how can he indulge private favor?
entries.literal: That the Emperor finds it difficult—how could shallow understanding easily achieve it? Yet to nominate those you know is not to seek many men. Relying on the insight of all officials—who can match a single man's knowing? The blame rests on oneself—how can one indulge private favoritism?

entries.zh: 今非以選曹所銓，果於乖謬，眾職所舉，必也惟良，蓋宜使求賢辟其廣塗，考績取其少殿。
entries.en: This is not to say that the selection office is always wrong while mass recommendation is always right; rather, open a broad road for seeking talent and let performance review catch the few who stumble.
entries.literal: It is not that the Selection Office's adjudication is more regularly in error than nominations by the multitude are invariably good; rather one should have seeking worth open its broad road and evaluation of achievement take the fewest stumbles.

entries.zh: 若才實拔群，進宜尚德，治阿之宰，不必計年，免徒之守，豈限資秩。
entries.en: When talent truly stands out, promotion should weigh virtue above all; a magistrate who straightens a crooked district need not be judged by years in office, and a warden of convicts need not be bound by seniority in rank.
entries.literal: If talent and substance are outstanding, promotion should emphasize virtue; a magistrate who governs crooked places need not be counted by years; a guard of criminals need not be limited by rank and seniority.

entries.zh: 自此以還，故當才均以資，資均以地。
entries.en: Below that level, talent and seniority should be weighed together, and seniority matched to the post.
entries.literal: From this point down, then talent and seniority should be balanced, and seniority and place matched.

entries.zh: 宰蒞之官，誠曰吏職，然監觀民瘼，翼化宣風，則隱厚之求，急於刀筆，能事之功，接於德心，以此論才，行之年歲，豈惟政無秕蠹，民庇手足而已，將使公路日清，私請漸塞。
entries.en: A district magistrate is indeed an administrative post, yet because he watches the people's hardships and helps spread civilizing influence, what is wanted is depth of character more than skill with the brush; real achievement must connect with moral purpose. Judge talent on that basis and let years in office count for something—not only will government be free of rot and the people sheltered like one's own limbs, but the public road will grow clearer day by day and private petitions will gradually be shut out.
entries.literal: A magistrate who oversees a district is indeed called an administrative office, yet supervising and viewing the people's afflictions and aiding transformation and disseminating policy—then the demand for hidden depth is more urgent than brush and knife; merit in ability touches upon moral mind; judging talent on this basis, acting by years in office—not only will governance be without waste but the people sheltered like hands and feet; it will also daily clarify the public road and gradually block private requests.

entries.zh: 士多心競，仁必由己，處士砥自求之節，仕子藏交馳之情。
entries.en: When gentlemen compete in their hearts, benevolence must begin with themselves; recluses will sharpen the integrity of self-reliance, and officeholders will curb the urge to court connections.
entries.literal: Officials mostly compete in heart—benevolence must come from oneself; retired scholars hone the self-seeking of integrity; officeholders hide the passion of rushing connections.

entries.zh: 甯子庸微，不識治體，冒昧陳愚，退懼違謬。」
entries.en: I, Ningzi, am mean and slight and do not understand the principles of government; rashly I offer this foolish counsel and withdraw in fear of error."
entries.literal: Ningzi is low and slight, unacquainted with the principles of governance; rashly I present this folly and withdraw in fear of violating truth."

entries.zh: 宋世惟華與南陽劉湛不為飾讓，得官即拜，以此為常。
entries.en: In the Song only Hua and Liu Zhan of Nanyang did not make a show of declining office; they accepted appointments at once, and this became their custom.
entries.literal: In the Song age only Hua and Liu Zhan of Nanyang did not make show of declining; receiving office they at once accepted it, and this became their custom.

entries.zh: 華以情事異人，未嘗預宴集，終身不飲酒，有燕不之詣。
entries.en: Hua differed from others in temperament; he never joined banquets, never drank wine in his life, and when there was a feast he did not attend.
entries.literal: Hua differed from others in temperament and circumstance; he never joined banquets, never drank wine in his life, and when there was a feast he did not go.

entries.zh: 若宜有論事者，乘車造門，主人出車就之。
entries.en: If there was business to discuss, he rode to their gate, and the host came out in his carriage to meet him.
entries.literal: If there was business to discuss, he rode in his carriage to their gate, and the host came out in his carriage to meet him.

entries.zh: 及王弘輔政，而弟曇首為太祖所任，與華相埒，華嘗謂己力用不盡，每歎息曰：「宰相頓有數人，天下何由得治！」
entries.en: When Wang Hong assisted in government and his younger brother Tanshou was entrusted by the Taizu, ranking with Hua, Hua once said his abilities were not fully used and often sighed, "There are suddenly several chief ministers—how can the realm be governed!"
entries.literal: When Wang Hong assisted in government and his younger brother Tanshou was entrusted by the Taizu, ranking with Hua, Hua once said his strength was not fully used and sighed each time, "There are suddenly several chief ministers—how can the realm be governed!"

entries.zh: 四年，卒，時年四十三。
entries.en: In the fourth year he died, at the age of forty-three.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged forty-three.

entries.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、衞將軍。
entries.en: Posthumously he was given regular attendant of scattered cavalry and general of the guards.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards.

entries.zh: 九年，上思誅羨之之功，追封新建縣侯，食邑千戶，諡曰宣侯。
entries.en: In the ninth year the emperor, remembering the merit of putting Xu Xianzhi to death, posthumously enfeoffed him as marquis of Xinjian county with a fief of one thousand households; his posthumous title was Marquis Xuan.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor, remembering the merit of executing Xianzhi, posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinjian County with a fief of one thousand households; his posthumous title was Marquis Xuan.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，配饗太祖廟庭。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Hua was given paired sacrifice in the temple of Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was given paired sacrifice in the Taizu temple court.

entries.zh: 王曇首，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘少弟也。
entries.en: Wang Tanshou came from Linyi in Langye and was the younger brother of Grand Tutor Wang Hong.
entries.literal: Wang Tanshou, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the younger brother of Grand Tutor Hong.

entries.zh: 幼有業尚，除著作郎，不就。
entries.en: From childhood he showed scholarly purpose; he was appointed librarian in the historiography office but declined the post.
entries.literal: In youth he possessed scholarly attainment; he was appointed Librarian but did not accept.

entries.zh: 兄弟分財，曇首唯取圖書而已。
entries.en: When the brothers divided the family property, Tanshou took only books and maps.
entries.literal: When the brothers divided property, Tanshou took only books and maps.

entries.zh: 辟琅邪王大司馬屬，從府公脩復洛陽園陵。
entries.en: He was recruited as an aide to the prince of Langye as grand marshal and accompanied him in restoring the imperial tombs at Luoyang.
entries.literal: He was recruited as Clerk to the Grand Marshal of Langye; he followed the Prince in restoring the imperial tombs at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 與從弟球俱詣高祖，時謝晦在坐，高祖曰：「此君並膏粱盛德，乃能屈志戎旅。」
entries.en: He went with his cousin Qiu to call on Gaozu while Xie Hui was present. Gaozu said, "Both of these men are noble scions of great families, yet they are willing to humble themselves to camp life."
entries.literal: Together with his cousin Qiu he visited Gaozu. Xie Hui was then present. Gaozu said, "These gentlemen are both noble scions of eminent virtue—yet they can humble their ambition to military service."

entries.zh: 曇首答曰：「既從神武之師，自使懦夫有立志。」
entries.en: Tanshou answered, "Once one has followed a commander of divine martial prowess, even a coward finds his resolve."
entries.literal: Tanshou replied, "Having followed the divine martial master's host, by nature even a coward gains resolution."

entries.zh: 晦曰：「仁者果有勇。」
entries.en: Hui said, "The benevolent man truly has courage."
entries.literal: Hui said, "The benevolent indeed have courage."

entries.zh: 高祖悅。
entries.en: Gaozu was delighted.
entries.literal: Gaozu was pleased.

entries.zh: 行至彭城，高祖大會戲馬台，豫坐者皆賦詩；
entries.en: At Pengcheng, Gaozu gave a great banquet at the Stage for Horse Games, and every guest was asked to compose a poem.
entries.literal: When they reached Pengcheng, Gaozu held a great gathering at Stage for Horse Games; those seated all composed poems.

entries.zh: 曇首文先成，高祖覽讀，因問弘曰：「卿弟何如卿？」
entries.en: Tanshou finished first. Gaozu read his poem and asked Hong, "How does your younger brother compare with you?"
entries.literal: Tanshou's text was finished first. Gaozu read it and asked Hong, "How does your younger brother compare with you?"

entries.zh: 弘答曰：「若但如民，門戶何寄。」
entries.en: Hong replied, "If he were no better than I, what would become of our house?"
entries.literal: Hong replied, "If he were only like me—on what would the family rely?"

entries.zh: 高祖大笑。
entries.en: Gaozu laughed aloud.
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed greatly.

entries.zh: 曇首有識局智度，喜慍不見於色，閨門之內，雍雍如也。
entries.en: Tanshou had judgment, breadth, and wisdom; pleasure and anger never showed on his face, and within his household all was harmony.
entries.literal: Tanshou had discernment, capacity, and intelligence; joy and anger did not show on his face; within the women's quarters all was harmonious.

entries.zh: 手不執金玉，婦女不得為飾玩，自非祿賜所及，一毫不受於人。
entries.en: He would not handle gold or jade in his own hands; the women of his house were forbidden ornaments; and except for salary and gifts from the throne, he would not accept the slightest thing from anyone.
entries.literal: His hand did not hold gold or jade; women of the household might not make decorative ornaments; unless from salary and reward, not a hair's worth did he accept from others.

entries.zh: 太祖為冠軍、徐州刺史，留鎮彭城，以曇首為府功曹。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Wen was champion general and governor of Xuzhou, left to hold Pengcheng, he made Tanshou merit officer of his headquarters.
entries.literal: When the Taizu was Champion General and Governor of Xuzhou, stationed at Pengcheng, he made Tanshou Merit Officer of the headquarters.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮江陵，自功曹為長史，隨府轉鎮西長史。
entries.en: When the prince was posted at Jiangling, Tanshou rose from merit officer to chief clerk, and when the headquarters became General Who Guards the West, he became its chief clerk as well.
entries.literal: When the Taizu was stationed at Jiangling, from Merit Officer he became Chief Clerk, and with the headquarters transferred to Chief Clerk of the General Who Guards the West.
