entries.zh: 高祖甚知之，謂太祖曰：「王曇首，沈毅有器度，宰相才也。
entries.en: Gaozu thought highly of him and told the prince, "Wang Tanshou is deep, resolute, and broad in capacity—a man fit to be chief minister.
entries.literal: Gaozu knew him well and told the Taizu, "Wang Tanshou is deep, resolute, and has capacity—ministerial talent.

entries.zh: 汝每事咨之。」
entries.en: Consult him in everything you do."
entries.literal: In every matter consult him."

entries.zh: 景平中，有龍見西方，半天騰上，廕五彩雲，京都遠近聚觀，太史奏曰：「西方有天子氣。」
entries.en: During the Jingping era a dragon was seen in the west, rising halfway up the sky beneath five-colored clouds. People from all around the capital flocked to look. The imperial astronomer reported, "There is the aura of a Son of Heaven in the west."
entries.literal: In the Jingping era a dragon appeared in the west, soaring halfway up the sky with five-colored clouds shading it. The capital from near and far gathered to view. The Imperial Historian reported, "In the west there is the aura of a Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 太祖入奉大統，上及議者皆疑不敢下，曇首與到彥之、從兄華固勸，上猶未許。
entries.en: The prince went in to accept the great succession. The emperor and his advisers were all afraid and hesitated to step down. Tanshou, Dao Yanzhi, and his cousin Hua pressed him hard, but the emperor still would not agree.
entries.literal: The Taizu entered to receive the great succession. The Emperor and all who deliberated were doubtful and dared not descend. Tanshou with Dao Yanzhi and his cousin Hua firmly urged him, but the Emperor still did not assent.

entries.zh: 曇首又固陳，並言天人符應，上乃下。
entries.en: Tanshou argued again at length, citing signs of Heaven's approval, and only then did the emperor yield the throne.
entries.literal: Tanshou again strongly stated it, and also spoke of the correspondence between Heaven and man. Only then did the Emperor descend.

entries.zh: 率府州文武嚴兵自衛，臺所遣百官眾力，不得近部伍，中兵參軍朱容子抱刀在平乘戶外，不解帶者數旬。
entries.en: The prince led the civil and military officers of his headquarters and province under strict guard. Officials sent from the court could not approach his ranks. Army adviser Zhu Rongzi stood outside the cabin door of the imperial barge with his sword in his arms and did not unbuckle his belt for several tens of days.
entries.literal: He led the military and civil officials of the headquarters and province in strict array to guard themselves. The various officials dispatched from the court—all could not draw near his ranks. Army Adviser Zhu Rongzi embraced his sword outside the cabin door of the pingcheng barge, not unbuckling his belt for several tens of days.

entries.zh: 既下在道，有黃龍出負上所乘舟，左右皆失色，上謂曇首曰：「此乃夏禹所以受天命，我何堪之。」
entries.en: After the abdication, on the road a yellow dragon appeared and bore up the boat in which the new emperor rode. His attendants turned pale. The emperor said to Tanshou, "This is how Yu of Xia received Heaven's mandate—how am I worthy of such a thing?"
entries.literal: Once he had descended and was on the road, a yellow dragon appeared bearing the boat the Emperor rode. His attendants all changed color. The Emperor said to Tanshou, "This is how Yu of Xia received Heaven's mandate—how could I bear it?"

entries.zh: 及即位，又謂曇首曰：「非宋昌獨見，無以致此。」
entries.en: When he took the throne he said again to Tanshou, "Had you not seen what Song Chang saw, this day would never have come."
entries.literal: When he took the throne he again said to Tanshou, "Had not Song Chang alone seen it, there would have been no reaching this day."

entries.zh: 以曇首為侍中，尋領右衛將軍，領驍騎將軍。
entries.en: He appointed Tanshou palace attendant and soon gave him command of the right guards and of the galloping cavalry as well.
entries.literal: He made Tanshou Palace Attendant and soon let him additionally command the Right Guards and Galloping Cavalry.

entries.zh: 以朱容子為右軍將軍。
entries.en: Zhu Rongzi was appointed general of the right army.
entries.literal: Zhu Rongzi was made General of the Right Army.

entries.zh: 誅徐羨之等，平謝晦，曇首及華之力也。
entries.en: The execution of Xu Xianzhi and his faction and the pacification of Xie Hui were largely the work of Tanshou and Hua.
entries.literal: The execution of Xu Xianzhi and others and the pacification of Xie Hui were due to the effort of Tanshou and Hua.

entries.zh: 七年，卒。
entries.en: In the seventh year he died.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he died.

entries.zh: 太祖為之慟，中書舍人周赳侍側，曰：「王家欲衰，賢者先殞。」
entries.en: The emperor grieved deeply for him. Zhou Qiu, a secretariat drafter, said at his side, "When the Wang house is about to decline, the worthy perish first."
entries.literal: The Taizu mourned him deeply. Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Zhou Qiu at his side said, "The Wang house will decline—the worthy die first."

entries.zh: 上曰：「直是我家衰耳。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "It is truly my own house that is failing."
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "It is truly my own house that declines."

entries.zh: 追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，詹事如故。
entries.en: He was posthumously made left grand master of splendid happiness and routinely attached gentleman, while retaining his post as steward of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, added Routinely Attached Gentleman, and Steward of the Heir Apparent as before.

entries.zh: 九年，以預誅羨之等謀，追封豫寧縣侯，邑千戶，諡曰文侯。
entries.en: In the ninth year, because he had taken part in the plot against Xu Xianzhi and his faction, he was posthumously made marquis of Yuning with a fief of a thousand households and given the posthumous title Wen.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, for participating in the plot to execute Xu Xianzhi and others, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuning, fief of one thousand households, posthumous title Marquis Wen.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，配饗太祖廟庭。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Tanshou was given paired sacrifice in the temple of Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was given paired sacrifice in the Taizu temple court.

entries.zh: 子僧綽嗣，別有傳。
entries.en: His son Sengchuo succeeded him; he has a separate biography.
entries.literal: His son Sengchuo succeeded; there is a separate biography.

entries.zh: 少子僧虔，昇明末，為尚書令。
entries.en: His younger son Sengqian, at the end of the Shengming era, served as minister president of the secretariat.
entries.literal: His younger son Sengqian, at the end of the Shengming era, was Minister President of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 殷景仁，陳郡長平人也。
entries.en: Yin Jingren came from Changping in Chen commandery.
entries.literal: Yin Jingren was a native of Changping in Chen commandery.

entries.zh: 曾祖融，晉太常。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Rong had been grand director of ceremonies under Jin.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Rong was Jin Grand Director of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 祖茂，散騎常侍、特進、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: His grandfather Mao had served as attendant gentleman, special advanced, and left grand master of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: His grandfather Mao was Attendant Gentleman, Special Advanced, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 父道裕，蚤亡。
entries.en: His father Daoyu died young.
entries.literal: His father Daoyu died early.

entries.zh: 景仁少有大成之量，司徒王謐見而以女妻之。
entries.en: From youth Jingren showed the makings of great accomplishment, and Steward Wang Mi, on meeting him, gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Jingren in youth had the capacity for great achievement; Steward Wang Mi saw him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 初為劉毅後軍參軍，高祖太尉行參軍。
entries.en: He began as a staff officer in Liu Yi's rear army, then served as an attendant army officer under Gaozu when he was grand marshal.
entries.literal: At first he was Rear Army Colonel staff officer under Liu Yi, then Attendant Army Officer under Gaozu as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 建議宜令百官舉才，以所薦能否為黜陟。
entries.en: He proposed that every official should recommend talent and that promotion and demotion should follow whether those recommendations proved sound.
entries.literal: He proposed that all officials should recommend talent, with promotion and demotion according to whether their recommendations succeeded.

entries.zh: 遷宋臺秘書郎，世子中軍參軍，轉主簿，又為驃騎將軍道憐主簿。
entries.en: He rose to secretary in the Song secretariat, then middle army colonel to the heir apparent, then chief clerk, and later chief clerk to Cavalry General Daoling.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Secretary of the Song Terrace, Heir Apparent Middle Army Colonel, then Chief Clerk, and again chief clerk to Cavalry General Daoling.

entries.zh: 出補衡陽太守，入為宋世子洗馬，仍轉中書侍郎。
entries.en: He served as governor of Hengyang, then returned as groom of the stud to the Song heir apparent, and was later made a gentleman of the secretariat.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of Hengyang, entered as Groom of the Stud to the Song Heir Apparent, and then transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 景仁學不為文，敏有思致，口不談義，深達理體；
entries.en: Jingren did not pursue learning for display; he was quick and thoughtful, rarely spoke of doctrine aloud, yet grasped underlying principles with depth.
entries.literal: Jingren's learning was not devoted to literary display; he was keen and thoughtful; he did not discuss principles orally but deeply grasped underlying patterns.

entries.zh: 至於國典朝儀，舊章記注，莫不撰錄，識者知其有當世之志也。
entries.en: On state law, court ritual, and old regulations and commentaries, he compiled and recorded everything, and those who knew him saw that he aimed to serve his own time.
entries.literal: As for state statutes, court ritual, old regulations and annotations, he compiled them all—knowing observers saw he had ambition for his age.

entries.zh: 高祖甚知之，遷太子中庶子。
entries.en: Gaozu thought highly of him and made him junior mentor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Gaozu knew him well and promoted him to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，葬竟，起為領軍將軍，固辭。
entries.en: While he was in mourning for his mother, after the burial was completed, he was recalled as general of the palace garrison but firmly declined.
entries.literal: When mourning for his mother ended after burial, he was recalled as General of the Palace Garrison and firmly declined.

entries.zh: 上使綱紀代拜，遣中書舍人周赳輿載還府。
entries.en: The emperor had his staff perform the ceremony of acceptance on his behalf and sent Zhou Qiu in a carriage to bring Jingren back to his residence.
entries.literal: The Emperor had the administrative officers perform the bow in his stead and sent Attendant Gentleman Zhou Qiu in a carriage to bring him back to his residence.

entries.zh: 九年，服闋，遷尚書僕射。
entries.en: In the ninth year, when his mourning was complete, he was made vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, when mourning ended, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太子詹事劉湛代為領軍，與景仁素善，皆被遇於高祖，俱以宰相許之。
entries.en: Liu Zhan, steward of the heir apparent, replaced him as commander of the garrison. He and Jingren had long been friends; both had won favor under Gaozu and both were expected to become chief ministers.
entries.literal: Steward of the Heir Apparent Liu Zhan replaced him as commander of the garrison. He and Jingren had long been on good terms; both were favored by Gaozu and both were regarded as future chief ministers.

entries.zh: 湛尚居外任，會王弘、華、曇首相係亡，景仁引湛還朝，共參政事。
entries.en: Zhan was still serving outside the capital when Wang Hong, Hua, and Tanshou died one after another. Jingren brought him back to court so they could share in government.
entries.literal: Zhan was still in an outside post when Wang Hong, Hua, and Tanshou died in succession. Jingren brought Zhan back to court to share in government together.

entries.zh: 湛既入，以景仁位遇本不逾己，而一旦居前，意甚憤憤。
entries.en: Once Zhan returned, he resented that Jingren—whose standing had never been above his own—had suddenly moved ahead of him.
entries.literal: Once Zhan had entered, because Jingren's rank and treatment had originally not exceeded his own yet suddenly stood before him, his mind was greatly resentful.

entries.zh: 知太祖信仗景仁，不可移奪，乃深結司徒彭城王義康，欲倚宰相之重以傾之。
entries.en: Knowing the emperor trusted Jingren and would not be swayed, he allied himself closely with Prince Pengcheng Yikang, hoping to use the prince's weight as de facto chief minister to bring Jingren down.
entries.literal: Knowing the Taizu trusted and relied on Jingren and could not be moved, he then formed deep ties with Steward Prince Pengcheng Yikang, wishing to lean on the weight of a chief minister to overthrow him.

entries.zh: 上與荊州刺史衡陽王義季書曰：「殷僕射疾患少日，奄忽不救。
entries.en: The emperor wrote to Prince Hengyang Yiji, governor of Jingzhou: "Vice Director Yin was ill only a few days and then was suddenly beyond help.
entries.literal: The Emperor wrote to Prince Hengyang Yiji, Governor of Jingzhou: "Vice Director Yin was ill only a few days and suddenly could not be saved.

entries.zh: 其識具經遠，奉國竭誠，周遊繾綣，情兼常痛。
entries.en: His knowledge was broad and far-sighted, and he served the state with complete loyalty. Our long intimacy makes this loss doubly painful.
entries.literal: His knowledge was comprehensive and far-reaching; serving the state he exhausted loyalty. Our long intimacy makes the feeling doubly painful.

entries.zh: 民望國器，遇之為難，惋歎之深，不能已已。
entries.en: He was a pillar of the people's hopes and of the state; men like him are hard to find. My grief is so deep it will not stop.
entries.literal: He was the people's hope and the state's vessel; to meet such a man is rare. My deep regret cannot cease.

entries.zh: 汝亦同不？
entries.en: Do you feel the same?
entries.literal: Do you feel the same?

entries.zh: 往矣如何！」
entries.en: He is gone—what can be done!"
entries.literal: He is gone—what can be done!"

entries.zh: 世祖大明五年，行幸經景仁墓，詔曰：「司空文成公景仁德量淹正，風識明允，徽績忠謨，夙達先照，惠政茂譽，實留民屬。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu passed Jingren's tomb on tour and issued an edict: "Minister of Works Duke of Literary Accomplishment Jingren was deep in virtue and upright in bearing, clear and trustworthy in judgment, loyal in counsel and far-sighted in service; his benevolent rule and fine reputation truly remain in the people's hearts.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Daming of Shizu, on an imperial progress passing Jingren's tomb, an edict said: "Minister of Works Duke of Literary Accomplishment Jingren's virtue and measure were deep and upright, his discernment clear and true, his emblematic achievement loyal counsel, early reaching foresight, his benevolent government and abundant reputation truly left in the people's hearts.

entries.zh: 近瞻丘墳，感往興悼，可遣使致祭。」
entries.en: Gazing on his mound, I am moved by the past and filled with mourning. Let an envoy be sent to offer sacrifice."
entries.literal: Drawing near and viewing the mound and grave, moved by the past I rise in mourning. An envoy may be sent to perform sacrifice."

entries.zh: 沈演之，字台真，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Shen Yanzhi, whose courtesy name was Taizhen, came from Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Shen Yanzhi, courtesy name Taizhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 高祖充，晉車騎將軍，吳國內史。
entries.en: His ancestor Chong had been general of chariots and cavalry under Jin and interior minister of Wu.
entries.literal: Ancestor Chong was Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry and Interior Minister of Wu.

entries.zh: 曾祖勁，冠軍陳祐長史，戍金墉城，為鮮卑慕容恪所陷，不屈節，見殺，追贈東陽太守。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Jin was chief clerk to Champion Chen You and held Jinyong when the Xianbei general Murong Ke took the city. He refused to yield and was killed, and was later posthumously made governor of Dongyang.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Jin was chief clerk to Champion Chen You, garrisoning the city of Jinyong; he was taken by the Xianbei Murong Ke, would not submit, and was killed; posthumously given Governor of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 祖赤黔，廷尉卿。
entries.en: His grandfather Chiqian had been minister of justice.
entries.literal: His grandfather Chiqian was Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 父叔任，少有幹質，初為揚州主簿，高祖太尉參軍，吳、山陰令，治皆有聲。
entries.en: His father Shuren showed ability from youth. He first served as chief clerk of Yangzhou, then as an army officer under Gaozu when he was grand marshal, and as magistrate of Wu and Shanyin, winning praise in every post.
entries.literal: His father Shuren in youth had capacity and substance; at first he was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou, Army Officer under Gaozu as Grand Marshal, and magistrate of Wu and Shanyin—his governance in each had reputation.

entries.zh: 朱齡石伐蜀，為齡石建威府司馬，加建威將軍。
entries.en: When Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu, Shuren served as chief clerk of his headquarters as general who establishes might and was given the additional title of that same rank.
entries.literal: When Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu, he was Chief Clerk of Lingshi's headquarters as General Who Establishes Might, with additional title General Who Establishes Might.

entries.zh: 平蜀之功，亞于元帥，即本號為西夷校尉、巴西梓潼郡太守，戍涪城。
entries.en: In the conquest of Shu his merit was second only to the commander-in-chief. He was made colonel of the western Yi and governor of Brazil and Zitong, and garrisoned Fucheng.
entries.literal: In the merit of pacifying Shu he was second only to the commander-in-chief; on his original title he was Colonel of the Western Yi, Governor of Brazil and Zitong commanderies, garrisoning Fucheng.

entries.zh: 東軍既反，二郡強宗侯勱、羅奧聚眾作亂，四面雲合，遂至萬餘人，攻城急。
entries.en: When the eastern army rebelled, the powerful clan leaders Hou Mo and Luo Ao of the two commanderies raised troops in revolt. Men converged from every side until they numbered more than ten thousand and pressed the siege hard.
entries.literal: Once the eastern army had rebelled, powerful clans of the two commanderies Hou Mo and Luo Ao gathered followers and made disorder; from all sides they clouded together until they reached more than ten thousand men and pressed the siege urgently.

entries.zh: 叔任東兵不滿五百，推布腹心，眾莫不為用，出擊大破之，逆黨皆平。
entries.en: Shuren had fewer than five hundred men in the east, but he won every man's loyalty with open-hearted trust. He went out, routed them completely, and pacified the rebels.
entries.literal: Shuren's eastern troops were fewer than five hundred; he extended trust with open heart and none did not serve him. Going out he struck and greatly defeated them; the rebel faction was all pacified.

entries.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，齡石遣叔任率軍來會。
entries.en: When Gaozu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Lingshi sent Shuren with troops to join the campaign.
entries.literal: When Gaozu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Lingshi sent Shuren to lead troops and join the rendezvous.

entries.zh: 時高祖領鎮西將軍，命為司馬。
entries.en: Gaozu was then general who guards the west and appointed Shuren his chief clerk.
entries.literal: At that time Gaozu held the post of General Who Guards the West and appointed him Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 及軍還，以為揚州別駕從事史。
entries.en: When the army returned he was made attendant administrative officer of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: When the army returned he was made Attendant Administrative Officer, Vice Director of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 以平蜀全涪之功，封寧新縣男，食邑四百四十戶。
entries.en: For pacifying Shu and holding Fucheng intact, he was enfeoffed as baron of Ningxin with a fief of four hundred forty households.
entries.literal: For the merit of pacifying Shu and preserving Fucheng intact, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningxin, fief of four hundred forty households.

entries.zh: 出為建威將軍、益州刺史，以疾還都。
entries.en: He went out as general who establishes might and governor of Yizhou, but returned to the capital because of illness.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Yizhou; because of illness he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 義熙十四年，卒，時年五十。
entries.en: He died in the fourteenth year of Yixi, at the age of fifty.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he died, aged fifty.

entries.zh: 長子融之，蚤卒。
entries.en: His eldest son Rongzhi died young.
entries.literal: His eldest son Rongzhi died early.

entries.zh: 元嘉十二年，東諸郡大水，民人饑饉，吳義興及吳郡之錢唐，升米三百。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies were flooded and the people starved. In Wu, Yixing, and Qiantang of Wu commandery, rice reached three hundred cash per sheng.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies suffered great flood; the people were in famine—in Wu, Yixing and Qiantang in Wu commandery, rice was three hundred cash per sheng.

entries.zh: 以演之及尚書祠部郎江邃並兼散騎常侍，巡行拯恤，許以便宜從事。
entries.en: Yanzhi and Jiang Sui of the ministry of rites were both given the additional post of routinely attached gentleman to tour the region and bring relief, with authority to act as circumstances required.
entries.literal: Yanzhi and Jiang Sui, Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, were both additionally made Routinely Attached Gentlemen to tour and relieve, permitted to act as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 演之乃開倉廩以賑饑民，民有生子者，口賜米一斗，刑獄有疑枉，悉制遣之，百姓蒙賴。
entries.en: Yanzhi opened the granaries to feed the hungry. Families with new births received a dou of rice for each mouth, and doubtful or wrongful prisoners were all released. The people owed him their survival.
entries.literal: Yanzhi then opened granaries to relieve the starving; for those who bore sons, each person was given one dou of rice; doubtful and wrongful cases in punishment and prison were all released—the people relied on him.

entries.zh: 轉別駕從事史，領本郡中正，深為義康所待，故在府州前後十餘年。
entries.en: He became attendant administrative officer and head of the provincial impartial judge. Deeply favored by Yikang, he remained at headquarters and in the province for more than ten years in all.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Administrative Officer, heading the provincial impartial judge; deeply treated by Yikang, so at headquarters and province for more than ten years before and after.

entries.zh: 後劉湛、劉斌等結黨，欲排廢尚書僕射殷景仁，演之雅仗正義，與湛等不同，湛因此讒之於義康。
entries.en: Later Liu Zhan, Liu Bin, and others formed a faction to drive out Vice Director Yin Jingren. Yanzhi stood on principle and broke with them, and Zhan therefore slandered him to Yikang.
entries.literal: Later Liu Zhan, Liu Bin and others formed a faction wishing to expel and ruin Vice Director Yin Jingren; Yanzhi by nature relied on righteousness and differed from Zhan and others—Zhan therefore slandered him to Yikang.

entries.zh: 嘗因論事不合旨，義康變色曰：「自今而後，我不復相信！」
entries.en: Once, when their discussion of policy failed to please him, Yikang turned dark and said, "From now on I will no longer trust you!"
entries.literal: Once in discussion of affairs they did not accord with the intent; Yikang changed color and said, "From now on I no longer trust you!"

entries.zh: 演之與景仁素善，盡心於朝庭，太祖甚嘉之，以為尚書吏部郎。
entries.en: Yanzhi had long been close to Jingren and gave his full loyalty to the court. The emperor praised him highly and made him gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: Yanzhi and Jingren had long been on good terms and devoted their hearts to the court; the Taizu greatly praised this and made him Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 演之昔與同使江邃字玄遠，濟陽考城人。
entries.en: Yanzhi had once served as envoy together with Jiang Sui, courtesy name Xuanyuan, from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
entries.literal: Yanzhi once with fellow envoy Jiang Sui, courtesy name Xuanyuan, a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

entries.zh: 頗有文義。
entries.en: He had considerable literary learning.
entries.literal: He had considerable literary understanding.

entries.zh: 官至司徒記室參軍，撰《文釋》，傳於世。
entries.en: He rose to recording colonel of the secretariat and wrote Literary Explication, which circulated in his day.
entries.literal: He reached office as Recording Colonel of the Secretariat and composed Literary Explication, transmitted in the world.

entries.zh: 演之子睦，至黃門郎，通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: Yanzhi's son Mu rose to gentleman at the Yellow Gate and direct, routinely attached gentleman.
entries.literal: Yanzhi's son Mu reached Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Direct and Routinely Attached Gentleman.

entries.zh: 世祖大明初，坐要引上左右俞欣之訪評殿省內事，又與弟西陽王文學勃忿鬩不睦，坐徙始興郡，勃免官禁錮。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, Mu was exiled to Shixing for drawing the emperor's attendant Yu Xin into discussions of inner-palace affairs and for feuding with his younger brother Bo, literary attendant to the prince of Xiyang. Bo was dismissed and barred from office.
entries.literal: Early in Daming of Shizu, for summoning and drawing in the Emperor's attendant Yu Xin to inquire and comment on inner-palace affairs, and for quarreling with his younger brother Prince Xiyang's literary attendant Bo, he was exiled to Shixing commandery; Bo was dismissed from office and forbidden.

entries.zh: 勃弟統，大明中為著作佐郎。
entries.en: Bo's younger brother Tong served as assistant gentleman of writings under Daming.
entries.literal: Bo's younger brother Tong, in the Daming era was Assistant Gentleman of Writings.

entries.zh: 先是，五省官所給幹僮，不得雜役，太祖世，坐以免官者，前後百人。
entries.en: Earlier, the dry servants assigned to officials of the five directorates were forbidden to perform miscellaneous labor. Under Emperor Wen, about a hundred officials were dismissed for violating this rule.
entries.literal: Earlier, the dry servants given to officials of the five directorates could not do miscellaneous labor; in the Taizu era those dismissed from office for this numbered a hundred before and after.

entries.zh: 統輕役過差，有司奏免。
entries.en: Tong overworked his servants beyond what was allowed, and the authorities memorialized for his dismissal.
entries.literal: Tong overused his assigned servants beyond the limit; the responsible offices memorialized dismissal.

entries.zh: 世祖詔曰：「自頃幹僮，多不祗給，主可量聽行杖。」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu decreed, "Lately dry servants have often failed in their duties. Masters may, within reason, apply the staff to them."
entries.literal: Shizu issued an edict: "Lately dry servants have mostly failed to attend to their duties; masters may, as a measure, be permitted to apply the staff."

entries.zh: 得行幹杖，自此始也。
entries.en: Permission to beat dry servants began from that time.
entries.literal: Permission to apply staff to dry servants—from this it began.

entries.zh: 列傳第二十三 王華王曇首殷景仁沈演之
entries.en: Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, and Shen Yanzhi
entries.literal: Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi

entries.zh: 吉翰，字休文，馮翊池陽人也。
entries.en: Ji Han, whose courtesy name was Xiuwen, came from Chiyang in Fengyi.
entries.literal: Ji Han, style name Xiuwen, was a native of Chiyang in Fengyi.

entries.zh: 初為龍驤將軍道憐參軍，隨府轉征虜左軍參軍，員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: He began as an aide on the staff of General of the Soaring Dragon Liu Daolian, then moved with the command to aide of the Left Army of the Vanquisher of Barbarians and finally to external attendant gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: At first he was aide to General of the Soaring Dragon Daolian; with the headquarters he was transferred to aide of the Left Army of the Vanquisher of Barbarians, then External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court.

entries.zh: 隨道憐北征廣固，賜爵建城縣五等男。
entries.en: He followed Daolian north to campaign at Guanggu and was granted the fifth-rank barony of Jiancheng County.
entries.literal: He accompanied Daolian on the northern campaign to Guanggu and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Jiancheng County.

entries.zh: 轉道憐驃騎中兵參軍，從事中郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to central army aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff and then to attending gentleman.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Central Army Aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff and then Attending Gentleman.

entries.zh: 為將佐十餘年，清謹剛正，甚為高祖所知賞。
entries.en: For over a decade he served as a military officer, noted for his integrity and strict probity, and won high esteem from the Founding Emperor.
entries.literal: For more than ten years he served as a military officer, pure, careful, and upright; the Founding Emperor knew and valued him greatly.

entries.zh: 永初三年，轉道憐太尉司馬。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongchu (422) he became chief of staff to Daolian in his capacity as Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he became Chief of Staff to Daolian as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 劉道產，彭城呂人，太尉諮議參軍簡之子也。
entries.en: Liu Daochan, a native of Lu in Pengcheng, was the son of Jian, consulting aide to the Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Liu Daochan was a man of Lu in Pengcheng, son of Jian, a consulting aide to the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 簡之事在弟子康祖傳。
entries.en: Jian's career is told in the biography of his younger brother Kangzu.
entries.literal: Jian's career is recorded in the biography of his younger brother Kangzu.

entries.zh: 道產初為輔國參軍，無錫令，在縣有能名。
entries.en: Daochan first served as aide to the State-Supporting General, then as magistrate of Wuxi, where he earned a name for capable administration.
entries.literal: Daochan first served as aide to the State-Supporting General, then as magistrate of Wuxi, where he gained a reputation for competence.

entries.zh: 高祖版為中軍行參軍，又為道憐驃騎參軍，襲父爵晉安縣五等侯。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor made him acting aide on the central army staff and then aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor appointed him acting aide on the Central Army staff, then aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.

entries.zh: 廣州群盜因刺史謝道欣死為寇，攻沒州城，道憐加道產振武將軍南討，會始興謙之已平廣州，道產未至而反。
entries.en: When bandits in Guangzhou seized the prefectural city after Inspector Xie Daoxin's death, Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells Martial Disorders and sent him south; but Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou before Daochan arrived, and he turned back.
entries.literal: Bandits in Guangzhou, taking advantage of the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin, rose as marauders and captured the prefectural city; Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells Martial Disorders and sent him south to attack, but by the time he arrived Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou, and Daochan turned back before reaching it.

entries.zh: 杜驥，字度世，京兆杜陵人也。
entries.en: Du Ji, whose courtesy name was Dushi, came from Duling in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Du Ji, style name Dushi, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 高祖預，晉征南將軍。
entries.en: His ancestor Yu served Jin as General of the South.
entries.literal: His ancestor Yu was Jin General of the South.

entries.zh: 曾祖耽，避難河西，因仕張氏。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Dan took refuge in Hexi and entered the service of the Zhang regime.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Dan fled to Hexi for refuge and entered the service of the Zhang clan.

entries.zh: 苻堅平涼州，父祖始還關中。
entries.en: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather returned to Guanzhong.
entries.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Liang Province, his father and grandfather returned to Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 兄坦，頗涉史傳。
entries.en: His elder brother Tan was well read in history.
entries.literal: His elder brother Tan was well versed in historical writings.

entries.zh: 高祖征長安，席捲隨從南還。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Chang'an, he joined the southward march and returned with the army.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Chang'an, he swept along in the train and returned south.

entries.zh: 太祖元嘉中，任遇甚厚，歷後軍將軍，龍驤將軍，青、冀二州刺史，南平王鑠右將軍司馬。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era Tan enjoyed exceptional favor, serving as rear guard general, soaring dragon general, inspector of Qing and Ji, and chief of staff to Prince of Nanping Liu Shuo's right general.
entries.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, Tan received very generous appointments, serving as General of the Rear Guard, General of the Soaring Dragon, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Chief of Staff to the Right General under Prince of Nanping Shuo.

entries.zh: 晚度北人，朝廷常以傖荒遇之，雖復人才可施，每為清塗所隔，坦以此慨然。
entries.en: As a northerner who had crossed south late, the court treated him as an outsider; though his talent was usable, the established elite kept him out, and Tan brooded bitterly over this.
entries.literal: As a northerner who had crossed south late, the court always treated him as crude and rustic; though his talent could have been used, he was repeatedly blocked by the pure elite, and Tan lamented this.

entries.zh: 嘗與太祖言及史籍，上曰：「金日磾忠孝淳深，漢朝莫及，恨今世無復如此輩人。」
entries.en: Once, discussing history with the Emperor, the Emperor said, "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial devotion were profound beyond anything in Han times—I regret that men like him no longer exist today."
entries.literal: Once when speaking with the Emperor about historical records, the Emperor said: "Jin Midi's loyalty and filial piety were pure and deep; the Han could not match him—I regret that our age has no such men."

entries.zh: 坦曰：「日磾之美，誠如聖詔。
entries.en: Tan replied, "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Majesty says.
entries.literal: Tan said: "Midi's excellence is indeed as Your Sacred Edict states.

entries.zh: 假使生乎今世，養馬不暇，豈辦見知。」
entries.en: Had he lived in our age, he would have had no time beyond tending horses—how could he ever have been noticed?"
entries.literal: Had he been born in our age, he would have had no leisure beyond tending horses—how could he have won recognition?"

entries.zh: 上變色曰：「卿何量朝廷之薄也。」
entries.en: The Emperor's face darkened. "Why do you think so little of the court?"
entries.literal: The Emperor changed color and said: "Why do you measure the court so meanly?"

entries.zh: 坦曰：「請以臣言之。
entries.en: Tan said, "Let me speak from my own case.
entries.literal: Tan said: "Allow me to speak from my own case.

entries.zh: 臣本中華高族，亡曾祖晉氏喪亂，播遷涼土，世葉相承，不殞其舊。
entries.en: I come from a distinguished Chinese house; my great-grandfather was driven to Liang in Jin's collapse, yet our line preserved its standing generation after generation.
entries.literal: I am originally of a lofty Chinese clan; my late great-grandfather, in Jin's turmoil, was scattered to Liang territory, yet generation after generation preserved our old standing.

entries.zh: 直以南度不早，便以荒傖賜隔。
entries.en: Simply because we crossed south too late, we are dismissed as crude outsiders.
entries.literal: Simply because we crossed south too late, we are set apart as crude outsiders.

entries.zh: 日磾胡人，身為牧圉，便超入內侍，齒列名賢。
entries.en: Midi was a foreigner who tended horses, yet he rose straight into the inner court and stood among the great men of his age.
entries.literal: Midi was a barbarian who tended horses, yet he rose at once to inner attendance and stood among the famed worthies.

entries.zh: 聖朝雖復拔才，臣恐未必能也。」
entries.en: Though our sage dynasty may promote talent, I doubt it could do the same today."
entries.literal: Though our sage dynasty may also promote talent, I fear it could not do the same."

entries.zh: 上默然。
entries.en: The Emperor said nothing.
entries.literal: The Emperor was silent.

entries.zh: 元嘉七年，隨到彥之入河南，加建武將軍。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yuanjia (430) he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was made General Who Establishes Martial Prestige.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he followed Dao Yanzhi into Henan and was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martial Prestige.

entries.zh: 索虜撤河南戍悉歸河北，彥之使驥守洛陽。
entries.en: The Northern Wei pulled all Henan garrisons back north of the river, and Yanzhi left Ji to hold Luoyang.
entries.literal: The Northern Wei withdrew all Henan garrisons north of the river; Yanzhi ordered Ji to hold Luoyang.

entries.zh: 洛陽城不治既久，又無糧食，及彥之敗退，驥欲棄城走，慮為太祖所誅。
entries.en: Luoyang had long been neglected and had no grain; when Yanzhi was routed, Ji wanted to abandon the city and flee but feared the Emperor would have him executed.
entries.literal: Luoyang had long gone unrepaired and had no provisions; when Yanzhi was defeated and withdrew, Ji wished to abandon the city and flee but feared execution by the Emperor.

entries.zh: 初，高祖平關洛，致鐘虡舊器南還，一大鐘墜洛水。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor had pacified Guan and Luo, he sent the ancient bells and vessels south; one great bell had fallen into the Luo River.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Founding Emperor pacified Guan and Luo, he sent the old bells and ritual vessels south; one great bell fell into the Luo River.

entries.zh: 至是太祖遣將姚聳夫領千五百人迎致之。
entries.en: The Emperor now sent General Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to recover it.
entries.literal: Now the Emperor sent the general Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to bring it back.

entries.zh: 時聳夫政率所領牽鐘于洛水，驥乃誑之曰：「虜既南渡，洛城勢弱，今修理城池，竝已堅固，軍糧又足，所乏者人耳。
entries.en: Songfu was then hauling the bell at the Luo when Ji deceived him: "The enemy has crossed south and Luoyang looks weak—but we have repaired the walls, provisions are ample, and we only lack men.
entries.literal: At that time Songfu was just leading his men to haul the bell at the Luo; Ji deceived him, saying: "The barbarians have crossed south and Luoyang is weak—but we have now repaired the walls and they are firm, provisions are ample, and all we lack is men.

entries.zh: 君率眾見就，共守此城，大功既立，取鐘無晚。」
entries.en: Bring your men and help hold the city; once we have done that, there will be time enough to fetch the bell."
entries.literal: Lead your men here and defend this city with us; once the great achievement is won, retrieving the bell will not be late."

entries.zh: 聳夫信之，率所領就驥。
entries.en: Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.
entries.literal: Songfu believed him and led his men to Ji.

entries.zh: 既至，見城不可守，又無糧食，於是引眾去。
entries.en: Once there, they saw the city could not be held and there was no food, and they led their men away.
entries.literal: When they arrived and saw the city could not be held and there was no food, they led their men away.

entries.zh: 驥亦委城南奔，白太祖曰：「本欲以死固守，姚聳夫及城便走，人情沮敗，不可復禁。」
entries.en: Ji too abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to the Emperor: "I had meant to die defending it, but when Yao Songfu arrived he fled at once; morale collapsed and could not be held."
entries.literal: Ji too abandoned the city and fled south, reporting to the Emperor: "I had meant to hold firm unto death, but when Yao Songfu reached the city he fled at once; morale collapsed and could not be restrained."

entries.zh: 上大怒，使建威將軍鄭順之殺聳夫於壽陽。
entries.en: The Emperor was furious and sent General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi to execute Songfu at Shouyang.
entries.literal: The Emperor was furious and sent General Who Establishes Prestige Zheng Shunzhi to execute Songfu at Shouyang.

entries.zh: 聳夫，吳興武康人。
entries.en: Songfu was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Songfu was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 勇果有氣力，宋世偏裨小將莫及。
entries.en: Brave, fierce, and immensely strong, no subordinate general of the Song could match him.
entries.literal: Brave, resolute, and strong, no subordinate general of the Song could match him.

entries.zh: 始隨到彥之北伐，與虜遇，聳夫手斬托跋燾叔父英文特勒首，燾以馬百匹贖之。
entries.en: He had first followed Dao Yanzhi north; in battle he personally beheaded Tuoba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele, and Tao ransomed the head with a hundred horses.
entries.literal: At first he followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign; meeting the enemy, Songfu personally beheaded Tuoba Tao's uncle Yingwen Tele; Tao ransomed the head with a hundred horses.

entries.zh: 以驥為通直郎，射聲校尉，世祖征虜諮議參軍。
entries.en: Ji was made direct attendant, colonel of the archers who shoot at sound, and consulting aide on the future Emperor Xiaowu's staff as Vanquisher of Barbarians.
entries.literal: Ji was made Direct Attendant, Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound, and consulting aide on the future Emperor Xiaowu's staff as Vanquisher of Barbarians.

entries.zh: 十七年，出督青、冀二州、徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、青、冀二州刺史。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year (440) he was sent out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji and in Dongguan and Dong'an of Xu, as General of Distant Pacification and inspector of Qing and Ji.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out to supervise military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces and the two Xu commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an, as General of Distant Pacification and Inspector of Qing and Ji.

entries.zh: 在任八年，惠化著於齊土。
entries.en: In eight years in office his benevolent rule became renowned throughout Qi.
entries.literal: In eight years in office his benevolent governance was renowned throughout Qi territory.

entries.zh: 自義熙至於宋末，刺史唯羊穆之及驥，為吏民所稱詠。
entries.en: From Yixi to the end of Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among provincial inspectors won lasting praise from officials and people alike.
entries.literal: From Yixi to the end of Song, only Yang Muzhi and Ji among inspectors were praised and celebrated by officials and people.

entries.zh: 二十四年，徵左軍將軍，兄坦代為刺史，北土以為榮焉。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year (447) he was recalled as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan took over as inspector, which northerners regarded as a great honor.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned as General of the Left Army; his elder brother Tan replaced him as inspector, and northerners took this as an honor.

entries.zh: 坦長子琬為員外散騎侍郎，太祖嘗有函詔敕坦，琬輒開視。
entries.en: Tan's eldest son Wan served as external attendant gentleman; once the Emperor sent Tan a sealed edict, and Wan opened and read it.
entries.literal: Tan's eldest son Wan was External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court; the Emperor once had a sealed edict for Tan, and Wan opened and read it.

entries.zh: 信未發又追取之，敕函已發，大相推檢。
entries.en: Before the messenger departed the letter was recalled; because the seal had been broken, a major investigation ensued.
entries.literal: Before the letter was sent it was recalled; since the sealed edict had been opened, a major investigation followed.

entries.zh: 丞都答云：「諸郎開視。」
entries.en: The prefectural chief clerk replied, "The young gentlemen opened it."
entries.literal: The chief clerk of the prefecture answered: "The young gentlemen opened and read it."

entries.zh: 上遣主書詰責，驥答曰：「開函是臣第四子季文，伏待刑坐。」
entries.en: The Emperor sent a chief clerk to investigate; Ji answered, "My fourth son Jiwen opened the seal; I await punishment."
entries.literal: The Emperor sent a chief clerk to question and rebuke him; Ji answered: "The one who opened the seal was my fourth son Jiwen; I submit myself to punishment."

entries.zh: 上特原不問。
entries.en: The Emperor specially pardoned him and dropped the matter.
entries.literal: The Emperor specially pardoned him and took no further action.

entries.zh: 二十七年，卒，時年六十四。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-seventh year (450), at the age of sixty-four.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died, at the age of sixty-four.

entries.zh: 申恬，字公休，魏郡魏人也。
entries.en: Shen Tian, whose courtesy name was Gongxiu, came from Wei in Wei commandery.
entries.literal: Shen Tian, style name Gongxiu, was a native of Wei in Wei commandery.

entries.zh: 曾祖鍾，為石虎司徒。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Zhong served Shi Hu as Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong served Shi Hu as Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 高祖平廣固，恬父宣、宣從父兄永皆得歸國，竝以幹用見知。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's cousin Yong both returned to Song and were valued for their practical ability.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified Guanggu, Tian's father Xuan and Xuan's cousin Yong were both able to return to the realm and were known for practical ability.

entries.zh: 永歷青、兗二州刺史。
entries.en: Yong served as inspector of Qing and Yan.
entries.literal: Yong served as Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜太中大夫。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Yong was made grand master of palace counsel.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Yong was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

entries.zh: 宣，太祖元嘉初，亦歷兗、青二州刺史。
entries.en: Xuan, at the start of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, also served as inspector of Yan and Qing.
entries.literal: Xuan, at the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, also served as Inspector of Yan and Qing provinces.

entries.zh: 恬兄謨，與朱脩之守滑臺，為虜所沒，後得叛還。
entries.en: Tian's elder brother Mo held Huatai with Zhu Xiuzhi, was captured by the enemy, and later defected back.
entries.literal: Tian's elder brother Mo, with Zhu Xiuzhi, held Huatai; he was captured by the enemy but later defected back.

entries.zh: 元嘉中，為竟陵太守。
entries.en: In the Yuanjia era he served as administrator of Jingling.
entries.literal: In the Yuanjia era he served as Administrator of Jingling.

entries.zh: 恬初為驃騎道憐長兼行參軍。
entries.en: Tian first served as senior acting aide on Liu Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff.
entries.literal: Tian first served as senior acting aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜東宮殿中將軍，度還臺。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Tian was made palace general of the Eastern Palace and then returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Tian was made Palace General of the Eastern Palace and then transferred back to the capital.

entries.zh: 直省十載，不請休息。
entries.en: For ten years on palace duty he never asked for a rest.
entries.literal: For ten years on palace duty he never asked for leave.

entries.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，出為綏遠將軍、下邳太守。
entries.en: He was transferred to external attendant gentleman, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and administrator of Xiapi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court, then went out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Xiapi.

entries.zh: 轉在北海，加寧遠將軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to Beihai and given the additional title General of Distant Pacification.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Beihai and given the additional title General of Distant Pacification.

entries.zh: 所至皆有政績。
entries.en: Wherever he served he left a record of good administration.
entries.literal: Wherever he went he achieved administrative results.

entries.zh: 又為北譙、梁二郡太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He also served as administrator of Beiqiao and Liang, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: He also served as Administrator of the two commanderies of Beiqiao and Liang, his general's rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 郡境邊接任榛，屢被寇抄。
entries.en: The commandery bordered Renzhen and suffered repeated raids.
entries.literal: The commandery bordered Renzhen and was repeatedly raided.

entries.zh: 恬到，密知賊來，仍伏兵要害，出其不意，悉皆禽殄。
entries.en: When Tian arrived he learned secretly that raiders were coming, laid ambush at a choke point, surprised them, and captured or killed them all.
entries.literal: When Tian arrived he secretly learned the raiders were coming, set ambush at a critical point, took them by surprise, and captured or killed them all.

entries.zh: 元嘉十二年，遷督魯、東平、濟北三郡軍事、泰山太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia (435) he was put in charge of military affairs in Lu, Dongping, and Jibei and made administrator of Taishan, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to supervise military affairs in the three commanderies of Lu, Dongping, and Jibei, and Administrator of Taishan, his general's rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 惠威兼著，吏民便之。
entries.en: His kindness and authority were both evident, and officials and people prospered under him.
entries.literal: His kindness and authority were both manifest; officials and people found him a benefit.

entries.zh: 臨川王義慶鎮江陵，為平西中兵參軍、河東太守。
entries.en: When Prince of Linchuan Liu Yiqing held Jiangling, Tian served as central army aide on the pacify-the-west staff and administrator of Hedong.
entries.literal: When Prince of Linchuan Yiqing garrisoned Jiangling, Tian served as Central Army Aide on the Pacify-the-West staff and Administrator of Hedong.

entries.zh: 衡陽王義季代義慶，又度安西府，加寧朔將軍。
entries.en: When Prince of Hengyang Liu Yiji replaced Yiqing, Tian was transferred to the pacify-the-west headquarters and made General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: When Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, Tian was again transferred to the Pacify-the-West headquarters and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 召拜太子屯騎校尉，母憂去職。
entries.en: He was summoned as colonel of the heir's garrison cavalry, then left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Heir's Garrison Cavalry, then left office for his mother's mourning.

entries.zh: 北虜入寇，恬摧擊之，為虜所破，被徴還都。
entries.en: When the northern barbarians invaded, Tian struck at them but was defeated and recalled to the capital.
entries.literal: When the northern barbarians invaded, Tian attacked and crushed them but was defeated by the enemy and was summoned back to the capital.

entries.zh: 二十七年，起為通直常侍。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year (450) he was recalled as regular attendant for direct communication.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was recalled to serve as Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.

entries.zh: 是歲，索虜南寇，其武昌王向青州。
entries.en: That year the Northern Wei invaded south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.
entries.literal: That year the Northern Wei invaded south; their Prince of Wuchang advanced on Qing Province.

entries.zh: 遣恬援東陽，因與輔國司馬、齊郡太守龐秀之保城固守。
entries.en: Tian was sent to relieve Dongyang and, with chief of staff Pang Xiuzhi of the state-supporting army and administrator of Qi commandery, held the city in a resolute defense.
entries.literal: Tian was sent to aid Dongyang and, with the State-Supporting Army's Chief of Staff and Administrator of Qi commandery Pang Xiuzhi, held the city in a firm defense.

entries.zh: 蕭斌遣青州別駕解榮之率垣護之還援恬等，仍傍南山得入。
entries.en: Xiao Bin sent Qing provincial attendant Xie Rongzhi with Yuan Huzhi to relieve Tian and the others; they entered along the southern hills.
entries.literal: Xiao Bin sent Qing Provincial Attendant Xie Rongzhi leading Yuan Huzhi back to aid Tian and the others; they entered by way of the southern hills.

entries.zh: 賊朝來脅城，日晚輒退。
entries.en: The enemy came each morning to threaten the city and withdrew each evening.
entries.literal: The enemy came each morning to threaten the city and withdrew each evening.

entries.zh: 城內乃出車北門外，環塹為營，欲挑戰，賊不敢逼。
entries.en: The defenders then sent chariots out the north gate, ringed the moat with camps, and offered battle; the enemy did not dare close in.
entries.literal: Those inside then sent chariots out the north gate, ringed the moat with camps, and sought battle; the enemy did not dare press close.

entries.zh: 停五日，東過抄略清河郡及驛道南數千家，從東安、東莞出下邳。
entries.en: After five days they moved east, raiding Qinghe commandery and thousands of households south of the post road, then passed through Dong'an and Dongguan toward Xiapi.
entries.literal: After five days' halt they passed east, raiding Qinghe commandery and several thousand households south of the post road, and left through Dong'an and Dongguan for Xiapi.

entries.zh: 下邳太守垣閬閉城距守，保全二千餘家。
entries.en: Xiapi administrator Yuan Lang shut the city and held out, saving more than two thousand households.
entries.literal: Xiapi Administrator Yuan Lang closed the city and resisted, preserving more than two thousand households.

entries.zh: 虜退，以恬為寧朔將軍、山陽太守。
entries.en: When the invaders withdrew, Tian was made General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Shanyang.
entries.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, Tian was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Shanyang.

entries.zh: 善於治民，所蒞有績。
entries.en: Skilled at governing the people, he achieved results in every office he held.
entries.literal: Skilled in governing the people, he achieved results in every post.

entries.zh: 世祖踐阼，遷青州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Tian was transferred to inspector of Qing Province, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: When the Heir ascended the throne, Tian was transferred to Inspector of Qing Province, his general's rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋加督徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事。
entries.en: Soon he was also put in charge of military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an of Xu Province.
entries.literal: Soon he was also given supervision of military affairs in the two Xu commanderies of Dongguan and Dong'an.

entries.zh: 明年，又督冀州。
entries.en: The next year he was also put in charge of Jizhou.
entries.literal: The following year he was also given supervision of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 齊地連歲興兵，百姓凋弊，恬初防衛邊境，勸課農桑，二三年間，遂皆優實。
entries.en: Qi had suffered years of war and the people were exhausted; when Tian first took up frontier defense he promoted farming and sericulture, and within two or three years the region prospered again.
entries.literal: Qi territory had seen war year after year and the people were depleted; when Tian first defended the frontier he urged agriculture and sericulture, and within two or three years all became prosperous and secure.

entries.zh: 性清約，頻處州郡，妻子不免饑寒，世以此稱之。
entries.en: By nature he was austere; though he often held high provincial office, his wife and children still knew hunger and cold—and the age praised him for it.
entries.literal: By nature he was austere and frugal; though he often held provincial posts, his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold—the age praised him for this.

entries.zh: 進號輔國將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to General Who Supports the State.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Supports the State.

entries.zh: 謨子元嗣，海陵、廣陵太守。
entries.en: Mo's son Yuansi served as administrator of Hailing and Guangling.
entries.literal: Mo's son Yuansi was Administrator of Hailing and Guangling.

entries.zh: 元嗣弟謙，太始初，以軍功歷軍校，官至輔國將軍、臨川內史。
entries.en: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the start of Taishi, rose through military ranks for merit to General Who Supports the State and interior administrator of Linchuan.
entries.literal: Yuansi's younger brother Qian, at the beginning of Taishi, for military merit rose through army commands to General Who Supports the State and Interior Administrator of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 永子坦，自巴西、梓潼遷梁、南秦二州刺史。
entries.en: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to inspector of Liang and Nanqin.
entries.literal: Yong's son Tan was transferred from Baxi and Zitong to Inspector of Liang and Nanqin provinces.

entries.zh: 元嘉二十六年，為世祖鎮軍諮議參軍，與王玄謨圍滑臺不克，免官。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia (449) he was consulting aide on the heir's pacification army staff; he joined Wang Xuanmo in besieging Huatai without success and was dismissed.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was consulting aide on the Pacification Army staff under the Heir; with Wang Xuanmo he besieged Huatai without success and was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 青州刺史蕭斌板行建威將軍、濟南、平原二郡太守，復攻確磝，敗退，下歷城。
entries.en: Qing inspector Xiao Bin appointed him acting General Who Establishes Prestige and administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan; he attacked Que'ao again, was routed, and withdrew to Licheng.
entries.literal: Qing Inspector Xiao Bin appointed him acting General Who Establishes Prestige and Administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan; he again attacked Que'ao, was defeated and withdrew, and went down to Licheng.

entries.zh: 蕭思話起義討元兇，假坦輔國將軍，為前鋒。
entries.en: When Xiao Sihua rose to punish the usurper, Tan was provisionally made General Who Supports the State and led the vanguard.
entries.literal: When Xiao Sihua raised forces to punish the usurper, Tan was provisionally made General Who Supports the State and served as vanguard.

entries.zh: 世祖至新亭，坦亦進克京城。
entries.en: When the heir reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital.
entries.literal: When the Heir reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured the capital.

entries.zh: 孝建初，為太子右衛率，寧朔將軍、徐州刺史。
entries.en: At the start of Xiaojian he was right commandant of the heir's guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was Right Commandant of the Heir's Guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 大明元年，虜寇兗州，世祖遣太子衛率薛安都、新除東陽太守沈法系北討，至兗州，虜已去。
entries.en: In the first year of Daming (457) the barbarians raided Yanzhou; Emperor Xiaowu sent Xue Andu, commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and the newly appointed Dongyang administrator Shen Faxing north; by the time they reached Yanzhou the enemy was gone.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daming the barbarians raided Yanzhou; Emperor Xiaowu sent Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard Xue Andu and the newly appointed Administrator of Dongyang Shen Faxing north to attack; when they reached Yanzhou the enemy had already gone.

entries.zh: 坦建議：「任榛亡命，屢犯邊民，軍出無功，宜因此翦撲。」
entries.en: Tan proposed: "The Renzhen outlaws have repeatedly raided the border; the campaign achieved nothing—we should use this chance to wipe them out."
entries.literal: Tan proposed: "The outlaws of Renzhen have repeatedly harmed border people; the campaign achieved nothing—we should use this opportunity to destroy them."

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The Emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Emperor followed this.

entries.zh: 亡命先已聞知，舉村逃走，安都與法系坐白衣領職，坦棄市。
entries.en: The outlaws had already heard and whole villages fled; Andu and Faxing were demoted to commoners while retaining office, and Tan was executed in the marketplace.
entries.literal: The outlaws had already heard and whole villages fled; Andu and Faxing were reduced to commoners retaining office, and Tan was executed in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 群臣為之請，莫能得。
entries.en: Ministers pleaded for him in vain.
entries.literal: The ministers pleaded for him but could not prevail.

entries.zh: 將行刑，始興公沈慶之入市抱坦慟哭曰：「卿無罪，為朝廷所枉誅，我入市亦當不久。」
entries.en: As execution neared, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the market, embraced Tan, and wept: "You are innocent, wrongly killed by the court—I too shall soon enter this market."
entries.literal: As execution was about to take place, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi entered the market, embraced Tan, and wept aloud: "You are guiltless, wrongly killed by the court—I too shall enter the market before long."

entries.zh: 市官以白上，乃原生命，繫尚方。
entries.en: The market official reported this to the emperor, who spared Tan's life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshops.
entries.literal: The market official reported this to the Emperor, who then spared his life and imprisoned him in the Imperial Workshops.

entries.zh: 尋被宥，復為驍騎將軍，病卒。
entries.en: Soon pardoned, he was restored as General of Valiant Cavalry and died of illness.
entries.literal: Soon he was pardoned, restored as General of Valiant Cavalry, and died of illness.

entries.zh: 子令孫，前廢帝景和中，為永嘉王子仁左軍司馬、廣陵太守。
entries.en: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the Former Deposed Emperor, was chief of staff to the left army under Prince of Yongjia Liu Ziren and administrator of Guangling.
entries.literal: His son Lingsun, in the Jinghe era under the Former Deposed Emperor, was Chief of Staff to the Left Army under Prince of Yongjia Ziren and Administrator of Guangling.

entries.zh: 太宗以為寧朔將軍、徐州刺史，討薛安都。
entries.en: Emperor Ming made him General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Xuzhou to campaign against Xue Andu.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming made him General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou to campaign against Xue Andu.

entries.zh: 行至淮陽，即與安都合。
entries.en: When he reached Huaiyang he immediately joined Andu.
entries.literal: When he reached Huaiyang he at once joined Andu.

entries.zh: 弟闡，時為濟陰太守，戍睢陵城，奉順不同安都，安都攻圍不能克。
entries.en: His younger brother Chan, then administrator of Jiyin, held Suiling city, remained loyal and refused to join Andu, and Andu could not take him by siege.
entries.literal: His younger brother Chan was then Administrator of Jiyin, garrisoning Suiling city; he remained loyal and would not follow Andu, and Andu besieged him without success.

entries.zh: 會令孫至，遣往睢陵令說闡降，闡既降，殺之，令孫亦見殺。
entries.en: When Lingsun arrived he sent envoys to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan surrendered he killed him, and Lingsun was killed as well.
entries.literal: When Lingsun arrived he sent someone to Suiling to persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan surrendered he killed him, and Lingsun was also killed.

entries.zh: 先是，清河崔諲亦以將吏見知高祖，永初末，為振威將軍、東萊太守。
entries.en: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe had also been known to the Founding Emperor as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Quells Martial Prestige and administrator of Donglai.
entries.literal: Earlier, Cui Yin of Qinghe was also known to the Founding Emperor as a military officer; at the end of Yongchu he was General Who Quells Martial Prestige and Administrator of Donglai.

entries.zh: 少帝初，亡命司馬靈期、司馬順之千餘人圍東萊，諲擊之，斬靈期等三十級。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Shao's reign, over a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and beheaded Lingqi and thirty others.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Short-Reigned Emperor's reign, more than a thousand outlaws under Sima Lingqi and Sima Shunzhi besieged Donglai; Yin attacked them and beheaded Lingqi and thirty others.

entries.zh: 太祖元嘉中，至青州刺史。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era he rose to inspector of Qing Province.
entries.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen he rose to Inspector of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 列傳第二十五 吉翰 劉道產 杜驥 申恬
entries.en: Biography 25 — Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, and Shen Tian
entries.literal: Biography 25: Ji Han, Liu Daochan, Du Ji, Shen Tian

entries.zh: 王敬弘，琅邪臨沂人也。
entries.en: Wang Jinghong was a native of Linyi in Langye.
entries.literal: Wang Jinghong was a man of Linyi in Langye.

entries.zh: 與高祖諱同，故稱字。
entries.en: His given name matched the founding emperor's taboo name, so people called him by his courtesy name instead.
entries.literal: His personal name was the same as the founding emperor's taboo name, so he was addressed by his courtesy name.

entries.zh: 曾祖廙，晉驃騎將軍。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Yi had served as Jin General of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was Jin General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 祖胡之，司州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Huzhi had been Inspector of Sizhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Huzhi was Inspector of Sizhou.

entries.zh: 父茂之，晉陵太守。
entries.en: His father Maozhi had been Administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: His father Maozhi was Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 高祖以為車騎從事中郎，徐州治中從事史，征西將軍道規諮議參軍。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu made him Attendant Gentleman of the Household Cavalry, Registrar of Xuzhou, and Advisory Army Aide on the staff of Liu Daogui, General Who Conquers the West.
entries.literal: The founding emperor appointed him Attendant Gentleman of the Household Cavalry, Registrar of Xuzhou, and Advisory Army Aide to the General Who Conquers the West, Liu Daogui.

entries.zh: 時府主簿宗協亦有高趣，道規並以事外相期。
entries.en: The headquarters registrar Zong Xie was likewise a man of refined tastes, and Daogui counted on both men for companionship outside the duties of office.
entries.literal: At the time the headquarters Registrar Zong Xie also had lofty tastes; Daogui counted on both men alike for companionship beyond official business.

entries.zh: 嘗共酣飲致醉，敬弘因醉失禮，為外司所白，道規即更引還，重申初讌。
entries.en: Once they drank together until drunk. Jinghong offended through drink and was reported by the supervisory office, but Daogui immediately had him brought back and held the feast again as before.
entries.literal: They once drank together until drunk; Jinghong through drunkenness breached etiquette and was reported by the external office. Daogui at once summoned him back and renewed the original banquet.

entries.zh: 召為中書侍郎，始攜家累自作唐還京邑。
entries.en: Summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, he brought his family for the first time from Zuotang back to the capital.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and for the first time brought his household dependents from Zuotang back to the capital.

entries.zh: 久之，轉黃門侍郎，不拜。
entries.en: After a time he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, but he declined the post.
entries.literal: After some time he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate but did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 仍除太尉從事中郎，出為吳興太守。
entries.en: He was next appointed Attendant of the Grand Marshal and then sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: He was then appointed Attendant of the Grand Marshal and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 舊居餘杭縣，悅是舉也。
entries.en: He had long lived in Yuhang County and was delighted with the appointment.
entries.literal: He had formerly lived in Yuhang County and was pleased with this appointment.

entries.zh: 尋徵為侍中。
entries.en: Before long he was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 高祖西討司馬休之，敬弘奉使慰勞，通事令史潘尚於道疾病，敬弘單船送還都，存亡不測，有司奏免官，詔可。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi, Jinghong was sent to comfort the army. Communications clerk Pan Shang fell ill on the road, and Jinghong sent him back to the capital alone by boat, with no certainty he would live. The authorities memorialized for Jinghong's dismissal, and the emperor approved.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Jinghong was sent on a mission to comfort the troops. The Communications Clerk Pan Shang fell ill on the road; Jinghong sent him back to the capital in a boat alone, his survival uncertain. The relevant offices memorialized to dismiss Jinghong from office, and the edict approved.

entries.zh: 未及釋朝服，值赦復官。
entries.en: He had not yet removed his court robes when an amnesty restored him to office.
entries.literal: Before he had laid aside court dress, an amnesty came and he was restored to office.

entries.zh: 宋國初建，為度支尚書，遷太常。
entries.en: When the Song state was first established, he became Minister of Revenue and was then promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: When the Song state was first established, he became Minister of Revenue and was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，補宣訓衛尉，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Jinghong was appointed Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor received the Mandate, Jinghong was appointed Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard and given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 永初三年，轉吏部尚書，常侍如故。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service while keeping his post as regular attendant.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service, retaining his regular attendant title as before.

entries.zh: 敬弘每被除召，即便祗奉，既到宜退，旋復解官，高祖嘉其志，不苟違也。
entries.en: Whenever Jinghong was appointed he dutifully accepted, but once he had taken up the post he thought it time to withdraw and soon resigned again. Emperor Gaozu admired this resolve and did not press him.
entries.literal: Whenever Jinghong was appointed and summoned, he at once reverently accepted; once he had arrived it was fitting to withdraw, and he would promptly resign. The founding emperor praised his intent and did not lightly go against it.

entries.zh: 復除廬陵王師，加散騎常侍，自陳無德，不可師範令王，固讓不拜。
entries.en: He was again made Tutor to the Prince of Luling with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, but he declared himself without virtue and unfit to instruct a prince, firmly declined, and refused the appointment.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Tutor to the Prince of Luling with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry. He declared himself without virtue and unfit to instruct and model the prince, firmly declined, and did not accept.

entries.zh: 又除祕書監，金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，本州中正，又不就。
entries.en: He was next appointed Director of the Secretariat and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Chief Rectifier of his native province, but again he did not accept.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Director of the Secretariat, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and as Chief Rectifier of his native province, but again he did not take office.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，又以為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，領江夏王師。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu came to the throne, Jinghong was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: When Emperor Taizu ascended the throne, Jinghong was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 尚之少時頗輕薄，好摴蒲，既長折節蹈道，以操立見稱。
entries.en: In youth Shangzhi was rather frivolous and fond of dice games, but once grown he restrained himself and followed the Way and was praised for his established conduct.
entries.literal: In youth Shangzhi was rather frivolous and fond of dice games; once grown he restrained himself and followed the Way, and was praised for his established conduct.

entries.zh: 為陳郡謝混所知，與之遊處。
entries.en: He was recognized by Xie Hun of Chen Commandery and became his companion.
entries.literal: He was recognized by Xie Hun of Chen Commandery and associated with him in friendship.

entries.zh: 家貧，起為臨津令。
entries.en: His family was poor, and he began his career as Magistrate of Linjin.
entries.literal: His family was poor; he began his career as Magistrate of Linjin.

entries.zh: 高祖領征西將軍，補府主簿。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu held the post of General Who Conquers the West, Shangzhi was appointed Headquarters Registrar on his staff.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor held the post of General Who Conquers the West, Shangzhi was appointed Headquarters Registrar on his staff.

entries.zh: 從征長安，以公事免，還都。
entries.en: He followed the campaign to Chang'an, was dismissed for an official matter, and returned to the capital.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign to Chang'an, was dismissed for an official matter, and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 因患勞疾積年，飲婦人乳，乃得差。
entries.en: He suffered from chronic consumptive illness for years and recovered only after drinking women's milk.
entries.literal: He suffered from chronic consumptive illness for years and drank women's milk before he recovered.

entries.zh: 以從征之勞，賜爵都鄉侯。
entries.en: For his service on the campaign he was granted the title Marquis of Duxiang.
entries.literal: For his service on the campaign he was granted the title Marquis of Duxiang.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，為廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Shaodi came to the throne, Shangzhi became Advisory Army Aide to the Prince of Luling, Yizhen, General of Chariots and Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shaodi ascended the throne, Shangzhi became Advisory Army Aide on the Household Cavalry staff of the Prince of Luling, Yizhen.

entries.zh: 義真與司徒徐羨之、尚書令傅亮等不協，每有不平之言，尚之諫戒，不納。
entries.en: Yizhen was at odds with Minister of Education Xu Xianzhi, Director Fu Liang, and others and often spoke resentfully. Shangzhi admonished him, but he would not listen.
entries.literal: Yizhen was at odds with the Minister of Education Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Fu Liang, and others, and often spoke resentfully. Shangzhi admonished him, but he would not listen.

entries.zh: 義真被廢，入為中書侍郎。
entries.en: After Yizhen was deposed, Shangzhi entered office as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Yizhen was deposed, Shangzhi entered office as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，出為臨川內史，入為黃門侍郎，尚書吏部郎，左衛將軍，父憂去職。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu came to the throne, Shangzhi was sent out as Interior Secretary of Linchuan, then served as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Director of Personnel, and General of the Left Guard before leaving office on his father's death.
entries.literal: When Emperor Taizu ascended the throne, Shangzhi was sent out as Interior Secretary of Linchuan, then entered office as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Director of Personnel in the Imperial Secretariat, and General of the Left Guard; he left office on his father's death.

entries.zh: 服闋，復為左衛，領太子中庶子。
entries.en: When mourning was complete, he again became General of the Left Guard and concurrently Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When mourning was complete, he again became General of the Left Guard and concurrently Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 尚之雅好文義，從容賞會，甚為太祖所知。
entries.en: Shangzhi loved literature and, in easy leisure, joined appreciative gatherings; Emperor Taizu knew him well.
entries.literal: Shangzhi by nature loved literary meaning and, in easy leisure, joined in appreciative gatherings; he was greatly known to Emperor Taizu.

entries.zh: 十二年，遷侍中，中庶子如故。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Palace Attendant while retaining his post as Senior Tutor.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Palace Attendant, retaining his post as Senior Tutor as before.

entries.zh: 尋改領游擊將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was changed to command the Mobile Strike General.
entries.literal: Soon he was changed to command the Mobile Strike General.

entries.zh: 尚之既還任事，上待之愈隆。
entries.en: Once Shangzhi had returned to his duties, the emperor treated him with ever greater favor.
entries.literal: Once Shangzhi had returned to his duties, the emperor treated him with ever greater favor.

entries.zh: 是時復遣軍北伐，資給戎旅，悉以委之。
entries.en: At this time armies were again sent north on campaign, and the supply of the military forces was entirely entrusted to him.
entries.literal: At this time armies were again sent north on campaign, and the supply of the military forces was entirely entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 元凶弒立，進位司空，領尚書令。
entries.en: When the Original Culprit usurped the throne by regicide, Shangzhi was promoted to Minister of Works and made Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: When the Original Culprit usurped the throne by regicide, Shangzhi was promoted to Minister of Works and made Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 時三方興義，將佐家在都邑，劭悉欲誅之，尚之誘說百端，並得免。
entries.en: At the time righteous armies rose in the three directions; the generals and aides had families in the capital, and Shao wished to execute them all. Shangzhi persuaded him by every argument, and all were spared.
entries.literal: At the time righteous armies rose in the three directions; the generals and aides had families in the capital, and Shao wished to execute them all. Shangzhi persuaded him by every argument, and all were spared.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，復為尚書令，領吏部，遷侍中、左光祿大夫，領護軍將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, Shangzhi again became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, oversaw the Ministry of the Civil Service, was promoted to Palace Attendant and Left Grand Master of the Palace, and commanded the General of the Guard Army.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, Shangzhi again became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, oversaw the Ministry of the Civil Service, was promoted to Palace Attendant and Left Grand Master of the Palace, and commanded the General of the Guard Army.

entries.zh: 尋辭護軍，加特進。
entries.en: Soon he resigned the Guard Army command and was given Special Advancement.
entries.literal: Soon he resigned the Guard Army command and was given Special Advancement.

entries.zh: 復以本官領尚書令。
entries.en: He again held his former office and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: He again held his former office and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 丞相南郡王義宣、車騎將軍臧質反，義宣司馬竺超民、臧質長史陸展兄弟並應從誅，尚之上言曰：「刑罰得失，治亂所由，聖賢留心，不可不慎。
entries.en: The Chancellor, Prince of Nan Commandery Yixuan, and Zang Zhi, General of the Household Cavalry, rebelled. Yixuan's Chief Clerk Zhu Chaomin and Zhi's Chief Clerk Lu Zhan and his brothers were all to be executed with the rebels. Shangzhi submitted a memorial: "The gain and loss of punishments are the source of order and chaos; sages attend to them and one cannot be inattentive.
entries.literal: The Chancellor, Prince of Nan Commandery Yixuan, and Zang Zhi, General of the Household Cavalry, rebelled. Yixuan's Chief Clerk Zhu Chaomin and Zhi's Chief Clerk Lu Zhan and his brothers were all to be executed with the rebels. Shangzhi submitted a memorial saying, "The gain and loss of punishments are the source of order and chaos; sages and worthies attend to them and one cannot be inattentive.

entries.zh: 竺超民為義宣司馬，賊既遁走，一夫可禽，若反覆昧利，即當取之，非唯免愆，亦可要不義之賞，而超民曾無此意，微足觀過知仁。
entries.en: Zhu Chaomin was Yixuan's Chief Clerk. Once the rebels had fled, a single man could have been captured; if one turned back for hidden profit, he should have been taken—not only to escape fault but also to demand an unrighteous reward. Yet Chaomin never had this intent, which is slightly enough to observe fault and know benevolence.
entries.literal: Zhu Chaomin was Yixuan's Chief Clerk. Once the rebels had fled, a single man could have been captured; if one turned back for hidden profit, he should have been taken—not only to escape fault but also to demand an unrighteous reward. Yet Chaomin never had this intent, which is slightly enough to observe fault and know benevolence.

entries.zh: 且為官保全城府，謹守庫藏，端坐待縛。
entries.en: Moreover, as an official he preserved the city walls and moat, carefully guarded the storehouses, and sat upright awaiting arrest.
entries.literal: Moreover, as an official he preserved the city walls and moat, carefully guarded the storehouses, and sat upright awaiting binding.

entries.zh: 今戮及兄弟，與向始末無論者復成何異。
entries.en: Now to execute him together with his brothers—how would that differ from punishing those who had nothing to do with the affair from start to finish?
entries.literal: Now to execute him together with his brothers—how would that differ from those whose beginning and end had nothing to do with the affair?

entries.zh: 陸展盡質復灼然，便同之巨逆，於事為重。
entries.en: Lu Zhan's devotion to Zhi was again clearly shown; to treat him the same as the great traitors is, in the matter, grave.
entries.literal: Lu Zhan's devotion to Zhi was again clearly shown; to treat him the same as the great traitors is, in the matter, grave.

entries.zh: 臣豫蒙顧待，自殊凡隸，苟有所懷，不敢自默。」
entries.en: I have received favored treatment and am unlike ordinary subordinates; if I have something in mind, I dare not keep silent."
entries.literal: I have beforehand received favored treatment and am unlike ordinary subordinates; if I have something in mind, I dare not keep silent."

entries.zh: 超民坐者由此得原。
entries.en: Those implicated with Chaomin were thereby pardoned.
entries.literal: Those implicated with Chaomin were thereby pardoned.

entries.zh: 時欲分荊州置郢州，議其所居。
entries.en: At the time they wished to divide Jingzhou and establish Yingzhou, and debated where its seat should be.
entries.literal: At the time they wished to divide Jingzhou and establish Yingzhou, and debated where its seat should be.

entries.zh: 江夏王義恭以為宜在巴陵，尚之議曰：「夏口在荊、江之中，正對沔口，通接雍、梁，實為津要，由來舊鎮，根基不易。
entries.en: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, held that it should be at Baling. Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangtze, directly facing the mouth of the Han, connecting with Yong and Liang—it is truly a strategic crossing. It has long been an old garrison and its foundations are not easily changed.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, held that it should be at Baling. Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangtze, directly facing the mouth of the Han, connecting with Yong and Liang—it is truly a strategic crossing. It has long been an old garrison and its foundations are not easily changed.

entries.zh: 今分取江夏、武陵、天門、竟陵、隨五郡為一州，鎮在夏口，既有見城，浦大容舫。
