entries.en: Now take Jiangxia, Wuling, Tianmen, Jingling, and Sui—five commanderies—as one province, with the garrison at Xiakou. There is already an existing city, and the harbor is large enough to hold ships.
entries.literal: Now take Jiangxia, Wuling, Tianmen, Jingling, and Sui—five commanderies—as one province, with the garrison at Xiakou. There is already an existing city, and the harbor is large enough to hold ships.

entries.zh: 竟陵出道取荊州，雖水路，與去江夏不異，諸郡至夏口皆從流，並為利便。
entries.en: From Jingling the route out to Jingzhou, though by water, differs little from going to Jiangxia; all commanderies reaching Xiakou follow the current, and all is convenient.
entries.literal: From Jingling the route out to Jingzhou, though by water, differs little from going to Jiangxia; all commanderies reaching Xiakou follow the current, and all is convenient.

entries.zh: 湘州所領十一郡，其巴陵邊帶長江，去夏口密邇，既分湘中，乃更成大，亦可割巴陵屬新州，於事為允。」
entries.en: The eleven commanderies under Xiangzhou include Baling along the Yangtze, close to Xiakou. Since central Xiang has been divided, it has become even larger; Baling may also be cut off to belong to the new province, which would be fitting."
entries.literal: The eleven commanderies under Xiangzhou include Baling along the Yangtze, close to Xiakou. Since central Xiang has been divided, it has become even larger; Baling may also be cut off to belong to the new province, which in the affair is fitting."

entries.zh: 上從其議。
entries.en: The emperor followed his view.
entries.literal: The emperor followed his view.

entries.zh: 荊、揚二州，戶口半天下，江左以來，揚州根本，委荊以閫外，至是並分，欲以削臣下之權，而荊、揚並因此虛耗。
entries.en: Jing and Yang, the two provinces, held half the empire's registered households. Since the east of the Yangtze, Yangzhou was the root and Jing was entrusted with matters beyond the gate; now both were divided to cut down the power of subjects below, and Jing and Yang were both thereby drained and weakened.
entries.literal: Jing and Yang, the two provinces, held half the empire's registered households. Since the east of the Yangtze, Yangzhou was the root and Jing was entrusted with matters beyond the gate; now both were divided to cut down the power of subjects below, and Jing and Yang were both thereby drained and weakened.

entries.zh: 尚之建言復合二州，上不許。
entries.en: Shangzhi proposed reuniting the two provinces; the emperor did not permit it.
entries.literal: Shangzhi proposed reuniting the two provinces; the emperor did not permit it.

entries.zh: 大明二年，以為左光祿、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。
entries.en: In the second year of Daming he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daming he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, retaining his post as Palace Attendant as before.

entries.zh: 尚之在家常著鹿皮帽，及拜開府，天子臨軒，百僚陪位，沈慶之於殿廷戲之曰：「今日何不著鹿皮冠？」
entries.en: At home Shangzhi often wore a deerskin cap. When he was invested with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, the Son of Heaven came to the hall and all officials attended. Shen Qingzhi jested in the court hall, "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?"
entries.literal: At home Shangzhi often wore a deerskin cap. When he was invested with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, the Son of Heaven came to the hall and all officials attended in place. Shen Qingzhi jested in the court hall, "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?"

entries.zh: 慶之累辭爵命，朝廷敦勸甚篤，尚之謂曰：「主上虛懷側席，詎宜固辭。」
entries.en: Qingzhi repeatedly declined ennoblement; the court earnestly urged him with great sincerity. Shangzhi said to him, "The sovereign opens his mind and keeps a seat at his side—how could you firmly decline?"
entries.literal: Qingzhi repeatedly declined ennoblement; the court earnestly urged him with great sincerity. Shangzhi said to him, "The sovereign empties his mind and sits sidewise—how could you firmly decline?"

entries.zh: 慶之曰：「沈公不効何公，去而復還也。」
entries.en: Qingzhi said, "Master Shen does not imitate Master He—going away and coming back again."
entries.literal: Qingzhi said, "Master Shen does not imitate Master He—going away and coming back again."

entries.zh: 尚之有愧色。
entries.en: Shangzhi showed a look of shame.
entries.literal: Shangzhi showed a look of shame.

entries.zh: 愛尚文義，老而不休，與太常顏延之論議往反，傳於世。
entries.en: He loved literature and, old though he was, did not cease. With Yan Yanzhi, Minister of Ceremonies, he debated back and forth, and their exchanges were transmitted in the world.
entries.literal: He loved and honored literary meaning and, old though he was, did not cease. With Yan Yanzhi, Minister of Ceremonies, he debated back and forth, and this was transmitted in the world.

entries.zh: 立身簡約，車服率素，妻亡不娶，又無姬妾。
entries.en: In personal conduct he was simple and restrained; carriages and dress were generally plain. When his wife died he did not remarry, nor did he keep concubines.
entries.literal: In personal conduct he was simple and restrained; carriages and dress were generally plain. When his wife died he did not remarry, nor did he keep concubines.

entries.zh: 秉衡當朝，畏遠權柄，親戚故舊，一無薦舉，既以致怨，亦以此見稱。
entries.en: Holding high office in the court, he feared and kept distant from power; among kin and old friends he made not a single recommendation. This both brought resentment and won him praise.
entries.literal: Holding the scales of office in the court, he feared and kept distant from power; among kin and old friends he made not a single recommendation. This both brought resentment and won him praise.

entries.zh: 復以本官領中書令。
entries.en: He again held his former office and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He again held his former office and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 四年，疾篤，詔遣侍中沈懷文、黃門侍郎王釗問疾。
entries.en: In the fourth year his illness grew grave; an edict sent Palace Attendant Shen Huaiwen and Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Wang Zhao to inquire after his health.
entries.literal: In the fourth year his illness grew grave; an edict sent Palace Attendant Shen Huaiwen and Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Wang Zhao to inquire after his health.

entries.zh: 薨于位，時年七十九。
entries.en: He died in office at the age of seventy-nine.
entries.literal: He died in office at the age of seventy-nine.

entries.zh: 追贈司空，侍中、中書令如故。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat as before.

entries.zh: 諡曰簡穆公。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Duke Jian Mu.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Jian Mu.

entries.zh: 子偃，別有傳。
entries.en: His son Yan has a separate biography.
entries.literal: His son Yan has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 湛出繼伯父淡，襲封安眾縣五等男。
entries.en: Zhan was adopted out to his uncle Liu Dan, written 淡, and succeeded to the fifth-grade marquisate of Anzhong County.
entries.literal: Zhan was given in adoption to his uncle Liu Dan, written 淡, and inherited enfeoffment as fifth-grade Marquis of Anzhong County.

entries.zh: 少有局力，不尚浮華。
entries.en: From youth he showed breadth of mind and force of character, and he did not care for flashy display.
entries.literal: In youth he had breadth and force, and did not esteem flashy display.

entries.zh: 博涉史傳，諳前世舊典，弱年便有宰世情，常自比管夷吾、諸葛亮，不為文章，不喜談議。
entries.en: He read widely in histories and chronicles and knew the statutes of earlier ages by heart; even in his youth he harbored ambitions to govern the realm and often likened himself to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang. He did not write belles lettres and disliked idle talk.
entries.literal: He broadly traversed histories and traditions, was versed in former-age old statutes, in weak years already had the sentiment of ruling the age, often compared himself to Guan Yiwu and Zhuge Liang, did not compose literary pieces, and did not enjoy talk and discussion.

entries.zh: 本州辟主簿，不就。
entries.en: When the province summoned him as Registrar, he declined the post.
entries.literal: The province summoned him as Registrar, and he did not accept.

entries.zh: 除著作佐郎，又不拜。
entries.en: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library but again refused to take office.
entries.literal: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library, and again did not accept the seal.

entries.zh: 高祖以為太尉行參軍，賞遇甚厚。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Acting Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and treated him with exceptional favor.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu made him Acting Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant, and rewarded and treated him very generously.

entries.zh: 高祖領鎮西將軍、荊州刺史，以湛為功曹，仍補治中別駕從事史，復為太尉參軍，世子征虜西中郎主簿。
entries.en: When Gaozu served as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jing Province, he appointed Zhan Merit Officer, then Headquarters Attending Clerk and Separate-Chariot Attending Clerk. Zhan later served again as Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and as Registrar to the heir apparent in his commands as General Who Conquers the Caitiffs and Western Center-Rank Commandant.
entries.literal: When Gaozu held the posts of General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jing Province, he made Zhan Merit Officer, then appointed him Headquarters Attending Clerk and Separate-Chariot Attending Clerk. Zhan later again served as Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and as Registrar to the heir apparent in his commands as General Who Conquers the Caitiffs and Western Center-Rank Commandant.

entries.zh: 父柳亡於江州，州府送故甚豐，一無所受，時論稱之。
entries.en: When his father Liu, written 柳, died in Jiang Province, the provincial and prefectural offices sent lavish funeral gifts, but he accepted none of them, and contemporaries praised him for it.
entries.literal: When his father Liu, written 柳, died in Jiang Province, the province and prefecture sent funeral goods in great abundance, and he accepted none of it; opinion of the time praised this.

entries.zh: 服終，除秘書丞，出為相國參軍。
entries.en: After his mourning period ended, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Library and then sent out as Staff Officer to the Chancellor of State.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Palace Library Assistant and went out as Staff Officer to the Chancellor of State.

entries.zh: 謝晦、王弘並稱其有器幹。
entries.en: Both Xie Hui and Wang Hong praised him for his talent and force of character.
entries.literal: Xie Hui and Wang Hong both praised him as having capacity and backbone.

entries.zh: 高祖入受晉命，以第四子義康為冠軍將軍、豫州刺史，留鎮壽陽。
entries.en: After Gaozu accepted the Jin mandate and took the throne, he appointed his fourth son Yikang General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Yu Province and left him to garrison Shouyang.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered and received the Jin mandate, he made his fourth son Yikang General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Yu Province, leaving him to garrison Shouyang.

entries.zh: 以湛為長史、梁郡太守。
entries.en: He appointed Zhan Chief Clerk and Grand Administrator of Liang Commandery.
entries.literal: He made Zhan Chief Clerk and Grand Administrator of Liang Commandery.

entries.zh: 義康弱年未親政，府州軍事悉委湛。
entries.en: Yikang was still young and did not administer affairs himself; Zhan was entrusted with all military affairs of the prefecture and province.
entries.literal: Yikang was young and had not personally taken government; all military affairs of the prefecture and province were entrusted to Zhan.

entries.zh: 府進號右將軍，仍隨府轉。
entries.en: When the headquarters was promoted to General of the Right, Zhan transferred with it as before.
entries.literal: The headquarters advanced in title to General of the Right, and he still followed the headquarters in transfer.

entries.zh: 義康以本號徙為南豫州，湛改領歷陽太守。
entries.en: When Yikang was transferred to Southern Yu Province under his existing title, Zhan was reassigned to serve concurrently as Grand Administrator of Liyang.
entries.literal: Yikang was moved on his original title to Southern Yu Province, and Zhan changed to hold concurrently the Grand Administrator of Liyang.

entries.zh: 為人剛嚴用法，奸吏犯贓百錢以上，皆殺之，自下莫不震肅。
entries.en: He was stern and rigorous in enforcing the law: any corrupt official guilty of embezzling as little as a hundred cash was executed, and everyone below him was awed into discipline.
entries.literal: As a man he was stern and strict in applying the law; corrupt officials who violated bribery for a hundred cash or more were all put to death, and from below none did not tremble into order.

entries.zh: 廬陵王義真出為車騎將軍、南豫州刺史，湛又為長史，太守如故。
entries.en: When Prince of Luling Yizhen was sent out as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Southern Yu Province, Zhan again became his Chief Clerk while retaining his post as Grand Administrator.
entries.literal: Prince of Luling Yizhen went out as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Southern Yu Province; Zhan again served as Chief Clerk, Grand Administrator as before.

entries.zh: 義真時居高祖憂，使帳下備膳，湛禁之，義真乃使左右索魚肉珍羞，於齋內別立廚帳。
entries.en: Yizhen was then observing mourning for Gaozu and had his attendants prepare meals, but Zhan forbade it; Yizhen then had his men procure fish, meat, and delicacies and set up a separate kitchen tent within the mourning compound.
entries.literal: Yizhen was then in Gaozu's mourning, and had his attendants prepare meals; Zhan forbade it, so Yizhen had his attendants seek fish, meat, and delicacies and separately set up a kitchen tent within the mourning quarters.

entries.zh: 會湛入，因命臑酒炙車螯，湛正色曰：「公當今不宜有此設。」
entries.en: When Zhan came in, Yizhen ordered cured meats, wine, roast crab, and other delicacies. Zhan said sternly, "Your Highness ought not have such provisions at a time like this."
entries.literal: When Zhan entered, he thereupon ordered cured meat, wine, roast, and chariot-claw [crab]; Zhan with stern countenance said: "Your Highness at present ought not have this spread."

entries.zh: 義真曰：「旦甚寒，一碗酒亦何傷！
entries.en: Yizhen replied, "The mornings are bitterly cold—what harm can there be in a single bowl of wine?
entries.literal: Yizhen said: "The morning is very cold—what harm is one bowl of wine!

entries.zh: 長史事同一家，望不為異。」
entries.en: The Chief Clerk and I are as one household; I hope you will not take exception."
entries.literal: The Chief Clerk's affairs are the same as one family—I hope you will not regard it as strange."

entries.zh: 酒既至，湛因起曰：「既不能以禮自處，又不能以禮處人。」
entries.en: When the wine was served, Zhan rose and said, "You cannot keep ritual discipline yourself, and you cannot treat others with ritual propriety either."
entries.literal: When the wine had arrived, Zhan thereupon rose and said: "You can neither conduct yourself by ritual, nor treat others by ritual."

entries.zh: 湛負其志氣，常慕汲黯、崔琰為人，故名長子曰黯字長孺，第二子曰琰字季珪。
entries.en: Proud of his own spirit, Zhan often admired the examples of Ji An and Cui Yan; he therefore named his eldest son An, courtesy name Changru, and his second son Yan, courtesy name Jigui.
entries.literal: Zhan relied on his will and spirit, often admired Ji An and Cui Yan as men, and therefore named his eldest son An, styled Changru, and his second son Yan, styled Jigui.

entries.zh: 琰於江陵病卒，湛求自送喪還都，義恭亦為之陳請。
entries.en: When Yan died of illness at Jiangling, Zhan asked permission to escort the coffin back to the capital himself, and Yigong also petitioned on his behalf.
entries.literal: Yan died of illness at Jiangling; Zhan requested to escort the coffin himself back to the capital, and Yigong also submitted a petition on his behalf.

entries.zh: 太祖答義恭曰：「吾亦得湛啟事，為之酸懷，乃不欲苟違所請。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu replied to Yigong, "I too have received Zhan's memorial, and it pains me; I do not wish lightly to refuse his request.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizu replied to Yigong: "I too have received Zhan's memorial; I am sore at heart for him and do not wish lightly to go against what he asks.

entries.zh: 但汝弱年，新涉庶務，八州殷曠，專斷事重，疇諮委仗，不可不得其人，量算二三，未獲便相順許。
entries.en: But you are still young and have only lately taken up civil administration; the eight provinces are vast and populous, and the power to decide affairs on your own is a heavy burden. I cannot do without the right man to advise and rely upon you. I have weighed the matter again and again and cannot yet readily grant your request.
entries.literal: But you are in weak years, newly entering the multitude of affairs; the eight provinces are vast and populous, and exclusive decision on affairs is weighty—whom to consult and entrust cannot be without the right man; I have reckoned two or three times and have not yet been able readily to grant assent.

entries.zh: 今答湛啟，權停彼葬。
entries.en: In my reply to Zhan's memorial I have provisionally deferred the burial there.
entries.literal: Now in answering Zhan's memorial, I provisionally halt the burial there.

entries.zh: 頃朝臣零落相係，寄懷轉寡，湛實國器，吾乃欲引其令還，直以西夏任重，要且停此事耳。
entries.en: Court ministers have been dying off one after another, and I have fewer men in whom I can place my hopes. Zhan is truly a pillar of the state, and I had intended to recall him—but the western command is too weighty a responsibility, so for now I must put off this matter.
entries.literal: Recently court ministers have fallen away one after another, and those in whom I place my hopes grow fewer; Zhan is truly a vessel of state—I wish to summon him back, but simply because the western region's burden is heavy, for now I must halt this matter.

entries.zh: 汝慶賞黜罰，豫關失得者，必宜悉相委寄。」
entries.en: Whatever concerns rewards, promotions, dismissals, and punishments that touch upon success or failure, you must entrust entirely to him."
entries.literal: Your rewards, promotions, dismissals, and punishments that bear on gain and loss—you must wholly entrust them to him."

entries.zh: 元嘉九年冬，彭城太妃薨，將葬，祖夕，僚故並集東府。
entries.en: In the winter of the ninth year of Yuanjia, the Grand Consort of Pengcheng died. As her burial approached, officials and old associates gathered at the Eastern Residence on the evening before the funeral procession set out.
entries.literal: In the winter of the ninth year of Yuanjia, the Grand Consort of Pengcheng died; when she was about to be buried, on the evening before the funeral procession set out, officials and former associates all gathered at the Eastern Residence.

entries.zh: 曄弟廣淵，時為司徒祭酒，其日在直。
entries.en: Ye's younger brother Guangyuan was then serving as Libationer to the Minister over the Masses and was on duty that day.
entries.literal: Ye's younger brother Guangyuan was then Libationer to the Minister over the Masses, and on that day he was on duty.

entries.zh: 曄與司徒左西屬王深宿廣淵許，夜中酣飲，開北牖聽挽歌為樂。
entries.en: Ye and Wang Shen, Left Western Subordinate to the Minister over the Masses, spent the night at Guangyuan's quarters. Late that night, deep in drink, they opened the northern window and amused themselves by listening to the funeral dirges.
entries.literal: Ye and Wang Shen, Left Western Subordinate of the Minister over the Masses, lodged at Guangyuan's place; in the middle of the night they drank heavily, opened the northern window, and took pleasure in listening to the funeral dirges.

entries.zh: 義康大怒，左遷曄宣城太守。
entries.en: Yikang was furious and demoted Ye to Administrator of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: Yikang was greatly angered and demoted Ye to be Administrator of Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 不得志，乃刪眾家後漢書為一家之作。
entries.en: With his ambitions blocked, Ye then edited the various existing histories of the Later Han into a single work of his own.
entries.literal: Unable to realize his ambitions, he then edited the many schools' Books of the Later Han into the work of a single school.

entries.zh: 在郡數年，遷長沙王義欣鎮軍長史，加寧朔將軍。
entries.en: After several years in the commandery, he was transferred to serve as Chief Clerk to Yixin, Prince of Changsha and General Who Pacifies the Army, and was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: After several years in the commandery, he was transferred to be Chief Clerk to Yixin, Prince of Changsha and General Who Pacifies the Army, and was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 兄暠為宜都太守，嫡母隨暠在官。
entries.en: His elder brother Fan Gao was Administrator of Yidu, and Ye's legal mother had accompanied Gao to his post.
entries.literal: His elder brother Fan Gao was Administrator of Yidu, and Ye's legal mother accompanied Gao at his post.

entries.zh: 十六年，母亡，報之以疾，曄不時奔赴，及行，又攜妓妾自隨，為御史中丞劉損所奏，太祖愛其才，不罪也。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, she died. Her death was reported to Ye as an illness, but he did not promptly hurry to her side; when he finally set out, he even brought singing girls and concubines with him. Liu Sun, Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, impeached him, but Taizu valued his talent and did not punish him.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, his mother died; the report to him described it as illness, but Ye did not hasten there in time, and when he went, he also took singing girls and concubines along with him; Liu Sun, Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, memorialized against him, but Taizu loved his talent and did not punish him.

entries.zh: 服闋，為始興王濬後軍長史，領南下邳太守。
entries.en: After completing mourning, he became chief clerk in the Rear Army of Jun, Prince of Shixing, while concurrently serving as Administrator of Southern Xiapi.
entries.literal: When the mourning period was completed, he became Chief Clerk in the Rear Army of Jun, Prince of Shixing, and concurrently served as Administrator of Southern Xiapi.

entries.zh: 及濬為揚州，未親政事，悉以委曄。
entries.en: When Jun took charge of Yang Province, he was not yet personally managing government affairs and entrusted them all to Ye.
entries.literal: When Jun became governor of Yang Province, he had not yet personally handled affairs of government, and entrusted all of them to Ye.

entries.zh: 尋遷左衛將軍、太子詹事。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was transferred to serve as Left Guard General and Household Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Guard General and Household Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 范曄，字蔚宗，順陽人，車騎將軍泰少子也。
entries.en: Fan Ye, courtesy name Weizong, was a native of Shunyang and the youngest son of General of Chariots and Cavalry Fan Tai.
entries.literal: Fan Ye, styled Weizong, was a man of Shunyang, the youngest son of General of Chariots and Cavalry Tai.

entries.zh: 母如廁產之，額為磚所傷，故以磚為小字。
entries.en: His mother gave birth to him in a privy; his forehead was struck by a brick, and therefore Zhuan, meaning "Brick," became his childhood name.
entries.literal: His mother bore him in the privy; his forehead was injured by a brick, and therefore Zhuan, meaning "Brick," was made his childhood name.

entries.zh: 出繼從伯弘之，襲封武興縣五等侯。
entries.en: He was adopted by his father's elder cousin Fan Hongzhi and inherited the fifth-grade marquisate of Wuxing County.
entries.literal: He was given in adoption to his father's elder cousin Hongzhi and inherited the fifth-grade marquisate of Wuxing County.

entries.zh: 少好學，博涉經史，善為文章，能隸書，曉音律。
entries.en: From youth he loved learning and read widely in the classics and histories; he was skilled at literary composition, could write clerical script, and understood music and pitch.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning, broadly traversed the classics and histories, was skilled at composing literary pieces, could write clerical script, and understood pitch and regulation.

entries.zh: 年十七，州辟主簿，不就。
entries.en: At seventeen the province summoned him as Registrar, but he declined.
entries.literal: At age seventeen the province summoned him as Registrar, and he did not accept.

entries.zh: 高祖相國掾，彭城王義康冠軍參軍，隨府轉右軍參軍，入補尚書外兵郎，出為荊州別駕從事史。
entries.en: He served as Staff Member to Emperor Gaozu when the latter was Chancellor of State, then as Staff Officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, General Who Conquers Champions; he transferred with the prince's staff to Staff Officer to the General of the Right, entered court as Outer Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and was sent out as Separate-Chariot Attending Clerk of Jing Province.
entries.literal: He was Staff Member to Gaozu's Chancellor of State, Staff Officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, General Who Conquers Champions; he followed the headquarters in transfer to Staff Officer to the General of the Right, entered to fill the post of Outer Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and went out as Separate-Chariot Attending Clerk of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 尋召為秘書丞，父憂去職。
entries.en: He was soon summoned to serve as Assistant Director of the Palace Library but left office upon his father's death.
entries.literal: Soon he was summoned as Assistant Director of the Palace Library; on his father's mourning he left office.

entries.zh: 服終，為征南大將軍檀道濟司馬，領新蔡太守。
entries.en: After his mourning period ended, he served as Major to General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji and concurrently as Grand Administrator of Xincai.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he served as Major to General Who Conquers the South Tan Daoji, holding concurrently the Grand Administrator of Xincai.

entries.zh: 道濟北征，曄憚行，辭以腳疾，上不許，使由水道統載器仗部伍。
entries.en: When Daoji marched north, Ye dreaded the campaign and pleaded foot ailment; the emperor refused and ordered him to travel by waterway to oversee the transport of weapons, equipment, and troops.
entries.literal: When Daoji campaigned north, Ye feared going and declined on grounds of foot ailment; the Emperor did not permit it and had him by waterway oversee loading of weapons, gear, and troops.

entries.zh: 軍還，為司徒從事中郎。
entries.en: After the army returned, he was appointed Attending Clerk to the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he became Attending Clerk to the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 頃之，遷尚書吏部郎。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing in charge of personnel.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 湛之、曄與行中領軍蕭思話、行護軍將軍臧質、行左衛將軍孔熙先、建威將軍孔休先，忠貫白日，誠著幽顯，義痛其心，事傷其目，投命奮戈，萬殞莫顧，即日斬伯符首，及其黨與。
entries.en: Zhanzhi, Ye, Acting General of the Center Army Xiao Sihua, Acting General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi, Acting General of the Left Guard Kong Xixian, and General Who Establishes Might Kong Xiuxian, Xixian's younger brother—loyalty shining like the sun, sincerity manifest in hidden and open realms—were pained in heart and wounded in spirit; they risked their lives and brandished weapons, heedless of ten thousand deaths, and on that day cut off Bofu's head and his faction.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi, Ye, Acting General of the Center Army Xiao Sihua, Acting General Who Protects the Army Zang Zhi, Acting General of the Left Guard Kong Xixian, and General Who Establishes Might Kong Xiuxian, Xixian's younger brother—loyalty pierced the white sun, sincerity showed in hidden and manifest; righteousness pained their hearts, affairs wounded their eyes; they cast their lives and brandished weapons, ten thousand deaths unheeded, and on that day cut off Bofu's head and his faction.

entries.zh: 雖豺狼即戮，王道惟新，而普天無主，群萌莫繼。
entries.en: Though the wolf was at once punished and the kingly Way renewed, all under Heaven lacked a ruler, and the people had none to succeed him.
entries.literal: Though the wolf was at once punished, the kingly Way was only renewed—yet all under Heaven had no lord, and the multitude of sprouts had none to succeed.

entries.zh: 彭城王體自高祖，聖明在躬，德格天地，勳溢區宇，世路威夷，勿用南服，龍潛鳳棲，於茲六稔，蒼生饑德，億兆渴化，豈唯東征有《鴟鴞》之歌，陝西有勿翦之思哉！
entries.en: Prince of Pengcheng springs from Gaozu's line; sagely brilliance resides in him, his virtue reaches heaven and earth, and his merit fills the realm. Through the world's vicissitudes he has gone unused in the southern lands, hidden like a dragon and roosting like a phoenix for six years. The people hunger for his virtue and the millions thirst for his rule. Is it only in the east that they sing the 'Owl,' or west of the passes that they cherish the memory of the tree that must not be cut?
entries.literal: Prince of Pengcheng descends in body from Gaozu; sagely brightness resides in him, his virtue reaches heaven and earth, and his merit overflows the realm. Through the dangers and ease of the worldly road he has gone unused in the southern lands, hidden like a dragon and roosting like a phoenix for six years. The people hunger for his virtue and the millions thirst for his transforming rule. Is it only the eastern campaign that had the song of the 'Owl,' or the lands west of the passes that cherished the thought of not cutting down the tree?

entries.zh: 靈祗告徵祥之應，讖記表帝者之符，上答天心，下愜民望，正位辰極，非王而誰？
entries.en: Spirits and gods proclaimed auspicious omens; prophecies displayed the marks of an emperor—answering heaven's will above and the people's hopes below—to take the throne at the celestial pole—if not the prince, who else?
entries.literal: Spirits and gods proclaimed responses of auspicious omens; charts and records displayed the talismans of an emperor—above answering heaven's heart, below satisfying the people's hopes—to set the throne at the celestial pole—if not the prince, who?

entries.zh: 十七年，所生母亡。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year Zhan's birth mother died.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhan's birth mother died.

entries.zh: 時上與義康形跡既乖，釁難將結，湛亦知無復全地。
entries.en: By then the emperor and Yikang had already grown estranged, and disaster was imminent; Zhan too knew he could no longer survive unscathed.
entries.literal: At that time the Emperor and Yikang's outward traces had already parted, and trouble was about to bind; Zhan also knew there was no longer any ground for preservation.

entries.zh: 及至丁艱，謂所親曰：「今年必敗。
entries.en: When Zhan entered mourning, he told his intimates, "This year I am sure to be ruined.
entries.literal: When Zhan entered mourning for his parent, he said to those close to him: "This year I am sure to be ruined.

entries.zh: 常日正賴口舌爭之，故得推遷耳。
entries.en: On ordinary days I could still argue my case in person and so win delays.
entries.literal: On ordinary days I just relied on tongue and mouth to contend—that is why I could be put off.

entries.zh: 今既窮毒，無復此望，禍至其能久乎！」
entries.en: Now I am utterly cornered and have no such hope left—when disaster strikes, how long can it be delayed?"
entries.literal: Now I am already cornered in poison, and have no more this hope—when disaster comes, how can it long endure!"

entries.zh: 十月，詔曰：「劉湛階藉門廕，少叨榮位，往佐歷陽，姧詖夙著。
entries.en: In the tenth month an edict declared, "Liu Zhan, relying on his family's rank and privilege, early gained honored office; when he formerly served at Liyang, his treachery and perversity were already well known.
entries.literal: In the tenth month an edict said: "Liu Zhan, relying on his family's rank and shade, in youth usurped honored position; formerly assisting at Liyang, treachery and perversity were long manifest.

entries.zh: 謝晦之難，潛使密告，求心即事，久宜誅屏。
entries.en: During Xie Hui's rebellion he secretly sent reports; he sought favor by seizing the moment and long ago deserved execution and removal.
entries.literal: In Xie Hui's crisis he secretly sent secret reports, seeking the heart and taking the matter at once—long ago he ought to have been executed and removed.

entries.zh: 朕所以棄罪略瑕，庶收後效，寵秩優忝，踰越倫匹。
entries.en: We therefore overlooked his crimes and flaws, hoping he would prove useful later; we favored him with rank beyond his desert, exceeding what his peers received.
entries.literal: We therefore set aside guilt and passed over flaws, hoping to gather later effect; favored rank was generous beyond desert, exceeding peers in order.

entries.zh: 而凶忍忌克，剛愎靡厭，無君之心，觸遇斯發。
entries.en: Yet he was fierce, cruel, jealous, and overbearing, stubborn and insatiable, with a heart that lacked loyalty to his ruler—he erupted at the slightest provocation.
entries.literal: Yet he was fierce, cruel, jealous, and overbearing, stubborn and self-willed without satiety, with a heart lacking a ruler—when touched he at once erupted.

entries.zh: 遂乃合黨連群，構扇同異，附下蔽上，專弄威權，薦子樹親，互為表裏，邪附者榮曜九族，乘理者推陷必至。
entries.en: He formed factions and stirred up discord, curried favor below while deceiving those above, and monopolized power; he promoted his sons and planted his kin as mutual insiders and outsiders—those who joined him in evil saw their whole clans glorified, while those who stood on principle were inevitably destroyed.
entries.literal: He then formed factions and linked cliques, framed and fanned dissension, attached to those below and screened those above, monopolized and played with authority, recommended sons and planted kin, mutually inner and outer—those who adhered in evil had their nine clans glorified in splendor; those who seized upon principle were pushed into traps without fail.

entries.zh: 旋觀姧慝，為日已久，猶欲弘納遵養，冀或悛革。
entries.en: We have long observed his treacherous wickedness, yet still wished to embrace and nurture him, hoping he might reform.
entries.literal: Looking back upon treacherous evil, the days have been long; we still wished broadly to accept and follow in nurturing him, hoping perhaps he would reform.

entries.zh: 自邇以來，凌縱滋甚，悖言懟容，罔所顧忌，險謀潛計，睥睨兩宮。
entries.en: Recently his arrogance has grown ever worse; his rebellious words and defiant bearing show no restraint; his treacherous plots and secret schemes cast a sidelong eye upon both palaces.
entries.literal: From recent times his overbearing license has grown ever worse; rebellious words and defiant countenance, with nothing heeded in restraint; treacherous plots and hidden schemes, glaring sidelong at the two palaces.

entries.zh: 豈唯彰暴國都，固亦達于四海。
entries.en: His outrages are manifest not only in the capital but reach to the four seas.
entries.literal: How could it be only that violence is displayed in the capital—it indeed reaches to the four seas.

entries.zh: 比年七曜違度，震蝕表災，侵陽之徵，事符幽顯。
entries.en: In recent years the seven luminaries have strayed from their courses; earthquakes and eclipses have proclaimed disaster—signs of encroachment upon the yang principle, matching what is hidden and what is manifest.
entries.literal: In recent years the seven luminaries have violated their degrees; earthquakes and eclipses display calamity; signs of encroaching upon yang—the matter accords with hidden and manifest.

entries.zh: 搢紳含憤，義夫興歎。
entries.en: Officials harbor indignation, and men of righteousness sigh in dismay.
entries.literal: Girdled officials harbor anger; men of righteousness raise sighs.

entries.zh: 昔齊、魯不綱，禍傾邦國；
entries.en: Formerly, when Qi and Lu fell out of order, disaster overturned their states;
entries.literal: Formerly, when Qi and Lu lacked order, disaster overturned their states;

entries.zh: 昭、宣電斷，漢祚方延。
entries.en: when Emperors Zhao and Xuan acted with lightning decisiveness, the Han mandate was thereby prolonged.
entries.literal: when Zhao and Xuan cut off like lightning, Han's mandate was then extended.

entries.zh: 便收付廷尉，肅明刑典。」
entries.en: He is therefore to be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that the penal code may be solemnly enforced."
entries.literal: Let him at once be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice, to make solemn and clear the penal statutes."

entries.zh: 於獄伏誅，時年四十九。
entries.en: He was executed in prison at the age of forty-nine.
entries.literal: In prison he submitted to execution; he was then forty-nine years old.

entries.zh: 子黯，大將軍從事中郎。
entries.en: His son An served as Attending Clerk to the Grand General.
entries.literal: His son An was Attending Clerk to the Grand General.

entries.zh: 黯及二弟亮、儼並從誅。
entries.en: An and his two younger brothers Liang and Yan were all executed with him.
entries.literal: An and his two younger brothers Liang and Yan were all executed along with him.

entries.zh: 湛弟素，黃門侍郎，徙廣州。
entries.en: Zhan's younger brother Su, a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, was banished to Guang Province.
entries.literal: Zhan's younger brother Su was Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and was banished to Guang Province.

entries.zh: 湛初被收，歎曰：「便是亂邪。」
entries.en: When Zhan was first arrested, he sighed and said, "So there will be disorder after all."
entries.literal: When Zhan was first taken into custody, he sighed and said: "So it is disorder after all."

entries.zh: 仍又曰：「不言無我應亂，殺我自是亂法耳。」
entries.en: He then added, "It is not that disorder would not occur without me—but killing me is itself a violation of proper law."
entries.literal: He then also said: "It is not to say that without me there ought to be disorder—killing me is itself disordering the law."

entries.zh: 入獄見素，曰：「乃復及汝邪？
entries.en: When he entered prison and saw Su, he said, "So it has reached even you?
entries.literal: Entering prison he saw Su and said: "So it has reached even you?

entries.zh: 相勸為惡，惡不可為；
entries.en: We urged one another to do evil, yet evil ought not to be done;
entries.literal: We urged one another to do evil—evil cannot be done;

entries.zh: 相勸為善，正見今日。
entries.en: we urged one another to do good—and just look at us today.
entries.literal: we urged one another to do good—and just look at today.

entries.zh: 如何！」
entries.en: What then!"
entries.literal: What of it!"

entries.zh: 湛生女輒殺之，為士流所怪。
entries.en: Zhan killed every daughter born to him, which the gentry found shocking.
entries.literal: Whenever Zhan fathered a daughter he at once killed her, which the gentry stream found strange.

entries.zh: 將出市，曄最在前，於獄門顧謂綜曰：「今日次第，當以位邪？」
entries.en: When led out to execution, Ye was foremost. At the prison gate he looked back at Zong and said: "Today's order—should it follow rank?"
entries.literal: When led out to execution, Ye was foremost; at the prison gate he looked back at Zong: "Today's order—should it follow rank?"

entries.zh: 綜曰：「賊帥為先。」
entries.en: Zong said: "The rebel chief goes first."
entries.literal: Zong said: "The rebel chief goes first."

entries.zh: 在道語笑，初無暫止。
entries.en: Along the way they talked and laughed without pause.
entries.literal: Along the way they talked and laughed without pause.

entries.zh: 至市，問綜曰：「時欲至未？」
entries.en: Reaching the market, he asked Zong: "Has the hour nearly come?"
entries.literal: Reaching the market, he asked Zong: "Has the hour nearly come?"

entries.zh: 綜曰：「勢不復久。」
entries.en: Zong said: "It surely will not be long."
entries.literal: Zong said: "It surely will not be long."

entries.zh: 曄既食，又苦勸綜，綜曰：「此異病篤，何事強飯。」
entries.en: After Ye had eaten, he earnestly urged Zong to eat. Zong said: "For this strange illness, what need to force food?"
entries.literal: After Ye had eaten, he earnestly urged Zong to eat; Zong said: "For this strange illness, what need to force food?"

entries.zh: 曄家人悉至市，監刑職司問：「須相見不？」
entries.en: Ye's family all arrived at the market. The execution supervisor asked: "Do you wish to see them?"
entries.literal: Ye's family all arrived at the market; the execution supervisor asked: "Do you wish to see them?"

entries.zh: 曄問綜曰：「家人已來，幸得相見，將不暫別。」
entries.en: Ye asked Zong, "My family has come. Since I have the chance to see them, should I not briefly say farewell?"
entries.literal: Ye asked Zong: "My family has come. Since I have the good fortune to see them, should I not briefly bid them farewell?"

entries.zh: 綜曰：「別與不別，亦何所存。
entries.en: Zong said: "Farewell or not—what does it matter?
entries.literal: Zong said: "Farewell or not—what does it matter?

entries.zh: 來必當號泣，正足亂人意。」
entries.en: They will surely wail and weep—just enough to unsettle the mind."
entries.literal: They will surely wail and weep—just enough to unsettle the mind."

entries.zh: 曄曰：「號泣何關人，向見道邊親故相瞻望，亦殊勝不見。
entries.en: Ye said: "Weeping concerns no one else. Earlier I saw relatives and old friends on the roadside gazing over—that too was splendid, better than not seeing.
entries.literal: Ye said: "Weeping concerns no one else; earlier I saw relatives and old friends on the roadside gazing over—that too was splendid, better than not seeing.

entries.zh: 吾意故欲相見。」
entries.en: I have always meant to see them."
entries.literal: My intention from the start has been to see them."

entries.zh: 於是呼前。
entries.en: Thereupon he had them called forward.
entries.literal: Thereupon he had them called forward.

entries.zh: 曄妻先下撫其子，回罵曄曰：「君不為百歲阿家，不感天子恩遇，身死固不足塞罪，奈何枉殺子孫。」
entries.en: Ye's wife came down first and comforted her child, then turned and cursed Ye: "You spare no thought for your hundred-year-old mother, you show no gratitude for the emperor's grace and favor—your death alone could never atone for this crime, so why must you wrongfully destroy our children and descendants?"
entries.literal: Ye's wife came down first and stroked her child; turning back she cursed Ye, saying: "You do not think of your hundred-year-old mother, you feel no gratitude for the Son of Heaven's grace and favor—death by itself surely cannot atone for the crime; why must you wrongfully kill our children and descendants?"

entries.zh: 曄乾笑云罪至而已。
entries.en: Ye gave a dry laugh and said only that punishment had come due.
entries.literal: Ye gave a dry laugh and said the crime had simply run its course.

entries.zh: 曄所生母泣曰：「主上念汝無極，汝曾不能感恩，又不念我老，今日奈何？」
entries.en: Ye's birth mother wept and said: "The sovereign has shown you boundless favor; you cannot even be grateful, nor spare a thought for my old age—what is to become of today?"
entries.literal: Ye's biological mother wept and said: "The sovereign thinks of you beyond measure; you cannot even be grateful, nor consider my old age—what of today?"

entries.zh: 仍以手擊曄頸及頰，曄顏色不怍。
entries.en: She still struck Ye's neck and cheeks with her hands, yet Ye's face showed no shame.
entries.literal: Still she struck Ye's neck and cheeks with her hands; Ye's expression showed no shame.

entries.zh: 妻云：「罪人，阿家莫念。」
entries.en: His wife said: "He is a condemned man. Mother, do not waste another thought on him."
entries.literal: His wife said: "A condemned man. Mother, do not think of him."

entries.zh: 妹及妓妾來別，曄悲涕流漣，綜曰：「舅殊不同夏侯色。」
entries.en: His sisters and concubines came to say farewell. Ye wept with tears streaming down. Zong said: "Uncle, you are nothing like Xiahou's composure."
entries.literal: His sisters and concubines came to bid farewell; Ye wept with flowing tears; Zong said: "Uncle, you are quite unlike Xiahou's composure."

entries.zh: 曄收淚而止。
entries.en: Ye wiped away his tears and stopped.
entries.literal: Ye wiped his tears and stopped.

entries.zh: 綜母以子弟自蹈逆亂，獨不出視。
entries.en: Zong's mother, because her sons and younger brothers had themselves plunged into treason, alone refused to come out and look.
entries.literal: Zong's mother, because her sons and younger brothers had themselves plunged into rebellion, alone did not come out to look.

entries.zh: 曄語綜曰：「姊今不來，勝人多也。」
entries.en: Ye said to Zong: "If my elder sister does not come today, that is better than a crowd of people."
entries.literal: Ye said to Zong: "If elder sister does not come today, that is better than many people."

entries.zh: 曄轉醉，子藹亦醉，取地土及果皮以擲曄，呼曄為別駕數十聲。
entries.en: Ye grew still more drunk. His son Fan Ai, also drunk, picked up dirt and fruit peels and threw them at Ye, calling him "Assistant Administrator" dozens of times.
entries.literal: Ye grew increasingly drunk; his son Fan Ai, also drunk, took earth and fruit peels to throw at Ye, calling Ye "Assistant Administrator" dozens of times.

entries.zh: 曄問曰：「汝恚我邪？」
entries.en: Ye asked: "Are you angry at me?"
entries.literal: Ye asked: "Are you angry at me?"

entries.zh: 藹曰：「今日何緣復恚？
entries.en: Fan Ai said: "What reason is there to be angry today?
entries.literal: Fan Ai said: "What cause today to be angry again?

entries.zh: 但父子同死，不能不悲耳。」
entries.en: Only that father and son die together — that is what grieves me."
entries.literal: Only that father and son die together—cannot but grieve, that is all."

entries.zh: 曄常謂死者神滅，欲著《無鬼論》；
entries.en: Ye had often maintained that the dead leave no surviving spirit and had wished to write On the Nonexistence of Ghosts;
entries.literal: Ye had often said that when the dead die their spirits are extinguished, and wished to write On the Nonexistence of Ghosts;

entries.zh: 至是與徐湛之書，云「當相訟地下」。
entries.en: yet now in a letter to Xu Zhanzhi he wrote, "We shall bring suit against each other in the underworld."
entries.literal: at this time in a letter to Xu Zhanzhi he wrote, "We shall sue each other in the underworld."

entries.zh: 其謬亂如此。
entries.en: His self-contradiction was as absurd as this.
entries.literal: His confusion and contradiction were such as this.

entries.zh: 又語人：「寄語何僕射，天下決無佛鬼。
entries.en: He also told others: "Send word to Vice Director He: there are absolutely no Buddhas or ghosts in this world.
entries.literal: He also told people: "Send word to Vice Director He: Under Heaven there are absolutely no Buddhas or ghosts.

entries.zh: 若有靈，自當相報。」
entries.en: If they truly have power, they will surely settle accounts with me."
entries.literal: If they exist with spiritual power, they will surely repay in kind."

entries.zh: 收曄家，樂器服玩，並皆珍麗，妓妾亦盛飾，母住止單陋，唯有一廚盛樵薪，弟子冬無被，叔父單布衣。
entries.en: When Ye's household was searched and confiscated, his musical instruments, clothing, and curios were all precious and splendid, and his concubines were richly adorned; yet his mother lived in bare poverty, with only one kitchen stacked with firewood, his younger brother's sons had no quilts in winter, and his uncle wore only a single layer of plain cloth.
entries.literal: When Ye's property was confiscated: musical instruments, apparel, and playthings were all precious and splendid; concubines also splendidly adorned; his mother lived in bare simplicity, with only one kitchen storing firewood; younger brother's sons had no quilts in winter; his uncle wore only plain cloth.

entries.zh: 曄及子藹、遙、叔蔞、孔熙先及弟休先、景先、思先、熙先子桂甫、桂甫子白民、謝綜及弟約、仲承祖、許耀，諸所連及，並伏誅。
entries.en: Fan Ye and his sons Fan Ai, Fan Yao, and Fan Shulou; Kong Xixian and his younger brothers Kong Xiuxian, Kong Jingxian, and Kong Sixian; Xixian's son Kong Guifu and Guifu's son Kong Baimin; Xie Zong and his younger brother Xie Yue; Zhong Chengzu; and Xu Yao—all those implicated were put to death.
entries.literal: Fan Ye and his sons Fan Ai, Fan Yao, and Fan Shulou; Kong Xixian and his younger brothers Kong Xiuxian, Kong Jingxian, and Kong Sixian; Xixian's son Kong Guifu and Guifu's son Kong Baimin; Xie Zong and his younger brother Xie Yue; Zhong Chengzu; and Xu Yao—all those implicated were executed.

entries.zh: 曄時年四十八。
entries.en: Ye was forty-eight at the time.
entries.literal: Ye was then forty-eight.

entries.zh: 曄兄弟子父已亡者及謝綜弟緯，徙廣州。
entries.en: The sons of Ye's brothers whose fathers were already dead, together with Xie Zong's younger brother Wei, were exiled to Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Ye's brothers' sons whose fathers had already died, and Xie Zong's younger brother Wei, were exiled to Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 藹子魯連，吳興昭公主外孫，請全生命，亦得遠徙，世祖即位得還。
entries.en: Fan Ai's son Lulian, a grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded for his life and was likewise exiled to a distant place; when Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, he was permitted to return.
entries.literal: Fan Ai's son Lulian, grandson of Princess Zhao of Wuxing, pleaded to spare his life; he too was exiled afar; when Shizu ascended the throne he was allowed to return.

entries.zh: 列傳第二十九 劉湛 范曄
entries.en: Biographies 29: Liu Zhan and Fan Ye
entries.literal: Biographies 29: Liu Zhan, Fan Ye

entries.zh: 世祖即位，使顏延之為詔曰：「夫輕道重義，亟聞其教；世弊國危，希遇其人。自非達義之至，識正之深者，孰能抗心衞主，遺身固節者哉。故太子左衞率淑，文辯優洽，秉尚貞慤。當要逼之切，意色不橈，厲辭道逆，氣震凶黨。虐刃交至，取斃不移。古之懷忠隕難，未云出其右者。興言嗟悼，無廢乎心。宜在加禮，永旌宋有臣焉。可贈侍中、太尉，諡曰忠憲公。」
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he had Yan Yanzhi draft an edict: "When the Way is slighted and righteousness weighed heavily, the teaching has long been heard; in an age of decay and a state in peril, such a person is rarely met. Unless one has reached the utmost in grasping righteousness and depth in knowing what is correct, who could brace the heart to guard his lord, leave the body, and hold fast to integrity? Former Left Guard General of the Heir Apparent Shu was eloquent and thorough and upheld pure sincerity. When coercion pressed hardest, his expression did not bend; with stern words he denounced rebellion, and his spirit shook the vicious faction. Cruel blades fell together, yet he met death without wavering. Among the loyal who fell in disaster in antiquity, none are said to surpass him. At these words we sigh and mourn, and our hearts cannot be unmoved. He deserves added honors, eternally displaying that Song had such a minister. He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Integrity."
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he had Yan Yanzhi draft an edict saying: "When the Way is slighted and righteousness weighed heavily, the teaching has long been heard; in an age of decay and a state in peril, such a person is rarely met. Unless one has reached the utmost in grasping righteousness and depth in knowing what is correct, who could brace the heart to guard his lord, leave the body, and hold fast to integrity? Former Left Guard General of the Heir Apparent Shu was eloquent and thorough in discourse and upheld pure sincerity. When coercion pressed hardest, his expression did not bend; with stern words he denounced rebellion, and his spirit shook the vicious faction. Cruel blades fell together, yet he met death without wavering. Among ancient men who cherished loyalty and fell in disaster, none are said to surpass him. At these words we sigh and mourn, and our hearts cannot be unmoved. He deserves added honors, eternally displaying that Song had such a minister. He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Integrity."

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「袁淑以身殉義，忠烈邈古。遺孤在疚，特所矜懷。可厚加賜卹，以慰存亡。」
entries.en: Another edict said: "Yuan Shu gave his body for righteousness; his loyal valor reaches antiquity. Bereaved orphans mourn him—this touches us deeply. Let generous funeral gifts be added to console the living and the dead."
entries.literal: Another edict said: "Yuan Shu gave his body for righteousness; his loyal valor reaches back to antiquity. Orphaned children mourn; this moves us especially. Let generous funeral gifts be added to console living and dead."

entries.zh: 淑及徐湛之、江湛、王僧綽、卜天與四家，於是長給稟祿。
entries.en: The four households of Shu, Xu Zhizhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo, and Bu Tianyu thereafter received permanent stipends.
entries.literal: For the four households of Shu, Xu Zhizhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo, and Bu Tianyu, permanent stipends were thereafter granted.

entries.zh: 文集傳於世。
entries.en: His collected works circulated widely.
entries.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 子幾、敳、稜、凝、標。
entries.en: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.
entries.literal: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.

entries.zh: 敳，世祖步兵校尉。
entries.en: Ai was commandant of the footsoldiers under Emperor Xiaowu.
entries.literal: Ai was Commandant of the Footsoldiers under the Shizu Emperor.

entries.zh: 凝，太宗世禦史中丞，出為晉陵太守。
entries.en: Ning was director of the censorate under the Taizong Emperor and went out as administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: Ning was Director of the Censorate under the Taizong Emperor and went out as Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 太宗初與四方同反，兵敗歸降，以補劉湛冠軍府主簿。
entries.en: In Taizong's first year he rebelled with the four quarters; defeated, he surrendered and was made chief clerk in Liu Zhan's champion army.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Taizong Emperor he rebelled with the four quarters; when his army was defeated he returned and surrendered, and was appointed chief clerk in Liu Zhan's army of the champion general.

entries.zh: 淑諸子並早卒。
entries.en: All Shu's sons died young.
entries.literal: All Shu's sons died young.

entries.zh: 或乃言約功深，事邇應廣，齊圉反駕，趙養還君，盡輿誦之道，畢能事之效。
entries.en: Or few words, deep merit, near affairs, wide response—Qi lord returned carriage, Zhao lord restored lord, all cart and recitation's ways, full able service.
entries.literal: Or words few and merit deep, affairs near yet response wide—Qi lord returned his carriage, Zhao lord restored his lord, all the ways of cart and recitation, the full effect of able service.

entries.zh: 臣幸得出內層禁，遊心明代，澤與身泰，恩隨年行，無以逢迎昌運，潤飾鴻法。
entries.en: I have been fortunate to leave the inner forbidden, wander heart in this bright age, grace with body, favor with years, yet have nothing to meet flourishing fortune and adorn great law.
entries.literal: Your servant has been fortunate to leave the inner forbidden, wander heart in the bright age, grace equal to body, favor following years, yet has nothing with which to meet the flourishing fortune and adorn the great law.

entries.zh: 今塗有遺鏃，蠆未息蜂，敢思涼識，少酬閎施。
entries.en: Now spent arrows lie on the road; the scorpion's sting has not ceased—I dare think cool thoughts and slightly repay broad grace.
entries.literal: Now on the road lie spent arrows; the scorpion's sting has not ceased—dare I think cool thoughts and slightly repay the broad bestowal.

entries.zh: 但坐幕既乏昭文，免胄不能致果，竊觀都護之邊論，屬國之兵謨，終、晁之抗辭，杜、耿之言事，咸云及經之棘，猶闕上算，燭郛之敬，裁收下策。
entries.en: Yet command lacks brilliance; without helmet no result—I have seen frontier discussions, dependency plans, Zhong and Chao's words, Du and Geng's policy—all say classics' thorns still lack highest calculation, beacon respect barely reaches lower strategy.
entries.literal: Yet the seat of command lacks brilliance in writing; without helmet one cannot achieve the result—your servant has seen the frontier discussions of the Protector-General, the military plans of the Commandant for Dependencies, the resisting words of Zhong and Chao, the policy speeches of Du and Geng—all say that even the thorns of the classics still lack the highest calculation, and the respect of beacon towers only barely reaches the lower strategy.

entries.zh: 自恥懦木，智不綜微，敢露昧見，無會昭采。
entries.en: Ashamed of timid wood, wisdom not gathering subtlety—I dare reveal dull views, without meeting bright selection.
entries.literal: Ashamed of my timid wood, my wisdom does not gather the subtle—I dare reveal dull views, without meeting bright selection.

entries.zh: 列傳第三十 袁淑
entries.en: Biography 30: Yuan Shu
entries.literal: Biographies 30: Yuan Shu

entries.zh: 徐湛之，字孝源，東海郯人。
entries.en: Xu Zhanzhi, styled Xiaoyuan, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.
entries.literal: Xu Zhanzhi, style name Xiaoyuan, was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.

entries.zh: 司徒羨之兄孫，吳郡太守佩之弟子也。
entries.en: He was a grandson of Minister over the Masses Xianzhi's elder brother and a nephew of Wu commandery Governor Peizhi.
entries.literal: He was a grandson of the elder brother of Minister over the Masses Xianzhi and a nephew of Peizhi, Governor of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 祖欽之，秘書監。
entries.en: His grandfather Qinzhi had served as Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His grandfather Qinzhi was Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 父逵之，尚高祖長女會稽公主，為振威將軍、彭城、沛二郡太守。
entries.en: His father Kuizhi had married Princess Kuaiji, Gaozu's eldest daughter, and held the posts of General Who Quells Might and governor of Pengcheng and Pei commanderies.
entries.literal: His father Kuizhi married Princess Kuaiji, the eldest daughter of Gaozu, and served as General Who Quells Might and Governor of the two commanderies of Pengcheng and Pei.

entries.zh: 高祖諸子並幼，以逵之姻戚，將大任之，欲先令立功。
entries.en: Gaozu's sons were still young; as a kinsman by marriage, Kuizhi was marked for high office, but first he was to earn distinction in the field.
entries.literal: Gaozu's sons were all still young; because Kuizhi was a kinsman by marriage, he was to be given a great charge and was first to be made to win merit.

entries.zh: 及討司馬休之，使統軍為前鋒，配以精兵利器，事克，當即授荊州。
entries.en: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he was placed at the head of the army as vanguard with elite troops and the best arms; on victory he was to receive Jing province immediately.
entries.literal: When he campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, Kuizhi was made to command the army as vanguard, furnished with picked troops and sharp weapons; once the affair succeeded, he was at once to be given Jing province.

entries.zh: 休之遣魯宗之子軌擊破之，於陣見害。
entries.en: Xiuzhi sent Gui, son of Lu Zong, who routed him and killed him on the field.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi sent Zongzi Gui of Lu to strike and break him; he was killed in battle.

entries.zh: 追贈中書侍郎。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given the title of Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 湛之幼孤，為高祖所愛，常與江夏王義恭寢食不離於側。
entries.en: Zhanzhi lost his father early and was cherished by Gaozu, who kept him at the side of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia day and night.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi was orphaned young and was loved by Gaozu; he constantly slept and ate beside Prince Yigong of Jiangxia without leaving his side.

entries.zh: 永初三年，詔曰：「永興公主一門嫡長，早罹辛苦。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongchu an edict declared: "Princess Yongxing, eldest in her line, has known hardship from an early age.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongchu an edict said: "Princess Yongxing is the eldest legitimate child of her house and early suffered hardship.

entries.zh: 外孫湛之，特所鍾愛。
entries.en: Her grandson Zhanzhi is especially dear to us.
entries.literal: Her grandson Zhanzhi is especially cherished.

entries.zh: 且致節之胤，情實兼常。
entries.en: Moreover, as one who has shown utmost integrity, his devotion is truly exceptional.
entries.literal: Moreover, as a descendant who has shown utmost integrity, his affection is truly beyond the ordinary.

entries.zh: 可封枝江縣侯，食邑五百戶。」
entries.en: Let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang with a fief of five hundred households."
entries.literal: He may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang county with a fief of five hundred households."

entries.zh: 年數歲，與弟淳之共車行，牛奔車壞，左右馳來赴之。
entries.en: While still a small boy, he was riding with his younger brother Chunzhi when the ox bolted and wrecked the carriage; attendants rushed to their aid.
entries.literal: When he was only a few years old, riding in a carriage with his younger brother Chunzhi, the ox bolted and the carriage broke; attendants galloped up to help.

entries.zh: 湛之先令取弟，眾咸歎其幼而有識。
entries.en: Zhanzhi told them to rescue his brother first; everyone marveled that even as a child he showed such judgment.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi first ordered them to take his brother; all sighed in admiration that even as a child he had such sense.

entries.zh: 及長，頗涉大義，善自位待。
entries.en: As he matured he gained a solid grasp of moral principle and knew how to conduct himself according to his rank.
entries.literal: When he grew up, he was well versed in great principles and knew how to comport himself in his station.

entries.zh: 事祖母及母，並以孝謹聞。
entries.en: His care of his grandmother and mother alike won him a reputation for filial devotion and reverence.
entries.literal: In serving his grandmother and his mother, he was alike renowned for filial piety and dutiful care.

entries.zh: 會稽公主身居長嫡，為太祖所禮，家事大小，必咨而後行。
entries.en: Princess Kuaiji, as eldest legitimate daughter, was held in honor by Emperor Wen; on household matters great and small he always sought her counsel before acting.
entries.literal: Princess Kuaiji, as the eldest legitimate daughter, was honored by the Taizu; in household affairs great and small, he always consulted her before acting.

entries.zh: 西征謝晦，使公主留止台內，總攝六宮。
entries.en: On the western campaign against Xie Hui he left the princess at court to oversee the inner palaces.
entries.literal: On the western campaign against Xie Hui, he had the princess remain within the terrace compound to oversee the six palaces in general.

entries.zh: 忽有不得意，輒號哭，上甚憚之。
entries.en: Whenever something displeased her she would burst into loud weeping, and the emperor was much afraid of it.
entries.literal: Whenever she was suddenly displeased, she would wail aloud; the emperor greatly feared this.

entries.zh: 初，高祖微時，貧陋過甚，嘗自往新洲伐荻，有納布衫襖等衣，皆敬皇后手自作；
entries.en: In his early days Gaozu had been desperately poor; he once went to Xinzhou himself to cut reeds. A cotton jacket and padded coat he owned had been sewn by Empress Jing with her own hands;
entries.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu was still obscure, he was exceedingly poor and mean; he once went himself to Xinzhou to cut reeds; there were garments such as a cotton jacket and padded coat, all made by the hand of Empress Jing herself;

entries.zh: 高祖既貴，以此衣付公主，曰：「後世若有驕奢不節者，可以此衣示之。」
entries.en: after he rose to power he gave those garments to the princess, saying, "If any descendant grows arrogant and extravagant, show him these clothes."
entries.literal: after Gaozu had risen to eminence, he gave these garments to the princess, saying, "If in later generations there is anyone arrogant, extravagant, and without restraint, you may show him these garments."

entries.zh: 湛之為大將軍彭城王義康所愛，與劉湛等頗相附協。
entries.en: Zhanzhi won the favor of Grand General Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, and aligned himself closely with Liu Tan and his circle.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi was loved by Grand General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and was rather closely allied with Liu Tan and others.

entries.zh: 及劉湛得罪，事連湛之，太祖大怒，將致大辟。
entries.en: When Liu Tan fell, the case implicated Zhanzhi; Emperor Wen was furious and was about to sentence him to death.
entries.literal: When Liu Tan was punished for his offense, the affair implicated Zhanzhi; the Taizu was greatly enraged and was about to impose the death penalty.

entries.zh: 湛之憂懼無計，以告公主。
entries.en: In dread and despair Zhanzhi confided in the princess.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi, anxious and at his wits' end, told the princess.

entries.zh: 公主即日入宮，既見太祖，因號哭下床，不復施臣妾之禮。
entries.en: The princess went to court that same day; as soon as she saw Emperor Wen she wailed and threw herself from the couch, abandoning all courtly decorum.
entries.literal: That very day the princess entered the palace; once she had seen the Taizu, she wailed and threw herself from the couch, no longer observing the rites due from a subject or consort.

entries.zh: 以錦囊盛高祖納衣，擲地以示上曰：「汝家本貧賤，此是我母為汝父作此納衣。
entries.en: She took Gaozu's cotton garments from a brocade pouch and flung them down before the emperor. "Your family was poor," she cried. "My mother sewed this cotton coat for your father.
entries.literal: She placed Gaozu's cotton garments in a brocade pouch and flung them to the ground to show the emperor, saying, "Your house was originally poor and base; this is the cotton garment my mother made for your father.

entries.zh: 今日有一頓飽食，便欲殘害我兒子！」
entries.en: Now that you have your fill, you would destroy my son!"
entries.literal: Now that you have one full meal, you wish to destroy my son!"

entries.zh: 上亦號哭，湛之由此得全也。
entries.en: The emperor wept as well, and Zhanzhi was spared.
entries.literal: The emperor also wailed aloud, and by this means Zhanzhi was spared.

entries.zh: 遷中護軍，未拜，又遷太子詹事，尋加侍中。
entries.en: He was appointed Central Army Protector but did not take up the post; he was then made Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and soon after Palace Attendant as well.
entries.literal: He was moved to Central Army Protector; before he took office he was again moved to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, and soon after was given the additional post of Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 上優詔不許。
entries.en: The emperor issued a gracious edict refusing his request.
entries.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict and did not permit it.

entries.zh: 二十四年，服闋，轉中書令，領太子詹事。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year, when his mourning was complete, he became Director of the Central Secretariat while retaining the post of Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when mourning was complete, he was transferred to Director of the Central Secretariat and concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.

entries.zh: 出為前軍將軍、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as Forward Army General and Governor of Southern Yan province.
entries.literal: He went out as Forward Army General and Governor of Southern Yan province.

entries.zh: 善於為政，威惠並行。
entries.en: He governed well, combining stern authority with kindness.
entries.literal: He was skilled in government, combining authority and kindness.

entries.zh: 廣陵城舊有高樓，湛之更加修整，南望鐘山。
entries.en: Guangling already had a tall tower; Zhanzhi restored and embellished it to look south toward Zhong Mountain.
entries.literal: Guangling city had long had a high tower; Zhanzhi further restored and adorned it, facing south toward Zhong Mountain.

entries.zh: 城北有陂澤，水物豐盛。
entries.en: North of the city lay ponds and marshes teeming with fish and waterfowl.
entries.literal: North of the city were ponds and marshes, rich in aquatic creatures.

entries.zh: 湛之更起風亭、月觀，吹台、琴室，果竹繁茂，花藥成行，招集文士，盡遊玩之適，一時之盛也。
entries.en: Zhanzhi added the Wind Pavilion and Moon View, the Flute Terrace and Zither Room; fruit trees and bamboo flourished, flowers and herbs lined the paths; he gathered literati and enjoyed every diversion—the glory of the age.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi further raised the Wind Pavilion and Moon View, the Flute Terrace and Zither Room; fruit trees and bamboo grew luxuriantly, flowers and herbs stood in rows; he gathered literary men and enjoyed every pleasure of diversion—it was the splendor of the age.

entries.zh: 時有沙門釋惠休，善屬文，辭采綺豔，湛之與之甚厚。
entries.en: At the time the monk Huixiu was skilled at composition, his style gorgeous and brilliant; Zhanzhi was very close to him.
entries.literal: At the time there was the monk Shi Huixiu, skilled at composition, his diction gorgeous and brilliant; Zhanzhi was very close to him.

entries.zh: 世祖命使還俗。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu ordered him to return to lay life.
entries.literal: The Shizu ordered him to return to lay life.

entries.zh: 本姓湯，位至揚州從事史。
entries.en: His original surname was Tang; he rose to staff officer of Yang province.
entries.literal: His original surname was Tang; he rose to Staff Officer of Yang province.

entries.zh: 二十六年，復入為丹陽尹，領太子詹事，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year he returned to the capital as Governor of Danyang while retaining the post of Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household; his general's rank was unchanged.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again entered the capital as Governor of Danyang, concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household; his generalship remained as before.

entries.zh: 二十七年，索虜至瓜步，湛之領兵置佐，與皇太子分守石頭。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year the Northern Wei reached Guabu; Zhanzhi took command and, with the crown prince, jointly defended Shitou fortress.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the northern barbarians reached Guabu; Zhanzhi led troops and set up his staff, sharing with the crown prince the defense of Shitou.

entries.zh: 二十八年春，魯爽兄弟率部曲歸順，爽等，魯軌子也。
entries.en: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year Lu Shuang and his brothers led their followers in submission to the Song; they were sons of Lu Gui.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year, Lu Shuang and his brothers led their followers in submission; Shuang and the rest were sons of Lu Gui.

entries.zh: 湛之以為廟算遠圖，特所獎納，不敢苟申私怨。
entries.en: Zhanzhi regarded their submission as part of the court's long-range strategy and warmly welcomed them, not daring to press a private grudge.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi regarded this as the court's far-reaching design and specially commended and accepted them; he did not dare lightly press a private grievance.

entries.zh: 乞屏居田里，不許。
entries.en: He asked to retire to the countryside; his request was refused.
entries.literal: He begged to withdraw and live in the countryside; permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 上每有疾，湛之輒入侍醫藥。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor fell ill, Zhanzhi attended him with medicine.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor fell ill, Zhanzhi would enter to attend him with medicine.

entries.zh: 二凶巫蠱事發，上欲廢劭，賜浚死。
entries.en: When the witchcraft plot of the two princes was exposed, the emperor wished to depose Shao and order Jun to take his own life.
entries.literal: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains broke open, the emperor wished to depose Shao and grant Jun death.

entries.zh: 而世祖不見寵，故累出外蕃，不得停京輦。
entries.en: Prince Jun, however, was not favored and was repeatedly posted to distant principalities, unable to remain at court.
entries.literal: The Shizu, however, was not favored and was repeatedly sent out to border principalities, unable to remain at the capital.

entries.zh: 南平王鑠、建平王宏並為上所愛，而鑠妃即湛妹，勸上立之。
entries.en: Princes Shuo of Nanping and Hong of Jianping were both favored by the emperor; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's sister and urged the emperor to name Shuo heir.
entries.literal: Prince Shuo of Nanping and Prince Hong of Jianping were both loved by the emperor; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister, and she urged the emperor to establish him.

entries.zh: 元嘉末，征鑠自壽陽入朝，既至，又失旨，欲立宏，嫌其非次，是以議久不決。
entries.en: Late in Yuanjia, Shuo was summoned from Shouyang to court; once he arrived he again displeased the emperor. The emperor wished to name Hong heir but hesitated over his birth order, and deliberation dragged on.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuanjia, Shuo was summoned from Shouyang to court; once he arrived he again fell from favor; the emperor wished to establish Hong but disliked his irregular order of birth; thus deliberation long went unresolved.

entries.zh: 與湛之屏人共言論，或連日累夕。
entries.en: He discussed the matter with Zhanzhi in private, sometimes for days and nights on end.
entries.literal: With Zhanzhi he discussed matters behind screened attendants, sometimes for days on end through successive nights.

entries.zh: 每夜常使湛之自秉燭，繞壁檢行，慮有竊聽者。
entries.en: Each night he had Zhanzhi carry a candle and patrol the walls, fearing eavesdroppers.
entries.literal: Each night he would have Zhanzhi himself hold the candle and walk around the walls inspecting, fearing eavesdroppers.

entries.zh: 劭入弑之旦，其夕，上與湛之屏人語，至曉猶未滅燭。
entries.en: On the night before Shao murdered him, the emperor had been speaking with Zhanzhi in private until dawn, candles still burning.
entries.literal: On the morning when Shao entered to commit regicide, that very evening the emperor had been speaking with Zhanzhi behind screened attendants; until dawn the candles were still not extinguished.

entries.zh: 湛之驚起趣北戶，未及開，見害。
entries.en: Zhanzhi sprang up in alarm and rushed to the north door; before he could open it he was slain.
entries.literal: Zhanzhi started up in alarm and rushed to the north door; before he could open it he was killed.

entries.zh: 時年四十四。
entries.en: He was forty-four.
entries.literal: He was forty-four years old.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，追贈司空，加散騎常侍，本官如故，諡曰忠烈公。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Zhanzhi was posthumously made Minister of Works with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former titles were confirmed; he was posthumously styled Duke of Loyal Valor.
entries.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, he was posthumously given the office of Minister of Works and the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former offices remained as before; his posthumous name was Duke of Loyal Valor.

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「徐湛之、江湛、王僧綽門戶荼酷，遺孤流寓，言念既往，感痛兼深。
entries.en: Another edict declared: "The houses of Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo have suffered bitter cruelty; orphaned survivors wander in exile; remembering what has passed fills us with deep grief.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "The houses of Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo have suffered bitter cruelty; orphaned survivors wander in exile; speaking of what has passed, grief and pain are alike deep.

entries.zh: 可令歸居本宅，厚加恤賜。」
entries.en: Let them return to their family homes and receive generous relief and gifts."
entries.literal: They may be ordered to return and dwell in their original residences, with generous relief and gifts."

entries.zh: 於是三家長給廩。
entries.en: Thereupon the three families received long-term grain stipends.
entries.literal: Thereupon the three families received long-term grain rations.

entries.zh: 上將廢劭，使湛具詔草。
entries.en: When the emperor prepared to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.

entries.zh: 劭之入弑也，湛直上省，聞叫噪之聲，乃匿傍小屋中。
entries.en: When Shao entered to murder the emperor, Zhan had gone to the Secretariat; hearing the uproar, he hid in a small room nearby.
entries.literal: When Shao entered to commit regicide, Zhan had gone straight up to the Secretariat; hearing cries and uproar, he hid in a small room nearby.

entries.zh: 劭遣收之，舍吏紿云：「不在此。」
entries.en: Shao sent men to seize him; an office clerk deceived them, saying, "He is not here."
entries.literal: Shao sent men to seize him; a clerk of the office deceived them, saying, "He is not here."

entries.zh: 兵士即殺舍吏，乃得湛。
entries.en: The soldiers killed the clerk and then seized Zhan.
entries.literal: The soldiers at once killed the clerk and thus seized Zhan.

entries.zh: 湛據窗受害，意色不撓。
entries.en: Zhan braced himself against the window as he was killed; his expression never changed.
entries.literal: Zhan braced himself against the window as he was killed; his expression did not flinch.

entries.zh: 時年四十六。
entries.en: He was forty-six.
entries.literal: He was forty-six years old.

entries.zh: 湛五子恁、恕、憼、愻、法壽，皆見殺。
entries.en: Zhan's five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all executed.
entries.literal: Zhan's five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all killed.

entries.zh: 初，湛家數見怪異，未敗少日，所眠床忽有數升血。
entries.en: Earlier strange omens had appeared in Zhan's household; a few days before his fall several pints of blood suddenly appeared on his bed.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhan's household had several times seen strange omens; a few days before his fall, several pints of blood suddenly appeared on the bed where he slept.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，本官如故，諡曰忠簡公。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Zhan was posthumously made Left Household Grandee with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former titles were confirmed; he was posthumously styled Duke of Loyal Simplicity.
entries.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, he was posthumously given the offices of Left Household Grandee and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; his former offices remained as before; his posthumous name was Duke of Loyal Simplicity.

entries.zh: 長子恁，尚太祖第九女淮陽長公主，為著作佐郎。
entries.en: His eldest son Ren married Eldest Princess Huaiyang, Emperor Wen's ninth daughter, and served as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.
entries.literal: His eldest son Ren married the Eldest Princess of Huaiyang, the ninth daughter of the Taizu, and served as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.

entries.zh: 及劭弑逆，江湛在尚書上省，聞變，歎曰：「不用僧綽言，以至於此。」
entries.en: When Shao murdered the emperor, Jiang Zhan was at the Masters of Writing offices; hearing the news he sighed, "Had we heeded Sengchuo's counsel, it would not have come to this."
entries.literal: When Shao committed regicide, Jiang Zhan was in the upper offices of the Masters of Writing; hearing the upheaval, he sighed and said, "Had we not taken Sengchuo's counsel, it would not have come to this."

entries.zh: 劭既立，轉為吏部尚書，委以事任，事在《二凶傳》。
entries.en: After Shao usurped the throne, Sengchuo was made Director of Personnel and entrusted with affairs of state; the account is in the 《Biography of the Two Villains》.
entries.literal: After Shao had usurped the throne, Sengchuo was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with affairs of office; the matter is recorded in the 《Biography of the Two Villains》.

entries.zh: 頃之，劭料檢太祖巾箱及江湛家書疏，得僧綽所啟饗士並廢諸王事，乃收害焉，時年三十一。
entries.en: Soon Shao searched the emperor's private chest and Jiang Zhan's papers; finding Sengchuo's reports on the feast for officers and the plan to depose the princes, he had him seized and killed; Sengchuo was thirty-one.
entries.literal: Before long, Shao examined the Taizu's scarf-box and the letters and documents in Jiang Zhan's household; he found Sengchuo's reports on feasting the officers and deposing the princes, and thereupon seized and killed him; he was thirty-one years old.

entries.zh: 因此陷北第諸王侯，以為與僧綽有異志，並殺僧綽門客太學博士賈匪之、奉朝請司馬文穎、建平國常侍司馬仲秀等。
entries.en: On this pretext he implicated the princes of the Northern Residence, claiming they shared Sengchuo's disloyal intent; he also executed Sengchuo's clients Jia Feizhi, Erudite of the National University, court attendant Sima Wenying, regular attendant Sima Zhongxiu of Jianping, and others.
entries.literal: On this pretext he implicated the princes and marquises of the Northern Residence, holding that they shared Sengchuo's disloyal intent; he also killed Sengchuo's clients Jia Feizhi, Erudite of the National University, Sima Wenying, Court Attendant, Sima Zhongxiu, Regular Attendant of the Principality of Jianping, and others.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，追贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰湣侯。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Sengchuo was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; he was posthumously styled Marquis of Lamentation.
entries.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, he was posthumously given the titles of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his posthumous name was Marquis of Lamentation.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：甚矣，宋氏之家難也，仇釁所鐘，親地兼極，雖復傾天滅道，跡非嫌路，而災隙內兆，邪蠱外興，天性既離，愛敬同盡，探雀請熊，非無前釁，猜防之道，有未足乎。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: How severe were the Liu Song's domestic calamities! Enmity converged upon them as kinship reached its breaking point. Though they overturned Heaven and extinguished the Way, their course was not mere suspicion—yet disaster sprouted within while witchcraft arose without; natural affection was severed and love and reverence alike exhausted. To take a sparrow and demand a bear—had there been no prior warning? Were suspicion and precaution not yet enough?
entries.literal: The historiographer says: How great were the domestic calamities of the house of Song! Enmity and strife converged upon them; kinship reached its extreme. Though they overturned Heaven and extinguished the Way, their tracks were not those of mere suspicion—yet disaster sprouted within, wicked witchcraft arose without; natural affection was already severed, love and reverence alike exhausted. To take a sparrow and ask for a bear—was there no prior omen? Were the ways of suspicion and guard not yet sufficient?

entries.zh: 世祖弱年輕躁，夙無朝寵，累任邊外，未嘗居中。
entries.en: Prince Jun in his youth was frivolous and impetuous; he had never enjoyed favor at court; repeatedly posted to the frontiers, he had never held power at the center.
entries.literal: The Shizu in his youth was frivolous and impetuous; from of old he had no favor at court; he was repeatedly posted to the border regions and never held the center.

entries.zh: 當璧之重，將由愛立，臣主回疑，事無蚤斷。
entries.en: The choice of heir was to be settled by affection; ruler and ministers wavered; the matter was never decided in time.
entries.literal: The weight of holding the jade disk was to be settled by affection; ruler and ministers wavered in doubt; the affair had no early resolution.

entries.zh: 若使守器以長，命不待賢，則密禍自銷，危機可免。
entries.en: If the heir had been kept by seniority and the throne had not awaited the worthy, hidden calamity would have dissolved and crisis been avoided.
