entries.literal: India's transmitted texts and the star-flowered cubic charts establish prior determination; karmic retribution points to its term; poor and great are not differentiated, long life and early death are not in error; there are trustworthy petty phrases and no fault in humble discourse—unified in speech, where does anything go that is not fate?

entries.zh: 冥期前定，各從所歸，善惡無所矯其趨，愚智焉能殊其理。
entries.en: Dark terms are fixed beforehand; each follows where he is bound; good and evil cannot alter their course—how can fool and sage differ in principle?
entries.literal: Dark terms are fixed beforehand; each follows where he is bound; good and evil cannot alter their course, fool and sage—how can they differ in principle?

entries.zh: 若乃得議其工，失嗤其拙，操之則栗，舍之則悲，斯固染情於近累，豈不貽誚於通識。
entries.en: If one praises another's skill when he succeeds and mocks his clumsiness when he fails, trembles when holding it and grieves when letting go—this is surely staining feeling with nearby entanglements; does it not invite reproach from penetrating understanding?
entries.literal: If one praises another's skill when he succeeds and mocks his clumsiness when he fails, trembles when holding it and grieves when letting go—this is surely staining feeling with nearby entanglements; does it not invite reproach from penetrating understanding?

entries.zh: 列傳第四十一 劉秀之 顧琛 顧覬之
entries.en: Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, and Gu Jizhi
entries.literal: Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi

entries.zh: 殷孝祖，陳郡長平人也。
entries.en: Yin Xiaozu was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery.
entries.literal: Yin Xiaozu was a man of Changping in Chen Commandery.

entries.zh: 曾祖羨，晉光祿勳。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Yin Xian had served the Jin as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xian was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness under Jin.

entries.zh: 父祖並不達。
entries.en: Neither his father nor his grandfather had risen to prominence.
entries.literal: His father and grandfather both did not attain success.

entries.zh: 孝祖少誕節，好酒色，有氣幹。
entries.en: In youth Xiaozu was rakish and fond of wine and women, yet he possessed vigor and practical ability.
entries.literal: Xiaozu in youth was extravagant in conduct, fond of wine and women, and possessed spirit and capacity.

entries.zh: 太祖元嘉末，為奉朝請，員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: At the end of the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, he served as court gentleman for the dynasty and supernumerary gentlemen-attendant at the palace gate.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, he served as Court Gentleman for the Dynasty and Supernumerary Gentlemen-Attendant at the Palace Gate.

entries.zh: 世祖以其有武用，除奮武將軍、濟北太守。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu, recognizing his martial talent, appointed him General Who Exerts Might and administrator of Jibei.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, seeing his military ability, appointed him General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of Jibei.

entries.zh: 入為積射將軍。
entries.en: He was summoned to court as general of accumulated archery.
entries.literal: He entered court as General of Accumulated Archery.

entries.zh: 大明初，索虜寇青州，上遣孝祖北援，受刺史顏師伯節度，累與虜戰，頻大破之，事在師伯傳。
entries.en: Early in the Daming era the Northern Wei raided Qing Province. The emperor sent Xiaozu north to reinforce the defense, placing him under Governor Yan Shibo. He fought the invaders again and again and won crushing victories; the full account appears in Shibo's biography.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Daming era, the northern barbarians raided Qing Province; the emperor sent Xiaozu north to reinforce. He was placed under the command of Governor Yan Shibo, fought the barbarians repeatedly, and inflicted great defeats—the account is in Shibo's biography.

entries.zh: 還授太子旅賁中郎將，加龍驤將軍。
entries.en: After returning he was appointed commander of the crown prince's household guards brigades and was also made general of the dragon cavalry.
entries.literal: On his return he was made Commander of the Household Guards of the Crown Prince's Brigades and additionally General of the Dragon Cavalry.

entries.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵為逆，孝祖隸沈慶之攻誕，又有戰功，遷西陽王子尚撫軍、寧朔將軍、南濟陰太守。
entries.en: When Prince Jingling Dan rebelled and held Guangling, Xiaozu served under Shen Qingzhi in the campaign against him and again distinguished himself in battle. He was then transferred to adjutant on the pacification staff of Prince Xiyang Zishang, made general who pacifies the north, and appointed administrator of Southern Jiyin.
entries.literal: When Prince of Jingling Dan seized Guangling in rebellion, Xiaozu served under Shen Qingzhi in attacking Dan, again achieved military merit, and was transferred to adjutant of the Prince of Xiyang Zishang's pacification army, General Who Pacifies the North, and Administrator of Southern Jiyin.

entries.zh: 出為盱眙太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was sent out to serve as administrator of Xuyi while retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuyi, his generalship unchanged.

entries.zh: 還為虎賁中郎將，仍除寧朔將軍、陽平、東平二郡太守。
entries.en: He returned to court as commander of the tiger guards and was also appointed general who pacifies the north and administrator of both Yangping and Dongping.
entries.literal: He returned as Commander of the Tiger Guards, and was also appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of both Yangping and Dongping commanderies.

entries.zh: 又遷濟南、南郡，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was transferred in turn to Jinan and Nan, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: He was transferred again to Jinan and Nan commanderies, his generalship unchanged.

entries.zh: 五年，汝陰太守楊文萇又頻破虜於荊亭及戍西。
entries.en: In the fifth year Runan administrator Yang Wenchang again repeatedly defeated the barbarians at Jingting and west of the garrison.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Runan Administrator Yang Wenchang again repeatedly defeated the barbarians at Jingting and west of the garrison.

entries.zh: 詔進勔號平西將軍、豫州刺史，餘如故，不拜。
entries.en: An edict advanced Mian to general who pacifies the west and governor of Yu Province, the rest unchanged; he declined.
entries.literal: An edict advanced Mian to General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yu Province, the rest unchanged; he did not accept.

entries.zh: 其年，徵拜散騎常侍、中領軍。
entries.en: That year he was summoned and appointed attendant-in-ordinary and general of the central army.
entries.literal: That year he was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 勔以世路糾紛，有懷止足，求東陽郡。
entries.en: Mian, seeing the age tangled in strife, felt a wish to stop and be content, and requested Dongyang commandery.
entries.literal: Mian, seeing the age tangled in strife, felt a wish to stop and be content, and requested Dongyang commandery.

entries.zh: 上以勔啟遍示朝臣，自尚書僕射袁粲以下，莫不稱讚，咸謂宜許。
entries.en: The emperor showed Mian's memorial to all court officials. From vice director of the Secretariat Yuan Can downward, none failed to praise it; all said it should be granted.
entries.literal: The emperor showed Mian's memorial to all court officials. From Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Can downward, none did not praise it; all said it should be granted.

entries.zh: 上曰：「巴陵、建平二王，並有獨往之志。
entries.en: The emperor said, "The two princes of Baling and Jianping both have a will to go their own way.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "The two princes of Baling and Jianping both have a will to go their own way.

entries.zh: 若世道寧晏，皆當申其所請。」
entries.en: If the age is peaceful and settled, each should be granted what he requests."
entries.literal: If the age is peaceful and settled, each should be granted what he requests."

entries.zh: 勔經始鍾嶺之南，以為棲息，聚石蓄水，仿佛丘中，朝士愛素者，多往遊之。
entries.en: Mian began construction south of Zhong Ridge as his dwelling, gathering stones and storing water in imitation of a hill retreat. Court gentlemen who loved simplicity often went there to visit.
entries.literal: Mian began construction south of Zhong Ridge as his dwelling, gathering stones and storing water in imitation of a hill retreat. Court gentlemen who loved simplicity often went there to visit.

entries.zh: 六年，改常侍為侍中。
entries.en: In the sixth year the attendant-in-ordinary post was changed to attendant.
entries.literal: In the sixth year the attendant-in-ordinary post was changed to attendant.

entries.zh: 其年，南兗州刺史齊王出鎮淮陰，以勔為使持節、都督南徐、兗、青、冀、囗五州諸軍事、平北將軍，侍中、中領軍如故，出鎮廣陵。
entries.en: That year Prince Qi, governor of Southern Yanzhou, went out to garrison Huaiyin. Mian was made bearer of the credentials staff, commander of military affairs in Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and [text defective] provinces, general who pacifies the north, with attendant and general of the central army unchanged, and went out to garrison Guangling.
entries.literal: That year the Prince of Qi, Governor of Southern Yanzhou, went out to garrison Huaiyin. Mian was made Bearer of the Credentials Staff, Commander of military affairs in Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and [text defective] provinces, General Who Pacifies the North, attendant and general of the central army unchanged, and went out to garrison Guangling.

entries.zh: 固辭侍中、軍號，許之，以為假平北將軍。
entries.en: He firmly declined the attendant post and military title. This was granted, and he was made acting general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: He firmly declined the attendant post and military title; this was granted, and he was made Acting General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 七年，解都督、假號、并節。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was relieved of command, acting rank, and credentials staff together.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was relieved of command, acting rank, and credentials staff together.

entries.zh: 太宗臨崩，顧命以為守尚書右僕射，中領軍如故，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming lay dying he entrusted him by final command as guardian minister and right vice director of the Secretariat, general of the central army unchanged, and granted one set of martial music.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming lay dying he entrusted him by final command as Guardian Minister and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, general of the central army unchanged, and granted one set of martial music.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，加兵五百人。
entries.en: When the deposed emperor took the throne, five hundred more troops were added to his guard.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, five hundred more troops were added to his guard.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：吳漢平蜀，城內流血沾踝，而其後無聞於漢；
entries.en: The historian says: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city soaked to the ankles, yet afterward nothing is heard of him in Han;
entries.literal: The historian says: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city soaked to the ankles, yet afterward nothing is heard of him in Han;

entries.zh: 陸抗定西陵，步氏禍及嬰孩，而機、雲為戮上國。
entries.en: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's calamity reached infants in arms, yet Lu Ji and Lu Yun were executed in the upper state.
entries.literal: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's calamity reached infants in arms, yet Ji and Yun were executed in the upper state.

entries.zh: 劉勔克壽春，士民無遺芻委粒之歎；
entries.en: When Liu Mian took Shouyang, soldiers and civilians had no lament over lost fodder and scattered grain;
entries.literal: When Liu Mian took Shouyang, soldiers and civilians had no lament over lost fodder and scattered grain;

entries.zh: 莫不扶老攜幼，歌唱而出重圍，美矣！
entries.en: all without exception supported the old and led the young, singing as they came out of the heavy encirclement—how beautiful!
entries.literal: all without exception supported the old and led the young, singing as they came out of the heavy encirclement—how beautiful!

entries.zh: 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔
entries.en: Biography 46: Yin Xiaozu and Liu Mian
entries.literal: Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian

entries.zh: 袁粲，字景倩，陳郡陽夏人，太尉淑兄子也。
entries.en: Yuan Can, styled Jingqian, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery and a nephew of Grand Marshal Shu.
entries.literal: Yuan Can, style name Jingqian, was a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, a nephew of Grand Marshal Shu.

entries.zh: 父濯，揚州秀才，蚤卒。
entries.en: His father Zhuo was a Yang Province outstanding youth and died young.
entries.literal: His father Zhuo was a Yang Province outstanding youth and died young.

entries.zh: 祖母哀其幼孤，名之曰愍孫。
entries.en: His grandmother pitied him as a young orphan and named him Min Sun.
entries.literal: His grandmother pitied him as a young orphan and named him Min Sun.

entries.zh: 伯叔並當世榮顯，而愍孫饑寒不足。
entries.en: His uncles were all illustrious in the age, yet Min Sun lacked food and clothing.
entries.literal: His uncles were all illustrious in the age, yet Min Sun lacked food and clothing.

entries.zh: 母琅邪王氏，太尉長史誕之女也，躬事績紡，以供朝夕。
entries.en: His mother was of the Wang clan of Langye, daughter of the Grand Marshal's chief clerk Dan; she personally spun and wove to supply their daily needs.
entries.literal: His mother was the Wang clan of Langye, daughter of the Grand Marshal's chief clerk Dan; she personally did spinning and weaving to supply morning and evening.

entries.zh: 愍孫少好學，有清才，有欲與從兄顗婚者，伯父洵即顗父，曰：「顗不堪，政可與愍孫婚耳。」
entries.en: Min Sun from youth loved learning and had pure talent; someone wished to marry him to his cousin Yi; his uncle Xun, who was also Yi's father, said: "Yi is not fit; he should marry Min Sun instead."
entries.literal: Min Sun from youth loved learning and had pure talent; someone wished to marry him to his cousin Yi; his uncle Xun, who was also Yi's father, said: "Yi is not fit; he should marry Min Sun instead."

entries.zh: 時愍孫在坐，流涕起出。
entries.en: Min Sun was present; weeping, he rose and left the room.
entries.literal: At the time Min Sun was present; weeping, he rose and went out.

entries.zh: 蚤以操立志行見知。
entries.en: Early on he was known for integrity in aspiration and conduct.
entries.literal: Early he was known for integrity in establishing aspiration and conduct.

entries.zh: 初為揚州從事，世祖安北、鎮軍、北中郎行參軍，侍中郎主簿。
entries.en: He began as a Yang Province attendant, then served as acting Army Staff Officer under the future Emperor Xiaowu in his Pacifying the North, Stabilizing the Army, and Northern Interior posts, and as chief clerk to the Secretariat Attendant.
entries.literal: Initially he was a Yang Province attendant; acting Army Staff Officer for the Shizuo's Pacifying the North, Stabilizing the Army, and Northern Interior posts; Secretariat Attendant chief clerk.

entries.zh: 世祖伐逆，轉記室參軍。
entries.en: When the future emperor campaigned against rebels, he was transferred to Recording Army Staff Officer.
entries.literal: When the Shizu campaigned against rebels, he was transferred to Recording Army Staff Officer.

entries.zh: 及即位，除尚書吏部郎，太子右衛率，侍中。
entries.en: When he took the throne, Min Sun was made Secretariat Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Guard of the Heir, and Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, Min Sun was made Secretariat Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Guard of the Heir, and Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 孝建元年，世祖率群臣並於中興寺八關齋，中食竟，愍孫別與黃門郎張淹更進魚肉食。
entries.en: In the first year of Xiaojian, the emperor led the hundred officials in the eight precepts fast at Zhongxing Temple; when the midday meal was finished, Min Sun separately with Cavalier Attendant Zhang Yan further took fish and meat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, the Shizu led the hundred officials together in the eight precepts fast at Zhongxing Temple; when the midday meal was finished, Min Sun separately with Cavalier Attendant Zhang Yan further took fish and meat food.

entries.zh: 尚書令何尚之奉法素謹，密以白世祖，世祖使御史中丞王謙之糾奏，並免官。
entries.en: Secretariat Director He Shangzhi, who always observed the law strictly, secretly reported it to the emperor; the emperor had Imperial Censor Wang Qianzhi impeach them, and both were dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Secretariat Director He Shangzhi in observing the law was always strict; secretly he reported it to the Shizu; the Shizu had Imperial Censor Wang Qianzhi impeach them, and both were dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 二年，起為廷尉，太子中庶子，領右軍將軍。
entries.en: In the second year, he was recalled as Minister of Justice, Household Mentor of the Heir, and concurrently General of the Right Army.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was recalled as Minister of Justice, Household Mentor of the Heir, and concurrently General of the Right Army.

entries.zh: 出為輔國將軍、西陽王子尚北中郎長史、廣陵太守，行兗州事。
entries.en: He went out as General Who Assists the State, Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Xiyang Zishang as Northern Interior Lord, and Governor of Guangling, acting for Yan Province affairs.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Assists the State, Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Xiyang Zishang as Northern Interior Lord, and Governor of Guangling, acting for Yan Province affairs.

entries.zh: 仍為永嘉王子仁冠軍長史，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: He was then Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Yongjia Ziren as Champion, with his general and governorship posts unchanged.
entries.literal: He was then Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Yongjia Ziren as Champion, with his general and governorship posts unchanged.

entries.zh: 大明元年，復為侍中，領射聲校尉，封興平縣子，食邑五百戶，事在顏師伯傳。
entries.en: In the first year of Daming, he was again made Palace Attendant and concurrently Commandant of the Archers' Corps, enfeoffed as Viscount of Xingping with a fief of five hundred households; the affair is treated in Yan Shibo's biography.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daming, he was again made Palace Attendant and concurrently Commandant of the Archers' Corps, enfeoffed as Viscount of Xingping with a fief of five hundred households; the affair is treated in Yan Shibo's biography.

entries.zh: 三年，坐納山陰民丁彖文貨，舉為會稽郡孝廉，免官。
entries.en: In the third year, he was punished for accepting goods from Ding Tuan, a commoner of Shanyin, and recommending him as a filial and incorrupt candidate for Kuaiji commandery; he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was punished for accepting goods from Ding Tuan, a commoner of Shanyin, and recommending him as a filial and incorrupt candidate for Kuaiji commandery; he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 尋為西陽王子尚撫軍長史，又為中庶子，領左軍將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Xiyang Zishang as Stabilizing Army, then Household Mentor, and concurrently General of the Left Army.
entries.literal: Soon he was Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Xiyang Zishang as Stabilizing Army, then Household Mentor, and concurrently General of the Left Army.

entries.zh: 四年，出補豫章太守，加秩中二千石。
entries.en: In the fourth year, he went out to fill the post of Governor of Yuzhang, with rank raised to equivalent to two thousand shi.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he went out to fill the post of Governor of Yuzhang, with rank raised to equivalent to two thousand shi.

entries.zh: 五年，復還為侍中，領長水校尉，遷左衞將軍，加給事中。
entries.en: In the fifth year, he returned as Palace Attendant, concurrently Commandant of the Chang River Corps, was transferred to General of the Left Guard, and additionally made Palace Provisioner.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he returned as Palace Attendant, concurrently Commandant of the Chang River Corps, was transferred to General of the Left Guard, and additionally made Palace Provisioner.

entries.zh: 七年，轉吏部尚書，左衞如故。
entries.en: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, with his Left Guard post unchanged.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, with his Left Guard post unchanged.

entries.zh: 其年，皇太子冠，上臨宴東宮，愍孫勸顏師伯酒，師伯不飲，愍孫因相裁辱，師伯見寵於上，上常嫌愍孫以寒素凌之，因此發怒，出為海陵太守。
entries.en: That year, when the Heir Apparent received the capping ceremony, the emperor attended a feast at the Eastern Palace; Min Sun urged Yan Shibo to drink wine, but Shibo refused; Min Sun therefore abused and humiliated him; Shibo was favored by the emperor, who had often resented Min Sun for lording over him on account of his humble origins; for this the emperor became angry and sent Min Sun out as Governor of Hailing.
entries.literal: That year, when the Heir Apparent received the capping ceremony, the emperor attended a feast at the Eastern Palace; Min Sun urged Yan Shibo to drink wine, but Shibo refused; Min Sun therefore abused and humiliated him; Shibo was favored by the emperor, who had often resented Min Sun for lording over him on account of his humble origins; for this the emperor became angry and sent Min Sun out as Governor of Hailing.

entries.zh: 前廢帝即位，除御史中丞，不拜。
entries.en: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was appointed Imperial Censor but did not accept.
entries.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was appointed Imperial Censor but did not accept.

entries.zh: 復為吏部尚書。
entries.en: He was again made Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was again made Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 永光元年，徙右衞將軍，加給事中。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongguang, he was moved to General of the Right Guard and additionally made Palace Provisioner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongguang, he was moved to General of the Right Guard and additionally made Palace Provisioner.

entries.zh: 景和元年，復入為侍中，領驍騎將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Jinghe, he again entered court as Palace Attendant and concurrently General of the Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jinghe, he again entered court as Palace Attendant and concurrently General of the Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 太宗泰始元年，轉司徒左長史，冠軍將軍，南東海太守。
entries.en: In the first year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education (Situ), Champion General, and Governor of Southern Donghai.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, he was transferred to Left Army Staff Officer of the Ministry of Rites, General Who Conquers, and Governor of Southern Donghai.

entries.zh: 愍孫清整有風操，自遇甚厚，常著《妙德先生傳》以續嵇康《高士傳》以自況，曰：
entries.en: Min Sun was pure, orderly, and possessed integrity; he thought highly of himself and often wrote "Biography of Mr. Wonderful Virtue" to continue Ji Kang's "Biographies of Lofty Men" as self-portrait, saying:
entries.literal: Min Sun was pure, orderly, and had wind and integrity; he thought highly of himself and often wrote "Biography of Mr. Wonderful Virtue" to continue Ji Kang's "Biographies of Lofty Men" as self-comparison, saying:

entries.zh: 愍孫幼慕荀奉倩之為人，白世祖，求改名為粲，不許。
entries.en: Min Sun from youth admired Xun Fengqian's conduct; he told the Shizu and asked to change his name to Can; permission was refused.
entries.literal: Min Sun from youth admired Xun Fengqian's conduct; he told the Shizu and asked to change his name to Can; it was not permitted.

entries.zh: 至是言於太宗，乃改為粲，字景倩焉。
entries.en: At this time he spoke to Emperor Ming, and was then changed to Can, with style name Jingqian.
entries.literal: At this time he spoke to Emperor Ming, and then was changed to Can, with style name Jingqian.

entries.zh: 二年，遷領軍將軍，仗士三十人入六門。
entries.en: In the second year, he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief, with thirty armed soldiers entering the Six Gates.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief, with thirty armed soldiers entering the Six Gates.

entries.zh: 其年，徙中書令，領太子詹事，增封三百戶，固辭不受。
entries.en: That year he was moved to Secretariat Director, concurrently Household Mentor of the Heir; his fief was increased by three hundred households, but he firmly declined.
entries.literal: That year he was moved to Secretariat Director, concurrently Household Mentor of the Heir; his fief was increased by three hundred households, but he firmly declined and did not accept.

entries.zh: 三年，轉尚書僕射，尋領吏部。
entries.en: In the third year, he was transferred to Secretariat Vice Director and soon headed the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Secretariat Vice Director and soon headed the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 五年，加中書令，又領丹陽尹。
entries.en: In the fifth year, he was additionally made Secretariat Director and also Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was additionally made Secretariat Director and also Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 六年，上於華林園茅堂講《周易》，粲為執經。
entries.en: In the sixth year, the emperor at the thatched hall of Hualin Garden lectured on the Book of Changes; Can held the classic.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, the Emperor at the thatched hall of Hualin Garden lectured on the Book of Changes; Can held the classic.

entries.zh: 又知東宮事，徙為右僕射。
entries.en: He also oversaw Eastern Palace affairs and was moved to Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: He also knew Eastern Palace affairs and was moved to Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 七年，領太子詹事，僕射如故。
entries.en: In the seventh year, he headed the Household of the Heir as Mentor, with his vice directorship unchanged.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he headed the Household of the Heir as Mentor, with his vice directorship unchanged.

entries.zh: 未拜，遷尚書令，丹陽尹如故。
entries.en: Before he received appointment, he was moved to Secretariat Director, with his Danyang governorship unchanged.
entries.literal: Before he received appointment, he was moved to Secretariat Director, with his Danyang governorship unchanged.

entries.zh: 坐前選武衛將軍江柳為江州刺史，柳有罪，降為守尚書令。
entries.en: He was punished because in a prior selection he had appointed Jiang Liu as General of the Martial Guard and Governor of Jiang Province; Liu was guilty, and Can was reduced to acting Secretariat Director.
entries.literal: He was punished because in a prior selection he had appointed Jiang Liu as General of the Martial Guard and Governor of Jiang Province; Liu had guilt, and Can was reduced to acting Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 三年，徙尚書令，衛軍、開府如故，並固辭，服終乃受。
entries.en: In the third year, he was moved to Secretariat Director, with his Guards General and Commissioner posts unchanged; again he firmly declined, and only after mourning ended did he accept.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was moved to Secretariat Director, with his Guards General and Commissioner posts unchanged; again he firmly declined, and only after mourning ended did he accept.

entries.zh: 加侍中，進爵為侯，又不受。
entries.en: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and advanced in rank to marquis; again he did not accept.
entries.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and advanced in rank to marquis; again he did not accept.

entries.zh: 時粲與齊王、褚淵、劉秉入直，平決萬機，時謂之「四貴」。
entries.en: At the time Can, with the Prince of Qi, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing, entered duty and jointly decided state affairs; the age called them "the Four Esteemed."
entries.literal: At the time Can, with the Prince of Qi, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing, entered duty and jointly decided the ten thousand affairs; the age called them "the Four Esteemed."

entries.zh: 粲閑默寡言，不肯當事，主書每往諮決，或高詠對之，時立一意，則眾莫能改。
entries.en: Can was quiet and taciturn, unwilling to take charge of affairs; when chief clerks came to consult and decide, he sometimes answered with lofty chanting; when he once set his mind, none could change it.
entries.literal: Can was quiet and taciturn, unwilling to take charge of affairs; when chief clerks came to consult and decide, he sometimes answered with lofty chanting; when he once set an intention, none could change it.

entries.zh: 宅宇平素，器物取給。
entries.en: His dwelling was plain and simple; utensils were taken as needed.
entries.literal: His dwelling was plain and simple; utensils were taken as needed.

entries.zh: 好飲酒，善吟諷，獨酌園庭，以此自適。
entries.en: He loved wine and was skilled at chanting; alone he poured wine in the garden courtyard and thereby found his ease.
entries.literal: He loved drinking wine and was skilled at chanting; alone he poured wine in the garden courtyard and thereby found his ease.

entries.zh: 居負南郭，時杖策獨遊，素寡往來，門無雜客。
entries.en: He lived facing the southern outer wall; he often walked with a staff and roamed alone; he had always few visitors, and his gate had no miscellaneous guests.
entries.literal: He lived facing the southern outer wall; he often walked with a staff and roamed alone; he had always few comings and goings, and his gate had no miscellaneous guests.

entries.zh: 及受遺當權，四方輻湊，閒居高臥，一無所接，談客文士，所見不過一兩人。
entries.en: When he received the entrustment and held power, the four directions converged like wheel spokes; he reclined in leisure and received none of them; talking guests and literary men—those he saw did not exceed one or two.
entries.literal: When he received the entrustment and held power, the four directions converged like wheel spokes; he reclined on high in leisure and received nothing; talking guests and literary men—those he saw did not exceed one or two.

entries.zh: 順帝即位，遷中書監，司徒、侍中如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Shun took the throne, he was moved to Supervisor of the Secretariat, with his posts as Minister of Education (Situ) and Palace Attendant unchanged.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun took the throne, he was moved to Supervisor of the Secretariat, with his posts as Minister of Rites and Palace Attendant unchanged.

entries.zh: 時齊王居東府，故使粲鎮石頭。
entries.en: At the time the Prince of Qi resided at the Eastern Headquarters, so Can was sent to garrison Stone Fortress.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Qi resided at the Eastern Headquarters, so Can was sent to garrison Stone Fortress.

entries.zh: 粲素靜退，每有朝命，多不即從，逼切不得已，然後方就。
entries.en: Can was by nature quiet and retiring; whenever there was a court command he often did not immediately comply; only when pressed urgently and with no alternative would he finally go.
entries.literal: Can was by nature quiet and retiring; whenever there was a court command he often did not immediately comply; only when pressed urgently and with no alternative would he finally go.

entries.zh: 及詔移石頭，即便順旨。
entries.en: When the edict ordered his move to Stone Fortress, he at once complied with the imperial will.
entries.literal: When the edict ordered his move to Stone Fortress, he at once complied with the imperial will.

entries.zh: 有周旋人解望氣，謂粲曰：「石頭氣甚乖，往必有禍。」
entries.en: A companion skilled in reading qi omens said to Can: "The qi at Stone Fortress is very adverse; if you go there will surely be calamity."
entries.literal: A companion skilled in reading qi omens said to Can: "The qi at Stone Fortress is very adverse; if you go there will surely be calamity."

entries.zh: 粲不答。
entries.en: Can did not answer.
entries.literal: Can did not answer.

entries.zh: 又給油絡通幰車，仗士五十人入殿。
entries.en: He was also given an oiled carriage with connecting canopy and fifty armed soldiers entering the hall.
entries.literal: He was also given an oiled carriage with connecting canopy and fifty armed soldiers entering the hall.

entries.zh: 時齊王功高德重，天命有歸，粲自以身受顧託，不欲事二姓，密有異圖。
entries.en: At the time the Prince of Qi's merit was high and his virtue weighty, and Heaven's mandate was tending toward him; Can, considering that he himself had received the dying imperial entrustment, did not wish to serve two dynasties and secretly harbored a separate plan.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Qi's merit was high and his virtue weighty, and Heaven's mandate was tending toward him; Can, considering that he himself had received the dying imperial entrustment, did not wish to serve two dynasties and secretly harbored a separate plan.

entries.zh: 丹陽尹劉秉，宋代宗室，前湘州刺史王蘊，太后兄子，素好武事，並慮不見容於齊王，皆與粲相結。
entries.en: Liu Bing, Governor of Danyang, a member of the Song imperial clan, and Wang Yun, former Inspector of Xiang Province, the Empress Dowager's elder brother's son, who had always loved military affairs—all feared they would not be tolerated by the Prince of Qi—and all joined with Can in conspiracy.
entries.literal: Liu Bing, Governor of Danyang, a member of the Song imperial clan, and Wang Yun, former Inspector of Xiang Province, the Empress Dowager's elder brother's son, who had always loved military affairs—all feared they would not be tolerated by the Prince of Qi—and all joined with Can in conspiracy.

entries.zh: 將帥黃回、任候伯、孫曇瓘、王宜興、彭文之、卜伯興等，並與粲合。
entries.en: The generals Huang Hui, Ren Houbo, Sun Tanjuan, Wang Yixing, Peng Wenzhi, Bu Boxing, and others all allied with Can.
entries.literal: The generals Huang Hui, Ren Houbo, Sun Tanjuan, Wang Yixing, Peng Wenzhi, Bu Boxing, and others all allied with Can.

entries.zh: 昇明元年，荊州刺史沈攸之舉兵，齊王自詣粲，粲稱疾不見。
entries.en: In the first year of Shengming, Jing Province Inspector Shen Youzhi raised troops; the Prince of Qi personally went to Can; Can claimed illness and did not see him.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shengming, Jing Province Inspector Shen Youzhi raised troops; the Prince of Qi personally went to Can; Can claimed illness and did not see him.

entries.zh: 粲宗人通直郎袁達以為不宜示異同，粲曰：「彼若以主幼時艱，與桂陽時不異，劫我入臺，便無辭以拒。
entries.en: Can's clansman the Imperial Courier Yuan Da thought one should not display difference of view; Can said: "If he, because the sovereign is young and the times hard, treats this as no different from the Guiyang affair, and forces me into the terrace, I will have no words to refuse.
entries.literal: Can's clansman the Imperial Courier Yuan Da thought one should not display difference of view; Can said: "If he, because the sovereign is young and the times hard, does not differ from the Guiyang time, and forces me into the terrace, I will have no words to refuse.

entries.zh: 一如此，不復得出矣。」
entries.en: Once it is like this, I will not be able to come out again."
entries.literal: Once it is like this, I will not be able to come out again."

entries.zh: 時齊王入屯朝堂，秉從父弟領軍將軍韞入直門下省，伯興為直閣，黃回諸將皆率軍出新亭。
entries.en: At the time the Prince of Qi entered and garrisoned the court hall; Bing's younger paternal cousin Yun, the Commander-in-Chief, went on duty in the Chancellery; Boxing served as Direct Attendant of the Pavilion; and Huang Hui and the other generals all led troops out to Xinting.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Qi entered and garrisoned the court hall; Bing's younger paternal cousin Commander-in-Chief Yun entered duty in the Chancellery; Boxing was Direct Attendant; Huang Hui and the various generals all led armies out to Xinting.

entries.zh: 粲謀克日矯太后令，使韞、伯興率宿衛兵攻齊王於朝堂，回率軍來應。
entries.en: Can plotted on a set day to forge the Empress Dowager's order, making Yun and Boxing lead palace guards to attack the Prince of Qi in the court hall; Hui would lead the army to respond.
entries.literal: Can plotted on a set day to forge the Empress Dowager's order, making Yun and Boxing lead palace guards to attack the Prince of Qi in the court hall; Hui would lead the army to respond.

entries.zh: 秉、候伯等並赴石頭，本期夜發。
entries.en: Bing, Hou Bo, and others all went to Stone Fortress; the original plan was to set out at night.
entries.literal: Bing, Hou Bo, and others all went to Stone Fortress; the original plan was to set out at night.

entries.zh: 其日秉恇擾不知所為，晡後便束裝，未闇，載婦女席捲就粲，由此事泄。
entries.en: That day Bing was fearful and disturbed and did not know what to do; after mid-afternoon he at once packed; before dark he loaded women and bedding and went to Can; thereby the affair was leaked.
entries.literal: That day Bing was fearful and disturbed and did not know what to do; after mid-afternoon he at once packed; before dark he loaded women and bedding and went to Can; thereby the affair was leaked.

entries.zh: 先是，齊王遣將薛淵、蘇烈、王天生等領兵戍石頭，云以助粲，實禦之也。
entries.en: Earlier, the Prince of Qi had sent generals Xue Yuan, Su Lie, Wang Tiansheng, and others to lead troops to garrison Stone Fortress, saying to assist Can but in truth to guard against him.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Qi had sent generals Xue Yuan, Su Lie, Wang Tiansheng, and others to lead troops to garrison Stone Fortress, saying to assist Can but in truth to guard against him.

entries.zh: 又令腹心王敬則為直閣，與伯興共揔禁兵。
entries.en: He also made his trusted follower Wang Jingze Direct Attendant, together with Boxing jointly commanding forbidden troops.
entries.literal: He also made his trusted follower Wang Jingze Direct Attendant, together with Boxing jointly commanding forbidden troops.

entries.zh: 王蘊聞秉已奔，歎曰：「今年事敗矣！」
entries.en: Wang Yun heard Bing had already fled and sighed: "This year's affair is lost!"
entries.literal: Wang Yun heard Bing had already fled and sighed: "This year's affair is lost!"

entries.zh: 時齊王使蘊募人，已得數百，乃狼狽率部曲向石頭。
entries.en: At the time the Prince of Qi sent Yun to recruit men; he had already gotten several hundred; then in distress he led his subordinates toward Stone Fortress.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Qi sent Yun to recruit men; he had already gotten several hundred; then in distress he led his subordinates toward Stone Fortress.

entries.zh: 本期開南門，時已闇夜，薛淵等據門射之，蘊謂粲已敗，即便散走。
entries.en: The original plan was to open the southern gate; it was already dark night; Xue Yuan and others held the gate and shot at them; Yun thought Can had already been defeated and at once scattered and fled.
entries.literal: The original plan was to open the southern gate; it was already dark night; Xue Yuan and others held the gate and shot at them; Yun thought Can had already been defeated and at once scattered and fled.

entries.zh: 齊王以報敬則，率所領收蘊殺之，并誅伯興。
entries.en: The Prince of Qi reported to Jingze; he led those under him to seize and kill Yun, and Boxing was also executed.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qi reported to Jingze; he led those under him to seize and kill Yun, and Boxing was also executed.

entries.zh: 又遣軍主戴僧靜向石頭助薛淵，自倉門得入。
entries.en: He also sent Army Commander Dai Sengjing toward Stone Fortress to assist Xue Yuan; he entered from the Granary Gate.
entries.literal: He also sent Army Commander Dai Sengjing toward Stone Fortress to assist Xue Yuan; he entered from the Granary Gate.

entries.zh: 時粲與秉等列兵登東門，僧靜分兵攻府西門。
entries.en: At the time Can and Bing and others arrayed troops and ascended the eastern gate; Sengjing divided troops to attack the headquarters' western gate.
entries.literal: At the time Can and Bing and others arrayed troops and ascended the eastern gate; Sengjing divided troops to attack the headquarters' western gate.

entries.zh: 粲與秉欲還赴府，既下城，列燭自照，僧靜挺身闇往，粲子最覺有異人，以身衛粲，僧靜直前斬之，父子俱殞，左右各分散。
entries.en: Can and Bing wished to return to the headquarters; having descended the wall, they set out candles to illuminate themselves; Sengjing advanced straight through the dark; Can's son Zui felt there was an unusual man and used his body to protect Can; Sengjing went straight forward and cut him down; father and son both perished; attendants each scattered.
entries.literal: Can and Bing wished to return to the headquarters; having descended the wall, they set out candles to illuminate themselves; Sengjing straightened his body in the dark and went forward; Can's son Zui felt there was an unusual man and used his body to protect Can; Sengjing went straight forward and cut him down; father and son both perished; attendants each scattered.

entries.zh: 粲死時，年五十八。
entries.en: When Can died, he was fifty-eight.
entries.literal: When Can died, he was fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 任候伯等其夜並乘輕舸，自新亭赴石頭，聞粲敗，乃馳還；
entries.en: Ren Houbo and others that night all rode light boats from Xinting toward Stone Fortress; hearing Can was defeated, they galloped back;
entries.literal: Ren Houbo and others that night all rode light boats from Xinting toward Stone Fortress; hearing Can was defeated, they galloped back;

entries.zh: 其後並誅。
entries.en: afterward they were all executed.
entries.literal: afterward they were all executed.

entries.zh: 秉事在《宗室傳》。
entries.en: Bing's affair is in the "Imperial Clan Biography."
entries.literal: Bing's affair is in the "Imperial Clan Biography."

entries.zh: 列傳第四十九 袁粲
entries.en: Biography Number Forty-Nine: Yuan Can
entries.literal: Biography 49: Yuan Can

entries.zh: 高祖起自匹庶，知民事艱難，及登庸作宰，留心吏職，而王略外舉，未遑內務。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu rose from humble origins and understood how hard life was for ordinary people. Once he took power as chief minister, he kept a close eye on local administration, but with his grand strategy focused abroad he had little time for domestic governance.
entries.literal: The Founder Emperor rose from commoner rank, knew the hardship of the people's affairs; when he was raised to serve as chief minister, he paid attention to officials' duties, but royal strategy looked outward and he had no leisure for internal administration.

entries.zh: 奉師之費，日耗千金，播茲寬簡，雖所未暇，而絀華屏欲，以儉抑身，左右無幸謁之私，閨房無文綺之飾，故能戎車歲駕，邦甸不憂。
entries.en: Army expenses ran to a thousand gold a day, and he had not yet found time to carry out the full program of leniency and simplicity he envisioned; still he cut back display, checked his desires, and practiced austerity in his own life. No favorite at court enjoyed private access, and his inner quarters held no silk brocade. Thus he could campaign every year without overwhelming the realm.
entries.literal: The cost of maintaining the army consumed a thousand gold daily; to spread such leniency and simplicity he had no leisure, yet he reined in splendor and barred indulgence, restraining himself through frugality; those at his side had no privilege of private audiences, inner chambers had no brocade ornaments; therefore the war chariot could set out year after year yet the realm was not troubled.

entries.zh: 太祖幼而寬仁，入纂大業，及難興陝方，六戎薄伐，命將動師，經略司、兗，費由府實，役不及民。
entries.en: Emperor Wen was gentle and magnanimous from childhood. When he inherited the throne and trouble flared in the northwest, with the northern peoples pressing south, he sent generals to campaign in the Si and Yan regions, paying for it all from the state treasury so that the burden did not fall on the common people.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen was from youth broad and benevolent; he entered to succeed the great enterprise; when trouble arose in the Shaan region and the six Rong pressed in attack, he ordered generals to move troops, planning strategy in Si and Yan provinces; expenses came from the treasury stores and corvée labor did not reach the people.

entries.zh: 自此區宇宴安，方內無事，三十年間，氓庶蕃息，奉上供徭，止於歲賦，晨出莫歸，自事而已。
entries.en: Thereafter the empire enjoyed peace and the heartland knew no unrest. For thirty years the population grew; what the people owed the state was limited to the annual land tax. They left at dawn and came home at dusk, minding only their own work.
entries.literal: From this the realm was tranquil and secure, within the four quarters there was no trouble; for thirty years the common people multiplied; what they offered to the state in labor and levies stopped at the annual tax; they went out at dawn and returned at dusk, attending only to their own affairs.

entries.zh: 守宰之職，以六期為斷，雖沒世不徙，未及曩時，而民有所係，吏無苟得。
entries.en: Prefects and magistrates served fixed six-year terms. Though an appointee might hold a post for life without transfer, this fell short of earlier practice; still the people had officials they could depend on, and magistrates could not seize profit as they pleased.
entries.literal: The office of prefect and magistrate was fixed at six-year terms; although one might serve until death without transfer, it did not match former times, yet the people had someone to rely on and officials could not grab gains at will.

entries.zh: 家給人足，即事雖難，轉死溝渠，于時可免。
entries.en: Households were supplied and people had enough to live on; even when times were hard, the fate of starving by the roadside could, in that age, largely be avoided.
entries.literal: Households had enough and people were provided for; even when affairs were difficult, dying abandoned in ditches and drains could at that time be avoided.

entries.zh: 凡百戶之鄉，有市之邑，歌謠舞蹈，觸處成群，蓋宋世之極盛也。
entries.en: In hamlets of a hundred households and in market towns alike, people sang and danced; crowds formed wherever one went. This was the Song dynasty at its height.
entries.literal: In every village of a hundred households, in every market town, songs and dances—wherever one touched, they gathered in groups; this was roughly the greatest flourishing of the Song age.

entries.zh: 暨元嘉二十七年，北狄南侵，戎役大起，傾資掃蓄，猶有未供，於是深賦厚斂，天下騷動。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia (450), the northern peoples invaded the south. Military levies surged; families spent their savings to the last coin and still could not meet the demand. Heavy taxes followed, and the whole empire was thrown into unrest.
entries.literal: When the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia arrived, northern barbarians invaded south; military service rose greatly; pouring out funds and sweeping away savings still could not meet demand; then deep taxes and heavy levies were imposed and the realm was thrown into turmoil.

entries.zh: 自茲至於孝建，兵連不息，以區區之江東，地方不至數千里，戶不盈百萬，薦之以師旅，因之以凶荒，宋氏之盛，自此衰矣。
entries.en: From then until the Xiaojian era (454–456), war never ceased. The southeast alone, a territory of less than a few thousand li and fewer than a million households, was burdened with armies and then struck by famine. The Song dynasty's prosperity waned from that point.
entries.literal: From this until Xiaojian, warfare continued without cease; with the mere Jiangdong region, territory not reaching several thousand li, households not filling a million—add military expeditions on top, follow with famine and disaster—the flourishing of the Song house from this declined.

entries.zh: 晉世諸帝，多處內房，朝宴所臨，東西二堂而已。
entries.en: Jin emperors mostly lived within the inner palace; court audiences and banquets were held in only the Eastern and Western halls.
entries.literal: The emperors of the Jin age mostly dwelt in inner chambers; for morning audiences and banquets they attended only the Eastern and Western halls.

entries.zh: 孝武末年，清暑方構，高祖受命，無所改作，所居唯稱西殿，不制嘉名；
entries.en: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Clear Summer Palace was under construction. When Gaozu took the throne he changed nothing, calling his residence simply the Western Hall and giving it no grand title;
entries.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu, the Clear Summer Palace was just being built; when the Founder Emperor received the Mandate he made no alterations, calling his residence only the Western Hall and giving it no fine name;

entries.zh: 太祖因之，亦有合殿之稱。
entries.en: Emperor Wen followed his example, and the hall was also called the Combined Hall.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen followed this, and there was also the name Combined Hall.

entries.zh: 及世祖承統，制度奢廣，犬馬餘菽粟，土木衣綈繡，追陋前規，更造正光、玉燭、紫極諸殿。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, luxury spread through the court. Horses and dogs had grain to spare while palaces were draped in silk; deeming earlier standards mean, he built anew the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded to the succession, institutions were extravagant and broad; dogs and horses had surplus grain and millet, earth and wood wore silk gauze and brocade; pursuing what he deemed shabby in former rules, he newly built the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls and others.

entries.zh: 雕欒綺節，珠窗網戶，嬖女幸臣，賜傾府藏，竭四海不供其欲，單民命未快其心。
entries.en: Carved beams bore brocade ornament; pearl windows and latticed doors adorned the halls. Favorites and trusted ministers received gifts that drained the treasury; the wealth of the entire realm could not satisfy their appetites, and the common people's very lives could not content them.
entries.literal: Carved beams with brocade ornament, pearl windows and latticed doors; favored women and trusted ministers received gifts that emptied the treasury; exhausting the four seas could not supply their desires, and the lives of common people could not satisfy their hearts.

entries.zh: 太宗繼阼，彌篤浮侈，恩不恤下，以至橫流。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming succeeded him, extravagance grew worse still. Favor no longer reached those below, and disorder spread like a flood.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne, even more devoted to frivolity and extravagance, grace not caring for those below, until it reached flood tide.

entries.zh: 蒞民之官，遷變歲屬，灶不得黔，席未暇暖，蒲、密之化，事未易階。
entries.en: Magistrates who governed the people were rotated every year; their stoves never blackened and their mats never grew warm. The gentle governance once seen under officials such as Pu and Mi could no longer be achieved.
entries.literal: Officials who governed the people changed with each year's turn; the stove could not be blackened, the mat had no time to grow warm—the transformation of Pu and Mi was not easily attained.

entries.zh: 豈徒吏不及古，民偽于昔，蓋由為上所擾，致治莫從。
entries.en: It was not merely that officials fell short of those of old or that the people had grown deceitful. The court itself disrupted governance, leaving no way to restore order.
entries.literal: Was it only that officials did not match antiquity and the people were false compared with the past? It was fundamentally because they were disturbed by those above, so that achieving good government had no path to follow.

entries.zh: 今採其風迹粗著者，以為良吏篇云。
entries.en: I now select those whose reputations stand out clearly enough to compose this chapter on good magistrates.
entries.literal: Now I gather those whose conduct and traces are roughly notable, to make the 'Good Officials' chapter.

entries.zh: 出為使持節、都督交、廣二州諸軍事、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, area commander of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Establishes Might, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander over military affairs of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Establishes Might, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖謂人曰：「王鎮之少著清績，必將繼美吳隱之。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu told his court: "Wang Zhenzhi has been known for integrity since his youth; he will surely follow in the footsteps of Wu Yinshi.
entries.literal: The Founder Emperor said to others: "Wang Zhenzhi from youth has shown a record of purity; he will surely continue the fine reputation of Wu Yinshi.

entries.zh: 嶺南之弊，非此不康也。」
entries.en: The troubles of the far south cannot be remedied without a man like him."
entries.literal: The ills of Lingnan, without this man, will not be made secure."

entries.zh: 在鎮不受俸祿，蕭然無所營。
entries.en: In his post he refused his salary and lived in austere simplicity, pursuing no private gain.
entries.literal: In his post he did not accept salary, desolate and with nothing he pursued.

entries.zh: 去官之日，不異始至。
entries.en: When he left office he was no richer than the day he had arrived.
entries.literal: On the day he left office, he was no different from when he first arrived.

entries.zh: 高祖初建相國府，以為諮議參軍，領錄事。
entries.en: When Gaozu first established his chancellor's office, Zhenzhi was made consulting adjutant and chief recorder.
entries.literal: When the Founder Emperor first established the Chancellor's Office, he was made Consulting Adjutant and concurrently Recorder.

entries.zh: 善於吏職，嚴而不殘。
entries.en: He excelled at administrative work, strict but never cruel.
entries.literal: He was skilled in official duties, strict but not cruel.

entries.zh: 遷宋臺祠部尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to Minister of Rites of the Song regime.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites of the Song Terrace.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，鎮之以腳患自陳，出為輔國將軍、琅邪太守，遷宣訓衛尉，領本州大中正。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Zhenzhi cited a foot ailment and left the capital to serve as General Who Assists the State and administrator of Langye, then became commandant of the Xuanxun guard and grand rectifier of his native province.
entries.literal: When the Founder Emperor ascended the throne, Zhenzhi reported himself on account of foot ailment; he went out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Langye, was transferred to Commandant of the Xuanxun Guard, and concurrently held Grand Rectifier of the original province.

entries.zh: 永初三年，卒官，時年六十六。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongchu (422) he died in office at the age of sixty-six.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died in office, age sixty-six.

entries.zh: 弟弘之，在《隱逸傳》。
entries.en: His younger brother Hongzhi is treated in the chapter on recluses.
entries.literal: His younger brother Hongzhi is in the 'Recluses' biography.

entries.zh: 杜慧度，交趾朱䳒人也。
entries.en: Du Huidu was from Zhuying in Jiaozhi commandery.
entries.literal: Du Huidu was a man of Zhuying in Jiaozhi.

entries.zh: 本屬京兆。
entries.en: The clan was originally registered in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: His clan originally belonged to Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 曾祖元，為寧浦太守，遂居交趾。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Du Yuan served as administrator of Ningpu and then settled in Jiaozhi.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Yuan was Administrator of Ningpu and thereafter settled in Jiaozhi.

entries.zh: 父瑗，字道言，仕州府為日南、九德、交趾太守。
entries.en: His father Du Yuan, courtesy name Daoyan, served the province as administrator of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi in succession.
entries.literal: His father Yuan, styled Daoyan, served the provincial administration as Administrator of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi in turn.

entries.zh: 初，九真太守李遜父子勇壯有權力，威制交土，聞刺史騰遯之當至，分遣二子斷遏水陸津要。
entries.en: Earlier, Li Xun, administrator of Jiuzhen, and his sons were powerful local strongmen who dominated the region. Learning that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was on his way, they sent two sons to seize the strategic passes by land and water.
entries.literal: At first Li Xun, Administrator of Jiuzhen, father and sons, were brave and strong with power, dominating Jiaozhi by might; hearing that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was about to arrive, they separately sent two sons to block and hold the water and land passes.

entries.zh: 瑗收眾斬遜，州境獲寧。
entries.en: Yuan raised troops, killed Li Xun, and restored peace to the province.
entries.literal: Yuan gathered troops and beheaded Xun; the province's territory was secured in peace.

entries.zh: 除龍驤將軍。
entries.en: He was appointed Dragon-soaring General.
entries.literal: He was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 遯之在州十餘年，與林邑累相攻伐。
entries.en: Dunzhi spent more than ten years in the province, fighting repeated campaigns against Linyi.
entries.literal: Dunzhi was in the province more than ten years and with Linyi repeatedly attacked and fought each other.

entries.zh: 遯之將北還，林邑王范胡達攻破日南、九德、九真三郡，遂圍州城。
entries.en: As Dunzhi prepared to return north, the king of Linyi, Fan Huda, overran Rinan, Jiude, and Jiuzhen and besieged the provincial capital.
entries.literal: When Dunzhi was about to return north, the King of Linyi Fan Huda broke through the three commanderies Rinan, Jiude, and Jiuzhen, and then besieged the provincial capital.

entries.zh: 時遯之去已遠，瑗與第三子玄之悉力固守，多設權策，累戰，大破之。
entries.en: Dunzhi was already far away. Yuan and his third son Xuanzhi defended the city with all their strength, using many stratagems through repeated battles until they routed the enemy.
entries.literal: At that time Dunzhi had already gone far; Yuan and his third son Xuanzhi exerted all strength to defend firmly, set many stratagems, fought repeatedly, and routed them greatly.

entries.zh: 追討於九真、日南。
entries.en: They pursued the enemy into Jiuzhen and Rinan.
entries.literal: They pursued and attacked in Jiuzhen and Rinan.

entries.zh: 連捷，故胡達走還林邑。
entries.en: Victory followed victory until Fan Huda fled back to Linyi.
entries.literal: Victories followed in succession, so Huda fled back to Linyi.

entries.zh: 乃以瑗為龍驤將軍、交州刺史。
entries.en: Yuan was then appointed Dragon-soaring General and inspector of Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yuan was made General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 義旗進號冠軍將軍。
entries.en: When Liu Yu raised the banner of righteous restoration, Yuan was promoted to Champion General.
entries.literal: When the Banner of Righteousness rose, his title was advanced to Champion General.

entries.zh: 盧循竊據廣州，遣使通好，瑗斬之。
entries.en: Lu Xun had seized Guangzhou and sent envoys offering alliance; Yuan had them executed.
entries.literal: Lu Xun seized and held Guangzhou and sent envoys to seek friendship; Yuan beheaded them.

entries.zh: 義熙六年，年八十四，卒，追贈右將軍，本官如故。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yixi (410), at the age of eighty-four, he died and was posthumously made Right General with his former titles confirmed.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yixi, age eighty-four, he died; posthumously he was given the Right General, his original office unchanged.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，進號輔國將軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Huidu was promoted to General Who Assists the State.
entries.literal: When the Founder Emperor ascended the throne, Huidu's title was advanced to General Who Assists the State.

entries.zh: 其年，率文武萬人南討林邑，所殺過半，前後被抄略，悉得還本。
entries.en: That same year he led ten thousand troops south against Linyi, killing more than half the enemy force and recovering all the people who had been carried off in earlier raids.
entries.literal: That year he led ten thousand civil and military men south to attack Linyi; more than half were killed; those who had earlier been raided and carried off all were returned to their homes.

entries.zh: 林邑乞降，輸生口、大象、金銀、古貝等，乃釋之。
entries.en: Linyi sued for peace, offering captives, elephants, gold, silver, and cowrie shells, and Huidu accepted their surrender.
entries.literal: Linyi begged to surrender, presenting captives, elephants, gold and silver, ancient cowries, and the like; he then released them.

entries.zh: 遣長史江悠奉表獻捷。
entries.en: He sent his chief clerk Jiang You to the capital with a report of victory.
entries.literal: He sent Chief Clerk Jiang You to present a memorial reporting victory.

entries.zh: 慧度布衣蔬食，儉約質素，能彈琴，頗好《莊》、《老》。
entries.en: Huidu dressed in plain cloth and ate simple fare, living frugally and without pretension. He played the zither and was fond of the Zhuangzi and Laozi.
entries.literal: Huidu wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, was frugal and simple in substance, could play the zither, and rather favored the Zhuangzi and Laozi.

entries.zh: 禁斷淫祀，崇脩學校。
entries.en: He suppressed illicit cults and promoted the schools.
entries.literal: He forbade and cut off improper sacrifices and honored and repaired schools.

entries.zh: 歲荒民饑，則以私祿賑給。
entries.en: In years of famine he used his private salary to feed the people.
entries.literal: When the year was barren and the people hungry, he used his private salary to relieve and supply them.

entries.zh: 為政纖密，有如治家，由是威惠沾洽，姦盜不起，乃至城門不夜閉，道不拾遺。
entries.en: He governed with the meticulous care of a household manager, so that his authority and kindness reached everyone. Crime vanished; city gates stood open at night and no one picked up lost goods on the road.
entries.literal: In governing he was meticulous, as if managing a household; thereby authority and kindness permeated, treachery and theft did not arise, until city gates were not closed at night and lost things were not picked up on the roads.

entries.zh: 少帝景平元年，卒，時年五十，追贈左將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Jingping (423), under Emperor Shao, he died at the age of fifty and was posthumously made Left General.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingping under Emperor Shao, he died, age fifty; posthumously he was given the Left General.

entries.zh: 以慧度長子員外散騎侍郎弘文為振威將軍、刺史。
entries.en: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat Outside the Palace, was appointed General Who Quells Might and inspector of Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat Outside the Palace, was made General Who Quells Might and Inspector.

entries.zh: 初，高祖北征關、洛，慧度板弘文為鷹揚將軍，流民督護，配兵三千，北係大軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu marched north against Guanzhong and Luoyang, Huidu commissioned Hongwen as General of Soaring Valor and protector of displaced persons, assigning him three thousand men to join the northern campaign.
entries.literal: At first, when the Founder Emperor campaigned north to Guan and Luo, Huidu commissioned Hongwen as General of Soaring Valor, Protector of Displaced Persons, with three thousand troops assigned, to join the northern army.

entries.zh: 行至廣州，關、洛已平，乃歸。
entries.en: He reached Guangzhou only to learn that Guanzhong and Luoyang had already been pacified, and he turned back.
entries.literal: When he reached Guangzhou, Guan and Luo had already been pacified, so he returned.

entries.zh: 統府板弘文行九真太守。
entries.en: The provincial headquarters appointed him acting administrator of Jiuzhen.
entries.literal: The area headquarters commissioned Hongwen to act as Administrator of Jiuzhen.

entries.zh: 及繼父為刺史，亦以寬和得眾，襲爵龍編侯。
entries.en: When he succeeded his father as inspector, he too won the people's loyalty through leniency and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.
entries.literal: When he succeeded his father as Inspector, he also won the people through leniency and harmony, and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.

entries.zh: 太祖元嘉四年，以廷尉王徽為交州刺史，弘文就徴。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Yuanjia (427), Emperor Wen appointed Wang Hui, Minister of Justice, as inspector of Jiaozhou, and Hongwen was recalled.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Wang Hui the Minister of Justice was made Inspector of Jiaozhou, and Hongwen was summoned to yield the post.

entries.zh: 會得重疾，牽以就路，親舊見其患篤，勸表待病癒。
entries.en: He fell gravely ill but was compelled to set out anyway. Friends and relatives, seeing how serious his condition was, urged him to petition the throne for leave to recover first.
entries.literal: He happened to contract a severe illness but was dragged along on the journey; relatives and friends seeing his illness grave urged him to memorialize and wait until the illness healed.

entries.zh: 弘文曰：「吾世荷皇恩，杖節三世，常欲投軀帝庭，以報所荷。
entries.en: Hongwen said: "Our family has borne the imperial favor for generations. For three generations we have held the staff of authority, and I have long wished to give my life at court in repayment.
entries.literal: Hongwen said: "Our family for generations has borne the imperial grace; bearing the staff of authority for three generations, I have always wished to cast my body before the imperial court to repay what I have borne.

entries.zh: 況親被徵命，而可宴然者乎！
entries.en: Now that I have been personally summoned, how can I remain at ease?
entries.literal: How much more when I have personally received a summons—can I remain at ease!

entries.zh: 如其顛沛，此乃命也。」
entries.en: If hardship should overtake me on the road, that is fate."
entries.literal: If I should suffer hardship and ruin, that is fate."

entries.zh: 弘文母既年老，見弘文輿疾就路，不忍分別，相與俱行。
entries.en: Hongwen's mother was elderly. Seeing her son set out in a sickbed carriage, she could not bear to part from him and traveled with him.
entries.literal: Hongwen's mother was already old; seeing Hongwen take to his carriage ill and set out on the road, she could not bear to part and traveled together with him.

entries.zh: 到廣州，遂卒。
entries.en: He reached Guangzhou and died there.
entries.literal: When he reached Guangzhou, he thereupon died.

entries.zh: 臨死，遣弟弘猷詣京，朝廷甚哀之。
entries.en: Before he died he sent his younger brother Hongyou to the capital; the court mourned him deeply.
entries.literal: On the verge of death he sent his younger brother Hongyou to the capital; the court greatly mourned him.

entries.zh: 江秉之字玄叔，濟陽考城人也。
entries.en: Jiang Bingzhi, courtesy name Xuanshu, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
entries.literal: Jiang Bingzhi, styled Xuanshu, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

entries.zh: 祖逌，晉太常。
entries.en: His grandfather Jiang You was grand minister of ceremonies under Jin.
entries.literal: His grandfather You was Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Jin.

entries.zh: 父纂，給事中。
entries.en: His father Jiang Zuan was attendant within the yellow gates.
entries.literal: His father Zuan was Attendant within the Yellow Gates.

entries.zh: 秉之少孤，弟妹七人，並皆幼稚，撫育姻娶，罄其心力。
entries.en: Bingzhi lost his father early. He had seven younger siblings, all still young, and he raised them and arranged their marriages, exhausting all his strength.
entries.literal: Bingzhi lost his father early; he had seven younger siblings, all still young. He raised them and arranged their marriages, exhausting all his heart and strength.

entries.zh: 初為劉穆之丹陽前軍府參軍。
entries.en: He first served as adjutant on Liu Muzhi's Danyang vanguard army staff.
entries.literal: At first he was Adjutant on Liu Muzhi's Danyang Vanguard Army staff.

entries.zh: 高祖督徐州，轉主簿，仍為世子中軍參軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu governed Xuzhou, Bingzhi was transferred to chief clerk and then served as adjutant in the heir's central army.
entries.literal: When Gaozu governed Xuzhou, he was transferred to Chief Clerk and then served as Adjutant in the Heir's Central Army.

entries.zh: 宋受禪，隨例為員外散騎侍郎，補太子詹事丞。
entries.en: When the Song received the mandate, he became attendant cavalier at the secretariat outside the palace by precedent and was appointed aide to the grand tutor of the heir.
entries.literal: When the Song received the mandate, following precedent he became Attendant Cavalier at the Secretariat Outside the Palace and was appointed Aide to the Grand Tutor of the Heir.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，入為尚書都官郎，出為永世、烏程令，以善政著名東土。
entries.en: When Emperor Shaodi ascended the throne, he entered office as gentleman of the punishments section and was sent out as magistrate of Yongshi and Wucheng, becoming famed in the eastern region for good governance.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shaodi ascended the throne, he entered office as Gentleman of the Punishments Section in the Secretariat and was sent out as Magistrate of Yongshi and Wucheng, becoming famed in the eastern region for good governance.

entries.zh: 徵建康令，為治嚴察，京邑肅然。
entries.en: Summoned as magistrate of Jiankang, his governance was strict and thorough, and the capital became orderly.
entries.literal: Summoned as Magistrate of Jiankang, his governance was strict and thorough, and the capital became orderly.

entries.zh: 殷景仁為領軍，請為司馬。
entries.en: When Yin Jingren was leader of the army, he requested Bingzhi as his marshal.
entries.literal: When Yin Jingren was Leader of the Army, he requested Bingzhi as Marshal.

entries.zh: 復出為山陰令，民戶三萬，政事煩擾，訟訴殷積，階庭常數百人，秉之御繁以簡，常得無事。
entries.en: Sent out again as magistrate of Shanyin, a district of thirty thousand households where affairs were complex and lawsuits piled up and the courtyard often held several hundred people, Bingzhi managed complexity through simplicity and usually kept the office untroubled.
entries.literal: Sent out again as Magistrate of Shanyin, with thirty thousand households, affairs were complex and lawsuits piled up; the courtyard often held several hundred people. Bingzhi managed complexity through simplicity and usually had no trouble.

entries.zh: 宋世唯顧覬之亦以省務著績，其餘雖復刑政脩理，而未能簡事。
entries.en: In the Song dynasty only Gu Jizhi was also noted for streamlining office work; the others, though their penal administration was well ordered, could not simplify affairs.
entries.literal: In the Song age only Gu Jizhi was also noted for streamlining office work; the others, though their penal administration was well ordered, could not simplify affairs.

entries.zh: 以在縣有能，遷補新安太守。
entries.en: Because of his ability as magistrate, he was transferred and appointed administrator of Xin'an.
entries.literal: Because of his ability in the district, he was transferred and appointed Administrator of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 時有北地傅僧祐、潁川陳瑉、高平張祐，並以吏才見知。
entries.en: At that time Fu Sengyou of Beidi, Chen Min of Yingchuan, and Zhang You of Gaoping were all known for administrative talent.
entries.literal: At the time there were Fu Sengyou of Beidi, Chen Min of Yingchuan, and Zhang You of Gaoping, all known for talent in administration.

entries.zh: 僧祐事在《臧燾傳》。
entries.en: Sengyou's career is treated in the biography of Zang Tao.
entries.literal: Sengyou's affairs are in the biography of Zang Tao.

entries.zh: 瑉為吳令，善發姦伏，境內以為神明。
entries.en: Chen Min served as magistrate of Wu and excelled at uncovering hidden crimes; the people regarded him as almost supernatural.
entries.literal: Min was Magistrate of Wu, skilled at exposing hidden wrongdoing; within the borders he was regarded as a spirit.

entries.zh: 祐祖父湛，晉孝武世，以才學為中書侍郎，光祿勳。
entries.en: Zhang You's grandfather Zhang Zhan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, rose by learning to secretariat gentleman and grand minister of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: You's grandfather Zhan, in the age of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, by talent and learning was Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Minister of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 祐歷臨安、武康、錢塘令，並著能名，宋世言長吏者，以三人為首。
entries.en: Zhang You served as magistrate of Lin'an, Wukang, and Qiantang in turn, earning a reputation for ability in each. In the Song dynasty these three were ranked foremost among district magistrates.
entries.literal: You successively held the magistracies of Lin'an, Wukang, and Qiantang, in all gaining a name for ability; when the Song age spoke of chief magistrates, these three men were placed first.

entries.zh: 元嘉中，高平太守潘詞，有清節。
entries.en: During the Yuanjia era Pan Ci, administrator of Gaoping, was known for integrity.
entries.literal: During Yuanjia, Pan Ci, Administrator of Gaoping, had pure integrity.

entries.zh: 子亮為昌慮令，亦著廉名，大明中，為徐州刺史劉道隆所表。
entries.en: His son Liang served as magistrate of Changlu and was also known for integrity; in the Daming era he was recommended by Liu Daolong, inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: His son Liang was Magistrate of Changlu and also had a name for purity; in Daming he was recommended by Liu Daolong, Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 世祖世，吳郡陸法真歷官有清節，嘗為劉秀之安北錄事參軍。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xiaowu, Lu Fazhen of Wu commandery held several posts marked by integrity and once served as recorder on Liu Xiuzhi's staff as army pacifying the north.
entries.literal: In the age of Emperor Xiaowu, Lu Fazhen of Wu commandery in successive offices had pure integrity and once was Recorder of Liu Xiuzhi's Army Pacifying the North.

entries.zh: 泰山羊希與安北諮議參軍孫詵書曰：「足下同僚似有陸錄事者，此生東南名地，又張玄外孫，持身至清，雅有志節。
entries.en: Yang Xi of Taishan wrote to Sun Shen, consulting adjutant pacifying the north: "Among your colleagues there seems to be a Recorder Lu. He comes from a distinguished southeastern family and is the maternal grandson of Zhang Xuan. He is utterly incorrupt and has lofty principles.
entries.literal: Yang Xi of Taishan wrote to Sun Shen, Consulting Adjutant Pacifying the North: "Among your colleagues below there seems to be Recorder Lu; this man's family is a famous house of the southeast, and he is also the maternal grandson of Zhang Xuan—he holds himself in utmost purity and has lofty will and integrity.

entries.zh: 年高官下，秉操不衰，計當日夕相與申意。」
entries.en: Though advanced in years he holds a humble post, yet his integrity has not faded. I expect we shall speak together soon."
entries.literal: His years are high yet his office low; he holds his conduct undiminished—I expect we shall before long share our feelings with each other."

entries.zh: 太宗初，為南海太守，卒官。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was appointed administrator of Nanhai and died in office.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was Administrator of Nanhai and died in office.

entries.zh: 列傳第五十二 良吏
entries.en: Biography 52: Good Magistrates
entries.literal: Biography 52: Good Officials

entries.zh: 先是晉末，金城東允街縣胡人乞伏乾歸擁部眾據洮河、罕幵，自號隴西公。
entries.en: Earlier, at the end of Jin, the Hu leader Qifu Gangui of Yunjie county east of Jincheng gathered his tribesmen, seized the Tao River region and Hanqian, and styled himself Duke of Longxi.
entries.literal: Earlier, at the end of Jin, the Hu man Qifu Gangui of Yunjie county east of Jincheng gathered tribesmen, held the Tao River and Hanqian, and styled himself Duke of Longxi.

entries.zh: 乾歸死，子熾磐立，遣使詣晉朝歸順，以為使持節、都督河西諸軍事、平西將軍，公如故。
entries.en: When Gangui died, his son Chipan succeeded and sent envoys to the Jin court to submit; he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Hexi, and General Who Pacifies the West, retaining his ducal title.
entries.literal: Gangui died; his son Chipan succeeded, sent envoys to the Jin court to submit, and was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Hexi, General Who Pacifies the West, duke as before.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，進號安西大將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Chipan's title was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the West.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 熾磐死，子茂蔓立。
entries.en: When Chipan died, his son Maoman succeeded.
entries.literal: Chipan died; his son Maoman succeeded.

entries.zh: [8]慕璝前後屢遣軍擊，茂蔓率部落東奔隴右，慕璝據有其地。
entries.en: [8] Mugui repeatedly sent armies against him; Maoman led his tribes in flight east to the Long region, and Mugui seized his lands.
entries.literal: [8] Mugui repeatedly sent armies to attack; Maoman led his tribes east fleeing to the right of Long, and Mugui seized his territory.

entries.zh: 是歲，赫連定於長安為索虜拓跋燾所攻，擁秦戶口十餘萬西次罕幵，欲向涼州，慕璝距擊，大破之，生擒定。
entries.en: That year Helian Ding at Chang'an was attacked by the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao; Ding gathered more than a hundred thousand Qin households and moved west to encamp at Hanqian, intending to march on Liangzhou. Mugui intercepted him, inflicted a crushing defeat, and took Ding alive.
entries.literal: That year Helian Ding at Chang'an was attacked by the Northern Wei barbarian Tuoba Tao; he gathered more than a hundred thousand Qin households and moved west to encamp at Hanqian, intending to go toward Liangzhou. Mugui resisted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat and capturing Ding alive.

entries.zh: 燾遣使求，慕璝以定與之。
entries.en: Tao sent envoys to demand Ding; Mugui handed him over.
entries.literal: Tao sent envoys to request him; Mugui gave Ding over to them.

entries.zh: 九年，慕璝遣司馬趙敍奉貢獻，幷言二萬人捷。
entries.en: In the ninth year Mugui sent Chief Clerk Zhao Xu with tribute and reported a victory over twenty thousand enemy troops.
entries.literal: In the ninth year Mugui sent Chief Clerk Zhao Xu to present tribute and also reported a victory over twenty thousand men.

entries.zh: 太祖加其使持節、散騎常侍、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、西秦河二州刺史、領護羌校尉，進爵隴西王。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu further appointed him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Western Qin and He, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, and advanced him to King of Longxi.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizu added for him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Governor of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, and advanced his rank to King of Longxi.

entries.zh: 弟慕延為平東將軍，慕璝兄樹洛干子拾寅為平北將軍，阿豺子煒代鎮軍將軍。
entries.en: His younger brother Muyan was made General Who Pacifies the East; Shiyin, son of Mugui's elder brother Shuluoqian, was made General Who Pacifies the North; and Wei, son of Achai, was made Acting General of the Garrison Army.
entries.literal: His younger brother Muyan was made General Who Pacifies the East; Mugui's elder brother Shuluoqian's son Shiyin was made General Who Pacifies the North; Achai's son Wei was made Acting General of the Garrison Army.

entries.zh: 詔慕璝南國將士，昔沒在佛佛者，並悉致。
entries.en: An edict instructed Mugui to return all officers and soldiers of the southern states who had formerly been lost among the Fofo.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Mugui: among the officers and soldiers of the southern states who in the past were lost among the Fofo, bring them all back.

entries.zh: 慕璝遣送朱昕之等五十五戶，一百五十四人。
entries.en: Mugui sent back Zhu Xinzhi and others—fifty-five households, one hundred fifty-four persons in all.
entries.literal: Mugui sent back Zhu Xinzhi and others—fifty-five households, one hundred fifty-four persons.

entries.zh: 慕延死，拾寅自立。
entries.en: When Muyan died, Shiyin took power on his own authority.
entries.literal: Muyan died; Shiyin established himself on his own.

entries.zh: 二十九年，以拾寅為使持節、督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、安西將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史、河南王。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year Shiyin was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, Governor of Western Qin and He, and King of Henan.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Shiyin was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Qiang, Governor of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, and King of Henan.

entries.zh: 拾寅東破索虜，加開府儀同三司。
entries.en: When Shiyin defeated the Northern Wei forces in the east, he was further granted the title of Director with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Shiyin defeated the Northern Wei barbarians in the east and was given the additional title of Director with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 世祖大明五年，拾寅遣使獻善舞馬，四角羊。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Emperor Shizu's Daming reign, Shiyin sent envoys presenting fine dancing horses and four-horned sheep.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Daming era of Emperor Shizu, Shiyin sent envoys presenting dancing horses of fine quality and four-horned sheep.

entries.zh: 皇太子、王公以下上舞馬歌者二十七首。
entries.en: The crown prince, princes, dukes, and officials below them submitted twenty-seven songs in praise of the dancing horses.
entries.literal: The crown prince, kings, dukes, and those below submitted twenty-seven songs on the dancing horses.

entries.zh: 太宗泰始三年，進號征西大將軍。
entries.en: In the third year of Emperor Taizong's Taishi reign, Shiyin's title was advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West.
entries.literal: In the third year of the Taishi era of Emperor Taizong, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West.

entries.zh: 五年，拾寅奉表獻方物，以弟拾皮為平西將軍、金城公。
entries.en: In the fifth year Shiyin sent a memorial with local tribute and appointed his younger brother Shipi General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jincheng.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Shiyin submitted a memorial presenting local products and made his younger brother Shipi General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jincheng.

entries.zh: 前廢帝又進號車騎大將軍。
entries.en: The Deposed Former Emperor further advanced his title to Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: The Deposed Emperor of the Former Reign again advanced his title to Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 阿柴虜吐谷渾，遼東鮮卑也。
entries.en: The Tuyuhun—whom the northwestern tribes called the "A-Chai" barbarians—were Xianbei from Liaodong.
entries.literal: The Tuyuhun, whom the northwestern tribes called the A-Chai barbarians, were Xianbei from Liaodong.

entries.zh: 父弈洛韓，有二子，長曰吐谷渾，少曰若洛廆。
entries.en: Their father Yiluohan had two sons—the elder named Tuyuhun, the younger Ruoluohe.
entries.literal: Their father Yiluohan had two sons: the elder was called Tuyuhun, the younger Ruoluohe.

entries.zh: 若洛廆別為慕容氏。
entries.en: Ruoluohe's descendants formed the Murong clan as a separate line.
entries.literal: Ruoluohe's line became the Murong clan separately.

entries.zh: 渾庶長，廆正嫡。
entries.en: Hun was the elder son of a concubine, while Hui was the legitimate heir.
entries.literal: Hun was the elder son by a concubine; Hui was the legitimate heir.

entries.zh: 父在時，分七百戶與渾，[2]渾與廆二部俱牧馬，馬鬭相傷，廆怒，遣信謂渾曰：「先公處分，與兄異部，牧馬何不相遠，而致鬭爭相傷？」
entries.en: While their father was still alive he allotted seven hundred households to Hun.
