[2] The two divisions of Hun and Hui pastured their horses together; when the herds fought and injured one another, Hui grew angry and sent a messenger to Hun, saying, "Our late father placed you and me in separate divisions—why not pasture farther apart, instead of letting the horses fight and wound each other?"
entries.literal: While their father was alive he allotted seven hundred households to Hun. [2] Hun and Hui's two divisions both pastured horses together; the horses fought and injured one another. Hui grew angry and sent a messenger to say to Hun: "Our late father's arrangement placed you and me in separate divisions—why do we not pasture our horses farther apart, yet instead bring fighting and injury?"

entries.zh: 渾曰：「馬是畜生，食草飲水，春氣發動，所以致鬭。
entries.en: Hun replied, "Horses are animals—they graze and drink; when spring stirs them, they fight. That is all.
entries.literal: Hun said: "Horses are beasts—they eat grass and drink water; when spring qi stirs, that is why they fight.

entries.zh: 鬭在於馬，而怒及人邪。
entries.en: The quarrel is between the horses—why turn your anger on me?
entries.literal: The fighting is among the horses—why take anger at a person?

entries.zh: 乖別甚易，今當去汝萬里。」
entries.en: Parting is easy enough—I shall now put ten thousand li between us."
entries.literal: Separation is very easy; now I shall leave you ten thousand li away."

entries.zh: 於是擁馬西行，日移一頓，頓八十里。
entries.en: With that he drove his herds westward, advancing one day's march at a time—eighty li per march.
entries.literal: Thereupon he drove his horses westward, moving one stage each day, each stage eighty li.

entries.zh: 經數頓，廆悔悟，深自咎責，遣舊父老及長史乙那樓追渾令還。
entries.en: After several days' march Hui repented and reproached himself deeply; he sent the old clan elders and Chief Clerk Yi Nalou to overtake Hun and bring him back.
entries.literal: After several stages Hui came to regret it, blamed himself deeply, and sent the elders of former days and Chief Clerk Yi Nalou to pursue Hun and bring him back.

entries.zh: [3]渾曰：「我乃祖以來，樹德遼右，又卜筮之言，先公有二子，福胙並流子孫。
entries.en: [3] Hun said, "Since my grandfather's day our house has built its virtue east of the Liao, and divination had declared that our late father had two sons and that blessing and sacrificial fortune would flow to both lines of descendants.
entries.literal: [3] Hun said: "From my grandfather's time we have planted virtue east of the Liao; moreover divination said our late father had two sons and that blessings and sacrificial portions would both flow to their descendants.

entries.zh: 我是卑庶，理無並大，今以馬致別，殆天所啟。
entries.en: I am of low birth and cannot by right stand equal with the heir; that horses should now force our parting is perhaps Heaven's own prompting.
entries.literal: I am lowborn and of inferior status; by principle I cannot stand equal with the great; now horses have brought about separation—perhaps Heaven is opening the way.

entries.zh: 諸君試擁馬令東，馬若還東，我當相隨去。」
entries.en: Try, all of you, driving the horses east—if they turn back eastward, I shall return with you."
entries.literal: You gentlemen, try driving the horses east; if the horses return east, I shall go back with you."

entries.zh: 樓喜拜曰：「處可寒。」
entries.en: Lou bowed gladly and said, "Chukhan!"
entries.literal: Lou bowed with joy and said: "Chukhan."

entries.zh: 虜言「處可寒」，宋言爾官家也。
entries.en: In their tongue "chukhan" means, in the language of Song, "your lordship."
entries.literal: In barbarian speech "chukhan" means, in Song language, "your lordship."

entries.zh: 即使所從二千騎共遮馬令回，不盈三百步，欻然悲鳴突走，聲若頹山。
entries.en: He then had the two thousand horsemen who had come with him try together to turn the herd back; within less than three hundred paces the horses suddenly gave mournful cries, broke away, and bolted—the noise like a mountain falling.
entries.literal: Thereupon he had the two thousand horsemen who had come with him together block the horses and turn them back; within less than three hundred paces they suddenly wailed, broke away, and fled—the sound like a collapsing mountain.

entries.zh: 如是者十餘輩，一向一遠。
entries.en: This happened more than ten times—each attempt sent them farther west.
entries.literal: This happened more than ten times—they went one direction, then farther away.

entries.zh: 樓力屈，又跪曰：「可寒，此非復人事。」
entries.en: Lou's strength gave out; he knelt again and said, "Chukhan, this is no longer within human power."
entries.literal: Lou's strength was exhausted; he knelt again and said: "Chukhan, this is no longer a matter within human power."

entries.zh: 渾謂其部落曰：「我兄弟子孫，並應昌盛，廆當傳子及曾孫玄孫，其間可百餘年，我乃玄孫間始當顯耳。」
entries.en: Hun told his tribesmen, "My brother's line and mine will both prosper; Hui's house will pass from son to great-grandson and beyond for perhaps a hundred years or more, while my line will not come to prominence until the generation of my great-great-grandsons."
entries.literal: Hun said to his tribesmen: "My brother's descendants and mine should both flourish; Hui will pass the succession to sons, great-grandsons, and great-great-grandsons—between them perhaps a hundred-odd years—and only among my great-great-grandsons' generation will my line begin to rise."

entries.zh: 於是遂西附陰山。
entries.en: With that he went west and settled by the Yin Mountains.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went west and attached himself to the Yin Mountains.

entries.zh: 遭晉亂，遂得上隴。
entries.en: When the Jin realm fell into chaos, he was able to reach the upper Long region.
entries.literal: When the Jin fell into disorder, he was able to reach the upper Long region.

entries.zh: 後廆追思渾，作阿干之歌。
entries.en: Later, missing Hun, Hui composed the Song of Aghan.
entries.literal: Later Hui, recalling Hun with longing, composed the Song of Aghan.

entries.zh: 鮮卑呼兄為「阿干」。
entries.en: The Xianbei call an elder brother "aghan."
entries.literal: The Xianbei call an elder brother "aghan."

entries.zh: 廆子孫竊號，以此歌為輦後大曲。
entries.en: When Hui's descendants assumed royal titles, they made this song the great processional hymn played behind the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: Hui's descendants usurped imperial titles and made this song the great piece behind the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 恭皇帝諱侑，元德太子之子也。
entries.en: Emperor Gong, whose personal name was You, was the son of the Yuande Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Gong's taboo name was You; he was the son of the Yuande Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 母曰韋妃。
entries.en: His mother was Consort Wei.
entries.literal: His mother was Consort Wei.

entries.zh: 性聰敏，有氣度。
entries.en: He was intelligent and quick-witted, with a dignified presence.
entries.literal: By nature he was clever and quick, and had dignified bearing.

entries.zh: 大業三年，立為陳王。
entries.en: In Daye year three, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: In the third year of Daye, he was established as Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 後數載，徙為代王，邑萬戶。
entries.en: A few years later he was transferred to the title of Prince of Dai, with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: After several years, he was transferred to be Prince of Dai, with a fief of ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 及煬帝親征遼東，令於京師總留事。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang marched personally against Liaodong, he was left in the capital to manage all affairs of state.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang personally campaigned in Liaodong, he was ordered to oversee all remaining affairs in the capital.

entries.zh: 十一年，從幸晉陽，拜太原太守。
entries.en: In year eleven he accompanied the court to Jinyang and was appointed governor of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he accompanied the emperor to Jinyang and was appointed Governor of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 尋鎮京師。
entries.en: Shortly thereafter he was stationed in the capital.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he garrisoned the capital.

entries.zh: 義兵入長安，尊煬帝為太上皇，奉帝纂業。
entries.en: When the volunteer army entered Chang'an, Emperor Yang was given the title of Retired Emperor, and Yang You was enthroned to continue the dynasty.
entries.literal: When the righteous army entered Chang'an, Emperor Yang was honored as Retired Emperor, and the emperor was installed to carry on the enterprise.

entries.zh: 義寧元年十一月壬戌，上即皇帝位於大興殿。
entries.en: On renxu day in the eleventh month of Yining year one, the emperor ascended the throne in Daxing Hall.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yining, on the day renxu, the emperor took the throne at Daxing Hall.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「王道喪亂，天步不康，古往今來，代有其事，屬之於朕，逢此百罹，彼蒼者天，胡寧斯忍！
entries.en: An edict proclaimed: "The royal Way lies in ruin and the steps of Heaven are unsteady. Every age, past and present, has seen such times—but that they should fall to me, that I should meet a hundred calamities—O azure Heaven, how can you be so merciless!
entries.literal: An edict said: "The royal way is lost in disorder, Heaven's steps are not tranquil—throughout antiquity and the present each age has had such events. That it should fall to me and that I meet these countless calamities—O azure Heaven, how can you be so cruel!

entries.zh: 襁褓之歲，夙遭憫凶，孺子之辰，太上播越，興言感動，實疚于懷。
entries.en: Still in my swaddling clothes I suffered early bereavement; while still a child the Retired Emperor was driven into exile. The thought of it moves me, and the sorrow weighs ever on my heart.
entries.literal: In my swaddling-clothes years I early met sorrowful loss; in my tender youth the Retired Emperor was driven into exile. To speak of it moves me—truly it weighs on my heart.

entries.zh: 太尉唐公，膺期作宰，時稱舟楫，大拯橫流，糾合義兵，翼戴皇室，與國休戚，再匡區夏，爰奉明詔，弼予幼沖，顯命光臨，天威咫尺，對揚尊號，悼心失圖。
entries.en: The Grand Marshal, the Duke of Tang, was born for the age and rose to lead the government—called the boat and oar of the realm, he rescued the nation from drowning waters, rallied the righteous armies, and upheld the imperial house, sharing its fortunes through good and ill and twice restoring order within the Four Seas. Now, bearing the bright edict, he assists my tender youth; his august commission shines upon us, Heaven's might is almost within reach. Facing him and accepting the honored title, my grieving heart knows no course.
entries.literal: The Grand Marshal, Duke of Tang, received the season to serve as chief minister; of the age he was called the boat and oars; he greatly rescued the flood-tide; he gathered righteous troops and supported and upheld the royal house, sharing the state's weal and woe; twice he restored the realm within the Four Seas; now he receives the bright edict, assists my tender youth; manifest mandate arrives in glory, Heaven's majesty is within a foot's distance; facing and proclaiming the honored title, my grieving heart loses its design.

entries.zh: 一人在遠，三讓不遂，僶俛南面，厝身無所，苟利社稷，莫敢或違，俯從羣議，奉遵聖旨。
entries.en: With one man still far away, thrice I declined and could not prevail; bowing low I take the south-facing throne with nowhere to rest myself. If the altars of state may benefit, I dare not refuse—humbly I follow the counsel of the assembly and obey the sacred command.
entries.literal: With one person far away, thrice I declined and could not succeed; bowing my head I face south, with no place to set my body; if it benefits the altars of soil and grain, I dare not disobey in any way; I humbly follow the multitude's counsel and respectfully obey the sacred intent.

entries.zh: 可大赦天下，改大業十三年為義寧元年。
entries.en: A general amnesty is hereby granted throughout the realm, and the thirteenth year of Daye is renamed the first year of Yining.
entries.literal: A general amnesty for All Under Heaven is permitted; Daye thirteenth year is changed to Yining first year.

entries.zh: 十一月十六日昧爽以前，大辟罪已下，皆赦除之；
entries.en: Before dawn on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, all offenses from capital crimes downward shall be pardoned and remitted;
entries.literal: Before dawn on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, for offenses from capital crimes downward, all are pardoned and remitted;

entries.zh: 常赦所不免者，不在赦限。」
entries.en: Crimes ordinarily exempt from amnesty remain outside the scope of this pardon."
entries.literal: Those whom ordinary amnesties do not exempt are not within the scope of the pardon."

entries.zh: 甲子，以光祿大夫、大將軍、太尉唐公為假黃鉞、使持節、大都督內外諸軍事、尚書令、大丞相，進封唐王。
entries.en: On jiazi day, the Duke of Tang—holding the posts of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General, and Grand Marshal—was given provisional authority over the yellow battle-axe, commissioned with imperial credentials as Grand Commander of all military affairs at home and abroad, made Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Chancellor, and advanced to the rank of Prince of Tang.
entries.literal: On the day jiazi, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General, Grand Marshal Duke of Tang was made provisional bearer of the yellow battle-axe, commissioner holding credentials, Grand Commander of all military affairs at home and abroad, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Chancellor, and was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Tang.

entries.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「朕惟孺子，未出深宮，太上遠巡，追蹤穆滿。
entries.en: On bingyin day an edict proclaimed: "I am but a child who has never left the inner palace; the Retired Emperor roams far abroad, following in the footsteps of King Mu of Zhou.
entries.literal: On the day bingyin, an edict said: "I am but a child, never having left the deep palace; the Retired Emperor tours afar, tracing the tracks of King Mu (Man).

entries.zh: 時逢多難，委當尊極，辭不獲免，恭己臨朝，若涉大川，罔知所濟，撫躬永歎，憂心孔棘。
entries.en: In this age of many calamities the supreme dignity has been laid upon me; though I decline I cannot be spared. Reverently holding myself in check I preside over court, as one crossing a great river without knowing how to reach the other shore. I sigh endlessly in self-reproach, and my heart is sorely troubled.
entries.literal: The times meet many difficulties; the supreme dignity is entrusted to me; declining, I cannot be exempted; reverently I hold myself and face court, as if crossing a great river, not knowing where to cross; stroking my person I sigh endlessly; my anxious heart is exceedingly troubled.

entries.zh: 民之情偽，曾未之聞，王業艱難，載云其易。
entries.en: I have never yet learned the ways of the people, yet I am told the royal enterprise is an easy thing!
entries.literal: The people's truth and falsehood I have never yet heard of; the royal enterprise's hardship—they say it is easy!

entries.zh: 賴股肱戮力，上宰賢良，匡佐沖人，輔其不逮。
entries.en: I rely on my ministers to exert their full strength, on wise and capable chief officials to support and counsel my youth and supply what I lack.
entries.literal: Relying on the limbs and trunks exerting their strength, the chief ministers wise and good, supporting and assisting the immature person, helping where I fall short.

entries.zh: 軍國機務，事無大小，文武設官，位無貴賤，憲章賞罰，咸歸相府，庶績其凝，責成斯屬，逖聽前史，茲為典故。
entries.en: All affairs of army and state, great and small alike; the appointment of civil and military officials regardless of rank; the statutes of reward and punishment—all shall lie with the chancellor's office, that achievements may be consolidated and responsibility fulfilled there. Listening to the records of antiquity, this is established precedent.
entries.literal: Military and state urgent affairs, matters without great or small; civil and military officials set in office, ranks without noble or base; statutes of reward and punishment—all return to the chancellor's office; may achievements be consolidated, responsibility fulfilled therein—hearing the former histories afar, this is established precedent.

entries.zh: 因循仍舊，非曰徒言，所存至公，無為讓德。」
entries.en: Continuing as before is no empty formula—the aim is utter fairness, not a show of yielding virtue."
entries.literal: Following precedent and continuing as before is not merely empty words; what is preserved is utter fairness, without pretense of yielding virtue."

entries.zh: 己巳，以唐王子隴西公建成為唐國世子，敦煌公為京兆尹，[2]改封秦公，元吉為齊公，食邑各萬戶。
entries.en: On jisi day, the Duke of Tang's son, the Duke of Longxi (Jiancheng), was named heir to the State of Tang; the Duke of Dunhuang was appointed Governor of Jingzhao, [2] and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Qin; Yuanji was made Duke of Qi; each received a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: On the day jisi, the Duke of Tang's son the Duke of Longxi Jiancheng was made Heir of the State of Tang; the Duke of Dunhuang was made Governor of Jingzhao, [2] changed in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin; Yuanji was made Duke of Qi; each received a fief of ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 太原置鎮北府。
entries.en: The Northern Garrison Office was established at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: At Taiyuan the Northern Garrison Office was established.

entries.zh: 乙亥，張掖康老和舉兵反。
entries.en: On yihai day, Kang Laohe of Zhangye raised an army in rebellion.
entries.literal: On the day yihai, Kang Laohe of Zhangye raised troops in rebellion.

entries.zh: 三月丙辰，右屯衞將軍宇文化及殺太上皇於江都宮，右禦衞將軍獨孤盛死之。
entries.en: In the third month, on bingchen day, Right Garrison Guard General Yuwen Huaji killed the Retired Emperor at the Jiangdu Palace; Right Imperial Guard General Dugu Sheng died defending him.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the day bingchen, Right Garrison Guard General Yuwen Huaji killed the Retired Emperor at the Jiangdu Palace; Right Imperial Guard General Dugu Sheng died in the event.

entries.zh: 齊王暕，趙王杲，燕王倓，光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、行右翊衞大將軍宇文協，金紫光祿大夫、內史侍郎虞世基，銀青光祿大夫、御史大夫裴蘊，通議大夫、行給事郎許善心，皆遇害。
entries.en: Prince of Qi Yang Jian, Prince of Zhao Yang Gao, Prince of Yan Yang Dan, Yuwen Xie (Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guard), Yu Shiji (Palace Secretary), Pei Yun (Censor-in-Chief), and Xu Shanxin (Acting Recorder)—all were killed.
entries.literal: Prince of Qi Yang Jian, Prince of Zhao Yang Gao, Prince of Yan Yang Dan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Master of the Palace with Honors Equal to the Three Lords and Acting General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guard Yuwen Xie, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Palace Secretary Yu Shiji, Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Grand Master for Discussion of Affairs, Acting Recorder Xu Shanxin—all met with violent death.

entries.zh: 化及立秦王浩為帝，自稱大丞相，朝士文武皆受其官爵。
entries.en: Huaji enthroned Prince of Qin Yang Hao as emperor, styled himself Grand Chancellor, and all officials at court received appointments and titles from him.
entries.literal: Huaji installed Prince of Qin Yang Hao as emperor, styled himself Grand Chancellor, and all court civil and military officials received offices and ranks from him.

entries.zh: 光祿大夫、宿公麥才，折衝郎將、朝請大夫沈光，同謀討賊，夜襲化及營，反為所害。
entries.en: Mai Cai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Su, and Shen Guang, vanguard lieutenant and Gentleman for Court Presentation, plotted together to attack the rebels; by night they raided Huaji's camp but were killed in turn.
entries.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Duke of Su Mai Cai, and Vanguard Lieutenant, Gentleman for Court Presentation Shen Guang, together plotted to strike down the rebels; by night they raided Huaji's camp and were in turn killed by him.

entries.zh: 戊辰，詔唐王備九錫之禮，加璽紱、遠遊冠、綠綟綬，位在諸侯王上。
entries.en: On wuchen day the Prince of Tang was granted the full Nine Bestowals—seal and ribbon, Far-Traveling Cap, and green cord with crimson sash—and his rank was placed above all feudal princes.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen, the Prince of Tang was granted the full Nine Bestowals; he was given the seal and ribbon, the Far-Traveling Cap, and the green cord and crimson sash; his rank was set above all feudal princes and kings.

entries.zh: 唐國置丞相已下，一依舊式。
entries.en: For the State of Tang, offices from Grand Chancellor downward were established entirely according to precedent.
entries.literal: For the State of Tang, offices from Grand Chancellor downward were established entirely according to the old pattern.

entries.zh: 天禍隋國，大行太上皇遇盜江都，酷甚望夷，釁深驪北。
entries.en: Heaven has calamitously struck the Sui state: the late Retired Emperor was murdered by bandits at Jiangdu—a cruelty surpassing the death at Wangyi, an outrage deeper than the killing at Mount Li.
entries.literal: Heaven calamity befell the Sui state; the late Retired Emperor met robbers at Jiangdu—the cruelty exceeding Wangyi, the outrage deeper than north of Mount Li.

entries.zh: 憫予小子，奄逮丕愆，哀號承感，心情糜潰，仰惟荼毒，仇復靡申，形影相弔，罔知啟處。
entries.en: Pity this child of mine, suddenly burdened with grievous fault! Wailing I am seized by grief; my heart and spirit are shattered. Looking up at this bitter calamity, I have no way to fulfill revenge. Shadow and form mourn each other; I know not how to conduct myself.
entries.literal: Pity this child of mine—suddenly I meet great fault; wailing I receive the stirring; heart and feelings are crushed and broken; looking up I contemplate the bitter poison; vengeance cannot be declared; shadow and form mourn each other; I know not how to conduct myself.

entries.zh: 予本代王，及予而代，天之所廢，豈期如是！
entries.en: I was originally Prince of Dai—and now "Dai" has become "replacement." What Heaven casts aside, who could have foreseen such an end!
entries.literal: I was originally Prince of Dai—"Dai" and "to replace"—what Heaven has cast aside, who could have expected it thus!

entries.zh: 庶憑稽古之聖，以誅四凶，幸值惟新之恩，預充三恪。
entries.en: May I rely on the sage who examines antiquity to punish the Four Evils; fortunate to receive the grace of the new dynasty, I may yet be counted among the Three Reverences.
entries.literal: May I rely on the sage who examines antiquity to execute the Four Evils; fortunately meeting the grace of renewal, I am beforehand enrolled among the Three Reverences.

entries.zh: 雪寃恥於皇祖，守禋祀為孝孫，朝聞夕殞，及泉無恨，今遵故事，遜於舊邸。
entries.en: To avenge the wrong done my imperial forebear, to keep the ancestral rites as a filial grandson—if I heard of it at dawn and died at dusk I would die without regret down to the Yellow Springs. Now following precedent I yield the throne at my former residence.
entries.literal: To wipe away shame and disgrace for the imperial ancestor, to keep the ancestral sacrifices as a filial grandson—hearing in the morning and dying at evening, down to the Yellow Springs without regret; now following old precedent I yield at the former residence.

entries.zh: 庶官羣辟，改事唐朝，宜依前典，趣上尊號。
entries.en: All officials and assembled lords: transfer your allegiance to the Tang dynasty; according to precedent, hasten to bestow the supreme title.
entries.literal: All officials and the assembled lords: change your service to the Tang dynasty; you should according to former canon hasten to bestow the honored title.

entries.zh: 若釋重負，感泰兼懷，假手真人，俾除醜逆。
entries.en: As if casting off a heavy burden, I feel both peace and gratitude—through the hand of the true sovereign, may the vile rebels be destroyed.
entries.literal: As if shedding a heavy burden; feeling both peace and gratitude; borrowing the hand of the true man, that he may remove the vile rebels.

entries.zh: 濟濟多士，明知朕意。
entries.en: You many officers—surely you understand my intent.
entries.literal: The multitude of worthy officers—clearly know my intent.

entries.zh: 晉武帝泰始二年，遣傅玄等造行禮及上壽食舉歌詩。
entries.en: In second year of Jin of Taishi, Fu Xuan and others were sent to write processional, longevity, and banquet songs.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, Fu Xuan and others were dispatched to compose songs for processional rites, longevity toasts, and banquet music.

entries.zh: 張華表曰：「按漢、魏所用，雖詩章辭異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗曲折，並系於舊，一皆因襲，不敢有所改也。」
entries.en: Zhang Hua wrote: "Han and Wei pieces differ in wording and came and went with the times, but their phrasing and turns all followed old models—nothing was boldly changed."
entries.literal: Zhang Hua memorialized: "Examining what Han and Wei used, although the texts of the poems differ and pieces rose and fell with the times, their cadences and turns all depend on the old models—every one was inherited, and none dared to be altered."

entries.zh: 九年，荀勖典樂，使郭夏、宋識造《正德》、《大豫》之舞。
entries.en: In year 9, Xun Xu had Guo Xia and Song Shi compose Correct Virtue and Great Yu.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, Xun Xu oversaw music and had Guo Xia and Song Shi create the Correct Virtue and Great Yu dances."

entries.zh: 改魏《昭武舞》曰《宣武舞》，羽籥舞曰《宜文舞》。
entries.en: Wei's Bright Martial became Propagating Martial, and the feather-flute dance became Propagating Culture.
entries.literal: The Wei Bright Martial Dance was changed to the Propagating Martial Dance, and the feather-and-flute dance to the Propagating Culture Dance.

entries.zh: 江左之初，典章堙紊，賀循為太常卿，始有登歌之樂。
entries.en: Early Eastern Jin law was in disarray; under He Xun as Grand Music Master, ascent hymns finally appeared.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Eastern Jin, statutes were buried in disorder; when He Xun became Director of Ceremonies, there were at last songs for the ascent hymn.

entries.zh: 大寧末，阮孚等又增益之。
entries.en: Late in Daning, Ruan Fu and others expanded the repertoire.
entries.literal: At the end of the Daning era, Ruan Fu and others added to them further.

entries.zh: 咸和間，鳩集遺逸，鄴沒胡後，樂人頗復南度，東晉因之，以具鐘律。
entries.en: In Xianhe, refugees were collected; after Ye fell, musicians fled south and Eastern Jin finally had bells and pipes.
entries.literal: During the Xianhe period, scattered survivors were gathered; after Ye fell to the barbarians, many musicians crossed south again, and Eastern Jin thereby acquired bells and pitch pipes.

entries.zh: 太元間，破苻永固，又獲樂工楊蜀等，閑練舊樂，於是金石始備。
entries.en: In Taiyuan, after Fu Yonggu was beaten, musicians like Yang Shu restored the old repertoire and metal-and-stone instruments were complete.
entries.literal: During the Taiyuan period, after the defeat of Fu Yonggu, the musicians Yang Shu and others were also captured; versed in the old music, they at last completed the full ensemble of metal and stone.

entries.zh: 尋其設懸音調，並與江左是同。
entries.en: Their pitch arrangements matched those of the Eastern Jin.
entries.literal: Examining their suspended-instrument pitch systems, they were the same as those of the Eastern Jin.

entries.zh: 牛弘遂因鄭譯之舊，又請依古五聲六律，旋相為宮。
entries.en: Niu Hong, building on Zheng Yi, also asked to restore cyclical palace modulation from the five tones and six pitch-pipes.
entries.literal: Niu Hong then, following Zheng Yi's earlier work, also requested that the ancient five tones and six pitch-pipes be used, cyclically modulating as palace keys.

entries.zh: 雅樂每宮但一調，唯迎氣奏五調，謂之五音。
entries.en: Court music used one mode per palace key; only qi-welcoming rites used five modes—the five tones.
entries.literal: In court ritual music each palace key had only one mode; only for welcoming the qi were five modes played—these were called the five tones.

entries.zh: 縵樂用七調，祭祀施用。
entries.en: Slow ceremonial music used seven modes for sacrifice.
entries.literal: Slow music used seven modes and was employed in sacrifices.

entries.zh: 各依聲律尊卑為次。
entries.en: Each was ranked by pitch hierarchy.
entries.literal: Each was ordered according to the rank of pitch and tone.

entries.zh: 高祖猶憶妥言，注弘奏下，不許作旋宮之樂，但作黃鐘一宮而已。
entries.en: Gaozu heeded Tuo's advice, annotated Niu Hong's memorial, and forbade cyclical modulation—only Yellow Bell palace would do.
entries.literal: Gaozu still remembered Tuo's words; he annotated Niu Hong's memorial and rejected cyclical-palace music, allowing only a single Yellow Bell palace key.

entries.zh: 於是牛弘及秘書丞姚察、通直散騎常侍許善心、儀同三司劉臻、通直郎虞世基等，更共詳議曰：
entries.en: Niu Hong, Yao Cha, Xu Shanxin, Liu Zhen, Yu Shiji, and others then deliberated jointly:
entries.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong, Secretariat Aide Yao Cha, Palace Attendant Xu Shanxin, Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes Liu Zhen, and Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji and others jointly deliberated further, saying:

entries.zh: 十四年三月，樂定。
entries.en: third year of Month, year 14—the music was fixed.
entries.literal: Third month of the fourteenth year—the music was fixed.

entries.zh: 秘書監、奇章縣公牛弘，秘書丞、北絳郡公姚察，通直散騎常侍、虞部侍郎許善心，兼內史舍人虞世基，儀同三司、東宮學士饒陽伯劉臻等奏曰：「臣聞蕢桴土鼓，由來斯尚，雷出地奮，著自《易經》。
entries.en: Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang County and Director of the Palace Library; Yao Cha, Assistant in the Palace Library and Duke of Beijiang Commandery; Xu Shanxin, Palace Attendant for Unrestricted Communication and Vice Minister of the Bureau of Receptacles; Yu Shiji, concurrently Secretariat Drafter; Liu Zhen, Equal to the Three Excellencies and Eastern Palace scholar, Baron of Raoyang; and others memorialized: "We have heard that rush drumsticks and earthen drums have been honored from antiquity, and that thunder emerging and earth stirring is set forth in the Book of Changes.
entries.literal: Secretariat Director and Qizhang County Duke Niu Hong, Secretariat Aide and Beijiang Commandery Duke Yao Cha, Palace Attendant and Yu Department Vice Minister Xu Shanxin, Concurrent Palace Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shiji, Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes and Eastern Palace Scholar Raoyang Marquis Liu Zhen and others memorialized: "Your subject has heard that earthen drums and earthen drums have been honored from old; thunder emerging from earth and leaping forth is recorded in the Changes.

entries.zh: 邃古帝王，經邦馭物，揖讓而臨天下者，祀樂之謂也。
entries.en: Ancient emperors governed through sacrificial music.
entries.literal: Remote ancient emperors, governing the state and mastering things, yielding the throne and facing all under Heaven—this is what sacrificial music means.

entries.zh: 秦焚經典，樂書亡缺，爰至漢興，始加鳩采，祖述增廣，緝成朝憲。
entries.en: Qin burned classics; Han began collecting music into court law.
entries.literal: Qin burned the classics and music books were lost; only when Han rose did collection begin, inheriting and expanding into court law.

entries.zh: 魏、晉相承，更加論討，沿革之宜，備於故實。
entries.en: Wei and Jin added discussion recorded in precedent.
entries.literal: Wei and Jin handed down and added further discussion—the appropriateness of succession and change is fully recorded in old fact.

entries.zh: 永嘉之後，九服崩離，燕、石、苻、姚，遁據華土。
entries.en: After Yongjia the realm collapsed; barbarian states held the Central Plains.
entries.literal: After Yongjia the nine domains collapsed; Yan, Shi, Fu, and Yao seized and held the Central Plains.

entries.zh: 此其戎乎，何必伊川之上，吾其左衽，無復微管之功。
entries.en: Barbarians everywhere—not only beyond the Yi; left lapels, no Guan Zhong.
entries.literal: These were barbarians—why must it be above the Yi River? Our left lapels—no more Guan Zhong's achievement.

entries.zh: 前言往式，於斯而盡。
entries.en: Former patterns ended there.
entries.literal: The former patterns end here.

entries.zh: 金陵建社，朝士南奔，帝則皇規，粲然更備，與內原隔絕，三百年於茲矣。
entries.en: Jinling rose; scholars fled south—three centuries cut off from the heartland.
entries.literal: Jinling established its altar; court scholars fled south—the imperial regulations brilliantly renewed, yet cut off from the inner heartland for three hundred years.

entries.zh: 伏惟明聖膺期，會昌在運。
entries.en: Enlightened sagacity received the era; fortune flourishes.
entries.literal: Your subject reverently considers that enlightened sagacity received the era; flourishing brilliance is in fortune.

entries.zh: 今南征所獲梁、陳樂人，及晉、宋旗章，宛然俱至。
entries.en: Liang-Chen musicians and Jin-Song regalia have all arrived.
entries.literal: Now musicians of Liang and Chen captured in the southern campaign, and Jin and Song banners and standards, have all duly arrived.

entries.zh: 曩代所不服者，今悉服之，前朝所未得者，今悉得之。
entries.en: Former non-submitters submit; former lacks are filled.
entries.literal: What former ages did not submit to now all submit; what former dynasties did not obtain now all obtain.

entries.zh: 化洽功成，於是乎在。
entries.en: Transformation harmonized, achievement complete.
entries.literal: Transformation harmonized and achievement complete—here it is.

entries.zh: 臣等伏奉明詔，詳定雅樂，博訪知音，旁求儒彥，研校是非，定其去就，取為一代正樂，具在本司。」
entries.en: We fixed court music as one generation's orthodox repertoire."
entries.literal: Your subjects reverently received the clear edict, thoroughly fixing court ritual music, broadly seeking those who know tone, seeking Confucian talents on all sides, examining right and wrong and fixing what to keep or discard, taking this as one generation's orthodox music—all detailed in this office."

entries.zh: 於是並撰歌辭三十首，詔並令施用，見行者皆停之。
entries.en: Thirty song texts were composed; edict ordered their use and stopped old practice.
entries.literal: Thereupon thirty song texts were composed together; an edict ordered all applied, and whatever was in practice was stopped.

entries.zh: 其人間音樂，流僻日久，棄其舊體者，並加禁約，務存其本。
entries.en: Popular music was restricted to preserve its root.
entries.literal: Popular music long flowing in vulgar ways, abandoning its old form—all were restricted to preserve the root.

entries.zh: 開皇九年，平陳，獲宋、齊舊樂，詔于太常置清商署以管之。
entries.en: ninth year of In of Kaihuang, after Chen fell, Song and Qi court music was seized and a Qing Shang Office was set up under the Grand Music Master.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, after the conquest of Chen, the court acquired the old music of Song and Qi; an edict ordered the establishment of a Qing Shang Office under the Director of Ceremonies to administer it.

entries.zh: 求陳太樂令蔡子元、於普明等，復居其職。
entries.en: Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and other former Chen music officials were found and reappointed.
entries.literal: Chen's former Director of Music Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others were sought out and restored to their posts.

entries.zh: 由是牛弘奏曰：
entries.en: Niu Hong then submitted a memorial:
entries.literal: Thereupon Niu Hong memorialized, saying:

entries.zh: 徐廣、徐爰、王隱等《晉書》云：「武帝泰始九年，中書監荀勖校太樂八音，不和，始知為後漢至魏，尺長於古四分有餘。
entries.en: The Jin History of Xu Guang, Xu Yuan, Wang Yin, and others records: "In the ninth year of Taishi, Xun Xu, Supervisor of the Secretariat, checked the eight timbres of the Grand Music and found them discordant; only then did he understand that from Later Han to Wei the chi had grown more than four fen longer than the ancient measure.
entries.literal: Xu Guang, Xu Ai, Wang Yin, and others' Jin History says: "In Emperor Wu's Taishi ninth year, Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu corrected the Grand Music eight timbres—they were not harmonious; then knowing that from Later Han through Wei the foot measure was more than four fen longer than antiquity.

entries.zh: 勖乃部著作郎劉恭，依《周禮》制尺，所謂古尺也。
entries.en: Xu ordered Liu Gong to make a Rites of Zhou foot measure—the ancient standard.
entries.literal: Xu then ordered Editorial Director Liu Gong to make a foot measure according to the Rites of Zhou—the so-called ancient foot measure.

entries.zh: 依古尺更鑄銅律呂，以調聲韻。
entries.en: Using the ancient measure, bronze pitch pipes were recast to restore harmony.
entries.literal: According to the ancient foot measure, bronze pitch pipes and bell tones were recast to tune sound and pitch.

entries.zh: 以尺量古器，與本銘尺寸無差。
entries.en: Ancient vessels measured against it matched their inscriptions exactly.
entries.literal: Using the foot measure to measure ancient vessels, there was no discrepancy with original inscription dimensions.

entries.zh: 又汲郡盜發魏襄王塚，得古周時玉律及鐘磬，與新律聲韻暗同。
entries.en: Ji commandery tomb robbers found Zhou jade pitch pipes and bells matching the new standards.
entries.literal: Also the Ji commandery tomb robbers opened King Xiang of Wei's tomb, obtaining ancient Zhou jade pitch standards and bells and chime stones—their sound and pitch darkly matched the new pitch standards.

entries.zh: 于時郡國或得漢時故鐘，吹新律命之，皆應。」
entries.en: Han-era bells found in the provinces all matched when tested against the new pipes."
entries.literal: At the time in commanderies and kingdoms, Han-era old bells were sometimes obtained; blowing the new pitch standards to tune them—all responded.

entries.zh: 梁武《鐘律緯》云：「祖沖之所傳銅尺，其銘曰：'晉泰始十年，中書考古器，揆校今尺，長四分半。
entries.en: Liang Wu's Treatise cites Zu Chongzhi's copper measure: "tenth year of Jin of Taishi—four fen and a half longer than the present measure.
entries.literal: Liang Wu's Treatise on Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes says: "The copper foot measure transmitted by Zu Chongzhi—its inscription says: 'Jin Taishi tenth year, the Secretariat examined ancient vessels and compared the present foot measure—it is four fen and a half longer.

entries.zh: 所校古法有七品：一曰姑洗玉律，二曰小呂玉律，三曰西京銅望臬，四曰金錯望臬，五曰銅斛，六曰古錢，七曰建武銅尺。
entries.en: Seven ancient reference standards were tested: Maiden Wash jade pipe, Lesser Bell jade pipe, Western Capital bronze gnomon, gold-inlaid gnomon, copper hu, ancient coins, and Jianwu copper measure.
entries.literal: The ancient methods examined had seven grades: first, Maiden Wash jade pitch standard; second, Lesser Bell jade pitch standard; third, Western Capital bronze gnomon table; fourth, gold-inlaid gnomon table; fifth, copper hu; sixth, ancient coins; seventh, Jianwu copper foot measure.

entries.zh: 姑洗微強，西京望臬微弱，其餘與此尺同。
entries.en: Maiden Wash ran slightly high; the Western Capital gnomon slightly low—the rest matched.
entries.literal: Maiden Wash was slightly strong; Western Capital gnomon table slightly weak—the rest matched this foot measure.

entries.zh: '銘八十二字。
entries.en: The inscription contains eighty-two characters.
entries.literal: Inscription: eighty-two characters.

entries.zh: 此尺者，勖新尺也。
entries.en: This is Xu's new measure.
entries.literal: This foot measure is Xu's new foot measure.

entries.zh: 今尺者，杜夔尺也。
entries.en: The contemporary measure is Du Kui's.
entries.literal: Today's foot measure is Du Kui's foot measure.

entries.zh: 雷次宗、何胤之二人作《鐘律圖》，所載荀勖校量古尺文，與此銘同。
entries.en: Lei Cizong and He Yin's Diagram records the same Xun Xu examination text.
entries.literal: Lei Cizong and He Yin's two authors' Diagram of Bell Standards and Pitch Pipes records Xun Xu's examination text of the ancient foot measure—the same as this inscription.

entries.zh: 而蕭吉樂譜，謂為梁朝所考七品，謬也。
entries.en: Xiao Ji wrongly attributes these to Liang-era examination.
entries.literal: But Xiao Ji's Music Treatise calls it the seven grades examined by the Liang court—this is erroneous.

entries.zh: 今以此尺為本，以校諸代尺」雲。
entries.en: This measure serves as the base for comparing all dynastic foot measures."
entries.literal: Now taking this foot measure as base to compare foot measures of various dynasties."

entries.zh: 蕭吉云：「出於《司馬法》。
entries.en: Xiao Ji says, "It comes from the Sima Methods.
entries.literal: Xiao Ji says: "It comes from the Sima Methods.

entries.zh: 梁朝刻其度於影表，以測影。」
entries.en: The Liang court carved its measure on a gnomon table for shadow measurement."
entries.literal: The Liang court carved its measure on the shadow table to measure shadows.

entries.zh: 案此即奉朝請祖暅所算造銅主影表者也。
entries.en: This is Court Gentleman Zu Geng's calculated bronze gnomon table.
entries.literal: Examining this—it is the bronze gnomon shadow table calculated and made by Court Gentleman Zu Geng.

entries.zh: 經陳滅入朝。
entries.en: It entered the court after Chen's fall.
entries.literal: After Chen's fall it entered the court.

entries.zh: 大業中，議以合古，乃用之調律，以制鐘磬等八音樂器。
entries.en: In Daye, it was deemed most antiquity-conforming and used to tune bells, chimes, and the eight timbres.
entries.literal: In the Daye era, discussion held it accorded with antiquity; therefore it was used to tune pitch standards and make bells, chime stones, and the eight timbres.

entries.zh: 蕭吉《樂譜》云：「漢章帝時，零陵文學史奚景於泠道縣舜廟下得玉律，度為此尺。」
entries.en: Xiao Ji records: "In Emperor Zhang of Han's time, the scholar Xi Jing of Lingling found a jade pitch pipe beneath Shun's temple in Lengdao county and derived this measure."
entries.literal: Xiao Ji's Music Treatise says: "In Emperor Zhang of Han's time, Lingling Literary Scholar Xi Jing at Shun's temple in Lengdao county obtained a jade pitch standard and made this foot measure from it.

entries.zh: 傅暢《晉諸公贊》云：「葛勖造鐘律，時人並稱其精密，唯陳留阮鹹，譏其聲高。
entries.en: Fu Chang records: "Ge Xun's standards were praised by contemporaries for precision; only Ruan Xian of Chenliu criticized the pitch as too high.
entries.literal: Fu Chang's Jin Worthies' Praise says: "Ge Xun made bell and pitch standards; people all praised their precision—only Chenliu Ruan Xian criticized their sound as high.

entries.zh: 後始平掘地，得古銅尺，歲久欲腐，以校荀勖今尺，短校四分。
entries.en: Later at Shiping, a decayed ancient copper measure proved four fen shorter than Xun Xu's—vindicating Ruan Xian.
entries.literal: Later at Shiping, excavating the ground, an ancient copper foot measure was obtained—long decayed; comparing with Xun Xu's present foot measure, it was four fen shorter in comparison.

entries.zh: 時人以咸為解。」
entries.en: Contemporaries acknowledged Ruan Xian was correct."
entries.literal: People of the time took Xian as having understood."

entries.zh: 此兩尺長短近同。
entries.en: These two measures are nearly identical.
entries.literal: These two foot measures' lengths are nearly the same.

entries.zh: 蕭吉雲，晉氏江東所用。
entries.en: Xiao Ji says Eastern Jin used this measure in Jiangdong.
entries.literal: Xiao Ji says the Jin clan used this in Jiangdong.

entries.zh: 自夫有天地焉，有人物焉，樹司牧以君臨，懸政教而成務，莫不擬乾坤之大象，稟中和以建極，揆影響之幽賾，成律呂之精微。
entries.en: From the moment Heaven and Earth existed and humanity arose, every ruler who governed and every state that taught its people modeled itself on the cosmos, drew on cosmic balance to set standards, read nature's hidden signs, and perfected the science of pitch and measure.
entries.literal: Since there have been Heaven and Earth, and since there have been people and things, in establishing rulers to govern and in setting forth government and teaching to accomplish their tasks, none have failed to take the great images of Heaven and Earth as their model, to receive the Mean and Harmony in establishing the supreme standard, to measure the hidden depths of shadow and influence, and to achieve the subtle refinements of pitch pipes and bell tones.

entries.zh: 是用範圍百度，財成萬品。
entries.en: Thus they regulated all standards and shaped the ten thousand kinds of things.
entries.literal: By this means they encompassed the hundred measures and completed the myriad things.

entries.zh: 昔者淳古葦籥，創睹人籟之源，女媧笙簧，仍昭鳳律之首。
entries.en: In deepest antiquity, reed flutes first disclosed the origin of human music; Nüwa's reed pipes still marked the first phoenix-toned pitch.
entries.literal: In antiquity, in the pure ancient age, reed pipes first revealed the source of human sounds; Nüwa's sheng and huang still proclaimed the beginning of the phoenix pitch.

entries.zh: 後聖廣業，稽古彌崇，伶倫含少，乃擅比竹之工，虞舜昭華，方傳刻玉之美。
entries.en: Later sages enlarged the tradition and revered the past: Ling Lun's "Containing the Lesser" perfected the art of calibrated bamboo pipes; Yu Shun's Bright Splendor preserved the craft of jade pitch pipes.
entries.literal: Later sages expanded the enterprise and honored antiquity ever more highly: Ling Lun's Han Shao mastered the craft of comparing bamboo tubes; Shun of Yu with Zhao Hua transmitted the beauty of carving jade.
